3. Est igitur nihil aliud, quam malitiosa & contumax repugnantia aduersus media gratiae omnia, tum ordinaria, tum extraordinaria atque abundantia (per princ. 5.): siue ea unquam fuerint cognita ac percepta, siue nunquam (per princ.

4.): praesertim vero, si ista repugnantia coniuncta fit cum contumelia, qua animus totus a veritate auersus est, eique aduersarius (per princ.

1.).

4. Ratio, quare hoc peccatum nunquam potest remitti, non sita est in gravitate huius delicti, tametsi omnium grauissimi (per princ. 11.): neque in eo, quod gratia Dei ac meritum Christi non ad hoc peccatum pertineant (per princ. 10.): sed tota posita est in ipsa natura huius peccati prorsus singulari ac propria, quoniam in hoc vno non potest fieri μετάνοια, ac salutis, per Christum recuperatae, recta adplicatio (per princ. 7. 12.

13. 14.).

5. Obstinatio animi perpetua vsque ad finem vitae, seu, vt moris est loqui, impoenitentia finalis, non est ipsa natura huius peccati, sed consequens atque adiunctum aliquid (per princ. 15.), quoniam hoc peccatum est eiusmodi, vt repudientur media gratiae omnia, siue ordinaria, siue extraordinaria atque abundantia (per definit. in confectar. 3.): fine his autem mediis nulla nunquam potest fieri μετάνοια (per princ. 14.): E. necessaria tunc erit obstinatio animi perpetua.

foederis communem existimare, Hebr. X, 29. At Filius Dei & sanguis foederis annuntiatur & offertur nobis per verbum evangelii.

2) Peccatores in Spiritum S. dicuntur gustasse bonum Dei verbum, Hebr. VI, 5. At bonum Dei verbum est evangelium, melle dulcius. Est enim laetus nuntius, Luc. II, 10. verbum pacis, Eph. II, 17. verbum reconciliationis nostrae cum Deo; 2 Cor. V, 19. Lex divina, quamuis per se bona fit, tanquam bona regula vitae, ab optimo auctore profecta: cuen-tualiter tamen homini peccatori non est bona, eo, quod ipsi iram Dei & maledictionem denuntiat, Rom. IV, 15. Deut. XXVII, 26. 3) Describitur peccatum in Spiritum S. per παράπτωσιν, apostasiam, aut defectionem a fide, qua homines illuminati gustarunt bonum Dei verbum & virtutes venturi saeculi, prolabentes autem, denuo crucifixerunt Filium Dei & ludibrio exposuerunt, Hebr. VI, 5. 6. At fides respicit evangelium, & apostasia a fide in Christum distincte ex evangelio cognoscitur.

Dicis: Omne peccatum prohibetur lege diuina. E. & peccatum in Spiritum S. Resp. Peccatum in Spiritum S. duobus modis consideratur: 1) generatim, quatenus est peccatum, & sic prohibetur lege: 2) speciatim, quatenus est peccatum in Spiritum S. & sic est voluntaria ac pertinax abnegatio veritatis evangelicae.


### Question XL. What are the formal requirements of the sin against the Holy Spirit?

The formal requirements of the sin against the Holy Spirit are: a plain, free, and malicious denial of the heavenly truth, clearly acknowledged and approved in the conscience; a hostile impugning of the maliciously denied truth; a voluntary blaspheming of the hostily impugned truth; a stubborn rejection of all means of salvation.

Proof a. That a clear acknowledgment and approval of divine truth is required for the sin against the Holy Spirit is evident from Heb. 10:26, where those who sin against the Holy Spirit are said to sin willfully, after they have received the knowledge of the truth, i.e., after they have been convicted in their conscience of the truth of the gospel. The same is gathered from Heb. 6:4, 5, 6, where it is asserted of sinners against the Holy Spirit that 1) they were enlightened, i.e., illuminated by the acknowledgment of Christian doctrine; 2) they tasted the super-celestial good, that is, they perceived by saving faith how sweet Christ is as the author of the forgiveness of sins and eternal life; 3) they were made partakers of the Holy Spirit, as a seal, pledge, and earnest of eternal salvation; 4) they tasted the good word of God, insofar as they perceived the sweetness of the gospel by experimental and affective knowledge (for taste, in the biblical style, denotes not a light or thin, but a rich perception joined with the affection of love and joy); 5) they tasted the powers of the age to come, by feeling and experiencing a most effective foretaste of the joys of eternal life. Therefore, that full acknowledgment of heavenly truth, appropriate to the state of the way, is graphically depicted by those words, most worthy of remembrance. From which we gather that Paul, in persecuting the divine truth, did not sin against the Holy Spirit; because he did this in ignorance, as he testifies of himself, 1 Tim. 1:13.

2) That a completely free denial of heavenly truth is required for the sin against the Holy Spirit, not extorted by fear of dangers, is evident from Heb. 10:26. For if we sin willfully after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there no longer remains a sacrifice for sins. Sinners against the Holy Spirit are said to sin ἑκουσίως, i.e., freely, voluntarily, maliciously, with a high hand, through contempt of the divine majesty, out of mere pride. But those who sin against the Holy Spirit sin τῷ παραπίπτειν, by falling away from illumination and taste, or experimental knowledge of the super-celestial gift, Heb. 6:6, and from the received knowledge of the truth, Heb. 10:26. But he who falls away is turned away from the illumination and accepted knowledge of the truth, he denies the divine truth once acknowledged, which he has from the grace of illumination. We gather from these things that Peter, in denying Christ, did not sin against the Holy Spirit, because he did not sin with a will that was entirely free, but one inclined by the fear of punishment. In the primitive church, when most grave persecutions arose, not a few, overcome by the force of torments or compelled by the fear of dangers, fell away from the doctrine of the Gospel; they sinned against the Son of man indeed, but not against the Holy Spirit.

Prob. b. That a hostile attack on the evangelical truth is required for the consummation of the sin against the Holy Spirit is evident from the description of those who sin against the Holy Spirit. For they crucify the Son of God again, i. e., they treat the Gospel of Christ as extinguished, Heb. VI, 4, they trample it underfoot, i. e., they treat it most contumeliously. By which words a hostile attack is indicated; by which either the whole doctrine of the faith is attacked, or one or another fundamental article of faith; the impugning of which also weakens the remaining connected articles of faith, if not directly and primarily, at least obliquely, secondarily, and by consequence; therefore, because with one article of faith denied, the evangelical doctrine no longer remains whole.

Prob. c. That a voluntary blaspheming is required to fill the measure of the sin against the Holy Spirit is clear from the fact that Christ expressly calls this sin the blasphemy of the Spirit, Matt. XII, 31, namely objectively; because by it the Holy Spirit is insulted. Whence also v. 32, it is expressed by λόγον κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ἁγίου, or a word against the Holy Spirit, and it is explicitly called blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, Mark III, 29. Paul calls it an insult offered to the Spirit of grace, Heb. X, 29. For sinners against the Holy Spirit τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίζουσι, they treat the Spirit of grace with contumely. The Spirit of grace is treated with contumely by those who argue that the doctrine of the Holy Spirit is false, or who attribute the miracles performed by the power of the Holy Spirit to confirm the doctrine to an unclean spirit, along with the Pharisees, Mark III. However, we do not understand here a blasphemy arising from ignorance, but one that is proæretic [deliberate], which is done by one who knows and wills. Wherefore Paul is to be excepted from this sin, who blasphemed the Son of God in ignorance, 1 Tim. I, 13. You may observe that some do not vomit blasphemies with their mouth, yet they press them in their heart, and harbor them, which are most known to God, the καρδιογνώστη [knower of hearts].

Prob. d. That an obstinate rejection of all the means of salvation is required for the complete notion of the sin against the Holy Spirit is evident from the fact that apostates consider the blood of the covenant, by which they were sanctified, to be common, Heb. X, 29. But the blood of the covenant is the blood of the Son of God, shed on the altar of the cross, by which the covenant of grace was sanctioned, and from which the sacraments, the means offering and sealing the covenant of grace, have their efficacy. Apostates consider this blood of the covenant to be common, i. e., profane, impure, and destitute of the power of sanctifying, and thus, together with the word of the Gospel, they morosely reject the sacraments, the organs and seals of the covenant, Luke VII, 30.

Latin:

Requisita formalia peccati in Spiritum S. sunt: veritatis coelestis luculenter agnitæ, in conscientia approbatæ, plane libera atque malitiosa abnegatio ; malitiose abnegatæ veritatis hostilis impugnatio ; hostiliter impugnatæ veritatis voluntaria blasphematio ; pertinax omnium mediorum salutis reiectio .

Prob. a. Requiri ad peccatum in Spiritum S. luculentum veritatis diuinae agnitionem & approbationem, liquet ex Hebr. X, 26. vbi delinquentes in Spiritum S. dicuntur voluntarie peccare, postquam acceperunt cognitionem veritatis, i. e. postquam in conscientia conuicti sunt de veritate evangelii. Idem colligitur ex Hebr. VI, 4. 5. 6. vbi de peccatoribus in Spiritum S. asseritur, quod 1) fuerint illuminati, i. e. illustrati agnitione doctrinae christianae; 2) gustauerint bonum supracaeleste, hoc est, fide salutari perceperint, quam suauis Christus fit auctor remissionis peccatorum & vitae aeternae; 3) participes facti sint Spiritus S., ceu sigilli, pignoris & arrhae aeternae salutis; 4) bonum Dei verbum gustauerint, in quantum dulcedinem evangelii cognitione experimentali & affectiua perceperunt (gustus quippe stilo biblico non leuem aut tenuem, sed vberem & cum affectu amoris ac laetitiae coniunctam perceptionem denotat); 5) gustauerint virtutes venturi seculi, praegustum efficacissimum vitae aeternae gaudiorum sentiendo ac experiendo. Graphice igitur depingitur verbis illis, memoratu dignissimis, plena pro statu viae agnitio veritatis coelestis. E quibus colligimus, Paullum persequendo veritatem diuinam, non peccasse in Spiritum S.; quoniam hoc fecit ignorans, sicut de seipso testatur, 1 Tim. I, 13.

2) Requiri ad peccatum in Spiritum S. abnegationem veritatis coelestis plane liberam, non periculorum metu extortam, patet ex Hebr. X, 26. Voluntarie peccantibus nobis post cognitionem veritatis, non amplius pro peccatis superest sacrificium. Peccatores in Spiritum S. dicuntur ἑκουσίως, i. e. libere, voluntarie, malitiose, elata manu, per contemptum maiestatis diuinae, ex mera superbia peccare. Peccant autem delinquentes in Spiritum S. τῷ παραπίπτειν, prolabendo ab illuminatione & gustu, siue experimentali cognitione doni supra-coelestis, Hebr. VI, 6. & ab accepta notitia veritatis, Hebr. X, 26. At qui prolabitur ab illuminatione & accepta cognitione veritatis, is agnitam veritatem diuinam, quam ex gratia illuminationis habet, abnegat. Colligimus ex his, Petrum abnegando Christum non peccasse in Spiritum S. ideo, quod non voluntate plane libera, sed metu pœnæ inclinata peccauit. In ecclesia primitiua, exortis persecutionibus grauissimis, haud pauci victi tormentorum vi, aut formidine periculorum compulsi, a doctrina euangelii defecerunt; qui in Filium hominis quidem, at non in Spiritum S. peccarunt.

Prob. b. Requirì ad consummationem peccati in Spiritum S. hostilem oppugnationem euangelicæ veritatis, patet ex descriptione peccantium in Spiritum S. Nam illi denuo Filium Dei crucifigunt, i. e. euangelium Christi exstinctum eunt, Hebr. VI, 4. pedibus conculcant, i. e. contumeliosissime tractant. Quibus verbis indigitatur hostilis impugnatio; qua oppugnatur vel tota doctrina fidei, vel unus alterue articulus fidei fundamentalis; cuius impugnatio etiam reliquos articulos fidei connexos labefactat, si non directe & primo, saltim oblique, secundo & per consequentiam; ideo, quod abnegato vno articulo fidei non amplius integra manet doctrina euangelica. Ceterum oppugnatio doctrinæ christianæ est vel immediata, qua quis per seipsum veritatem cœlestem vel ore, vel calamo, vel armis opprimere nititur; vel mediata, qua hostes euangelicæ veritatis alios rogant, aut iubent, aut ipsis suadent, vt eandem conuellant. Neque semper hostilis impugnatio ex effectu æstimanda est. Multis quippe desunt vires, quibus non deest voluntas veritatem opprimendi.

Prob. c. Ad mensuram peccati in Spiritum S. implendam, requiri voluntariam blasphemiationem, liquet ex eo, quod Christus expresse hoc peccatum vocat blasphemiam Spiritus, Matth. XII, 31. scilicet obiective; quia eadem Spiritus S. laceffitur. Vnde & v. 32. per λόγον κατὰ τοῦ πνεύματος ἁγίου, siue, verbum contra Spiritum S., exprimitur, & diserte blasphemia in Spiritum S. Marc. III, 29. dicitur. Paullus appellat contumeliam Spiritui gratia illatam, Hebr. X, 29. Peccatores quippe in Spiritum S. τὸ πνεῦμα τῆς χάριτος ἐνυβρίζουσι, Spiritum gratiæ contumelia afficiunt. Afficitur ab iis contumelia Spiritus gratiæ, qui doctrinam Spiritus S. falsitatis arguunt, aut miracula virtute Spiritus S. ad confirmandam doctrinam patrata, spiritui immundo cum Phariseis tribuunt, Marc. III. Non intelligitur autem hic a nobis blasphemia ex ignorantia profecta, sed proæretica, quæ fit a sciente & volente. Quare ab hoc peccato excipiendus est Paullus, qui ignorans Filium Dei blasphemauit, 1 Tim. I, 13. Obserues, quod quidam blasphemias ore non euomant, corde tamen premant, ac gerant, quæ Deo καρδιογνώστῃ sunt notissimæ.

Prob. d. Ad completam peccati in Spiritum S. rationem requiri obstinatam omnium mediorum salutis reiectionem, constat ex eo, quod apostatæ sanguinem fœderis, quo sanctificati sunt, communem esse existimant, Hebr. X, 29. Est autem sanguis fœderis sanguis Filii Dei, fusus in ara crucis, quo fœdus gratiæ sancitum est, & a quo sacramenta, gratiæ fœderalis media offerentia & obsignantia, suam efficaciam habent. Hunc sanguinem fœderis apostatæ communem, i. e. profanum, impurum, virtute sanctificandi destitutum esse ducunt, atque adeo vna cum verbo euangelii sacramenta, fœderis organa & sigilla, morose reiiciunt, Luc. VII, 30.


### Quæst. XLI. Are those essential requirements to be taken together when a judgment is to be formed concerning the sin against the Holy

He who is about to form a judgment concerning the sin against the Holy Spirit should accurately consider the συνδρομήν, or the confluence of the essential requirements, by which the measure of this most atrocious sin is filled.

Proof. The requirements reviewed above concern the formal nature of the sin against the Holy Spirit; therefore, if one is absent, the sin against the Holy Spirit has not been committed. This is shown by examples. Peter had truly and certainly known the heavenly truth about Christ, whom he nevertheless denied. But that denial of the truth, certainly acknowledged, does not complete the sin against the Holy Spirit, because Peter did not deny Christ with a full and deliberate will, but struck by the fear of death, and thus not with predetermined malice; nor did he blaspheme the same gospel, oppose it, and obstinately reject all means of salvation. Paul indeed persecuted the divine truth and its pious confessors with rage, Acts 9:1. Moreover, he blasphemed it and them, and impelled others to blaspheme, 1 Tim. 1:13, Acts 26:10, 13. Yet he did not then sin against the Holy Spirit. For he had neither a) acknowledged the divine truth about Christ, nor was he convinced of its truth and certainty: Hence, neither before his illumination could he fall away from Christ, nor deny the same. For a fall requires a term from which, and the denial of Christ demands a preceding acknowledgment and affirmation of him, at least in the conscience. b) Nor did he obstinately reject all means of salvation. For he admitted the word of Christ, and received baptism from Ananias, Acts 9:5, 18, and thus obtained mercy, 1 Tim. 1:16.

Latin:

Iudicium formaturus de peccato in Spiritum S., συνδρομήν, siue confluxum requisitorum essentialium, quibus mensura atrocissimi huius peccati impletur, accurate consideret.

Prob. Supra recensita requisita sunt de formali ratione peccati in Spiritum S., proinde absente uno, non commissum est peccatum in Spiritum S. Id quod ostenditur exemplis. Petrus vere & certo cognoverat veritatem coelestem de Christo, quem tamen abnegavit. At illa abnegatio veritatis, certo agnitae, non complet peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum, quia Petrus non voluntate plena & deliberata, sed metu mortis perculsa, adeoque non destinata malitia Christum abnegavit; neque idem evangelium blasphemavit, oppugnavit, & omnia salutis media pertinaciter repudiavit. Paullus quidem veritatem divinam, piosque eiusdem confessores rabie persecutus est, Actor. IX, 1. Quinimmo illam & hos blasphemavit, & alios ad blasphemandum impulit, 1 Tim. I, 13. Act. XXVI, 10. 13. Necdum tamen peccavit in Spiritum Sanctum. Neque enim a) veritatem divinam de Christo agnoverat, neque de illius veritate & certitudine convictus erat: Hinc neque ante fui illuminationem potuit a Christo prolabi, eundemque abnegare. Prolapsus enim requirit terminum a quo, & abnegatio Christi postulat antegressam ipsius agnitionem & affirmationem saltim in conscientia. b) Neque omnia salutis media obstinate repulit. Admisit enim verbum Christi, & accepit baptismum ab Anania, Act. IX, 5. 18. adeoque misericordiam consecutus est, 1 Tim. I, 16.


### Question XLII. Who therefore commits the sin against the Holy Spirit?

The sin against the Holy Spirit is committed not by infants, but by adults a), not by those destitute of the knowledge of the divinely revealed word, but by those who are illuminated and convinced in their conscience of the certainty of the heavenly truth b), yet who have fallen from a zeal and love for the truth into a hostile hatred of the same c).

Proof. a. 1) Actual proaeretic, or voluntary, sins do not fall upon infants; because they are destitute of the full use of reason: But the sin against the Holy Spirit is an actual voluntary sin, Heb. X, 26. Therefore. 2) Infants neither deny, nor blaspheme, nor impugn the gospel of Christ, nor do they obstinately reject it along with the sacraments, therefore they do not sin against the Holy Spirit.

Proof. b. For those who sin against the Holy Spirit are called φωτιθέντες, illuminated, Heb. 6:4, whether that illumination was pedagogical and merely literal, or spiritual, joined with the γεύσεις of heavenly things, says DANNHAV. in hodof. phanom. 11, p. 1419. The Pharisees in their infancy had been admitted into the covenant of divine grace through circumcision, and thus were truly regenerate: yet in adult age, the grace of regeneration having been shaken off through lethal crimes, and only the external knowledge of heavenly truth being retained (which truly was in them, witness Nicodemus John 3:2, witness also the disciples of the Pharisees, Matt. 22:16), they committed the sin against the Holy Spirit, of which Christ pronounced them guilty, Matt. 12:32. To this is added that Stephen so convinced his adversaries in his συζητήσει [disputation] that they could not resist the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke, Acts 6:9, 10. These worst of scoundrels had therefore arrived at a knowledge of the divine truth, which they had sufficiently heard from the mouth of Stephen, and yet they continued to resist the Holy Spirit, Acts 7:52, and were cut to the heart, gnashing their teeth, v. 54, and stoning Stephen, v. 59. Although it may be truly said of these enemies of Stephen that they defiled themselves with the crime against the Holy Spirit; yet it must be noted that not indiscriminately all and every one of their individuals committed this sin. For Paul also consented to the death of Stephen, Acts 7:58, who nevertheless was not stained by this crime. Cf.

D. FEVRBORNII differt. de peccato in Spiritum S. c. 8, p. 62. The doubt remains: Do men who have never been regenerate commit this most atrocious sin?

e.g. Pharaoh, having recognized the divine truth, spurned it. D. MEISNER affirms this in Anthropologia, decad. I, disp. X, de P. in Sp. S., p. 316. GERHARD, HUTTER, BALDUIN, HULSEMANN, DORSCHAEUS, and other theologians deny it. For the apostle describes sinners against the Holy Spirit as those who not only have been enlightened, but have also tasted the heavenly gift, have become partakers of the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, Heb. VI, 4, 5, 6.

Prob. c. The regenerate, remaining in the state of grace, commit no voluntary sin, 1 John III, 9. But if they allow themselves to be overcome by the flesh, they certainly fall from the state of regeneration, fail in the study and love of truth, and love darkness more than light, 1 John III, 19.

Latin:

Peccatum in Spiritum S. committunt non infantes, sed adulti a), non destituti cognitione verbi divinitus revelati, sed illuminati, & de veritatis coelestis certitudine in sua conscientia convicti b), ex studio tamen & amore veritatis in eiusdem hostile odium prolapsi c).

Prob. a. 1) In infantes non cadunt peccata actualia proaeretica, sive voluntaria; propterea quod pleno rationis usu destituuntur: At peccatum in Spiritum S. est peccatum actuale voluntarium, Hebr. X, 26. Ergo. 2) Infantes evangelium Christi neque abnegant, neque blasphemant, neque impugnant, neque id ipsum cum sacramentis pertinaciter reiiciunt, E. non delinquunt in Spiritum S.

Prob. b. Dicuntur enim peccatores in Spiritum S. φωτιθέντες, illuminati, Hebr. VI, 4. sive paedagogica fuerit illa illuminatio, & litterae tantum, sive spiritualis, cum γεύσεις coelestium coniuncta, inquit DANNHAV. in hodof. phanom. XI. p. 1419. Pharisaei in infantia sua per circumcisionem fuerant in foedus gratiae divinae adsciti, adeoque vere regeniti: in adulta tamen aetate, per letalia flagitia, gratia regenerationis excussa, & duntaxat externa veritatis coelestis cognitione retenta (quae vere in illis fuit, teste Nicodeino Io. III, 2. testibus etiam discipulis Pharisaeorum, Matth. XXII, 16.), commiserunt peccatum in Spiritum S. cuius eos pronunciavit Christus reos, Matth. XII, 32. Huc accedit, quod Stephanus suos aduersarios in sua συζητήσει ita convicerit, vt non potuerint resistere sapientiae & Spiritui, quo ipse loquebatur, Act. VI, 9. 10. Deuenerant ergo pessimi isti nebulones in cognitionem divinae veritatis, quam ex ore Stephani satis audierant, & tamen ii perrexerunt Spiritui S. resistere, Act. VII, 52. cordibusque fuerunt dissecti, suis dentibus stridentes, v. 54. & Stephanum lapidantes, v. 59. De his Stephani inimicis etsi vere dici queat, quod se flagitio in Spiritum S. polluerint; hoc tamen oportet moneri, quod non promiscue omnia & singula illorum individua commiserint hoc peccatum. Nam Paullus etiam consensit in necem Stephani, Act. V, 58. qui hoc tamen flagitio non fuit maculatus. Conf.

D. FEVRBORNII differt. de peccato in Spiritum S. c. VIII. p. 62. Reinanet dubium: An homines nunquam renati committant hoc atrocissimum peccatum? atrocissimum peccatum? atrocissimum peccatum?

v. gr. Pharao, agnitam veritatem divinam aspernatus. Affirmat D. MEISNERVS in anthropol. decad. I. disp. X. de P. in Sp. S. p. 316. Negant GERHARDVS, HVTTERVS, BALDVINVS, HVLSEMANNVS, DORSCHAEVS & alii theologi. Describit enim apostolus peccatores in Spiritum S. quod non tantum fuerint illuminati, sed & gustaverint donum supracaeleste, participes facti sint Spiritus S. & gustaverint bonum Dei verbum, atque virtutes venturi saeculi, Hebr. VI, 4. 5. 6.

Prob. c. Renati, in statu gratiae permanentes, nullum patrant peccatum voluntarium, Io. III, 9. At si patiantur se a carne vinci, vtique e statu regenerationis prolabuntur, a studio & amore veritatis deficiunt, & tenebras magis, quam lucem diligunt, Io. III, 19.


### Question XLIII. What are the causes moving a man to sin against the Holy Spirit?

The causes moving one to this enormous sin are: the devil, blinding the mind and filling the heart with malice a), the flesh, or the corrupt nature of man, obtaining dominion b), and the habitual malice of the will, contracted by frequent illicit acts c).

Prob. a. The devil blinds the senses of unbelievers, lest the light of the gospel shine upon them, Eph. II, 2, and fills the heart of the sinner to tell a lie, Acts V, 3. This capital enemy of the human race blinds the eyes of the mind, so that those sinning against the Holy Spirit do not perceive the most clear light of the gospel; he turns the will away from divine truth, so that they send a message to it, heap reproaches upon it, and declare war. Prob. b.

If the regenerate, by the power of the Holy Spirit, mortified the actions of the flesh, they would live continuously in the state of grace, Rom. VIII, 13. But if they obey the suggestions of the flesh, which solicit them to ambition, avarice, and the desire for earthly wisdom, it can happen that they treat the office of the Spirit with contempt and utterly reject the offered aids of grace and salvation.

Prob. c. Men do not suddenly rush into sin against the Holy Spirit, but when, like the Pharisees, they are full of hypocrisy and iniquity, Matt. XXIII, 2.

Latin:

Causæ mouentes ad enorme istud peccatum sunt: diabolus, mentem excæcans, & cor malitia implens a), caro, siue corrupta hominis natura, dominium obtinens b), habitualis voluntatis malitia, crebris actibus illicitis contracta c).

Prob. a. Diabolus excæcat sensus incredulorum, ne illuceat illis lumen euangelii, Eph. II, 2. & implet cor peccatoris ad dicendum mendacium, Act. V, 3. Hic capitalis humani generis hostis excæcat oculos mentis, ne peccantes in Spiritum S. clarissimam euangelii lucem perspiciant, auertit voluntatem a veritate diuina, vt huic nuntium mittant, probra ingerant, bellum indicant.

Prob. b. Quod si renati virtute Spiritus S. actiones carnis mortificarent, continuo viuerent in statu gratiae, Rom. VIII, 13. At si obsequantur suggestionibus carnis, qua sollicitant ad ambitionem, auaritiam, sapientiae terrestris cupiditatem, fieri potest, vt officium Spiritus susque deque habeant, & oblata gratiae salutisque subsidia penitus repudient.

Prob. c. Non subito ruunt homines in peccatum aduersus Spiritum sanctum, sed quando, instar Pharisæorum, pleni sunt hypocrisi & iniquitate, Matth. XXIII, 2.


### Question XLIV. What adjuncts accompany the sin against the Holy Spirit?

The adjuncts, on the part of the man sinning against the Holy Spirit, are: extreme hardening a), and final impenitence b). On the part of the sin against the Holy Spirit itself, its individual and inseparable companion is irremissibility c). Prob. a. Here is understood primarily doctrinal hardening, although moral hardening is joined with it. It is an act of the will, incurably evil, stubbornly rejecting the evangelical doctrine and all means of salvation.

One may see this doctrinal hardening in the Jews who overwhelmed Stephen with stones, whom that martyr of Christ gravely rebukes, Acts VII, 51: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit.

Those who morosely oppose the Holy Spirit, who is working, enlightening, and converting through the ministry of the word and sacraments, contumaciously reject the offered aids of grace. Prob. b.

Although many deliberate sins may have final impenitence as a companion, it is nevertheless separable from them, and it happens only by accident that persevering impenitence accompanies them; but the sin against the Holy Spirit by itself and by its own nature obstructs or shuts off the way to repentance, and therefore final impenitence is inseparable from it. The apostle teaches this, Heb. VI, 4, 5, 6. It is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted the heavenly gift, and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit, and have tasted the good word of God and the powers of the age to come, and have fallen away, to be renewed again to repentance, since they crucify the Son of God for themselves again and put him to an open shame.

The mind of the apostle is: Those sinning against the Holy Spirit [are in a]

they pollute themselves with a most grievous wickedness; for it, by the force of its atrocious nature, precludes a return to repentance, and renders them incapable of ordinary renewal unto contrition and faith. For those apostates, falling away from the Christian faith, reject all principles and means of grace and salvation; because, a) they crucify the author of salvation, Christ, again for themselves and expose him to mockery, while they cherish in their mind the worst intention of extinguishing Christ and faith in Christ, as if Christ were not the Son of God, not the author of our salvation, but a seducer, just as the Jews of old blasphemed the Savior hanging on the cross, and thus the doctrine concerning him becomes a mere fable or an impious fiction. But they do this to themselves, i.e., to their own destruction, so that Christ cannot profit them. b) They treat with contumely the Spirit of grace, who offers his grace and wishes to confer or seal what is offered, by denying that truth exists in his testimony. c) They repel the means of grace; because they sin willfully after having received the knowledge of the truth, Heb. X, 26, and fall away from the taste of the good word of God, Heb. VI, 5, i.e., they renounce the gospel, of which they had a sweet taste, just as they count the blood of the covenant, which is exhibited to us in the sacrament of the Supper and held out for drinking, as common, or profane and impure. But for those who petulantly reject all principles and ordinary means of salvation to their own destruction, there is no return to repentance open. For although the absolute power and extraordinary grace of the Holy Spirit can undoubtedly overcome and conquer the contumacy of those apostates: yet nowhere in Holy Scripture is that absolute and irresistible converting grace promised.

Prob. c. That irremissibility is a perpetual and inseparable adjunct of the sin against the Holy Spirit, Christ teaches in Matt. XII, 31, 32. Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men. Indeed, if anyone shall speak a word against the Son of man, it shall be forgiven him: but whoever shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this age, nor in the future. By the words of Christ, not only τὸ γινόμενον, the act of remission, is denied, but also τὸ δυνατὸν, or the power of the gift, is removed. Imagine that only the act is noted, the sense would be: all other sins will actually be forgiven; which is false. Therefore, Christ speaks of the power, that the sin against the Holy Spirit cannot be forgiven, neither in this age, nor in the future, i.e., eternally, as is explained in Mark III, 29. Furthermore, Dr. GERHARD states in disputat. isagog. p. 941, that if the sin against the Holy Spirit is considered before final impenitence, those committing this sin can, by the absolute power of God, be converted and obtain the remission of sins, although according to the ordinary mode of acting divinely instituted they cannot be converted.

Latin:

Adiuncta, ex parte hominis, in Spiritum S. peccantis, sunt: extrema induratio a), impoenitentia finalis b). Ex parte ipsius peccati in Spiritum S. indiuidua & inseparabilis comes est irremissibilitas c). Prob. a. Intelligitur heic potissimum induratio doctrinalis, quamuis induratio moralis cum ea coniuncta sit. Ea est actus voluntatis, insanabiliter malæ, doctrinam euangelicam & omnia salutis media pertinaciter reiicientis.

Hanc indurationem doctrinalem cernere licet in Iudæis, qui Stephanum lapidibus obruerunt, quos ille martyr Christi grauiter compellat, Act. VII, 51: Duræ ceruicis homines & incircumcisi corde & auribus, vos perpetuo Spiritui S. resistitis.

Qui Spiritui S. per ministerium verbi & sacramentorum operanti, illuminanti, & conuertenti, morose obsistunt, illi oblata gratiae subsidia contumaciter repudiant.

Prob. b. Quamuis plura peccata proæretica impoenitentiam finalem comiteant, ab iisdem tamen est separabilis, & ex accidenti tantum contingit, vt impoenitentia perseuerans ea comitetur; at peccatum in Spiritum S. per se & natura sua viam ad pœnitentiam obstruit aut intercludit, adeoque impoenitentia finalis ab eo est inseparabilis. Docet hoc apostolus, Hebr. VI, 4. 5. 6. Impossibile est, eos, qui semel illuminati sunt, & gustaverint donum supracaeleste, & participes facti sunt Spiritus sancti, & qui bonum gustaverint Dei verbum, virtutesque futuri saeculi, & prolapsi sunt, iterum renouari in pœnitentiam, denuo crucifigentes sibi ipsis Filium Dei & ludibrio exponentes.

Mens apostoli est: Peccantes in Spiritum S.

gravissimo se polluunt flagitio; quippe quod, vi atrocis suae naturae, reditum ad poenitentiam praecludit, eosque ordinariae renovationis ad contritionem & fidem incapaces reddit. Nam apostatae illi, a fide christiana deficientes, omnia principia & media gratiae atque salutis abiiciunt; propterea, quod a) auctorem salutis Christum denuo sibi ipsis crucifigunt & ludibrio exponunt, dum pessimam fouent animo intentionem exstinguendi Christum & fidem in Christum, quasi Christus non sit Filius Dei, non auctor salutis nostrae, sed seductor, vt olim Iudaei pendentem in cruce Saluatorem blasphemabant, atque adeo doctrina de illo mera fabula aut impium commentum fit. Sed hoc faciunt sibi ipsis, i. e. in suam ipsimet perniciem, vt Christus ipsis prodesse nequeat. b) Spirituum gratiae, qui gratiam suam offert, oblatam conferre aut obsignare vult, contumelia afficiunt, ipsius testimonio veritatem inesse negando. c) Media gratiae repellunt; quia voluntarie peccant post acceptam cognitionem veritatis, Hebr. X, 26. & a gustu boni Dei verbi prolabuntur, Hebr. VI, 5. i. e. euangelium, cuius dulcem habuerunt gustum, abnegant, iuxta atque sanguinem foederis, qui sacramento coenae nobis exhibetur, & ad bibendum porrigitur, communem, siue profanum ac impurum ducunt. At qui omnia principia & ordinaria media salutis in suammet perniciem petulanter respuunt, illis non patet reditus ad poenitentiam. Quamuis enim absoluta potentia & extraordinaria gratia Spiritus S. contumaciam illorum apostatarum haud dubie expugnare & vincere queat: nullibi tamen in S. scriptura absoluta ista & irresistibilis gratia conuertens promissa est.

Prob. c. Irremissibilitatem esse perpetuum & inseparabile peccati in Spiritum S. adiunctum, docet Christus Matth. XII, 31. 32. Omne peccatum & blasphemia remittetur hominibus. Immo si quis dixerit verbum contra Filium hominis, remittetur illi: qui vero dixerit contra Spiritum S. non remittetur illi, neque in hoc saeculo, neque in futuro. Verbis Christi non tantum τὸ γινόμενον, actus remissionis negatur, sed & τὸ δυνατὸν, siue potentia donationis remouetur. Finge, solum actum notari, sensus erit: omnia peccata reliqua actu remittentur; quod falsum. Ergo loquitur Christus de potentia, quod peccatum in Spiritum S. remitti non possit, neque in hoc saeculo, neque in futuro, i. e. in aeternum, vti explicatur Marc. III, 29. Ceterum statuit D. GERHARDVS in disputat. isagog. p. 941. quod si peccatum in Spiritum S. ante finalem impoenitentiam consideretur, per absolutam Dei potentiam committentes hoc peccatum conuerti & remissionem peccatorum consequi posse, quamuis secundum ordinarium agendi modum diuinitus institutum conuerti nequeant.


### Question XLV. Does final impenitence enter into the essential constitution of the sin against the Holy Spirit?

If by final impenitence is understood the stubborn and hardened purpose of the will to reject all means of grace, it is certainly of the essence of the sin against the Holy Spirit a): If final impenitence denotes a persevering duration, it is not an essential requirement of that most atrocious sin, but a common adjunct, and that an inseparable one b).

Prob. a. Because the sinner against the Holy Spirit opposes himself directly and with stubborn malice to the means of conversion divinely ordained, God by a most just judgment withdraws his indwelling grace from him, and delivers him over to a reprobate mind. Therefore, left to himself, he retains and hardens the deliberate purpose of blaspheming and persecuting the doctrine of the Holy Spirit. By which reasoning it is not ill asserted that final impenitence is of the formal concept of the sin against the Holy Spirit. Prob. b. 1) Christ pronounced the Pharisees, still wayfarers, guilty of blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, Matt. XII, 24. Therefore perseverance in this sin is not what is formally required of it; it is what is formally required of it, since its completion by Christ in this age is reckoned to occur before departure from that age.

2) Christ would not have spoken distributively, that the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven, neither in this age nor in the age to come, unless He had presupposed that it is, or can be, consummated even in this age before departure. 3) This sin is not to be estimated from final impenitence, which is common to other sins, but from its quiddity and formal nature, which is completed by the aforementioned requirements.

You say: The door of grace is closed to no sinner before the end of life. Resp. However much the door of grace may be open to sinners against the Holy Spirit as long as they live, according to the antecedent will of God: they themselves nevertheless maliciously cut themselves off from the gate of grace, and thus are reprobated by the consequent will of God, and fall from grace.

Latin:

Si per impoenitentiam finalem intelligitur pertinax & obfirmatum voluntatis propositum, omnia gratiae media reiiciendi, vtique ea de essentia peccati in Spiritum S. est a): Sin impoenitentia finalis durationem perseuerantem notet, non essentiale requisitum atrocissimi istius peccati, sed adiunctum commune, idque inseparabile est b).

Prob. a. Quia peccator in Spiritum S. directe, & pertinaci malitia mediis conuersionis diuinitus ordinatis se opponit, Deus iustissimo iudicio gratiam suam inhabitantem ipsi subtrahit, eundemque in sensum reprobum tradit. Proinde sibi relictus deliberatum propositum blasphemandi & persequendi doctrinam Spiritus S. retinet, & obfirmat. Qua ratione haud male asseritur, impoenitentiam finalem esse de formali conceptu peccati in Spiritum S. Prob. b. 1) Christus Pharisaeos, adhuc viatores, blasphemiae in Spiritum S. reos pronunciavit, Matth. XII, 24. Ergo permansio in hoc peccato non est eius formale requisitum, est eius formale requisitum, cum a Christo consummatum in hoc saeculo ante excessum ex illo censeatur.

2) Non fuisset Christus distributive locutus, blasphemiam Spiritus non remissum iri neque in hoc, neque in futuro saeculo, nisi praesupposuisset, etiam in hoc saeculo ante excessum illud esse, vel esse posse consummatum. 3) Non ex impoenitentia finali, quae communis est reliquis peccatis, aestimandum est hoc peccatum, sed ex quidditate & formali ratione, quae supra dictis requisitis absolvitur.

Dicis: Ianua gratiae ante finem vitae nulli peccatori est occlusa. Resp. Utcunque pateat ianua gratiae peccatoribus in Spiritum S. quamdiu vivunt, secundum voluntatem Dei antecedentem: illi ipsi tamen ad portam gratiae malitiose sibi praecidunt, adeoque voluntate Dei consequente reprobantur, & gratia excidunt.


### Question XLVI. Why is sin against the Holy Spirit unforgivable?

The sin against the Holy Spirit is irremissible not because of a defect of divine grace, nor because of a defect of the satisfaction of Christ, nor because of a defect of the efficacious operation of the Holy Spirit, but because of the malicious rejection of all means of grace, and because of final impenitence.

Prob. a. The mercy of God is universal, and thus its defect is not the cause of the irremissibility of the sin against the Holy Spirit. For the grace of God has appeared to all men, Tit. II, 11. Therefore, it has shone even upon those sinning against the Holy Spirit. Prob. b.

The satisfaction and merit of Christ is also universal. For Christ gave Himself as a ransom for all, 1 Tim. II, 6. And for those sinning against the Holy Spirit, inasmuch as they trample underfoot the Son of God, and count the blood of the covenant, by which they were sanctified, as common, Hebr. X, 29. And from which we gather: For whom the blood of Christ was shed, for them the blood of Christ was shed. But sinners against the Holy Spirit, etc. Therefore. Prob. c.

From the effects of the grace of the Holy Spirit as the applier, conspicuous in those great apostates. For they are enlightened by the Holy Spirit, Hebr. VI, 4. Prob. d.

Therefore those sinning against the Holy Spirit are worthy of punishment because they trample underfoot the Son of God, and count the blood of the covenant, by which they were sanctified, as common, and blaspheme the Spirit of grace, Hebr. X, 29. As a disease, curable in itself, becomes absolutely incurable when the patient tramples upon the medicine: so every sin is by its nature irremissible, but remissible through supernatural grace, by what they call obediential potency: but when the offered remission itself is rejected, it becomes simply ἀνίατον διὰ μοχθηρίαν, incurable through malice, and irremissible; because such contumacy cannot be overcome by free will, the power of which is here nothing, or by an ordinary means, which is rejected; an extraordinary one is owed to no man. Con. DANNHAVER. in hodof. phaenom. XI. p. 1420.

Prob. e. That sin which is followed by no repentance, God deems worthy of no pardon: for an impenitent heart treasures up wrath for itself, Rom. II, 6. Therefore. Antithesis

1) Of the Papists, asserting that the sin against the Holy Spirit is irremissible ordinarily, but not absolutely. 2) Of the Socinians, establishing that the sin against the Holy Spirit is irremissible unless earnest repentance is performed, or, unless God provides most efficacious remedies for conversion: who also deny that any voluntary sin, and thus also the blasphemy of the Spirit, has a sacrifice. Whose arguments are:

1. He who wills the death of no sinner, does not will the death of the sinner against the Holy Spirit, but wills that he be converted and live. But God, etc. Ezech. XVIII, 23. E. Resp. God, by His antecedent will, wills the death of no sinner, but that he be converted through the ordinary means of grace, and live: But when the sinner against the Holy Spirit maliciously and perseveringly repudiates the divinely ordained means of grace until the end of life, he shuts up for himself the way to repentance.

concludes. Therefore God, the most just judge, wills by a consequent and judicial will that the finally impenitent should perish eternally.

1. Objection: God can supply extraordinary and more powerful remedies for converting such a sinner. Response: Extraordinary remedies, and superabundant grace, God has neither promised nor does He owe to any mortal. One must attend not to what God can do, but to what He wills to do, with Holy Scripture shining as a light.

2. If the sin against the Holy Spirit were simply irremissible on account of final impenitence, God would not invite apostates to repentance: But He does invite them through the voice of nature, conscience, and Scripture. Therefore. Response: By inviting apostates to repentance, God clearly shows that the cause of irremissibility is not to be attributed to denied grace, but to the stubborn malice of incurable men, whom God does not entice to repentance in vain, but so that His gratuitous mercy may be acknowledged and celebrated, and the contumacious sinner may be rendered inexcusable (ἀναπολόγητος).

3. Sin against the Holy Spirit is irremissible, for the reason that for it there remains no more sacrifice, Heb. 10:26. Response: The apostle speaks of the sacrifice of Christ, insofar as it is applicable, or insofar as it can be applied through faith, so that the sense of the apostolic statement is: Those who sin willfully after having acknowledged the truth, by trampling upon Christ, by considering profane His blood shed on the altar of the cross and offered in the sacrament of the Supper, and by stubbornly blaspheming the Spirit of grace, the author of conversion, the sacrifice of Christ can no longer be apprehended by them through faith for salvation. For those enemies (ὑπεναντίοι), or enemies of grace, are not capable of repentance or faith. See Calovius, Biblia Illustrata on this passage, p. 1336.

4. Whatever sin has a price of redemption, that can be remitted: But the sin against the Holy Spirit, according to the mind of the evangelical doctors, has a price of redemption. Therefore. Response: Distinguish between the price paid and the price accepted. For two things are required for the remission of sin: 1) The price of redemption, by which remission is acquired; 2) Faith, by which the price of redemption is accepted. But the sinner against the Holy Spirit does not have faith, nor can he have it; since he opposes himself directly and with full will to the means of grace by which faith is kindled. By his own fault, he himself is impotent to accept the price of redemption.

Latin:

Peccatum in Spiritum S. est irremissibile non ob defectum gratiae divinae , neque ob defectum satisfactionis Christi , neque ob defectum efficacis operationis Spiritus S. , sed ob malitiosam omnium mediorum gratiae reiectionem , & ob finalem impoenitentiam .

Prob. a. Misericordia Dei est vniversalis, adeoque non eius defectus est caussa irremissibilitatis peccati in Spiritum S. Apparuit enim gratia Dei omnibus hominibus. Tit. II, 11. Ergo affulsit etiam peccantibus in Spiritum S. Prob. b.

Satisfactio & meritum Christi etiam vniversale est. Dedit enim Christus se in pretium redemptionis pro omnibus, 1 Tim. II, 6. Et pro peccatoribus in Spiritum S. quippe qui conculcant Filium Dei, & sanguinem foederis communem existimant, per quem sanctificati sunt, Hebr. X, 29. Et quibus colligimus: Qui per sanguinem Christi sanctificati sunt, pro illis sanguis Christi est effusus. Atqui peccatores in Spiritum S. &c. Ergo. Prob. c.

Ab effectis gratiae Spiritus S. applicatricis, conspicuis in magnis illis apostatis. Sunt enim illuminati a Spiritu sancto, Hebr. VI, 4. Prob. d.

Ideo poena digni sunt peccantes in Spiritum S. quod conculcant Filium Dei, & sanguinem foederis communem existimant, per quem sanctificati sunt, & Spiritum gratiae blasphemant, Hebr. X, 29. Vt morbus per se medicabilis, tum fit absolute immedicabilis, cum aeger medicinam conculcat: ita omne peccatum natura sua est irremissibile, per gratiam supernaturalem remissibile, potentia, ut vocant, obedientiali: sed cum oblata remissio ipsa respuitur, fit simpliciter ἀνίατον διὰ μοχθηρίαν, insanabile per malitiam, ac irremissibile; quia non potest tanta contumacia superari a libero arbitrio, cuius vis hic nulla, aut a medio ordinario, quod reiicitur; extraordinarium nulli hominum debetur. Con. DANNHAVER. in hodof. phaenom. XI. p. 1420.

Prob. e. Quod peccatum nulla sequitur poenitentia, id Deus nulla dignatur venia: nam cor impoenitens sibi ipsi thesaurizat iram, Rom. II, 6. Ergo. Antithesis

1) Pontificiorum, asserentium, peccatum in Spiritum S. esse irremissibile ordinarie, sed non absolute. 2) Socinianorum, statuentium, peccatum in Spiritum S. esse irremissibile, nisi feria poenitentia agatur, sive, nisi Deus efficacissima remedia ad convertendum suppeditet: qui etiam negant, vllum peccatum voluntarium, adeoque etiam blasphemiam Spiritus habere sacrificium. Quorum argumenta sunt.

1. Qui nullius peccatoris vult mortem, ille non vult mortem peccatoris in Spiritum S. sed vult, vt convertatur & viuat. Atqui Deus &c. Ezech. XVIII, 23. E. Resp. Deus voluntate antecedente nullius peccatoris vult peccatoris mortem, sed vt convertatur per ordinaria media gratiae, & viuat: At cum peccator in Spiritum S. divinitus ordinata media gratiae malitiose & perseveranter vsque ad finem vitae repudiet, sibi ipsi viam ad poenitentiam praecludit.

Propterea Deus iustissimus iudex vult voluntate consequente & iudiciali, vt finaliter impoenitens aeternum pereat.

1. Inslantia: Potest Deus extraordinaria & valentiora suppeditare remedia ad convertendum eiusmodi peccatorem. Resp. Extraordinaria remedia, & superabundantem gratiam Deus nec promisit, nec vlli mortalium debet. Non quid Deus possit, sed quid praelucente S. scriptura facere velit, attendendum est.

2. Si peccatum in Spiritum S. esset simpliciter irremissibile ob finalem impoenitentiam, Deus apostatas ad poenitentiam non inuitaret: Sed inuitat eos per vocem naturae, conscientiae, & scripturae. E. Resp. Deus inuitando apostatas ad poenitentiam, luculenter ostendit, caussam irremissibilitatis non esse tribuendam denegatae gratiae, sed pertinaci malitiae hominum infanabilium, quos Deus non frustra ad poenitentiam allicit, sed vt misericordia ipsius gratuita agnoscatur & celebretur, iuxta atque peccator contumax ἀναπολόγητος reddatur.

3. Peccatum in Spiritum S. est irremissibile, ideo, quod pro eodem non amplius superest sacrificium, Hebr. X, 26 . Resp. Loquitur apostolus de sacrificio Christi, quatenus est applicabile, siue quatenus per fidem applicari potest, vt sensus effati apostolici sit: Qui post agnitam veritatem peccant voluntarie, Christum conculcando, sanguinem ipsius fusum in ara crucis & in sacramento cenae oblatum profanum ducendo, & Spiritum gratiae, auctorem conuersionis, praefracte blasphemando, ab illis sacrificium Christi non amplius per fidem apprehendi potest ad salutem. Neque enim illi ὑπεναντίοι, siue hostes gratiae, sunt poenitentiae, aut fidei capaces. Vid. CALOVII bibl. illustrat. in h. l. p. 1336 .

4. Quodcunque peccatum habet pretium redemptionis, illud potest remitti: Atqui peccatum in Spiritum S. ex mente doctorum euangelicorum habet pretium redemptionis. Ergo. Resp. Dist. inter pretium persolutum, & acceptatum. Nam ad remissionem peccati requiruntur duo: 1) Pretium redemptionis, quo remissio est acquisita; 2) Fides, qua pretium redemptionis acceptatur. Atqui peccator in Spiritum S. fidem non habet, nec habere potest; quoniam mediis gratiae, quibus fides accenditur, directe & plena voluntate se opponit. E propria culpa ipse impotens est ad pretium redemptionis acceptandum.


### Question XLVII. Must one pray for the sinner against the Holy Spirit?

If anyone has certainly and evidently known that a man is sinning against the Holy Spirit, let him send no prayers to heaven for his salvation a) . But since it is difficult to pronounce concerning a man still alive that he has sinned against the Holy Spirit, it is safest to pray for apostates and blasphemers conditionally, with the hypothesis added or understood: if they can be converted, if they are curable or corrigible b) .

Proof a) St. John says gravely in 1 Ep. ch. 5:16: If anyone sees his brother sinning a sin not unto death, let him ask, and He will give him life, to those (I say) who do not sin unto death. There is a sin unto death, I do not say that he should pray for that: Observation. By the sin unto death, the apostle understands the sin against the Holy Spirit, which is distinguished by Christ Himself from other sins, Matt. 12:31. The remaining sins, whether they be venial or mortal, indeed deserve the eternal punishment of death, or are even imputed unto death in the second act; yet the punishment of death can be averted through repentance; but the sin against the Holy Spirit certainly and infallibly leads the sinner unto death on account of his stubborn rejection of the office of the Holy Spirit and his final impenitence. 2) Not without reason did the apostle premise these words: If anyone sees, by which he indicates not so much an external seeing, which occurs with bodily eyes, as the knowledge of the intellect and the judgment of discretion. But if anyone possess such perspicacity of intellect that he see that the sinner by his sins is not to summon upon himself the inevitable punishment of death, let him pray to God for his salvation. But if he clearly knows that the transgression of the sinning brother is so atrocious that he rejects all medicine, and draws upon himself the unavoidable punishment of eternal death, let him abstain from untimely prayers, and those ungrateful to God. For it would be the same as if someone were to pray that God might save a man without Christ, without the grace of the Holy Spirit, without repentance and faith, without the word and sacraments .

Prob. b. 1) St. Paul admonishes in 1 Tim. II, 1 that we should pour out prayers for all men.

2) Moses prayed for Pharaoh, Exod. IX, 33. Christ for his crucifiers, Luc. XXIII, 14. Stephen for those stoning him, Act. VII, 60. Wherefore we also pray for apostates, not insofar as they are sinners against the Holy Spirit, but insofar as they are still wayfarers, concerning whom we doubt whether all the formal requirements of the sin against the Holy Spirit apply, and according to the judgment of charity toward our neighbor, we hope for better things, 1 Cor. XIII, 5.

Q.

In a singular manner, the sin against the Son of Man is distinguished from the sin against the Holy Spirit; this is a grave sin, by which the evangelical doctrine concerning Christ, either not yet clearly acknowledged, is blasphemed and opposed, or, once acknowledged, is denied under the stimulation of the fear of dangers, without blasphemy.

Prob. from Matth. XII, 31. 32. Every sin and blasphemy shall be forgiven unto men, but the blasphemy against the Spirit shall not be forgiven unto men. Indeed, if anyone shall speak a word against the Son of Man, it shall be forgiven him: but he who shall speak against the Holy Spirit, it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, nor in the future.

Obs. 1) By the Son of Man is understood Christ, considered not by reason of the natures of which he consists, but by reason of the prophetic office, by which he himself proposed the evangelical doctrine in the days of his flesh, and even today commands it to be expounded by his ministers. Obs.

Obs. 2 A word is spoken against the Son of Man when his evangelical doctrine is either blasphemed and opposed by the ignorant, or denied, without blasphemy, by a will not entirely free, but inclined by fear, e.g., Paul blasphemed and opposed the evangelical doctrine of Christ while ignorant, 1 Tim. 1:13. Peter denied Christ, spurred by the fear of punishment, but without blasphemy and hostile opposition. Both sinned against the Son of Man .

Obs. 3 An adjunct of this sin is its remissibility; because he who sins against the Son of Man does not resist the doctrine of Christ with stubborn malice, but having fallen, he rises again, prevented and raised up by the grace of God, and admits better instruction. Although, therefore, by accident this sin is sometimes not remitted; it is not, however, impossible that it be pardoned. But the sin against the Holy Spirit is neither actually remitted, nor is it possible that it be remitted.

Q.

A solid consideration of actual sins brings much moment to the serious performance of repentance, and to the discerning of the state of grace and regeneration from the state of wrath and death.

Prob. a He who feels the diseases of his soul flees anxiously to Christ the physician: he who acknowledges his misery seeks divine mercy. David, confused by the filthiness of his sins, implored this, Ps. 51:1-4. Have mercy on me, O God, according to thy mercy! According to the multitude of thy tender mercies blot out my transgressions! Multiply, wash me from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin! For I acknowledge my transgressions, and my sin is ever before me. Against thee only have I sinned, and done evil in thy sight.

Prob. b We enjoy the tranquility of conscience when we have it ascertained that we live in a state of grace, and are beloved children of God. From this blessed state the regenerate fall, succumbing to the flesh, and contaminating themselves with proaeretic sins. These are lethal and deadly; since they are incompatible with living faith, with the grace of the Holy Spirit inhabiting our breasts, with cannot consist with peace of conscience. Wherefore let us daily examine our conscience, weighing from time to time whether we cherish in our mind a προαίρεσιν, or a purpose of sinning. Let us exterminate this, nor suffer the sin of origin to reign in our mortal body! Rom. VI, 12. For this, obtaining dominion, begets proæretic sin.

Latin:

Si quis certo & euidenter cognouerit, hominem peccare in Spiritum S. pro illius salute nullas in coelum mittat preces a) . At cum difficile sit de homine adhuc viuo pronuntiare, quod in Spiritum S. peccauerit, tutissimum est pro apostatis & blasphemia orare conditionate, addita, vel subintellecta hypothesi: si conuerti possint, si sanabiles aut corrigibiles sint b) .

Prob. a) Grauiter inquit S. IOANNES 1 ep. c. V, 16. Si quis viderit fratrem suum peccantem peccatum non ad mortem petat, tum dabit ei vitam, iis (inquam) qui non peccant ad mortem. Est peccatum ad mortem, non de illo dico, vt oret: Obs. Per peccatum ad mortem apostolus intelligit peccatum in Spiritum S. quod aliis peccatis ab ipso Christo contra distinguitur, Matth. XII, 31. Reliqua peccata, siue venialia, siue mortalia sint, aeternam quidem merentur poenam mortis, vel etiam actu secundo ad mortem imputantur; auerti tamen potest poena mortis per poenitentiam; At peccatum in Spiritum S. certo & infallibiliter peccantem ad mortem adducit ob pertinacem repulsam officii Spiritus S. & finalem impoenitentiam. 2) Haud abs re praemisit apostolus haec verba: Si quis viderit, quibus indigitat non tam externum visum, qui fit oculis corporeis, quam cognitionem intellectus & iudicium discretionis. Quod si quis ea polleat intellectus perspicacia, vt videat peccatorem suis peccatis non accersere sibi poenam mortis inevitabilem, pro eius salute Deum precetur. At si liquido sciverit, tam atrox esse fratris peccantis delictum, vt omnem respuat medicinam, & indeclinabile aeternae mortis supplicium attrahat, abstineat precibus intempestivis, Deoque ingratis. Perinde enim foret, ac si quis oraret, vt Deus hominem sine Christo, sine gratia Spiritus S., sine poenitentia & fide, sine verbo & sacramentis saluaret .

Prob. b. 1) Monet S. Paullus 1 Tim. II, 1. vt preces fundamus pro omnibus hominibus.

2) Moses orauit pro Pharaone, Exod. IX, 33. Christus pro crucifixoribus, Luc. XXIII, 14. Stephanus pro lapidatoribus, Act. VII, 60. Quare & nos precamur pro apostatis, non quatenus sunt peccatores in Spiritum S. sed quatenus adhuc sunt viatores, quibus an omnia formalia requisita peccati in Spiritum S. conueniant, dubitamus, & secundum iudicium caritatis de proximo meliora speramus, 1 Cor. XIII, 5.

Quæst. XLVIII. Quod peccatum singulari ratione peccato in Spiritum S. opponitur?

Singulari ratione peccato in Spiritum S. contra distinguitur peccatum in Filium hominis, quod est graue peccatum, quo doctrina euangelica de Christo vel nondum euidenter agnita blasphematur & oppugnatur, vel iam agnita, stimulante formidine periculorum, sine blasphemia abnegatur.

Prob. ex Matth. XII, 31. 32. Omne peccatum & blasphemia remittetur hominibus, Spiritus vero blasphemia non remittetur hominibus. Immo si quis dixerit verbum contra Filium hominis, remittetur illi: qui vero dixerit contra Spiritum S. non remittetur illi, neque in hoc saeculo, neque in futuro.

Obs. 1) Per Filium hominis intelligitur Christus, consideratus non ratione naturarum, e quibus constat, sed ratione officii prophetici, quo doctrinam euangelicam & ipse in diebus carnis proposuit, & hodienum per ministros suos exponi iubet. Obs.

Obs. 2 Contra Filium hominis verbum dicitur, quando ipsius doctrina evangelica vel ab ignorantibus blasphematur & oppugnatur, vel abnegatur, sine blasphemia, voluntate non plane libera, sed metu inclinata, v. gr. Paullus blasphemavit & oppugnavit doctrinam Christi evangelicam ignorans, 1 Tim. I, 13. Petrus Christum abnegavit stimulante metu poenae, sed sine blasphemia & hostili impugnatione. Uterque peccavit in filium hominis .

Obs. 3 Peccati huius adiunctum est remissibilitas; quia peccans in Filium hominis pertinaci malitia doctrinae Christi non obnititur, sed lapsus resurgit, gratia Dei praeuentus & erectus, melioremque admittit informationem. Quamuis igitur ex accidenti interdum peccatum hoc non remittatur; non tamen impossibile est, quin condonetur. At vero peccatum in Spiritum S. neque actu remittitur, neque possibile est, vt remittatur.

Quaest. XLIX Quos colliges fructus e solida peccatorum actualium consideratione?

Solida peccatorum actualium consideratio plurimum momenti affert ad seriam agendam poenitentiam , ad dignoscendum statum gratiae atque regenerationis a statu irae & mortis .

Prob. a Qui animae suae morbos sentit, confugit anxius ad medicum Christum: qui agnoscit miseriam, diuinam quaerit misericordiam. Hanc, peccatorum suorum foeditate confusus, Dauid implorauit, Ps. LI, 1. 2. 3. 4. Miserere mei, Deus, iuxta misericordiam tuam! Iuxta multitudinem miserationum tuarum dele praeuaricationes meas! Multiplica, laua me ab iniquitate mea, & a peccato meo munda me! Nam praeuaricationes meas ego agnosco, & peccatum meum coram me est iugiter. Tibi soli peccaui, & malum in oculis tuis feci.

Prob. b Tranquillitate conscientiae perfruimur, cum exploratum habemus, nos viuere in statu gratiae, & esse dilectos Dei filios. Ex hoc beato statu excidunt renati, carni succumbentes, & peccatis proaereticis se contaminantes. Haec letalia & mortifera sunt; quippe quae cum viua fide, cum gratia Spiritus S., pectora nostra inhabitante, cum tranquillitate conscientiæ consistere nequeunt. Quare quotidie conscientiam nostram excutiamus subinde pensitantes, an προαίρεσιν, siue propositum peccandi animo foueamus. Exterminemus hoc, neque patiamur, peccatum originis regnare in mortali nostro corpore! Rom. VI, 12. Hoc enim, dominium obtinens, parit peccatum proæreticum.


### Q. L. How are those to be treated who are touched by no care for their sins?

For the conversion of those secure men, one must pray assiduously a); a sleeping conscience must be awakened by serious exhortations taken from the divine word b); temporal calamities, the companions of sins, must be placed before their eyes c); they must be warned that the course of this life is short, but the everlasting torments, by which the finally impenitent will be tortured, are eternal d).

Proof a. He who is about to put effort into converting secure sinners should obtain the success of such a great work from God by pious prayers. Thus Samuel prayed for the salvation of Saul, 1 Sam. XV, 35. Paul for the Ephesians, Eph. I, 16. And that we may do the same, he seriously admonished, 1 Tim. II, 1. 2.

Proof b. About to awaken a sleeping conscience, Sirach says: Flee from sin, as from the face of a serpent: for if you approach, it will bite you. The teeth of a lion are its teeth, taking away the souls of men. As a two-edged sword is all iniquity: there is no healing of its wounds, c. XXI, 2. 3.

Proof c. Sin is an evil root, the fruits of which are calamities of every kind, Deut. XXVIII, 16.

Proof d. The life of the sinner is short, but the punishments of sin are eternal. Wherefore let the sinner repent in time, lest he perish eternally.

Latin:

Pro securorum illorum hominum conuersione assidue orandum est a); conscientia dormiens seriis adhortationibus e verbo diuino sumtis excitanda b); calamitates temporales, peccatorum comites, ob oculos ipsis ponendæ c); monendi sunt, exiguum huius vitæ esse curriculum, perennes autem cruciatus, quibus finaliter impœnitentes torquebuntur d).

Prob. a. Positurus operam in conuertendis securis peccatoribus, tanti operis succefsum a Deo precibus piis impetret. Sic orauit Samuel pro salute Saulis, 1 Sam. XV, 35. Paullus pro Ephesiis, Eph. I, 16. Et vt nos idem faciamus, serio monuit, 1 Tim. II, 1. 2.

Prob. b. Conscientiam dormientem exsuscitaturus Siracides inquit: Fuge a peccato, sicut a facie serpentis: si enim accesseris, mordebit te. Dentes leonis sunt dentes eius, tollentes animam hominum. Sicut romphæa anceps est omnis iniquitas: plagæ eius non est sanatio, c. XXI, 2. 3.

Prob. c. Peccatum est mala radix, cuius fructus sunt omnigenæ calamitates, Deut. XXVIII, 16.

Prob. d. Vita peccatoris breuis, sed pœnæ peccati æternæ sunt. Quare peccator mature resipiscat, ne æternum pereat.


### Q. LI. How are sinners who have fallen gravely, and are near to despair, to be raised up?

There must be inculcated to afflicted sinners and those struggling with despair, the mercy of God the Father, kindly looking upon and receiving contrite sinners a), the universal merit of Christ b), the help of the Holy Spirit c).

Proof a. God the Father invites the greatest sinners to repentance, and does not reject those who repent, but receives them most kindly. Return, O backsliding Israel, says Jehovah! For I will not cause my angry faces to fall upon you: for I am merciful, says Jehovah, I will not hold anger forever. Only acknowledge your iniquity, that you have transgressed against Jehovah your God! Jer. III, 12. 13.

Proof b. Most sweet are the words of St. John 1 epist. c. II, 1. 2. My little children, these things I write to you, that you may not sin. But if anyone has sinned, we have an advocate with the Father, Christ the righteous. And he is the propitiation for our sins: indeed not for ours only, but also for the sins of the whole world.

Proof c. The sinner not completely succumbing to despair, but struggling with it, is not abandoned by the help of the present Holy Spirit. For He helps our infirmities. For what we ought to pray for, as is fitting, we do not know, but the Spirit Himself intercedes for us with groanings which cannot be uttered, Rom. VIII, 26.

SIGH.

…I have sinned, O most just God, I have sinned before your face most often and most gravely. Woe to my life, if you examine it according to the rigor of your law! Nothing tortures my soul so much as that I have so often offended you, my most bountiful benefactor, supreme legislator, omniscient judge! Turn away, I beseech you, your wrath and the punishment due to my sins, and turn your fatherly affection back toward me, unworthy as I am! Look kindly upon the λύτρον of the blood shed for me on the altar of the cross by your most beloved Son, Jesus Christ, and on account of this price of redemption, erase my great debts from the book of your accounts! For the rest, I desire your most holy Spirit as the guide of my life! May He preserve me from the poison of sin: may He fortify me against falling; may He lead and strengthen me, so that I may run the unoffended path of sincere piety!

Latin:

Inculcanda est peccatoribus afflictis & cum desperatione conflictantibus, misericordia Dei Patris, peccatores contritos benigne respiciens & recipiens a), meritum Christi vniuersale b), auxilium Spiritus S. c).

Prob. a. Deus Pater peccatores maximos inuitat ad resipiscentiam, resipiscentes non reiicit, sed perbenigne recipit. Reuertere auersa Israël, dictum Iehouæ! Non enim faciam cadere facies meas iratas super te: quoniam misericors ego sum, dictum Iehouæ, non tenebo iram in æternum. Tantummodo agnosce iniquitatem tuam, quod contra Iehouam Deum tuum præuaricata sis! Ier. III, 12. 13.

Prob. b. Perquam dulcia sunt verba S. Ioannis 1 epist. c. II, 1. 2. Filioli mei, hæc scribo vobis, vt non peccetis. Quod si quis peccauerit, paracletum habemus apud patrem Christum iustum. Et ille est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris: immo non pro nostris tantum, sed etiam pro totius mundi peccatis.

Prob. c. Peccator non penitus succumbens desperationi, sed cum ea luctans, non destituitur ope præsentis Spiritus S. Hic enim coadiuuat infirmitates nostras. Nam quid precari debeamus, sicut decet, non scimus, sed ipse Spiritus insuper intercedit pro nobis gemitibus, qui dici nequeunt, Rom. VIII, 26.

SVSPIRIVM.

Peccaui, o Deus iustissime, peccaui coram facie tua sæpissime & grauissime. Væ vitæ meæ, si secundum rigorem legis tuæ eandem discusseris! Nihil peræque animum meum excruciat, quam quod toties offenderim te, benefactorem meum largissimum, legislatorem summum, iudicem omniscium! Auerte, obsecro, iram pœnamque peccatis meis debitam, paternum vero affectum ad me indignum iterum conuerte! Benigne respice λύτρον sanguinis, a Filio tuo dilectissimo, Iesu Christo, pro me in ara crucis effusi, & propter hoc pretium redemtionis grandia mea debita e libro rationum tuarum expunge! De cetero rectorem vitæ meæ exopto Spiritum tuum sanctissimum! Hic præseruet me a veneno peccati: præmuniat me a lapsu; ducat & corroboret me, vt inoffensum sinceræ pietatis tramitem decurram!


## 15 On the Defect of Free Will in Spiritual Matters


### Ques. I. What do you understand by the defect of free will in spiritual matters?

The defect of free will in spiritual matters is the common inability of unregenerate men, arising from original sin, to know and choose spiritual good in a saving way, and thus to fulfill the divine law and to conceive a saving faith in Christ.

Obs. Spiritual good is the triune God, and divine things, which are saving to sinful man, and knowable from the light of supernatural revelation.

Latin:

Defectus liberi arbitrii in spiritualibus est communis ex originali peccato orta impotentia hominum irregenitorum, ad salutariter cognoscendum & eligendum bonum spirituale, atque adeo ad legem diuinam implendam & saluificam in Christum fidem concipiendam.

Obs. Bonum spirituale est Deus triunus, & res diuinæ, homini peccatori salutares, e lumine supernaturalis reuelationis cognoscibiles.


### Ques. II. What is free will?

Free will is the active faculty of the will, by which it, regarding an actionable object, with all things required for acting being posited, holds itself indifferently, both as to the species and as to the exercise of the act.

Obs. I. Arbitrium (will/judgment) is said from arbitrando (judging). But to judge is taken either in the common sense, and signifies to judge, to pass judgment or sentence, and thus it is referred to the intellect; or in the forensic sense, and it is the same as seriously to will and decree something; in which sense it is referred to the will.

Obs. II. The word, liberty, sustains various meanings: a) it denotes exemption from the obligation of law. Thus God alone is absolutely without law, although He is a law unto Himself: a king is released from the laws which he himself makes, unless he submits himself to them of his own accord. b) Liberty from coercion, which is immunity from external violence, brought upon a suffering subject against his own inclination, is otherwise called spontaneity, and is common to man with the brutes. c) Liberty from internal necessity, which is proper to agents endowed with intellect and will, God, angels, and men (*). By this very thing man is distinguished from creatures devoid of reason, which are necessaand by the instinct of nature act uniformly, e.g., the Sun necessarily shines, fire warms, a hungry wolf devours the lamb, of which it becomes the master. Liberty is distinguished from necessity into liberty of contrariety and of contradiction. Liberty of contrariety is that which is concerned either with diverse objects or with diverse acts of one object, e.g., it was free for Jacob to take Leah as a wife, or Rachel: it was free for him to speak with Rachel, to walk, to play. It is also called liberty of specification, since through it man is immune from determination to a species of act or object. Liberty of contradiction is that which is concerned with one and the same object between contradictory terms, to will and not to will, to act and not to act, e.g., it is free for a student of philosophy to love philosophy and not to love it, to practice it and not to practice it. It is also called liberty of exercise; because after the will has determined itself to one or the other part of the contradiction, it nevertheless remains free in the exercise.

4) It notes liberty from the guilt, dominion, sense, and root of sin. Liberty from the guilt of sin is that by which sins are not imputed to a repentant man for guilt and punishment: this, converted sinners obtain through the grace of justification. Liberty from the dominion of sin is when the flesh is subject to the spirit and the servitude of sin is dissolved: this, the justified obtain by the benefit of renewal. Liberty from the sense and root of sin is that by which, in renewed men, the stimulus and fuel of sin is removed through the dissolution of soul and body.

5) It designates liberty from misery, by which the blessed, triumphing in heaven, are completely freed not only from the sense and root of sin, but also from the chastisements following sin. For they are not subject to diseases, death, or any calamity.

Obs. III. Man's liberty is divided into liberty of nature, of grace, and of glory. Liberty of nature is immunity from internal coercion and necessity, with respect to natural and civil things subject to reason. To this point the words of Paul, 1 Cor. VII, 37, refer: He who stands firm in his heart, and has no necessity, but has power over his own will, and has determined this in his heart, that he wishes to keep his virgin, does well. Liberty of grace is that through which the reborn are freed from the guilt and dominion of sin, of which the apostle says, Rom. VI, 18: Freed from sin, you have been made servants of righteousness. Liberty of glory is immunity from the sense and root of sin and from all misery; of which mention is made, Rom. VIII, 21: The creature itself shall be delivered from the servitude of corruption into the liberty of the glory of the children of God.

Obs. IV. Necessity and servitude are opposed to liberty. For 1) absolute necessity and necessity of the consequent, by which something cannot be otherwise on account of the indissoluble connection of cause with effect, is repugnant to liberty: just as water necessarily moistens. However, hypothetical necessity and necessity of the consequence, by which something cannot be otherwise on account of the act of existing or an extrinsic condition, can stand with liberty. Thus it is necessary for a man to be learned if he strives to act as a professor of philosophy. 2) Liberty fights with the external necessity of coercion, which is the determination of nature to one thing, beyond or against its will, done by an external violent principle. Authors are accustomed to distinguish between acts of the will that are elicited and those that are commanded. The will, as regards elicited acts, cannot be forced. Now, elicited acts are those which are exercised immediately by the will, e.g., to will, to love, to choose. To these are opposed commanded acts, which [are] coming.

Evil: if someone, with darkened intellect, having followed a false and rash reason, cannot but will so evilly, just as he falsely and imprudently opines and judges. This is contrary to liberty; that is not, but is closely coupled with true liberty, which indeed differs much from vague lust and untamed license; just as in God there is indeed the highest moral necessity of never deciding and acting except well, nay, optimally; yet nevertheless, there is the highest liberty, circumscribed by no limits, to be restrained by no impediments ever. See the note to page 435.

which are indeed performed by the command of the will, but by means of another faculty, e.g., to speak, to walk, to write. Therefore, a man cannot be compelled to the elicited acts of the will, because compulsion comes from an external principle, but volition from an internal principle. Wherefore, to will something under compulsion introduces a contradiction in the subject. A man can be compelled to commanded acts, but then he does not act according to free will, but beside or against his will. Thus, a man can be carried off somewhere by force, but that this carried-off state should be violent from the will of him who is carried off, cannot happen. For if it is voluntary, it ceases to be violent. 3) The internal necessity of immutability is repugnant to liberty, which is the determination of the acting subject to one thing, proceeding from an internal principle, behaving immutably toward the effect. But whatever is determined to one thing is not free. Thus, an action is called free which proceeds from the agent in such a way that it was in the power of the agent to act and not to act, to do this and to do that. However, the necessity of obligation can consist with liberty, which is the directive determination of the will to embrace the good and to flee the evil, according to the norm of a superior's command. Thus, angels and men are determined to the norm of divine law, subject to the laws of a prince, who nevertheless possess free will. For moral or legal determination does not captivate the liberty of the will, nor does it necessitate irresistibly. Indeed, divine law determines intelligent creatures by persuading and commanding those things which are according to the will of the Deity, and by prohibiting and dissuading those which are against it; yet ordinarily without compelling and as it were inflicting force. Nothing indeed happens against the absolute and most powerful will of the Deity, yet many things, and many more, happen beside, rather than according to, the nod of the Deity, says DANNHAV. in hodof. phænom. III. p. 312.

4) Ugly and disgraceful servitude is repugnant to liberty, not decorous and honorable servitude. Honorable servitude consists both in the duty of living piously and in the ministry rendered to God. Thus regenerated men are called servants of justice, Rom. VI, 18, because according to the prescription of the divine law they willingly cultivate justice. The same are said to serve God, Rom. VI, 22, because they consecrate themselves wholly to divine worship. On the contrary, disgraceful servitude is the captivity of the will, by which through sin the will of man is so bound and captivated that it serves only sin, Io. VIII, 34. This servitude is opposed to liberty from the necessity of immutability.

Latin:

Liberum arbitrium est facultas actiua voluntatis, qua illa circa obiectum agibile, positis omnibus ad agendum requisitis, indifferenter se habet, tum quoad speciem, tum quoad exercitium actus.

Obs. I. Arbitrium dicitur ab arbitrando. Arbitrari autem sumitur vel sensu vulgari, & significat iudicare, iudicium vel sententiam ferre, atque sic refertur ad intellectum; vel sensu forensi, & idem est, quod serio aliquid velle & decernere; quo sensu refertur ad voluntatem.

Obs. II. Vox, libertas, varias sustinet significationes: a) notat exemtionem ab obligatione legis. Sic solus Deus absolute exlex est, quaiuis sibi ipsi lex sit: rex iis, quas fert ipse, legibus solutus est, nisi sponte sua iisdem se submittat. b) Libertatem a coactione, quæ est immunitas a violentia externa, subiecto patienti contra ipsius inclinationem illata, vocatur alias spontaneitas, & est homini cum brutis communis. c) Libertatem a necessitate interna, quæ agentium, intellectu & voluntate præditorum, Dei, angelorum & hominum, propria est (*). Hac ipsa distinguitur homo a creaturis, rationis expertibus, quæ necessainstinctu naturae vniformiter agunt, v. gr. Sol necessario lucet, ignis calefacit, lupus famelicus agnum, cuius compos redditur, deuorat. Distinguitur libertas a necessitate, in libertatem contrarietatis, & contradictionis. Libertas contrarietatis est, quae versatur vel circa diuersa obiecta, vel circa vnius obiecti diuersos actus, v. gr. Iacobo liberum erat ducere vxorem Leam, vel Rachelem: liberum ipsi erat, cum Rachele loqui, ambulare, lusitare. Vocatur etiam libertas specificationis, quoniam per eam homo immunis est a determinatione ad speciem actus, vel obiecti.
