They are regenerated, therefore, and gifted with faith, as many as do not reject or neglect, but admit, the τάξιν [order], or the order divinely prescribed. Prob. c. 1) Whoever are born flesh of flesh, and yet can enter the kingdom of heaven; it behooves them to be regenerated: But infants, etc.

Therefore. The major is clear from John III, 5, 6; Rom. VIII, 6, 7, 8. The minor is evident from Luke XVIII, 16; Matt. XVIII, 10, compared with Heb. I, 14. 2) Whoever believe are regenerated, John I, 12.

Infants believe, Matt. XVIII, 6; Mark IX, 42. Therefore. 3) Infants escape eternal damnation, Matt. XVIII, 14. Therefore, they are not incapable of regeneration, through which they become children of God, John I, 12, 13. But the children of God escape eternal damnation, since they are heirs of God and joint-heirs with Christ, Rom.

VIII, 17. Prob. d. In adults, eyes are opened through instruction, that they may be converted from darkness to the light of faith, and from the power of Satan to God, and thus be truly regenerated, Acts XXVI, 18. God crushes the stony hearts of these through the law, so that contrition may be a disposition for kindling faith in them.

Whence our D. Chemnitius says gravely, loc. theol. P. II, p. 1: Unless the stony heart has first been subdued and crushed by the hammer of the law, Jer.

XIII, 19, it is not capable of evangelical doctrine, but new wine is poured into old skins, Matt. IX, 17. The antithesis is that of the Anabaptists and Socinians, who deny that infants are capable of regeneration. Their stronger arguments are:

I. In whom the corruption of life does not fall, in them regeneration does not fall: But it does not fall in infants, etc. Therefore. The major is certain: because regeneration is the reformation of a corrupt life. Resp. 1) The reformation of a corrupt life is not regeneration, but renewal.

Conf. D. Scherz. in colleg. Anti-Socinian. Disp. LXXVI, p. 670. 2) Distinguish between the corruption of life that is original and that which is actual and proaretic. While the latter does not fall upon infants, the former does. For whatever is born of the flesh is corrupt flesh; consequently, it is regenerable by the Spirit, John III, 5, 6.

II. Infants are not capable of faith: because they do not use reason, not knowing what is right or left, Jonah IV, 11. Therefore, they are not capable of regeneration. Resp. 1) Many adults who are phrenetic, dying, and buried in sleep do not use reason, and yet they have faith.

Faith does not depend on the use of reason, but reason must be taken captive under the obedience of faith, 2 Cor. X, 5; nay, rather, raging reason often hinders the generation of faith. 2) Infants have faith, not reflexive or discursive, but direct and simple, kindled by the Holy Spirit, to whom they do not maliciously resist, through baptism.

III. For the kindling of faith, the hearing of the divine word is required, Rom. X, 17, which infants, by reason of their age, can neither hear nor understand.

For the kindling of faith, the word of the Gospel and baptism are required: which means of grace are not opposed, but consonant. In adults, faith is kindled through the hearing of the word; in infants, through the use of baptism.

Quaest. VII. Whether the intellect or the will of the sinner is regenerated? Through regenerating grace, there is in the intellect of the adult sinner a more intense and fuller light of the true knowledge of God, and indeed so much as is [required] for justifying faith in the soul is required to be conceived in the mind, is kindled a).

In the will of the same, illuminated through the Gospel, trust in Christ is excited b). Objection In the present case, we are primarily concerned with the regenerating of the intellect and will of adult sinners: the regeneration of infants is somewhat more difficult to understand. Yet, that the intellect of infants in regeneration through baptism is imbued by the Holy Spirit with the saving knowledge of God, and their will is gifted with trust in Christ, we do not doubt.

We acquiesce here in the judgment of D. Chemnitz in Exam. Conc. Trid. f. 246. Although we neither sufficiently understand, nor can explain in words, what kind of action and operation of the Holy Spirit that is in infants who are baptized: that it is and comes to pass from the Word of God, is certain.

That action, or operation of the Holy Spirit in little ones, we call faith, and we say that little ones believe. For that medium, or organ, by which the kingdom of God, which is offered in the Word and Sacraments, is received, Scripture calls faith: and says that those who believe receive the kingdom of God.

And indeed, Mark X, 15, Christ affirms that adults receive the kingdom of God in the same way that little ones receive it.

And Matthew XVIII, 6, He says: Whoever shall cause one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble. And among these little ones, He also counts a παιδίου, a little child.

Furthermore, circumcision in general is called a seal of the righteousness of faith, Rom. IV, 11. But if the righteousness of faith is attributed to circumcised infants, then faith itself is also attributed to them.

Prob. a. Although the intellect of an adult sinner, before the act of conversion and regeneration, pertains to a pedagogical and imperfect illumination regarding the literal knowledge of things to be believed: yet in conversion, through the Law, the knowledge of sin—practically applied to the detestation of sin—is kindled, and in regeneration, a fuller knowledge of Christ is kindled, so that it may manifest itself more clearly, diffuse itself more abundantly into the will, and instruct and direct this will firmly toward the trustful embrace of the Mediator.

To this seem to point the words of the Apostle, Eph. V, 14. Therefore he says: Awake, you who sleep, and arise from the dead, that Christ may shine upon you.

As soon as the lethargy of security is shaken off from the sinner through conversion by the Law, and he is raised from spiritual death through regeneration, Christ, the light of the world, fills his intellect with a distinct knowledge of Himself, so that through it he may be constituted spiritually alive.

Prob. b. Through regeneration, trust in Christ is excited in the will of the contrite sinner, so that he may approach this throne of grace μετὰ παρῥησίας, with confidence, receive mercy, and find grace for timely help, Hebr.

IV, 16. Quest. VIII. Did regeneration also take place in the O. T.? The faithful of the Old Testament were truly reborn.

Prob. 1 Faith and salvation took place in the O.

T. Therefore, also regeneration. The antecedent is clear from the statement of the Apostle James, Acts XV, 11.

By the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ we believe that we are saved, even as they . 2 In the O. T., God was the Father of the faithful, Deut.

XXXII, 6, and they were His children, Is. I, 2, Jer. XXXI, 20. Therefore, the faithful of the O.

T. were reborn. The antithesis is that of the Socinians, who deny that regeneration took place in the O.

T., whose chief argument is: We have been reborn through the resurrection of Christ, 1 Pet. I, 3. Therefore, before the resurrection of Christ, no one was reborn.

Resp. We have been reborn through the resurrection of Christ as the meritorious cause, or rather of the merit, which operates backward and forward, and as the sealing cause.

The Fathers in the O.

T. believed in Christ who was to be incarnate, to die, and to be raised from the dead.

Latin:

Regenerantur homines vita spirituali carentes a), sed pertinaciter non repugnantes b), tam infantes c), quam adulti e verbo Dei informati, legisque divinae fulmine perculsi & contriti d).

Prob. a. Homines viventes in fide, quae est in Filium Dei, prout describuntur renati a Paullo, Gal. II, 20., non sunt proprie loquendo subiectum regenerationis. Sicut enim e morte temporali ad vitam gloriae resuscitantur non viventes, sed mortui: ita e morte spirituali ad vitam gratiae non resuscitantur renati, sed vita fidei carentes.

Prob. b. Gratia praeveniens & praeparans repugnantiam naturalem quidem imminuit & infringit, ne gratiam regenerantem impediat; at peccator mediis gratiae voluntaria & pertinaci resistentia se opponens, non est subiectum capax regenerationis per verbum ἄκυσον καὶ ὀρατόν, i.e. per evangelium & baptismum. Affertum hoc nostrum claret exemplis. Pharisaei & legisperiti voluntatem Dei reiecerunt contra seipsos, ideoque non sunt baptizati a Ioanne, Luc. VII, 30. Paullus & Barnabas dixerunt Iudaeis: Vobis erat necesse primo dici verbum Dei: quoniam vero repellitis illud, & non dignos iudicatis vos ipsos vita aeterna; ecce, vertimus nos ad ipsos vita æterna; ecce, vertimus nos ad gentes. Ita namque mandauit nobis Dominus: Posui te lumen gentium, vt sis tu in salutem vsque ad extremum terrae. Cum ergo audirent gentiles, gauisi sunt & glorificarunt verbum Domini, quotquot erant ordinati in vitam aeternam, Act.

XIII, 46. 47. 48. Ex his liquido patet, quod neque per baptismum irregenerentur, qui consilium Dei de communicanda aeterna salute per ordinaria media aduersus seipsos, h. e. maximo suo damno, reiiciunt, neque per euangelium ad fidem perducantur, qui illud malitiose repellunt.

Regenerantur ergo & fide donantur, quotquot τάξιν, vel ordinem diuinitus praescriptum in reprobant, aut negligunt, sed admittunt. Prob. c. 1) Quicunque sunt caro de carne nati, & tamen regnum coelorum ingredi possunt; illos oportet regenerari: Atqui infantes &c.

Ergo. Maior liquet ex Io. III, 5. 6. Rom. VIII, 6. 7. 8. Minor patet e Luc. XVIII, 16. Matth. XVIII, 10. collat. Hebr. I, 14. 2) Quicunque credunt, sunt regeniti, Io. I, 12.

Infantes credunt, Matth. XVIII, 6. Marc. IX, 42. Ergo. 3) Infantes aeternam damnationem effugiunt, Matth. XVIII, 14. E. non sunt incapaces regenerationis, per quam fiunt filii Dei, Io. I, 12. 13. Filii Dei autem effugiunt aeternam damnationem, cum sint haeredes Dei, & cohaeredes Christi, Rom.

VIII, 17. Prob. d. Adultis per informationem aperiuntur oculi, vt conuertantur a tenebris ad lucem fidei, & de potestate Satanae ad Deum, adeoque vere regenerentur, Act. XXVI, 18. Horum corda lapidea Deus per legem conterit, vt contritio sit dispositio ad accendendam in illis fidem.

Vnde grauiter inquit noster D. Chemnitius loc. theol. P. II. p. 1. Nisi cor lapideum malleo legis prius subactum & contusum fuerit, Ier.

XIII, 19. non est capax doctrinae euangelicae, sed vinum nouum in uteres veteres infunditur, Matth. IX, 17. Antithesis est Anabaptistarum & Socinianorum, negantium, infantes esse capaces regenerationis. Quorum potiora sunt argumenta: I.

In quos non cadit vitae corruptio, in illos non cadit regeneratio: Atqui in infantes non cadit &c. E. Maior constat: quia regeneratio est vitae corruptae reformatio. Resp. 1) Vitae corruptae reformatio non est regeneratio, sed renouatio.

Conf. D. Scherz. in colleg. Anti-Socinian. Disp. LXXVI. p. 670. 2) Dist. inter corruptionem vitae originalem, & actualem proareticam. Non quidem haec, illa tamen cadit in infantes. Quidquid enim ex carne natum est, caro corrupta, consequenter ex Spiritu regenerabile est, Io.

III, 5. 6. II. Infantes non sunt capaces fidei: quia non vntuntur ratione, nescientes, quid dextrum aut sinistrum sit, Ion. IV, 11. E. non sunt capaces regenerationis. Resp. 1) Multi adulti phrenetici, agonizantes, & somno sepulti, non vtuntur ratione, & tamen fidem habent.

Non pendet fides ab vsu rationis, sed ratio captiuanda est sub obsequium fidei, 2 Cor. X, 5. quin immo ratio ferociens saepe generationem fidei impedit. 2) Habent infantes fidem non reflexam aut discursiuam, sed directam & simplicem, a Spiritu S., cui malitiose non resistunt, per baptismum accensam.

III. Ad accensionem fidei requiritur auditus verbi diuini, Rom. X, 17. quod infantes per aetatem nec audire, nec intelligere possunt.

Ad accensionem fidei requiritur verbum euangelii & baptismus: quae media gratiae non sunt opposita, sed consentanea. In adultis accenditur fides per auditum verbi, in infantibus per vsum baptismi.

Quaest. VII. Vtrum intellectus, an voluntas peccatoris regeneretur? Per gratiam regenerantem in intellectu peccatoris adulti intensior & plenior verae cognitionis Dei lux, & quidem tanta, quanta ad fidem iustificantem in animo concipiendam requiritur, accenditur a).

In voluntate eiusdem illuminata per evangelium fiducia in Christum excitatur b). Obiectio In praesenti nobis potissimum sermo est de regenerando intellectu et voluntate peccatorum adultorum: infantum regeneratio intellectu aliquanto difficilior est. Quin tamen intellectus infantum in regeneratione per baptismum a Spiritu S. imbuatur notitia Dei salutari, et voluntas eorum donetur fiducia in Christum, nulli dubitamus.

Acquiescimus hic in iudicio D. Chemnitii in exam. Conc. Trid. f. 246. Licet nec satis intelligamus, nec verbis explicare possimus, qualis fit illa Spiritus S. actio et operatio in infantibus, qui baptizantur: esse tamen et fieri ex verbo Dei, certum est.

Illam autem actionem, seu operationem Spiritus S. in infantulis vocamus fidem, et dicimus, paruulos credere. Illud enim medium, seu organon, quo regnum Dei, quod in verbo et sacramentis offertur, accipitur, scriptura vocat fidem: et credentes dicit accipere regnum Dei.

Et quidem Marc. X, 15. Christus affirmat, adultos ita accipere regnum Dei, sicut paruuli illud accipiunt.

Et Matth. XVIII, 6. inquit: Qui scandalizauerit vnum ex pusillis istis, qui in me credunt. Et inter pusillos istos etiam παιδίου, puerulum numerat.

Praeterea circumcisio in genere vocatur signaculum iustitiae fidei, Rom. IV, 11. Quod si infantibus circumcisis tribuitur iustitia fidei, etiam ipsa fides illis tribuitur.

Prob. a. Quamuis intellectus peccatoris adulti, ante actum conversionis et regenerationis, paedagogica et imperfecta illuminatione ad litteralem credendorum notitiam pertineat: in conversione tamen per legem notitia peccati, practice ad detestandum peccatum applicata, et in regeneratione notitia Christi plenior accenditur, vt clarius se exserat, vberius in voluntatem se diffundat, atque hanc ad fiducialem mediatoris amplexum solidus instruat atque dirigat.

Quo spectare videntur verba Apostoli, Eph. V, 14. Propterea dicit: expergiscere, qui dormis, et surge ex mortuis, vt illucescat tibi Christus.

Simul atque per conversionem ex lege peccatori veternus securitatis excutitur, et is per regenerationem a morte spirituali resuscitatur, Christus lumen mundi intellectum eius distincta sui cognitione implet, vt per eam spiritualiter viuus constituatur.

Prob. b. Per regenerationem in voluntate peccatoris contriti excitatur fiducia in Christum, vt ad hunc thronum gratiae μετὰ παρῥησίας, cum confidentia, accedat, misericordiam accipiat, et ad opportunum auxilium gratiam inueniat, Hebr.

IV, 16. Quaest. VIII. An regeneratio etiam in V. T. locum obtinuit? Fideles veteris testamenti vere renati fuerunt.

Prob. 1 Fides et salus in V. T. locum obtinuit. E., et regeneratio.

Antecedens claret effato Apostoli Iacobi, Act. XV, 11. Per gratiam Domini nostri Iesu Christi credimus nos saluari, quemadmodum etiam illi .

2 In V. T. Deus fidelium fuit Pater, Deut.

XXXII, 6. et hi eius filii, Es. I, 2. Ierem. XXXI, 20. E. fideles V.

T. fuerunt renati. Antithesis est Socinianorum, negantium, regenerationem in V.

T. locum obtinuisse, quorum praecipuum argumentum est: Regeniti sumus per resurrectionem Christi, 1 Petr. I, 3. Ergo ante resurrectionem Christi nemo regenitus fuit.

Resp. Regeniti fuimus per resurrectionem Christi tanquam caussam meritariam, vel potius meriti, quod ante et retro operatur, obsignatoriam.

Patres in V.

T. crediderunt in Christum incarnandum, moriendum, e mortuis resuscitandum. resuscitandum. Quæft. resuscitandum. Quæft.


### IX. In what does regeneration formally consist?

Regeneration formally consists in the donation of faith.

Obs. I. The formal aspect of faith is explained by Dr. CALOVIUS thus: that it is the procreation of saving faith, and likewise the excitation of trust in our heart, in his Bibl. illustr. on John 3:5, fol. 692. By Dr. KOENIGIUS it is explained through the bestowing of spiritual life. However, he does not take spiritual life totally, as it includes, beyond the acquisition of the powers of believing, immunity from the dominion and guilt of sin; but partially, in so far as it denotes the supernatural powers of believing that have been conferred. See Theol. positiv. p. 191. It is therefore explained more clearly by Dr. QVENSTEDT in his Systémat. Part III, ch. VI, fol. 482. The form of regeneration consists in the donation of spiritual life, in the bestowing of the powers of believing and of saving faith, or in the illumination of our mind and the excitation of our trust in our heart. It is also vigorously expressed by Dr. FECHTIUS in his Syllog. controuerf. disp. XXVII: Regeneration is the conferring of the powers of a new and spiritual life, which consists in faith.

Obs. II. The conferring of the powers of believing, through which some authors explain the form of regeneration, and the donation of faith, agree in a certain respect. For those powers either receive the saving object, and thus formally are faith itself (John 1:12), or they are considered outside of this reception, and thus are merely passive, until they embrace Christ, upon whom the efficacy of faith depends.

Prob. 1) From Galatians 2:20: "I live, yet not I; but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God." We gather from this saying that the life of the regenerate is faith, and that regeneration consists in the donation of faith.

2) The regenerate are described in the Holy Scriptures as being those who believe in Jesus Christ: Therefore, regeneration is the action through which a man is made a believer, i.e., through which faith is excited. The antecedent is clear a) from John 1:13: "As many as believe in his name (Christ), which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God." Dialectically it is certain: those who are born of God believe in his name. b) 1 John 5:1: "Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God." 3) The action through which we are constituted spiritual children of God is that which is properly called regeneration: But this is through the donation of faith, etc. Therefore. The major premise is clear from the analogy of carnal generation. Just as through this, natural children of God are made, so through regeneration, spiritual children are procreated. The minor is proved a) from John 1:12: "As many as received Christ, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, (namely) to them that believe on his name." b) Galatians 3:26: "Ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus." Q.

Latin:

Regeneratio formaliter consistit in donatione fidei.

Obs. I. Formale fidei a D. CALOVIO sic exponitur, quod sit salvificae fidei procreatio, item fiduciae in corde nostro excitatio, in bibl. illustr. in Io. III, 5. fol. 692. A D. KOENIGIO explicatur per vitae spiritualis largitionem. Vitam autem spiritualem non totaliter sumit, prout praeter adeptionem virium credendi immunitatem a dominio & reatu peccati includit; sed partialiter, in quantum collatas vires credendi supernaturales notat. Vid. theol. positiv. p. 191. Luculentius igitur explanatur & a D. QVENSTED. systémat. Part. III. c. VI. fol. 482. Forma regenerationis consistit in spiritualis vitae donatione, in virium credendi, fideique salvificae largitione, sive in mentis nostrae illuminatione, & fiduciae nostrae in corde nostro excitatione. Neruose etiam exprimitur a D. FECHTIO in syllog. controuerf. disp. XXVII. Regeneratio est virium nouae & spiritualis vitae, quae in fide consistit, collatio.

Obs. II. Collatio virium credendi, per quam nonnulli auctores regenerationis formam explincant, & donatio fidei certo respectu conueniunt. Nam vires illae vel recipiunt obiectum salutare, & sic formaliter sunt ipsa fides, Io. I, 12. vel extra hanc receptionem considerantur, & sic mere-passiue sunt, donec Christum, a quo pendet efficacia fidei, complectantur.

Prob. 1) Ex Gal. II, 20. Viuo autem non amplius ego; sed viuit in me Christus: quod vere nunc viuo in carne, in fide viuo, quae est in Filium Dei. Colligimus ex hoc dicto, quod vita regeneratorum sit fides, & in fidei donatione consistat regeneratio.

2) Renati describuntur in sacris litteris, quod sint credentes in Iesum Christum: E. Regeneratio est actio, per quam homo efficitur credens, h. e. per quam fides excitatur, Antecedens liquet a) ex Io. I, 13. Qui credunt in nomen ipsius (Christi), non ex sanguinibus, neque ex voluntate carnis, neque ex voluntate viri, sed ex Deo nati sunt. Dialectice ceres: qui nati sunt ex Deo, credunt in nomen ipsius. b) I Io. V, 1. Omnis, qui credit, Iesum esse Christum, ex Deo natus est. 3) Per quam actionem diuinam constituimur filii Dei spirituales, illa est proprie dicta regeneratio: Atqui per donationem fidei &c. Ergo. Maior claret analogia generationis carnalis. Sicut per hanc fiunt filii Dei naturales: ita per regenerationem procreantur filii spirituales. Minor probatur a) ex Io. I, 12. Quotquot receperunt Christum, dedit illis potestatem, ut filii Dei fierent (nempe) credentibus in nomen ipsius. b) Gal. III, 26. Omnes Filii Dei estis per fidem in Christo Iesu. Quaest.


### Q. X. What is the terminus a quo and the terminus ad quem of regeneration?

The terminus a quo of regeneration in the abstract is spiritual death, in so far as this denotes ἀπισίαν (unbelief), and the lack of the powers of believing. The terminus ad quem in the abstract is spiritual life, or true faith, joined with Christ the mediator, and uniting his merit with us, so that it becomes ours. The terminus a quo of regeneration in the concrete is the sinner, indeed contrite through the divine law, but lacking the powers of believing, and thus far spiritually dead. The terminus ad quem in the concrete is the man who believes, or who is endowed through the Gospel with living faith in Christ, and is therefore spiritually alive.

Obs. Spiritual death is not taken here ὁλικῶς (wholly), or totally, as it imports, beyond the privation of the powers of believing, also the lack of the powers of living holily, along with the dominion and guilt of sin; but μερικῶς (partially), in so far as it denotes ἀπισίαν (unbelief), or the impotence of believing in Christ, and of embracing the grace of God founded upon this.

From Gal. II, 20. *I live, yet not I, but Christ liveth in me. And the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.* The sense is: Whatever spiritual life is in me, it is not from me, or from my carnal birth, but proceeds from Christ, and His merit and efficacy, through spiritual regeneration; inasmuch as it has gifted me with faith, which apprehends the grace and merit of Christ, and unites Christ with me, so that Christ may live in me, and I in Christ. Concerning which fiducial apprehension the apprehension of Faith is attributed, not because it joins or unites in any way whatsoever, but because it unites Christ the Mediator, and His merit, to us, so that it may become ours; which it does on the part of the intellect by believing that Christ is my, your, and everyone’s Mediator, who by His passion and death satisfied God for the sins of all and each, etc.; but on the part of the will, by securely resting and acquiescing in Him, as the Mediator and the sole author of the grace and remission of sins to be obtained for us. For not every act is an uniting apprehension, but only that by which a thing is united to us, so that it may become ours, help us, raise us up, and sustain us. Therefore, the union between faith and Christ is such as that between an apprehension and the good apprehended; which union, if you weigh it rightly, you may not incongruously call the formal union of faith, so that it may be distinguished from the mystical union, as the effect of the former. Whence it is concluded that faith does not become alive outside of Christ, but when united with Christ. For just as the body is said to be alive because it is united with the soul, by which it is perfected: so faith is alive which is united with Christ, by whom it is animated. See D. Dannh. in the disp. on the nexus and origin of the gifts of grace.

§. XV. Prob. b. From Eph. II, 5. God, who is rich in mercy, when we were dead in sins, hath quickened us together with Christ. Before regeneration, the sinner is dead, and thus destitute of the powers to receive spiritual life: which he also does not obtain from the law, inasmuch as it is the letter that killeth; but from the gospel, through which the Holy Spirit quickeneth, 2 Cor. III, 6, by kindling true faith, which unites Christ with us, so that, being joined with Him, we may live the life which is from God; Eph. IV, 18.

Latin:

Terminus regenerationis a quo in abstracto est mors spiritualis, quatenus haec denotat ἀπισίαν, incredulitatem, & carentiam virium credendi. Terminus ad quem in abstracto est vita spiritualis, seu vera fides, coniuncta cum Christo mediatore, illiusque meritum nobiscum vniens, vt nostrum fiat . Terminus regenerationis a quo in concreto est peccator, per legem diuinam quidem contritus, sed viribus credendi carens, & hactenus spiritualiter mortuus. Terminus ad quem in concreto est homo credens, seu viua in Christum fide per euangelium donatus, adeoque spiritualiter viuus .

Obs. Mors spiritualis hic non sumitur ὁλικῶς, siue totaliter, prout praeter priuationem virium credendi, etiam carentiam virium sancte viuendi, vna cum dominio, & reatu peccati importat; sed μερικῶς partialiter, in quantum dicit ἀπισίαν, seu impotentiam credendi in Christum, & in hoc fundatam gratiam Dei amplectendi.

Ex Gal. II, 20. Vivo non amplius ego, sed vivit in me Christus. Quod vero nunc vivo in carne, in fide vivo, quae est in Filium Dei, qui dilexit me, et tradidit seipsum pro me. Sensus est: Quidquid vitae spiritualis in me est, non a me, aut carnali mea nativitate est, sed a Christo, eiusque merito et efficacia proficiscitur, per spiritualem regenerationem; quippe quae me donavit fide, quae gratiam meritumque Christi apprehendit, et Christum mecum vnit, vt Christus in me vivat, et ego in Christo. De qua fiduciali apprehensione Fidei tribuitur apprehensio, non quod qualitercunque coniungat, aut uniat, sed quod uniat Christum mediatorem, eiusque meritum ad nos, ut fiat nostrum; quod ex parte intellectus facit, credendo, Christum esse meum, tuum, et omnium mediatorem, qui passione et morte sua pro omnium et singulorum peccatis Deo satisfecerit etc. ex parte voluntatis autem, in ipso, ut mediatore et auctore nobis impetrandae gratiae et remissionis peccatorum unico credito, secure recumbendo et acquiescendo. Non enim quilibet actus uniens est apprehensio, sed ille denum, quo res ad nos vnitur, ut nostra fiat, nos iuuet, erigat, sustentet. Est itaque vnio inter fidem et Christum talis, qualis est inter apprehensionem et bonum apprehensum; quam quidem vnionem, si recte expendes, formalem fidei vnionem haud incongrue dixeris, vt ab vnione mystica, ceu illius effectu, distinguatur. Vnde conficitur, quod fides non extra Christum, sed vnita cum Christo viva fit. Quem ad modum enim corpus ideo dicitur vivum, quia est vnitum cum anima, a qua perficitur: ita fides viva est, quae est vnita cum Christo, a quo animatur. Vid. D. Dannh. in disp. de nexu et origine donorum gratiae.

§. XV. Prob. b. Ex Eph. II, 5. Deus diues misericordia nos, quum essemus mortui in peccatis, vivificauit cum Christo. Ante regenerationem peccator est mortuus, adeoque destitutus viribus ad accipiendam vitam spiritualem: quam etiam non adipiscitur ex lege, quippe quae est littera occidens; sed ex euangelio, per quod Spiritus S. vivificat, 2 Cor. III, 6. veram accendendo fidem, quae Christum nobiscum vnit, vt cum illo coniuncti viuamus vitam, quae est ex Deo; Eph. IV, 18.


### Q. XI. What kind of change does regeneration bring about?

Regeneration brings about a change in the sinner that is not substantial, but accidental.

Prob. 1) Regeneration is a spiritual quickening, Gal. II, 2. Now, those very same who are dead in sins are spiritually quickened, Eph. II, 1. Therefore also those very same who were previously unregenerate are regenerated by the Holy Spirit.

2) Just as the very substance of man is not lost through sin: so neither is a new essence created through regeneration, but the state of man is accidentally changed; because through regeneration he is transferred from the state of unbelief into the state of faith.

The antithesis is 1) of the Schwenckfeldians, Weigelians, and Anabaptists, who dream that through regeneration the prior substance of the body is abolished, and that, while the soul remains the same, a new body is given that is essentially different from the former: 2) of the Flacians, who posit that God in conversion and regeneration creates a new heart, and thus a new man, in such a way that the substance of the old Adam, and especially the rational soul, is utterly abolished, and a new essence of the soul is created out of nothing.

I. Creation is the production of substance, for it is an …action with a substantial term. Regeneration is the creation of a new heart, Ps. LI, 10 [12]. Therefore, regeneration is the production of a new substance. Resp. Creation properly so called is the production of substance. But in the cited passage, creation is taken improperly, and does not denote the production of a heart substantially different, but the renewal of the heart with new and spiritual powers. For David is not speaking of the creation of the heart, by which the essence is new, but of the creation of a pure heart, i.e., purged from the filth of sins.…

II. The reborn is called a new creature, 2 Cor. V, 17, a new man, Eph. IV, 24, Col. III, 10. Whence arises the argument: He who through regeneration becomes a new man and a new creature, he receives a new substance through regeneration. But the contrite sinner &c. Therefore. The major is evident; because a new man and a new creature denotes a new substance. Resp. He is called a new man and a new creature on account of the new spiritual powers bestowed in regeneration and renewal, by which the image of God is repaired, consisting in the knowledge of God, Col. III, 10, in righteousness and holiness of truth, Eph. IV, 24. Therefore, he is called a new man not physically, by reason of substance, but mystically, by reason of spiritual powers and qualities.

Ques. XII. Do the reborn receive a new nature from God by the benefit of regeneration? By the benefit of regeneration, the reborn obtain from God not a new nature, but supernatural powers.

Prob. If the reborn obtain a new nature by the benefit of regeneration, this will be either a new substance or new natural powers. But a new substance is not given divinely through regeneration; because regeneration brings about a change of the sinner that is not substantial, but accidental: nor are new natural powers conferred through regeneration; therefore, because the powers of believing are not native or natural, but given and supernatural. Therefore, the reborn do not obtain a new nature from God by the benefit of regeneration.

The antithesis is that of the Anabaptists and Weigelians, whose chief argument is: Those to whom God imparts a divine nature by the benefit of regeneration, they obtain a new nature: But God to converted sinners &c. Therefore. The minor is clear from 2 Pet. I, 4, where the Apostle Peter asserts that the reborn are κοινωνοὶ θείας φύσεως, partakers of the divine nature. Resp. The reborn are rendered partakers of the divine nature, not through regeneration, but through the gracious indwelling of God and spiritual union with Christ. D. GERHARD clearly explains the words of Peter in harm. eu. p. 552. Christ, through the donation of τῆς θείας φύσεως, renders us κοινωνὸς 2 Pet. I, 4, which is to be understood not of the transfusion of the divine essence into us, nor of any essential conversion of our souls or bodies into the divine nature, but of the spiritual union of the faithful with God, and the spiritual and mystical communication arising from the same.

Ques. XIII. Is regeneration a reformation of life and actions? Regeneration formally is not a reformation of a life previously led.

Prob. a) Because regeneration differs from renewal, and the former is prior to the latter, Tit. III, 5. Therefore, one cannot be defined by the other. The antecedent is confirmed: regeneration confers the first spiritual being, when through faith we are begotten as sons of God; but this reformation, or change, presupposes that first being, and belongs to a man already reborn.

b) As natural generation is not a change of natural life: so spiritual regeneration is not a change of spiritual life.

c) Infants are truly reborn through baptism; who, however, if prevented by death, cannot change their life for the better. The thief on the cross, having been converted, Luc. XXIII, 40, was certainly reborn, otherwise he would not have entered the kingdom of God, Io. III, 5, 1 Cor. XV, 50, yet he could not amend his previously led life.

The antithesis is that of the Socinians, who describe regeneration through the reformation of a life previously led according to the precepts of Christ. Their arguments are:

I. Regeneration in the Holy Scriptures is described through the putting on of the new man, and the putting off of the old man, Eph. IV, 24, through a solicitous flight from and hatred of sin, 1 Io. III, 9. Resp. These not pertain to regeneration, but to renewal. They do not enter into the essence and form of regeneration, but are its fruits, indications, and testimonies.

II. Just as he who is begotten is changed from non-being to being: so he is reborn who, as far as the manner of life is concerned, turns out to be what he was not before, namely, devoted to the pursuit of righteousness and holiness, whereas he once gave himself over to sin. Resp. I invert the argument: Just as he who is naturally begotten is changed from non-being to the first natural being: so he who is reborn is changed from non-being to the first spiritual being: But a reformed life is not the first spiritual being, but arises from the first.

Instance: A regenerated man changes his life: Therefore, regeneration is a change of life. Resp. I deny the consequence. By the same reasoning, someone might conclude: The quickened Lazarus walked. Therefore, quickening is walking. Trifles!

Latin:

Regeneratio infert mutationem peccatoris non substantialem, sed accidentalem.

Prob. 1) Regeneratio est spiritualis vivificatio, Gal. II, 2. Iam vero iidem illi, qui in peccatis mortui sunt, spiritualiter vivificantur, Eph. II, 1. E. etiam iidem illi, qui prius erant non renati, per Spiritum S. regenerantur.

2) Sicut per peccatum non ipsa substantia hominis deperditur: ita nec per regenerationem noua essentia creatur, sed status hominis accidentaliter mutatur; propterea quod per regenerationem e statu infidelitatis in statum fidei transfertur.

Antithesis est 1) Schwenckfeldianorum, Weigelianorum et Anabaptistarum, somniantium, per regenerationem aboleri priorem corporis substantiam, ac manente anima eadem dari corpus nouum essentialiter a priori differens: 2) Flacianorum, statuentium, Deum in conversione et regeneratione nouum cor, atque adeo nouum hominem ita creare, vt veteris Adami substantia inprimis vero anima rationalis penitus aboleatur, et noua animae essentia ex nihilo creetur. Quorum palmaria sunt argumenta:

I. Creatio est productio substantiae, est enim actio termini substantialis. Regeneratio est noui cordis creatio, Ps. LI, 12. E. regeneratio est nouae substantiae productio. Resp. Creatio proprie dicta est productio substantiae. At l. c. creatio sumitur improprie, et non notat productionem cordis substantialiter diuersi, sed instaurationem cordis, nouis, iisque spiritualibus tualibus viribus instructi. Sermo enim est Dauidi non de creatione cordis, qua essentiam novi, sed de creatione cordis puri, i. e. a sordibus peccatorum repurgati.

II. Renatus dicitur noua creatura, 2 Cor. V, 17. nouus homo, Eph. IV, 24. Col. III, 10. Vnde nascitur argumentum: Qui per regenerationem fit nouus homo & noua creatura, is per regenerationem nouam accipit substantiam. Atqui peccator contritus &c. Ergo. Maior constat; quia nouus homo & noua creatura notat nouam substantiam. Resp. Nouus homo & noua creatura dicitur, ob nouas vires spirituales in regeneratione & renouatione collatas, quibus reparatur imago Dei consistens in agnitione Dei, Col. III, 10. in iustitia & sanctitate veritatis, Eph. IV, 24. Dicitur itaque nouus homo non physice, ratione substantiæ, sed mystice, ratione virium & qualitatum spiritualium.

Quæst. XII. An renati beneficio regenerationis nouam a Deo accipiunt naturam? Renati beneficio regenerationis a Deo consequuntur non nouam naturam, sed vires supernaturales.

Prob. Si renati beneficio regenerationis consequuntur nouam naturam, hæc erit vel noua substantia, vel nouæ vires naturales. At non datur diuinitus per regenerationem nova substantia; quia regeneratio infert mutationem peccatoris non substantialem, sed accidentalem: neque per regenerationem conferuntur nouæ vires naturales; ideo, quod vires credendi non sunt natiuae, aut naturales, sed datiuæ & supernaturales. E. renati beneficio regenerationis non consequuntur a Deo nouam naturam.

Antithesis est Anabaptistarum & Weigelianorum, quorum præcipuum argumentum est: Quibus Deus beneficio regenerationis impertitur naturam diuinam, illi nouam consequuntur naturam: Atqui Deus peccatoribus conuersis &c. E. Minor liquet ex 1 Petr. I, 4. vbi Apostolus Petrus asserit, quod regeniti sint κοινωνοὶ θείας φύσεως, participes naturæ diuinæ. Resp. Regeniti redduntur participes naturæ diuinæ, non per regenerationem, sed per gratiosam Dei inhabitationem, & spiritualem cum Christo vnionem. Luculenter verba Petrina exponit D. GERHARD. in harm. eu. p. 552. Christus per donationem τῆς θείας φύσεως nos κοινωνὸς reddit 2 Petr. I, 4. quod non de diuinæ essentiæ in nos transfusione, nec de essentiali quadam animarum, vel corporum nostrorum in diuinam naturam conuersione, sed de spirituali fidelium cum Deo vnione, ex eademque orta spirituali & mystica communicatione accipiendum est.

Quæst. XIII. Estne regeneratio vitæ & actionum reformatio? Regeneratio formaliter non est vitæ ante actæ reformatio.

Prob. a) Quia regeneratio a renouatione differt, hacque prior est illa, Tit. III, 5. E. vna per alteram definiri nequit. Antecedens confirmatur: regeneratio confert esse primum spirituale, quando per fidem gignimur filii Dei; hæc autem reformatio, seu immutatio, præsupponit primum illud esse, estque hominis iam regeniti.

b) Vt generatio naturalis non est vitæ naturalis mutatio: ita regeneratio spiritualis non est vitæ spiritualis mutatio.

c) Infantes per baptismum vere regenerantur; qui tamen, morte præuenti, vitam in melius mutare nequeunt. Latro in cruce conuersus, Luc. XXIII, 40. vtique regenitus fuit, alioqui regnum Dei ingressus non fuisset, Io. III, 5. 1 Cor. XV, 50. nec tamen vitam ante actam emendare potuit.

Antithesis est Socinianorum, qui describunt regenerationem per reformationem vitæ ante actæ secundum præcepta Christi. Quorum argumenta sunt:

I. Regeneratio in sacris litteris describitur per induitionem noui hominis, & depositionem veteris hominis, Eph. IV, 24. per sollicitam fugam & odium peccati, 1 Io. III, 9. Resp. Hæc prædicata non pertinent ad regenerationem, sed ad renouationem. Non ingrediuntur essentiam & formam regenerationis, sed sunt illius fructus indicia & testimonia.

II. Quem ad modum qui gignitur, a non esse ad esse mutatur: ita regignitur, qui quod ad vitæ rationem attinet, is euadit, qui antea non fuit, nimirum iustitiæ sanctimoniæque deditus studio, cum aliquando peccato dederit operam. Resp. In uerto argumentum: Sicut, qui naturaliter gignitur, a non esse ad esse primum naturale mutatur: ita, qui regignitur, a non esse ad esse primum spirituale mutatur: At uita reformata non est primum esse spirituale, sed a primo ortum.

Instantia: Homo regeneratus uitam mutat: E. regeneratio est uitæ mutatio. Resp. Nego consequentiam. Eadem ratione quispiam colligeret: Viuificatus Lazarus ambulauit. E. uiuificatio est ambulatio. Nugæ!


### Quest. XIV. Whether the regeneration of a sinful man is completed in a moment, or whether it occurs successively?

The regeneration of infants is instantaneous ), but the ordinary regeneration of adults is successive ).

Prob. a. In infants, there is no affected and stubborn repugnance; indeed, the grace of the Holy Spirit, joined to baptism, breaks and restrains their natural resistance, so that it does not impede regeneration. For this reason, their rebirth is completed in one moment.

Prob. b. For an adult Jew, Turk, or Gentile to be regenerated, there are many scruples which must be removed by applying care, and he must be enlightened and informed from the divine word over a longer tract of time, until a full faith is kindled in his soul.

Rightly, therefore, OLEARIUS teaches in the index to Balduin, p. 155: The form of regeneration consists in the successive communication of grace, and the bestowal of faith and spiritual life: it is not a sudden action, but one to be perfected in a certain order. Nor is there any reason for us to doubt this, since Paul, by his anxious labor (which is the emphatic meaning of the word ὠδῖνα), quite obscurely hints at the delay and duration of regeneration, .

You say: I. Theologians of great name assert that regeneration is instantaneous. Conf. D. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 924. D. CALOV. in bibl. illustr. ad Io. III, 3. f. 692. D. QVENSTED. in system. part. III. f. 632.

Resp. Those theologians seem to have looked to 1) the regeneration of infants; 2) the bestowal of the beginnings of faith in adults regarding the first holy thought and desire. You say: II. Natural generation happens in an instant: Therefore, so does spiritual regeneration. Resp. That analogy is not to be extended beyond its third point. The reason for the diversity is that through natural generation, substance is produced in an instant because there is no objective impediment, whereas through regeneration, new qualities are produced successively in adults, who not rarely place an impediment in the way of the regeneration being perfected.

Latin:

Regeneratio infantum est momentanea ), sed ordinaria hominum adultorum regeneratio est successiua ).

Prob. a. In infantibus non datur repugnantia affectata & morosa; naturalem uero eorundem resistentiam gratia Spiritus S., baptismo coniuncta, frangit & cohibet, ne regeneratio nem impediat. Quam ob rem eorum renascentia uno momento absoluitur.

Prob. b. Adulto Iudæo, Turcæ, uel gentili regenerando multi sunt scrupuli, qui adhibita cura euellendi sunt, iisque illuminandus & informandus est e verbo diuino longiori temporis tractu, donec plena fides in animo eius accendatur.

Recte igitur docet OLEARIVS in indiculo Balduin. p. 155. Forma regenerationis consistit in successiua gratiæ communicatione, & fidei atque uitæ spiritualis collatione: non est ea actio subitanea, sed certo ordine perficienda. Nec est, quod hac de re dubitemus, cum Paullus anxio suo partu (quæ est uerbi ὠδῖνα emphatica significatio) moram & tractum regenerationis haud obscure innuat, .

Dicis: I. Theologi magni nominis asserunt, regenerationem esse momentaneam. Conf. D. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 924. D. CALOV. in bibl. illustr. ad Io. III, 3. f. 692. D. QVENSTED. in system. part. III. f. 632. Resp. Theologi illi respexisse uidentur 1) regenerationem infantum; 2) collationem initiorum fidei in adultis quoad primam cogitationem sanctam & desiderium.

Dicis: II. Generatio naturalis fit in instanti: E. & regeneratio spiritualis. Resp. Simile illud non est extendendum ultra suum tertium. Ratio diuersitatis est, quod per generationem naturalem substantia in instanti ob nullum impedimentum obiectum, per regenerationem nouæ qualitates successiue in adultis, qui haud raro impedimentum regenerationi perficiendæ obiiciunt, producuntur.


### Quest. XV. Is regeneration an efficacious act of the Holy Spirit?

Regeneration is an action of the Holy Spirit, efficacious and sufficient for producing faith ), but it is not irresistible ).

Prob. a. Paul wishes that we know what is the excellent greatness of the power of God toward us who believe, according to the operation of the strength of his might, . The Apostle indicates that our faith is owed not to our natural powers, but to the most efficacious divine operation. The teacher of the Gentiles does not speak of the absolute power of God, by which He can also effect those things which He does not will; but of the power joined with the will, and that, not insofar as it exerted itself in creating the world, and still exerts itself in governing the same, but insofar as it is occupied with sinners to be converted, whom God endows with true faith by his ordinary power, and preserves in faith: For we are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation, .

Prob. b. Because God does not exert his absolute power in regenerating men, it often happens that a contumacious sinner places a malicious obstacle to the regenerating grace, and petulantly rejects the offered means of salvation. When the Apostle Paul, agitated by the Holy Spirit and testifying that Jesus is the Christ, was opposed by the Jews, and they blasphemed to such a degree that the Apostle, shaking his garments, said to them: Your blood be upon your own head; I am clean, from now on I will go to the Gentiles, .

Latin:

Regeneratio est actio Spiritus S. efficax & sufficiens ad producendam fidem ), sed non est irresistibilis ).

Prob. a. Paullus uult, ut sciamus, quæ fit excellens magnitudo uirtutis Dei erga nos, qui credimus, iuxta operationem roboris potentiæ ipsius, . Indicat Apostolus, quod fides nostra debeatur non naturalibus nostris uiribus, sed efficacissimæ operationi diuinæ. Non loquitur gentium doctor de absoluta Dei potentia, qua is illa etiam potest efficere, quæ non uult; sed de potentia coniuncta cum uoluntate, eaque, non quatenus se exseruit in creando mundo, & adhuc se exserit in eodem regendo, sed quatenus occupata est circa peccatores se exserit in eodem regendo, sed quatenus occupata est circa peccatoconvertendos, quos Deus ordinaria sua potentia vera fide donat, & in fide conservat: Virtute quippe Dei custodimur per fidem ad salutem, .

Prob. b. Quia Deus in regenerandis hominibus non absolutam suam potentiam exserit, sæpe numero usu venit, ut peccator contumax gratiæ regeneratrici malitiosum obicem ponat, & oblata salutis media petulanter reiiciat. Apostolo Paulo, a Spiritu S. agitato & contestanti, Iesum esse Christum, Iudæi se opponebant, & adeo blasphemabant, vt Apostolus excutiens vestimenta, diceret ad eos: Sanguis vester sit super capite vestro; purus ego nunc ad gentes abibo, .


### Question XVI. Is the regeneration of a sinful man perfect?

Regeneration on the part of God is a perfect action ); but on the part of the receiving subject, or the sinful man, regeneration is not simply perfect ).

Prob. a. Since every work of God is good and perfect, certainly regeneration on the part of the efficient cause, or God, is perfect without any defect.

Prob. b. Although the Holy Spirit acts perfectly when about to regenerate a sinner; yet the sinner does not perfectly receive the influx of the Holy Spirit. Hence it happens that faith, toward which regeneration tends, can grow and diminish. See Luc. XVII, 5. And although faith is essentially perfect by reason of its parts; yet it is not always perfect accidentally by reason of its degrees.

Latin:

Regeneratio ex parte Dei est actio perfecta ); ex parte autem subiecti recipientis, siue hominis peccatoris, regeneratio non simpliciter perfecta est ).

Prob. a. Cum omne opus Dei bonum & perfectum sit, vtique regeneratio ex parte causæ efficientis, siue Dei, fine vllo defectu perfecta est.

Prob. b. Licet Spiritus S. perfecte agat, peccatorem regeneraturus; peccator tamen influxum Spiritus S. non perfecte recipit. Inde fit, vt fides, ad quam tendit regeneratio, crescere & imminui queat. Vid, Luc. XVII, 5. Et quamuis fides essentialiter perfecta sit ratione partium; non tamen semper perfecta est accidentalter ratione graduum.


### Question XVII. Is regeneration losable?

By sins committed with deliberate purpose, and which lay waste the conscience, the grace of regeneration is lost.

Prob. From 1 Tim. I, 19. Wage the good warfare, having faith and a good conscience, which some have rejected, and concerning the faith have made shipwreck. From this apostolic oracle we argue: He who makes shipwreck of faith, he loses the grace of regeneration: But a man reborn, by sinning ἐκ προαιρέσεως (from choice), lays waste his conscience, and makes shipwreck of faith. E.

There is an antithesis of the Anabaptists, who maintain that the reborn cannot lose the Holy Spirit. They go about fortifying their opinion with the following arguments:

I. The children of God are born of incorruptible seed, . E. that seed cannot be lost. Resp. That seed of the divine word is incorruptible absolutely and in itself, yet relatively, namely with respect to man, who sins by choice (proæretice), it is losable; for it is often taken away from the heart, . Just as solar rays are incorruptible, yet when night approaches, they are withdrawn from our sight.

II. Everyone who is born of God does not commit sin; because his seed remains in him: indeed he cannot sin, insofar as he is born of God, . Resp. The reborn, insofar as he is reborn, and as long as the seed of regeneration remains vigorous in his heart, does not commit sin that proceeds from a deliberate purpose of mind against conscience. Indeed, he cannot sin ἐκ προαιρέσεως (from choice), so as to remain a child of God at the same time. Yet he can sin even mortally, insofar as he allows himself to be overcome by the snares of the devil, the love of the world, and the allurements of the flesh.

III. Nothing can separate the faithful from the love of God. Rom. VIII, 38. Resp. No external creature can separate the faithful from the love of God: but indwelling sin (which is not a creature), if dominion is permitted to it, separates them from God.

Latin:

Peccatis deliberato proposito admissis, & conscientiam vastantibus, gratia regenerationis amittitur.

Prob. Ex I Tim. I, 19. Milita bonam militiam, habens fidem & bonam conscientiam, quam quidam repulerunt, & circa fidem naufragium fecerunt. Ex hoc oraculo apostolico argumentamur: Qui naufragium facit fidei, is amittit gratiam regenerationis: Atqui homo renatus ἐκ προαιρέσεως peccando, conscientiam vastat, fideique naufragium facit. E.

Antithesis est Anabaptistarum, statuentium, renatos Spiritum S. amittere non posse. Qui suam opinionem sequentibus argumentis munitum eunt:

I. Filii Dei semine incorruptibili sunt geniti, . E. illud semen amitti non potest. Resp. Semen illud verbi diuini est incorruptibile absolute & in se, respectiue tamen, scilicet respectu hominis, proæretice peccantis, est amissibile; aufertur enim sæpe ex corde, . Sicut radii solares sunt incorruptibiles, appetente tamen nocte, visu nostro subducuntur.

II. Omnis, qui natus est ex Deo, peccatum non facit; quia semen ipsius in eo manet: immo non potest peccare, quatenus ex Deo natus est, . Resp. Renatus, quatenus est renatus, & quamdiu semen regenerationis in corde ipsius vegetum manet, peccatum, contra conscientiam ex deliberato animi proposito profectum non committit. Immo non potest peccare ἐκ προαιρέσεως, vt simul filius Dei maneat. Peccare tamen potest etiam mortifere, quatenus ab insidiis diaboli, amore mundi, & illecebris carnis se vinci patitur.

III. Nihil fideles separare potest a dilectione Dei. Rom. VIII, 38. Resp. Nulla creatura externa fideles separare potest a dilectione Dei: at inhabitans peccatum (quod non est creatura), si ei permittatur dominatus, eosdem a Deo diuellit.


### Question XVIII. Is lost regeneration repeatable?

Lost regeneration can be recovered by a penitent sinner.

Prob. From Gal. IV, 19. Τεκνία με, ὃς πάλιν ὠδίνω, my little children, of whom I travail in birth again. Ὠδίνεσθαι belongs to mothers, who carry the fetus in the womb with great difficulty, until it puts on the form of a perfect human. The Apostle therefore implies that he bears anxious care for the Galatians, because they had been corrupted by the Pseudo-apostles and had lost the form of Christ, and that he strives intensely so that, through the seed of the gospel sown in their hearts, they might be formed anew, whereby the image of Christ, which they had lost, might shine forth in them through repeated regeneration. You say: Baptism, the ordinary medium of regeneration, cannot be repeated: Therefore, neither can lost regeneration be recovered.

I answer: Regeneration is recovered not through baptism, but through the seed of the divine word, from which faith in Christ is conceived again, and thus the converted sinner begins to revive.

Latin:

Amissa regeneratio a peccatore pœnitente recuperari potest.

Prob. Ex Gal. IV, 19. Τεκνία με, ὃς πάλιν ὠδίνω, filioli mei, quos iterum parturio. Ὠδίνεσθαι est matrum, magna cum molestia foetum in utero gestantium, donec formam perfecti hominis induat. Innuit igitur Apostolus, se anxiam Galatarum curam gerere, ideo quod a Pseudo-apostolis depravati formam Christi amiserant, & impense anniti, vt per semen evangelii in corda ipsorum sparsum de integro formentur, quo imago Christi, quam deperdiderant, iterata regeneratione ipsis refulgeat. Dicis: Baptismus, ordinarium regenerationis medium, non potest repeti: E. nec amissae regeneratio potest recuperari.

Resp. Recuperatur regeneratio non per baptismum, sed per semen verbi divini, ex quo iterum concipitur fides in Christum, atque adeo peccator conversus reviviscere incipit.


### Question XIX. Does God wish to convert and regenerate a sinner three, four, or more times?

Reborn men, aided by the conserving grace of God, carefully guard themselves, lest by repeated sin they maliciously wound their own conscience ): but if, however, overcome by the machinations of the devil, the allurements of the world, and the suggestions of the flesh, they fall three, four, or more times into mortal sin, they should not in the least doubt of the converting and regenerating grace of God ).

Prob. a. From 1 John V, 18. We know that everyone who is born of God does not sin; but he who is born of God keeps himself, and the wicked one does not touch him. The reborn watch over their own salvation, lest, polluted by deliberate sins, they fall from the hope of eternal life; and although they are solicited by the devil to sin, yet with the shield of faith they repel his fiery darts, Eph. VI, 6.

Prob. b. 1) So stupendous is the clemency of God, that He calls back to Himself a soul polluted by repeated sins, and invites it to perform penance, Jer. III, 1. You have played the harlot with many companions; yet return to me! says the Lord. 2) When Peter asked of Christ: Lord, how often shall my brother sin against me, and I forgive him? Up to seven times? Jesus said to him: I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven, Matt. XVIII, 21. From these arises the argument: That which Christ commands men, that they should do by the example of His Father, God performs in an infinitely more excellent way. But Christ commands men that, by the example of His Father (see Matt. V, 48), even the reborn, after having acknowledged the truth, should forgive each other even grave sins more often. Therefore, God, moved by mercy, forgives sins much more readily and more often; but He would not forgive them, unless He wished to convert and regenerate the man more often.

3) That God converts and regenerates a sinner three, four, or more times can be proven by clear examples. a) In Moses, God reckoned that as a mortal crime, that he omitted circumcision for the sake of his wife and young son, Exod. IX, 24. The same man sinned so gravely at the waters of strife that he even lost his faith, Num. XX, 12. That he was converted and reborn three times, we affirm as true. b) We observe three mortal sins of Aaron. The first was idolatry, Exod. XXXII. The second was contumely against Moses, Num. XII, 1. The third was ἀπισία (unbelief), by which at the waters of strife, together with his brother Moses, he had rendered himself hateful to God, Num. XX, 12. Thus he was reborn four times (in infancy, when he was circumcised, and after having committed three great crimes). c) Notorious are the two deadly sins of King David. The first was adultery with Bathsheba, and the slaughter of Uriah procured by him, 2 Sam. XI, 4, 15. The second was the proud and unfortunate numbering of the people. Confer 2 Sam. XXIV, 1 ff. with 1 Chron. XXI ff. Which sin was indeed mortal. For it was committed at the instigation of the devil, with God angry and punishing most severely. David confessed: I have sinned greatly, 1 Chron. XXI, 8.

You say: Only one mortal sin of David is recounted in 1 Kings 15:5. David did what was right in the eyes of Jehovah, and did not turn aside from all that He had commanded him, all the days of his life; except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite. Resp. 1) David did what was right in the eyes of the Lord by acting uprightly, as long as he stood in faith, and then by rising again through repentance, when he fell from the state of faith. 2) David did not turn aside from the divine precepts written explicitly and in express letter, except in the matter of Uriah the Hittite. For then, by committing adultery and killing, he sinned against the express divine precepts V, VI, VIII, X. It was therefore a most scandalous external sin, against so many precepts written by the divine finger; such as no other of David's was. But the numbering of the people was not prohibited by any divine precept and in express letters; but the internal pride of the mind, from which the numbering of the people proceeded, God, the καρδιογνώστης (knower of hearts), saw, and He esteemed and punished it as a deadly sin. The antithesis is that of the Socinians, who deny that God converts and regenerates a man three or four times (*). Their principal arguments are: I. The regenerate do not commit sin, 1 John 3:9. Therefore, they do not need a triple regeneration. Resp. The regenerate, as long as they are regenerate, and as long as they retain the seed of the divine word in a lively mind, do not sin by proairesis (deliberate choice); but the same, insofar as they succumb to the temptations of the devil and the incitements of the flesh, commit a deadly sin. II. The regenerate are perfect. For Noah, Gen. 6:9, Abraham, Gen. 17:1, and David, 1 Kings 15:1, and others, are called perfect. Therefore, they neither fall back into sins of proairesis, nor are they in need of a regeneration repeated twice or thrice. Resp. In the cited place, absolute perfection is not meant, but comparative; not of consummation, but of sincerity; not continuous, but temporary, indeed sometimes liable to defect, but to be repaired, or already repaired, through repentance. III. The faith was once delivered to the saints, Ep. Jude v. 3. Therefore, faith cannot be lost and given again, since it is given only once. Resp. In the cited place, it is not subjective faith, or the trust of the heart by which one believes in Christ, that is denoted, but objective faith, or the doctrine of faith which is believed, to which the participle παραδοθεῖσα, delivered, properly belongs. But faith is said to be once delivered to the saints because it was delivered once and for all and most …sufficiently, not to be changed or interpolated with new additions. IV. Whomever God has once liberated, if they fall back a second time, τὸ δεύτερον, into ἀπιστίαν (unbelief), He destroys; He does not convert or regenerate them twice, thrice, four times, or more often: But the faithful, etc. Therefore. The minor is evident from Ep. Jude v. 5. Resp. The words of the cited text flow thus: I wish to remind

Latin:

Homines renati, gratia Dei conservante adiuti, sollicite sibi cavent, ne repetito peccato malitiose conscientiam suam laedant ): quod si tamen a machinis diaboli, illecebris mundi, carnisque suggestionibus superati, ter, quater, aut pluries in peccatum mortiferum prolabantur, de gratia Dei convertente & regenerante minime dubitent ).

Prob. a. Ex I Io. V, 18. Scimus, quod omnis, qui natus est ex Deo, non peccet; sed qui natus est ex Deo, obseruat se ipsum, & malignus non tanget eum. Renati in suam vigilant salutem, ne peccatis proæreticis polluti spe vitæ æternæ excidant; & quamuis a diabolo ad peccandum sollicitentur, scuto tamen fidei ignita eius tela repellunt, Eph. VI, 6.

Prob. b. 1) Tam stupenda est clementia Dei, vt animam iteratis peccatis pollutam ad se reuocet, & ad pœnitentiam agendam inuitet, Ier. III, 1. Tu scortata es cum sociis multis; reuertere tamen ad me! dictum Iehouæ. 2) Cum Petrus quæreret ex Christo: Domine, quoties peccabit in me frater meus, & remittere debeo illi? Num vsque ad septies? Dixit illi Iesus: Non dico tibi vsque ad septies, sed vsque ad septuagies septies, Matth. XVIII, 21. Nascitur ex his argumentum: Quod mandat Christus hominibus, vt exemplo Patris sui faciant, id Deus infinities excellentiori modo præstat. At Christus mandat hominibus, vt exemplo Patris sui, (vid. Matth. V, 48.) etiam renati, post agnitam veritatem, grauia quoque peccata fæpius sibi remittant. E. Deus motus misericordia longe propensiore fæpius peccata remittit; non remitteret autem, nisi fæpius hominem conuertere & regenerare vellet.

3) Deum ter, quater, aut pluries peccatorem conuertere & regenerare, luculentis exemplis comprobari potest. a) In Mose Deus illud pro crimine mortifero reputauit, quod in gratiam coniugis & tenelli filii circumcisionem omisit, Exod. IX, 24. Idem ad aquas iurgii tam grauiter deliquit, vt etiam fidem amiserit, Num. XX, 12. Hunc ter conuerfum & renatum esse, ex vero afferimus. b) Aaronis tria mortifera obferuamus peccata. Primum erat idololatria, Exod. XXXII. Alterum contumelia in Mosen, Num. XII, 1. Tertium erat ἀπισία, qua ad aquas iurgii vna cum fratre Mose se Deo exosum reddiderat, Num. XX, 12. Fuit itaque quater renatus (in infantia, cum circumcisus est, & post commissa tria grandia crimina). c) Notoria sunt regis Dauidis duo peccata letifera. Primum erat adulterium cum Bathseba, & cædes Vriæ ab ipso procurata, 2 Sam. XI, 4. 15. Alterum numeratio populi fastuosa & infausta. Confer. 2 Sam. XXIV, 1. sqq. cum 1 Chron. XXI. sqq. Quod peccatum vtique fuit mortiferum. Nam commissum est concitante diabolo, irascente Deo, & grauissime puniente. Confessus est Dauid: Peccaui valde, 1 Chron. XXI, 8.

Dicis: Vnicum tantum peccatum mortale Dauidis recensetur 1 Reg. XV, 5. Fecit Dauid rectum in oculis Iehovæ, nec recessit ab omni, quod præceperat illi, omnibus diebus vitæ suæ; nisi in negotio Vriæ Chittæi. Resp. 1) Dauid rectum fecit in oculis domini cum probe agendo, quamdiu stetit in fide, tum resurgendo per pœnitentiam, cum lapsus est e statu fidei. 2) Non recessit Dauid a præceptis diuinis explicite & expressa littera scriptis, nisi in negotio Vriæ Chittæi. Nam tum mœchando, & occidendo peccauit contra expressa Dei præcepta V. VI. VIII. X. Erat itaque peccatum externum scandalosissimum, contra tot præcepta diuino digito scripta; quale nullum aliud fuit Dauidis. Numeratio autem populi nullo præcepto diuino, disertisque litteris prohibita erat; internam autem animi superbiam, e qua recensio populi proficiscebatur, Deus καρδιογνώστης vidit, eamque peccatum letiferum æstimauit & vindicauit. Antithesis est Socinianorum, negantium, Deum ter, aut quater hominem conuertere & regenerare (*). Quorum præcipua sunt argumenta: I. Renati peccatum non faciunt, 1 Io. III, 9. E. trina regeneratione non indigent. Resp. Renati, quousque sunt renati, & quamdiu semen verbi diuini vegetum memori mente retinent, non peccant ex proæresi; at iidem, quatenus diaboli tentationibus carnisque irritamentis succubunt, mortiferum peccatum committunt. II. Renati sunt perfecti. Nam Noachus, Gen. VI, 9. Abrahamus, Gen. XVII, 1. & Dauid, 1 Reg. XV, 1. aliique, perfecti dicuntur. E. neque in peccata proæretica recidunt, neque bis aut ter repetitæ regenerationis sunt indigi. Resp. L. c. non intelligitur perfectio absoluta, sed comparata; non consummationis, sed sinceritatis; non continua, sed temporaria, defectui quidem aliquando obnoxia, sed per pœnitentiam reparanda, vel reparata. III. Sanctis fides semel est tradita, ep. Iudæ v. 3. E. fides non potest amitti, & iterum dari, cum semel tantum detur. Resp. L. c. denotatur non fides subiectiua, siue fiducia cordis, qua in Christum creditur, sed fides obiectiua, siue doctrina fidei, quæ creditur, cui proprie competit participium, παραδοθεῖσα, tradita. Dicitur autem fides semel tradita sanctis, quod sit aliquando perfecte & sufficientissime tradita, non immutanda, aut nouis additamentis interpolanda. IV. Quoscunque semel liberatos, τὸ δεύτερον, secundo in ἀπιστίαν relapsos, Deus perdit, eos bis, ter, quater aut pluries non conuertit, neque regenerat: Atqui fideles &c. E. Minor patet ex ep. Iudæ v. 5. Resp. Verba citati textus ita fluunt: Commonefacere au-


### Question XXI. What is the end of regeneration?

you, that you may know this once, that the Lord, after He had saved the people from the land of Egypt, destroyed those who did not believe. Cf. Num. XIV, 35.…

Wherefore τὸ ἅπαξ (once) pertains not to the participle σώσας (having saved), but to εἰδότες (knowing), so that the sense may be: know once, i.e., know in summary; but τὸ δεύτερον (the second time) here signifies the contrary, just as πάλιν (again) is taken in Matt. IV, 1; Jas. V, 18. See HVG. GROTIUS on this passage.

Furthermore, that the Israelites sinned mortally not once, but more often, is evident from Num. XIV, 22.

For this reason, persevering in infidelity and the atrocity of their sins, they were destroyed by God.

V. Whoever, relapsing into sins, are rendered worse than before, they cannot be converted and regenerated: But the reborn, etc.

E. The major premise is evident: because conversion and regeneration make a man better; but he who is rendered worse is not improved.

The minor premise is clear from the sayings of scripture, 2 Pet. II, 20 ff.; Luke XI, 24; John V, 14. Resp.

1) 2 Pet. II, 20 and Luke XI, 24 deal with apostates who fall away either from the true doctrine of faith to heretical doctrine, or plainly to gentile infidelity, or from piety to Epicureanism. Their conversion and regeneration is difficult, but not simply impossible.

For they are called back by God to repentance, Jer. III, 11; 2

Pet. III, 9, and are regenerated when they leave room for divine grace.

2) The saying in John V, 14 contains a dissuasion from relapsing into graver sins, a dissuasion which faithful ministers of the church use to this day. But from the same, a denial of regeneration repeated three or four times cannot be established.

Q. XX. Is regeneration necessary for a sinner for salvation? Regeneration is absolutely and simply necessary for a sinful man for salvation.

Prob. 1) From the words of Christ, John III, 3: Unless one is born ἄνωθεν (from above, or again), he cannot see the kingdom of God.

By which words He teaches that regeneration is necessary: a) universally, for all, without distinction.

For He says: Unless one is reborn, i.e., Everyone who is born needs spiritual regeneration. b) By reason of the end, to obtain eternal salvation.

The "cannot" implies a simple impossibility; because flesh and blood will not inherit the kingdom of God, 1 Cor. XV, 50. 2) Just as faith in Christ is necessary to obtain eternal life, John III, 36: So is regeneration necessary, by which faith is given.

You say: If regeneration is necessary for a man to obtain eternal salvation, then infants of Christian parents who die in the mother's womb, or are born recently and snatched away by sudden death before receiving baptism, will perish eternally; which is harsh to say.

Resp. Ordinary regeneration happens through the word, 1

Pet. I, 23, and through baptism, John III, 5; Tit. III, 5. Extraordinary regeneration, however, happens without external means, such as the regeneration of infants who perish before receiving baptism.

For although we are bound by divine command to the use of external means, God has not so bound His regenerating grace to baptism that He would not both will and be able to regenerate infants extraordinarily and immediately in a case of deprivation. How this happens, we do not anxiously pry into, but commit it to the infinite wisdom and power of God.

Q. XXI. What is the end of regeneration? The intermediate ends of regeneration are justification a), υἱοθεσία (adoption as sons), the final cause of God b), and renewal c): The ultimate end on the part of men is eternal salvation d); on the part of God, the glory of divine mercy e).

Prob. a. By the benefit of regeneration, the sinner, crushed by the hammer of the law, is gifted with faith, and thus is spiritually changed and fitted so that he may be justified, or absolved from the guilt of sin and punishment.

can. This is what Paul hints at, Tit. III, 5, where, having made mention of the washing of regeneration, he soon adds in verse 7: that being justified by his grace we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life. Regeneration therefore precedes justification in the order of nature, not in the order of time. For, at the moment the sinner is gifted with faith in Christ, he is justified at the same time.

Prob. b. Adoption as sons of God is the end of regeneration, by means of justification. For by regeneration, insofar as it is the bestowing of faith, or of a gift inherent in the sons of God, we are not adopted; otherwise faith would save inherently and by reason of its own quality, which is false. Wherefore it is necessary that the reborn be first reconciled to God through faith, before they become sons of God. But they are reconciled to God through Christ; inasmuch as he redeemed us, that we might receive the adoption of sons, Gal. IV, 5. Add that no one becomes a spiritual son of God who has not obtained the remission of sins.

Prob. c. We are baptized and reborn, that we may walk in newness of life, Rom. VI, 4. For we are gifted through regenerating grace with true faith in Christ, which works through love, Gal. V, 6. Wherefore if we live in the Spirit, let us also walk in the Spirit, Gal. V, 25.

Prob. d. God has regenerated us into an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled, and that fadeth not away, reserved in heaven for us. 1 Pet. I, 3. Prob. e. God is to be celebrated with eternal praises, who regenerated and quickened men dead in sins out of grace unmerited and most liberal, that from children of wrath they might become children of grace. Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who according to his abundant mercy has regenerated us, 1 Pet. I, 3.

Latin:

vos volo, ut sciatis vos semel hoc, quod Dominus populum, quum e terra Aegypti servasset, secundum eos, qui non crediderunt, perdiderit. Conf. Num. XIV, 35.

Quare τὸ ἅπαξ pertinet non ad participium σώσας, qui servavit, sed εἰδότες, scientes, ut sensus sit: semel i. e. summatim sciatis; τὸ δεύτερον autem hic valet e contrario, quomodo & πάλιν sumitur Matth. IV, 1. Iac. V, 18. Vid. HVG. GROTIVM in h. l.

Ceterum Israëlitas non semel, sed saepius mortaliter peccasse, constat ex Num. XIV, 22.

Quam ob rem perseverantes in infidelitate & peccatorum atrocitate a Deo perditi sunt.

V. Quicunque relabentes in peccata praeretica redduntur deteriores, illi converti & regenerari nequeunt: Atqui renati &c.

E. Maior constat: quia conversio & regeneratio hominem efficit meliorem; sed qui deterior redditur, is non emendatur.

Minor patet ex dictis scripturae, 2 Petr. II, 20. sqq. Luc. XI, 24. Io. V, 14. Resp.

1) 2 Petr. II, 20. & Luc. XI, 24. agitur de apostatis, qui vel a vera doctrina fidei ad doctrinam haereticam, aut plane ad infidelitatem gentilem, vel a pietate ad Epicureismum prolabuntur. Illorum conversio & regeneratio est difficilis, sed non simpliciter impossibilis.

Revocantur enim a Deo ad poenitentiam, Ier. III, 11. 2

Petr. III, 9. & regenerantur, quando gratiae divinae locum relinquunt.

2) Dictum Io. V, 14. feriam continet dehortationem a recidivatu in peccata graviora, qua dehortatione hodienum fideles ecclesiae ministri utuntur. At ex eadem negatio ter aut quater repetita regenerationis stabiliri nequit.

Quæst. XX. Estne regeneratio peccatori ad salutem necessaria? Regeneratio homini peccatori ad salutem absolute & simpliciter necessaria est.

Prob. 1) E verbis Christi, Io. III, 3. Nisi quis generetur ἄνωθεν (desuper, vel denuo), non potest videre regnum Dei.

Quibus verbis docet, regenerationem esse necessariam: a) universaliter, omnibus, citra distinctionem.

Dicit enim: Nisi quis renatus fuerit, q. d. Omnis, qui nascitur, indiget regeneratione spirituali. b) Ratione finis, ad consequendam salutem aeternam.

Tὸ non potest simplicem inferre impossibilitatem; quia caro & sanguis regnum Dei non haereditario possidebunt, 1 Cor. XV, 50. 2) Sicut necessaria est fides in Christum ad consequendam vitam aeternam, Io. III, 36: Ita necessaria est regeneratio, qua fides donetur.

Dicis: Si homini, aeternam salutem adepturo, necessaria est regeneratio; infantes parentum christianorum in utero materno exstincti, vel recens nati, subitaque morte ante perceptum baptismum rapti, aeternum peribunt; quod dictu asperum est.

Resp. Ordinaria regeneratio fit per verbum, 1

Petr. I, 23. & per baptismum, Io. III, 5. Tit. III, 5. Extraordinaria autem fit sine externis mediis, qualis est regeneratio infantum, ante baptismum perceptum pereuntorum.

Quamvis enim nos divino mandato obligati fimus ad usum externorum mediorum, non tamen Deus suam gratiam regeneratricem ita alligavit baptismo, quin in casu privationis infantes extraordinarie atque immediate regenerare & velit & possit. Quomodo id fiat, non rimamur follicite, sed infinitae Dei sapientiae & potentiae committimus.

Quæst. XXI. Quis est finis regenerationis? Fines intermedii regenerationis sunt iustificatio a), υἱοθεσία, adoptio in filios Causa finalis Dei b), & renouatio c): Finis ultimus ex parte hominum est aeterna salus d); ex parte Dei gloria misericordiae divinae e).

Prob. a. Beneficio regenerationis peccator, malleo legis contritus, fide donatur, atque adeo spiritualiter mutatur, & aptatur, vt iustificari, siue a reatu culpae & poenae absolui possit. iustificari, fiue a reatu culpæ & pœnæ abfolui

Id quod innuit Paulus, Tit. III, 5. vbi facta mentione lauacri regenerationis, mox versu 7. addit: vt iustificati ipsius gratia haeredes fimus secundum spem vitae aeternae. Praecedit igitur regeneratio iustificationem ordine naturae, non ordine temporis. Etenim, quo momento peccator fide in Christum donatur, eodem iustificatur.

Prob. b. Adoptio in filios Dei est finis regenerationis, mediante iustificatione. Per regenerationem enim, quatenus est collatio fidei, seu doni inhaerentis in filiis Dei, non adoptamur; alias fides inhaesive & ratione suae qualitatis saluaret, quod est falsum. Quare necesse est, vt renati Deo prius per fidem reconcilientur, quam fiant filii Dei. Reconciliantur autem Deo per Christum; quippe qui nos redemit, vt adoptionem filiorum acciperemus, Gal. IV, 5. Adiice, quod nemo fit filius Dei spiritualis, qui remissionem peccatorum non est consecutus.

Prob. c. Baptizati & renati sumus, vt in nouitate vitae ambulemus, Rom. VI, 4. Donamur quippe per gratiam regenerantem vera in Christum fide, quae per dilectionem operatur, Gal. V, 6. Quocirca si in spiritu viuimus, spiritu etiam ambulemus, Gal. V, 25.

Prob. d. Deus regenerauit nos in hereditatem incorruptibileem, immaculatam & immarcescibilem, seruatam in caelis erga nos. 1 Petr. I, 3. Prob. e. Aeternis laudibus celebrandus est Deus, qui homines in peccatis mortuos regenerauit & viuificauit ex gratia indebita & liberalissima, vt ex filiis irae fierent filii gratiae. Benedictus sit Deus & Pater Domini nostri Iesu Christi, qui iuxta multam misericordiam regenerauit nos, 1 Petr. I, 3.


### Quaest. XXII. Whether Christ is generated in us through regeneration, so that he himself becomes the new man in us, and flesh of our flesh?

Properly speaking, neither is Christ born in us a), nor is he the new man in us b), nor by the benefit of regeneration does he become flesh of our flesh c).

Prob. a. 1) Because that assertion, that Christ is generated in us, is ἀγεωμετρητον [geometrically absurd]. Holy Scripture teaches clearly that God the Father has regenerated us through the resurrection of Jesus Christ, 1 Pet. I, 3, and that we have been generated in Christ Jesus through the gospel, 1 Cor. IV, 15. These utterances of the Holy Spirit are clear and perspicuous; but the manner of speaking by which Christ himself is said to be generated in us is obscure and intricate. 2) Christ is the father of regeneration, Eph. VIII, 18 [sic]; Heb. II, 13, who generates us spiritually, but is not generated in us. 3) The Son of God is generated from eternity in the bosom of the heavenly Father, John I, 18, not in our bosom. The generation of the Son of God is an immanent action, not an emanating or transient one.

4) Our Jesus, as man, was born in and of the Virgin Mary, Luke I, 35, but is not born in or of us; otherwise he would proceed from the essence of the faithful man. For generation is a communication of essence. 5) The Quakers use that assertion, that Christ is generated in us, to corrupt the article concerning the justification of the sinner. For ROBERT BARCLAY does not blush in his Apol. § 7, p. 141, to assert: that the sinner is justified when Christ is formed in him, generated, and brought to light. Moreover, it is a most absurd dogma of the Mystics that the generation of Christ in us occurs through introversion to God. The Word of the heavenly Father is effectively generated in us as often as we perfectly introvert ourselves to God, says GERLACUS PETRI, cited by Dr. LOESCHER in the preface to theol. myst. orthod.

§ 8. Prob. b. 1) Nowhere does Holy Scripture teach that Christ is the new man. But it does not teach us to be wise above that which is written, 1 Cor. IV, 6.

Christ is the cause of the new man. But a cause is never predicated of the caused, nor the caused of the cause, in the direct case.

3) The new man, considered formally and abstractly, is an accident, namely the knowledge of God, Col. III, 10, justice and true holiness, Eph. IV, 24. But as it is impossible for a substance to be transmuted into an accident, so it is also impossible for Christ to be changed into new qualities, new powers, and new motions, which, in conformity with the Word of God, we call the new man (taken abstractly).

4) The new man, taken concretely, is a mere man (ψιλὸς ἄνθρωπος), instructed by new powers from God: But Christ is God-man (θεάνθρωπος). Therefore, he is not the new man.

Prob. c. Christ was made flesh of our flesh both by the incarnation, Hebr. II, 14, and also by the mystical union and communication, the faithful are rendered partakers of the flesh and blood of Christ, Eph. V, 30, and become living members of the mystical body of Christ, that is, the church. But by regeneration, faith in Christ is kindled.

The antithesis is that of the Weigelians and Quakers, who maintain that Christ is generated in us, and is the new man, and that in regeneration he becomes flesh of our flesh. Their stronger arguments are:

I. Whoever is formed in us is regenerated in us (for formation indeed presupposes generation): But Christ, etc. Therefore. The minor is proved from Gal.
