Qui namque, ad instar Pauli, inuenitur in Christo, non habens propriam iustitiam, quae ex lege est, sed eam, quae ex fide Christi, is profecto Pharisaeorum ritu non intumescit, sed submisse se gerit, non inflatur, sed quidquid habet benedictionis diuinae, Saluatori suo acceptum refert. e) Gaudium spirituale, quod expressura ecclesia Israelitica canit: Laetando laetabor in Iehouah: exultabit anima mea in Domino meo: quia induit me vestibus salutis, amiculo iustitiae texit me, Es. LXI, 10. f) Gratiarum actio, ad quam nos tam non-imputatio peccatorum, quam imputatio iustitiae Christi excitat, monente Paulo, Col. I, 12. sqq. Gratias agite Patri, qui idoneos fecit nos in partem sortis sanctorum in luce; qui eripuit nos e potestate tenebrarum, & transtulit in regnum Filii dilectionis suae; in quo habemus redemptionem per sanguinem ipsius, remissionem peccatorum.

Quainobrem adstipulamur non hostibus veritatis, negantibus, imputatam Christi iustitiam quicquam momenti ad sincerae pietatis studium conferre, sed Paulo, grauiter inquitienti: Liberi facti a peccato, serui vero facti Deo, habetis fructum vestrum in sanctificationem, Rom. VI, 22.


### Q. XI. Does God also use ministers in the justification of a sinner?: Resolution

RESOLUTION

WEIGELIUS objects part. III. postill. p. 15. 16. It is a terrible error among false Christians that they let another do the law, suffer, and die, and they want to get by without repentance with the Imputativa.

Resp. This is a most virulent and clearly diabolical slander, by which Weigel, a man of brazen face, and his accomplices strive to corrupt and denigrate the religion of the Protestants (*).

But indeed our symbolic books refute that malicious slander. Let them read, I pray, the epitome of the Form. concord. p. 586, where these most memorable words are found: We believe, teach, and confess, although antecedent contrition and subsequent new obedience do not pertain to the article of justification before God: yet such a justifying faith is not to be imagined, which can exist and stand together with an evil purpose, namely, of sinning and acting against conscience.

Let them also read the declarat. p. 688. Therefore, true and saving faith is not in those who lack contrition and have the purpose of continuing and persevering in sins. For true contrition precedes, and justifying faith is in those who truly, not feignedly, perform repentance.

With what face, therefore, do the Weigelians attribute this profane opinion to the Evangelical teachers, that they teach that justifying faith, which neither earnest contrition precedes, nor and should not a new obedience follow? I call the immortal God to witness that Protestant doctors utterly reject and abhor that monster of an opinion. Let us hear the apologist of the Augsburg Confession, defending heavenly truth in most memorable words: "When we speak of such faith, which is not an idle thought, but which delivers from death, and brings forth a new life in hearts, and is the work of the Holy Spirit, it does not stand with mortal sin, but as long as it is present, it brings forth good fruits," p. 71.

II. WEIGELIUS continues: It helps you nothing from the outside, jump high or low, the life of Christ in you must do it, Christ inhabiting, not remaining from the outside. Now the true faith, which is the life of Christ in us, brings with it without any contradiction the being baptized with, the suffering with, the being crucified with, the dying with, the being buried with, the rising with. The essential union must do it, that we have Him spiritually and bodily in us. Where do you remain now with your imputation? You will not be able to cover yourself with it before the wrath of God. Put on Christ, put on the new man, then what Christ has done for you will be imputed to you by grace, otherwise you remain eternally damned with your imputation.

Resp. Weigelius proposes everything confusedly and preposterously. For 1) he opines that the mystical union precedes the imputed righteousness of Christ in the order of nature; but he errs and is deceived. For our iniquities, unless they are forgiven on account of the satisfaction of Christ, divide us from God, Is. LIX, 2.

2) WEIGELIUS confuses the mystical union and sanctification with the formal and relative union of faith. Through the latter, Christ dwells, lives, and works in us; through the former, we apprehend and put on Christ, and appropriate to ourselves the fruit of His satisfactory passion and vicarious fulfillment of the law. That this distinction is solid is evident from Gal. II, 19. 20. "I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me." A Christian is so closely united with Christ through faith that he certainly appropriates to himself the fruit of the crucifixion, no differently than if he had hung on the cross with the Savior in his own person. Thereafter, Christ lives and works in the justified man. Weigelius foolishly calls the mystical union "essential." For a) for this it is required that two incomplete substances coalesce into one complete substance. But in the mystical union, God and man are complete substances; nor is one changed into the other. b) God dwells in us as in temples, I Cor. III, 16. But the inhabitant and the temple are not of one essence. 4) Weigelius errs most gravely by putting renewal before justification, otherwise than Paul teaches, Rom. VI, 22.

III. CHRIST. HOBURGIUS in the apology of the Praetorium p. 202 says: The preachers of today do not want the merit and death of Christ to be alive and powerful in their hearers, but only hold it for a work of imputation, and lay it over all persistent wickedness like a plaster, and thereby whitewash the carnal, luxurious nature of their hearers as with loose lime. Page 204 HOBURGIUS says: It is by no means shadow or lip-work, with which one only whitewashes from the outside, while the damage inside becomes worse and greater. Resp. 1) HOBURGIUS has brought the most atrocious injury upon Protestants, alleging that they teach that the righteousness of Christ is imputed to an impious man remaining in impiety, which they have never asserted, but they teach with great consensus that the subject of the gracious imputation of the righteousness of Christ is a penitent man who believes in Christ.

2) HOBURGIUS labored under such gross ignorance that he did not even understand the force of the word "to impute," opining that it meant the same as "to encrust." But he ought to have known that "to impute" denotes a moral act, whereas "to encrust" denotes a physical act. The confusion of a moral and a physical act cannot but produce a gross error. 3) Through conversion and regeneration, the sinner is intrinsically changed so that he is justifiable, or so that he can be absolved from the guilt of sins while divine justice is preserved; but through justification, he is extrinsically, yet most truly, changed, insofar as he is transferred from a miserable state to a more blessed one.

IV. The Quakers object: The righteousness which we lost through the fall of Adam, that Christ repaired: But inherent righteousness [is that righteousness] &c. Therefore. The major is clear; because whatever we lost through Adam, has been restored through Christ, Rom. V, 15. Resp. 1) The conclusion may be granted in an inclusive sense; because righteousness inherent in the regenerate must be attributed to the merit of Christ. But if it be understood in an exclusive sense; namely, that through Christ inherent righteousness alone and only has been repaired, we deny the major. To its proof we say, that Christ did not only restore that which was lost through Adam, but also acquired for us other goods, or benefits, e.g., penitential conversion, faith leaning upon the merit of Christ, imputed righteousness, brotherhood with Christ, which were not lost. 2) Inherent righteousness is so imperfect and impure that it either blushes before the divine judgment, or melts away like wax. Instance: But the righteousness of Christ is a) external and alien; b) it seems to be only imaginary: Therefore, by it we cannot be denominated righteous before God. Resp. a) The righteousness of Christ imputed is indeed external and alien, with respect to the meritorious cause; yet it is also ours, both by reason of the intention of Christ, by which He merited the same not for Himself, but for us, and by reason of the fiducial appropriation, by which we apprehend and put on Christ the satisfier, and thus appropriate His righteousness to ourselves, and make it our own. b) The righteousness of Christ imputed is real, on account of the real foundation, which is the satisfaction of Christ, and on account of the true and real intention of Christ to procure it for us. And therefore also the estimation and judgment of God, through which the imputation is made, is true and real.

Latin:

ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ

Obiicit WEIGELIVS part. III. postill. p. 15. 16. Ein treslicher Irrsal ist bey den falschen Christen, dass sie einen andern lassen das Gesetz thun, leiden, sterben, und sie wollen ohne Busse sich behelfen mit der Imputatiua.

Resp. Haec est virulentissima & plane diabolica calumnia, qua Weigelius, homo perfrictae frontis, & eius complices religionem Protestantium confurcare & denigrare nituntur (*).

At vero malitiosam illam calumniam refellunt libri nostri symbolici. Legant, quaeso, epitomen Form. concord. p. 586. vbi haec memoratu dignissima habentur verba: Credimus, docemus & confitemur, etsi antecedens contritio, & subsequens noua obedientia ad articulum iustificationis coram Deo non pertinent: non tamen talem fidem iustificantem esse fingendam, quae una cum malo proposito, peccandi videlicet, & contra conscientiam agendi, esse & stare potest.

Legant etiam declarat. p. 688. Quare vera & saluans fides in iis non est, qui contritione carent, & propositum in peccatis pergendi & perseuerandi habent. Vera enim contritio praecedit, & fides iustificans est in iis, qui vere, non ficte paenitentiam agunt.

Qua fronte itaque Weigeliani doctoribus Euangelicis profanam hanc opinionem affingunt, quod doceant, fidem iustificantem, quam nec feria praecedat contritio, nec noua subsequatur obedientia? Testor Deum immortalem, quod doctores Protestantes illud opinionis monstrum auersentur penitus & abominentur. Audiamus apologetam Augustanae confessionis, veritatem coelestem verbis perquam memorabilibus tuentem: Cum de tali fide loquamur, quae non est otiosa cogitatio, sed quae a morte liberat, & nouam vitam in cordibus parit, & est opus Spiritus Sancti, non stat cum peccato mortali, sed tantisper, dum adest, bonos fructus parit, p. 71.

II. Pergit WEIGELIVS: Es hilft dich nichts von aussen, spring hoch, oder nieder, vita Christi in dir muss es thun, Christus inhabitans, non ab extra manens. Nun bringt der wahre Glaube, der da ist vita Christi in uns, mit sich ohne alle Widerrede das conbaptizari, das compati, concrucifigi, commori, consepeliri, das consurgere. Die vnio essentialis muss es thun, dass wir ihn geistlich und leiblich in uns haben. Wo bleibst du nun mit deiner imputatia? Du wirst vorm Zorn Gottes dich nicht damit bedecken können. Indue Christum, ziehe an den neuen Menschen, alsdenn wird dir aus Gnaden imputiret, was Christus für dich gethan hat, sonst bleibest du ewiglich verdammt mit deiner imputatia.

Resp. Omnia confuse & praepostere proponit Weigelius. Nam 1) opinatur, vnionem mysticam ordine naturae praecedere iustitiam Christi imputatam; sed fallit & fallitur. Nam nostrae iniquitates, nisi ob satisfactionem Christi remissae sint, nos inter & Deum diuidunt, Es. LIX, 2.

2) Confundit WEIGELIVS vnionem mysticam & sanctificationem cum vnione fidei formali & relatiua. Per illam Christus in nobis habitat, viuit & operatur; per hanc Christum apprehendimus, & induimus, atque fructum satisfactoriae passionis & impletionis legis vicariae nobis appropriamus. Quam distinctionem solidam esse patet ex Gal. II, 19. 20. Cum Christo crucifixus sum. Viuo autem non amplius ego, sed Christus viuit in me. Christianus per fidem tam arcte cum Christo vnitus est, vt crucifixionis fructum certo sibi appropriet, haud secus, ac si in propria persona cum Saluatore in cruce pependisset. Deinceps Christus in homine iustificato viuit & operatur. Weigelius vnionem mysticam insulse vocat essentialem. Nam a) ad hanc requiritur, vt duae substantiae incompletae in vnam substantiam completam coeant. Ac vero in vnione mystica Deus & homo sunt substantiae completae; neque vna in alteram mutatur. b) Deus habitat in nobis tanquam in templis, I Cor. III, 16. Sed incola & templum non sunt vnius essentiae. 4) Grauissime errat Weigelius, renouationem iustificationi praemittendo, secus, ac docet Paullus, Rom. VI, 22.

III. CHRIST. HOBVRGIVS in apol. Praetorii p. 202. ait: Die heutige Prediger wollen das Verdienst und den Tod Christi in ihren Zuhörern nicht lassen lebendig und kräftig seyn, sondern es nur für ein Imputationswerk halten, und es als ein Pflaster über alle beharrliche Bosheit überlegen, und damit das fleischliche üppige Wesen ihrer Zuhörer als mit losem Kalk übertünchen Pag. 204. ait HOBVRGIVS: Es ist mit nichten Schattenoder Mundwerk, damit man nur von aussen übertünche, da doch der Schade inwendig schlimmer und grösser wird. Resp. 1) HOBVRGIVS atrocissimam iniuriam protestantibus intulit, causatus, eosdem docere, iustitiam Christi homini impio, in impietate manenti, imputari, quod illi nunquam asseruerunt, sed docent magno consensu, subiectum gratiosae imputationis iustitiae Christi esse hominem poenitentem & in Christum credentem.

2) HOBVRGIVS tam crassa laborauit ignorantia, vt ne vim quidem vocis, imputare, intellexeret, opinatus, id valere idem, quod incrustare. At debebat scire, imputare actum moralem, incrustare autem actum physicum denotare. Confusio actus moralis, & physici, non potest non crassum gignere errorem. 3) Per conuersionem & regenerationem peccator intrinsece mutatur, vt sit iustificabilis, siue vt salua iustitia diuina a reatu peccatorum absolui queat; per iustificationem autem extrinsece, verissime tamen mutatur, quatenus e statu misero in beatiorem transfertur. statu misero in beatiorem transfertur.

IV. Quackeri obiiciunt: Quam iustitiam per lapsum Adami amisimus, illam Christus reparauit: Atqui iustitiam inhærentem &c. E. Maior liquet; quia quidquid per Adamum amisimus, per Christum est restitutum, Rom. V, 15. Resp. 1) Conclusio potest concedi in sensu incluso; quia iustitia renatis inhærens merito Christi accepta ferenda est. Sin intelligatur sensu exclusiuo; scilicet quod per Christum vnice & tantum iustitia inhærens sit reparata, negamus maiorem. Ad eius probationem dicimus, quod Christus non id tantum restituerit, quod amissum est per Adamum, sed etiam alia bona, vel beneficia nobis acquisiuerit, v. gr. conuersionem pœnitentialem, fidem merito Christi innixam, iustitiam imputatam, confraternitatem cum Christo, quæ non fuerunt amissa. 2) Iustitia inhærens adeo imperfecta & impura est, vt coram iudicio diuino vel erubescat, vel ceræ instar diffluat. Instantia: Sed iustitia Christi est a) externa & aliena; b) videtur tantum esse imaginaria: E. ab ea coram Deo iusti denominari non possumus. Resp. a) Iustitia Christi imputata est quidem externa & aliena, respectu causæ promerentis; est tamen etiam nostra, tum ratione intentionis Christi, qua non sibi, sed nobis eandem promeruit, tum ratione fiducialis appropriationis, qua satisfactorem Christum apprehendimus & induimus, atque adeo iustitiam eius nobis appropriamus, & nostram facimus. b) Iustitia Christi imputata est realis, ob reale fundamentum, quod est satisfactio Christi, & ob veram & realem intentionem Christi, eam nobis conciliandi. Ideoque etiam æstimatio & iudicium Dei, per quod fit imputatio, verum & reale est.


### Q. XVI. Can righteousness, inherent in the regenerate, stand before the divine tribunal?

Since righteousness inherent in the regenerate is not perfect, nor pure in every part, it cannot sustain the rigorous examination of the divine judgment.

Prob. 1) From I Cor. IV, 4. I am conscious of nothing, yet I am not justified by this. The Apostle proves by his own example that no one is justified by the innocence of life before the censorial judgment of God.

2) From Ps. CXLIII, 3. Enter not into judgment with thy servant: for no one living shall be righteous before thee. David, most adorned with virtues, did not wish to rely upon these before the divine judgment: because God is far more discerning than man in judging.

The antithesis is that of the Papists, Anabaptists, and Socinians, who teach that a man is justified in the sight of the heavenly judge by his own virtues. Their stronger arguments are: I. Judge me, O Lord, according to my righteousness, Ps. VII, 9. Resp. Distinguish between the righteousness of the cause, and of the person. King David understands the righteousness of the cause, or of the fact, because in the case against Saul, by whom he was accused of affecting the kingdom, he was innocent; otherwise the person of David was not immune from sins, as he confesses and deprecates in the psalms in many places.

II. Remember, O Lord, how I have walked before thee in truth and with a perfect heart, and have done what is good in thine eyes, Is. XXXVIII, 3. King Hezekiah seems to appear before the divine tribunal trusting in the innocence of his life. Resp. The passage cited does not treat of the justification of a sinner before God, but of a corporal benefit, namely, liberation from sickness and the danger of death. In dispensing corporal benefits, God indeed regards the holiness of life, Ps. XLI, 2. III. I John III, 7. Little children, let no one deceive you. He who does righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous. Whoever by doing righteousness are righteous, they are justified before God by inherent righteousness: But the regenerate &c. Therefore. Resp. Deny the major. Because doing righteousness is not the cause of justification before God, but its effect, judgment and testimony. The holy man does not act

John does not explain the formal cause of justification, but only who is just, not by what a man is constituted just before the tribunal of God, which happens solely through the obedience of Christ, Rom. 5:19. The Apostle is therefore occupied with the article of sanctification. And so we do not deny that he who does justice is called just intrinsically; primarily, because it is added: as he is just. For those who have been justified before God through faith in Christ, they both do justice, and on account of their zeal for justice are rightly called just. But the perfection of those just ones is not such as is required before the divine tribunal. Objection: They are called just, as he is: Christ is perfectly just: Therefore, they are perfectly just. Response: The particle, as, designates not equality, but similarity, and that not absolute or in every way, but respective and appropriate. We are in need of the remission of sins, Christ is not in need. We are justified as sinners, justification does not apply to Christ.

Question XVII. Are sins completely extirpated in justification?

In justification, the liability of guilt and punishment resulting from sin a), not the stock or root of sin b), is taken away.

Proof a. From Rom. 4:7. Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered. Blessed is the man to whom God does not impute sin. God forgives sins when, out of grace in view of the satisfaction of Christ, apprehended by true faith, he absolves the repenting sinner from the liability of guilt and punishment. He absolves from the liability of guilt when, by a gracious estimation on account of Christ the mediator, whom the sinner embraces by faith, he imputes his justice to him. He absolves from the liability of punishment when, having laid aside his wrath, on account of the imputed passion and death of Christ, he does not think of inflicting punishment. God covers sins with the cloak of mercy and the garment of Christ's imputed justice, so that he may not see them with a practical and judicial vision. He does not impute sins, by abolishing the obligation to punishment (*).

Proof b. 1 John 1:8. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. The justified have original sin with the concupiscences and inordinate motions bursting forth from it; but they do not commit sin by deliberate counsel against their conscience. Whence they pray daily: Forgive us our debts, Matt. 6:12.

The antithesis is that of the Papists, who maintain that sins are extirpated by justification. They urge that God blots out sins, Isa. 44:22, washes them away, Ps. 51:4, cleanses the sinner from all impurities, Ezek. 34:25. Response: God in justification blots out sins by abolishing the liability of guilt and punishment contracted from them: by the benefit of renewal he blots them out, by taking away the dominion of original sin, and by diminishing the remnants of the old man, not by extirpating them.

Latin:

Cum iustitia renatis inhærens non sit perfecta, neque omni ex parte pura, rigorosum iudicii diuini examen sustinere nequit.

Prob. 1) Ex I Cor. IV, 4. Nihil mihi conscius sum, sed in hoc non iustificatus sum. Apostolus exemplo suo comprobat, neminem innocentia vitæ coram censorio Dei iudicio iustificari.

2) E Ps. CXLIII, 3. Ne intra in iudicium cum seruo tuo: quia non iustus erit coram te vllus viuens. Dauid, ornatissimus virtutibus, his coram iudicio diuino nolebat inniti: quia Deus homine longe perspicacior est in censendo.

Antithesis est Pontificiorum, Anabaptistarum & Socinianorum, docentium, hominem in conspectu iudicis cœlestis propriis virtutibus iustificari. Quorum potiora sunt argumenta: I. Iudica me, Domine, secundum iustitiam meam, Ps. VII, 9. Resp. Dist. inter iustitiam causæ, & personæ. Intelligit rex Dauid iustitiam causæ, siue facti, quod in causa aduersus Saulem, a quo affectati regni accusabatur, erat innocens; ceteroqui persona Dauidis non immunis erat a peccatis, vtpote quæ in psalmis passim locorum confitetur & deprecatur.

II. Memento, Domine, quomodo ambulauerim coram te in veritate & corde perfecto, & quod bonum est in oculis tuis, fecerim, Es. XXXVIII, 3. Videtur Rex Hiskias coram tribunali diuino comparare fretus vitæ innocentia. Resp. Agitur loco citato non de iustificatione peccatoris coram Deo, sed de beneficio corporali, nempe liberatione ex morbo & periculo mortis. In corporalibus beneficiis dispenfandis vtique Deus sanctimoniam vitæ respicit Ps. XLI, 2. III. I Io. III, 7. Filioli, nemo seducat vos. Qui facit iustitiam, iustus est, quem ad modum ille influs est. Quicunque faciendo ...iustitiam iusti sunt, illi inhærente iustitia coram Deo iustificantur: Atqui renati &c. E. Resp. Neg. mai. Quia facere iustitiam non est causa iustificationis coram Deo, sed eius effectus, iudicium & testimonium. Non agit S.

Ioannes de caussa formali iustificationis, sed duntaxat, quisnam iustus sit, explicat, non per quod homo coram tribunali Dei iustus constituitur, quod fit vnice per obedientiam Christi Rom. V, 19. Occupatur itaque Apostolus in articulo de sanctificatione. Ideoque non abnuimus, iustum intrinsece dici, qui facit iustitiam; inprimis, quia additur: sicut ille iustus est. Nam qui coram Deo iustificati sunt per fidem in Christum, illi & iustitiam faciunt, & ob studium iustitiæ recte dicuntur iusti. At illorum iustorum perfectio talis non est, qualis coram tribunali diuino requiritur. Instantia: Dicuntur iusti, sicut ille: Christus perfecte iustus est: E. perfecte iusti sunt. Resp. Particula, sicut, non æqualitatem, sed similitudinem, eamque non absolutam, aut omnimodam, sed respectiuam & accommodam designat. Nos indigemus remissione peccatorum, Christus non indiget. Nos ceu peccatores iustificamur, Christo non conuenit iustificatio.

Quæst. XVII. An peccata in iustificatione plane exstirpantur?

In iustificatione reatus culpæ & pœnæ ex peccato resultans a), non stirps, aut radix peccati b) tollitur.

Prob. a. Ex Rom. IV, 7. Beati, quorum remissæ sunt iniquitates, & quorum obtecta sunt peccata. Beatus vir, cui Deus non imputat peccatum. Deus peccata remittit, cum ex gratia intuitu satisfactionis Christi, vera fide apprehensæ, peccatorem resipiscentem a reatu culpæ & pœnæ absoluit. Absoluit a reatu culpæ, cum gratiosa æstimatione propter Christum mediatorem, quem peccator fide amplectitur, illius iustitiam huic imputat. Absoluit a reatu pœnæ, cum deposita ira, propter imputatam Christi passionem & mortem, non cogitat de infligenda pœna. Tegit Deus peccata pallio misericordiæ, & veste iustitiæ Christi imputatæ, ne ea videat visione practica & iudiciali. Non imputat peccata, obligationem ad pœnam abolendo (*).

Prob. b. 1 Io. I, 8. Si dixerimus, nos peccatum non habere, nos ipsos fallimus, & veritas in nobis non est. Habent iustificati peccatum originale cum concupiscentiis & motibus inordinatis ex eo prorumpentibus; sed deliberato consilio contra conscientiam peccatum non faciunt. Vnde quotidie orant: Dimitte nobis debita nostra, Matth. VI, 12.

Antithesis est Pontificiorum, statuentium, peccata iustificatione exstirpari. Vrgent, quod Deus peccata deleat, Es. XLIV, 22. eluat, Ps. LI, 4. peccatorem mundet ab omnibus immunditiis, Ezech. XXXIV, 25. Resp. Deus in iustificatione peccata delet, contractum ex illis reatum culpæ & pœnæ abolendo: beneficio renouationis eadem delet, dominium peccati originalis tollendo, & reliquias veteris hominis imminuendo, non exstirpando.


### Q. XVIII. How is the sinner changed by the benefit of justification?

The sinner is changed by the benefit of justification extrinsically, by reason of status, in so far as he is transferred by God, the most just judge, but reconciled through Christ, from a state of sin and wrath into a state of grace and justice. Obs.

Obs. Obs. I. Through conversion and regeneration, the sinner is changed intrinsically, so that he becomes justifiable, or so that, divine justice being saved, he may be absolved from the guilt of sins; but through justification he is changed extrinsically, yet most truly, insofar as he is judicially transferred from a miserable state into a more blessed one.

Obs.

II. The terminus a quo [starting point] of this extrinsic change is the state of sin and wrath, or the guilt of fault and punishment; because through the guilt of fault and punishment, the sinner remains in the state of sin and wrath.

The terminus ad quem [end point] is the state of grace and justice; because God, having forgiven sins, receives the sinner who believes in Christ into grace, and imputes the justice of Christ to him.

Prob. Justification is a judicial act, and a gracious one, by which God, reconciled by the satisfaction of Christ, absolves the sinner who believes in Christ from the charged crimes, and deems and declares him just.

Since this action is outside of man in God, it cannot change man intrinsically. Therefore, just as a debtor, for whom another pays the debt so that he is considered free from debt, is changed not intrinsically but extrinsically by reason of his status: so the sinner, who on account of the satisfaction of Christ, applied by true faith, is reputed and pronounced free from sins, is not changed intrinsically, but extrinsically, by reason of a better status.

Quæst. XIX. How is justification distinguished?

Division of justification.

Justification is distinguished into primary and continued.

The former is an act of grace by which God, in view of the merit of Christ apprehended by true faith, first absolves the sinner—who is guilty of eternal death but converted and reborn—from sins and their punishments, and by a gracious estimation deems and declares him just.

The latter is an act of grace by which God preserves in the state of justice the man who is penitent and who, by true faith in Christ, continually seeks the remission of sins.

Prob. From Apoc.

XXII, 11. He who is just, let him be justified still.

Which words of John are to be understood concerning the preservation of justification, lest we fall from the same: which happens through heresy and sins against conscience, and thus apostasy from the faith: just as the particle ἔτι signifies "still," so that the sense may be: let him be justified further through perseverance in faith and the non-admission of the contrary, let him remain and persevere in the state of justification: Cf.

CALOV. bibl. illustr. in h. l. f. 1923. Five sacred expressions signify this significantly: α) to cover sins, Ps.

XXXII, 1. β) to blot out Ps.

LI, 3.

11. γ) not to remember, Ezech.

XVIII, 22. δ) to cast into the deep sea, Mich.

VII, 19. ε) to hide and turn away the face from sins, Ps.

LI, 11. XX. What is the end of justification? The end of justification on the part of men, who are justified, is their eternal salvation.

Proof a. From Rom. IV, 6. 9. where justification itself is called μακαρισμὸς, or beatification; namely, that it may befall men for the sake of eternal salvation, the inheritance of which it also confers.

For we who are justified by the grace of God are heirs according to the hope of eternal life, Tit. III, 7. Proof b. God has blessed us with every spiritual blessing (and thus also with the benefit of justification), in Christ, Eph. I, 3. that the glory of His grace might be praised. Paul commends the righteousness of God, Rom. III, 24. 25. We are justified freely by the grace of God through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus; whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in His blood, for the demonstration of His righteousness. God demonstrates His righteousness when He does not forgive sins without satisfaction, but most severely punishes them in His Son, who was made a surety for sinners.

Question. XXI. What are the effects of justification? The effects of justification are adoption as sons of God, our mystical union with God, peace of conscience, the certain hearing of prayers, renewal, and sanctification.

Proof a. From Gal. IV, 4. When the fullness of the time had come, God sent forth His Son, born of a woman, born under the law, to redeem those who were under the law, that we might receive the adoption as sons of God.

Obs. a) that by the Apostle is understood ἐξαγορασμὸς, or satisfactory and meritorious redemption. Christ redeemed us from the law, not by reason of the obligation to perform it, but by reason of the curse, which He transferred onto Himself, Gal. III, 13. b) Since Christ is the Lord of the law, He voluntarily subjected Himself to the law, so that His active obedience might be imputed to us for righteousness, Rom. X, 1. Which imputed righteousness of Christ is followed in the order of nature by adoption as sons of God with the usufruct of all goods that depend on spiritual sonship.

By the benefit of regeneration we are indeed granted ἐξουσία, the right and power, that we may become sons of God, but by means of justification we are actually sons of God: Before justification no one is called a son of God, but in justification itself man rises to such a state, says DANNHAV. in hodof. phaenom.

IX. p. 924. Proof b. From Gal. II, 19. 20. I have been crucified with Christ. It is no longer I who live, but Christ lives in me.

Obs. a) The faithful have been crucified with Christ, insofar as through faith they appropriate the crucifixion of Christ to themselves, so that the penalty which the crucified One took upon Himself might not be imputed to them as the righteousness of the law: because the law, as long as it condemns, does not justify, and it condemns everyone who has deviated from the standard even in one word, Gal. III, 10. add. Jas. III, 2.: because Christ becomes our perpetual sponsor, even in the state of justification, Heb. X, 14. Phil. III, 8-12. where PAUL speaks not only of the past, but also of the condition in which he was now, having long since been born again and renewed.

No less contrary to the clearest sayings is the opinion of those which we reject, among which these two stand out, Ps. CXLIII, 2. David, who and what kind? Certainly pious: Yet he frankly confesses that neither he nor anyone else, even if like a son, is righteous in the divine court, 1 Cor. IV, 4. in which place PAUL differs from himself, professing that he, most studious of true piety and conscious of no voluntary sin, does not think so arrogantly of himself as to persuade himself that he is justified before God by his own piety.

What? That those works which the adversaries think are of the greatest value for making a man righteous before God are not even truly good. Arbitrary worship is, in the highest degree, that to which they think such dignity should be deferred.

be thought. b) Thence flows a spiritual union, through which Christ the author of life lives in the justified.

Prob. c. Therefore, being justified by faith, we have peace toward God through our Lord Jesus Christ, Rom. V, 1. By peace is understood both reconciliation with God; because πρὸς τὸν θεὸν (toward God) is added, and also the quiet and tranquility of conscience; which consists in the sense and certainty of that reconciliation; which peace the justified have through our Lord Jesus Christ, who by his merit has reconciled peace to them, and through faith in Christ, by which they possess and enjoy the peace reconciled through Christ.

Prob. d. From Rom. VIII, 32. He who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all, how shall he not also with him freely give us all things?

He who, unasked, gave the greatest good, his own Son, as a victim for our sins, will certainly give, when asked, the lesser benefits which depend on the merit of Christ. Wherefore let us ask in faith, doubting nothing, Iac. I, 6. Prob. e. From Rom. VI, 22. Having been made free from sin, and having become servants to God, you have your fruit unto sanctification. To those freed from the guilt of sin, the fruit is sanctification.

Latin:

Peccator beneficio iustificationis mutatur extrinsece, ratione status, in quantum a Deo iudice iustissimo, sed per Christum reconciliato, e statu peccati & iræ in statum gratiæ & iustitiæ transfertur. Obs.

Obs. Obs. I. Per conuersionem & regenerationem intrinsece peccator mutatur, vt fit iustificabilis, siue vt salua iustitia diuina, a reatu peccatorum absolui queat; per iustificationem autem extrinsece, verissime tamen, mutatur, quatenus a statu misero in beatiorem iudicialiter transfertur.

Obs.

II. Terminus a quo huius mutationis extrinsecæ est status peccati & iræ, siue reatus culpæ & pœnæ; quia per reatum culpæ & pœnæ peccator in statu peccati & iræ manet.

Terminus ad quem est status gratiæ & iustitiæ; quia Deus peccatorem, in Christum credentem, remissis peccatis in gratiam recipit, & iustitiam Christi ei imputat.

Prob. Iustificatio est actus iudicialis, isque gratiosus, quo Deus, satisfactione Christi reconciliatus, peccatorem, in Christum credentem, ab obiectis criminibus absoluit, & iustum æstimat atque declarat.

Quæ actio cum sit extra hominem in Deo, non potest hominem intrinsece mutare. Sicut igitur debitor, pro quo alius debitum dissoluit, vt liber a debito censeatur, non intrinsece, sed extrinsece, ratione status mutatur: Ita peccator, qui ob satisfactionem Christi, vera fide applicatam, a peccatis liber reputatur & pronuntiatur, non mutatur intrinsece, sed extrinsece, ratione melioris status.

Quæst. XIX. Quomodo distinguitur iustificatio?

Divisio iustificationis.

Iustificatio distinguitur in primam, & continuatam.

Illa est actus gratiæ, quo Deus peccatorem, reum æternæ mortis, sed conuersum & renatum, intuitu meriti Christi, vera fide apprehensi, a peccatis, eorumque pœnis primum absoluit, & gratiosa æstimatione iustum reputat atque declarat.

Hæc est actus gratiæ, quo Deus hominem pœnitentem, & vera in Christum fide iugiter remissionem peccatorum expetentem, in statu iustitiæ conseruat.

Prob. Ex Apoc.

XXII, 11. Qui iustus est, iustificetur adhuc.

Quæ verba Ioannis intelligenda sunt de iustificationis conseruatione, ne excidamus eadem: quod fit per hæresin, & peccata contra conscientiam, adeoque ἀποστασίαν a fidem: quem ad modum particula ἔτι significat adhuc, vt sensus sit: iustificetur porro per fidei perseuerantiam & non-admissionem contrarii, maneat & perseueret in statu iustificationis: Conf.

CALOV. bibl. illustr. in h. l. f. 1923. Quæst. gnificanter indicant quinque locutiones sacræ: α) peccata tegere, Ps.

XXXII, 1. β) delere Ps.

LI, 3.

11. γ) non meminisse, Ezech.

XVIII, 22. δ) in profundum mare deiicere, Mich.

VII, 19. ε) abscondere atque auertere faciem a peccatis, Ps.

LI, 11. XX. Quis est finis iustificationis? Finis iustificationis ex parte hominum, qui iustificantur, est eorum salus aeterna

Prob. a. Ex Rom. IV, 6. 9. vbi iustificatio ipsa dicitur μακαρισμὸς, seu beatificatio; scilicet quod hominibus obtingat salutis aeternae causa, cuius hereditatem ipsa quoque confert.

Etenim iustificati gratia Dei heredes sumus secundum spem vitae aeternae, Tit. III, 7. Prob. b. Benedixit nobis Deus omni benedictione spirituali (adeaque etiam iustificationis beneficio), in Christo, Eph. I, 3. vt laudetur gloria gratiae suae. Iustitiam Dei commendat Paullus, Rom. III, 24. 25. Iustificamur gratis gratia Dei per redemptionem, quae est in Christo Iesu; quem proposuit Deus propitiatorium per fidem in ipsius sanguine, in demonstrationem iustitiae suae. Demonstrat Deus iustitiam suam, dum peccata sine satisfactione non condonat, sed in filio suo vade facto pro peccatoribus seuerissime punit.

Quaest. XXI. Quaenam sunt effecta iustificationis? Effecta iustificationis sunt adoptio in filios Dei , vnio nostri mystica cum Deo , pax conscientiae , certa precum exauditio , renouatio & sanctificatio .

Prob. a. Ex Gal. IV, 4. Quando venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus filium suum, natum ex muliere, factum sub lege, vt eos, qui sub lege erant, redimeret, vt adoptionem filiorum Dei acciperemus.

Obs. a) quod ab Apostolo intelligitur ἐξαγορασμὸς, siue redemtio satisfactoria & meritoria. Redemit Christus nos a lege, non ratione obligationis praestandae, sed ratione maledictionis, quam in se transtulit, Gal. III, 13. b) Cum Christus sit dominus legis, sponte se legi subiecit, vt obedientia eius actiua nobis in iustitiam imputaretur, Rom. X, 1. Quam iustitiam Christi imputatam ordine naturae sequitur adoptio in filios Dei cum vsu fructu omnium bonorum, quae a spirituali filiatione pendent.

Beneficio regenerationis nobis quidem conceditur ἐξουσία, ius & potestas, vt fiamus filii Dei, sed mediante iustificatione actu sumus filii Dei: Ante iustificationem nemo dicitur filius Dei, sed in ipsa iustificatione ad tantam fortem homo assurgit, ait DANNHAV. in hodof. phaenom.

IX. p. 924. Prob. b. Ex Gal. II, 19. 20. Cum Christo crucifixus sum. Viuo autem non amplius ego, sed viuit in me Christus.

Obs. a) Fideles crucifixi sunt cum Christo, quatenus per fidem crucifixionem Christi sibi appropriant, ne poena, quam crucifixus in se deuoluit, ipsis imputetur legis iustitia: quod lex, quam diu damnat, tam diu non iustificet, damnat autem vnum quemque, qui vel vno in verbo deflexerit a uorma, Gal. III, 10. add. Iac. III, 2.: quod Christus fit perpetuus sponsor noster, etiam in statu iustificationis, Hebr. X, 14. Phil. III, 8-12. vbi PAVLLVS loquitur non solum de praeterita, sed de ea etiam, qua nunc erat conditione, iam dudum denuo natus ac renouatus.

Non minus contraria est, quam repudiamus, illorum sententia clarissimis dictis, inter quae eminent hae duo, Ps. CXLIII, 2. Dauid, quis & qualis? Certe pius: Ipse tamen nec se, nec vllum alium, tametsi finii similem, iustum in foro diuino esse, ingenue fatetur, i Corinth. IV, 4. quo in loco PAVLLVS difere de se profitetur, se, verae pietatis studiosissimum, neque vllius peccati voluntarii conscium, non tam arroganter de se sentire, vt sua pietate se coram Deo iustificatum esse, sibi persuadeat.

Quid? Quod ne vere quidem bona sint illa opera, quae ad efficiendum coram Deo iustum hominem plurimum valere, aduersarii arbitrantur. Cultus arbitrarius est vel maxime, cui tantam illi dignitatem deferendam censent.

putetur. b) Inde fluit vnio spiritualis, per quam Christus auctor vitæ in iustificatis viuit.

Prob. c. Iustificati itaque fide, pacem habemus erga Deum per dominum nostrum Iesum Christum, Rom. V, 1. Per pacem tum reconciliatio cum Deo intelligitur; quia additur πρὸς τὸν θεὸν, tum quies & tranquillitas conscientiæ; quæ in sensu & certitudine illius reconciliationis consistit; quam pacem iustificati habent per dominum Iesum Christum, qui merito suo ipsis pacem conciliauit, & per fidem in Christum, qua potiuntur & fruuntur (*) pace per Christum conciliata.

Prob. d. Ex Rom. VIII, 32. Qui & proprio filio non pepercit, sed pro nobis omnibus tradidit illum, quomodo non etiam cum ipso omnia nobis gratificabitur? Qui non rogatus dedit bonum maximum, filium suum, vt victimam pro peccatis nostris, vtique dabit rogatus beneficia minora ex merito Christi pendentia. Quare petamus in fide, nihil addubitantes, Iac. I, 6.

Prob. e. Ex Rom. VI, 22. Liberi facti a peccato, serui vero facti Deo, habetis fructum in sanctificationem. Liberatis a reatu peccati fructus est sanctificatio.


### Q. XVIII. How is the sinner changed by the benefit of justification?: Q. XXII

Q. XXII.

Can a man who is converted and reborn be certain of his justification before God? A man who is converted and reborn is absolutely certain of his present justification a), but he is certain of his future and persevering justification with a hypothetical certainty, if he constantly employs the means of salvation, and avoids proæretic (deliberate) sins b).

Prob. a. 1) On the part of God, the divine promises concerning the remission of sins are universal, Act. X, 43. Io. III, 16. Marc. XVI, 16. Confirmed by divine oath, Ezech. XXXIII, 18. Sealed by the sacraments, as if by seals, Rom. IV, 11. 1 Petr. II, 21. Which universal promises the penitent sinner, believing in Christ, applies to himself with undoubting faith.

2) Every one who is truly reborn, or believing in Christ, feels and experiences in himself the testimony of the Holy Spirit, that he is a son of God, Rom. VIII, 15. He is certain that he cannot be separated from the love of God by any creature, Rom. VIII, 38. He knows in whom he believes, 2 Tim. I, 12. He knows that he has passed from death into life, 1 Ioann. III, 14. He has peace with God, stands in grace, and glories in the hope of the glory of God, Rom. V, 1, 2. Therefore he is certain that he is established in the present state of justification.

Prob. b. From Rom. VIII, 13. If you live according to the flesh, you will die; but if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live. They fall from salvation in whom the works of the flesh reign, since inasmuch as they cannot consist with true faith.

Whence the certainty of future salvation is hypothetical. The antithesis is of the Papists, who maintain that no one is infallibly certain of his own justification before God.

They contend against us with the following arguments: I.

Ecclesiastes IX, 1. 2. Man does not know either love or hatred.

Resp.

The Preacher speaks of the knowledge of love and hatred not as absolute, but as limited, or respective; insofar as love and hatred are estimated from external events, common to the pious and the impious. For in verse 2 he says: the same accident (is) to the just and the impious, to the good and clean, and to the unclean. From this, however, it is not permitted to infer: From no other causes or signs is a man converted and reborn certain of justifying grace.

II. Prov. XX, 9. Who can say: my heart is clean?

Resp.

No one can boast of inherent cleanliness; because it is imperfect, 1 John I, 8.

1 Kings VIII, 46. Yet he can be certain of imputed cleanliness, because he has been cleansed by the blood of Christ.

III. Many penitents have been uncertain of their justification. Job says, ch. IX, 20. If I justify myself, my mouth shall condemn me.

Paul says 1 Cor. IV, 4: I am conscious of nothing, yet I am not hereby justified.

David asks Ps. XIX, 13: who understands his errors? Resp.

These sayings prove the imperfection of inherent justice, by which a sinner cannot rely or stand before the rigid judgment of God; otherwise these holy men were certain of the gratuitous remission of sins.

Job in his temptation did not wish to bring the justice of works to divine examination, relying on the sole divine mercy founded in his Redeemer, ch. XIX, 25.

Paul was conscious to himself of the faithfulness performed in his apostolic office, yet he did not pronounce himself immune from every defect if he were to be brought to the tribunal of the omniscient judge, but he found his justice in Christ, Phil.

III, 9. David complains of sins of memory not occurring to him, for whose pardon he seeks, and by seeking is rendered certain of the remission of sins, Ps. XXXII, 4. IV.

Sacred scripture teaches us to doubt concerning the remission of sins, Joel II, 4. Who knows if he will turn and repent?

Dan. IV, 24.

Perhaps God will forgive your sins.

Resp. The prophets Joel and Jonah speak not of the remission of sins, but of the removal of temporal chastisement, which in the justified is not punishment (τιμωρία), but discipline (παιδεία).

God pardoned David's adultery, yet he chastised him with the death of the son born of it, 2 Kings XII, 18. The words of Daniel in the Vulgate version are poorly expressed; in the original text they stand thus: if there shall be a lengthening of your tranquility.

The Chaldean הֵן never signifies perhaps.

V. Objection: But the Apostle Peter taught Simon Magus to doubt concerning the remission of sins, Acts VIII, 22. Repent of this wickedness, and pray to God, if perhaps the thought of your heart may be forgiven you.

Resp. In the Greek text there is the particle, ἄρα, which is not always of one doubting, but often of one asserting.

Whence it is rendered by D. Seb. Schmid, Verily. Furthermore, the question is concerning that certainty by which a penitent sinner is certain of his own, not another's, justification.

Simon was a malicious man, whom St. Peter was exhorting to serious repentance. VI.

Whoever are always fearful, and work out their salvation with fear and trembling, they are not certain of their salvation: But faithful men, etc.

Therefore. The major is evident: because fear and trembling cannot consist with certainty.

The minor is clear from Prov.

XXVIII, 14. Blessed is the man who is always fearful.

Phil.

II, 14. Work out your salvation with fear and trembling.

Resp. Distinguish between servile fear and filial fear.

The former, not the latter, is repugnant to the certainty of faith. Filial fear is opposed to carnal security, not to the full assurance (πληροφορία) of faith.

It becomes the reborn to have a fear of vigilance, of prudence, and of caution, lest the celestial Deity be offended by more grievous sins, and that the hope of future salvation, of which we are certain not absolutely, but hypothetically, should fall away.

what I, or he, believe with firm faith, is not revealed: Therefore. I answer by limiting the major premise. Whatever we hold by divine faith, that is either revealed αὐτολεξεὶ (in the very words), or deduced by valid consequence from revelation. Thus the minor premise is denied. For this is revealed: To everyone who believes in Christ, sins are forgiven, Acts 10:43. I subsume: I believe in Christ: Therefore. I prove the minor premise from all the criteria (κριτηρίοις) of true faith, concerning which [we speak] below.

VII. That certainty of justification begets pride, or sluggishness in exercising good works. I answer: If we were to trust in inherent righteousness, we would certainly be proud; but we rely on the righteousness of Christ, which we receive with the hand of faith, as beggars, and are thus obligated to the most humble thanksgiving. Moreover, true faith, which justifies, is not sluggish in working, but living and efficacious; since it works through love, Galatians 5:6.

Latin:

Quæst. XXII. Potestne homo conuersus & renatus suæ coram Deo iustificationis esse certus?

Homo conuersus & renatus præsentis iustificationis absolute certus est a), at futuræ & perseuerantis iustificationis certus est certitudine hypothetica, si media salutis constanter adhibeat, & peccata proæretica evitet b).

Prob. a. 1) Ex parte Dei promissiones diuinæ de peccatorum remissione sunt vniuersales, Act. X, 43. Io. III, 16. Marc. XVI, 16. Iuramento diuino confirmatæ, Ezech. XXXIII, 18. Sacramentis, velut sigillis, obsignatæ, Rom. IV, 11. 1 Petr. II, 21. Quas promissiones vniuersales peccator pœnitens, & in Christum credens, sibi non dubitante fide applicat.

2) Omnis vere renatus, seu in Christum credens, sentit & experitur in se testimonium Spiritus S., quod sit filius Dei, Rom. VIII, 15. Certus est, quod per nullam creaturam a dilectione Dei separari queat, Rom. VIII, 38. Scit, in quem credit, 2 Tim. I, 12. Scit, se ex morte in vitam transiuisse 1 Ioann. III, 14. Habet pacem cum Deo, stat in gratia, & gloriatur super spe gloriæ Dei, Rom. V, 1, 2. Ergo certus est, se constitutum esse in præsenti statu iustificationis.

Prob. b. Ex Rom. VIII, 13. Si secundum carnem viuitis, moriemini; si vero spiritu actiones corporis mortificatis, viuetis. Excidunt salute, in quibus opera carnis regnant, quippe quae cum vera fide consistere nequeunt.

Vnde certitudo futurae salutis est hypothetica. Antithesis est Pontificiorum, statuentium, neminem coram Deo iustificationis suae infallibiliter certum esse.

Dimicant aduersus nos sequentibus argumentis: I.

Ecclesiastes IX, 1. 2. Tam amorem, quam odium non est sciens homo.

Resp.

Loquitur ecclesiastes de nscientia amoris & odii non absoluta, sed limitata, siue respectiua; quatenus aestimatur amor & odium ex euentibus externis, piis & impiis communibus. Nam versu 2. inquit: idem accidens (est) iusto & impio, bono mundoque, atque immundo. Exinde tamen colligere non licet: Ex nullis aliis caussis, aut indiciis homo conuersus & renatus gratiae iustificantis certus est.

II. Prou. XX, 9. Quis potest dicere: mundum est cor meum?

Resp.

Nemo potest gloriari munditie inhaerente; quia est illa imperfecta, 1 Io.

I, 8. 1 Reg. VIII, 46. Potest tamen certus esse munditiei imputatae, propterea, quod sanguine Christi emundatus est.

III. Multi poenitentes iustificationis suae fuerunt incerti. Iobus inquit, cap. IX, 20. Si iustificauero me, os meum condemnabit me.

Paullus 1 Cor. IV, 4. inquit: Nihil mihi conscius sum, sed in hoc non sum iustificatus. Dauid Ps.

XIX, 13. quaerit: delicta quis intelligit? Resp.

Hae dicta probant imperfectionem iustitiae inhaerentis, qua peccator coram rigido Dei iudicio non potest niti aut consistere; ceteroqui sancti hi viri gratuitae peccatorum remissionis fuerunt certi.

Iobus in tentatione iustitiam operum ad examen diuinum nolebat adducere, nixus sola misericordia diuina fundata in Goële suo, c.

XIX, 25. Paullus sibi conscius erat fidelitatis in munere apostolico praestitae, neque tamen se immunem pronuntiabat ab omni defectu, si fiatatur ad tribunal iudicis omniscii, sed iustitiam suam inueniebat in Christo, Phil.

III, 9. Dauid conqueritur de peccatis memoriae non fuccurrentibus, quorum veniam expetit, expetendo certus redditur remissionis peccatorum, Ps. XXXII, 4. IV.

Sacra scriptura nos docet dubitare de remissione peccatorum, Ioël II, 4. Quis scit, si conuertatur & poeniteat eum?

Dan.

IV, 24. Forsitan ignoscet Deus delictis tuis. Resp.

Prophetae Ioël & Ionas loquuntur non de remissione peccatorum, sed ablatione castigationis temporalis, quae in iustificatis non est τιμωρία, sed παιδεία.

Deus condonauit adulterium Dauidi, castigauit tamen eum morte filii, ex ipso geniti, 2 Reg. XII, 18. Verba Danielis in vulgata versione male sunt expressa, in textu originali ita se habent: si futura fit diuturnitas tranquillitatis tuae.

Chaldaicum הֵן nunquam significat forsitan.

V. Instantia: Sed Apostolus Petrus docebat Simonem Magum dubitare de remissione peccatorum, Act. VIII, 22. Poenitentiam age ob malitiam hanc, & ora Deum, si forte remittatur tibi cogitatio cordis tui.

Resp. in graeco textu est particula, ἄρα, quae non semper est dubitantis, sed saepe asseuerantis.

Vnde a D. SEB. SCHMIDIO redditur, Vtique. Ceterum quaeritur de certitudine ea, qua peccator poenitens suae, non alienae iustificationis certus est.

Simon malitiosus erat homo, quem S. Petrus ad feriam resipiscentiam cohortabatur. VI.

Quicunque semper sunt pauidi, & salutem suam operantur cum timore & tremore, illi non sunt salutis suae certi: Atqui homines fideles &c.

E. Maior constat: quia timor & tremor cum certitudine non potest consistere.

Minor liquet ex Prou.

XXVIII, 14. Beatus homo, qui semper est pauidus.

Phil.

II, 14. Operamini salutem vestram cum timore & tremore. Resp.

Dist. inter timorem seruilem, & filialem.

Ille, non hic certitudini fidei repugnat. Timor filialis opponitur carnali securitati, non fidei πληροφορία.

Decet renatos timor vigilantiae, prudentiae & cautionis, ne offendatur Numen coeleste peccatis grauioribus, & spes futurae salutis, cuius non absolute, sed hypothetice certi sumus, decollet.

quod ego, aut ille, firma fide credimus, non est revelatum: E. Resp. limitando maiorem. Quidquid fide divina tenemus, illud aut αὐτολεξεὶ est revelatum, aut per validam consequentiam ex revelatione deductum. Sic negatur minor. Nam hoc est revelatum: Omni in Christum credenti peccata remittuntur, Act. X, 43. Subsumo: Ego credo in Christum: E. Minorem probo ex omnibus veræ fidei κριτηρίοις, de quibus infra. VII.

Illa iustificationis certitudo parit superbiam, aut torporem in exercendis bonis operibus. Resp. Si inhærenti iustitiæ confideremus, vtique foremus superbi; sed nitimur iustitia Christi, quam manu fidei, mendica recipimus, atque adeo obligamur ad humillimam gratiarum actionem. Ceterum vera fides, quæ iustificat, non est torpida in operando, sed viva & efficax; quippe quæ per caritatem operatur, Gal. V, 6.


### Q. XVIII. How is the sinner changed by the benefit of justification?: Sigh

SIGH.

I station myself at your tribunal, O eternal God, most high judge! Since you are an omniscient judge, nothing is closed to you, nothing abstruse, nothing veiled. While you are also a most just judge, nothing stands before your sight except what is holy, pure, and refined. Wherefore, the imperfect righteousness inherent in us blushes at the rigor of your law and melts like wax. Because of this, remembering my sins, I do not cover them with silence, or dissimulate, but openly confess that I am guilty of many crimes, guilty of eternal death. But as a suppliant I flee to the altar of mercy, and I embrace the throne of your grace! Look, O most merciful Father, upon the most precious blood which your only-begotten Son shed for me; behold his death, which he underwent for me, that he might satisfy your offended justice! This death of my mediator, as a most valid ransom (λύτρον), I apprehend with the hand of faith, I claim for myself, and I present it to you, O best Father, most greatly, most humbly beseeching that you most clemently grant me its fruit! Blot out, I beseech you, my debts from your ledger, and obliterate them with the red of the Redeemer's blood: derive into me the righteousness of Christ, which he procured for me by most exactly fulfilling your law, so that, my debts being paid, I may be accounted free, clothed in the righteousness of Christ, just, received into grace, your friend, your son, and heir of heaven by your most gracious estimation!

Latin:

SVSPIRIVM.

Sisto me ad tribunal tuum, o Deus æterne, iudex celsissime! Cum tu sis iudex omnisciens, nil tibi clausum, nil abstrusum, nil velatum est. Dum etiam sis iudex iustissimus, coram conspectu tuo nil, nisi sanctum, purum, defecatum consistit. Quare imperfecta nobis inhærens iustitia ad rigorem legis tuæ erubescit & ceræ instar diffluit. Quod subinde recordatus peccata mea non tego silentio, aut dissimulo, sed aperte fateor, me esse reum multorum criminum, reum æternæ mortis. Sed supplex confugio ad aram misericordiæ, & complector thronum gratiæ tuæ! Aspice, o pater misericordissime, sanguinem pretiosissimum, quem filius tuus vnigenitus, pro me effudit; intuere mortem ipsius, quam pro me oppetiit, vt læsæ iustitiæ tuæ faceret satis! Hanc mediatoris mei mortem vt λύτρον validissimum manu fidei apprehendo, mihi vindico, tibique, Pater optime, maxime exhibeo, humillime obtestans, vt illius fructum mihi clementissime indulgeas! Dele, obsecro, debita mea e rationario tuo, eaque oblittera minio sanguinis redemptoris: iustitiam Christi, quam pro me, legem tuam exactissime implendo, mihi peperit, in me deriva, vt solutis debitis, liber, indutus iustitia Christi, iustus, receptus in gratiam, amicus tuus, filius tuus, & heres cœli censear æstimatione tua gratiosissima!


## 24 On Inhabiting Grace, and the Mystical Union


### Question II. How many-fold is the union of God with men?

Mystical union is the spiritual conjunction of the Triune God with the justified man, by which He dwells in this as in a consecrated temple by a special, and that substantial, presence, and works in the same by a gracious influx.

It is described more fully: Mystical union is an act of applying grace, by which the Triune God, out of special love, in view of the merit of Christ, apprehended by true faith, dwells in the reborn and justified man, as in a consecrated temple, by a substantial presence, fills the same with all the fullness of gifts, and works in him by a special concurrence, so that, cerof present grace & future glory, may persevere in communion with Christ and the church, be sanctified, and be saved eternally.

Obs.

Obs. I. The moment of mystical union is entirely the same as the moment of regeneration, justification, and renovation; for all these ἀποτελέσματα (effects) occur simultaneously and in an instant; for as soon as a man is regenerated and justified, by that very fact he is also joined to God and united with Him.

And yet one is prior to the other, according to our mode of conceiving, on account of different connotations.

Thus, regeneration and justification are prior to that union, as it is something that finally exists from faith and after faith has been received in regeneration: and sins, unless they are remitted, hinder the gracious union, Is.

LIX, 2. But the mystical union is prior to renovation: for from the effects of the latter, namely good works, as from what is posterior, I can know the existence of the former, I John

III, 6. 23.

24. ch. IV, 12.

13. See

KOENIGII theol. positiva p. 212.

Obs.

Obs. II. Although the mystical union, by which God dwells in the soul as in a temple, follows justification in the order of nature according to our mode of conceiving; yet it must be admitted that the formal union of faith, by which Christ is apprehended, put on, and united with us as mediator and author of the grace and remission of sins to be obtained, is prior to justification in the sign of reason.

For faith is imputed for righteousness, insofar as it receives the merit of Christ and unites it with us, so that it becomes ours.

Confer.

D. QVENSTED. part.

Confer. D. QVENSTED. part. III. system. fol. 524. D. clearly teaches this.

BROCHMAND. T.

BROCHMAND. T. II. system. p. 485. But if regeneration is taken for that spiritual birth from God, which consists primarily in the union of ourselves with Christ; it differs from justification, as a cause from its effect.

For we are justified because we are from God, or because we are in Christ, according to that of Paul, Rom.

VIII, 1. There is no condemnation to those who are in Christ Jesus.

The righteousness of Christ, as the spiritual head, is imputed to believers, who are most closely united with Him, and who are found in Him as members, Phil.

III, 9. Cf.

D.

D. LYSERVS in syst. p. 1548. Quest.

II. How manifold is the union of God with men?

Quest. II. How manifold is the union of God with men? The union of God with men is twofold: a) general, by which all men, faithful and unfaithful, live, move, and have their being in God: b) special, and that either gracious, by which God dwells by substantial presence in the reborn who still live in the militant church, and works in them by a special concurrence, c), or glorious, by which God fills and satisfies the elect in the triumphant church with the fullness of His grace.

Proof a.

From Acts XVII, 28.

In Him we live, move, and have our being.

As fish in water and birds in the air: so all men live, move, and have their being in God, in that He gives to all life and breath and all things, v. 25. Proof b.

From John XIV, 23.

If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our abode with him. In the phraseology of Scripture, God does not dwell in the unfaithful or the impious, but in the reborn and justified, who love Christ and keep His word.

For God, reconciled to man, joins Himself to him as a friend to a friend, and converses with him intimately and familiarly.

Whence Abraham is called by God Himself אהבי (my friend), Is.

XLI, 8. Proof c.

In the triumphant church, God will be all in all.

For in eternal life, God will not deal with the blessed mediately; He will not enlighten them through the word and sacraments, He will not teach them through ministers, He will not rule them through princes, He will not defend them through angels, but He will do all things in all immediately.

There God will be the most splendid light to the intellect, the highest good to the will, the sweetest joy to the appetite; He Himself will be the teacher, king, and protector of the blessed, in knowing and celebrating whom they will entirely exist.

Rev. XXI, 3.

4. XXII, 5.

Latin:

Unio mystica est coniunctio spiritualis Dei trinunius cum homine iustificato, qua in hoc velut consecrato templo præsentia speciali, eaque substantiali habitat, & gratioso influxu in eodem operatur.

Plenius describitur: Unio mystica est actus gratiæ applicatricis, quo Deus trinunus, ex speciali amore, intuitu meriti Christi, vera fide apprehensi, in homine renato atque iustificato, velut consecrato templo, præsentia substantiali habitat, omni plenitudine donorum eundem implet, & in ipso speciali concursu operatur, vt, certus de praesente gratia & futura gloria, in communione cum Christo & ecclesia perseveret, sanctificetur, & aeternum salvetur.

Obs.

Obs. I. Momentum unionis mysticae cum momento regenerationis, iustificationis & renovationis idem omnino est; fiunt enim haec ἀποτελέσματα omnia simul & in instanti; simul ac enim homo regeneratur & iustificatur, ea ipso etiam Deo coniungitur, & cum ipso vnitur.

Et tamen unum altero prius est, quoad nostrum concipiendi modum ob diversa connotata.

Sic regeneratio & iustificatio priores sunt unione ista, utpote quae ex fide & post fidem in regeneratione acceptam demum est: & peccata, nisi remittantur, impediunt unionem gratiosam, Es.

LIX, 2. Unio autem mystica prior est renovatione: ex huius namque effectibus, bonis scil. operibus, tanquam e posteriori, existentiam illius possum cognoscere, I Io.

Obs. II. Quamvis unio mystica, qua Deus in anima velut templo habitat, nostro concipiendi modo iustificationem sequatur ordine naturae; fatendum tamen est, unionem formalem fidei, qua apprehenditur, induitur, & nobiscum unitur Christus, ut mediator & auctor impetrandae gratiae & remissionis peccatorum, in signo rationis priorem esse iustificatione.

Fides enim ad iustitiam imputatur, quatenus meritum Christi recipit, & nobiscum vnit, vt fiat nostrum.

Nam iustificamur, quia ex Deo sumus, sive quia in Christo sumus, iuxta illud Pauli Rom.

VIII, 1. Nihil condemnationis est in his, qui sunt in Christo Iesu.

Iustitia Christi, tanquam capitis spiritualis, imputatur credentibus, arctissime cum ipso vnitis, qui velut membra in ipso inueniuntur, Phil.

II. Quotuplex est unio Dei cum hominibus?

Quaest. II. Quotuplex est unio Dei cum hominibus? Unio Dei cum hominibus est duplex: a) generalis, qua omnes homines fideles & infideles in Deo vivunt, mouentur & sunt: b) specialis, eaque vel gratiosa, qua Deus substantiali praesentia in renatis in ecclesia militante adhuc degentibus habitat, & speciali concursu in iisdem operatur, c), vel gloriosa, qua Deus electos in ecclesia triumphante plenitudine gratiae suae implet, & exfatiat.

Prob. a.

Ex Act. XVII, 28.

In ipso vivimus, mouemur & sumus.

Vt pisces in aqua & aves in aere: ita omnes homines in Deo vivunt, mouentur & sunt, eo, quod ipse dat omnibus vitam & spiritum & omnia, v. 25. Prob. b.

Ex Io. XIV, 23.

Si quis dilexerit me, verbum meum servabit, & pater meus diliget illum, & ad illum veniemus, & mansionem apud illum faciemus. Phrasi scripturae non habitat Deus in infidelibus, aut impiis, sed in renatis & iustificatis, qui Christum diligunt; & verbum eius servant.

Deus enim homini reconciliatus, vt amicus amico sese coniungit, intimeque & familiariter cum ipso conversatur.

Vnde Abraham a Deo ipso vocatur אהבי amicus meus, Es.

XLI, 8. Prob. c.

In ecclesia triumphante Deus erit omnia in omnibus.

In vita namque aeterna Deus cum beatis non aget mediate, non illuminabit eos per verbum & sacramenta, non docebit per ministros, non reget per principes, non defendet per angelos, sed omnia in omnibus aget immediate.

Erit ibi Deus intellectui lux splendidissima, voluntati summum bonum, appetitui gaudium dulcissimum; ipse erit beatorum doctor, rex, protector, in quo cognoscendo & celebrando toti erunt.

Apoc. XXI, 3.

4. XXII, 5.


### Q. III. Why is this union called mystical and spiritual?

This union is called mystical because it is an astonishing mystery that the immense and infinite God dwells in the human heart . It is called spiritual because it is perfected through the Holy Spirit, who graciously indwells the regenerate, not in a carnal or bodily way, but in a spiritual and supernatural manner .

Proved a. From Eph. V, 32: "This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church." It is called a great mystery because the specific mode of this union is inscrutable.

Proved b. From 1 Cor. VI, 17: Ὁ δὲ κολλώμενος, "but he who adheres," is glued, "to the Lord, is one spirit." The Apostle had said in v. 16 that everyone who adheres to a harlot becomes one flesh with her; now, however, in v. 17, he asserts that he who adheres to Christ is one spirit with Him, i.e., he coheres with the Lord through one and the same Holy Spirit, and is moved and ruled by one and the same Spirit.

Latin:

Unio haec dicitur mystica ideo, quod stupendum est mysterium, quod Deus immensus & infinitus in corde humano habitat . Spiritualis appellatur; quoniam per Spiritum S. gratiose inhabitantem renatos non carnali, aut corporali, sed spirituali & supernaturali modo perficitur .

Prob. a. Ex Eph. V, 32. Mysterium hoc magnum est: ego vero loquor inter Christum & ecclesiam, Mysterium magnum vocatur; quia huius unionis modus specificus est imperscrutabilis.

Prob. b. Ex 1 Cor. VI, 17. Ὁ δὲ κολλώμενος, qui vero adhaeret, conglutinatus est, Domino, unus Spiritus est. Dixerat Apostolus, v. 16. omnem adhaerentem scorto cum eo fieri unam carnem, iam vero v. 17. asserit, adhaerentem Christo cum eo unum esse spiritum, i. e. per unum eundemque Spiritum S. cum domino cohaerere, per unum eundemque Spiritum agi & regi.


### Q. IV. In how many ways is the name of mystical union taken?

The term mystical union sometimes denotes the transient act of applying grace, by which God is mystically joined with the faithful; at other times, it designates the state or bond of God, graciously united with the faithful, which remains permanent.

We observe the former signification here primarily. Proved. At present, we are occupied with explaining the acts of God’s applying grace: therefore, union here signifies the same as "uniting," or the act of union, which is transient and momentary, and occurs at the same moment as regeneration and justification, although in our mode of understanding, it occurs after both; however, the state of union, which is properly and specifically called union, remains intact as long as the justified man avoids proeretic sins.

Latin:

Terminus unionis mysticae interdum notat actum transeuntem gratiae applicatricis, quo Deus cum fidelibus mystice iungitur: interdum designat statum, vel copulam Dei, cum fidelibus gratiose vniti, permanentem.

Priorem significationem hic potissimum obseruamus. Prob. In praesenti occupati sumus in actibus gratiae diuinae applicatricis explicandis: Ideoque unio idem hic valet, quod vnitio, siue actus unionis, qui est transiens & momentaneus, & fit eodem momento, quo regeneratio & iustificatio, quamuis vtraque nostro intelligendi modo fit posterior: status vero unionis, qui proprie & specifice dicitur unio, integer permanet, quamdiu homo iustificatus peccata proeretica euitat.


### Question III. Why is this union called mystical and spiritual?

Synonymy.

There are elegant periphrases in Holy Scripture by which the mystical union is described. For it is called the betrothal of believers with Christ , the mystical marriage of Christ and the church , the conjunction of members and the head , the grafting of spiritual branches into the spiritual vine, Christ , and the dwelling of the entire Holy Trinity with the regenerate man .

Proved a. From Hos. II, 19: "I will betroth you to me forever." This is a spiritual and evangelical promise, by which God promises that He will be joined with us by the bond of betrothal.

God the Father procures the betrothal, Matt. XXII, 2. The Son of God is the bridegroom, John III, 29. The earnest and pledge of love is the Holy Spirit, 2 Cor. I, 22. Therefore, this spiritual betrothal can be attributed to all three persons of the Godhead; yet it is appropriated, or claimed by a peculiar reason, for the Son of God; because as a bridegroom and bride are united in body and soul, so that they become one flesh and one soul; so the Son of God willed to be joined to us both by reason of the flesh, while He assumed our flesh into the unity of His person and coupled it to Himself, and through the incarnation betrothed Himself to us; and then by reason of the Spirit, because He communicates His Spirit to us, and unites and joins our spirit to His, so that we become one spirit with the Lord, 1 Cor. VI, 17. This betrothal was made forever; for the reason that it is indissoluble on the part of the bridegroom, Christ; on the part of the bride, or our soul, it ought to be perpetual.

Latin:

Synonymia. Dantur elegantes periphrases in sacra scriptura, quibus unio mystica describitur.

Vocatur enim desponsatio credentium cum Christo , mysticum Christi & ecclesiae coniugium , membrorum & capitis coniunctio , insitio palmitum spiritualium in viti spirituali Christo , mansio totius SS. Trinitatis apud hominem renatum .

Prob. a. Ex Hos. II, 19. Desponsabo te mihi in aeternum. Est haec promissio spiritualis ac euangelica, qua Deus pollicetur, se vinculo desponsationis nobiscum coniunctum iri.

Desponsationem procurat Deus Pater, Matth. XXII, 2. Filius Dei est sponsus, Io. III, 29. Arrha & pignus amoris est Spiritus S. 2 Cor. I, 22. Potest itaque haec spiritualis desponsatio omnibus tribus personis diuinitatis tribui: appropriatur tamen, siue peculiari ratione vindicatur, Filio Dei; quia vt sponsus & sponsa corporibus & animis vniuntur, vt vna caro, & vna sint anima; ita Filius Dei nobis iungi voluit cum ratione carnis, dum nostram carnem in vnitatem suae personae assumsit, sibique copulauit, & per incarnationem se nobis desponfauit; tum ratione Spiritus; quia Spiritum suum nobis communicat, & nostrum suo vnit ac coniungit, vt fimus vnus Spiritus cum Domino, 1 Cor. VI, 17. Facta est haec desponsatio in aeternum; ideo, quod indissolubilis est ex parte sponsi Christi; ex parte sponsae, siue animae nostrae, perpetua esse debet.


### Question VI. Who perfects the mystical union?

Prob. b. From Eph. V, 32. A man shall leave his father and mother, and shall be joined unto his wife, and they two shall be one flesh. This is a great mystery: but I speak concerning Christ and the church. Bodily marriage shadows forth the mystical union of Christ with the church. For just as the marital bond is most intimate, and greater than that which exists between parents and children, to be dissolved only by the force of death: so Christ has joined the church to Himself by such a firm covenant, that for its sake He went forth from the Father, and came into the world, by putting on our flesh. And just as marriage brings about a communion of name, honor, and goods: so the church is called Christian from this King Christ, and becomes a participant both in the grace of Christ in this age, and in the glory in the age to come.

Prob. c. From Eph. V, 23. Christ is the head of the church, and He is the savior of the body. The members of the body are connected with the head through the intervention of certain ligaments: so the members of the church are joined with Christ through the ligaments of the word, the sacraments, and faith. Just as sense, life, and motion flow down from the head into the members: so spiritual life, the salvation of the soul, the sense of faith, and every motion of good descend from Christ into Christians.

Prob. d. From John XV, 5. I am the vine; you are the branches. He who abides in me, and I in him, he bears much fruit. The branches are in the vine in such a way that they do not contribute to the vine, but receive from it that by which they live; but the vine is in the branches in such a way that it supplies vital nourishment to them, and does not receive it from them, as AUGUSTINE says in tract. LXXXI on John. By a similar reasoning, Christians are in Christ, not so that they may impart any good to Him, but so that they may receive grace for grace from His fullness, John I, 16. And Christ is in Christians in such a way that He gives them of His Spirit, 1 John IV, 13, that is, that He fills them with the gifts of the Holy Spirit. Prob. e. If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him and we will come to him, and make our abode with him, John XIV, 23. FULGENTIUS explains these words concisely in book II to Trasimundus, ch. 3. The Father, Son, and Holy Spirit know how to come and how to depart in such a way that they neither come to a place locally, nor depart from a place locally. The Trinity fills all things, contains all things: it is said to come to him to whom it deigns to manifest itself, and it departs from him from whom it hides the light of its love: yet it is not rendered locally absent when it justly leaves the unworthy: nor is it rendered locally present when it mercifully visits him whom it has made worthy.

Furthermore, the Holy Trinity remains with us by a special presence, by illuminating us more and more, by justifying us from sins from time to time, by sanctifying, by protecting, and by assisting us in every necessity.

Quæst. VI. Who perfects the mystical union? The efficient cause of the mystical union is the triune God, the Father a), the Son of God b), and the Holy Spirit c). Prob. a. From Eph. I, 17. 22. The God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, gave Him as head over all things to the church, which is His body, who fills all in all. God the Father is the fountain and root of the mystical union; inasmuch as He appointed Christ as the head of the church to this end, that He might not only govern it by the rite of a prince, but that He might be joined to it like a head connected with its members, be most present to it, and diffuse spiritual life with the powers of acting into the whole mystical body and its true members.

Prob. b. That the mystical union takes its origin from the Son of God is clear from the fact that the Son of God espouses the church to Himself, Hos. II, 19, is coupled with it just as a husband with a wife, Eph. V, 31, adheres to it as a head with its body, as a spiritual body, Eph. I, 23. Christians are in Him, as a branch in the vine, John XV, 5. And together with the Father, He makes His abode with them, John XIV, 23.

Latin:

Prob. b. Ex Eph. V, 32. Relinquet homo patrem suum & matrem, & adhærebit uxori suæ, & erunt duo in carnem unam. Mysterium hoc magnum est: ego vero loquor in Christum & ecclesiam. Coniugium corporale adumbrat mysticam Christi cum ecclesia unionem. Vt enim arctissimus est nexus coniugalis, maiorque illo, qui versatur inter parentes & liberos, sola vi mortis dissoluendus: ita Christus tam firmo fœdere sibi sociauit ecclesiam, vt eius gratia a Patre exiuerit, & in mundum, carnem nostram induendo, venerit. Et vt coniugium infert communionem nominis, honoris & bonorum: ita ecclesia a Christo Christiana ab hoc rege dicitur, & fit particeps tum gratiæ Christi in hoc seculo, tum gloriæ in seculo futuro.

Prob. c. Ex Eph. V, 23. Christus est caput ecclesiæ, idemque est seruator corporis. Membra corporis connexa sunt cum capite, interuentu certorum ligamentorum: ita membra ecclesiæ coniunguntur cum Christo per ligamenta verbi, sacramentorum & fidei. Sicut sensus, vita & motus defluit a capite in membra: ita vita spiritualis, salus animæ, sensus fidei, omneque boni motus descendunt a Christo in Christianos.

Prob. d. Ex Io. XV, 5. Ego sum vitis; vos palmites. Qui manet in me, & ego in illo, hic fert fructum multum. Ita in vite palmites sunt, vt viti non conferant, sed inde accipiant, vnde viuant; ita vero vitis est in palmitibus, vt vitale alimentum subministret eis, non accipiat ab eis, dicente AVGVSTINO tract. LXXXI. in Io. Pari ratione Christiani sunt in Christo, non vt quidquam boni illi impertiant, sed vt ex eius plenitudine accipiant gratiam pro gratia, Io. I, 16. Et Christus sic est in Christianis, vt illis det de Spiritu suo, 1 Io. IV, 13. h. e. vt donis Spiritus S. illos impleat. Prob. e. Si quis dilexerit me, verbum meum seruabit, & Pater meus deliget illum & ad illum veniemus, & mansionem apud illum faciemus, Io. XIV, 23. Quæ verba concinne exponit FVLGENTIVS l. II. ad tr.reg.c. 3. Pater, Filius & Spiritus S. nouerunt sic venire, sic abire, vt nec ad locum localiter veniant, nec localiter de loco discedant. Omnia implet Trinitas, omnia continet: illi venire dicitur, cui se manifestare dignatur, & ab illo discedit, a quo lumen suæ dilectionis abscondit: nec tamen localiter absens efficitur, cum iuste relinquit indignum: nec loco præsens efficitur, cum misericorditer visitat, quem fecit dignum.

Ceterum manet SS. Trinitas apud nos præsentia speciali, nos magis magisque illuminando, a peccatis subinde iustificando, sanctificando, protegendo, in omni necessitate nobis subueniendo.

Quæst. VI. Quis unionem mysticam perficit? Causa efficiens vnionis mysticæ est Deus triunus, Pater a), Filius Dei b), & Spiritus S. c). Prob. a. Ex Eph. I, 17. 22. Deus Domini nostri Iesu Christi, Pater gloriæ, dedit illum caput super omnia ecclesiæ, quæ est corpus eius, qui omnia in omnibus implet. Deus Pater est fons & radix vnionis mysticæ; quippe qui eo fine Christum constituit caput ecclesiæ, vt non tantum ritu principis eam gubernaret, sed instar capitis cum membris connexi cum ea iungeretur, præsentissime ei adesset, & in totum corpus mysticum, eiusdemque vera membra vitam spiritualem cum viribus operandi diffunderet.

Prob. b. Vnionem mysticam a Filio Dei originem ducere, liquet ex eo, quod Filius Dei ecclesiam sibi desponsat, Hos. II, 19. cum ea perinde, ac maritus cum uxore, copulatur, Eph. V, 31. velut caput cum ipsa, tanquam corpore spirituali, cohæret, Eph. I, 23. Christiani in eo sunt, vt palmes in viti, Io. XV, 5. Et vna cum Patre mansionem apud eos facit, Io. XIV, 23.


### Question VIII. By what means is the mystical union of God with the reborn man accomplished?
