Prob. c. From 1 Cor. III, 16. Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you? The Solomonic temple was filled with the glory of Jehovah, 1 Kings VIII, 11. Faithful men are living temples of God, inaugurated by the regenerating and justifying grace of the Holy Spirit, and filled by the indwelling grace of the Holy Spirit.

Question VII.

That God might be joined with the reborn by the bond of mystical union, He was moved internally by a special love, by which He embraces them, and externally by the merit of Christ, apprehended by them through true faith.

Prob. a. Jer. XXXI, 3. I have loved you with an everlasting love: therefore with mercy I have drawn you. The most benign Deity entices and draws the hearts of the faithful with cords of love, Hos. XI, 4, by which He has bound Himself to them. The proof of supreme love is that God is joined to the reborn man, as a friend to a friend, and dwells in him just as the soul dwells in the body.

Prob. b. Eph. II, 20, 21. Built upon the foundation of the Apostles and Prophets, whose cornerstone (ἀκρογωνιαῖος) is Jesus Christ, through whom the whole structure, joined together, properly grows into a holy temple in the Lord. Obj. a) that the doctrine of the Apostles and Prophets becomes the dogmatic foundation of faith, exhibiting the substantial foundation of faith, Christ; who is called the cornerstone, for the reason that the spiritual temple, which is the church, and in it every reborn soul, relies upon His merit. This cornerstone connects the converted, not more Jews than Gentiles, so that they may become one holy mystical body in the Lord, i.e., a dwelling place, consecrated to the indwelling Lord. Obj. b) When in Holy Scripture Christ is called the cornerstone, regard is had to the passion and death of Christ, Ps. CXVIII, 21; Matt. XXI, 42; 1 Pet. II, 7. In what way, therefore, the merit of Christ is the foundation of regeneration: in the same way it is the basis of mystical union. Aptly says Cyril, book XI, ch. 27, on John: Christ is the nexus of our union with God; to us indeed as man, but to God the Father, as God, He is naturally united. For it was not possible for the corrupt nature of man to ascend to immortality, unless an immortal nature, by communion and participation of itself, should lift us up, reformed, from the limits of our mortality to its own good. We are therefore perfected, and led back to union with the Father by the mediation of the Savior.

Question VIII.

By what means is the mystical union of God with the reborn man accomplished? The means on the part of God, effecting and confirming the mystical union, are the word of the gospel , baptism , and the Lord's Supper .

The medium on the part of man, receiving and embracing God, is faith .

Prob. a. From John XIV, 24. If anyone loves me, he will keep my word, and my Father will love him, and we will come to him, and make our abode with him. To him who keeps the word of Christ, i.e., who embraces the word of the gospel, is promised both the coming and the constant indwelling of the whole Most Holy Trinity.

Prob. b. From Gal. III, 24. As many of you as have been baptized have put on Christ. Baptism is the medium of putting on Christ. The garment which is put on; externally with the body, Christ is united internally with the soul and body.

Prob. c. From 1 Cor. X, 16, 17. The cup of blessing, which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, one body: for we all partake of that one bread.

Since Christians, partaking of the one eucharistic bread, are rendered one spiritual body, certainly the medi-

Latin:

Prob. c. Ex 1 Cor. III, 16. Nonne scitis, quod templum Dei sitis, & Spiritus Dei in vobis habitet? Templum Salomonæum gloria Iehovæ implebat, 1 Reg: VIII, 11. Homines fideles sunt viva templa Dei gratia Spiritus S. regenerante & iustificante inaugurata, gratia Spiritus S. inhabitante impleta.

Quæst. VII. Quid impulit Deum, ut arctissime se cum renatis coniungeret?

Vt Deus cum renatis vinculo vnionis mysticæ iungeretur, interne dilectione speciali, qua ipsos complectitur , externe merito Christi, vera fide ab ipsis apprehensio , permotus est.

Prob. a. Ier. XXXI, 3. Dilectione perpetua dilexi te: per misericordiam traxi te. Numen benignissimum corda fidelium ad se allicit & trahit funibus amoris, Hos. XI, 4. quibus se cum illis deuinxit. Summi amoris argumentum est, quod Deus homini renato iungitur, vt amicus amico, & in eodem perinde, ac animus in corpore, habitat.

Prob. b. Eph. II, 20. 21. Superædificati (estis) super fundamento Apostolorum & Prophetarum, cuius lapis (ἀκρογωνιαῖος) angularis est Iesus Christus, per quem totum ædificium coagmentatum probe crescit in templum sanctum in domino. Obs. a) quod doctrina Apostolorum & Prophetarum fit fundamentum fidei dogmaticum, exhibens fundamentum fidei substantiale, Christum; qui dicitur lapis angularis, ideo, quod templum spirituale, quod est ecclesia, & in ea quæuis anima renata, merito ipsius innititur. Connectit hic lapis angularis conuersos non magis Iudæos, quam gentiles, vt fiant vnum corpus mysticum sanctum in Domino, h. e. domicilium, Domino inhabitanti consecratum. Obs. b) Quando in Scriptura S. Christus lapis angularis dicitur, respectus habetur ad passionem & mortem Christi, Ps. CXVIII, 21. Matth. XXI, 42. 1 Petr. II, 7. Qua ratione itaque meritum Christi est fundamentum regenerationis: eodem pacto est basis vnionis mysticæ. Apposite inquit Cyrillus, libr. XI. c. 27. in Io. Nexus vnionis nostræ ad Deum Christus est; nobis quidem, vt homo, Deo autem Patri, vt Deus naturaliter vnitus. Non enim possibile erat, corruptam hominis naturam ad immortalitatem conscendere, nisi natura immortalis communione ac participatione sui a mortalitatis nostræ terminis ad suum bonum nos reformatos eleuaret. Consummati igitur sumus, reductique ad vnionem Patris mediatione Saluatoris.

Quæst. VIII. Quibus mediis perficitur unio mystica Dei cum homine renato?

Media ex parte Dei efficientia & confirmantia vnionem mysticam sunt verbum euangelii baptismus & cœna dominica .

Medium ex parte hominis recipiens & amplectens Deum est fides .

Prob. a. Ex Io. XIV, 24. Qui me diligit, sermonem meum seruabit, & Pater meus ipsum diliget, & veniemus ad eum, & mansionem apud eum faciemus. Seruanti sermonem Christi, h. e. verbum euangelii amplectenti, promittitur tum aduentus, tum constans inhabitatio totius SS. Trinitatis.

Prob. b. Ex Gal. III, 24. Quotquot baptizati estis, Christum induistis. Baptismus est medium induendi Christum. Vestimentum, quod induitur; externe cum corpore, Christus indutus interne cum anima & corpore vnitur.

Prob. c. Ex 1 Cor. X, 16. 17. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne est communicatio sanguinis Christi? Quem panem frangimus, nonne communicatio corporis Christi? Quia vnus panis, vnum corpus multi sumus: omnes enim ex vno pane participamus.

Cum Christiani participantes ex vno pane, eucharistico, vnum spirituale corpus redduntur, vtique


### Question X. What are the extremes that are joined by mystical union?

by means of that bread, which is the communion of the body of Christ, they are united with Christ himself.

For although Christ is already united to the faithful before the use of the Supper through faith, received from baptism and the preaching of the word, and consequently the communion of Christ is brought to the Lord’s Supper: yet the same communion is increased, confirmed, and sealed through the Lord’s Supper, and the union itself with Christ is rendered closer through it.

To this point refer the words of the Savior in John, ch. VI, 56: "He who eats my flesh and drinks my blood abides in me, and I in him."

Indeed, the substance of the sacrament of the Supper is not described in John ch. VI, yet the fruit redounding from the spiritual eating of the sacrament of the Supper is explained. Concerning which HILARY, book VIII de Trinit., discourses excellently: "These things taken and drunk cause that we abide in Christ and Christ in us."

And CYRIL OF ALEXANDRIA says learnedly in book VI on John, ch. 17: "Just as if someone were to pour one wax into another that has been melted: he mixes the one entirely with the other; so it is necessary, if anyone receives the flesh and blood of the Lord, to be joined with him, so that Christ may be found in him, and he himself in Christ."

Proved from Eph. III, 17: "Christ dwells in our hearts through faith."

CHEMNITZ explains these words clearly in *de D. N. in Christo*, ch. 30: "Faith is the medium, organ, or instrument by which we apprehend, receive, and retain Christ in the word, so that he does not pass by like a stranger, or stay with us only as a guest for the night; but so that he may remain through the grace of indwelling, and dwell perpetually in us, so that we may always be and remain members of God’s household."

GREGORY OF NYSSA also says elegantly in Orat. VI in Cantic.: "We receive God by faith, so that he may come into the chamber of our heart, and we may retain him once received by faith." Quest.

IX. By what ministers does God fashion the mystical union? God fashions the mystical union by the ministry of holy heralds, who are the ministerial cause as it were paranymphs, leading the bride to Christ, so that she may be joined with him in this spiritual marriage.

Proved from 2 Cor. XI, 2: "I have betrothed (ἡρμοσάμην) you to one husband, that I might present you as a chaste virgin to Christ." Christ is the bridegroom of the church, and of every reborn soul; the minister of the church is the groomsman, striving with all his might in his office so that the bride may be led to the bridegroom, as it were delivered into his hands, and be bound to him in spiritual marriage.

Quest. X. What are the extremes which are joined in the mystical union? On one side is the substance of the whole holy Trinity a), as well as the human substance of Christ’s nature b).

On the other side is the substance of the reborn man, considered according to body and soul c).

The extremes . Proved a. From 2 Petr. I, 4: "Exceeding great and precious promises have been given to us, that through them you might become κοινωνοὶ τῆς θείας φύσεως, partakers of the divine nature, escaping the corruption that is in the world through lust."

Where observe a) that the communion of the divine nature presupposes or infers the union of the divine substance; because no communion is given without union. b) The communion of the divine nature infers some participation of divine gifts as a condition of the mystical union.

For it cannot be that the most holy Trinity joins itself to the soul and body of the faithful without filling them with all the divine fullness of righteousness, peace, and holiness, Eph. III, 18, according to measure, Eph. IV, 7. HULSEMANN says excellently in *brev. c.

XIV. §. 4*: "The communion of the divine nature denotes the gracious indwelling of the divine essence in us, and the faculty received from it of striving for divine innocence and purity."

Prob. b. Through the mystical union we are members of the body of Christ, of his flesh and of his bones. Eph. V, 30. Which words of Paul are to be understood concerning the ὁμοουσία [consubstantiality], or our consanguinity with Christ, on account of the assumption of our flesh, which consanguinity is common to the pious and the impious, but concerning the mystical union proper to the faithful alone; because the Apostle treats of the head of the church, which is his spiritual body, v. 23. But since Christ becomes the head of the church not only according to his divine, but also his human nature; it follows that we are united not only with the divine nature, but also with the substance of the flesh of Christ sacramentally in the use of the supper, and spiritually outside the sacrament.

That a reborn man, consisting of soul and body, is joined with God, is evident from 1 Cor. III, 16. Do you not know that you are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God dwells in you? Which words St. Paul applies to the body of the reborn, 1 Cor. VI, 19. Do you not know that your body is the temple of the Spirit, who is in you, which is holy? Hvlsemannvs observes, l. c. p. 920, that this union, when it occurs by way of dependence, participation, and subordination of the secondary cause, or the faithful man, under Christ the head, brings about a closer mode of connecting the physical substance of the human body with the body of Christ, for the sealing of the certainty of resurrection and immortality, than with the spiritual substance of the Most Holy Trinity.

Latin:

mediante illo pane, qui est communio corporis Christi, cum ipso Christo uniuntur.

Quamvis enim iam ante coenae usum salutarem Christus sit fidelibus unitus per fidem, ex baptismo & verbi praedicatione acceptam, & proinde communio Christi ad coenam Domini afferatur: tamen eadem communio per coenam Domini augetur, confirmatur & obsignatur, ipsaque vnio cum Christo per eam arctior redditur.

Quo spectant verba Saluatoris apud Ioannem, cap. VI, 56. Qui manducat meam carnem, & bibit meum sanguinem, in me manet, & ego in ipso.

Non describitur quidem cap. VI, Ioannaeo substantia sacramenti coenae, fructus tamen e spirituali sacramenti coenae manducatione redundans exponitur. De quo praeclare disserit HILARIVS l. VIII. de trinit. Haec sumta & hausta faciunt, vt nos in Christo & Christus in nobis maneat.

Et scite ait CYRILLVS ALEXANDR. libr. VI. in Io. cap. 17. Perinde, ac si quis liquefactae cerae aliam ceram infuderit: alteram cum altera totam commiscet: ita necesse est, si quis carnem & sanguinem domini recipit, cum ipso coniungi, vt Christus in eo, & ipse in Christo inueniatur.

Prob. d. Ex Eph. III, 17. Habitat Christus per fidem in cordibus nostris.

Quae verba perspicue explicat CHEMNIT. de D. N. in Christo, cap. 30. Fides est medium, organon, seu instrumentum, quo Christum in verbo apprehendimus, accipinus ac retinemus, vt non quasi peregrinus transeat, vel ut hospes pernoctet tantum apud nos; sed ut per inhabitationis gratiam maneat, ac perpetuo in nobis habitet, vt semper nos simus ac maneamus domestici Dei.

Eleganter etiam GREGOR. NYSSEN. Orat. VI. in Cantic. Fide Deum recipimus, vt intra conclaue cordis nostri veniat, & receptum fide retineamus.

Quaest. IX. Quibus ministris Deus vnionem mysticam concinnat? Deus vnionem mysticam concinnat ministerio praeconum sacrorum, qui sunt Causa ministerialis quasi paranymphi, adducentes sponsam Christo, vt illa cum hoc connubio spirituali coniungatur.

Prob. Ex 2 Cor. XI, 2. Desponsavi (ἡρμοσάμην) vos vni viro, virginem puram vt sisterem Christo. Christus est sponsus ecclesiae, & cuiuslibet animae renatae, minister ecclesiae est pronubus, in officio suo pro virili annitens, vt sponsa sponso adducatur, in manus eius quasi tradatur, & connubio spirituali cum ipso deuinciatur.

Quaest. X. Quae sunt extrema; quae vnione mystica coniunguntur? Ex vna parte est substantia totius sanctae Trinitatis a), nec non substantia humanae Christi naturae b).

Ab altera parte est substantia hominis renati, secundum corpus & animam considerati c).

Extrema . Prob. a. Ex 2 Petr. I, 4. Maxima nobis & pretiosa promissa data sunt, vt per ea reddamini κοινωνοὶ τῆς θείας φύσεως, diuinae participes naturae, effugientes eam, quae in mundo est per concupiscentiam, corruptionem.

Vbi obs. a) quod communio naturae diuinae vnionem substantiae diuinae supponat, aut inferat; propterea, quod nulla communio sine vnione datur. b) Inferit communio naturae diuinae aliquam participationem diuinorum donorum pro conditione vnionis mysticae.

Fieri enim nequit, vt sanctissima Trias animae & corpori fidelium se iungat, quin eosdem omni plenitudine diuina iustitiae, pacis, sanctitatis, Eph. III, 18. secundum mensuram Eph. IV, 7. impleat.

Egregie inquit HVLSEMANNVS in breu. c. XIV. §. 4. Communio diuinae naturae notat gratiosam inhabitationem essentiae diuinae in nobis, & ab ea acceptam facultatem studendi innocentiae & puritatis diuinae. innocentiæ & puritati diuinæ.

Prob. b. Per vnionem mysticam sumus membra corporis Christi de eius carne & ossibus. Eph. V, 30. Quae verba Pauli intelligenda sunt de ὁμοουσία, siue consanguinitate nostra cum Christo, propter carnis nostrae assumptionem, quae consanguinitas piis & impiis communis est, sed de vnione mystica solis fidelibus propria; quia Apostolus agit de capite ecclesiae, quae spirituale eius est corpus, v. 23. Cum autem Christus caput ecclesiae non tantum secundum diuinam, sed & humanam naturam fit; consequitur, nos non tantum cum diuina natura, sed & substantia carnis Christi sacramentaliter in vsu coenae, spiritualiter extra sacramentum vniri.

Prob. c. Quod homo renatus anima & corpore constans cum Deo fungatur, patet ex 1 Cor. III, 16. Nonne scitis, quod templum Dei sitis, & Spiritus Dei habitet in vobis? Quae verba S. Paullus corpori renatorum applicat, 1 Cor. VI, 19. Annon scitis, quod corpus vestrum templum Spiritus, qui in vobis, sancti fit? Observat Hvlsemannvs l. c. p. 920. quod haec vnio, cum fit dependentiae, participationis & subordinationis caussae secundae, seu hominis fidelis, sub capite Christo, inferat arctiorem modum connectendi substantiam physicam corporis humani cum corpore Christi, ad resurrectionis & immortalitatis certitudinem obsignandam, quam cum substantia spirituali SS. Trinitatis.


### Quaest. XI. In what does the mystical union formally consist?

The mystical union formally consists both in a special and intrinsic conjunction of the substance of the faithful man with the substance of the Most Holy Trinity and the flesh of Christ ; and in a gracious operation, by which the most benign God works in the reborn man by a special and efficacious influx .

Prob. a & b. From Lev. XXVI, 11. 12. In the first place I will set my habitation in the midst of you, and my soul shall not abhor you; but I will walk in the midst of you, and I will be your God; and you shall be my people. Which words Paul repeats, 2 Cor. VI, 16. God said: for I will dwell in them, and I will walk in them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. The good and great God promises two things: a) A gracious indwelling, which cannot be conceived without a substantial presence; since indwelling is of a person, whereas gifts are said not to inhabit, but to be present: b) A walking in the midst of us, which denotes a gracious operation. A prince walks among his subjects, ruling them; a father among his children, providing for their needs; a teacher among his disciples, instructing them: so God the Holy Spirit rules the reborn, counsels them, and teaches and illuminates them. Therefore, two things pertain to the form of the mystical union: 1) A true and real ἀδιαστασία [inseparability], or nearness through the approach of the divine substance to the believing man: by which the triune God comes to us, and makes his abode with us: which therefore is not merely a naked operation, without the approximation of God, but an approach or advent of nearness to us, so that he may be and remain in us, John XIV, 23 (*). 2) A gracious ἐνέργεια [energy], or operation, by which God so comes to us and dwells in us, that he fills us with all the fullness of wisdom, holiness, power, and other divine gifts, Eph. III, 18. Which also implies a mystical περιχώρησιν [interpenetration], by which God is in us and remains through grace, and we are truly in God, and adhere to him through faith, so that nothing, we who are united to God through faith, can separate us from God, Rom. VIII, 38.

Question XII. Can you now explain distinctly what kind of union the spiritual conjunction of God with the reborn and justified man is?

The mystical union is of substances, but not formally substantial a); it is of persons, but not by reason of the term to which it is personal b); it is accidental, not by reason of the extremes, but by reason of the term to which c); it is not *parasatike* [external/juxtaposed], or external without communication, but *perichoretike* [circumincessive], implying mutual immanence d); it is not a bare presence, but an *energetike* [active], or operative presence of God e); it is, finally, a conjunction of God with the faithful man that is *harmonike* [harmonic], or one that effects a tempering of the affections f).

Proof a. The mystical union is not formally, or by reason of the mode, substantial. For one substance does not result from the divine and human substance, just as a graft coalesces with a trunk into one substance of a tree. It can, however, be called substantial objectively, from the extremes of the union; since not only divine gifts and operations, but the very substance of God is spiritually joined with the substance of man. It is more accurately called a union of substances than a substantial union; because for a formally substantial union it is required that two incomplete substances coalesce into one complete substance. But in the mystical union, God and the reborn man are complete substances; nor is one changed or transubstantiated into the other. For a) by the benefit of the mystical union, God dwells in us as in temples, 1 Cor. III, 16. But a dwelling is not changed into the inhabitant, nor the inhabitant into the dwelling. b) Through the mystical union we put on Christ, Gal. III, 27. But a garment is not essentially one with the man who is clothed. c) The divine nature is most distinct from the human, although God comes to us and makes His abode with us, John XIV, 23. For He can withdraw from the man to whom He has drawn near. Thus the Holy Spirit withdrew from King Saul, 1 Sam. XVI, 14; and David, from whom He had departed after he had fallen into the crime of adultery, implores God with most ardent sighs not to withdraw the Holy Spirit again, Ps. LI, 13. Therefore, the Holy Spirit is essentially distinct from the reborn soul.

Proof b. Paul teaches that Christ and the faithful remain distinct persons when mystically united, Gal. II, 20: "I live now, not I" (Paul implies that he is a person distinct from Christ), "but Christ lives in me" (in Paul). Wherefore Paul and Christ, as two distinct persons, are distinguished by different operations, which belong to the supposita. Otherwise the sense would be: "Not I, i.e., Christ, but Christ lives in me, i.e., in Christ," than which nothing more absurd can be said. Therefore, the personal union differs from the mystical: 1) In the extremes. The former is the divine nature of the *Logos*, *anypostatos* [possessing its own subsistence], joined to the assumed human nature, *anypostatos* [destitute of its own hypostasis]: the latter is the whole Holy Trinity joined with several completely subsisting men by the bond of faith: 2) In the term to which. The former is terminated at one *syntheton* [composite] person; the latter at one mystical [entity] united by accident: 3) In the mode. The former is indissoluble, the latter is dissoluble: through the former, the nature of the *Logos* dwells in the assumed flesh *somatikos* [bodily], as in a singular temple; through the latter, the Triune God dwells in the reborn man *pneumatikos* [spiritually], as in a common temple: 4) In degree, which the mystical union receives, inasmuch as it is now tighter, now weaker, according to the increase or decrease of faith; but the personal union admits no degree, since it is always the same: 5) In the consequent communication. By the personal union, infinite gifts are communicated to the flesh of Christ for possession and usurpation: by the mystical union, finite gifts are communicated to the reborn for subjective inhesion: 6) In the predications, which the former generates as personal, the latter as accidental.

Proof c. The mystical union is called accidental, not from the united extremes, since they are substances; but from the term to which; because it is not terminated at one [thing] *per se*; just as two substances incomplete substances concur to constitute one complete substance; e.g., soul and body constitute one human being. But God and man are complete substances, and they constitute one mystical [union] united by accident. Wherefore the mystical union is not indeed essential, nor yet accidental by reason of the extremes; since not only divine gifts, nor merely the gracious operation of God, but the very substance of God itself is intimately united with the substance of the faithful human.

Which is demonstrated: 1) Because the three persons of the Deity are said to come to the faithful and to make a dwelling with them, John 14:23. But the persons of the Deity are not accidents, and to come to someone denotes an approximation to the same. To make a dwelling is never said of gifts or operations considered abstractly; but of the persons acting.

2) God dwells in the faithful as in temples, 1 Cor. 3:16. Temples are said to be consecrated to God, not to gifts, not to divine operations. To dwell in a temple denotes a substantial presence. Mere gifts, mere operations are not said to dwell.

3) From Gal. 4:6. God has sent the Spirit of his Son into your hearts crying: Abba Father. Here the Apostle openly distinguishes the substantial approximation of the Holy Spirit from the gracious cry, and thus declares that the substance of the Holy Spirit approaches more closely, and exerts his gifts more.

4) From 1 Cor. 6:15, 16, 17. Do you not know that your bodies are members of Christ? How then shall I take away the members of Christ, and make them members of a harlot? Do you not know that he who adheres to a harlot is made one body? For they shall be, says the scripture, two in one flesh, but he who adheres to the Lord is one spirit with him.

Whence arises the argument: In the same way that by reason of the extremes being united, man and woman become one flesh, in that same way Christ and the faithful are one spirit: But man and woman become one flesh through the union of substances: Therefore.

5) Those who are members of the body of Christ, of his flesh and of his bones, they are united with Christ by reason of substance: But the reborn, etc. Therefore. The minor is evident from Eph. 5:30.

6) Those who are united to Christ in that way in which branches are to the vine, they are joined by their substance to the substance of Christ: But the reborn, etc. Therefore.

7) The reborn are κοινωνοὶ θείας φύσεως, partakers of the divine nature, 2 Pet. 1:4. But the communication of the divine nature denotes more than the participation of gifts or operations, since reborn and justified men have communion not only with divine gifts or operations, but also with God the Father, and his Son, 1 John 1:3.

From which we gather: To whom God is so united that he makes them partakers of his divine nature, to them he is joined not only by his gifts and operation, but also by the conjunction of his divine essence: But God is so united to faithful men, etc. Therefore.

8) The doctrine concerning the peculiar approximation of the divine substance to pious men is in conformity with our symbolic books, the Fathers, and orthodox theologians.

For the Formula of Concord, art. III, rejects the false doctrine of those who assert: That God himself does not dwell in believers, but only his gifts. LUTHER writes thus on this question in Ps. 51: I omit the useless disputations of the schools, whether it speaks of the divine person or of the gift of the spirit? For what do these things, even if accurately disputed, edify? Since we have the clear testimony of Christ: We will come to him, and make our dwelling with him.

Therefore the Holy Spirit truly dwells in believers not only through gifts, but also as regards his substance. Nor does he give his gifts here so that he himself may be elsewhere, or sleep; but he is present to his gifts and to his creature, by preserving and adding strength.

Confer D. HULSEM. breviar. enucl. p. 906. & D. CALOV. in system. tom. X. p. 509. Prob. d.

That the mystical union is not παρασάτικη, or external through mere assistance, but περιχωρητική, or internal through intimate immanence, is clear from the fact that, as Holy Scripture testifies, God is in the faithful through efficacious grace, and the faithful are in God through trust, and

Latin:

Vnio mystica formaliter consistit tum in speciali & intrinseca coniunctione substantiae hominis fidelis cum substantia SS. Trinitatis & carnis Christi a); tum in gratiosa operatione, qua Deus benignissimus in homine renato operatur influxu speciali & efficaci b).

Prob. a & b. Ex Lev. XXVI, 11. 12. In primis dabo habitaculum meum in medio vestri, nec fastidiet anima mea vos; sed ambulabo in medio vestri, ero que vobis in Deum; vos autem eritis mihi in populum. Quae verba Paullus repetit, 2 Cor. VI, 16. Deus dixit: quia inhabitabo in illis, & in iis circumambulabo, & ero ipsorum Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus. Duo promittit Deus optimus, maximus: a) Inhabitationem gratiosam, quae sine praesentia substantiali concipi nequit; siquidem inhabitatio est persona, quae donorum, quae non inhabitare, sed inesse dicuntur: b) Ambulationem in medio nostri, quae gratiosam notat operationem. Ambulat princeps inter subditos, eos regendo; pater inter liberos, eorum rationibus prospiciendo; praeceptor inter discipulos, eos informando: ita Deus Spiritus S. renatos regit, consulit, & eosdem docet atque illuminat. Duo ergo ad formam vnionis mysticae pertinent 1) vera & realis ἀδιαστασία, vel propinquitas per appropinquationem substantiae diuinae ad hominem credentem: qua Deus triunus ad nos venit, & mansionem apud nos facit: quae proinde non est nuda tantum operationis, fine approximatione Dei, sed propinquationis ad nos accessus, vel aduentus, vt in nobis sit & maneat, Io. XIV, 23 (*). 2) Gratiosa ἐνέργεια, siue operatio, qua Deus ita ad nos venit & in nobis habitat, vt impleat nos omni plenitudine sapientiae, sanctitatis, potentiae & aliorum donorum diuinorum, Eph. III, 18. Quae etiam mysticam περιχώρησιν importat, qua Deus in nobis est & manet per gratiam, nos vere in Deo sumus, eique adhaeremus per fiduciam, vt nihil nos, qui Deo vnimur per fidem, separare a Deo possit, Rom. VIII, 38.

Quæst. XII. Poterne iam distincte explicare, qualis unio sit spiritualis coniunctio Dei cum homine renato & iustificato?

Vnio mystica est substantiarum, sed non formaliter substantialis a); est personarum, sed non ratione termini ad quem personalis b), est accidentalis, non ratione extremorum, sed ratione termini ad quem c); non est παρασατική, sive externa sine communicatione, sed περιχωρητική, mutuam immanentiam inferens d); non est nuda adessentia, sed præsentia Dei ἐνεργητική, sive operosa e); est denique coniunctio Dei cum homine fideli ἀρμονική, sive contemperationem affectuum efficiens f).

Prob. a. Vnio mystica non est formaliter, sive ratione modi, substantialis. Neque enim ex substantia diuina & humana una resultat substantia, sicut furculus cum trunco in unam arboris substantiam coalescit. Potest tamen vocari substantialis obiective, ab extremis vnionis; quoniam non tantum dona & operationes diuinæ, fed & ipsa substantia Dei cum substantia hominis spiritualiter coniungitur. Accuratius dicitur vnio substantiarum, quam substantialis; quia ad vnionem formaliter substantialem requiritur, vt duæ substantiæ in-completæ in unam substantiam completam coëant. At vero in vnione mystica Deus & homorenatus sunt substantiæ completæ; neque altera in alteram mutatur, aut transubstantiatur. Nam a) beneficio vnionis mysticæ Deus in nobis, tanquam in templis habitat, 1 Cor. III, 16. Sed domicilium non in incolam, nec incola in domicilium commutatur. b) Per vnionem mysticam Christum induimus, Gal. III, 27. Sed indumentum non est essentialiter unum cum homine induto. c) Diuina natura ab humana distinctissima est, licet Deus ad nos veniat & mansionem apud nos faciat, IO. XIV, 23. Potest enim recedere ab homine; cui appropinquauit. Sic recessit Spiritus S. a rege Saule, 1 Sam. XVI, 14. & Dauid, a quo, prolapso in adulterii crimen, discesserat, ardentissimis suspiriis Deum implorat, ne denuo Spiritum S. subtrahat, Pf. LI, 13. E. Spiritus S. ab anima renata essentialiter distinctus est.

Prob. b. Christum & fideles mystice vnitos manere distinctas personas, Paullus docet, Gal. II, 20. Viuo autem nunc non ego (Paullus innuit, se distinctam a Christo esse personam), sed viuit in me (Paullo) Christus. Quare Paullus & Christus, vt duæ personæ distinctæ, diuersis operationibus, quæ suppositorum sunt, discernuntur. Alias sensus foret: Non vero ego i. e. Christus, sed Christus viuit in me, i. e. Christo, quo nihil insulsius dici potest. Differt igitur unio personalis a mystica: 1) Extremis. Illa natura diuina τῦ λόγυ ἀνυποστάτος, i. e. propria subsistentia gaudens, assumtæ humanæ naturæ ἀνυποστάτῳ, i. e. propria hypostasi destitutæ, vnitur: hac tota SS. Trinitas cum pluribus hominibus complete subsistentibus vinculo fidei coniungitur: 2) Termino ad quem. Illa terminatur ad vnam personam σύνθετον; hæc ad vnuin mysticum per accidens vnitum: 3) Modo. Illa est indissolubilis, hæc solubilis: per illam habitat naturæ τῦ λόγυ in carne assumta σωματικῶς, tanquam in templo singulari; per hanc habitat Deus triunus in homine renato πνευματικῶς, tanquam templo communi: 4) Gradu, quem recipit vnio mystica, vtpote quæ, pro augmento aut decremento fidei, modo arctior, modo debilior est; fed vnio personalis nullum admittit gradum, cum fit semper eadem: 5) Consequente communicatione. Vnione personali communicantur carni Christi dona infinita ad possessionem & usurpationem: vnione mystica communicantur renatis dona finita ad subiectiuam inhasionem: 6) Prædicationibus, quas illa personales, hæc accidentales gignit.

Prob. c. Vnio mystica vocatur accidentalis, non ab extremis vnitis; quippe quæ sunt substantiæ: sed a termino ad quem; quia non terminatur ad vnum per se; sicut duæ substantia stantiæ incompletæ concurrunt ad constituendam unam substantiam completam; v. gr. anima & corpus constituunt unum hominem. Sed Deus & homo sunt substantiæ completæ, & constituunt unum mysticum per accidens vnitum. Quamobrem vnio mystica non est quidem essentialis, neque tamen ratione extremorum accidentalis; quoniam non tantum dona diuina, neque duntaxat operatio Dei gratiosa, sed ipsa etiam substantia Dei cum substantia fidelis hominis intime vnitur.

Id quod demonstratur: 1) Quia tres personæ Deitatis dicuntur venire ad fideles & mansionem apud eos facere, Io. XIV, 23. At personæ Deitatis non sunt accidentia, & aduenire ad aliquem notat approximationem ad eundem. Mansionem facere nunquam dicitur de donis, aut operationibus abstracte consideratis; sed de personis operantibus.

2) Deus in fidelibus, tanquam templis habitat, 1 Cor. III, 16. Templa dicuntur Deo consecrata, non donis, non operationibus diuinis. Inhabitare in templo notat præsentiam substantialem. Sola dona, solæ operationes non dicuntur inhabitare.

3) Ex Gal. IV, 6. Emisit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda vestra clamantem: Abba Pater. Hic Apostolus approximationem Spiritus S. substantialem a clamore gratioso aperte distinguit, adeoque & substantiam Spiritus S. propius accedere, & dona sua magis exserere enuntiat.

4) Ex 1 Cor. VI, 15. 16. 17. An nescitis, quod corpora vestra membra Christi sint? Quomodo igitur eripiam Christo membra sua, & efficiam ea membra meretricis? An nescitis, quod, qui adhæret meretrici, unum corpus efficitur? Erunt enim, inquit scriptura, duo in carne una, Qui autem adhæret Domino, unus spiritus est cum illo.

Vnde nascitur argumentum; Quo pacto ratione extremorum vniendorum vir & mulier fiunt una caro, eo pacto Christus & fideles sunt unus spiritus: Atqui vir & mulier fiunt caro per vnionem substantiarum: E.

5) Qui sunt membra corporis Christi, ex carne eius & ossibus eius, illi ratione substantiæ cum Christo sunt vniti: Atqui renati &c. E. Minor patet ex Eph. V, 30.

6) Qui Christo vniti sunt ea ratione, qua palmites viti, illi substantia sua iuncti sunt substantiæ Christi: Atqui renati &c. E.

7) Renati sunt κοινωνοὶ θείας φύσεως, participes diuinæ naturæ, 2 Petr. I, 4. Sed communicatio diuinæ naturæ plus notat, quam participationem donorum aut operationum, siquidem homines renati ac iustificati non tantum cum donis aut operationibus diuinis, sed etiam cum Deo Patre, & ipsius Filio communionem habent, 1 Io.

I, 3. E quibus colligimus: Quibus ita vnitur Deus, vt naturæ suæ diuinæ participes faciat, illis non tantum iungitur donis ac operatione sua, sed & essentiæ suæ diuinæ coniunctione: Atqui hominibus fidelibus Deus ita vnitur &c. E.

8) Doctrina de peculiari substantiæ diuinæ approximatione ad homines pios conformis est libris nostris symbolicis, Patribus & Theologis orthodoxis.

Reiicit enim Form. concord. art. III. falsam doctrinam eorum, qui afferunt: Non ipsum Deum, sed tantum dona in credentibus habitare. LVTHERVS hac de quæstione ita scribit in Ps. LI. Omitto inutiles disputationes scholarum, an loquatur de persona diuina, an de dono spiritus? Quid enim hæc etiam accurate disputata ædificant? Cum habeamus clarum testimonium Christi: Veniemus ad eum, & mansionem apud eum faciemus.

Habitat ergo vere Spiritus S. in credentibus non tantum per dona, sed & quoad substantiam suam. Neque hic dona sua dat, vt ipse alibi fit, aut dormiat; sed adest donis suis & creaturæ suæ, conferuando & addendo robur.

Confer. D. HVLSEM. breuiar. enucl. p. 906. & D. CALOV. in system. tom. X. p. 509.

Prob. d. Quod vnio mystica non fit παρασάτικη, siue externa per nudam assistentiam, sed περιχωρητική, siue interna per intimam immanentiam, liquet ex eo, quod teste S. scriptura Deus est in fidelibus per gratiam efficacem, & fideles sunt in Deo per fiduciam, &


### Quaest. XI. In what does the mystical union formally consist? (continued)

the love flowing from this. To which the words of St. John, 1 Epist. IV, 15, look: Whosoever shall confess that Jesus is the Son of God, God abideth in him, and he in God. And we have known and believed the love that God hath to us. God is love; wherefore, he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God, and God in him. The faith of the reborn rests upon the philanthropy of God, which He has testified most clearly by sending Jesus the Redeemer; in whom the reborn believe with the heart, and whom they confess to be the Son of God, bringing forth this their faith by love toward God. Thence it comes to pass that they abide in God, as in an ocean of goodness and charity, they abide in Christ, as branches in the vine, and God abides in them, as in consecrated temples, which He purifies, adorns, and fills with all the fullness of wisdom, righteousness, and active holiness: the truly reborn soul is passively perfected, and is filled as a vessel with grace.

Prob. e. That the mystical union of God is not completed by a bare presence of the divine substance, but also embraces an efficacious operation, is proved: 1) Just as the presence of God to creatures is not terminated in mere presence, but in presence joined with operation; so our spiritual conjunction with God is not terminated in the bare presence of the divine substance to the substance of the faithful man, but embraces the efficacious operation of God in man, so that we rightly conclude: Wherever God is by general presence, there He also operates by general concurrence. Therefore, where God is present by special presence, there He also operates by special and gracious concurrence.

2) God not only dwells in justified men, but also walks in them, 2 Cor. VI, 16, i.e., He is present to them, exciting and working in them the various actions of virtues by which they worship Him.

3) Christ is in the faithful in such a way that He lives in them, Gal. II, 20, brings forth the notable fruits of faith, Jo. XV, 5, and erects a spiritual kingdom in their hearts, Luc. XVII, 21.

4) The Holy Spirit is united with the faithful, that He may teach them all things (necessary to be known for salvation), 1 Jo. II, 27, excite prayers and sighs, Rom. VIII, 15, 16, comfort them, Jo. XVI, 7, lead them into the land of uprightness, Ps. CXLIII, 10, and sanctify them, Rom. XV, 16.

Prob. f. That the mystical union procures for the reborn a harmony of affections with the triune God, is evident: because 1) they become one spirit with God, to whom they are glued, 1 Cor. VI, 17, i.e., partakers of divine holiness, goodness, righteousness, and truthfulness. 2) They imitate God by loving, 1 Jo. IV, 10, by exercising mercy after the example of the heavenly Father, Luc. VI, 36, by striving for holiness, 1 Petr. I, 15, 16.

3) Since, by the benefit of the mystical union, the image of Christ is imprinted upon our minds, so that He may be formed in us, μορφωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν, Gal. IV, 19.

The Antithesis is 1. Of the Weigelians and Schvenckfeldians, who posit that the mystical union with God is, in respect of the mode, also corporeal: 2. Of certain Scholastics, Papists, Socinians, and Arminians, who deny that God dwells in the faithful by a special presence in a substantial manner.

The stronger arguments of the Weigelians are: I. Whoever are one in God the Father and the Son, just as the Father is in the Son and the Son in the Father, their union is essential (for the union of the Father and the Son is essential); But the reborn &c. Therefore. The minor is evident from Jo. XVII, 20, 21.

Resp. The words of the cited text are: Neither pray I for these alone, but for them also which shall believe on me through their word; that they all may be one; as thou, Father, art in me, and I in thee, that they also may be one in us. From which words it may be observed that the particle of similitude καθὼς, as, is not to be referred to the mystical union with God, but to the ecclesiastical union of the reborn among themselves, which is the effect of the mystical union. Besides, even if the particle of similitude were transferred to the mystical union with God, it would still import not equality, but a certain conformity, not an absolute similitude, but a relative one. mystic union with God, it would still import not equality, but a certain conformity, not an absolute similitude, but a refpective one.

II. Who

II. Whoever are partakers of the divine nature, their union with God is essential: But the regenerate, etc. 2 Pet. 1:4. Therefore. Resp. Whoever are partakers of the divine nature by an essential participation, by which they become ὁμοούσιοι (consubstantial) with God, their union with God is essential; I concede. But whoever are partakers of the divine nature by a spiritual and gracious participation through faith, they are not essentially united to God.

III. Whoever are one spirit with God, their union with God is essential: But regenerate men, etc. 1 Cor. 6:17. Therefore. Resp. Whoever are one with God per se (in themselves), their union with God is essential. Having thus limited the major premise, we deny the minor; for the reason that by mystical union one is not constituted one per se, but per accidens (accidentally). The reason is at hand; because God and the regenerate man exist and subsist completely, and therefore they cannot be united per se.

IV. Whoever are members of Christ, they are essentially the same with Christ: But the regenerate, etc. Eph. 5:30. Therefore. Resp. Distinguish between natural and mystical members. Believers are not called members of Christ because they have the same nature as Christ; of which even unbelievers are partakers: but because of a spiritual kinship, which is connected on the part of God by the bond of the Word and sacraments, and on the part of the regenerate man by the bond of faith. But spiritual kinship does not imply essential union.

V. Those who are united with God, as branches with the vine, are joined with Him essentially: But the regenerate, etc. John 15:5. Therefore. The major is evident; because the union of branches with the vine is essential. Resp: A comparison is not to be extended beyond the third point. Christians are joined to Christ truly and really, but not essentially. Spiritual branches differ from natural ones in this part, that the latter are joined by nature, the former by supernatural grace.

The arguments of the Papists, Socinians, and Arminians are as follows:

I. Whoever is by essence immense, infinite, omnipresent, and locally distant from no created thing, he, when he begins to be specially present with the saints, cannot come to or approach them by a special substantial presence; But God, etc. Therefore. The major is clear: because where any being is present by substantial presence, it does not come there except by an effect, an affection, or some gift.

Resp. I deny the major, the reason for which is valid for a finite being, having a determinable, definitive, and circumscriptive presence, but not for an infinite being, or God, who is present in distinct modes of presence. The infinity and immensity of the Holy Spirit did not prevent Him from being joined more closely to that dove, in which He visibly descended upon Christ at His baptism, than to other creatures. Indeed, the infinite and immense ὁ λόγος (Word) also dwells more closely in His own assumed flesh, and indeed σωματικῶς (bodily), Col. 2:9, than in other holy men. The entire Most Holy Trinity is present and united more closely to angels and blessed men than to devils and the damned. Therefore, it does not follow: Wherever God is already present according to substance, He cannot in any way come or approach there according to substance; but this only follows: that God cannot approach according to substance in the same way in which He is already present.

You say: The formal aspect of gracious presence is founded and terminated not in a new approximation of substance, but in a new, and therefore special, mode of operating. Resp. A new mode of operating does not exclude, but includes, a peculiar approximation of the divine essence. In all degrees or modes of divine presence, the operation of substantial presence is joined with the operation [of grace]. This we learn from the words of Christ, John 14:26: "But the Paraclete, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, He will teach you all things." Where Christ promises to the disciples, who were already regenerate, both the gracious coming of the Holy Spirit as to substance, and His special operation, or instruction. II. If God were more strictly united with the faithful by reason of substance, he would also recede from the unfaithful by reason of substance: But he does not recede from the unfaithful by reason of substance; because otherwise he would not be omnipresent: Therefore, he is not more strictly joined with the faithful by reason of substance.

In terms of substance, it is not more closely joined with the faithful.

Resp. God does not recede from the unfaithful, as regards general presence; he recedes, however, by a special presence by disdaining them, for the reason that the malicious iniquities of the sinner divide and separate God and the sinner, Is. LIX, 2.

LIX, 2.

Nor yet is the divine omnipresence infringed thereby; because God does not depart physically and locally, by changing place, but hyperphysically and illocally, by not inhabiting the defiled domicile of the heart.

Instantia: God recedes from the unfaithful by withdrawing his grace.

Resp.

God recedes from the impious by withdrawing both grace and the special proximity of his essence.

Hence when God was threatening the disobedient Israelites, Exod. XXXIII, 3. I will not go up in the midst of thee, for thou art a stiffnecked people, lest I consume thee in the way.

God himself was denying his special proximity to them.

III. He who unites himself with us to the end that he may work in us, is united with us only by the benefit of gracious operation: But the Holy Spirit, etc.

1 Cor. XII, 11. Therefore.

Resp.

The Holy Spirit works not absent, but present.

Gracious operation does not exclude special substantial presence, but presupposes it.

IV. The presence, inhabitation, and union of God the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit is the same: But the presence, inhabitation, and union of God the Father and the Holy Spirit and of Christ with us occurs according to divinity.

Resp.

The union and presence of the persons of the Trinity agrees by reason of the mode of uniting, which is divine and supernatural: nor does the human nature of Christ itself approach and unite with us in any other than a divine mode: but the notion of the union of the Father and the Son is different with respect to the object, or extreme.

The Father is a simple person, the Son is σύνθετος (composite): and therefore the latter is united with us according to both natures, since Christ is not some third thing, distinct from deity and humanity.

Furthermore, Christ is our head, spouse, vine, and mediator according to both natures, and so by reason of his mediatorial office he is also united with us according to the flesh.

V. Whoever are built together in the spirit with Christ, so that he may dwell in them through faith, they are not joined with the body of Christ: But the reborn, etc.

Eph. II, 22. c. III, 17. Therefore.

The major is clear: because the union which occurs in the spirit through faith is spiritual: but that which occurs with the body of Christ is corporal.

This therefore does not seem to be established, because Christ dwells in us through faith.

Resp.

Spiritual union is named from the mode of uniting, not from the object, or the extremes united.

Hence, although we are united with the body of Christ: it is not, however, to be called a corporal union, because it occurs through faith, kindled by the Holy Spirit, and therefore in a spiritual mode.

VI. The Weigelians and Schwenckfeldians maintain that the substance of God is united with the substance of the reborn man, from whose follies Catholics abhor.

Resp.

Our doctrine differs greatly from the opinion of the Weigelians and Schwenckfeldians: a) by reason of the productive and receptive medium.

For the adversaries subtract the power of uniting from the divine word, and say that faith consists in the imitation of Christ: b) by reason of the mode; since they assert that the mystical union occurs σωματικῶς (bodily), so that the divine essence becomes one essence with ours: c) by reason of the effect; because they opine that justification consists in the mystical union, so that by the benefit of this union the reborn are natural sons of God: d) by reason of the consequences; since the Weigelians invent that personal predications flow from the mystical union, so that a faithful man can affirm of himself: I am Christ.

Instantia: But LUTHER himself used that proposition in his commentary on Gal.

II, where he writes thus: Faith must be taught purely, namely that through it you are so glued into Christ, that from you & it becomes, as it were, one person, which cannot be separated, but perpetually adheres to Him, so that you may say with confidence: I am Christ, i.e., Christ’s righteousness, victory, and life are mine. And conversely, let Christ say: I am that sinner, i.e., his sins, death, etc., are mine; because he adheres to me, and I to him.

Resp. 1) LUTHER does not call Christ and the faithful man one person, but as it were a person. 2) Megalander should have shown that the regenerated man, having been made a partaker of the merit of Christ, applies it to himself by true faith in this way: Christ’s righteousness, victory, and life are mine. For just as Christ is imputatively a sinner, insofar as He voluntarily took upon Himself the sins of the world, so that the punishments for sins were transferred to Him by divine judgment: so the regenerated man, apprehending the merit of Christ by true faith and uniting it to himself, is imputatively Christ, insofar as the righteousness, victory, and life, procured by the merit of Christ, are transferred to him by divine estimation. 3) Luther speaks of the formal union of faith, by which Christ the mediator is apprehended; not of the mystical union, by which God dwells in the reconciled soul, which follows justification in the order of nature. But indeed, we rightly and deservedly abstain from this agraphon (unwritten) formula of speaking—difficult to understand, easy to twist—because of the corruptions of our adversaries after the controversies were stirred up, moved by the following reasons: a) Because John the Baptist explicitly says: I am not the Christ, Jo. I, 20. b) Paul does not say: I am Christ; but: Christ lives in me, Gal. II, 20. c) If that proposition "I am Christ" is deduced from the mystical union, a man who is out of his mind could say: I am God the Father, I am the Holy Spirit; because God the Father and the Holy Spirit also dwell in us. d) The Weigelians have progressed to such a degree of vanity that they have added to the aforementioned proposition predicates and works proper to Christ, and incommunicable to anything outside: *Christus wohnet also in den Wiedergebohrnen, daß ein solcher Mensch zu dem andern sagen könne: Ich Christus Jesus, das lebendige Wort Gottes, habe dich erlöset durch mein unschuldiges leiden.* Than which nothing more monstrous can be imagined.

Latin:

hinc fluentem amorem. Quo spectant verba S. Ioannis, 1 epist. IV, 15. Quisquis confessus fuerit, quod Iesus sit filius Dei, Deus in eo manet, & ipse in Deo. Et nos cognouimus, & credidimus dilectionem, quam habet Deus erga nos. Deus dilectio est; vnde, qui manet in dilectione, in Deo manet, & Deus in ipso. Fides renatorum nititur philanthropia Dei, quam luculentissime testatus est mittendo Iesum redemptorem; in quem renati credunt corde, & quem confitentur esse Filium Dei, hanc suam fidem amore in Deum exferentes. Inde fit, vt maneant in Deo, tanquam oceano bonitatis & caritatis, maneant in Christo, vt palmites in vite, & Deus maneat in ipsis, tanquam templis consecratis, quæ purificat, exornat, & omni plenitudine sapientiæ, iustitiæ & sanctitatis actiue implet: anima vere renata passiue perficitur, & velut vas gratia impletur.

Prob. e. Quod vnio Dei mystica non nuda adessentia substantiæ diuinæ absoluatur, sed efficacem etiam operationem complectatur, probatur: 1) Quemadmodum præsentia Dei ad creaturas non terminatur in sola adessentia, sed in adessentia cum operatione coniuncta; ita spiritualis nostra coniunctio cum Deo non terminatur in nuda adessentia substantiæ diuinæ ad substantiam hominis fidelis, sed efficacem operationem Dei in homine complectitur, vt recte colligamus: Vbicunque Deus est præsentia generali, ibi etiam operatur concursu generali. Ergo, vbi Deus præsens est præsentia speciali, ibi etiam operatur concursu speciali & gratioso.

2) Deus in hominibus iustificatis non tantum habitat, sed etiam ambulat, 2 Cor. VI, 16. h. e. præsens est ipsis, varias virtutum actiones, quibus ipsum colant, in iisdem excitando & operando.

3) Christus ita in fidelibus est, vt in iis viuat, Gal. II, 20. insignes fructus fidei pariat, Io. XV, 5. & regnum spirituale in cordibus eorum erigat, Luc. XVII, 21.

4) Spiritus S. vnitur cum fidelibus, vt eos omnia (ad salutem cognitu necessaria) doceat, 1 Io. II, 27. preces & suspiria excitet, Rom. VIII, 15. 16. consoletur, Io. XVI, 7. ducat in terra recta, Ps. CXLIII, 10. eosque sanctificet, Rom. XV, 16.

Prob. f. Quod vnio mystica renatis harmoniam affectuum cum Deo triuno conciliet, patet: quia 1) vnus cum Deo, cui agglutinati sunt, fiunt spiritus, 1 Cor. VI, 17. h. e. diuinæ sanctitatis, bonitatis, iustitiæ, veracitatis participes. 2) Imitantur iidem Deum amando, 1 Io. IV, 10. misericordiam ad exemplum patris cœlestis exercendo, Luc. VI, 36. sanctitati studendo, 1 Petr. I, 15. 16.

3) Quoniam beneficio vnionis mysticæ mentibus nostris imago Christi imprimitur, vt μορφωθῇ ἐν ἡμῖν, formam in nobis naiscatur, Gal. IV, 19.

Antithesis est 1. Weigelianorum & Schvenckfeldianorum, statuentium, mysticam cum Deo vnionem ratione modi esse & corporalem: 2. Quorundam Scholasticorum, Pontificiorum, Socinianorum & Arminianorum, negantium, Deum speciali præsentia substantialis modo in fidelibus habitare.

Weigelianorum potiora argumenta sunt: I. Quicunque vnum sunt in Deo Patre & Filio, sicut Pater est in Filio & Filius in Patre, vnio illorum est essentialis (nam vnio Patris & Filii est essentialis); Atqui renati &c. E. Minor patet e Io. XVII, 20. 21.

Resp. Verba textus citati sunt: Non pro his oro tantum, sed etiam pro iis, qui crediderint per verbum illorum in me; vt omnes vnum sint, sicut tu Pater in me, & ego in te, vt etiam in nobis vnum sint. E quibus verbis obseruare licet, particula a similitudinis καθὼς, sicut, non referendam esse ad vnionem mysticam cum Deo, sed vnionem ecclesiasticam renatorum inter se, quæ vnionis mysticæ effectus est. Ad hæc, licet particula similitudinis transferretur ad vnionem cum Deo mysticam, non tamen æqualitatem, sed aliquam conformitatem, non similitudinem absolutam, sed respectiuam inferret. mysticam, non tamen æqualitatem, sed aliqualem conformitatem, non similitudinem absolutam, sed refpectiuam inferret.

II. Qui

II. Quicunque sunt participes divinae naturae, illorum unio cum Deo est essentialis: Sed renati &c. 2 Petr. I, 4. E. Resp. Quicunque sunt participes divinae naturae participatione essentiali, qua Deo fiunt ὁμοούσιοι, illorum unio cum Deo est essentialis; concedo. At quicunque sunt participes naturae divinae participatione spirituali & gratiosa per fidem, illi Deo non sunt essentialiter vniti.

III. Quicunque cum Deo sunt vnus spiritus, illorum vnio cum Deo est essentialis: Atqui homines renati &c. 1 Cor. VI, 17. Resp. Quicunque cum Deo sunt vnum per se, illorum vnio cum Deo est essentialis. Sic limitata maiori negamus minorem; propterea, quod vnione mystica non constituitur vnum per se, sed per accidens. Ratio in promptu est; quia Deus & homo renatus complete existunt & subsistunt, adeoque per se vniri nequeunt.

IV. Quicunque sunt membra Christi, illi cum Christo sunt essentialiter iidem: Atqui renati &c. Eph. V, 30. E. Resp. Dist. inter membra naturalia, & mystica. Fideles non dicuntur membra Christi, ideo, quod eandem cum Christo habent naturam; quippe cuius etiam infideles sunt participes: sed ob cognationem spiritualem, quae connectitur ex parte Dei, vinculo verbi & sacramentorum, ex parte hominis renati, vinculo fidei. Sed cognatio spiritualis non infert vnionem essentialem.

V. Qui vniuntur cum Deo, vt palmites cum vite, coniunguntur cum illo essentialiter: Atqui renati &c. Io. XV, 5. E. Maior constat; quia vnio palmitum cum vite est essentialis. Resp: Simile non est extendendum vltra tertium. Christiani Christo iunguntur vere & realiter, non autem essentialiter. Differunt hac in parte palmites spirituales a naturalibus, quod hi iunguntur per naturam, illi per supernaturalem gratiam.

Argumenta Pontificiorum, Socinianorum atque Arminianorum sunt sequentia:

I. Quicunque per essentiam est immensus, infinitus, omnipraesens, & a nulla re creata localiter distans, is, cum sanctis specialiter praesens esse incipit, non potest speciali praesentia substantiali ad ipsos venire aut appropinquare; Atqui Deus &c. E. Maior patet: quia, vbi ens aliquod substantiali praesentia adest, eo non nisi per effectum, affectum, aut aliquod donum venit.

Resp. Neg. maiorem, cuius adducta ratio valet de ente finito, determinabilem, definitiuam ac circumscriptiuam praesentiam habente, non de ente infinito, siue Deo, qui distinctis adessendi modis praesens est. Infinitas & immensitas Spiritus S. non obstabat, quo minus is propius iungeretur columbae illi, in qua visibiliter descendebat super Christum in huius baptismo, quam aliis creaturis. Quin ὁ λόγος etiam infinitus & immensus proximius habitat in assumta carne propria & quidem σωματικῶς, Col. II, 9. quam in aliis hominibus sanctis. Tota SS. Trinitas propius adest & vnitur angelis & hominibus beatis, quam diabolis & damnatis. Non ergo sequitur: Vbicunque Deus secundum substantiam iam adest, eo non potest vllo modo secundum substantiam venire, aut appropinquare; sed hoc tantum sequitur, Deum secundum substantiam eo modo, quo iam adest, non posse approximare.

Dicis: Praesentiae gratiosae formale non in noua substantiae approximatione, sed in nouo, eoque speciali, operandi modo fundatur & terminatur. Resp. Nouus operandi modus peculiarem essentiae divinae approximationem non excludit, sed includit. In omnibus praesentiae divinae gradibus, siue modis, cum operatione praesentiae substantialis operatio est coniuncta. Id quod discimus e verbis Christi, Io XIV, 26. Paracletus autem Spiritus S. quem mittet Pater in nomine meo, ille vos docebit omnia. Vbi Christus discipulis iam ante regenitis tum gratiosum Spiritus S. aduentum, qua substantiam, tum specialem ipsius operationem, siue informationem promittit. II. Si Deus ratione substantiae arctius vniretur cum fidelibus, ratione substantiae etiam ab infidelibus recederet: Sed non recedit ratione substantiae ab infidelibus; quia ceteroqui non foret omnipraesens: E.

Ratione substantiae cum fidelibus non arctius iungitur.

Resp. Deus non recedit ab infidelibus, qua praesentiam generalem; recedit tamen, speciali praesentia eos dedignando, eo quod peccatoris malitiosae iniquitates Deum & peccatorem diuidunt atque separant, Es.

LIX, 2.

Neque tamen exinde infringitur omnipraesentia diuina; quia Deus non discedit physice & localiter, mutando locum, sed hyperphysice & illocaliter, domicilium cordis conspurcatum non inhabitando.

Instantia: Deus recedit ab infidelibus, gratiam suam subtrahendo.

Resp.

Deus recedit ab impiis tum gratiam, tum specialem essentiae suae propinquitatem subtrahendo.

Hinc cum Deus immorigeris Israëlitis comminaretur, Exod. XXXIII, 3.

Non ascendam in medio tui, eo quod populus durus ceruice tu, vt consumam te in via. ipse Deus propinquitatem suam specialem denegabat iisdem.

III. Qui cum in finem se nobiscum vnit, vt in nobis operetur, is beneficio gratiosae operationis tantum nobiscum vnitur: Atqui Spiritus S. &c.

1 Cor, XII, 11. E.

Resp.

Spiritus S. operatur non absens, sed praesens.

Gratiosa operatio specialem praesentiam substantialem non excludit, sed supponit.

IV. Dei Patris, Filii & Spiritus S. eadem est praesentia, eadem inhabitatio, eadem vnio: At Dei Patris & Spiritus S. & Christi praesentia, inhabitatio & vnio nobiscum fit secundum diuinitatem.

Resp.

Vnio & praesentia personarum Trinitatis conuenit ratione modi vniendi, qui diuinus & supernaturalis est: neque ipsa natura humana Christi alio, quam diuino modo nobis appropinquat & vnitur: sed diuersa est ratio vnionis Patris & Filii respectu obiecti, seu extremi.

Pater est persona simplex, Filius est σύνθετος: ideoque hic secundum vtramque naturam nobiscum vnitur, cum Christus non sit aliquod tertium, a deitate & humanitate distinctum.

Praeterea Christus est caput, sponsus, vitis & mediator noster secundum vtramque naturam, adeoque ratione officii mediatorii etiam secundum carnem nobiscum vnitur.

V. Quicunque cum Christo sunt coaedificati in spiritu, vt in ipsis per fidem habitet, illi cum corpore Christi non coniunguntur: Atqui renati &c.

Eph. II, 22. c. III, 17. E.

Maior liquet: quia vnio, quae fit in spiritu per fidem, est spiritualis: sed, quae fit cum corpore Christi, est corporalis.

Haec ideo statuenda non videtur, quia Christus per fidem in nobis habitat.

Resp.

Vnio spiritualis appellatur a modo vniendi, non ab obiecto, aut extremis vnitis.

Hinc, licet vniamur cum corpore Christi: non tamen vocanda est vnio corporalis, quia fit per fidem, a Spiritu S. accensam, adeoque modo spirituali.

VI. Weigeliani & Schwenckfeldiani statuunt, substantiam Dei cum substantia hominis renati vniri, a quorum omniis abhorrent Catholici.

Resp.

Nostra doctrina ab opinione Weigelianorum & Schwenckfeldianorum maxime differt: a) ratione medii productiui & receptiui.

Nam aduersarii vim vniendi verbo diuino subtrahunt, & fidem in imitatione Christi consistere aiunt: b) ratione modi; quoniam illi afferunt, vnionem mysticam fieri σωματικῶς, vt essentia diuina cum nostra fiat vna essentia: c) ratione effectus; quia opinantur, iustificationem in vnione mystica consistere, vt beneficio huius vnionis renati sint filii Dei naturales: d) ratione consequentium; quoniam Weigeliani comminiscuntur, ex vnione mystica fluere praedicationes personales, vt homo fidelis de seipso affirmare possit: Ego sum Christus.

Instantia: Sed ipse LVTHERVS ea propositione vsus est in commentar. ad Gal.

II. vbi ita scribit: Fides pure docenda est, quod scilicet per eam sic conglutineris in Christo, vt ex te & ipso fiat una quasi persona, quæ non possit segregari, sed perpetuo adhærescat ei, ut cum fiducia dicere possis: Ego sum Christus, h. e. Christi iustitia, victoria, vita est mea. Et vicissim Christus dicat: Ego sum ille peccator, h. e. eius peccata, mors & c. sunt meæ; quia adhæret mihi, & ego illi.

Resp. 1) LUTHERUS Christum & hominem fidelem non vocat unam personam, sed quasi personam. 2) Megalander ostensurus fuit, hominem renatum effectum, merito Christi partum, vera fide sibi applicare hoc modo: Christi iustitia, victoria, vita est mea. Quemadmodum enim Christus imputative est peccator, quatenus is peccata mundi sponte sua in se suscepit, ut pænæ peccatorum iudicio divino in ipsum sint translatæ: ita homo renatus, meritum Christi vera fide apprehendens, fibique uniens, est imputative Christus, quatenus iustitia, victoria & vita, merito Christi conciliata, æstimatione divina in ipsum transfertur. 3) Loquitur Lutherus de unione formali fidei, qua Christus mediator apprehenditur; non de unione mystica, qua Deus in anima reconciliata habitat, quæ iustificationem ordine naturæ sequitur. At vero a formula loquendi ἀγράφῳ, intellectu difficili, contortu facili, ob corruptelas adversariorum post mota certamina iure meritoque abstinemus moti sequentibus rationibus: a) Quia Ioannes baptista diserte dicit: Ego non sum Christus, Io. I, 20. b) Paullus non dicit: Ego sum Christus; sed: Christus vivit in me, Gal. II, 20. c) Si propositio illa: Ego sum Christus ex unione mystica deducitur, posset homo mentis impos dicere: Ego sum Deus Pater, ego sum Spiritus Sanctus; quia etiam Deus Pater & Spiritus S. in nobis habitat. d) Eo vanitatis progressi sunt Weigeliani, ut fæpius memoratæ propositioni addiderint prædicata & opera Christo propria, & ad extra incommunicabilia: Christus wohnet also in den Wiedergebohrnen, daß ein solcher Mensch zu dem andern sagen könne: Ich Christus Jesus, das lebendige Wort Gottes, habe dich erlöset durch mein unschuldiges leiden. Quo nihil monstrosius fingi potest.


### Q. XIII

What is the end of the mystical union? The ultimate end of the mystical union is eternal life a). The intermediate ends and effects are various: communion with God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit b), the certification of faith c), divine aid d), efficacious consolation e), the excitation of prayers and their hearing f), preservation in the state of grace, from which arises the perseverance of the faithful g), sanctification h), the sealing of the future glorious resurrection and heavenly inheritance i), the union of the regenerated among themselves and the communion of the church k).

Prob. b. From 1 Jo. I, 3. That which we have seen and heard, we announce to you, that you also may have communion with us, and our communion is truly with the Father, and with His Son Jesus. Compare 2 Cor. XIII, 13. The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit (be) with you all! Amen! Since the mystical union is perichoristic, it brings about our communion with the Triune God. Therefore, the regenerated, through communion with God the Father, are His own sons and heirs of eternal life; through communion with the Holy Spirit, they are His vessels, dwellings, and temples. Prob. c.

From 2 Cor. XIII, 5. Test yourselves, whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Do you not recognize yourselves, that Jesus Christ is in you? Those in whom Jesus Christ is by special presence, they certainly know that they are ingrafted into Christ by faith, while they test and prove their faith from the peace of conscience, inward joy, living hope, unto which they are regenerated through the resurrection of Christ from the dead, 1 Petr. I, 3. But he who proves his faith by careful examination, and knows, that Christ is in him and lives, he is certain of his faith, and consequently of the grace, which is apprehended by faith. Conf. 2 Tim. I, 12. Prob. d. From 1 John IV, 4. Little children, you are of God, and have overcome them (the false prophets), because greater is he, who is in you, than he who is in the world.

Men reborn and confirmed in the knowledge of heavenly truth overcome the temptations of false teachers, aided by the Holy Spirit dwelling in them, who is greater and more powerful than that spirit which is in the world, i.e., the devil. Prob. e.

From Ps. LVII, 15. Thus said the high and lofty one, who inhabits eternity, and whose name is holy: I dwell in the high and holy place; yet with the contrite and humble I am, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the contrite heart. God, joined in a spiritual manner with the contrite and humble heart, fills it with living consolation, just as if a torrent of pleasure were flooding it. Prob. f. Prob. f.

From Gal. IV, 6. Because you are sons, God has sent forth the Spirit of his Son into your hearts, crying: Abba Father! Which words the blessed Hunnivs explains

Q. XIV.

What things dissolve the mystical union? The mystical union is dissolved by a) ἀπισία, or unbelief, b) impiety of life.

Prob. a. Just as true faith is the chain by which God is connected with the reborn soul; Cant. IV, 9. so unbelief is the dissolution of that chain. But since faith exerts itself through desires, groans, and prayers; it is easily conjectured that by the intermission of prayers the mystical union with God is broken. God abandons him by whom He is abandoned.

Prob. b. Your iniquities have been separating between you and your God, Is. LIX, 2. Those who live according to the flesh, die, that is, they lose the grace of God, the Holy Spirit, and faith, Rom. VIII, 13. These being lost, the bond of gracious union is dissolved.

Q. XV.

What kinds of predications arise from the mystical union? Predications from the mystical union flow appropriately a), and causally b).

Prob. a. He who persecutes true Christians, persecutes Christ, Acts IX, 4. Predications from the mystical union flow in the communion of Christ the head with Christians, as spiritual members. He who inflicts injury upon these, or does them good, is considered to inflict injury upon, or do good to, the head Christ Himself; since Christ appropriates their injury or good deeds to Himself, not ὑποστατικῶς (hypostatically), on account of personal communion, but σχετικῶς (relatively), on account of spiritual communion and respect. Prob. b.

From Gal. II, 20. But I live no longer, but Christ lives in me. The sense is: I do not live by myself independently, but Christ effects in me the motion, sense, and continuation of spiritual life.

SIGH.

It is a stupendous mystery that Thou, immortal God, in me a mortal, most high in me most humble, most rich in me most poor, most holy in me a sinner, shouldst not disdain to fix a seat and dwelling for Thyself! I ingenuously confess that I am unworthy that Thou shouldst enter into the chamber of my heart. Nevertheless, it pleased Thy majesty to be in me through grace, that I might be in Thee through trust. Therefore Thou art present, Thou reignest, Thou teachest in my soul, as a Bishop in a temple, a King in a palace, a Doctor in a school: but I am in Thee, as a branch in a tree, a shoot in a vine, a ray in the sun. To whom is there available such an abundant supply of speech, that by speaking he could express the inestimable benefit and incomparable bond of union, by which Thou hast bound me closely to Thee, that I might be one spirit with Thee, a partaker of Thy wisdom, justice, holiness, peace, joy, and glory? Nothing is so much a care and concern to my heart as that I may be Thy son and that this most pleasant communion may be constant, perennial, and indissoluble. I pray, therefore, and beseech Thee, God the Father, that Thou mayest eternally be and remain my most benign father, and I may be and remain Thy most obedient son! Remain, Lord Jesus, my head, that I may remain Thy member! Remain, O Holy Spirit, my perpetual guest, that I may remain Thy dwelling-place, so that neither the rage of the devil, nor the snares of the world, nor the allurements of the flesh may ever dissolve or tear apart our conjunction!

Latin:

Finis unionis mysticæ ultimus est vita æterna a). Fines intermedii & effectus sunt varii: communio cum Deo Patre, Filio & Spiritu S. b), certificatio fidei c), auxilii divini d), efficacis solatii e), excitatio precum, earumque exauditio f), conferuatio in statu gratiæ, unde nascitur perseverantia fidelium g), sanctificatio h), obsignatio futuræ gloriosæ resurrectionis & cœlestis hereditatis i), unio renatorum inter se & communio ecclesiæ k). Prob. a. Si in vobis manet, quod ab initio audivistis, etiam vos in Filio, & in Patre manebitis. Et hæc est promissio, quam ille promisit nobis, vitam æternam, 1 Io. II, 24. 25.

Prob. b. Ex 1 Io. I, 3. Quod vidimus & audivimus, annuntiamus vobis, ut etiam vos communionem habeatis nobiscum, & communio vero nostra cum Patre, & cum Filio eius Iesu. Confer. 2 Cor. XIII, 13. Gratia Domini Iesu Christi, & amor Dei, & communicatio S. Spiritus (fit) cum omnibus vobis! Amen! Cum unio mystica fit perichoristica, infert communionem nostri cum Deo trinuno. Sunt igitur renati per communionem cum Deo Patre ipsius filii & heredes vitæ æternæ; per communionem cum Spiritu S. sunt ipsius vasa, domicilia & templa. Prob. c.

Ex 2 Cor. XIII, 5. Vos ipsos tentate, num sitis in fide? vos ipsos probate. An non cognoscitis vos ipsos, quod Iesus Christus in vobis sit. In quibus Iesus Christus est præsentia speciali, illi certo sciunt, se per fidem Christo esse insitos, dum fidem suam tentant & probant ex pace conscientiæ, gaudio interno, spe viva, ad quam regenerati sunt per resurrectionem Christi ex mortuis, 1 Petr. I, 3. Qui autem accurato examine fidem suam probat, cognoscit, Christum in se esse ac vivere, is fidei suae, atque adeo gratiae, quae fide apprehenditur, certus est. Conf. 2 Tim. I, 12.

Prob. d. Ex 1 Io. IV, 4. Filioli, vos ex Deo estis, & vicistis illos (pseudo-prophetas), quia maior est..., qui in vobis est, quam qui in mundo. Homines renati atque in agnitione veritatis coelestis confirmati vincunt tentamenta falsorum doctorum, adiuti a Spiritu S. in ipsis habitante, qui maior & potentior est eo spiritu, qui in mundo est, h. e. diabolo.

Prob. e. Ex Ps. LVII, 15. Sic dixit altus & excelsus, habitans aeternum, & cuius nomen sanctum: In alto & sancto habito; attamen cum contrito & humili sum ad vivificandum spiritum humilium, & ad vivificandum cor contritum. Deus cum corde contrito & humili modo spirituali coniunctus illud vivo solatio perfundit, perinde, ac si torrens voluptatis illud inundaret.

Prob. f. Ex Gal. IV, 6. Quia filii estis, emisit Deus Spiritum Filii sui in corda vestra, clamantem: Abba Pater! Quae verba exponit B. Hunnivs

Quæst. XIV.

Quænam dissoluunt vnionem mysticam? Unionem mysticam dissoluit a) ἀπισία, siue infidelitas, b) vitæ impietas.

Prob. a. Quemadmodum vera fides est catena, qua Deus cum anima renata connectitur; Cant. IV, 9. ita incredulitas est dissolutio illius catenæ. Cum autem fides se exserat desideriis, gemitibus & precibus; coniectu proclue est, intermissione precum vnionem cum Deo mysticam disrumpi. Deserit illum Deus, a quo deseritur.

Prob. b. Iniquitates vestræ fuerunt diuidentes inter vos, & Deum vestrum, Es. LIX, 2. Qui secundum carnem viuunt, moriuntur, h. e. gratiam Dei, Spiritum S. & fidem amittunt, Rom. VIII, 13. Quibus amissis, vinculum vnionis gratiosæ solutum est.

Quæst. XV.

Quales prædicationes fiunt ex vnione mystica? Prædicationes ex vnione mystica fluunt appropriatiue a), & causales b).

Prob. a. Qui veros christianos persequitur, persequitur Christum, Act. IX, 4. Prædicationis ex vnione mystica fluunt in communione capitis Christi cum christianis, tanquam spiritualibus membris. Qui his iniuriam infert, aut benefacit, ipsi capiti Christo iniuriam inferre, aut benefacere censetur; cum Christus illorum iniuriam, aut benefacta sibi appropriet, non ὑποστατικῶς, ob communionem personalem, sed σχετικῶς, ob communionem & respectum spiritualem.

Prob. b. Ex Gal. II, 20. Viuo autem non amplius ego, sed viuit in me Christus. Sensus est: Non viuo per me ipsum independenter, sed spiritualis vitæ motum, sensum, continuationem Christus in me efficit.

SVSPIRIVM.

Stupendum est mysterium, quod tu, Deus immortalis, in me mortali, celsissimus in me humillimo, ditissimus in me pauperrimo, sanctissimus in me peccatore, sedem tibi atque domicilium figere, haud dedigneris! Indignum me esse, qui in conclaue cordis mei intres, ingenue fateor. Nihilo tamen minus collibuit maiestati tuæ, esse in me per gratiam, vt in te sim per fiduciam. Idcirco præsto es, regnas, doces in anima mea, vt Episcopus in templo, Rex in regia, Doctor in schola: ego autem in te sum, vt ramus in arbore, palmes in vite, radius in sole. Eccui suppetit tam vber fandi copia, vt dicendo exprimere queat inæstimabile beneficium & incomparabile vnionis vinculum, quo me arte tibi deuinxisti, vt vnus tecum sim spiritus, tuæ sapientiæ, iustitiæ, sanctitatis, pacis, gaudii, gloriæ particeps? Nihil adeo mihi curæ cordique est, quam vt tuus filius & iucundissima hæc communio fit constans, perennis, indissolubilis. Precor igitur, & obtestor te, Deus Pater, vt æternum fis & maneas meus pater benignissimus, & ego sim maneamque tuus filius obedientissimus! Maneas, Domine Iesu, meum caput, vt ego maneam tuum membrum! Maneas, o Spiritus S., meus hospes perpetuus, vt ego maneam tuum habitaculum, quo nostram coniunctionem neque diaboli rabies, neque mundi insidiæ, neque carnis illecebræ soluant vnquam, aut diuellant!


## 25 On Renewing Grace, and Renewal

Q. I.

What is renewal? Renewal is an act of grace by which the Holy Spirit endows a justified man, with vices expelled, with inherent holiness. The ultimate end of the mystical union is eternal life a). The intermediate ends and effects are various: communion with God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit b), certification of faith c), divine aid d), efficacious consolation e), the stirring up of prayers and their being heard f), preservation in the state of grace, from which arises the perseverance of the faithful g), sanctification h), the sealing of the future glorious resurrection and heavenly inheritance i), the union of the reborn among themselves and the communion of the church k).

It is more fully defined: Renovation is an act of the applying grace, by which the Holy Spirit abolishes in the justified man the remnants of sin inherent in him, so that they may not rule, and produces in him internal and external motions conformable to the divine will, and thus spiritually good, so that, endowed with the restored divine image, he may live soberly, justly, and piously to the praise of the most holy God.

Obs. I. Renovation in general denotes any action by which those things which have been worn away, weakened, or corrupted by age are restored. And thus in the spiritual renovation of man, taken more broadly, the old man is understood to be abolished according to all his condition, i.e., the total lack of spiritual powers, the guilt and dominion of sin, and the new man is understood to be produced according to his breadth, i.e., the spiritual powers themselves, absolution from guilt, and the habitual gift by which the dominion of sin is suppressed. In this broader sense, the word "renovation" is taken in the Declar. Form.
