At renati vincunt, sicut Iosua superauit Cananeos, næs, non vt exstirpentur carnales mundi cupiditates, sed vt hi hostes spirituales mittantur sub iugum, quamuis impatientes iugi dominium subinde affectent.


### Q. XVIII. Is the renewal of the justified man in this life perfect?

The renewal of the justified man in this life is imperfect. The defect of perfection in the work of renewal, however, is not on the part of God, but on the part of man, who does not sufficiently receive the action of the renewing God.

Proved a. 1) There is no man who does not sin, 1 Kings VIII, 46. There is no just man upon earth, who does good, so that he does not sin, Eccles. VII, 20. 2) The regenerate have sin, 1 John I, 8; they often slip, James III, 2. 3) The struggle of the flesh and the spirit in the regenerate abundantly testifies to the imperfection of renewal. For in those in whom the flesh lusts against the spirit, so that they do not do whatever they wish, they, even if they do not wish to sin, nevertheless sometimes do sin: But in the regenerate the flesh lusts &c: Therefore. The minor is evident from Gal. V, 17; Rom. VII, 14 seqq. 4) The exhortations of the Holy Spirit to the regenerate also testify to the imperfection of renewal, by which they are reminded not to walk according to the flesh, but according to the spirit, Rom. VIII, 13; Gal. V, 24; Eph. IV, 22; Col. III, 9, 10; 1 Pet. II, 11; 1 John II, 1. 5) The regenerate must daily ask God for the remission of sins, Matt. VI, 12; Ps. XXXII, 6. Therefore they are not devoid of sins. 6) Many regenerate have fallen gravely, such as Noah, Lot, Aaron, David, Peter & others, whose renewal, had it been perfect, would have averted every moral fall.

From Rom. VIII, 3. For what was impossible for the law, in that it was weak through the flesh, God (did), who sent his own son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin condemned sin in the flesh, that the justification of the law might be fulfilled in us, who walk not according to the flesh, but according to the spirit. Obj. a) The ἀδυναμία, or inability to justify and save [*], is attributed to the law, not intrinsic, but external, which is not so much of the law as of the flesh that weakens it; insofar as after the fall there no longer survive in man the powers necessary for rendering the due obedience to the law. b) What Christ acquired for us by his death did not beget in us the power of meriting, nor did it instill into the law some new faculty; but it consists in his vicarious obedience and satisfaction, which excludes our satisfaction or perfect fulfillment of the law.

The antithesis is that of the Papists, Socinians, Arminians, Anabaptists, Schwenckfeldians & Weigelians, who dream of the perfection of renewal. They oppose us with the following arguments:

1. Christ commands: Be perfect, as your heavenly father is perfect, Matt. V, 48. Resp. The consequence from a precept to an effect, from a duty to the δύναμιν, or faculty of performing, is not valid. The particle, as, denotes not equality, but similarity, insofar as we strive to imitate God in the sincerity of love []. II. Renewed men are perfect: Therefore, renewal is perfect. The antecedent is established from Phil. 3:15, Heb. 5:14. Response: Renewed men are called perfect not absolutely, but comparatively, by comparing men. He therefore commands us to be perfect as God is, not in every way and degree, but in the matter of love toward men, so that we may pursue all with love, even those who are our enemies, for he who is accustomed to hate them cannot be born again. It is indeed a very true distinction of perfection—that one kind is of parts, another of degrees—but it must be used cautiously and accurately. I. The perfection of parts is the religious observance of all those things which are contained within the entire scope of the law. See Rom. 13:8, 9, 10; Jas. 2:10 ff. These parts can conveniently be divided into major and essential ones, so to speak, and minor and integral ones. The former are as many as there are precepts and prohibitions. By the name of the latter, I understand the individual circumstances in each case, whether commanded or forbidden, such as: the subject, both objects (both real and personal), the manner of acting, the place, the time, and the end. Our Liberator discusses this integral perfection of parts in Matt. 5:48. He explains there a certain part of the divine laws, namely that by which we are bound to love men, and specifically regarding that circumstance which is wont to be called the personal object—who ought to be understood by this name, *ho plēsion* (the neighbor). Every renewed man, therefore, cultivates these parts, and indeed of both kinds, so holily that he does not deviate from any of them knowingly and willingly; for it is acknowledged that not even one voluntary sin can be committed by a man as long as he is and remains in a state of renewal. II. The perfection of degrees is the highest integrity of mind, and altogether so great and so perpetual that at no time and in no way does a man think or undertake anything contrary to any part of the law, nor does he even feel any enticements to sin; indeed, he even casts off, having been torn out by the roots, the innate propensity to sin. This is something that has never happened to anyone in this mortality, nor will it happen. Ps. 19:13, 143:3, Phil. 3:12, Jas. 3:2, 1 Cor. 4:4. If any perfection of degrees seems to be attributed to some, it is so called not simply, but comparatively; for one who is progressing has certainly attained a greater degree than one who is beginning. Eph. 4:13, 14; 1 Cor. 2:6 and 3:1; Heb. 5:13, 14.

A controversy was once agitated concerning this: whether a renewed man is able, in this life, to arrive at a degree of legal perfection next to the highest? We deny and utterly deny this. The matter will be clear if we explain it by definition. This highest degree would be: if there were no hereditary sin in man, no propensity to do evil. But such integrity is proper to Christ alone (Luke 1:35, 1 John 3:5) and is never to be attributed to us as long as we are mortal (1 John 1:8). The second degree, next to that one, would be if there never existed in us any motion of innate propensity enticing us to sin, no forbidden thought, no unjust desire. But in truth, no one among the renewed is free and void of the stimuli and enticements *tēs sarkos* (of the flesh) (Rom. 6:12, 7:17, 23; Gal. 5:16, 17, 24). The third degree, inferior to the second, would be if no external act contrary to the law were ever committed out of ignorance, error, or haste of mind. And not even this is anyone able to do in this mortality (Jas. 3:2). The fourth degree is an effective endeavor and most ardent zeal for acquiring a richer knowledge of things and for correcting one's life more and more, with easier effort and firmer alacrity. Those who are progressing do this (Eph. 4:13, 14; 1 Thess. 4:1). The fifth and lowest degree is resistance against the motions of innate desire and the studious avoidance of all voluntary sins. And this belongs to all the renewed, even if they are beginners (1 John 3:6, 9; Gal. 5:16, 24). Most correctly, therefore, our elders pronounced: that the begun fulfillment of the law is far removed from perfection. In *Apol. Aug. Conf.*, ch. 3, p. 115, and thus frequently.

Therefore, legal perfection does not fall to any renewed man. Therefore, everyone needs evangelical perfection, which we shall accurately define as to what kind it is. It is, indeed,

I. One kind falsely so called, by an intolerable opinion

Generally of all those who confuse these two, the law and the gospel, with each other, and indeed even err vehemently in the definition of both.

Specifically of two sects above all:

1) The Roman Catholics, who, having taken this principle—that Christ added certain evangelical counsels to the laws—say that evangelical perfection is the observance not only of the precept. prepared, so that the perfect may be opposed to the infirm, who like children had scarcely learned the first rudiments of the Christian doctrine.

The Apostle himself denies that he is absolutely perfect, Phil. III, 12. III. Noah is said to have been a just and perfect man, Gen. VI, 9. Josiah, 2 Chron. XXXIV, 2. Daniel, ch. VI, 22. They were men praised for perfect sincerity, not for consummation.

Their lapses and blemishes are recounted: namely, Noah overwhelmed himself with wine,

Gen. IX, 21. Josiah brought an unnecessary war upon Pharaoh Necho, to his own and his people's detriment, 2 Chron. XXXV, 20. Daniel confesses his sins, ch. IX, 5. IV. The love of God is said to be perfect in us, 1 John IV, 12: But love is the formal effect of renewal: Therefore renewal is also perfect; because an effect is not more excellent than its cause. Resp.

In the place cited, it is not understood as the active love of God, by which we love God, but the passive, by which we are loved by God. Not the former, but the latter is perfect in us, since it is perfectly declared toward us, and sealed in our hearts by the Holy Spirit. V. In whom Christ dwells, in them there is no iniquity: because there is no communion of justice with iniquity, 2 Cor. VI, 15: But in the justified, etc. Eph. III, 17. Resp.

In the justified there is no iniquity: because a) sins are remitted to them in justification: b) because they are freed from the dominion of sin in renewal: yet there remain in them inordinate motions and sins of infirmity.

VI. Whoever are dead to sin, in them sin is not given: for to whom one is dead, to him one is no longer devoted or subject: But renewed men, etc. Rom. VI, 2. Resp. Renewed men are dead to sin, so that it may not reign in their mortal body, Rom. VI, 22, although it dwells in the same and occasionally affects dominion. VII. Whoever is so renewed that he is a new creature, and all his things are new, he is perfectly renewed. But justified men, etc. 2 Cor. V, 17. Resp.

A justified man is said to be a new creature proximately and immediately on account of regeneration, which is as it were a new creation, which we do not deny to be perfect; but consequently, only mediately and remotely, on account of the gift of renewal. Conf. Hülsemann, Brev. enucl. p. 692. Furthermore, old things are said to have passed away, and all things to be new: a) because Christ has acquired new grace and a new spirit for all: b) because He offers new grace to all, and confers it upon believers; which new grace would also work perfectly in all, were it not hindered by the oldness of indwelling sin. VIII. Every action of the Holy Spirit is perfect: But renewal, etc. Therefore. The major is evident: because the Holy Spirit, possessing infinite power, acts perfectly.

Resp. Every action of the Holy Spirit in of those who have begun, but also of their counsels; but in very truth it is nothing but arbitrary worship, confirmed by the authority of the Roman Pontiff, especially the monastic kind of life.

This error of theirs is detested by our countrymen, in the Aug. Conf. p. 17 & 36, and its Apology p. 282, 286. 2) Of the Socinians, who, as they invent new laws, finally laid down by Christ, and are accustomed to wrongly designate them by the name of the Gospel, so they place evangelical perfection in obedience, rendered equally to all these new commands of Christ, as well as to the ancient moral and natural law.

II. But the other is true, which is the remission of all sins, liberation and freedom from all both guilt and punishment, on account of the most consummate righteousness and vicarious obedience of Christ, rendered entirely to the law, and imputed to us. Rom. VIII, 1, 2, 3. Eph. V, 26, 27. Col. II, 10, coll. with the following verses 12, 13.

Latin:

Renouatio hominis iustificati in hac vita est imperfecta . Defectus autem perfectionis in opere renouationis non est ex parte Dei, sed ex parte hominis, actionem Dei renouantis non sufficienter recipientis .

Prob. a. 1) Non est homo, qui non peccet, 1 Reg. VIII, 6. Non est homo iustus in terra, qui faciat bonum, ita, ut non peccet, Ecclef. VII, 20. 2) Renati habent peccatum, 1 Io. I, 8. sæpe labuntur, Iac. III, 2. 3) De imperfectione renouationis abunde testatur lucta carnis & spiritus in renatis. In quibus enim caro concupiscit aduersus spiritum, vt non faciant, quæcunque volunt, illi, etiamsi peccare nolint, quandoque tamen peccant: Atqui in renatis caro concupiscit &c: E. Minor patet ex Gal. V, 17. Rom. VII, 14. seqq. 4) De imperfectione renouationis testantur etiam adhortationes Spiritus S. ad renatos, quibus commonefiunt, ne secundum carnem ambulent, sed secundum spiritum, Rom. VIII, 13. Gal. V, 24. Eph. IV, 22. Col. III, 9. 10. 1 Petr. II, 11. 1 Io. II, 1. 5) Renatis quotidie a Deo petenda est remissio peccatorum, Matth. VI, 12. Pf. XXXII, 6. E. peccatorum non sunt expertes. 6) Multi renati grauiter lapsi sunt, vt Noachus, Lothus, Aaron, Dauid, Petrus & alii, quorum renouatio si fuisset perfecta, omnem lapsum moralem auertisset.

Prob. b. Ex Rom. VIII, 3. Nam impossibile legis, dum infirmatum est per carnem, Deus (præstitit), qui fuit ipsus filium misit in similitudine carnis peccati, & pro peccato condemnavit peccatum in carne, ut iustificatio legis in nobis impleretur, qui non secundum carnem ambulamus, sed secundum spiritum. Obf. a) Legi tribuitur ἀδυναμία, seu impotentia iustificandi & faluandi [*], non intrinseca, sed externa, quæ non est tam legis, quam carnis infirmantis; quatenus non amplius post lapsum superstites sunt vires in homine, ad obedientiam debitam, legi præstandam, necessariæ. b) Quod Christus morte sua nos acquisivit, non peperit in nobis vim merendi, nec legi indidit facultatem quandam nouam; sed consistit in obedientia & satisfactione vicaria, quæ nostram satisfactionem, aut perfectam legis impletionem excludit.

Antithesis est Pontificiorum, Socinianorum, Arminianorum, Anabaptistarum, Schwenckfeldianorum & Weigelianorum, perfectionem renouationis somniantium. Obluctantur nobis sequentibus argumentis:

1. Christus præcipit: Estote perfecti, sicut pater vester cœlestis perfectus est, Matth. V, 48. Resp. A præcepto ad effectum, a debito ad præstandi δύναμιν, feu facultatem, non valet consequentia. Particula, sicut, non æqualitatem, sed similitudinem notat, in quantum conamur Deum sinceritate dilectionis imitari []. II. Homines renouati funt perfecti: E. renouatio eft perfecta. Antecedens conftat ex Phil. III, 15. Hebr. V, 14. Refp. Homines renouati dicuntur perfecti non abfolute, fed comparate, confert homines. Iubet igitur nos ita perfectos effe, vt Deus eft, non omni modo & gradu, fed ratione amoris in homines, vt eos amore profequamur omnes, etiam nobis inimicos, quos qui odiffe folet, is non poteft effe denuo natus. Eft profecto veriffima; fed & caute adcurateque vfurpanda, diftinctio perfectionis, quod alia fit partium, alia graduum. I. Perfectio partium eft religiofa obferuantia eorum omnium, quæ vniuerfo legis ambitu continentur. Vid. Rom. XIII, 8. 9. 10. Iac. II, 10. feqq. Hæ partes commode poffunt diuidi in maiores atque effentiales, vt ita dicam, & minores atque integrales. Ille tot funt, quot funt præcepta & vetita. Harum nomine intelligo fingulas res circumftantes in vno quoque, fiue imperato, fiue interdicto, vt funt: Subiectum, Obiectum vtrumque, tum reale, tum perfonale, modus agendi, locus, tempus, finis. De hac partium perfectione integrali differit Liberator nofter, Matth. V, 48. Exponit ibi de quadam parte legum diuinarum, quippe de ea, qua hominibus amandis deuincti fumus, & fingulatim quidem de ea re circumftante, quæ vocari folet Obiectum perfonale, quis nomine hoc, ὁ πλησίον, debeat intelligi. Has igitur partes, & quidem vtriufque generis, homo renouatus quifque adeo fancte colit, vt a nulla earum fciens volenfque deflectat: eft enim in confeffo, quod ne vnum quidem peccatum voluntarium committi poffit ab homine, quoad ipfe eft manetque in ftatu renouationis. II. Graduum perfectio eft fumma animi integritas, atque omnino tanta, tamque perpetua, vt nullo tempore, nulloque modo, aliquid, vlli legis parti contrarium, homo cogitet fufcipiatque, ac ne vllas quidem fentiat peccandi illecebras, immo & innatam ad peccandum propenfionem radicitus euulfam abiiciat. Id quod in hac mortalitate nemini vnquam contigit, aut continget. Pf. XIX, 13. CXLIII, 3. Phil. III, 12. Iac. III, 2. 1 Corinth. IV, 4. Si qua graduum perfectio quibufdam tribui videtur, eft ea non fimpliciter, fed comparate fic dicta; proficiens enim maiorem profecto gradum affequutus eft, quam incipiens. Eph. IV, 13. 14. 1 Cor. II, 6. & III, 1. Hebr. V, 13. 14.

Controuerfia quondam agitata fuit de eo: an ne valeat homo renouatus, in hac vita, pervenire ad gradum perfectionis legalis a fummo proximum? Hoc negamus ac pernegamus. Perfpicua res erit, fi eam definitione explicauerimus. Summus gradus hic effet: fi nullum in homine effet peccatum hæreditarium, nulla ad male agendum propenfio. Atqui tanta integritas eft vnius Chrifti propria, Luc. I, 35. 1 Ioann. III, 5. nobis, quoad mortales fumus nunquam tribuenda, 1 Ioann. I, 8. Secundus gradus, ab illo proximus, foret, fi nulli vnquam in nobis exfifteret motus innatæ propenfionis, nos ad peccandum adlicientis, nulla cogitatio vetita, nulla cupiditas iniufta. At enim vero ftimulis atque illecebris τῆς σαρκὸς liber ac vacuus eft nemo renouatorum, Rom. VI, 12. VII, 17. 23. Gal. V, 16. 17. 24. Tertius gradus, fecundo inferior, effet, fi actus externus, legi contrarius, nullus vnquam committeretur, ex ignorantia, errore, aut feftinatione animi. Ac ne id quidem valet quifquam in hac mortalitate, Iac. III, 2. Quartus gradus eft conatus efficax, ftudiumque ardentiffimum, vberioris rerum cognitionis adquirendæ, & vitæ magis magifque corrigendæ, faciliore negotio, ac firmiore alacritate. Hoc agunt proficientes, Eph. IV, 13. 14. 1 Theff. IV, 1. Quintus atque infimus gradus eft repugnantia aduerfus motus innatæ cupiditatis, ac ftudiofa deuitatio omnium peccatorum voluntariorum. Atque hoc eft renouatorum omnium, etiam fi fint incipientes. 1 Io. III, 6. 9. Gal. V, 16. 24. Rectiffime igitur pronuntiarunt Maiores noftri: quod inchoata legis impletio procul abfit a perfectione. In Apol. Aug. Conf. c. III. p. 115. atque ita fæpius.

Itaque perfectio legalis non cadit in vllum hominem renouatum. Ergo indiget vnus quifque perfectione euangelica, quæ cuiufmodi fit, adcurate definiamus. Eft nimirum ea

I. Alia quidem falfo fic dicta, intolerabili opinione

Generatim eorum omnium, qui hæc duo, legem & euangelium inter fe confundunt, immo etiam in definitione vtriufque vehementer errant.

Speciatim duarum potiffimum fectarum:

1) Romano-Catholicorum, qui, fumto hoc principio, quod Chriftus confilia quædam euangelica legibus adiunxerit, perfectionem euangelicam dicunt effe obferuantiam non folum præcepto. parate, ut perfecti opponantur infirmis, qui instar puerorum vix prima rudimenta doctrinae christianae didicerant.

Ipse Apostolus negat, se absolute perfectum esse, Phil. III, 12. III. Noachus dicitur fuisse vir iustus & perfectus, Gen. VI, 9. Iosias, 2 Paral. XXXIV, 2. Daniel, cap. VI, 22. Fuerunt viri laudati perfectae sinceritatis, non consummationis.

Recensentur illorum lapsus & naevi: nimirum Noachus vino se obruit,

Gen. IX, 21. Iosias bellum non necessarium Pharaoni Necho, suo suorumque damno, intulit, 2 Paral. XXXV, 20. Daniel peccata sua confitetur, c. IX, 5. IV. Dilectio Dei dicitur perfecta esse in nobis, 1 Io. IV, 12: Sed dilectio est effectus formalis renovationis: E. renovatio etiam perfecta est; quia effectus non est praestantior sua causa. Resp.

L. c. non intelligitur dilectio Dei activa, qua nos Deum diligimus, sed passiva, qua a Deo diligimur. Non illa, sed haec in nobis perfecta est, quoniam erga nos perfecte declarata, & in cordibus nostris per Spiritum S. obsignata est. V. In quibus Christus habitat, in illis nulla est iniquitas: quia nulla est communio iustitiae cum iniquitate, 2 Cor. VI, 15: Atqui in iustificatis &c. Eph. III, 17. Resp.

In iustificatis nulla est iniquitas: quia a) peccata illis in iustificatione sunt remissa: b) quia a dominio peccati in renovatione sunt liberati: remanent tamen in illis inordinati motus & peccata infirmitatis. VI. Quicumque peccato sunt mortui, in illis non datur peccatum: nam cui quis mortuus est, illi non amplius deditus aut obnoxius est: Atqui homines renovati &c. Rom. VI, 2. Resp.

Homines renovati mortui sunt peccato, vt non regnet in mortali eorum corpore, Rom. VI, 22. quamuis in eodem habitet & dominium subinde affectet. VII. Quicumque sic renovatus est, vt sit nova creatura, & omnia eius sint nova, ille perfecte renovatus est. Atqui homines iustificati &c. 2 Cor. V, 17. Resp.

Homo iustificatus dicitur nova creatura proxime & immediate propter regenerationem, quae est nova quasi creatio, quam perfectam esse non negamus; consequenter vero, mediate & remote tantum, propter donum renovationis. Conf. Hvlsemann. breu. enucl. p. 692. Ceterum vetera dicuntur transiisse, & omnia nova esse: a) quia Christus omnibus novam gratiam, nonumque spiritum acquisiuit: b) quia novam gratiam omnibus offert, & credentibus confert; quae nova gratia etiam in omnibus perfecte operaretur, nisi peccati inhabitantis vetustate impediretur. VIII. Omnis actio Spiritus S. est perfecta: Atqui renovatio &c. E. Maior est evidens: quia Spiritus S. infinita pollens potentia, perfecte agit. Resp.

Omnis actio Spiritus S. in ceptorum, sed etiam consiliorum illorum; re autem vera nihil est, nisi cultus arbitrarius, Romani Pontificis auctoritate confirmatus, praesertim vero monasticum vitae genus.

Hunc eorum errorem detestantur Nostrates, in Aug. Conf. p. 17. & 36. & eius Apolog. p. 282. 286. 2) Socinianorum, qui, vt novas comminiscuntur leges, a Christo demum latas, easque nomine Evangelii perperam designare soliti sunt, sic perfectionem evangelicam ponunt in obedientia, omnibus hisce novis Christi imperatis pariter, atque antiquae legi morali ac naturali, praestita.

II. Alia autem vera, quae est remissio peccatorum omnium, liberatio vacuitasque omnis & culpae, & poenae, propter consummatissimam Christi iustitiam obedientiamque vicariam, legi omnino praestitam, & nobis tributam. Rom. VIII, 1. 2. 3. Eph. V, 26. 27. Coloss. II, 10. coll. cum seqq. vv. 12: 13.


### Question XX. How does a renewed man aspire to the perfection of inherent righteousness?

considered in itself and absolutely, it is perfect; but considered respectively, namely with respect to the receiving subject, it is called imperfect, not because of a defect in the power of the Holy Spirit, but because of a defect of capacity in the justified man. For the action occurs not by the mode of the one impressing, but of the one receiving according to the receptivity which is given in the capable subject.

Question XIX. Must a renewed man aspire to the perfection of holiness? A renewed man must certainly aspire to the perfection of holiness, so that day by day he may take hold of increases of inherent righteousness.

Proof a. Let the command of Christ be perpetually observed by the mind of the renewed man, Matt. V, 48. Be you perfect, even as your Father, who is in heaven, is perfect.

Proof b. Paul gravely admonishes: My most beloved brethren, be firm, immovable, always abounding in the work of the Lord! 1 Cor. XV, 58. The Papists object: No sane person aspires to that which he cannot attain: But in the opinion of the Protestants, no one can attain perfection: Therefore. Resp. I deny the major. For he who aspires to the highest, obtains the middle, according to that Greek proverb: take the extreme, you will have the middle. A student strives to attain the highest degree of learning, even if he does not possess it.

Question XX. How does a renewed man aspire to the perfection of inherent righteousness? A renewed man, aspiring to the perfection of inherent righteousness, having implored the help of the Holy Spirit and having instituted an examination of his life, morally abolishes the remnants of sin through displeasure and detestation of all moral filth, and a continuous struggle against the flesh. He expels them really through the exercise of contrary virtues.

Proof a. Just as the repentance of those standing is that of renewed men: so it brings about a moral retraction and detestation of all defilements, and a continued struggle of the spirit against the flesh, of which Paul treats in Rom. VII, 14. sqq. 2 Cor. VII, 1. Gal. V, 16. 17.

Proof b. Vices are really expelled through contrary virtues, e.g., lying through truth, lust through chastity, drunkenness through sobriety. See Eph. IV, 25. sqq.

SIGH.

Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me! Do not cast me away from your presence and do not take your Holy Spirit from me! Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and let a willing spirit sustain me, so that, having laid aside the old man, who is rendered worse day by day by depraved and deceitful lusts, I may put on the new man, who was originally created in your image in true righteousness and holiness! Restore in me, most benign Father, your image, radiant with the lights of wisdom, righteousness, and a serene conscience, so that I may be righteous from you, and holy in Christ!

Latin:

in se & absolute considerata, est perfecta; at considerata respective, nempe respectu subiecti recipientis, imperfecta dicitur, non ob defectum potentiae Spiritus S. sed ob defectum capacitatis in homine iustificato. Nam actio fit non per modum imprimentis, sed recipientis secundum receptivitatem, quae datur in subiecto capaci.

Quaest. XIX. Estne homini renouato ad perfectionem sanctitatis adspirandum? Homini renouato vtique adspirandum est ad perfectionem sanctitatis , vt in dies noua iustitia inhaerentis incrementa capiat .

Prob. a. Hominis renouati animo perpetuo obseruetur mandatum Christi, Matth. V, 48. Estote vos perfecti, quemadmodum Pater vester, qui est in caelis, perfectus est.

Prob. b. Paullus grauiter monet: Fratres mei dilectissimi, firmi estote, immobiles, abundantes in opere Domini semper! 1 Cor. XV, 58. Excipiunt Pontificii: Nemo sanus adspirat ad id, quod assequi non potest: Sed ex mente Protestantium nemo perfectionem assequi potest: E. Resp. Neg. maiorem. Nam qui ad summum adspirat, medium obtinet iuxta illud Graecorum prouerbium: ἄκρον λάβε, μέσον ἔξεις. Discipulus summum eruditionis gradum assequi nititur, licet eodem non potiatur.

Quaest. XX. Quomodo homo renouatus ad perfectionem iustitiae inhaerentis adspirat? Homo renouatus ad perfectionem iustitiae inhaerentis adspirans, implorato auxilio Spiritus S. & instituto examine vitae suae, reliquias peccati moraliter abolet per displicentiam & detestationem omnium sordium moralium, atque continuam luctam aduersus carnem . Easdem realiter expellit per virtutum contrariarum exercitium .

Prob. a. Quemadmodum poenitentia stantium est hominum renouatorum: ita eadem infert moralem retractationem & detestationem omnium inquinationum, atque continuatam luctam spiritus aduersus carnem, de qua Paullus Rom. VII, 14. seq. 2 Cor. VII, 1. Gal. V, 16. 17. agit.

Prob. b. Realiter expelluntur vitia per virtutes contrarias, v. gr. mendacium per veritatem, libido per castitatem, ebrietas per sobrietatem. Vid. Eph. IV, 25. seqq.

SVSPIRIVM.

Cor mundum crea mihi, Deus, & spiritum firmum innoua in medio mei! Ne abiice me a facie tua & Spiritum Sanctum ne aufer a me! Reduc mihi gaudium salutis tuae, & Spiritus spontaneus sustentet me, vt, deposito vetere homine, qui concupiscentiis prauis & fallacibus indies redditur deterior, induam nouum hominem, qui primitus conditus fuit ad imaginem tuam in vera iustitia & sanctitate! Instaura in me, Pater benignissime, imaginem tuam, luminibus sapientiae, iustitiae, serenae conscientiae radiantem, vt sim iustus ex te, & sanctus in Christo!


## 26 On Preserving Grace, and Perseverance


### Of Preserving Grace, and the Perseverance of the Faithful

Quest. I. What is the preservation of the faithful? Preservation is an act of grace, by which the Holy Spirit, dwelling in justified and renewed men, fortifies them with supernatural powers against the temptations of the devil, the world, and the flesh, by which they are solicited to sin and apostasy from God, and confirms and increases their faith and the holiness of their life, so that they do not fall from the state of grace, but persevere in the same, and are saved eternally. Quest.

II. Who is the author of this preservation? The author of the preservation of the faithful is the one triune God, Father, Son of God, and Holy Spirit, to whom this act of grace is ascribed in a peculiar manner, both by reason of the powers bestowed in regeneration and renewal, and by reason of actual assistance.

Proof a. From Phil. 1: 6. "Being confident of this very thing, that he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ." God, who planted Christianity among us, and regenerated and sanctified us, is about to complete this very work of His in us, provided we use the powers divinely granted in a becoming manner, and do not place an impediment before God the preserver.

Proof b. From 1 Thess. 5: 23. "And the very God of peace sanctify you wholly; and I pray God your whole spirit and soul and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ." God the Father sanctifies the spirit of man, lest it be corrupted by distrust or error; He preserves the soul, lest it succumb to inordinate affections; He preserves the body, lest it be defiled by some pollution.

Proof c. From John 10:27, 28. "My sheep hear my voice, and I know them, and they follow me: And I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand." Christ, the good shepherd, protects His sheep, so that they may remain in the hand of the Father, and obtain eternal life.

To Him Paul attributes his own perseverance of faith, 2 Tim. 4:17. "Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion." Proof d.

The preservation and confirmation of the faithful is peculiarly ascribed to the Holy Spirit; since from Him, by the benefit of regeneration and renewal, they have received the powers of persevering, Tit. 3:6.

He bears witness with the spirit of justified men that they are the children of God, Rom. 8:16; He helps their infirmities, ibid. v. 26; He is their paraclete, John 15:26; He is the earnest by which they are sealed, 2 Cor. 1:22.

Quest. III. What impelled God to preserve the faith and holiness of life? To preserve and strengthen the faith, no less than the piety of the justified and renewed man, God was impelled internally by mercy, externally by the merit and intercession of Christ.

Prob. a. From 1 Pet. V. 10. The God of all grace, who called us to his eternal glory in Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a little, will himself restore, establish, strengthen, and settle you! The Apostle teaches that from the same grace flows both the first calling to heavenly glory, and the final consummation of this benefit, namely, confirmation in good, and introduction into heavenly glory.

Prob. b. From Rom. VIII, 34. Who is it that condemns? It is Christ, who died, who is also at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us. Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? So much did God love us in Christ, that he might instruct us with the gift of perseverance; because Christ for our sake died, rose again, and being exalted to the right hand of God the Father, intercedes for us. I have prayed for you, that your faith may not fail, says Christ to Peter, Luke XXII, 32.

Latin:

Quaest. I. Quid est conservatio fidelium? Conservatio est actus gratiae, quo Spiritus Sanctus habitans in hominibus iustificatis & renouatis, hos aduersus diaboli, mundi & carnis tentationes, quibus ad peccatum & apostasiam a Deo sollicitantur, supernaturalibus viribus praemunit, fidemque ipsorum & vitae sanctitatem confirmat & auget, ne e statu gratiae excidant, sed in eodem perseuerent, & aeternum saluentur. Quaest.

II. Quis est auctor huius conseruationis? Auctor conseruationis fidelium est Deus trinus unus, Pater, Filius Dei, & Spiritus Sanctus, cui hic actus gratiae peculiari ratione adscribitur, tum ratione virium in regeneratione & renouatione collatarum, tum ratione auxilii actualis. Prob. a.

Ex Phil. I, 6. Persuastus sum, quod, qui incepit in vobis bonum opus, absoluturus sit vsque in diem Iesu Christi. Deus, qui Christianismum inter nos plantauit, nosque regenerauit & sanctificauit, hoc ipsum suum opus in nobis absoluturus est, modo viribus diuinitus concessis decenter vtamur, neque Deo conseruatori impedimentum obiiciamus.

Prob. b. Ex 1 Thess. V, 23. Ipse Deus pacis sanctificet vos integros, & integer vester spiritus, & anima & corpus irreprehensibiliter in aduentum Domini nostri Iesu Christi feruetur. Deus Pater spiritum hominis sanctificat, ne diffidentia aut errore corrumpatur; animam, ne inordinatis affectibus succumbat; corpus, ne pollutione quadam foedetur, conseruat.

Prob. c. Ex Io. X, 27. 28. Oues meae vocem meam audiunt; & ego cognosco eas, & sequuntur me; & ego vitam aeternam do illis; & non peribunt in saeculum; nec rapiet quis eas e manu Patris mei. Christus, bonus pastor, tuetur oues suas, vt maneant in manu Patris, & vitam aeternam adipiscantur.

Huic suam fidei perseuerantiam acceptam refert Paullus, 2 Tim. IV, 17. Dominus mihi adstitit & confortauit me, vt per me praeconium adimpleretur, & audirent omnes gentes, & ereptus sum ex ore leonis.

Prob. d. Spiritui S. peculiariter adscribitur conseruatio & confirmatio fidelium; quippe a quo, beneficio regenerationis & renouationis, vires perseuerandi acceperunt, Tit. III, 6. Hic testatur cum spiritu hominum iustificatorum, quod sint filii Dei, Rom.

VIII, 16. coadiuuat infirmitates eorum, ibid. v. 26. est ipsorum paracletus, Io. XV, 26. est arrhabo, quo obsignati sunt, 2 Cor. I, 22.

Quaest. III. Quid impulit Deum ad conseruandam fidem & sanctimoniam vitae? Ad conseruandam firmandamque fidem non minus, quam pietatem hominis iustificati & renouati, Deum impulit interne misericordia, externe meritum & intercessio Christi. misericordia a), externe meritum pulfiua. & intercessio Christi b).

Prob. a. Ex 1 Petr. V. 10. Deus omnis gratiae, qui vocavit nos ad aeternam suam gloriam in Christo Iesu, postquam parum passi fueritis, instauret vos, stabiliat, confortet, fundet! Docet Apostolus, ex eodem gratiae fluere & primam ad gloriam caelestem vocationem, & ultimam huius beneficii consummationem, videlicet confirmationem in bono, & introductionem in gloriam caelestem.

Prob. b. Ex Rom. VIII, 34. Quis est, qui condemnet? Christus est, qui mortuus est, qui etiam est in dextra Dei, qui & intercedit pro nobis. Quis nos separabit a dilectione Christi? Adeo Deus in Christo nos dilexit, ut dono perseverantiae nos instrueret; quia Christus nostri causa mortuus resurrexit, & evectus ad dextram Dei Patris pro nobis intercedit. Ego oraui pro te, ut non desinat fides tua, dicit Christus Petro, Luc. XXII, 32.


### Of Preserving Grace, and the Perseverance of the Faithful: Q. IV

Q. IV.

The means preserving and confirming faith in Christ and the holiness of life are the word of God a) and the sacrament of the supper b).

Prob. a. 1) By the word of God we are preserved from the plague of sin. I have hidden your word in my heart, that I might not sin against you, says the Psalmist, Ps. CXIX, 11.

2) By the word of God heard, and brought into use, our heart is strengthened; so that our faith may not be shaken by any temptations. Everyone who hears these words of mine and does them; I will compare him to a wise man who built his house upon the rock; and the rain descended, and the rivers came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house: yet it did not fall: for it was founded upon the rock, Matt. VII, 24. 25.

25. 3) By the word of God, as with the sword of the Spirit, we conquer and put to flight the enemies of our soul, Eph. VI, 17.

Prob. b. By the use of the S. Eucharist, mystical union with God and the state of grace is preserved. He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, abides in me, and I in him, John VI, 50. From this union with Christ it comes about that we obtain new strength as branches from the vine, through faith to overcome the world, the devil, and our flesh, and to bear more abundant fruits of righteousness.

Q. V.

What ministers does God use to confirm faith and holiness of life? Ordinarily God uses sacred heralds to confirm the weak . Extraordinarily any renewed man, partly by the proposal of the divine word, partly by his own example, can incite others to the perseverance of faith and piety .

Prob. a. Sacred heralds offer their hearers milk and solid food. Milk to infants, i.e., to those unskilled in the word of righteousness, that they may grow in grace and the knowledge of Christ. Solid food to the perfect, who by habit have their senses exercised to the discernment of good and evil, that they may be preserved from evil, and confirmed in good, Hebr. V, 13. 14.

Prob. b. It is the duty of all more perfect Christians to lift up the drooping hands and strengthen the weak knees. And to make straight paths for their feet: so that the lame may not be turned aside, but rather be healed, Hebr. XII, 12. 13. This pertains primarily to the mind to be confirmed in faith, because the Apostle does not want the hands of faith to be drooping, nor the knees weak, when one must approach the throne of grace. Wherefore let more mature Christians make straight paths with their feet, i.e., by the proposal of the divine word, and by their own example let them shine before the more unskilled, lest those who are weak fall away completely from the faith, and deny Christ.

Latin:

Quæst. IV. Quibus mediis renati in fide & sanctitate a Deo conservantur?

Media conservantia & confirmantia fidem in Christum atque sanctimoniam vitae, sunt verbum Dei a) & sacramentum cenae b).

Prob. a. 1) Verbo Dei a lue peccati praeferuamur. In corde meo abscondidi verbum tuum, ut non peccem tibi, inquit Hierofaltes, Ps. CXIX, 11.

2) Verbo Dei audito, & in usum traducto, confortatur cor nostrum; ne ullis tentationibus fides nostra labefactetur. Omnis, qui audit mea verba haec & facit ea; comparabo eum cum viro prudenti, qui aedificavit domum suam supra petram; & descendit imber veneruntque flumina, ac flarunt venti, irrueruntque in domum illam: tamen non cecidit: fundata enim erat supra petram, Matth. VII, 24. 25.

3) Verbo Dei, tanquam gladio spiritus, hostes animae nostrae vincimus & profligamus, Eph. VI, 17.

Prob. b. S. Eucharistiae usu unio mystica cum Deo & status gratiae conservatur. Qui manducat meam carnem, & bibit sanguinem meum, in me manet, & ego in ipso, Io. VI, 50. Ex hac unione cum Christo prouenit, ut nouas vires tanquam palmites ex vite consequamur, per fidem vincendi mundum, diabolum, carnemque nostram, & copiosiores fructus iustitiae ferendi.

Quæst. V. Quibus ministris Deus utitur ad confirmandum fidem & sanctitatem vitae?

Ordinarie utitur Deus praeconibus sacris ad confirmandos infirmos a). Extraordinarie cuius homo renouatus, partim propositione verbi diuini, partim proprio suo exemplo, alios ad perseuerantiam fidei & pietatis incitare potest b).

Prob. a. Praecones sacri offerunt auditoribus suis lac & solidum cibum. Lac infantibus, h. e. imperitis sermonis iustitiae, ut crescant in gratia & cognitione Christi. Solidum cibum perfectis, qui per habitum sensus exercitatos habent, ad diiudicationem boni & mali, ut a malo praeferuentur, & in bono confirmentur, Hebr. V, 13. 14.

Prob. b. Omnium Christianorum perfectiorum est, remissas manus & soluta genua rectificare. & semitas rectas facere pedibus suis: ut claudum non peruertatur, sed curetur potius, Hebr. XII, 12. 13. Hoc in primis ad animum in fide confirmandum pertinet, quia Apostolus manus fidei non vult esse remissas, nec soluta genua, cum accedendum est ad thronum gratiae. Quare adultiores Christiani pedibus suis rectas faciant semitas, i. e. propositione verbi diuini, proprioque exemplo imperitioribus praeluceant, ne, qui infirmi sunt, a fide penitus excidant, & Christum abnegent.


### Of Preserving Grace, and the Perseverance of the Faithful: Quest. VI. Whose faith and holiness does God preserve?

Quest. VI. Whose faith and holiness does God preserve?

God preserves the faith and holiness of men who are reborn, justified, united with God and Christ, and renewed by the Holy Spirit.

Proof. The preservation of a thing presupposes its existence. For this reason, since faith and the holiness of life exist only in men who are reborn, justified, united with God, and renewed, they are divinely preserved only in these same persons. This we gather from Rom. V, 1. 2. Therefore, being justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ: through whom we have access by faith into this grace, in which we stand: and from 1 Cor. XV, 1. Moreover, I make known to you, brethren, the gospel which I preached to you, which you also received, in which you also stand. To stand in the Holy Scriptures is the same as to persist, or to persevere. For standing here is not opposed to running; since Christians are not to stand idly, but to run, following the example of Lot: but rather it is opposed to falling, whether in doctrine or in life, and thus standing in this context denotes perseverance. Therefore, since, as Paul teaches, only those brothers stand who have received the gospel and, being justified, enjoy the friendship of God, it remains firm and fixed that only their faith and piety are divinely preserved.

Quest. VII. Is only the soul with its faculties confirmed in good, or also the body with its members?

Primarily the soul and its faculties—the intellect, the will, and the sensitive appetite—are preserved from evil and confirmed in good; secondarily, the body and its members.

Proof. May your whole spirit, and soul, and body be preserved blameless unto the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, 1 Thess. V, 23. Obs. Spirit, to Paul, is the higher faculty of the soul, by which we understand and will. Faith, by which we have knowledge and assent, is in the intellect; by which we have trust, it is in the will. The soul is the lower faculty, by which we feel and desire the good that is pleasing to the senses. The workshop of holiness of life is both the spirit and the soul, i.e., the intellect, the will, and the sensitive appetite are capable of sanctification. Holy actions are exercised through the members of the body, as organs and weapons of righteousness. For this reason, primarily the soul, and secondarily the body and its members themselves, are preserved from evil and confirmed in good by the Holy Spirit.

Quest. VIII. In what does the preservation of the faithful formally consist?

The preservation of the faithful comprises: a) preserving or fortifying grace, by which God fortifies justified and renewed men against the temptations of the devil, the world, and the flesh with supernatural powers, so that they are not swept headlong by these enemies into apostasy from faith and piety: b) confirming grace, by which the faith and piety of justified and renewed men are stabilized through means divinely ordained; to this also pertains comforting grace, by which the faithful, pressed by the burden of afflictions of body and soul, are raised up: c) enriching grace, by which both faith in Christ and piety of life are subsequently increased by the Holy Spirit with new and greater powers.

Proof. a. From 2 Thess. III, 3. The Lord is faithful, who will confirm you and guard you from evil. The mind of the Apostle is: God is faithful and constant: therefore He will not allow you to fall away from the gift of faith bestowed, but will stabilize you in it, and guard you from all evil, from the fiery darts of Satan, from the snares of the world, from the allurements of the flesh, lest they shake or weaken your faith. To which end God, most merciful, in regeneration and renewal imparts those strengths, by which, being girded, they are by no means unequal to repelling and overcoming the enemies. Resist the devil: and he will flee from you, says St. James, ch. IV, 7. And St. John commends the grace of God that protects, 1 ep. ch. V, 4. Everything that is born of God overcomes the world. And this is the victory that overcomes the world, our faith.

Prob. b. St. Paul proclaims the grace of God that confirms with a memorable array of words, 2 Cor. I, 21. 22. But he who confirms us with you in Christ, and has anointed us, is God. Who also has sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts. The evangelical promises, of which the Apostle had spoken in the preceding verse, being most certain in themselves, God confirms in us, through the anointing and collation of divine gifts, by which we not only believe them, but also conceive from them the highest joy of mind and conscience. Moreover, he has sealed us, and given the earnest of the Spirit in our hearts. God confirms our faith, leaning upon evangelical promises, by sacraments, as if by seals, and by the internal testimony of the Holy Spirit, as if by a certain earnest, binding more strongly and more powerfully than any pledge, by which the bridegroom binds his faith to the bride most tightly and most intimately, and renders it clearly certain and indubitable of his perpetual and indissoluble love. By which infallible testimony of the Holy Spirit this grace is called συμμάρτυροῦσα, testifying, in that it testifies to our hearts by its power, implanted in the word, that we are children of God, and can call upon God with the highest confidence: Abba, Father! Rom. VIII, 15. Indeed, divine grace renders not only the hope of salvation certain to us, but always more certain, nay, most certain. To this confirming grace must also be referred the consoling grace, by which the afflicted minds of the faithful are refreshed and sustained, lest, having cast aside faith, they be carried headlong into despair. Of which Paul, 1 Cor. I, 3. Blessed be God and the Father of our Lord, Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies, and the God of all consolation, who consoles us in all our affliction, that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction, through the consolation which we ourselves receive from God: for, just as the sufferings of Christ abound in us, so also through Christ our consolation abounds.

Prob. c. God, in preserving faith and the holiness of life, enriches and strengthens the same with more abundant increases, We do not cease to pray and ask for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding, that you may walk worthily of the Lord to all pleasing, in every good work bearing fruit and growing in the knowledge of God, strengthened with all might, says Paul, Col. I, 9. 10. 11.

Latin:

Quaest. VI. Cuius hominis fidem & sanctitatem Deus conservat?

Deus conservat fidem & sanctitatem hominum renatorum, iustificatorum, cum Deo & Christo unitorum, atque per Spiritum Sanctum renovatorum.

Prob. Conservatio rei supponit eius existentiam. Quam ob rem, cum fides & sanctimonia vitae non, nisi in hominibus renatis, iustificatis, cum Deo unitis, & renovatis existant, in iisdem duntaxat divinitus conservantur. Id quod colligimus e Rom. V, 1. 2. Iustificati itaque fide pacem habemus erga Deum per Dominum nostrum, Iesum Christum: per quem aditum habemus fide in gratiam hanc, in qua stamus: & ex 1 Cor. XV, 1. Ceterum notum facio vobis, fratres, euangelium, quod euangelizaui vobis, quod & accepistis, in quo etiam statis. Stare in sacris litteris idem est, ac persistere, vel perseuerare. Neque enim statio hic opponitur cursui; cum Christianis non otiose standum, sed currendum sit, exemplo Lothi: verum lapsui, seu in doctrina, seu in vita, adeoque statio in praeserti notat perseuerantiam. Idcirco cum, docente Paulo, tantum stent fratres illi, qui euangelium acceperunt, & iustificati amicitia Dei fruuntur, firmum fixumque manet, illorum tantum fidem & pietatem divinitus conservari.

Quaest. VII. Utrum tantum anima cum suis facultatibus, an etiam corpus cum suis membris in bono confirmatur?

Primario anima, eiusque facultates, intellectus, voluntas & appetitus sensitivus: secundario corpus, eiusque membra, a malo praeservantur & in bono confirmantur.

Prob. Integer vester spiritus, & anima & corpus irreprehensibiliter in aduentum Domini nostri Iesu Christi seruetur, 1 Thess. V, 23. Obs. Spiritus Paulo est facultas animae superior, qua intelligimus & volumus. Fides, qua notitiam & assensum, est in intellectu; qua fiduciam, in voluntate. Anima est facultas inferior, qua sentimus & bonum sensibus gratum appetimus. Sanctitatis vitae officina tam spiritus, quam anima est, h. e. sanctificationis capaces sunt intellectus, voluntas & appetitus sensitivus. Actiones sanctae exercentur per membra corporis, tanquam organa & arma iustitiae. Quam ob rem primario anima, secundario corpus & ipsius membra, per Spiritum Sanctum a malo praeservantur & in bono confirmantur.

Quaest. VIII. In quo formaliter consistit conservatio fidelium?

Conservatio fidelium complectitur a) gratiam praeservantem, seu praemunientem, qua Deus homines iustificatos & renovatos aduersus tentationes diaboli, mundi & carnis, viribus supernaturalibus praemunit, ne ab istis hostibus in apostasiam a fide & pietate praecipites rapiantur: b) gratiam confirmantem, qua per media, diuinitus ordinata, fides pietasque hominum iustificatorum & renovatorum stabiliuntur: quo etiam pertinet gratia consolans, qua fideles, onere afflictionum corporis & animae pressi, eriguntur: c) gratiam locupletantem, qua tum fides in Christum, tum pietas vitae subinde nouis maioribusque viribus per Spiritum Sanctum augentur.

Prob. a. Ex 2 Thess. III, 3. Fidelis est Dominus, qui confirmabit vos & custodiet a malo. Mens Apostoli est: Deus est fidelis & constans: Idcirco non sinet vos dono fidei collato exsidere, sed stabiliet vos in eo, & custodiet ab omni malo, ab ignitis Satanae telis, ab insidiis. Satanæ telis, ab infimundi, ab illecebris carnis, ne fidem vestram concutiant, aut labefactent. Quem in finem Deus misericordissimus in regeneratione & renovatione eas impertit vires, quibus succincti hostibus reprimendis & superandis haud inpares sunt. Resistite diabolo: fugiet enim a vobis, inquit S. Iacobus, c. IV, 7. Et S. Ioannes commendat gratiam Dei præmunientem, 1 ep. c. V, 4. Omne, quod natum est ex Deo, vincit mundum. Hæc autem est victoria, quæ vicit mundum, fides nostra.

Prob. b. Gratiam Dei confirmantem memorabili verborum apparatu prædicat S. Paulus, 2 Cor. I, 21. 22. Qui autem confirmat nos vobiscum in Christum, & unxit nos, Deus est. Qui etiam obsignavit nos, & dedit arrhabonem Spiritus in cordibus nostris. Promissiones euangelicas, de quibus Apostolus versu præcedente locutus erat, in se certissimas, Deus confirmat in nobis, per vnctionem & collationem diuinorum donorum, qua illis non credamus tantum, sed summam animi & conscientiæ lætitiam inde concipiamus. Quin & obsignavit nos, & dedit arrhabonem Spiritus in cordibus nostris. Confirmat Deus fidem nostram, promissionibus euangelicis innixam, sacramentis, velut sigillis, & interno Spiritus S. testimonio, quasi arrhabone quodam, omni pignore magis fortiusque obligante, quo sponsus sponsæ fidem suam arctissime penitissimeque obstringit, ipsamque amoris sui perpetui & indissolubilis plane certam & indubiam reddit. A quo infallibili Spiritus S. testimonio hæc gratia & συμμάρτυροῦσα, contestans dicitur, eo, quod cordibus nostris vi sua, verbo insita, testatur, nos filios Dei esse, & summa cum fiducia Deum appellare posse: Abba, Pater! Rom. VIII, 15. nempe non certam nobis tantum gratia diuina reddit spem salutis, sed semper certiorem, immo certissimam. Ad hanc gratiam confirmantem etiam referenda est gratia consolans, qua afflicti fidelium animi recreantur, & sustentantur, ne, abiecta fide, in desperationem præcipites ferantur. De qua Paullus, 1 Cor. I, 3. Benedictus esto Deus & Pater Domini nostri, Iesu Christi, Pater misericordiarum, & Deus omnis consolationis, qui consolatur nos in omni afflictione nostra, ut possimus nos consolari eos, qui in omni afflictione sunt, per consolationem, quam accipimus ipsi a Deo: quia, quem ad modum abundant passiones Christi in nobis, sic per Christum abundat etiam consolatio nostra.

Prob. c. Deus conferuando fidem vitæque sanctimoniam, vberioribus eandem incrementis locupletat, & firmat, Non cessamus pro vobis orare & petere, ut impleamini cognitione voluntatis ipsius in omni sapientia & intelligentia spirituali, ut vos ambuletis digne Domino ad omnem complacentiam, in omni opere bono fructificantes & crescentes in cognitionem Dei, omni robore corroborati, ait Paullus, Col. I, 9. 10. 11.


### Quest. IX. What duty is required of all the reborn and renewed, that they may be preserved in faith and holiness?

That the faith and holiness of Christians may remain whole and inviolable, it is their duty a) to use decently the means divinely ordained for the perseverance of faith and holiness; b) to implore divine aid with most ardent prayers; c) to watch, and cautiously avoid all the snares of faith, and occasions of sinning; d) to fight fiercely against the enemies of the soul with all the spiritual strengths received in regeneration and renewal; e) to strive with tireless effort for the increase of faith and piety. Prob. a. The means of confirming faith are the word and the sacraments.

He who meditates on the word of God day and night is like a tree planted by the streams of waters, which gives its fruit in season in its time, and its leaf does not wither, Ps. I, 3.

Who worthily eats in the sacrament of the supper the flesh of Christ, and drinks his blood, he remains in Christ, and Christ in him, John VI, 56.

Prob. b. Watch and pray, that you may not enter into temptation, Matt. XXVI, 41.

King David prays : Uphold my steps in your paths: that my goings may not be moved, Ps. XVII, 5.

Prob. c.

Saint Peter gravely exhorts: You beloved, beware, lest being led away by the error of the wicked you fall from your own steadfastness, 2 Pet. III, 17.

Men ἄθεσμοι, or wicked, are those who can be kept in order by no law, by no statutes: the company of these must be fled, lest by their deception we be led away from the way of truth and piety, and lose the firmness of faith. Prob. d.

From Eph. VI, 10.

11. Finally, my brethren, be strong in the Lord, and in the power of his might. Put on the armor of God, so that you may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.

Prob. e. From 2 Pet.

III, 18.

Grow in grace and the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. The faithful grow in grace when they embrace it with a firmer trust; they grow in the knowledge of Christ when, eagerly drinking in the milk of the gospel, they grow through it, tasting more and more how kind the Lord is, 1 Pet.

II, 2. 3.

Quest. X.

Is saving faith preserved through good works? Faith, properly speaking, is not preserved through good works, but through the same causes by which it is generated, namely through the word and sacraments; through good works it is exercised, manifested, and made known.

Prob. a.

The word and sacraments are the means, divinely instituted, for kindling, nourishing, strengthening, and preserving saving faith in the hearts of men: the pursuit of good works, however, is its consequence, which testifies of faith, just as fruit does of a tree. Prob. b.

The faith of Abraham ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἐτελειώθη, was known as perfect from works, James II, 22.

CALOV. explains these words accurately in his Biblia Illustrata: A thing is understood to be perfected, according to the usage of Scripture, which either acquires a just perfection of parts or degrees, or also becomes more evidently known to others by its excellence. And thus we do not deny that Abraham’s faith was intrinsically strengthened by these notable works of obedience in terms of degrees; that it became more extrinsically known to all those who were to hear of them now and in the past, no one can doubt.

It is worth noting here also the words of the Aug. Apol.

Conf. p. 117.

Alms are exercises of faith, which receives remission, which conquers death, while it exercises itself more and more, and receives strength in those exercises. Quest. XI.

What is the end of the preservation of the faithful? The ultimate end of this preservation, on the part of God, is the glory of the grace of God; the end on the part of men, eternal salvation and consistency in the final judgment.

The proximate effect of the end is perseverance.

Prob. a. From 1 Thess.

I, 3.

We ought to give thanks to God always for you, brethren, as it is fitting: because your faith grows more, and the charity of every one of you all toward each other becomes fuller. Prob. b.

Whoever shall have persevered to the end, he shall be saved, Matt. X, 22.

Watch therefore at all times, praying, that you may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that are to come, and to stand before the son of man, Luke

XXI, 36.

It is proved by the fact that it is God who works in us both to will and to do, for His good pleasure, Phil. 2:13. Whence, He who began a good work in us will complete it, even unto the day of Jesus Christ, c. 1:6. Perseverance is therefore a gift of God, concerning which AUGUSTINE, in his book On Rebuke and Grace, ch. VI, discourses excellently: If we say that this perseverance, so praiseworthy and so happy, is of man, such that it is not from God, we make void that which the Lord says to Peter: I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not.

Question XII.

What is the perseverance of the faithful? The perseverance of the faithful is a gift of God, by which the faith and holiness of a man justified and renewed remain.

Question XIII.

How many kinds of perseverance of the faithful are there?

The perseverance of the faithful is either temporary or final. The former is that by which justified and renewed men persist in faith and in the holiness of their ways for a time only, but not unto the end of life a). The latter is that by which Christians, retaining faith and a good conscience unto the end of life, remain in a state of grace b).

Proof a. There are men who hear the word of God and receive the word with joy; but they have no root, but are πρόσκαιροι, or temporary. When, therefore, affliction or persecution arises because of the word, they are immediately offended, Matt. 13:20, 21. The perseverance of these is temporary.

Proof b. There are, on the contrary, men faithful unto death, to whom is given the crown of life, Rev. 2:10. The perseverance of these is final: which final perseverance is called perseverance κατ' ἐξοχὴν (by way of eminence).

Question XIV.

How many kinds of final perseverance are there? Final perseverance is either continuous or interrupted. The former is that by which the faithful one, from the time he first began to believe and was justified, remains in a state of grace and union with God unto the end, in such a way that he never falls from grace or interrupts his union with God. The latter is that which indeed suffers some interruption, but, being subsequently repaired, endures unto the end.

Observation I. Distinction between the regenerate and the elect. The regenerate are estimated by present faith; the elect by final faith. And therefore, not all the regenerate are elect; nor are all the elect always and at every time regenerate. For there are regenerate persons who, having fallen into mortal sins, are reprobated on account of final impenitence: there are also elect persons who, on account of proaeretic (deliberate) sins in which they indulge, are for a time not in a state of regeneration. The regenerate can fall totally and finally, i.e., through mortal sins they can fall from a state of grace, so that they are never restored to the same: The elect can fall totally, but not finally, i.e., their perseverance is broken for a time by proaeretic sins, so that from children of grace they become children of wrath; but they cannot remain in a state of wrath, but return to friendship with God through sincere repentance, because they were elected by God in view of a persevering faith, which is to embrace the merit of Christ; the foreknowledge of God never fails.

Observation II. Continuous perseverance, by reason of time, is that of those who sin only out of infirmity, but never out of determined malice, or who commit only sins that are venial by event: such as, on account of indwelling sin, Rom. 7:17, the infirmity of fallen flesh, Rom. 8:3, and the imperfection of renewal in this mortality, scarcely or rarely happens to wayfarers.

Which is even more true from the same foundations, concerning equal perseverance. For who will give me an adult traveler, in whom throughout his whole life the degree of faith and piety is not diminished even in the slightest? says B. HULSEM. in breu. p. 937.

Obf. III. We have proven above that the perseverance not only of the reborn, but even of the elect, can for a time be ruined.

Latin:

Vt Christianorum fides sanctitasque perstet integra & inuiolabilis, illorum est, a) mediis, ad perseuerantiam fidei & sanctitatis diuinitus ordinatis, decenter vti; b) auxilium diuinum ardentissimis precibus implorare; c) vigilare, cauteque declinare omnes fidei scopulos, peccandique occasiones; d) omnibus viribus spiritualibus in regeneratione & renovatione acceptis aduersus hostes animæ acriter dimicare; e) indefesso conatu ad incrementum fidei & pietatis contendere. Prob. a. Media confirmandæ fidei sunt verbum & sacramenta.

Verbum Dei diu noctuque meditans est sicut arbor plantata iuxta riuos aquarum, quæ fructum suum dat in pore suo, foliumque eius non decidit, Ps. I, 3.

Qui digne comedit in sacramento coenae carnem Christi, et bibit eius sanguinem, ille manet in Christo, et Christus in ipso, Io. VI, 56.

Prob. b. Vigilate et orate, ne ingrediamini in tentationem, Matth. XXVI, 41.

Precatur Rex Dauid: Fulci gressus meos in orbitis tuis: ut non dimoueantur incessus mei, Ps. XVII, 5.

Prob. c.

Grauiter hortatur S. Petrus: Vos dilecti, cauete vobis, ne nefariorum errore una abducti excidatis e propria stabilitate, 2 Petr. III, 17.

Homines ἄθεσμοι, siue nefarii sunt, qui nullo iure, nullis legibus in ordine retineri possunt: horum consortium fugiendum est, ne ipsorum deceptione a via veritatis et pietatis abducti, firmitatem fidei amittamus. Prob. d.

Ex Eph. VI, 10.

11. Quod reliquum est, fratres mei, confortamini in Domino, et in robore potentiae illius. Induite armaturam Dei ad hoc, ut possitis vos stare contra insidias diaboli.

Prob. e. Ex 2 Petr.

III, 18.

Crescite in gratia et cognitione Domini nostri et Saluatoris Iesu Christi. Crescunt fideles in gratia, quando firmiore fiducia eam amplectuntur; crescunt in cognitione Christi, cum lac euangelii auide imbibentes, per illud crescunt, plus plusque gustando, quam benignus sit Dominus, 1 Petr.

II, 2. 3.

Quæst. X.

An fides saluifica per bona opera conseruatur? Fides proprie loquendo non per bona opera, sed per easdem caussas, per quas generatur, nempe per verbum et sacramenta conseruatur , per bona opera exercetur, exseritur et innotescit .

Prob. a.

Verbum et sacramenta sunt media, diuinitus instituta, ad fidem saluificam in hominum cordibus accendendam, nutriendam, roborandam et conseruandam: studium vero bonorum operum est eius consequens, quod de fide, perinde ac fructus de arbore, testatur. Prob. b.

Fides Abrahami ἐκ τῶν ἔργων ἐτελειώθη, ex operibus pro perfecta cognita est Iac. II, 22.

Accurate haec verba CALOV. in bibl. illustr. explicat: Perfici intelligitur res, ex vsu scripturae, quae vel iustam partium, vel graduum perfectionem acquirit, vel etiam a praestantia sua aliis euidentius innotescit. Atque ita etiam intrinsece ratione graduum roboratam fuisse Abrahami per haec insignia obedientiae opera, non diffitemur: extrinsece magis innotuisse omnibus iis, qui nunc et olim de iis audituri erant, dubitari a nemine potest.

Notari hic merentur etiam verba Apolog. Aug.

Conf. p. 117.

Eleemosynae sunt exercitia fidei, quae accipit remissionem, quae vincit mortem, dum se magis magisque exercet, et in illis exercitiis vires accipit. Quæst. XI.

Quis est finis conseruationis fidelium? Finis conseruationis huius vltimus, ex parte Dei, est gloria gratiae Dei ; Finis ex parte hominum, aeterna salus et consistentia in extremo iudicio .

Finis effectus proximus est perseuerantia .

Prob. a. Ex 1 Thess.

I, 3.

Gratias agere debemus Deo semper pro vobis, fratres, quem ad modum aequum est: quia amplius crescit fides vestra, et plenior fit caritas vnius cuiusque omnium vestrum erga vos inuicem. Prob. b.

Quisquis perseuerauerit in finem, hic seruabitur, Matth. X, 22.

Vigilate ergo in omni tempore, precantes, ut digni habeamini ad effugiendum haec omnia, quae futura sunt, et ad consistendum coram filio hominis, Luc.

XXI, 36.

Prob. c. Deus est, qui operatur in nobis tam velle, quam perficere, pro beneplacito, Phil. II, 13. Vnde, qui bonum opus in nobis coepit, id ipsum absoluturus est, usque in diem Iesu Christi, c. I, 6. Est igitur perseverantia donum Dei, de quo AVGVSTIN. libr. de corrupt. & gratia c. VI. praeclare disserit: Si dixerimus, istam perseverantiam tam laudabilem, tam felicem, esse hominis, ut non sit ex Deo; illud euacuamus, quod ait Dominus Petro: rogaui pro te, ne deficiat fides tua.

Quaest. XII. Quid est perseverantia fidelium?

Perseverantia fidelium est donum Dei, quo fides & sanctitas hominis iustificati & renouati permanent.

Quaest. XIII. Quotuplex est perseverantia fidelium?

Perseverantia fidelium est vel temporaria, vel finalis.

Illa est, qua homines iustificati & renouati ad tempus tantum, non autem usque ad finem vitae in fide, morumque sanctimonia persistunt a). Haec est, qua Christiani, usque ad finem vitae, fidem & bonam conscientiam retinentes, in statu gratiae manent b).

Prob. a. Dantur homines, qui verbum Dei audiunt, auditum cum gaudio accipiunt; non habent autem radicem, sed πρόσκαιροι, seu temporarii sunt. Quando ergo incidit afflictio, aut persecutio propter verbum, continuo scandalizantur, Matth. XIII, 20. 21. Horum perseverantia est temporaria.

Prob. b. Dantur contra homines fideles usque ad mortem, quibus datur corona vitae, Apoc. II, 10. Horum perseverantia est finalis: quae perseverantia finalis κατ' ἐξοχὴν perseverantia dicitur.

Quaest. XIV. Quotuplex est perseverantia finalis?

Perseverantia finalis est vel continua, vel interrupta. Illa est, qua fidelis, ex quo semel credere coepit, & iustificatus est, in statu gratiae & vnione cum Deo ad finem ita permanet, vt nunquam gratia excidat, aut vnionem cum Deo interrumpat. Haec est, quae interruptionem aliquam quidem patitur, sed subinde resarta ad finem usque perdurat.

Obs. I. Dist. inter renatos, & electos. Renati aestimantur ex fide praesente; electi ex fide finali. Ideoque non omnes renati sunt electi; nec omnes electi semper & omni tempore sunt renati. Dantur enim renati, qui, prolapsi in peccata mortifera, ob finalem impoenitentiam reprobantur: dantur etiam electi, qui ob peccata proaeretica, quibus indulgent, ad tempus non sunt in statu regenerationis. Renati possunt labi totaliter & finaliter, i. e. per peccata mortalia possunt excidere statu gratiae, vt nunquam in eundem restituantur: Electi possunt labi totaliter, sed non finaliter, i. e. illorum perseverantia ad tempus rumpitur peccatis proaereticis, vt ex filiis gratiae fiant filii irae; in statu irae autem permanere nequeunt, sed per feriam poenitentiam in amicitiam cum Deo redeunt, eo, quod intuitu perseverantis fidei, meritum Christi amplexurae, a Deo electi sunt; praescientia Dei nunquam fallitur. perfeuerantis fidei, meritum Christi amplexuræ, a Deo electi sunt; præfcientia Dei autem nunquam fallitur.

Obs. II. Perfeuerantia continua, ratione temporis, est illorum, qui tantum ex infirmitate, nunquam vero ex destinata malitia peccant, feu sola peccata ex euentu venialia committunt: qualis propter inhabitans peccatum, Rom. VII, 17. infirmitatem carnis lapfæ, Rom. VIII, 3. & imperfectionem renouationis in hac mortalitate viatoribus vix, vel raro continObs. II. Perseverantia continua, ratione temporis, est illorum, qui tantum ex infirmitate, nunquam vero ex destinata malitia peccant, seu sola peccata ex euentu venialia committunt: qualis propter inhabitans peccatum, Rom. VII, 17. infirmitatem carnis lapsae, Rom. VIII, 3. & imperfectionem renouationis in hac mortalitate viatoribus vix, vel raro contingit.

Quod adhuc magis verum est ex iisdem fundamentis, de perseverantia æquali. Quis enim dabit mihi viatorem adultum, in quo per totam vitam gradus fidei ac pietatis ne tantillum quidem imminuatur? inquit B. HULSEM. in breu. p. 937.

Obs. III. Perseverantiam non tantum renatorum, sed etiam electorum, ad tempus ruinari posse, supra probatum dedimus.


### Q. XV. What is opposed to the perseverance of the faithful?

Opposed to the perseverance of the faithful is a fall from faith and piety, which if it is continued with morose delight, is called apostasy.

Latin:

Perseverantiæ fidelium opponitur lapsus a fide & pietate, qui si cum morosa delectatione continuetur, vocatur apostasia.


### Q. XVI. What is apostasy?

Apostasy is a deliberate, deceitful withdrawal from faith and piety, continued with frequent acts of infidelity and impiety with morose delight in them and contempt for the divine word.

Obf. Apostasy is said to be, not a fall from faith and piety committed through ignorance or precipitation, even while the conscience protests, and corrected by immediately following repentance: but a clearly deliberate and deceitful withdrawal from faith and piety, a frequent continuation of acts of infidelity and impiety, morose delight in them, and contempt for the divine word is called apostasy, in the opinion of D. HULSEMANN. in breu. p. 861. Conf. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 860.

Latin:

Apostasia est recessus a fide & pietate deliberatus, dolosus, crebris infidelitatis & impietatis actibus cum morosa in iis delectatione & contemptu verbi diuini continuatus.

Obs. Apostasia dicitur, non lapsus a fide & pietate per ignorantiam, aut præcipitantiam, etiam reclamante conscientia commissus, mox insequente pænitentia correctus: sed plane deliberata & dolosa recessio a fide & pietate, frequens actuum infidelitatis & impietatis continuatio, morosa in iis delectatio, & contemptus verbi diuini dicitur apostasia, censente D. HULSEMANN. in breu. p. 861. Conf. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 860.


### Q. XVII. How many kinds of apostasy are there?

Apostasy is twofold, dogmatic and moral. The former is a defection from the true doctrine of the Holy Spirit, by which, once rejected, saving faith is extinguished a). The latter is a deliberate fall from the pursuit of holiness, continued with frequent acts of malice, and bringing about a shipwreck of faith b).

Prob. a. The term from which there is apostasy is faith, as CALOVIUS says in bibl. illustr. on 2 Thess. II, 3. fol. 900. Therefore the Apostle warns in Hebr. III, 12. See, brothers, lest there be in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God, ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ζῶντος. The Apostle implies that apostasy from the living God consists in the malicious rejection of faith. Faith is lost, however, both by the denial of the doctrine of faith and by deliberate sins. Confer. HULSEM. breuiar. p. 962. Paul speaks of dogmatic apostasy, 1 Tim. IV, 1. But the Spirit says expressly, that in the last times some ἀποστήσονται, shall fall away from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils. He who falls away from the true doctrine of faith, and adheres to false doctrine originating from the devil, in the judgment of Paul, is an apostate. By the Pontificians, apostasy is defined somewhat more strictly, as being infidelity, through which one completely withdraws from the true faith, as when one becomes a Jew or a pagan from a Christian. See BECAN. c. XIV. de fide, quæst. 3. & conf. CALOV. bibl. illustr. on 2 Thess.

II, 3. Prob. b. From 1 Tim. I, 19. Holding faith and a good conscience, which some having put away, concerning faith have made shipwreck. The Apostle teaches that faith cannot persevere unless a good conscience is kept, and voluntary sins, by which the conscience is wounded, are avoided; which doctrine he confirms by proposing the examples of those who made shipwreck concerning faith, having cast away a good conscience through deliberate sins.

Latin:

Apostasia est duplex, dogmatica, & moralis. Illa est defectio a vera Spiritus S. doctrina, qua reiecta, fides saluifica exstinguitur a). Hæc est deliberatus lapsus a sanctitatis studio, crebris malitiæ actibus continuatus, fideique naufragium inferens b).

Prob. a. Terminus a quo apostasiæ fides est, dicente CALOVIO in bibl. illustr. ad 2 Thess. II, 3. fol. 900. Idcirco monet Apostolus Hebr. III, 12. Videte, fratres, ne forte sit in aliquo vestrum cor pravum incredulitatis in recedendo a Deo viuo, ἐν τῷ ἀποστῆναι ἀπὸ θεοῦ ζῶντος. Innuit Apostolus, apostasiam a Deo viuo consistere in malitiosa abiectione fidei. Amittitur autem fides, tum abnegatione doctrinæ fidei, tum peccatis proæreticis. Confer. HULSEM. breuiar. p. 962. De apostasia dogmatica loquitur Paullus, 1 Tim. IV, 1. Spiritus autem diserte dicit, quod in extremis temporibus quidam ἀποστήσονται, defecturi sint a fide, attendentes spiritibus erroneis, & doctrinis dæmoniorum. Qui a vera fidei doctrina deficit, & doctrinæ falsæ a dæmone oriundæ adhærescit, iudice Paullo, apostata est. A Pontificiis apostasia aliquanto strictius definitur, quod sit infidelitas, per quam quis omnino recedit a vera fide, vt, quando ex Christiano fit Iudæus, vel paganus. Vid. BECAN. c. XIV. de fide, quæst. 3. & conf. CALOV. bibl. illustr. in 2 Thess. II, 3.

Prob. b. Ex 1 Tim. I, 19. Habe fidem & bonam conscientiam, quam quidam repulerunt, & circa fidem naufragium fecerunt. Docet Apostolus, non posse perseverare fidem, nisi feruetur bona conscientia, & declinentur peccata voluntaria, quibus conscientia vulneratur; quam doctrinam confirmat propositis exemplis eorum, qui circa fidem fecerunt naufragium, abiecta per peccata proæretica bona conscientia.


### Q. XVIII. Is it to be doubted by reborn and renewed men concerning the perseverance of faith and piety?

The present state of grace, in which the reborn and renewed live, excludes every reason for doubting concerning the perseverance of faith and piety; since they are certain of it. are a), not indeed with absolute certainty, yet ordered, and conditioned b).

Proof a. The reborn and renewed are certain, because a) God the Father will grant the perseverance of faith, as Paul testifies, 1 Cor. 1:8. b) They are certain of the intercession of Christ, which He Himself promised, Luke 22:32. c) They are certain of the sealing of the Spirit, 2 Cor. 1:21, 22, see what was adduced above. They are therefore persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

Rom. 8:39. Proof b. The reborn, justified, and renewed are certain of their perseverance, not absolutely, but conditionally; if they duly perform their duty, concerning which see above, question 9. This the Formula of Concord, p. 803, teaches: It is the eternal decree of God that He wills to promote, confirm, and preserve unto the end that good work begun by Himself in them; provided only that they constantly lean upon His word as a staff, implore His aid with ardent prayers, persevere in the grace of God, and faithfully and well employ the gifts received.

SIGH.

Guard and seal in my heart, O eternal God, the true faith which Thou hast kindled by mere grace in regenerating me! Save and strengthen in my soul Thine image, which Thou hast restored in renewing me! For indeed the devil, the world, and the flesh strive to extinguish saving faith and to destroy Thine image. The devil entices me to apostasy, the world and the flesh to impiety. I am unequal to repelling these enemies, unless Thou, Savior, workest what Thou hast effected, fortifiest me with Thy divine strength, and supportest me with Thy most present aid. Wherefore I beseech and implore that Thou wouldst perpetually rule, sustain, and strengthen me by Thy most Holy Spirit, so that I may fight the good fight against all enemies, finish the course of piety with unoffending foot, retain faith persevering even unto the last breath of life, and by Thy most liberal grace carry away the crown of righteousness and glory!

Latin:

Præsens status gratiæ, in quo viuunt renati & renouati, omnem dubitandi rationem de perseverantia fidei & pietatis excludit; quippe cuius certi sunt. a), non quidem certitudine absoluta, attamen ordinata, atque conditionata b).

Prob. a. Certi sunt renati & renovati, quod a) Deus Pater fidei perseverantiam sit largiturus, teste Paulo, 1 Cor. I, 8. b) Certi sunt intercessionis Christi, quam ipse promisit, Luc. XXII, 23. c) Certi sunt obsignationis Spiritus 2 Cor. I, 21. 22. vid. supra adducta. Persuasi igitur sunt, quod neque mors, neque vita, neque angeli, neque principatus, neque virtutes, neque instantia, neque futura, neque altitudo, neque profunditas, neque aliqua creatura alia poterit nos separare a dilectione Dei, quae in Christo Iesu, Domino nostro, est.

Rom. VIII, 39. Prob. b. Certi sunt renati, iustificati & renovati, suae perseverantiae, non absolute, sed conditionate; si officio suo rite perfungantur, de quo supra, quaest. 9. Quod condocefacit Formula Concord. p. 803. Aeternum Dei decretum est, quod opus illud bonum, a se in illis inceptum, promovere, atque confirmare, & ad finem usque conservare velit; si modo verbo ipsius, tanquam scipioni, constanter innitantur, ipsius opem ardentibus precibus implorent, in gratia Dei perseverent, & dona accepta fideliter & bene collocent.

SUSPIRIUM.

Tuere & obsigna in corde meo, o Deus aeterne, veram fidem, quam ex mera gratia me regenerando accendisti! Serva & firma in anima mea imaginem tuam, quam me renovando instaurasti! Etenim & fidem salvificam extinguere, & imaginem tuam destruere connituntur diabolus, mundus, caro. Diabolus ad apostasiam, mundus & caro ad impietatem me follicitant. Quibus hostibus repellendis impar sum, nisi tu, feruator, opereris, quod efficisti, diuino tuo robore me praemunias, & praesentissima tua ope suffulcias. Quare obtestor & obsecro, vt Spiritu tuo sanctissimo perpetuo me regas, sustentes, corrobores, quo aduersus omnes hostes bonum certamen decertem, cursum pietatis inoffenso pede soluam, fidem vsque ad nouissimum vitae halitum perseuerantem retineam, atque ex gratia tua liberalissima coronam iustitiae & gloriae reportem!


## 27 On Glorifying Grace, and Eternal Blessedness

Question I.

What is glorification? Glorification is an act of grace by which God transfers men who are justified, persevering in faith unto the end, and having departed from this life, from the kingdom of grace into the kingdom of glory, so that they may obtain eternal blessedness and celebrate the divine name with everlasting praises.

Latin:

Quaest. I. Quid est glorificatio?

Glorificatio est actus gratiae, quo Deus homines iustificatos, in fide vsque ad finem perseuerantes, & ex hac vita egressos, e regno gratiae in regnum gloriae transfert, vt aeternam beatitudinem obtineant, nomenque diuinum sempiternis laudibus concelebrent.


### Question II. Who glorifies us?
