Antithesis est Pontificiorum, asserentium, promissiones euangelicas requirere conditionem operum. Quorum argumenta sunt:

I. Christus legisperito ad æternam vitam adspiranti dicit: Hoc fac, & viues! Luc. X, 28. E. Christus in euangelio suo ab homine vitam æternam adepturo requirit conditionem operum. Resp. Quæstio legisperiti erat legalis, his proposita verbis: Quidnam faciens vitam æternam hereditate accepturus sum? Qualis autem erat quæstio, talis responsio. Hinc Christus dicit: Diliges Dominum, Deum tuum &c.

Instantia: Responsio Christi exstat in euangelio: E. est euangelica. Resp. Euangelium hic sumitur sensu speciali, prout legi opponitur.

II. Euangelium requirit fidem: E. & bona opera. Ratio consequentiæ est; quia fides est genitrix bonarum actionum. Resp. Fidem gignere bona opera in iustificatis, largimur faciles; iustificatis, largimur faciles; iustificatis, largimur faciles;

quaeritur autem, an remissio peccatorum & vita aeterna sub conditione bonorum operum promissa sit? quod negamus. Pertinent bona opera ad hominis renovationem, non ad iustificationem, aut beatificationem: Et norma bonorum operum est lex, non euangelium.

III. Quidquid promittitur sub conditione mortificationis carnis, illud promittitur sub conditione boni operis: Atqui vita aeterna &c. E. Maior claret: quia mortificatio carnis est bonum opus, praecepto decalogi nono mandatum. Minor probatur ex Rom. VIII, 13. Si spiritu actiones carnis mortificatis, vivetis. Resp. Dist. inter conditionem subiecti, cui possessio vitae aeternae contingit, & inter conditionem rei, sub qua vita aeterna promittitur. Mortificatio carnis est conditio subiecti, antecedens vitam aeternam antecedens ordinis, non causalitatis; cum nec medium salutis, nec causa meritoria vitae aeternae fit.


### On the Difference Between the Old and New Testament

Obs. Since the solemn promulgation of the law properly pertains to the old, but the solemn promulgation of the gospel to the new testament, therefore, having explained the differences between the law and the gospel, we shall append the distinction between the O. and N. T.

Latin:

Obs. Cum solemnis promulgatio legis ad vetus, solemnis autem promulgatio euangelii ad novum testamentum proprie pertineat, ideo, differentiis inter legem & euangelium explicatis, discrimen V. & N. T. subiungemus.


### Quest. XVI. What is the divine testament?

Testament is the most free disposition of the will of God concerning divine worship, and the means of salvation and the form of government in the church, confirmed by the death and blood either of a typical animal, or of the testator himself, to the praise of divine grace and justice and for the salvation of men.

Obs. I. Testament is called in Hebrew בְּרִית, which word in general signifies a covenant, or pact sanctioned between two or more. It is derived from the root בָּרָה, he chose; because in a covenant both the persons between whom, and the things and conditions for which the covenant is entered into, are chosen. This Hebrew name was expressed by AQUILA the Pontian, SYMMACHUS, and THEODOTION by συνθήκην, i.e., covenant or pact; but the LXX interpreters, and the writers of the new testament who followed them, rendered it everywhere by διαθήκην, which name denotes a disposition, as much federal as testamentary, or similar to a covenant, and to the disposition of a last will.

Obs. II. Pact, covenant, and testament are used by some in this sacred matter as equipollent terms; yet they differ in certain respects. For a pact is the consensus of two or more, concerning some matter, either to be given or to be done, conceived in express words: a covenant, as SUIDAS defines it, is a mutual obligation, by which the contracting parties agree concerning certain conditions to be mutually performed, e.g., concerning society, concerning commerce, concerning judgments, etc.: a testament is the legitimate disposition of a testator, by which, being about to die, he distributes his goods among his heirs. Therefore, a covenant differs from a testament: 1) In a covenant the consensus of both parties is required; but in constituting a testament the consensus of both parties is not necessary: 2) From a covenant certain benefits accrue to each party; in a testament, to the heir: 3) A covenant is valid between the living, and is extinguished when one party is dead; but a testament is confirmed by the death of the testator: 4) One party cannot make a confirmed covenant void against the will of the other; but a testator, while he lives, can change and correct his testament. 5) In a covenant a mediator is required, not in a testament.

Obj. III. In the divine arrangement concerning the dispensation of the means of salvation, and in divine worship and the government of the church, some tempering of a covenant and a testament, properly so called, is discerned, so that it may be called by the compound term testament-covenant or federal testament, or testamentary covenant. For it is a testament on account of the most ample bequeathed goods, and the necessity of intervening death; which two things are not necessarily required in a covenant. One of the covenanters does not transcribe or destine all his goods to the other, nor does he devote himself to death for the same. But the sanction of our mediator has from the covenant a certain immutability and personal obligation.

Obj. IV. Our discourse at present is not concerning the most ancient legal covenant, which God entered into with Adam in his integrity, and demanded from man the most perfect observation of the divine law, both natural and positive, and liberally promised him eternal life as a reward, with the addition of a commination of punishment if he should transgress the law, Gen. 2:16: nor concerning the covenant of grace, sanctioned with the fathers after the fall, by which God promised His grace, the remission of sins, and eternal life to all who believe in the Messiah, and demanded from them the obedience of constant faith; which promise of grace made to Abraham, the father of believers, comes under the name of διαθήκης, or testament, Gal. 3:17: nor concerning the external sign or instrument of the testament, or the testimony of the tablets; in which way the sign of circumcision is called a testament, Acts 7:8, and the federal tablets, or prophetic books, come under the name of testament, 2 Cor. 3:6, 14; they are called a divine testament ὡς ἐν πλάτει, metonymically and improperly. But we must accurately consider what is denoted by the name of testament, when the old and new testaments, taken in the proper sense, are opposed to each other and distinguished from one another.

Latin:

Testamentum est dispositio liberrimae voluntatis Dei de cultu divino, mediisque salutis ac forma regiminis in ecclesia, confirmata morte & sanguine vel pecuino typico, vel ipsius testatoris, in gratiae ac iustitiae divinae laudem & hominum salutem.

Obs. I. Testamentum Hebraeis dicitur בְּרִית, quae vox in genere significat foedus, aut pactum inter duos, pluresue sancitum. Deducitur a rad. בָּרָה, elegit; quia in foedere eliguntur tum personae, inter quas, tum res ac conditiones, propter quas foedus initur. Nomen hoc hebraeum ab AQVILA Pontico, SYMMACHO & THEODOTIONE per συνθήκην, i. e. foedus, vel pactum, expressum est; LXX. vero interpretes, & hos secuti scriptores novi testamenti ubique per διαθήκην reddiderunt, quod nomen notat dispositionem, tam foederalem, quam testamentariam, vel similem a foederi, & ultimae voluntatis dispositioni.

Obs. II. Pactum, foedus, & testamentum a nonnullis in hac materia sacra ut termini aequipollentes usurpantur; certis tamen respectibus differunt. Nam pactum est consensus duorum, aut plurium, de re quapiam, vel danda, vel facienda, expressis verbis conceptus: foedus, definiente SVIDA, est obligatio mutua, qua partes contrahentes de certis conditionibus, mutuo praestandis, conveniunt, v. gr. de societate, de commerciis, de iudiciis &c.: testamentum est legitima dispositio testatoris, qua moriturus bona sua inter heredes dispensat. Differt itaque foedus a testamento: 1) In foedere requiritur utriusque partis consensus; in testamento vero constituendo utriusque partis consensus non est necessarius: 2) Ex foedere utrique parti certa commoda conveniunt; in testamento heredi: 3) Foedus valet inter viuos, altera parte mortua exstinguitur; testamentum vero morte testatoris firmatur: 4) Foedus confirmatum altera pars, inuita altera, non potest irritum facere; testator vero, quod viuit, testamentum suum mutare & corrigere potest. 5) In foedere mediator requiritur, non in testamento.

Obf. III. In dispositione divina de mediorum salutis dispensatione, cultuque divino & gubernatione ecclesiae deprehenditur temperamentum aliquod foederis & testamenti, proprie dicti, ut composita voce testamento-foedus vel testamentum foederale, aut foedus testamentarium dici queat. Nam est testamentum propter legata bona amplissima, & mortis intervenientis necessitatem; quae duo in foedere non necessario requiruntur. Vnus foederatorum alteri omnia sua bona non transcribit, aut destinat, neque pro eodem se morti devovet. A foedere vero sanctio mediatoris nostri habet quandam immutabilitatem & personalem obligationem.

Obf. IV. In praesenti nobis sermo non est de foedere legali antiquissimo, quod Deus cum Adamo integro iniuit, & ab homine perfectissimam divinae legis tum naturalis, tum positivae observationem postulauit, atque eidem vitam aeternam in praemium liberaliter promisit, addita comminatione poenae, si legem transgrederetur, Gen. II, 16.: neque de foedere gratiae, cum patribus post lapsum sancito, quo Deus gratiam suam, remissionem peccatorum & vitam aeternam omnibus in Messiam credentibus promisit, constantisque fidei obedientiam ab iisdem postulauit; quae promissio gratiae facta Abrahae, patri credentium, διαθήκης, siue testamenti nomine venit, Gal. III, 17.: neque de externo testamenti vel signo, vel instrumento, seu testimonio tabularum; quomodo fignum circumcisionis testamentum dicitur, Act. VII, 8. & tabulae foederales, siue libri prophetici nomine testamenti veniunt, 2 Cor. III, 6. 14.; dicuntur autem testamentum divinum ὡς ἐν πλάτει, metonymice & improprie. Nobis autem accurate considerandum est, quid nomine testamenti denotetur, cum vetus & nouum testamenta, proprio sensu accepta, sibi opponantur, & a se inuicem discriminentur.


### Quest. XVI. What is the divine testament?: Q. XVII

Q. XVII.

How many are the divine testaments? The divine testaments are two, the old and the new.

Proof 1) From Jer. 31:31-34. Behold, the days come, saith Jehovah, that I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah, not according to the covenant that I made with their fathers, in the day that I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; because they broke my covenant; although I was a husband unto them, saith Jehovah: but this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, saith Jehovah: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it upon their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people. And they shall teach no more every man his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, Know Jehovah! For they shall all know me, from the least of them unto the greatest of them, saith Jehovah: For I will be merciful to their iniquity, and I will remember their sin no more.

Obj. The prophet speaks 1) of the days of the Messiah to come: 2) of the evangelical covenant, which is of a different kind than that old legal pact. For the evangelical pact is a covenant of grace and faith: the legal pact is a covenant of justice and works. The covenant of grace is called by the Apostle the new testament: the covenant of justice and works is called the old testament, Heb. 8:8. The new testament was indeed instituted after the fall in paradise, as regards the promises and the saving applicability to men through faith in the promises: but it was consummated and solemnly promulgated when Christ was exhibited in the flesh. The old testament, or legal pact, was instituted before the fall with man in his integrity, and was solemnly promulgated on Mount Sinai. 3) God made the new testament with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah not exclusively, as if it pertained only to those houses; but inchoatively, because in the first place it was to be revealed and preached to the houses of Israel and Judah, but then to be transferred to other peoples. 4) The old covenant, or testament, was made with the fathers of the Israelites from Mount

Sinai not exclusively, as if it were made before with no human beings; but affirmatively, because it was given to all men from the beginning of the world, and was newly confirmed and solemnly promulgated to the fathers of the Israelites.

5) By the law, which God is about to write in the hearts of men, is denoted the salvific doctrine, or the law of faith, Rom. III, 27, which is the gospel; since under the New Testament the moral law is not to be observed in order to justify, but to teach new obedience, as the fruit of faith and a document of gratitude. It easily appears, therefore, what it is to inscribe upon the heart, and to put into the mind; namely, to illuminate the heart and soul through the Holy Spirit unto the true knowledge of faith, and to renew them unto new obedience, to mortify the old man, and to excite the new.

6) The doctrine of the Old Testament is legal outside of Christ: the doctrine of the New Testament is evangelical in Christ. For the teachers of the law always urged a perfect knowledge of God, and worship proceeding from that knowledge; which, because after the fall no man can perform, the law threatened, cursed, and condemned all who were under it.

For the perpetual voice of the law is: Know God, do this and you shall live! Cursed is everyone who does not do all things!

Which legal knowledge of God is not urged under the New Testament; yet the evangelical knowledge of faith is to be taught, which is not impossible, but falls upon all men through its own means, so that not only are the great to be capable of it, but also the small, indeed infants, inasmuch as they are not incapable of faith, Matt. XVIII, 6.

7) The doctrine concerning the remission of sins is proper to the New Testament; by the power of which God is propitious to iniquity, by pardoning it, and forgets sin, by not avenging the same.

Confer, D. SEBAST. SCHMID. in comment. on Hebr. VIII, 10. 11. 12. page 856. seqq. (*). 2) From (*)

In the doctrine concerning covenants and divine testaments, the greater care must be applied, the more serious are the controversies which intervene for us on this matter partly with the Reformed, partly with the Roman Catholics, partly with the Socinians.

I. Indeed, no one denies, 1) that a covenant sanctioned by God, as being worthy of God, cannot but be altogether singular, nor at all comparable with all those things which are required for covenants entered into by men, these in particular: a) the equality of the parties, b) the mutual and most free will on both sides, not only without any coercion, but also without any obligation by which either one might already be bound to the other beforehand, g) mutual utility, such as indeed falls upon no one in God, who needs no one, d) mutual and equal obligation, so that one might call the other, and the latter in turn the former, into court, if he should not wish to keep the pact.

But this also is confessed: 2) that those things cannot but be present which necessarily pertain to the nature of a covenant, whatever it may be, and these are the stipulation and the restipulation.

II. There are altogether two covenants which God made with the whole human race, of which indeed one is the legal covenant, or, as it is otherwise accustomed to be called, the covenant of works; the other, however, is the evangelical covenant, or, which is the same thing said, the covenant of grace.

The name of grace, in this argument, is used in that signification by which it is opposed 1) to the natural corruption of man and the wrath of God, 2) to the dignity of works, Eph. II, 3. & 4. 8.

9. Concerning the covenant of works, it is treated in Deut. VII, 9. 12. Hos. VI, 7. Concerning the covenant of grace, these sayings are to be understood, Gen. XVII, 7. coll. with Rom. IX, 5--8. Gal. III, 14. Isa. LIV, 10. LV, 3. Mal. III, 1. Luke I, 72. 74.

III. The covenant of works was made void without delay, as soon as the common parents of men broke it by their perfidy, and thus weakened it Rom. VIII, 3. so that from that time no mortal could be just before God by the sentence of the law, Gal. III, 21.

Immediately, therefore, the covenant of grace succeeded into its place, Gen. III, 15. declared in the first announcement.

This we defend with the greatest zeal against the Socinians. Confectar.

The giving and promulgation of the law, especially that most solemn one on Mount Sinai, was made by no means for the renewal of the covenant of works, but altogether for its perpetual remembrance, Hebr. X, 3. on account of the use of the law, both epanorthotic-pedagogical, by which everyone, guilty of sin, might be led to implore grace, and didactic, by which man, a participant of grace, might indeed act in accordance with the prescribed norm, yet always feeling that he still labors under many defects, and is never not in need of grace. 2) From Gal. IV, 21-26. Tell me, you who desire to be under the law: (Do) you not hear the law? For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by a slave woman, and the other by a free woman. But he who was of the slave woman was born according to the flesh. But he who was of the free woman, through the promise. Which things contain an allegory in themselves. For these are the two covenants: One indeed from Mount Sinai, which IV.

Latin:

Quæst. XVII. Quot sunt testamenta diuina?

Testamenta diuina sunt duo, vetus & nouum.

Prob. 1) E Ier. XXXI, 31-34. Ecce dies veniunt, dictum Iehouae, quibus pangam cum domo Israëlis, & cum domo Iudae, foedus nouum, non sicut foedus, quod pepigi cum patribus eorum, quo die apprehendi manum eorum ad educendum eos e terra Aegypti; quia illi irritum fecerunt foedus meum; ideo ego dominatus sum in eos, dictum Iehouae: sed hoc foedus, quod pangam cum domo Israëlis post dies hos, dictum Iehouae: Dabo legem meam in medio eorum, & super cor eorum scribam illam; eroque iis in Deum, & ipsi erunt mihi in populum. Neque docebunt amplius vir focium suum, aut vir fratrem suum dicendo: Cognoscite Iehouam! Omnes enim cognoscent me, a minimo eorum usque ad maximum eorum, dictum Iehouae: Quia propitius ero iniquitati eorum, & peccati eorum non amplius recordabor.

Obf. Loquitur propheta 1) de diebus Messiae venturis: 2) de foedere euangelico, quod alterius est generis, quam vetus illud pactum legale. Nam pactum euangelicum est foedus gratiae & fidei: Pactum legale est foedus iustitiae & operum. Foedus gratiae dicitur ab Apostolo testamentum nouum: Foedus iustitiae & operum vocatur testamentum vetus, Hebr. VIII, 8. Nouum testamentum quidem institutum est post lapsum in paradiso, quoad promissiones & salutarem applicabilitatem ad homines per fidem in promissiones: consummatum autem & solemniter promulgatum est Christo in carne exhibito. Vetus autem testamentum, siue pactum legale, institutum est ante lapsum cum homine integro, & solemniter promulgatum est in monte Sinai. 3) Pepigit Deus testamentum nouum cum domo Israëlis & cum domo Iudae non exclusive, quasi ad solas istas domos pertineat; sed inchoatiue, quod primo loco domibus Israël & Iuda reuelandum & praedicandum, deinde vero ad alios populos transferendum fuerit. 4) Vetus foedus, siue testamentum, factum est cum patribus Israëlitarum de monte

Sinai non exclusive, quasi prius cum nemine hominum factum fit; sed confirmative, quia ab initio mundi hominibus omnibus datum, patribus Israelitarum denuo confirmatum & solemniter promulgatum est.

5) Per legem, quam Deus scripturus est in ...corda hominum, denotatur doctrina salvifica, sive lex fidei, Rom. III, 27. quae est evangelium; cum sub novo testamento lex moralis non sit observanda, ut iustificet, sed ut doceat novam obedientiam, vt fructum fidei & gratitudinis documentum. Facile itaque apparet, quid fit inscribere cordi, & indere menti; nimirum, cor animumque per Spiritum S. illuminare ad veram cognitionem fidei, & renouare ad novam obedientiam, veterem hominem mortificare, & novum excitare.

6) Doctrina veteris testamenti est legalis extra Christum: novi testamenti doctrina est evangelica in Christo. Legis enim doctores semper vrgebant perfectam Dei cognitionem, cultumque, ex ista cognitione profectum; quem quia post lapsum nemo hominum praestare potest, lex comminabatur, maledicebat, & contemnabat omnes, qui sub illa erant.

Perpetua quippe legis vox est: Cognosce Deum, fac hoc & viues! Maledictus omnis, qui non facit omnia!

Quae cognitio Dei legalis non vrgetur sub novo testamento; docenda tamen est cognitio fidei evangelica, quae non est impossibilis, sed cadit in omnes homines per sua quidem media, ita vt non tantum magni eius futuri sint capaces, sed etiam parui, immo infantes, vtpote qui fidei non sunt incapaces, Matth. XVIII, 6.

7) Doctrina de remissione peccatorum est propria novi testamenti; vi cuius Deus est propitius iniquitati, eam condonando, & obliuiscitur peccati, idipsum non vindicando.

Confer, D. SEBAST. SCHMID. in comment. in Hebr. VIII, 10. 11. 12. pag. 856. seqq. (*). 2) Ex (*)

In doctrina de foederibus, ac testamentis divinis, eo maior adhibenda est cura, quo grauiores sunt, quae nobis de hac caussa partim cum Reformatis, partim cum Romanocatholicis, partim cum Socinianis intercedunt controversiae.

I. Id quidem nemo negat, 1) quod foedus a Deo sancitum, vtpote Deo dignum, non possit non prorsus singulare esse, nec omnino comparandum cum iis omnibus, quae ad foedera ab hominibus inita requiruntur, haec in primis: a) partium aequalitas, b) mutua vtrimque ac liberrima voluntas, non solum sine vlla coactione, sed etiam sine vlla obligatione, qua alteruter alteri iam ante devinctus sit, g) mutua vtilitas, qualis profecto nulla in Deum cadit, qui nemine indiget, d) mutua atque aequalis obligatio, vt alter alterum, & hic vicissim illum in ius vocare possit, si pactum seruare noluerit.

Est vero etiam hoc in confesso: 2) quod ea non possint non adesse, quae ad naturam foederis, qualecunque sit illud, necessario pertinent, & sunt stipulatio ac restipulatio.

II. Omnino duo sunt foedera, quae Deus cum vniverso hominum genere fecit, quorum quidem unum est foedus legale, seu, vt alias vocari solet, foedus operum; alterum vero foedus evangelicum, siue, quod idem dictum est, foedus gratiae.

Nomen gratiae, in hoc argumento, vsurpatur ea significatione, qua opponitur 1) naturali corruptioni hominis atque irae Dei, 2) operum dignitati, Eph. II, 3. & 4. 8.

9. De foedere operum agitur Deut. VII, 9. 12. Hos. VI, 7. De foedere gratiae intelligenda sunt haec dicta, Gen. XVII, 7. coll. cum Rom. IX, 5--8. Gal. III, 14. Ies. LIV, 10. LV, 3. Mal. III, 1. Luc. I, 72. 74.

III. Foedus operum sine mora irritum factum fuit, quam primum communes hominum parentes sua illud perfidia fregerunt, atque adeo infirmarunt Rom. VIII, 3. vt ab eo tempore nemo mortalium ex legis sententia iustus coram Deo esse potuerit, Gal. III, 21.

Continuo igitur in eius locum successit foedus gratiae, Gen. III, 15. primo nuntio declaratum.

Id quod summo nos studio aduersus Socinianos tuemur.

Confectar. Legum latio ac promulgatio, maxime solemnis illa in monte Sinai, facta fuit neutiquam ad renovationem foederis operum, sed prorsus ad eius recordationem perpetuam, Hebr. X, 3. propter vsum legis, tum epanorthotico-paedagogicum, quo quisque, peccati reus, ad gratiam implorandam duceretur, tum didactictum, quo gratiae particeps homo, normae praescriptae convenienter quidem ageret, semper tamen sentiens, se multis adhuc defectibus laborare, & nunquam non gratiae indigentem esse. gratiæ indigentem esse. gratiæ indigentem esse. 2) Ex Gal. IV, 21-26. Dicite mihi, qui sub lege esse vultis: (An) legem non audivistis? Scriptum enim est, quod Abrahamus duos filios habuerit, unum ex ancilla, & alterum ex libera. Sed qui quidem ex ancilla erat, iuxta carnem natus erat. Qui vero ex libera, per promissionem. Quae allegoriam in se continent. Haec enim sunt duo testamenta: Vnum quidem de monte Sinai, quod IV.


### Quest. XVI. What is the divine testament?: The agreement and difference of both covenants must be accurately known

The agreement and difference of both covenants must be accurately known.

Namely, ) they agree in a certain way, by reason of 1) the parties; for in both there are God and all men, not even one excepted (which the Reformed determine much otherwise, by whose opinion the covenant of works indeed pertains to all and singular men, but the covenant of grace to a few elect): 2) the foundation, which in both is the eternal counsel and decree of God: 3) the nature, since indeed in both there is a certain stipulation and restipulation: 4) the End; for both look to the glory of God, and the salvation of men, not only temporal, but also eternal.

Here the Reformed differ much from us, since 1) they falsely persuade themselves concerning the number of men, that all are entirely excluded from the covenant of grace, except the elect, 2) they invert the order of things, thinking the decree concerning the election of a few certain ones to be prior to that concerning Christ the sponsor, having satisfied for the guilt and punishment of men.

Our theologians have well understood, by an argument by far the most valid, that for the saving grace prepared equally for all in common, it is to be effected from the comparison of the covenant of works, and the covenant of grace, which indeed cannot be of a lesser condition than we know that to have been.

PAUL certainly has gravely taught us, that the covenant of grace, as far as it pertains to sinning men, extends as widely as the legal covenant, Rom.

V, 12, 18. and, as far as concerns sins committed by men, much more widely, ibid. 15, 16, 20. They differ among themselves, 2) by reason of the foundation.

That indeed in the covenant of works is the eternal decree of God, altogether congruent with his own kindness, holiness, and remunerating justice, and the state of integrity of men. But in the covenant of grace it is ) the eternal decree of God, not only consonant to holiness and vindicating justice, so that a necessary satisfaction is demanded, to be rendered for all the guilt and punishment of all men, but also convenient to mercy, by which God looked upon the misery of men, and the extreme lack of powers, and willed to accept the vicarious satisfaction of Christ the sponsor, as our own: ) the eternal pact of the Father with the Son.

Concerning this pact, classic passages exist:

Ps. II, 6. XXII, 26. XL, 8, 9. add. Hebr. X, 5. seqq. Io. XVII, 4, 5, 19. It consists 1) of the stipulation and pledge of the Son, in which these three things are contained: ) That he wills to take upon himself the guilt and punishment of all and singular men, Ps. XL, 8, 9. Io.

XVII, 19. ) That he therefore will render vicarious satisfaction fully, Isa. LIII, 12. ) That he will also reconcile all men, alienated from God, to God, by procuring the turning of souls from sins to God, and by the application of the satisfaction rendered, by offering it equally to all, to die ) These two covenants differ among themselves 1) by reason of the parties, to be considered in one way or another. For God in the covenant of works, or legal, is to be considered only as kind as well as just, and immutable: but in the evangelical, or covenant of grace, also as violated, angry, yet having pity on men, and prepared for reconciliation. Then as far as men are concerned, all are to be considered, in the legal covenant indeed, as innocent, of integrity of life, and instructed with powers sufficient for rendering to the law obedience entirely perfect and perpetual; but in the evangelical ) as perfidious, and for that reason guilty of damnation, ) as those, of all and singular of whom God has had pity; ) as those, for whom the eternal Son of God pledged himself, in their name, to satisfy fully the vindicating justice of God; ) as those, to each one of whom the vicarious satisfaction of Christ, and recovered salvation, as also the saving faith, by which each might receive it, is seriously to be offered; ) as those, from whose number some indeed, on account of an obstinacy of mind foreseen by God, because they would always be ἄπισοι (unbelieving), were adjudged to perfidy and inconstancy, because they would be at the end of this life πρόσκαιροι (temporary), to eternal damnation, already merited by sins, but others indeed, through a true faith in Christ foreseen by God, are to be led to eternal blessedness.

which generates into slavery, which is Hagar. For Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia; and she corresponds to the Jerusalem which now is, for she is in slavery with her children: But the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all. Paul expresses by these words two covenants, and says that they were prefigured in the wives of Abraham. The old in Hagar, the new in Sarah. Hagar is a bondwoman: thus the O.T. is a law of slavery. Sarah is a free woman: thus the N.T. is a promise of liberty. Hagar generates according to the flesh: thus the O.T. holds those subject to it liable by a certain obligation of nature. Sarah generates according to the promise: thus the N.T. regenerates through the evangelical promise. That which is signified by Hagar, and Sinai, a mountain in Arabia, not insofar as it is a natural mountain, but insofar as that mountain is the place where the law was given, and it shadows forth the Jerusalem which now is, i.e., the legal Jewish people, desiring to be justified by the law, by imparting to whose obedient ones, Isa. LIII, 11. Ps. XXII, 23, 28. Luke XXIV, 47. II) From the restipulation of the Father, who promised: α) That He willed to accept this pledge of the Son entirely, and to hold as ratified all things performed by Him, nay, even those still to be performed, as if they were already performed, Isa. LIII, 6.: β) That He, after the satisfaction had been performed, would adorn His Son with supreme glory, not for His own sake, but for our sake and for our salvation, Ps. VIII, 6. coll. with Heb. II, 7, 8, 9, 10. Isa. LIII, 10, 11.: γ) That He would give to the Son most perfect power to lead all who are obedient to Him unto salvation, but to exclude the obstinate despisers of grace from the possession of salvation: Ps. II, 8, 12. Isa. LIII, 10, 12. John XVII, 2. They differ 3) in their nature: For the stipulation and restipulation is one thing in the legal covenant, namely this: Do this, and you shall live! but another in the evangelical covenant, the sum of which is indeed this: Believe and you shall be saved! Rom. X, 4. seqq. And this opinion is opposed to the Roman Catholics, and others, who do not hesitate to mix the good works of man, and those which indeed seem good to them, into the covenant of grace.

V. Great caution is needed, lest anyone think that the covenant of works, or legal, and the Old Testament are one and the same thing. These two, which must be accurately distinguished, the Socinians always confuse with each other, and few are unaware of the false principles of this error. I will explain the force and reason of this distinction as briefly as I can. 1) In the covenant of works there was no one, nor could there be, who would make a testament, no death of his by which he would confirm it, no inheritance to be expected after his death. Christ would never have come if men had never sinned, He would never have undergone death for liberating men if men had never had to undergo the penalty of death. 2) The covenant of works ceased entirely to have its force for effecting the salvation of man as soon as man, perfidious by that vice, made it void, Rom. VIII, 3. add. Gal. III, 21. 22. The efficacy of the covenant of grace, on the contrary, existed continuously after man's first defection from the law, the πρωτευαγγέλιον [first gospel] having been received. (Propos. III. Confect.) Therefore, the covenant of grace was no less valid before Christ was born and died than after His birth and death. 3) The covenant of grace is called a testament, for this reason above all, because it was confirmed by the death of Christ, Heb. IX, 15. 16. which death of Christ, from the time when the πρωτευαγγέλιον [first gospel] had been heard, was signified by the death and blood of piacular victims, as by a type. 4) The Old Testament, therefore, is the covenant of grace itself, and it differs from the New Testament in no other way than by reason of a different οἰκονομία [dispensation], since in the O.T. the saving grace of God was conferred upon men on account of Christ still to come, through the shadow of many types, but especially preannounced by the death and blood of beasts; today in the N.T. the same grace is bestowed upon us through the same Christ, dead for us, all types having been abrogated. Therefore the antitypical grace of the N.T. is said to have succeeded in the place of the typical grace of the O.T., John I, 16. 17. 5) The ritual law of the O.T., insofar indeed as it was a law, availed unto the remembrance of the covenant of works, ἀνάμνησιν ἁμαρτιῶν [a remembrance of sins], Heb. X, 3. but by no means unto its renewal (Propos. III, Confect.); insofar however as it was ritual and typical, a preannouncement of Christ to come, it was to be referred entirely to the Gospel and to the covenant of grace. Thus the meaning of the words will be easily perceived, Heb. VIII, 8. seqq. coll. with IX, 15. 18. 22. X, 6. 9. I judged it my duty to note these things, since the b. Author, whose merits I indeed venerate, seems to me not to have explained distinctly enough in this place concerning one covenant of works, another of grace, and likewise concerning the old and new testament. whose metropolis is Jerusalem. Therefore the Old Testament is a legal covenant. Conversely, the seat of the New Testament is the Jerusalem above and free. It is above, because it has its origin from heaven and savors the things that are above (τὰ ἄνω), Col. III, 2. It is free, because it is immune from servitude and curse. Therefore the New Testament is an evangelical covenant, promising heavenly goods and freedom from the guilt and dominion of sin.

Q. XVII. What is the Old Testament? The Old Testament is the solemn disposition of the most free divine will, by which God, through the ministry of Moses, gave to the Israelite people, led out of Egypt, on Mount Sinai His law concerning divine worship and the government of the church and the Jewish polity, and promised to all who perfectly kept the law given, goods both corporal and temporal, and spiritual and eternal, but threatened temporal and eternal punishments to those transgressing the law, and willed that this federal disposition be confirmed by the sacraments of circumcision and the paschal lamb and the typical blood of animals, so that the divine justice might be manifested through the law, and the Israelites, convicted of their sins, might be driven to Christ the mediator.

Latin:

Adcurate cognoscenda est utriusque foederis & convenientia, & differentia.

Scilicet ) conveniunt quodammodo, ratione 1) partium; in vtroque enim sunt Deus & homines omnes, ne vno quidem excepto (quod multo aliter statuunt Reformati, quorum opinione foedus operum quidem ad omnes ac singulos pertinet homines, gratiae autem foedus ad paucos electos): 2) fundamenti, quod in vtroque est aeternum Dei consilium ac decretum: 3) natura, quoniam quidem in vtroque est quaedam stipulatio & restipulatio: 4) Finis; nam vtrumque spectat ad gloriam Dei, & salutem hominum, non modo temporalem, verum etiam aeternam.

Multum hic a nobis dissentiunt Reformati, cum 1) de numero hominum falso sibi persuadent, gratiae foedere prorsus exclusos esse omnes, praeter electos, 2) ordinem rerum inuertunt, decretum de electione paucorum quorundam putantes prius esse eo, de Christo sponsore, pro hominum culpa poenaque satis facto.

Nostrates Theologi probe intellexerunt, argumentatione longe validissimam, pro communi omnibusque pariter parata gratia salutari, efficiendam esse ex comparatione foederis operum, & foederis gratiae, quod nimirum hoc non possit esse minoris conditionis, quam illud fuisse scimus.

PAVLLVS certe grauiter nos edocuit, foedus gratiae, quod ad homines peccantes attinet, tam late patere, quam foedus legale, Rom.

V, 12, 18. &, quantum ad peccata, ab hominibus commissa, multo latius, ibid. 15. 16. 20. Differunt inter se, 2) ratione fundamenti.

Id nimirum in foedere quidem operum est aeternum Dei decretum, cum ipsius benignitate, sanctitate, & iustitia remunerante, hominumque statu integritatis, omnino congruens. In foedere autem gratiae est ) aeternum Dei decretum, non solum sanctitati, ac iustitiae vindicanti consentaneum, vt necessaria postuletur satisfactio, pro omni culpa & poena hominum omnium praestanda, sed etiam misericordiae conveniens, qua Deus respexit hominum miseriam, extremamque inopiam virium, & voluit vicariam Christi sponsoris satisfactionem, velut nostram, accipere: ) aeternum Patris pactum cum Filio.

De hac pactione loca classica exstant Ps.

II, 6. XXII, 26. XL, 8. 9. add. Hebr. X, 5. seqq. Io. XVII, 4. 5. 19. Ea constat 1) ex stipulatione ac sponsione Filii, in qua continentur haec tria: ) Se hominum omnium ac singulorum culpam poenamque omnem velle in se recipere, Ps. XL, 8. 9.

Io. XVII, 19. ) Se proinde satisfactionem vicariam ex asse praestiturum esse, Ies. LIII, 12. ) Se etiam homines omnes, a Deo abalienatos, Deo reconciliaturum esse, procuranda reuersione animorum a peccatis ad Deum, & satisfactionis praestitae adplicatione, omnibus eam peraeque offerendo, mori ) Differunt inter se haec duo foedera 1) ratione partium, aliter atque aliter considerandarum. Etenim Deus in foedere operum, sive legali, considerandus est tantum, vt benignus aeque ac iustus, atque immutabilis: in evangelico autem, sive gratiae foedere, etiam vt violatus, iratus, at hominum tamen misertus, atque ad reconciliationem paratus. Deinde quod ad homines attinet, omnes considerandi sunt, in legali quidem foedere, vt innocentes, integri vitae, ac viribus sufficientibus ad praestandam legi obedientiam omnino perfectam ac perpetuam instructi; in evangelico autem ) vt perfidi, ob eamque caussam damnationis rei, ) vt illi, quorum vniuersorum ac singulorum Deus misertus est; ) vt illi, pro quibus aeternus Dei filius spopondit, se, eorum nomine, diuinae iustitiae vindicanti satis ex asse facturum esse; ) vt illi, quorum vni cuique vicaria Christi satisfactio, ac recuperata salus, vt & fiducia salutaris, qua eam quisque acciperet, serio offerenda est; ) vt illi, quorum ex numero alii quidem, ob prauisam a Deo aut obstinationem animi, quod semper ἄπισοι futuri essent, ad perfidiam atque inconstantiam, quod futuri essent tandem in vitae huius termino πρόσκαιροι, damnationi aeternae, peccatis iam promeritae, adiudicati sunt, alii vero per prauisam a Deo veram eorum, & constantem in Christo fiduciam, ad beatitatem aeternam perducendi.

quod in servitutem generat, quae est Agar. Agar enim Sina mons est in Arabia; adumbrat autem eam, quae nunc est, Hierosolymam; servit autem cum liberis suis: Ea vero, quae sursum est, Hierosolyma, libera est illa, quae est mater omnium nostrum. Exprimit Paullus his verbis bina testamenta, & dicit ea praefigurata fuisse in uxoribus Abrahae. Vetus in Agare, novum in Sara. Agar est serva: ita V. T. est lex servitutis. Sara est libera: ita N. T. est promissio libertatis. Agar generat secundum carnem: ita V. T. naturae quadam obligatione sibi subiectos obnoxios habet. Sara generat secundum promissionem: ita N. T. regenerat per promissionem evangelicam. Id quod per Hagarem significatum est, et Sina, mons in Arabia, non quatenus est mons naturalis, sed quatenus mons iste est locus legis latae, & adumbrat Hierosolymam, quae nunc est, i. e. populum Iudaicum legalem, cupientem per legem iustificari, cuius morigeris impertiendo, Ies. LIII, 11. Ps. XXII, 23. 28. Luc. XXIV, 47. II) Ex restipulatione Patris, qui promisit: α) Se velle hanc Filii sponsionem omnino accipere, omniaque ab eo praestita, immo adhuc praestanda, ac si iam essent praestita; rata habere, Ies. LIII, 6.: β) Suum se Filium, praestita satisfactione, non propter se, sed propter nos, nostramque salutem, summa gloria ornaturum esse, Ps. VIII, 6. coll. cum Hebr. II, 7. 8. 9. 10. Ies. LIII, 10. 11.: γ) Se perfectissimam Filio potestatem daturum esse, omnes ipsi dicto audientes ad salutem perducendi, obstinatos autem gratiae contemptores salutis possessione excludendi: Ps. II, 8. 12. Ies. LIII, 10. 12. Ioan. XVII, 2. Differunt 3) natura sua: Nam stipulatio ac restipulatio alia quidem est in foedere legali, nimirum haec: Fac hoc, & vives! alia autem in foedere evangelico, cuius quippe summa haec est: Crede & salvus eris! Rom. X, 4. seqq. Atque haec sententia opposita est Romano-catholicis, aliisque, qui opera hominis bona, & quae ipsis quidem videntur bona, foederi gratiae immiscere non dubitant.

V. Magna cautione opus est, ne quis putet, foedus operum, sive legale, & vetus Testamentum rem unam eamdemque esse. Hac duo, accurate discernenda, semper inter se confundunt Sociniani, & falsa huius erroris principia pauci nesciunt. Distinctionis huius vim ac rationem explicabo, quam brevissime potero. 1) In foedere operum nullus fuit, nec esse potuit, qui testamentum faceret, nulla eius mors, qua illud ipse confirmaret, nulla hereditas, post eius mortem exspectanda. Christus nunquam venisset, si homines nunquam peccassent, nunquam ipse pro hominibus liberandis mortem oppetiisset, si homines nunquam mortis poenam subire debuissent. 2) Foedus operum suam vim ad salutem hominis efficiendam habere prorsus desiit, simul atque homo perfidus illo vitio illud irritum fecit, Rom. VIII, 3. add. Gal. III, 21. 22. Foederis, contra, gratiae efficacitas exstitit continuo post primam hominis a lege defectionem, πρωτευαγγέλιον percepto. (Propos. III. Confect.) Ergo foedus gratiae non minus ante Christum natum ac mortuum valuit, quam post ipsius nativitatem ac mortem. 3) Foedus gratiae dicitur testamentum, hanc potissimum ob causam, quia morte Christi confirmatum fuit, Hebr. IX, 15. 16. quae Christi mors ab eo tempore, quo πρωτευαγγέλιον auditum fuerat, morte ac sanguine victimarum piacularium, tanquam typo, significata fuit. 4) Vetus igitur testamentum est ipsum foedus gratiae, neque aliter a novo testamento differt, nisi ratione diversae οἰκονομίας, quando quidem in V. T. gratia Dei salutaris in homines conferebatur propter Christum adhuc venturum, multorumque typorum vmbra, praesertim vero morte ac sanguine pecudum praenuntiatum; hodie in N. T. eadem gratia nobis tribuitur per eumdem Christum, pro nobis mortuum, abrogatis typis omnibus. Idcirco gratia antitypica N. T. dicitur successisse in locum gratiae typicae V. Testamenti, Ioan. I, 16. 17. 5) Lex ritualis V. T. quatenus quidem lex fuit, valuit ad recordationem foederis operum, ἀνάμνησιν ἁμαρτιῶν, Hebr. X, 3. minime vero ad eius renovationem (Propos. III, Confect.); quatenus autem ritualis fuit ac typica, Christi aduenturi praenuntia, prorsus ad Evangelium ac foedus gratiae referenda fuit. Ita facile percipienda erit sententia verborum, Hebr. VIII, 8. seqq. coll. cum IX, 15. 18. 22. X, 6. 9. Haec adnotare, mearum partium esse ratus sum, quoniam b. Auctor, cuius equidem merita veneror, hoc in loco non satis distincte de foedere alio operum, alio gratiae, itemque de antiquo ac novo testamento exposuisse mihi visus est. cuius metropolis est Hierosolyma. Ergo vetus testamentum est pactum legale. Ex adverso sedes novi testamenti est Hierosolyma superna & libera. Superna est, quia habet originem suam e caelo & sapit τὰ ἄνω, Col. III, 2. Libera est, quia est immunis a servitute & maledictione. Ergo novum testamentum est pactum evangelicum, promittens bona coelestia & libertatem a reatu & dominio peccati.

Quaest. XVII. Quid est vetus testamentum? Vetus testamentum est solemnis dispositio liberrimae voluntatis divinae, qua Deus, interveniente Mosis ministerio, populo Israelitico, ex Aegypto educto, in monte Sinai legem suam de cultu divino, & gubernatione ecclesiae atque politiae Iudaicae dedit, omnibusque latam legem perfecte servantibus bona tum corporalia & temporalia, tum spiritualia & aeterna promisit, legem vero transgredientibus temporales aeternasque poenas comminatus est, iuxta atque foederalem hanc dispositionem sacramentis circumcisionis & agni paschalis atque sanguine animalium typico confirmatam voluit, vt iustitia divina per legem manifestaretur, & Israelitae, peccatorum suorum convicti, ad Christum mediatorem compellerentur.


### Quest. XVI. What is the divine testament?: The agreement and difference of both covenants must be accurately known (continued)

Obj. I. We consider here the Old Testament, or legal [testament], not according to its first institution, made in paradise before the fall with man in his integrity (where the foundation of it was laid, as Dannhauer says in Hodof. phaenom. VI. p. 492), but according to its solemn promulgation, made on Mount Sinai.

Obj. II. Ecclesiastical writers by the Old Testament understand a) the covenant of grace, which God made after the fall with the fathers, in which He promised that He would freely receive and save sinners, through and because of the merit of the Messiah to come, but under the condition of persevering faith, to be fixed on the Messiah to come.

For that there is something older than the Sinaitic covenant, Paul clearly teaches, Gal. III, 16. But indeed when the Old Testament is distinguished from the New, it is said to have been sanctioned after the departure of the Israelites from Egypt, Jer. XXXI, 31, on Mount Sinai, Gal. IV, 24. b) The state of the church from the beginning of the world until the advent of the Messiah. In which sense the patriarchs, Moses, and the prophets are said to have lived in the Old Testament. c) The writings of Moses and the prophets, comprising the history of the church from the created world until Christ was born.

See 2 Cor. III, 14. d) In the most special sense it denotes the legal covenant entered into on Mount Sinai between God and the people, through the ministry of Moses, with great solemnity and majesty.

Q. XIX. What is the New Testament? The New Testament is the solemn disposition of the most free divine will concerning the Christian religion and the government of the church, confirmed by the blood and death of the mediator Christ, by which God calls all men through the gospel and the sacraments of baptism and the Lord's supper to the church, and seriously intends to illuminate, regenerate, justify, renew, and glorify them, so that they may be through faith in Christ the sons of God, and heirs of eternal life, and may celebrate the grace of God with perpetual praises.

Obs. I. We consider here the new testament, or gospel, not according to its first institution, made in paradise after the fall with the first-formed pair, where its foundation was laid, and repeated to Abraham, but according to its solemn promulgation, made in Zion, or Jerusalem, Eph. II, 3 [sic; likely referring to Isa. 2:3 or similar]. Luke XXIV, 47. The new testament was consummated by the exhibition of Christ.

Obs. II. The name of the new testament is taken 1) for the doctrine, comprised in the writings of the Evangelists and Apostles: 2) For the whole state of the church, from the birth of the Savior until the very end of the world: 3) For the gracious covenant of the remission of sins, righteousness, and eternal life in Christ: which indeed God entered into with the first-formed humans after the fall and with the fathers, yet it was finally dedicated and confirmed by the death of the only-begotten Son, exhibited in the flesh: in which sense it is accepted by us here. Worthy of note here are the words of our CHEMNITIUS in *loc. theol.* part. III. fol. 70: "The doctrine of the law, insofar as it is a ministry of death and condemnation, wherever it is found in Scripture, pertains to the old testament. And the doctrine concerning the righteousness of faith in Christ, wherever it exists in Scripture, pertains to the new testament. Unless the new testament had been known to the fathers, whence, I ask, would Abraham and the remaining faithful have had the Spirit and life, since the new testament is the ministry of the Spirit and of life?"

Question XX. Do the old and new testaments agree in certain predicates? The old and new testaments agree in certain general predicates.

Prob. The O. and N. T. agree 1) In genus, or common concept. For each is a federal testament and a testamentary covenant, or a disposition of the will of God concerning divine worship and testamentary goods. 2) In author, who is the triune God, and in a peculiar way the Son of God, by whom both testaments were founded. 3) In testamentary goods. For in both testaments goods are promised, both temporal and eternal. 4) In dedication and confirmation. For each testament was dedicated and confirmed by blood. For the first testament was not dedicated without blood, says the Apostle, Heb. IX, 18. Each also has its own seals, or sacraments. 5) In publication. Both the old and the new testament, after their first institution, were solemnly promulgated in the fullness of time. 6) In the direction and preservation of order in the church. For each testament was sanctioned by the most wise God with this end and purpose, that the people of God might not wander by their own will, and stray in some mere *ataxia*, or confusion, but be contained within a certain form of polity, distinct from all other peoples.

Quæst. XXI. How do the old and new testaments differ? The old and new testaments differ: a) in specific form: b) in mediator: c) in the substance of confirmation: d) in sacraments: e) in the goods promised in each testament: f) in the condition under which they are promised: g) in constitutions and ceremonies: h) in effects: i) in the circumstances of the mode of promulgation, place, breadth, and time: k) in dignity and excellence.

Prob. a. The old testament is entirely legal, comprising the moral, ceremonial, and forensic law: The new testament is the gospel. The former is a testament of righteousness and works; because it exhibits the image of the righteousness and holiness which is in God, and urges the pursuit of good works. of works under the communion of temporal and eternal punishment. This is the testament of grace and faith. The former demands debt; the latter remits debt on account of the merit of Christ apprehended by true faith, Jer. 31:31 ff. The decree of the former is: Do this, and you shall live! Luke 10:28; Gal. 3:12. The decree of the latter is: Believe and you shall live! Rom. 10:9; Acts 16:31. Whence all who have been saved (even under the state of the Old Testament, in which the moral, ceremonial, and forensic law of Moses still flourished) were saved no otherwise than through the grace of Jesus Christ (and thus by the power of the Gospel and the New Testament), Acts 15:11. Cf. Hulsemann, Brev. cap. 8, p. 493. Prob. b. The mediator of the New Testament is Christ, Heb. 9:15. The messenger and interpreter of the Old Testament was Moses, who is not indeed called a mediator anywhere, but the servant of the Lord, Num. 12:7; Heb. 3:4. Yet he received the tables of the covenant from God, and brought them down to the people, and sprinkled the volume of the covenant with sacrificial blood, Exod. 24:7. Whence he is called by some authors a typical legal mediator, on account of his office of interpreting; but Christ is the evangelical mediator, true and ἱλασμὸς (propitiation), on account of the benefit of satisfaction.

For the law was given through Moses, but grace and truth were made through Christ, John 1:17, where John opposes grace to the moral law, and truth to the ceremonial law, which consists of types, and the Lord to the servant. For the law was given through Moses the servant, but grace was made, i.e., meritoriously acquired through Christ, the true mediator. Prob. c.

The Old Testament was ratified with animal and typical blood, Exod. 24:8; Heb. 9:20. But the New Testament was confirmed with the blood of the Son of God, Matt. 26:28. Whence animal blood pertains to the substance of the O.T., but the blood of the Son of God to the substance of the N.T. Prob. d.

The sacraments of the O.T. are circumcision and the passover, or the paschal lamb: the sacraments of the N.T. are baptism and the Lord's supper.

Prob. e. The Old Testament had special promises concerning the glorious occupation and happy possession of the land of Canaan, and the preservation of the Jewish polity until the coming of the Messiah. It also had promises concerning eternal spiritual goods, but less open and for the most part covered by the shadows and figures of types. The New Testament contains promises concerning spiritual goods that are open, but it promises bodily goods generally with the exception of the cross. Prob. f.

In the legal covenant God promised His people temporal and eternal, bodily and spiritual goods, under the condition of proper and perfect obedience, Exod. 19:5, and the people promised obedience, Exod. 24:3-7. But in the evangelical covenant God has promised us the gratuitous remission of sins, righteousness, and eternal life, in view of faith, which apprehends the satisfaction and merit of Christ, Jer. 31:31.

The Old Testament consisted of a huge multitude of constitutions, rites, and ceremonies, joined with infinite burdens. But the New Testament has rites very few in number, most easy to perform, most august in understanding, restricted to baptism and the eucharist. Whence Augustine, Contra Adimant. cap. 16, writes: In the Old Testament were the burdens of servants, but in the New is the glory of the free. Prob. h.

The effects of the O.T. and N.T. are plainly diverse and opposite. The O.T., insofar as it denotes a legal pact, urges the pursuit of good works; but it does not confer the strength to perform good works. But the N.T. inscribes faith into the heart of the faithful, and grants strength, by which they do not indeed perfectly fulfill the moral law, but by which, instructed, they may serve God with a sincere heart, and walk more and more worthily of the Gospel, Phil. 1:27. The O.T. demonstrates sins, Rom. 7:7. The N.T. offers the remission of sins, Jer. 31:34. The O.T. works wrath, Rom. 4:15; curses, Deut. 26:26; kills, 2 Cor. 3:6. The N.T. promises grace, Heb. 8:8. blesses, Gal. III, 14. makes alive, 2 Cor. III, 6.

Whence gratuitous justification is from the new, but not from the old testament. For if a law had been given which could make alive, truly righteousness would be from the law, Gal. III, 21. Which ἀδυναμία [impotence] of justifying, however, is not absolute and simple: for the law is in itself good and holy, Rom. VII, 12. 1 Tim. I, 8. and could justify man in the state of integrity: but it is respective and accidental, by reason of our flesh, which weakens the law of God, however holy and good it is in itself, so that it cannot fulfill the condition of the law, i.e., it cannot render perfect obedience to the law, Rom. VII, 14. c. VIII, 3.

Prob. i. The old and new testaments differ in the manner of promulgation. The former was published amidst thunders, Exod. XIX, 16. The latter was promulgated with a sweet invitation, Matth. XXVIII, 19. The former was promulgated on Mount Sinai: The latter went forth from Mount Zion, Is. II, 2. The former was entered into with the Israelites: The latter offers the grace of God to all men, Mark XVI, 15. The former was promulgated after the departure of the Israelites from Egypt: The latter was consummated when Christ was exhibited. The former was to be abrogated with the Jewish polity, Heb. VII, 18. c. VIII, 13. The latter will stand firm until the consummation of the age, 1 Cor. XV, 2.

Prob. k. The old and new testaments differ in dignity and excellence. For the old testament has a shadow of good things to come; but the new testament exhibits to us the body itself or the complement in Christ exhibited, Heb. X, 1. Wherefore from all these differences we gather the prerogative of the new testament: By as much as the causal means of salvation is more excellent than the pedagogical means, Christ than Moses, the blood of the mediator than the blood of cattle, a clear and gratuitous promise than a less clear and conditional one, liberty than servitude, the ministry of life than the ministry of death, a universal and eternal covenant than a particular and temporary one, the body than the shadow; by so much is the new testament more excellent than the old testament. Quest.

Latin:

Obs. I. Consideramus hic testamentum vetus, sive legale, non secundum primam institutionem, factam in paradiso ante lapsum cum homine integro (ubi fundamentum illius iactum est, dicente Dannhav. in hodof. phaenom. VI. p. 492.) sed secundum solemnem eius promulgationem, factam in monte Sinai.

Obs. II. Scriptores ecclesiastici per vetus testamentum intelligunt a) foedus gratiae, quod Deus post lapsum pepigit cum patribus, in quo promisit, se peccatores gratis recepturum & salvaturum esse, per & propter meritum Messiae venturi, sed sub conditione fidei perseverantis, in Messia venturo defigendae.

Dari enim foedere Sinaitico vetustius aliquod, clare docet Paullus Gal. III, 16. At vero cum vetus testamentum novo contradistinguitur, illud sancitum esse dicitur post egressum Israelitarum ex Aegypto, Ier. XXXI, 31. in monte Sinai Gal. IV, 24. b) Statum ecclesiae ab exordio mundi vsque ad adventum Messiae. Quo sensu patriarchae, Moses, & prophetae dicuntur vixisse in veteri testamento. c) Scripta Mosis & prophetarum, complectentia historiam ecclesiae a condito mundo vsque ad natum Christum.

Vid. 2 Cor.

III, 14. d) Sensu specialissimo notat pactum legale in monte Sinai inter Deum & populum, interveniente ministerio Mosis, magna solemnitate & maiestate initum. Quaest. XIX. Quid est novum testamentum? Novum testamentum est solemnis dispositio liberrimae voluntatis divinae de christiana religione & gubernatione ecclesiae, sanguine & morte mediatoris Christi confirmata, qua Deus omnes homines per evangelium & sacramenta baptismi & coenae dominicae ad ecclesiam vocat, eosdemque illuminare, regenerare, iustificare, renovare, glorificare serio intendit, vt sint per fidem in Christum filii Dei, haeredesque vitae aeternae, & gratiam Dei perpetuis laudibus concelebrent.

Obs. I. Consideramus hic nouum testamentum, siue euangelium, non secundum primam institutionem, factam in paradiso post lapsum cum protoplastis, vbi fundamentum eius iactum est, & repetitam Abrahamo, sed secundum solemnem eius promulgationem, factam in Sione, siue Hierosolyma, Ef. II, 3. Luc. XXIV, 47. Nouum testamentum consummatum est exhibito Christo.

Obs. II. Nomen noui testamenti sumitur 1) pro doctrina, scriptis Euangelistarum & Apostolorum comprehensa: 2) Pro toto statu ecclesiæ, a Saluatoris natiuitate vsque ad vltimum mundi finem: 3) Pro pacto gratioso remissionis peccatorum, iustitiæ & vitæ æternæ in Christo: quod quidem cum hominibus protoplastis post lapsum & patribus iniuit Deus, tandem tamen morte filii vnigeniti, in carne exhibiti, dedicatum & confirmatum est: Quo sensu hic a nobis accipitur. Notari hic merentur verba nostri CHEMNITII in loc. theol. part. III. fol. 70. Doctrina legis, quatenus est ministerium mortis & damnationis, vbicunque in scriptura inuenitur, pertinet ad vetus testamentum. Et doctrina de iustitia fidei in Christum, vbicunque in scriptura exstat, pertinet ad nouum testamentum. Nisi nouum testamentum partribus innotuisset, vnde quæso Abraham & reliqui fideles Spiritum & vitam habuissent, cum nouum testamentum sit ministratio Spiritus & vitæ?

Quæst. XX. An vetus & nouum testamentum quibusdam prædicatis conueniunt? Vetus & nouum testamentum conueniunt quibusdam prædicatis generalibus.

Prob. Vetus & N. T. conueniunt 1) Genere, siue conceptu communi. Vtrumque enim est testamentum fœderale & fœdus testamentarium, siue dispositio voluntatis Dei de cultu diuino & bonis testamentariis. 2) Auctore, qui est Deus triunus, & peculiari ratione Filius Dei, a quo vtrumque testamentum conditum est. 3) Bonis testamentariis. Vtroque enim testamento promittuntur bona, tum temporalia, tum æterna. 4) Dedicatione & confirmatione. Vtrumque enim testamentum dedicatum & confirmatum est sanguine. Neque enim prius testamentum sine sanguine dedicatum est, ait Apostolus Hebr. IX, 18. Vtrumque etiam sua habet sigilla, siue sacramenta. 5) Publicatione. Tam vetus, quam nouum testamentum post primam institutionem in plenitudine temporis solemniter promulgatum est. 6) Directione & conseruatione ordinis in ecclesia. Vtrumque enim testamentum a Deo sapientissimo hoc fine ac consilio sancitum est, vt ne populus Dei proprio vagetur arbitrio, & in inera quapiam ἀταξίᾳ, siue confusione oberret, sed intra certam politiæ formam, a reliquis omnibus populis distinctam contineatur.

Quæst. XXI. Quomodo vetus & nouum testamentum differunt? Vetus & nouum testamentum differunt: a) forma specifica: b) mediatore: c) confirmationis substantia: d) sacramentis: c) bonis, in vtroque testamento promissis: f) conditione, sub qua promissa sunt: g) constitutionibus & cærimoniis: h) effectis: i) circumstantiis modi promulgationis, loci, latitudinis, & temporis: k) dignitate & præstantia.

Prob. a. Testamentum vetus totum est legale, complectens legem moralem, cærimonialem & forensem: Testamentum nouum est euangelium. Illud est testamentum iustitiæ & operum; quia exhibet imaginem iustitiæ & sanctitatis, quæ est in Deo, & vrget studium bonorum. operum sub communione temporalis aeternaeque poenae. Hoc est testamentum gratiae & fidei. Illud exigit debitum; hoc debitum propter meritum Christi vera fide apprehensum remittit, Ier. XXXI, 31. seqq. Illius decretum est: Fac hoc, & viues! Luc. X, 28. Gal. III, 12. Huius decretum est: Crede & viues! Rom. X, 9. Act. XVI, 31. Vnde omnes, qui saluati sunt (etiam sub statu veteris testamenti, in quo vigebat adhuc lex Mosis moralis, caerimonialis & forensis) non aliter, quam per gratiam Iesu Christi (adeoque vi euangelii ac noui testamenti) sunt saluati, Act. XV, 11. Conf. Hvlsemann. breu. cap. VIII. p. 493. Prob. b. Noui testamenti mediator est Christus, Hebr. IX, 15. Veteris testamenti internuntius & interpres fuit Moses, qui non quidem mediator vspiam vocatur, sed seruus Domini, Num. XII, 7. Hebr. III, 4. Accepit tamen tabulas foederis a Deo, detulitque ad populum, & volumen foederis sanguine sacrificiali conspersit, Exod. XXIV, 7. Ex quo a nonnullis auctoribus mediator legalis typicus, ob interpretandi officium, nuncupatur; Christus autem est mediator euangelicus, verus & ἱλασμὸς, ob satisfaciendi beneficium.

Lex enim per Mosen data est, gratia & veritas per Christum facta est, Io. I, 17. vbi Ioannes legi morali opponit gratiam, legi caerimoniali, quae constat typis, veritatem, seruo dominum. Lex enim data est per Mosen seruum, gratia vero facta, i. e. meritorie acquisita est per Christum, verum mediatorem. Prob. c.

Vetus testamentum sancitum est sanguine pecuino & typico, Exod. XXIV, 8. Hebr. IX, 20. Nouum vero testamentum confirmatum est sanguine Filii Dei, Matth. XXVI, 28. Vnde sanguis pecuinus ad substantiam V. T., sanguis vero filii Dei ad substantiam N. T. pertinet. Prob. d.

Sacramenta V. T. sunt circumcisio & pascha, siue agnus paschalis: sacramenta N. T. sunt baptismus & coena dominica. Prob. e.

Vetus testamentum habuit promissiones speciales de gloriosa occupatione & felici possessione terrae Canaan, & conseruatione politiae Iudaicae vsque ad aduentum Messiae. Habuit etiam promissiones de bonis spiritualibus aeternis, sed minus apertas & magnam partem typorum vmbris & figuris tectas. Nouum testamentum continet promissiones de bonis spiritualibus apertas, bona autem corporalia promittit generatim cum exceptione crucis. Prob. f.

In foedere legali Deus populo suo promisit bona temporalia & aeterna, corporalia & spiritualia, sub conditione propriae & perfectae obedientiae, Exod. XIX, 5. & populus pollicitus est obedientiam, Exod. XXIV, 3--7. In foedere autem euangelico Deus nobis promisit gratuitam peccatorum remissionem, iustitiam & vitam aeternam, intuitu fidei, satisfactionem & meritum Christi apprehendentis, Ierem XXXI, 31.

Hebr. VIII, 8. Rom. III, 24. Prob. g. Vetus testamentum constabat ex ingente constitutionum, rituum & caerimoniarum multitudine, cum infinitis molestiis coniuncta. At nouum testamentum habet ritus numero paucissimos, factu facillimos, intellectu augustissimos, ad baptismum & eucharistiam restrictos. Vnde Avgvstinvs, contra Adimant. cap. XVI. scribit: In veteri test. erant onera seruorum, in nouo autem est gloria liberorum. Prob. h.

Effecta V. & N. T. sunt plane diuersa & opposita. V. T. quatenus pactum legale notat, vrget studium bonorum operum; sed non confert vires, bona opera patrandi. At N. T. inscribit fidem in cor fidelium, & donat vires, quibus non quidem perfecte legem moralem implent, sed quibus instructi Deo sincero corde seruiant, & magis magisque digne euangelio ambulent, Phil. I, 27. V. T. peccata demonstrat, Rom. VII, 7. N. T. peccatorum condonationem offert, Ier. XXXI, 34. V. T. operatur iram, Rom. IV, 15. maledicit, Deut. XXVI, 26. occidit, 2 Cor. III, 6. N. T. promittit gratiam, Hebr. VIII, 8. benedicit, Gal. III, 14. viuificat, 2 Cor.

III, 6. Vnde ex nouo, non autem ex veteri testamento est gratuita iustificatio. Si enim data esset lex, quæ posset viuificare, reuera ex lege esset iustitia, Gal. III, 21. Quæ tamen ἀδυναμία iustificandi non est absoluta & simplex: est enim lex per se bona & sancta, Rom VII, 12. 1 Tim. I, 8. hominemque in statu integritatis iustificare potuit: sed respectiua & accidentaria, ratione carnis nostræ, quæ legem Dei, quantumuis in se sanctam bonamque, infirmat, tum conditionem legis implere, i. e. perfectam legi obedientiam præstare nequit, Rom VII, 14. c. VIII, 3.

Prob. i. Vetus & nouum testamenta differunt modo promulgationis. Illud inter tonitrua publicatum est, Exod. XIX, 16. Hoc promulgatum est cum suaui compellatione, Matth. XXVIII, 19. Illud in monte Sinai promulgatum est: Hoc exiuit ex monte Sion, Es. II, 2. Illud cum Israëlitis initum est: Hoc offert gratiam Dei omnibus hominibus, Marc. XVI, 15. Illud promulgatum est post egressum Israëlitarum ex Ægypto: Hoc consummatum est Christo exhibito. Illud cum politia Iudaica abrogandum fuit, Hebr. VII, 18. c. VIII, 13. Hoc vsque ad consummationem sæculi firmum stabit, 1 Cor. XV, 2.

Prob. k. Vetus & nouum testamenta differunt dignitate & præstantia. Vetus enim testamentum habet vmbram futurorum bonorum; sed testamentum nouum nobis exhibet ipsum corpus siue complementum in Christo exhibito, Hebr. X, 1. Quare ex omnibus recentis differentiis prærogatiuam noui testamenti colligimus: Quanto præstantius est medium salutis causale medio pædagogico, Christus Mose, sanguis mediatoris sanguine pecuino, promissio clara & gratuita minus clara & conditionata, libertas seruitute, ministerium vitæ ministerio mortis, fœdus vniuersale & æternum particulari & temporario, corpus vmbra; tanto præstantius est testamentum nouum testamento veteri.


### XXII. Did God in the old testament promise spiritual and eternal goods?

God in the old testament did indeed promise spiritual and eternal goods, but under the condition of perfect obedience. Obs.

I. By the old testament we understand the legal covenant entered into by God with the Israelites; for this is properly called by the phrase of Scripture, the old testament, and is diametrically opposed to the new testament, Jer. XXX, 31. seq. Heb. VIII, 8. Gal. IV, 24. 2 Cor. III, 6.

Obs. II. The covenant of grace, which God struck with Adam, Abraham, and the remaining fathers from the first time of the fall, is indeed sometimes called the old testament by ecclesiastical writers, from Gal. III, 17. but speaking accurately, it pertains to the new testament. However, a distinction must be made between the new testament begun and consummated. God, by promising the Messiah the redeemer to fallen men, began the N.T.; but by sending his son into the flesh, he consummated it; by virtue of the covenant of grace (which is also called the gospel). That the fathers before Christ were justified and saved, we showed above, quest. V.; at present our discourse is concerning the old testament properly so called, or the legal covenant.

Prob. 1) From Lev. XVIII, 15. Ye shall observe my statutes, and my judgments, which if a man do, he shall live by them; for I am Jehovah. Conf. Ezek. XX, 11. That this promise of the law regards not only temporal life, but also eternal, is evident a) from the undoubted interpretation of Christ, Matth. XIX, 17. Luke X, 28. b) From the apostolic declaration, Rom. X, 5. Moses describeth the righteousness which is of the law, That the man which doeth those things shall live by them. Conf. Gal. III, 12. where the Apostle, from the opposition of the evangelical and legal promise, teaches that eternal life was promised also in the law, but under the condition of fulfilling the law. promised in the law, but under the condition of fulfilling the law. 2) From

2) From Lev. XXVI, 3. 11. 12. If you walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them: --- I will set my tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not abhor you; but I will walk among you, and will be your God: and you shall be my people. That this legal promise is to be understood concerning spiritual goods, Paul teaches in 2 Cor. VI, 16. The antithesis is that of the Anabaptists and Socinians, who assert that in the O.T. only bodily and temporal goods were promised, but not spiritual and eternal ones. Their stronger arguments are:

Their stronger arguments are: 1. If in the Old Testament heavenly goods had been promised to sinful men, the Apostle would not say that the new testament is more excellent, and that it itself has more excellent promises, Hebr. VIII, 6. Therefore, in the Old Testament, spiritual and eternal goods are not promised. Resp. 1) Why the new testament is said to be more excellent, see above quest. XXI. prob. k. 2) The N.T. has more excellent promises, not materially, on account of the things contained, or by reason of the good promised, but formally, or by reason of the manner of promising; and indeed a) by reason of the required condition. For in the Old Testament there are promises of eternal life that are conditional, or suspended upon the condition of the perfect fulfillment of the law; but the promises of the new testament are gratuitous, offering to those who believe in Christ the remission of sins and eternal life freely. b) By reason of clarity. For the promises of the new testament are clearer and more open: the promises of the old testament concerning eternal life are wrapped in shadows and types. c) By reason of efficacy. The legal covenant promises eternal life to those who exactly fulfill the law, but it does not supply the strength to fulfill the law; but the evangelical covenant promises eternal life to those who believe in Christ and confers the strength to believe.

II. Whatever covenant does not justify man, but is only ἐπεισαγωγὴ, an introduction of a better hope, that does not promise spiritual goods. But the legal covenant &c.. Therefore. The minor is proved from Hebr. VII, 19. The law made nothing perfect (perfectly justified): But the superinduction of a better hope, by which we draw near to God. Resp. The better hope is the hope of the gospel, founded in Christ. It is called a better hope, however, not because of the things promised, but because of the reason and the way of arriving at the things promised. The law creates a hope of eternal life, but under a condition impossible for us: whence it is also called weak and useless to us by the Apostle. But the hope in Christ is certain, since it is an easy and infallible way in Christ through faith alone to arrive at the things promised.

III. Whatever Christ, exhibited in the flesh, first revealed, that was not promised in the Old Testament: But Christ, exhibited in the flesh, first revealed life and immortality: Therefore. The minor is clear from 2 Tim. I, 10. Christ brought life and incorruption to light through the gospel. Resp. Distinguish between the promise of eternal life, and its more abundant manifestation. Christ brought life and immortality to light through the gospel; not as if it had not been promised to, or known by, the faithful fathers of the old testament; but for two other reasons, one of which is the clarity of the manifestation, the other the breadth of the notification. In the times of the Old Testament, eternal life was promised, but less clearly, and it was known only to the Israelite people; but Christ through the gospel manifested the way to eternal life more clearly, with the shadows of the figures removed, and notified it to the whole world.

the whole world. S I G H.

Prostrate at the feet of thy mercy, O eternal God, most clement Father, I give thee thanks as great as I can possibly conceive in my mind, for thy revealed gospel concerning the conferring of eternal salvation upon us, on account of the merits of Christ.

This word of grace teaches me, trembling, in comparison with eternal salvation, on account of the merits of Christ. This word of grace teaches me, trembling, in comparison with myself and with the divine precepts, and by no means ignorant of my imperfection, to flee for refuge into the bosom of Christ, and under his goodness, as under a most firm shield, to hide safely from the punishments which the law threatens.

This gospel of peace confirms that Christ, for us who rely on him with certain faith, has produced righteousness by his obedience, rest for his labors, solace for his torments, and finally life by his death. Therefore, to me, no treasure is more precious than the gospel of Christ, no food sweeter, no medicine more wholesome, no light more serene. For by this light, the way is shown clearly to those tending toward the heavenly fatherland: by this medicine, the wounds of the conscience are healed: by this food, those hungering for righteousness are refreshed: by this treasure, the poor in spirit are enriched. Store up, O Holy Spirit, this treasure in my soul, so that, having spurned and trampled upon the riches of this age, I may uniquely desire, seek, find, and possess heavenly goods. And you, O my soul, grasp Jesus, the author and defender of your salvation, with true faith; hold him once grasped, and once held, cherish him with holy thoughts, pious prayers, and actions worthy of the gospel.

Latin:

Deus in veteri testamento promisit quidem bona spiritualia & æterna, sed sub conditione perfectæ obedientiæ.

Obs. I. Per vetus testamentum intelligimus fœdus legale a Deo cum Israëlitis initum; nam hoc phrasi scripturæ proprie appellatur, vetus testamentum, & nouo testamento e diametro opponitur, Ier. XXX, 31. seq. Hebr. VIII, 8. Gal. IV, 24. 2 Cor. III, 6.

Obs. II. Fœdus gratiæ, quod Deus a primo lapsus tempore cum Adamo, Abrahamo & reliquis patribus pepigit, a scriptoribus quidem ecclesiasticis interdum dicitur vetus testamentum, ex Gal. III, 17. accurate autem loquendo pertinet ad nouum testamentum. Distinguendum autem est inter nouum testamentum inchoatum, & consummatum. Deus hominibus lapsis promittendo Messiam redemtorem, N. T. inchoauit; sed mittendo filium suum in carnem, consummauit; vi fœderis gratiæ (quod etiam euangelium appellatur). Patres ante Christum iustificatos & saluatos esse, supra, quæst. V. ostendimus; in præsenti nobis sermo est de veteri testamento proprie dicto, siue fœdere legali.

Prob. 1) Ex Leu. XVIII, 15. Obseruabitis statuta mea, & iudicia mea, quæ si fecerit homo, viuet per ea; quia ego sum Iehouah. Conf. Ezech. XX, 11. Hanc promissionem legem non respicere tantum vitam temporalem, sed etiam æternam, patet a) ex interpretatione indubitata Christi, Matth. XIX, 17. Luc. X, 28. b) Ex declaratione apostolica, Rom. X, 5. Moses describit iustitiam, quæ ex lege, quod qui facit illa homo, victurus fit per illa. Conf. Gal. III, 12. vbi Apostolus ex oppositione promissionis euangelicæ & legalis docet, etiam in lege vitam æternam promissam esse, sed sub conditione implendæ legis. promissam esse, sed sub conditione implendæ legis. 2) Ex

2) Ex Lev. XXVI, 3. 11. 12. Si in statutis meis ambulaveritis, & praecepta mea observaveritis, feceritisque ea: --- in primis dabo habitaculum meum in medio vestri, nec fastidiet anima mea vos; sed ambulabo in medio vestri, eroque vobis in Deum: Vos autem eritis mihi in populum. Quam promissionem legalem de bonis spiritualibus intelligendam esse, docet Paulus 2 Cor. VI, 16. Antithesis est Anabaptistarum & Socinianorum, statuentium, in V. T. tantum bona corporalia & temporalia, non autem spiritualia & aeterna esse promissa.

Quorum potiora sunt argumenta: 1. Si in veteri testamento hominibus peccatoribus bona caelestia fuissent promissa, Apostolus non diceret, novum testamentum esse praestantius, atque id ipsum habere promissiones praestantiores, Hebr. VIII, 6. E. in veteri testamento non promittuntur bona spiritualia & aeterna. Resp. 1) Quare novum testamentum dicatur praestantius, vid. supra quaest. XXI. prob. k. 2) N. T. habet promissiones praestantiores, non materialiter, ob res contentas, sive ratione boni promissi, sed formaliter, sive ratione boni promittendi; & quidem a) ratione requisitae conditionis. Nam in veteri testamento habentur promissiones vitae aeternae conditionata, sive suspensae a conditione perfectae legis impletionis; at promissiones novi testamenti sunt gratuitae, credentibus in Christum gratis offerentes remissionem peccatorum & vitam aeternam. b) Ratione claritatis. Nam promissiones novi testamenti sunt clariores & apertiores: promissiones veteris testam. de vita aeterna umbris & typis sunt involutae. c) Ratione efficaciae, Foedus legale exacte implentibus legem pollicetur vitam aeternam, sed non suppeditat vires legem implendi; at foedus evangelicum credentibus in Christum vitam aeternam promittit & vires credendi confert.

II. Quodcunque foedus hominem non justificat, sed est tantum ἐπεισαγωγὴ, introductio melioris spei, illud non promittit bona spiritualia. Atqui foedus legale &c.. E. Minor probatur ex Hebr. VII, 19. Nihil consummavit (perfecte justificavit) lex: Superinductio vero melioris spei, per quam appropinquamus Deo. Resp. Spes melior est spes evangelii, fundata in Christo. Dicitur autem spes melior, non propter res promissas, sed propter rationem & viam, ad res promissas perveniendi. Facit lex spem vitae aeternae, sed sub conditione nobis impossibili: unde & infirma & nobis inutilis ab Apostolo dicta est. At spes in Christo certa est, dum facilis & infallibilis via est in Christo per solam fidem ad res promissas perveniendi.

III. Quidquid Christus, in carne exhibitus, primum revelavit, illud non fuit in veteri testamento promissum: Atqui vitam & immortalitatem Christus, in carne exhibitus, primum revelavit: E. Minor liquet ex 2 Tim. I, 10. Christus in lucem produxit vitam & incorruptionem per evangelium. Resp. Dist. inter promissionem vitae aeternae, & uberiorem eius manifestationem. Christus produxit in lucem vitam & immortalitatem per evangelium; non quali patribus fidelibus vet. testamenti non fuerit promissa, aut cognita; sed duas ob caussas alias, quarum una est manifestationis claritas, altera notificationis latitudo.
