In eodem momento temporis, quo fides datur, etiam recipit; momenta tamen naturæ distinguenda sunt. Prius datur fides, quam vt illa gratiam amplectatur; uterque tamen actus dationis & amplexus eodem quasi momento temporis fit.

Prob. c. 1) Quia vox illa, opus operatum, est barbara; quoniam contra regulam grammaticæ operatum passive accipitur, perinde ac si dicas opus perpetratum, peractum, perfectum.

2) Quia opinio de opere operato in sacramentis N. T. fingit manum dantem, sine accipiente, relatum sine correlato, promissionem sine fide salutarem. 3) Quia

3) Quia hoc commento confunduntur digne & indigne utentes; cum tamen, teste S. Paulo, indigne manducantes sibi manducent iudicium, 1 Cor. XI, 29.


### Quest. XVI: The antithesis is that of the Papists, some of whom establish that the sacraments of the N

The antithesis is that of the Papists, some of whom establish that the sacraments of the N.

T. confer evangelical grace ex opere operato (by the work performed), without a good motion of the user; some concede that in adults prior dispositions are required, to which dispositions they count faith, but that the sacraments of the N. T. confer grace ex opere operantis (by the work of the worker), so that the worker, or the one using the sacraments, is prepared, well-disposed, and instructed with the necessary qualities. The Evangelicals reject the opus operatum for the reasons brought forward above, nor do they admit the opus operantis for obtaining justification and salvation, because we are justified not by works, but by faith.

The arguments of the adversaries are:

I. Whatever justifies and saves by an intrinsic power, divinely implanted, confers justifying and saving grace ex opere operato: But the sacraments, etc. The major is proven: because grace of God is said to be obtained through the sacrament ex opere operato, since it is conferred upon us not because of qualities inherent in us, or prior dispositions, but solely by the power and efficacy implanted in the sacrament.

1) Distinguish between absolute and ordained. The sacraments justify and save not as absolute, but as ordained, and therefore they require a subject that submits itself to the divine order and uses them worthily.

2) Distinguish between the offering and the conferring of divine grace. Divine grace is offered through the sacraments to all, even to those using them unworthily; but it is not conferred upon the unworthy, because they are destitute of faith.

II. Whoever, being destitute of faith, is regenerated through baptism, to them the sacrament of baptism confers evangelical grace ex opere operato: But infants, etc. Therefore. Resp. Distinguish between regenerating grace and justifying grace. The first, regenerating grace, is conferred upon infants through baptism, since they do not place a malicious obstacle to the operation of the Holy Spirit; but while they are being regenerated, they are gifted with faith, so that they may put on the righteousness of Christ and apply it to themselves.

III. That whose legitimate use can exist without faith, faith is not required for its use: But the sacraments, etc. Therefore. The minor is evident: because an adult hypocrite, baptized with water in the name of the Most Holy Trinity, uses the sacrament correctly.

Resp. Distinguish between the formal use of the sacraments and the final, or saving, use. An adult hypocrite is indeed capable of the formal use of the sacraments, but not the final.

IV. Whatever does not give efficacy to a sacrament can work effectively without it. Faith does not give, etc.

Latin:

Antithesis est Pontificiorum, quorum nonnulli statuunt, sacramenta N.

T. conferre gratiam evangelicam ex opere operato, sine bono motu utentis; nonnulli concedunt, in adultis requiri praevias dispositiones, quibus dispositionibus annumerant fidem, sacramenta autem N. T. conferre gratiam ex opere operantis, ut operans, sive utens sacramentis sit praeparatus, beneque dispositus, & necessariis qualitatibus instructus. Evangelici opus operatum reiiciunt ex rationibus supra adductis, nec opus operantis ad consequendam iustitiam & salutem admittunt, propterea, quod non ex operibus, sed ex fide iustificamur.

Argumenta adversariorum sunt:

I. Quidquid vi intrinseca, divinitus indita, iustificat & salvat, illud ex opere operato gratiam iustificantem & salvantem confert: Atqui sacramenta &c. Maior probatur: quia ex opere operato gratia Dei per sacramentum obtingere dicitur, cum ea non propter inhaerentes nobis qualitates, vel praevias dispositiones, sed solum ex vi & efficacia sacramenti indita nobis confertur.

1) Dist. inter absolutam, & ordinatam. Iustificant & salvant sacramenta non ut absoluta, sed ordinata, atque adeo requirunt subiectum, ordini divino se subiiciens atque digne utens.

2) Dist. inter oblationem & collationem gratiae divinae. Omnibus etiam indigne utentibus gratia divina per sacramenta offertur; sed indignis non confertur, quia destituuntur fide.

II. Quicunque fide destituti per baptismum regenerantur, illis sacramentum baptismi ex opere operato gratiam evangelicam confert: Atqui infantes &c. E. Resp. Dist. inter gratiam regenerantem, & iustificantem. Prima gratia regenerans infantibus confertur per baptismum, quoniam operationi Spiritus S. malitiosum non ponunt obicem; sed dum regenerantur, fide donantur, ut eadem iustitiam Christi induant, & sibi applicent.

III. Cuius legitimus usus esse potest sine fide, ad illius usum non requiritur fides: Sed sacramentorum &c. E. Minor constat: quia adultus hypocrita, baptizatus aqua in nomine SS. Trinitatis, recte utitur sacramento.

Resp. Dist. inter usum sacramentorum formalem, & finalem, sive salutarem. Hypocrita adultus est quidem capax usus sacramentorum formalis, sed non finalis.

IV. Quidquid non dat efficaciam sacramento, sine eo potest illud efficaciter operari. Fides non dat &c.


### Quest. XVI: Therefore

Therefore.

Resp. Deny the major, and by arguing with equal reason: Whatever does not give efficacy to a present medicine can heal effectively without it: The mouth of the sick person does not give it: Therefore. Wherefore, in order for the sacrament to exert its efficacy in actu secundo (second act), faith is required as the receiving organ.

V. If faith is required as a receptive medium for the efficacy of the sacrament, the sacrament will not justify or save immediately, but through another medium: But it is absurd that one medium of justification should justify through another medium: Therefore, faith, as a receptive medium, is not required for the efficacy of the sacrament.

Resp. The offering medium is wrongly opposed to the receiving medium. The physician heals through medicine, yet he does not wish the receiving mouth of the sick person to be excluded.

Quest. XVIII. Are the sacraments necessary? The sacraments are necessary by necessity of precept a), and of means b). They are not necessary by that necessity by absolute necessity, but by ordained or conditional necessity c); yet the sacraments of initiation are more necessary than those of confirmation d).

Prob. a. The sacraments are necessary by necessity of precept; because they were instituted by God; and their external symbols were determined by an express divine mandate. See above, quest.

IV. Prob. b. The sacraments are necessary by necessity of means; for the reason that they are means of salvation, offering, conferring, and sealing it. See above, quest.

XV. Prob. c. The sacraments are not absolutely necessary for obtaining salvation; because it is possible that the use of a sacrament may be excluded not by contempt of religion, but by a point of necessity, as AUGUSTINE says, book IV against the Donatists, ch. 22. Whence it is not the lack, but the contempt of the sacraments that damns, as BERNARD judges, ep. 77. For God has not bound His power to the sacraments. Indeed, the grace of God, the merit of Christ, and faith are absolutely and simply necessary for justification and salvation; but when and where the sacraments cannot be had, God, out of mere grace, for Christ's sake, produces justifying faith in an extraordinary way. The converted thief entered paradise, but unbaptized. Catechumens, among whom was the Emperor Valentinian, who died before baptism, were saved. Nor were infants who were not circumcised excluded from salvation in the O.T., Jo. V, 22. Matth. II, 16. 1 Maccab. I, 51.

Prob. d. Concerning the sacrament of initiation, Christ says, Jo. III, 5: Unless one is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God. The same is not said of the sacrament of confirmation. The sacrament of initiation is conferred upon infants and adults, the sacrament of confirmation only upon believing adults.

Latin:

E.

Resp. Neg. maiorem, & pari ratione argumentando: Quidquid non dat efficaciam praesenti medicamento, sine eo potest illud efficaciter mederi: Os aegroti non dat: E. Quamobrem, ut sacramentum actu secundo efficaciam suam exserat, requiritur fides, ut organum recipiens.

V. Si fides ut medium receptivum requiritur ad efficaciam sacramenti, sacramentum non iustificabit, aut salvabit immediate, sed per aliud medium: Sed absurdum est, unum iustificandi medium iustificare per aliud medium: E. fides, ut medium receptivum, non requiritur ad efficaciam sacramenti.

Resp. Medium offerens male opponitur medio recipienti. Medicus sanat per medicamentum, neque tamen os recipiens aegroti vult exclusum.

Quaest. XVIII. Suntne sacramenta necessaria? Necessaria sunt sacramenta necessitate praecepti a), & medii b). Non sunt ea necessitate necessaria necessitate absoluta, sed ordinata, sive conditionata c); magis tamen necessaria sunt sacramenta initiationis, quam confirmationis d).

Prob. a. Necessaria sunt sacramenta necessitate præcepti; quia a Deo instituta; & eorum symbola externa, mandato diuino expresso determinata sunt. Vid. supra, quæst.

IV. Prob. b. Necessitate medii necessaria sunt sacramenta; ideo, quod sunt media salutis offerentia, conferentia & obsignantia. Vid. supra, quæst.

XV. Prob. c. Sacramenta non sunt absolute necessaria ad obtinendam salutem; quia fieri potest, vt vsum sacramenti non contemptus religionis, sed articulus necessitatis excludat, dicente AVGVSTINO, libr. IV. contra Donatist. c. 22. Vnde non defectus, sed contemptus sacramentorum damnat, censente BERNHARDO ep. 77. Neque enim Deus suam potentiam sacramentis alligauit. Gratia quidem Dei, meritum Christi & fides absolute & simpliciter necessaria sunt ad iustificationem & salutem; sed quando & vbi sacramenta haberi nequeunt, Deus ex mera gratia, propter Christum, modo extraordinario fidem iustificantem producit. Ingressus est paradisum latro conuersus, sed ἀβάπτισος. Catechumeni, quos inter fuit imperator Valentinianus, ante baptismum defuncti, sunt saluati. Neque in V. T. salute exclusi sunt infantes non circumcisi, Io. V, 22. Matth. II, 16. 1 Maccab. I, 51.

Prob. d. De sacramento initiationis inquit Christus, Io. III, 5. Nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua & Spiritu, non potest introire in regnum Dei. De sacramento confirmationis idem non dicitur. Sacramentum initiationis confertur infantibus & adultis, sacramentum confirmationis tantum adultis credentibus.


### Quest. XVI: Quest. XIX. How many kinds of sacraments are there?

Quest. XIX. How many kinds of sacraments are there?

The sacraments are twofold; some are of the Old, others of the New Testament. The former are those which, instituted before the coming of Christ, shadowed forth Him who was to be incarnated and slain through external elements: The latter are those which testify that Christ has been manifested in the flesh, has suffered and died, and exhibit Him as really present.

Obs. I. The sacraments of both testaments agree: 1) in author; for all sacraments were instituted by God: 2) in common matter; for all sacraments consist of an earthly thing, which is an external, corporeal, visible, and tangible element, and a heavenly thing, from which, as a cause, the effect of the sacrament flows: 3) in generic form; which is the action, undertaken according to the word of institution: 4) in final cause; which is in both cases the offering, conferring, and sealing of evangelical grace: 5) in identity of application; which is done through faith, as an ὄργανον ληπτικόν, or receptive medium.

Obs. II. The sacraments of the Old and New Testament differ: 1) in duration. The sacraments of the O.T. were eventually to be abrogated, to last μέχρι καιρῦ διορθώσεως, until the time of correction, Hebr. IX, 20. The sacraments of the N.T. will have the same end as the world. 2) in extension of places and objects. The sacraments of the O.T. pertained to the Israelites within the Jewish boundaries, Gen. XVII, 7. Exod. XII, 2. But the sacraments of the N.T. are catholic, common to all nations, Matth. XXVIII, 19. 1 Cor. XI, 16. 3) in proper matter and form, which is one thing in the sacraments of the O.T. and another in the sacraments of the N.T. 4) in the manner of exhibiting the heavenly thing. For the ancient sacraments shadowed forth Christ the God-man, and exhibited Him as present only morally, Jo. VIII, 6. Apoc. XIII, 8. But our sacraments present and exhibit Christ in the very substance of the flesh assumed. AUGUSTINE says excellently in Ps. LXXIII, The sacraments of the O.T. were announcements of Christ who was to come: but the sacraments of the N.T. are announcements of Christ, exhibited in the flesh. Nor does our D. DANNHAV. speak badly in his Hodof. p. 1030. In the O.T. there was a typical lamb: In the N.T. the God-man. There He lay hidden in a shadow, here He presented Himself in the body, Col. II, 17. Hebr. X, 1. There was a sign without the presence of the body, here a sign of the body being offered.

Latin:

Quæst. XIX. Quotuplicia sunt sacramenta?

Sacramenta sunt duplicia, alia sunt veteris, alia noui testamenti. Illa sunt, quæ ante aduentum Christi instituta, eumdem per externa elementa incarnandum, & occidendum adumbrarunt: Hæc sunt, quæ testantur, Christum in carne esse manifestatum, passum & mortuum, eumdemque realiter præsentem exhibent.

Obs. I. Sacramenta vtriusque testamenti conueniunt: 1) auctore; omnia enim sacramenta a Deo sunt instituta: 2) materia communi; omnia quippe sacramenta constant re terrestri, quæ est elementum externum, corporeum, visibile & tractabile, & cælesti, a qua, vt causa, fluit effectus sacramenti: 3) forma generica; quæ est actio, secundum verbum institutionis suscepta: 4) causa finali; quæ est vtrobique oblatio, collatio & obsignatio gratiæ euangelicæ: 5) identitate applicationis; quæ fit per fidem, tanquam ὄργανον ληπτικόν, seu medium receptiuum.

Obs. II. Differunt sacramenta veteris & noui testamenti: 1) duratione. Sacramenta V. T. fuerunt tandem abroganda, duratura μέχρι καιρῦ διορθώσεως, vsque ad tempus correctionis, Hebr. IX, 20. Sacramenta N. T. eumdem cum mundo terminum habebunt. 2) extensione locorum & obiectorum. Sacramenta V. T. intra pomæria Iudaica ad Israëlitas pertinuerunt, Gen. XVII, 7. Exod. XII, 2. Sacramenta autem N. T. sunt catholica, omnibus nationibus communia, Matth. XXVIII, 19. 1 Cor. XI, 16. 3) materia & forma propria, quæ alia est in sacramentis V. T. alia in sacramentis N. T. 4) modo exhibendi rem cælestem. Nam sacramenta prisca Christum θεάνθρωπον adumbrarunt, & non nisi moraliter præsentem exhibuerunt, Io. VIII, 6. Apoc. XIII, 8. Nostra vero sacramenta Christum ipsa carnis assumptæ substantia præsentem sistunt & exhibent. Præclare inquit AVGVSTINVS in Ps. LXXIII, Sacramenta V. T. fuerunt prænuntiatua Christi venturi: sacramenta vero N. T. sunt annuntiatua Christi, in carne exhibiti. Nec male noster D. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 1030. In V. T. fuit agnus typicus: In N. T. θεάνθρωπος. Latuit illic in vmbraculo, hic in corpore se stitit Col. II, 17. Hebr. X, 1. Fuit ibi signum sine corporis præsentia, hic signum corporis προσφερόμενον.


### On Circumcision, the Former Sacrament of the O

Q. XX. What is circumcision? Circumcision is a sacrament of the O. T., by which God, ordinarily through a minister of the church, conferred and sealed federal grace upon a male human being, being brought into the Jewish church, by the bloody resection of the foreskin, prefiguring the future shedding of the blood of the Messiah in the assumed flesh, and with the word of institution accompanying it, to the praise of divine goodness and the salvation of the circumcised man.

Obj. I. Circumcision is named from cutting around; because the foreskin, which is the skin covering the extremity of the genital member, was cut off.

Obj. II. The name of circumcision is taken in three ways: a) metonymically, b) metaphorically, c) properly.

Metonymically it denotes the circumcised people, Rom. XV, 8. Metaphorically it signifies the internal circumcision of the heart, Rom. II, 29. Deut. X, 16. Properly it is taken either partially, for the external amputation of the skin alone, Rom. II, 28, or wholly, for the whole act of sacramental circumcision, consisting of the external sign, typically representing the heavenly thing, and the word of command and promise, concerning which the classic passage and proper seat of this sacrament is to be seen, Gen. XVII, 7. seqq.

Quest. XXI. Who instituted the sacrament of circumcision? The triune God, the author of the federal grace of salvation, instituted the sacrament of circumcision.

Proof. From Gen. XVII, where God commanded circumcision, v. 10, 11, 12, annexed a promise, v. 7, prescribed the form by the word of institution, v. 11, and seqq., and threatened destruction to those despising this sacrament, v. 14.

Quest. XXII. By whose ministry was circumcision performed? The ministerial cause of circumcision was first Abraham: then the succeeding patriarchs a): afterwards, the Mosaic polity having been established, the Levitical priests b): Extraordinarily, however, and in case of necessity, even private members of the church performed the rite of circumcision c).

Proof. a. From Gen. XVII, 7, and seqq., where we read that God made a covenant with Abraham, of which circumcision was to be the sign, v. 11. Whence also Abraham received the command to circumcise, v. 10, and executed it, v. 25. Abraham, however, is to be viewed not precisely as a head of a family, but as a minister of sacred things in the church of his house. Abraham himself, however, seems not to have circumcised himself, but to have been circumcised by Eliezer, the steward of his house and vicar of sacred things. Thus also the succeeding patriarchs are to be considered not so much as heads of families, but as ministers of sacred things and teachers of the church.

Proof. b. There does not indeed exist an express law which clearly binds the office of circumcision to the priestly order: Nevertheless, since the divine worship, accustomed to be performed by the patriarchs, was committed to the Levitical priests once the Mosaic polity was established, it is not difficult to conclude that the rite circumcision belonged to the presbyters and Levites, distributed throughout all the Israelite tribes. Certainly, Matthias circumcised the children of the presbyters who had defected to ethnic superstitions, 1 Macc. II, 46. It is conjectured, however, from the example of Abraham, Gen. XVII, 23, and from the circumcision of John, Luke I, 59, that the domestics of any family, as far as it was permitted, provided assistance to the public minister.

Proof c: Joshua, the prince of the Israelite people, by a special divine mandate, circumcised the sons of Israel on the hill of Araloth, Josh. V, 3. Zipporah circumcised her son, Exod. IV, 29. Israelite women, during the time of the Antiochene persecution, circumcised infants, 1 Macc. I, 63; 2 Macc. VI, 10.

Latin:

T. SACRAMENTO. Quaest. XX. Quid est circumcisio? Circumcisio est sacramentum V. T. prius, quo Deus, ordinarie per ecclesiae ministrum, homini masculo, ecclesiae iudaicae inferendo, praeputii cruenta resectione, futuram sanguinis Messiae in assumta carne effusionem praefigurante, atque verbo institutionis accedente, gratiam foederalem contulit et obsignauit, ad diuinae bonitatis laudem, et hominis circumcisi salutem.

Obi. I. Circumcisio dicitur a circumcidendo; quia praeputium, quod est pellicula extremitatem membri genitalis tegens, praecidebatur.

Obi. II. Nomen circumcisionis sumitur trifariam: a) metonymice, b) metaphorice c) proprie.

Metonymice notat populum circumcisum, Rom. XV, 8. Metaphorice significat internam cordis circumcisionem, Rom. II, 29. Deut. X, 16. Proprie sumitur vel μερικῶς, siue partialiter, pro sola externa pelliculae amputatione, Rom. II, 28, vel ὅλως, pro toto actu sacramentalis circumcisionis, constante ex signo externo, rem coelestem typice repraesentante, atque verbo mandati et promissi, de quo videndus locus classicus et propria sedes huius sacramenti, Gen XVII, 7. seqq.

Quaest. XXI. Quis instituit sacramentum circumcisionis? Sacramentum circumcisionis instituit Deus triunus, gratiae foederalis salutis auctor.

Prob. Ex Gen. XVII. vbi Deus circumcisionem mandauit, v. 10. 11. 12. promissionem annexuit, v. 7. formam verbo institutionis praescripsit, v. 11. et seqq. fastidientibus hoc sacramentum exitium interminatus est, v. 14.

Quaest. XXII. Cuius ministerio circumcisio peracta est? Causa ministerialis circumcisionis primum fuit Abraham: deinde patriarchae succedentes a): postea, constituta politia Mosaica, sacerdotes Leuitici b): Extraordinarie vero, et in casu necessitatis, etiam priuata ecclesiae membra circumcisionis ritum peregerunt c).

Prob. a. Ex Gen. XVII, 7. et seqq. vbi legimus, Deum cum Abrahamo pepigisse foedus, cuius signum esse debebat circumcisio, v. 11. Vnde et Abrahamus mandatum circumcidendi accepit, v. 10. et exsecutus est, v. 25. Spectandus autem est Abraham non praecise vt paterfamilias, sed vt minister sacrorum in ecclesia domus suae. Ipse tamen Abraham non seipsum circumcidisse, sed ab Eliefere, praefecto domus suae et sacrorum vicario, circumcisus esse videtur. Sic et patriarchae succedentes non tam vt capita familiarum, quam vt ministri sacrorum ac doctores ecclesiae considerandi sunt.

Prob. b. Non exstat quidem expressa lex, quae diserte alliget munus circumcisionis ordini sacerdotali: Attamen quoniam constituta politia Mosaica cultus diuinus, a patriarchis obiri solitus, commissus est sacerdotibus Leuiticis, haud difficulter colligitur, ritum circumcisionis fuisse penes sacerdotes & Levitas, per omnes tribus Israeliticas distributos. Certe Matthias sacerdotes liberos eorum, qui ad ethnicas superstitiones defecerant, circumcidit, 1 Macc. II, 46. domesticos autem cuiuslibet familiæ, quantum licitum fuit, suppetias ministro publico tulisse, conicitur ex Abrahami exemplo, Gen. XVII, 23. & ex circumcisione Ioannis, Io. I, 59.

Prob. c. Iosua, princeps populi Israelitici, ex speciali mandato divino filios Israël in colle Arolath circumcidit, Ios. V, 3. Zippora circumcidit filium suum, Exod. IV, 29. Fœminæ Israeliticæ, tempore persecutionis Antiochenæ, infantes circumciderunt, 1 Macc. I, 63. 2 Macc. VI, 10.


### Q. XXIII. With what instrument was circumcision performed?

The instrument of circumcision was a sharp knife, made of stone, or even of iron, or steel.

Proof: By the phrase of Scripture, the instrument of circumcision is called a rock, Exod. IV, 25, and a knife of rocks, Josh. V, 3, i.e., stony or made of stone. Today, the Jews use a very sharp steel knife.

Latin:

Instrumentum circumcisionis fuit culter acutus, petrinus, vel etiam ferreus, aut chalybeus.

Prob. Phrasi scripturæ instrumentum circumcisionis dicitur petra, Exod. IV, 25. & culter petrarum, Ios. V, 3. i. e. petrinus, vel lapideus. Hodie Iudæi utuntur cultro chalybeo acutissimo.


### Q. XXIV. Who were circumcised?

Israelite males were circumcised, as well as the domestics of Israelites a), and proselytes b): and infants, indeed, when they were in their eighth day, were to be initiated into the sacred rites of the Jews c). Proof a: From Gen. XVII, 12. When he is a son of eight days, every male among you shall be circumcised throughout your generations (i.e., every son born of you), one born in the house (a home-born slave, or a servant born in the house) and one bought with money (who became a servant not by right of birth, but by right of purchase) of any son of a foreigner, who is not of your seed, i.e., a servant who has come into your power, even if he was not bought from an Israelite people, but from a foreigner. Nevertheless, servants were not compelled to circumcision, but were invited, and if they refused to be circumcised, they were dismissed or sold again.

Proof b: From Exod. XII, 48. And if a stranger shall sojourn with you, and will keep the passover to Jehovah, let every male of his be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it; and he shall be as one that is born in the land: but no uncircumcised person shall eat thereof. From which it appears that no one was admitted to the Israelite sacred rites, especially to the eating of the paschal lamb, unless he had been consecrated by the sacrament of circumcision. Proof c: The time of administration for boys was the eighth day from birth, Gen. XVII, 12. The circumcision of infants was delayed until the eighth day so that the tender bodies of the newborn might be spared; yet it was not delayed further, so that they might be received into the covenant of grace as soon as possible, to the great consolation of the parents: although the act of circumcision could be deferred on account of dangerous illness or journeys; just as God allowed circumcision to be omitted for 40 years, when the Israelite people were making their journey into the land of Canaan, Josh. V, 5, 6, 7.

Latin:

Circumcidebantur masculi Israelitici, & Israeliticarum domestici a), ac proselyti b): & infantes quidem, cum octavum agerent diem, sacris Iudæorum initiandi erant c). Prob. a. Ex Gen. XVII, 12. Quum filius fuerit octo dierum, circumcidetur vobis omnis masculus in generationes vestras (i e. omnis filius, a vobis genitus), natus domus (verna, seu servus in domo natus) & emtus argento (qui non natiuitatis, sed emtionis iure, servus factus) de omni filio alienigenæ, qui non de semine tuo, i. e. servus, qui in potestatem tuam venerit, licet non a populo Israelitico, sed ab alienigena emtus fuerit. Neque tamen servi cogebantur ad circumcisionem, sed invitabantur, & si recusarent circumcidi, dimittebantur, aut iterum vendebantur.

Prob. b. Ex Exod. XII, 48. Quodsi peregrinabitur tecum peregrinus, & voluerit facere pascha Iehouæ, circumcidetur etiam masculus, & tunc accedet ad faciendum illud, eritque sicut incola terræ: sed ullus præputiatus non comedet de eo. Ex quo apparet, neminem admissum esse ad sacra Israelitica, in primis ad esum agni paschalis, nisi circumcisionis sacramento consecratus esset. Prob. c. Tempus administrationis in pueris fuit dies a natiuitate octavus, Gen. XVII, 12. Vsque ad octavum diem dilata fuit circumcisio infantum, vt tenellis corporibus recens natorum consuleretur; neque tamen vlterius differebatur, vt in fœdus gratiæ quam primum reciperentur, ingenti parentum solatio: quamuis propter morbum periculosum atque itinera differri potuerit actus circumcisionis; sicut passus est Deus circumcisionem omitti per annos 40., cum populus Israeliticus iter faceret in terram Canaan, Ios. V, 5. 6. 7.


### Q. XXV. Were females also circumcised?

The females of the Israelites were indeed not circumcised, yet they were participants and certain of the federal grace, not by an incised mark, but by λογισμῷ, or divine imputation.

Proof. Israelite women, born of circumcised fathers, were married to circumcised men at the appropriate time, and were destined for the bearing of sons who were to be circumcised. For which reason, Israelite women were indeed excluded from the sign of the covenant, but not from the grace of the covenant initiated with Abraham. For God promises that He will be the God of Abraham and of his seed, Gen. 17:7, under which seed women are certainly included, 1 Pet. 3:6. Whence it was also permitted for them to celebrate the Passover, which otherwise was not lawful for the uncircumcised.

Q.

XXVI. What was the matter of circumcision? The matter of circumcision, the earthly element, was the foreskin . The matter, or the heavenly thing, was the Messiah to be born from the seed of Abraham, to be cut off with the shedding of blood, and to be cast away like the amputated foreskin .

Proof a. From Gen. 17:11: "You shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin." Now the foreskin is the little skin by which the extreme part of the virile member, or the glans, is covered. ARISTOTLE calls it ἀκροποσθίαν, as if to say ἄκρον τῆς πόσθης, i.e., the extreme skin of the genital member. Paul, with a slightly inflected word, calls it ἀκροβυστίαν, Rom. 2:25. In Hebrew it is called עָרְלָה, by which word, according to Rabbi DAVID KIMCHI, every superfluous and heavy thing is signified, which it is right to remove and cast away. THOMAS, P. III, qu. 70, art. 3, brings forward three causes for why circumcision was performed on the genital member: 1) Because it was a sign of the faith by which Abraham believed that Christ would be born from his seed: 2) Because it was a remedy for original sin, which is transmitted through the act of generation: 3) Because it was ordained for the diminution of carnal concupiscence, which thrives especially in those members.

Proof b. The heavenly thing of circumcision was Christ, arising from the seed of Abraham, and to be cut off with the shedding of blood: concerning whose excision, see Dan. 9:26, Isa. 53:8, where the same words are used concerning Christ as are used concerning circumcision. Now Christ was comprehended with the earthly matter, as a divine person really, as one to be incarnate typically and relatively, insofar as the amputated foreskin, as a type, had a relation to Christ the antitype, from whom the efficacy of circumcision flows. For in Christ we are heaped with every blessing, Eph. 1:3.

Q.

XXVII. What was the form of circumcision? The form of circumcision is the bloody and painful amputation of the foreskin joined with the word of institution applied .

Proof. From Gen. 17:11, where the word of institution is held, which was preceded by the word of promise, v. 7. There also undoubtedly accompanied it the word of ordination, or application, and invocation, which exists at least as to its traces among the Rabbis, and is recounted by D. SEB. SCHMID, in tract. de circumcif. p. 423: "Blessed art Thou, O Lord our God, King of the world, who hast sanctified us with Thy precepts, and hast commanded us that we initiate him into the covenant of Abraham, our father."

Q.

The union of the earthly and heavenly thing in the sacrament of circumcision? The union of the earthly and heavenly thing in the act of circumcision, according to the nature of the O.T., was σχετική, relative and typical a), insofar as the amputated foreskin prefigured the Messiah to be incarnate, and to be sprinkled with His own blood in most bitter passion, whom it did not exhibit substantially present according to both natures, but stood morally present b).

Prob. a. Just as the sacraments of the Old Testament were foretelling of the Messiah to come, not announcing of the Messiah exhibited: So the union of the earthly and heavenly thing in the sacrament of circumcision was not exhibitive of the blood of Christ substantially present, but typical and prefigurative of the blood of Christ, to be shed at a time divinely appointed.

Prob. b. In the sacrament of circumcision, federal grace and the remission of sins were offered and effectively conferred, Gen. XVII, 7. But Christ is the sole meritorious cause of grace and the remission of sins, Acts X, 43. Therefore, although Christ was not present in circumcision according to the substance of the flesh to be assumed, and the blood to be shed at some time; yet He was present, as to His person and according to the efficacy of the merit to be performed by Him, which avails backward and forward, and was profitable before it existed. For this is common to all meritorious causes, that as the occasion arises, even before they exist, they can exert their causal power by the value of the foreknown merit, and move the will of the efficient cause to act. Therefore, the fruit of circumcision is to be derived from nowhere else than from the union of the earthly thing with the heavenly, i.e., the blood of Christ foreknown and foretold.

Latin:

Fœmellæ Israelitarum non quidem circumcisæ, gratiæ tamen fœderalis participes certæque fuerunt, non ex inciso stigmate, sed ex λογισμῷ, sive imputatione diuina.

Prob. Foeminae Israelitarum, ex patribus circumcisis natae cum circumcisis opportuno tempore maritatae, & ad pariendum filios circumcidendos destinatae fuerunt. Quam ob rem foeminae Israeliticae quidem a signo foederis, non autem a gratia foederis, cum Abrahamo initi, exclusae fuerunt. Promittit enim Deus, se futurum Deum Abrahami & seminis eius, Gen. XVII, 7. sub quo semine-vtique & feminae comprehenduntur, 1 Petr. III, 6. Vnde & pascha illis celebrare licuit, quod alias incircumcisis integrum non erat.

Quaest. XXVI. Quae fuit materia circumcisionis?

Circumcisionis materia terrestris atque elementum externum erat praeputium . Materia, siue res caelestis erat Messias ex semine Abrahami nascendus, cum sanguinis effusione exscindendus, & instar praeputii amputati abiiciendus .

Prob. a. Ex Gen. XVII, 11. Circumcidetis carnem praeputii vestri. Est autem praeputium cuticula, qua extrema membri virilis pars, siue glans obtegitur. ARISTOTELES vocat ἀκροποσθίαν, quasi ἄκρον τῆς πόσθης, i. e. pelliculam extremam membri genitalis. Paullus inflexa nonnihil voce appellat ἀκροβυστίαν, Rom. II, 25. Hebraeis dicitur עָרְלָה, qua voce, secundum Rabbi DAVID KIMCHI, significatur omnis res superflua & grauis, quam amouere & abiicere par est. Caussas, ob quas circumcisio in membro genitali facta fit, tres adducit THOMAS P. III. qu. 70. art. 3. Fiebat circumcisio in membro generationis propterea: 1) Quia erat signum fidei, qua Abraham credidit, Christum ex semine suo nasciturum: 2) Quia erat in remedium peccati originalis, quod per actum generationis traducitur: 3) Quia ordinabatur ad diminutionem carnalis concupiscentiae, quae praecipue in membris illis viget.

Prob. b. Circumcisionis res caelestis fuit Christus, e semine Abrahami oriundus, & cum sanguinis effusione excidendus: De cuius excisione, vid. Dan. IX, 26. Es. LIII, 8. vbi de Christo eadem habentur verba, quae de circumcisione adhibentur. Fuit autem Christus cum materia terrena compraefens, vt persona diuina realiter, vt incarnandus typice & relatiue, in quantum praeputium amputatum, velut typus, respectum habuit ad Christum antitypum, a quo efficacia circumcisionis fluit. Nam in Christo cumulamur omni benedictione, Eph. I, 3.

Quaest. XXVII. Quae fuit forma circumcisionis?

Forma circumcisionis est cruenta & dolorosa praeputii amputatio cum verbo institutionis applicato coniuncta .

Prob. Ex Gen. XVII, 11. vbi habetur verbum institutionis, cui praecessit verbum promissionis, v. 7. Accessit etiam procul dubio verbum ordinationis, siue applicationis, & invocationis, quod saltim quoad vestigia apud Rabbinos exstat, & recensetur a D. SEB. SCHMID, in tract. de circumcis. p. 423. Benedictus tu, Domine Deus noster, Rex mundi, qui sanctificasti nos praeceptis tuis, & praecepisti, vt initiemus eum foederi Abrahami, patris nostri.

Quaest. XXVIII. Qualis fuit

vnio rei terrestris & caelestis in sacramento circumcisionis? Vnio rei terrestris & caelestis in actu circumcisionis, iuxta naturam V. T. fuit, σχετική, relatiua & typica a), quatenus praeputium amputatum praefigurauit Messiam incarnandum, & in acerbissima passione sanguine suo conspergendum, quem non exhibuit secundum vtramque naturam substantialiter praesentem, sed stitit praesentem moraliter b).

Prob. a. Sicut sacramenta V. T. fuerunt praenuntiativa Messiae venturi, non annuntiativa Messiae exhibiti: Ita unio rei terrestris & coelestis in sacramento circumcisionis non fuit exhibitiva sanguinis Christi substantialiter praesentis, sed typica & praefigurativa sanguinis Christi, divinitus statuto tempore effundendi.

Prob. b. In sacramento circumcisionis oblata & efficaciter collata fuit gratia foederalis & remissio peccatorum, Gen. XVII, 7. At Christus est unica causa meritoria gratiae & remissionis peccatorum, Act. X, 43. Ergo licet Christus in circumcisione non fuerit praesens secundum substantiam carnis assumendae, & sanguinis aliquando effundendi; adfuit tamen, quoad personam & secundum efficaciam praestandi a se meriti, quod retrorsum & antrorsum valet, atque profuit, antequam fuit. Id enim commune est omnibus causis meritoriis, vt pro re nata etiam prius, quam exsistant, valore meriti praecogniti suam causandi vim exerere, & voluntatem causae efficientis ad agendum mouere possunt. Idcirco fructus circumcisionis non aliunde deriuandus est, quam ex vnione rei terrestris cum coelesti, i. e. sanguine Christi praecognito & praenuntiato.


### Q. XXIX. What is the end of circumcision?

The primary end of circumcision is either organic, according to which circumcision was an effective medium of offering and conferring federal grace a); or sigillary, according to which circumcision is a seal of the righteousness of faith b). The intermediate ends are, the segregation of the Israelites from other peoples c), an admonition concerning original sin d), and spiritual circumcision e). Prob. a. From Gen. XVII, 7. I will establish my covenant between me and thee, and between thy seed after thee, in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be a God unto thee, and to thy seed after thee. From which words we gather that circumcision was a federal act, uniting to God and regenerative. For to be a God to someone signifies that God is the most merciful father of that man. But where there is fatherhood, there cannot be absent regeneration and the remission of sins, Jer. XXXI, 33. Cf. II, 23.

Prob. b. From Rom. IV, 11. Abraham received the sign of circumcision, a seal of the righteousness of faith.

Prob. c. From Gal. II, 7. When they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the circumcision was unto Peter. St. Paul distinguishes the Gentiles from the Jews, marking the former with the name of uncircumcision, the latter with that of circumcision. He placed, however, the abstract for the concrete; uncircumcision for the uncircumcised, circumcision for the circumcised.

Prob. d. Circumcision was performed on the genital member, because original sin is propagated through carnal generation, Ps. LI, 7. Prob. e. The circumcised Jews are admonished of internal circumcision, Jer. IV, 4. Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart, O men of Judah, and inhabitants of Jerusalem, i.e., it does not suffice that the foreskin of the flesh be removed from us, cut off also the foreskin of the heart, for the most humble obedience to be rendered to God.

Latin:

Finis primarius circumcisionis est vel organicus, secundum quem circumcisio fuit efficax medium offerendae & conferendae gratiae foederalis a); vel sigillaris, secundum quem circumcisio est sigillum iustitiae fidei b). Fines intermedii sunt, segregatio Israelitarum ab aliis populis c), admonitio de peccato originis d), & circumcisio spiritualis e). Prob. a. Ex Gen. XVII, 7. Erigam foedus meum inter me & inter te, & inter semen tuum post te, in generationes ipsorum, in foedus aeternum, vt sim tibi in Deum, & semini tuo post te. E quibus verbis colligimus, circumcisionem fuisse actum foederalem, Deo vnitivum & regenerativum. Nam esse alicui in Deum, significat, Deum hominis esse patrem clementissimum. Sed vbi est paternitas, ibi non potest abesse regeneratio & peccatorum remissio, Ier. XXI, 33. Cf. II, 23.

Prob. b. Ex Rom. IV, 11. Abraham accepit signum circumcisionis, sigillum iustitiae fidei.

Prob. c. Ex Gal. II, 7. Cum viderent, quod concreditum mihi esset euangelium praeputii, sicut Petro circumcisionis. S. Paullus gentiles a Iudaeis discernit, illos praeputii, hos circumcisionis nomine insigniens. Posuit autem abstractum pro concreto; praeputium pro praeputiatis, circumcisionem pro circumcisis.

Prob. d. Facta est circumcisio in membro genitali, quia peccatum originis per carnalem generationem propagatur, Ps. LI, 7. Prob. e. Circumcisi Iudaei admonentur circumcisionis internae, Ier. IV, 4. Circumcidite vos Iehovae, & remouete praeputia cordis vestri, o viri Iudae, & habitatores Hierosolymae, q. d. non sufficit, praeputium carnis nobis esse refectum, praecidite etiam praeputium cordis, ad humillimum obsequium Deo praestandum.


### Q. XXX. Was circumcision necessary?

Circumcision was indeed necessary by necessity of precept and means a); yet not by absolute necessity, but ordered and conditional b). Prob. a. From Gen. XVII, 14. The male, whose flesh of his foreskin shall not be circumcised, that soul shall be cut off from his people, because he has made void my covenant. From which words we conclude it is permitted: If neglected circumcision condemned, assumed saved: If those omitting circumcision broke the divine covenant, those receiving it were co-opted into the divine covenant. Circumcision was therefore necessary not only by necessity of precept, because God commanded it; but also by necessity of means, because it was a means of federal grace and eternal salvation to be conferred.

Prob. b. God ordained circumcision, but did not precisely bind His power to this ordinary means: He ordained it, I say, under the condition of possibility, if the infant lived long enough that he could be circumcised on the eighth day. Yet one must not therefore despair of the salvation of infants who died before the eighth day: 1) Because the promise was made to Abraham: I will be thy God, and of thy seed after thee: 2) Because those infants did not transgress the law; for the reason that they ceased to live before the time destined by divine law for circumcision; But where there is no law, there is no transgression, Rom. IV, 15. 3) If all uncircumcised infants had perished, then certainly those infants would have been damned who were cast into the river by Pharaoh before the eighth day; who were born and died in the course of the 40 years in the desert; who were killed by Antiochus before receiving circumcision; who were slaughtered in the vicinity of Bethlehem by the satellites of Herod not yet circumcised . But it would be too cruel to adjudge these to eternal damnation.

Latin:

Necessaria quidem fuit circumcisio necessitate praecepti & medii a); non tamen necessitate absoluta, sed ordinata & conditionata b). Prob. a. Ex Gen. XVII, 14. Masculus, cuius praeputii caro non fuerit circumcisa, exscidetur anima illa de populo suo, quia irritum fecit pactum meum. E quibus verbis concludere licet: Si neglecta circumcisio damnauit, assumpta saluauit: Si intermittentes circumcisionem fregerunt pactum diuinum, eam suscipientes in foedus diuinum cooptati sunt. Fuit itaque circumcisio necessaria non solum necessitate praecepti, quia eam Deus praecepit; sed & necessitate medii, quia fuit medium gratiae foederalis & aeternae salutis conferendae.

Prob. b. Deus circumcisionem ordinauit, sed suam potentiam huic ordinario medio non praecise alligauit: Ordinauit, inquam, illam sub conditione possibilitatis, si infans tamdiu vixerit, vt octauo die posset circumcidi. Neque tamen ideo desperandum est de salute infantum ante octauum diem extinctorum: 1) Quia promissio facta est Abrahamo: Ero Deus tuus, & feminis tui post te: 2) Quia infantes illi legem non transgressi sunt; eo, quod ante tempus lege diuina circumcisioni destinatum viuere desierunt; Sed vbi nulla lex, ibi nulla transgressio, Rom. IV, 15. 3) Si omnes infantes incircumcisi periissent, vtique damnati essent infantes, qui a Pharaone ante octauum diem in profluentem abiecti; qui in deserto 40. annorum decursu nati & denati; qui ab Antiocho ante susceptam circumcisionem occisi; qui in vicinia Bethlehemi a satellitibus Herodis nondum circumcisi obtruncati sunt . At nimis crudele foret, hos aeternae damnationi adiudicare.


### Quæst. XXXI. How long ought circumcision to have lasted?

The term of the duration of circumcision was the time of Christ, manifested in the flesh and affixed to the cross that it is a figure of this.

For the prophet describes the things of the N. T. with the phrases of the O. T. Thus, making mention of the circumcision of the flesh, he designates the antitype by the word of the type, namely baptism, where we are circumcised by putting off the body of the sins of the flesh through the circumcision of Christ, buried together with him through baptism, Col. 2:11. So that the sense of the prophet Ezekiel is: that no one would be a member of the church of Christ unless he had been baptized and reborn, clearly as Christ Jn. 3:5 says concerning the necessity of regenerating baptism: unless one is born again of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of heaven.

III. If God had abrogated circumcision, he would be mutable: but he is not mutable: Therefore. Resp. If God had instituted circumcision for this end, that it might be a perpetual sacrament of the church, and yet nevertheless had abrogated the same, he would certainly be mutable; but it was instituted for a certain time of the pedagogy and pupilage of the Jews, after which it was bound to cease. Therefore, God is not mutable, but is constant in his counsels.

Latin:

Terminus durationis circumcisionis fuit tempus Christi, in carne manifestati & cruci affixi quod illa huius figura fit.

Describit namque propheta phrasibus V. T. res N. T. Ita mentionem faciens circumcisionis carnis, vocabulo typi designat antitypum, nempe baptismum, ubi circumcidimur exuendo corpus peccatorum carnis per circumcisionem Christi, consepulti simul cum illo per baptismum, Col. II, 11. vt sensus sit prophetæ Ezechielis: neminem ecclesiæ Christi membrum fore, nisi baptizatus & renatus fuerit, plane vt Christus Io. III, 5. de necessitate baptismi regenerantis inquit: nisi quis renatus fuerit ex aqua & spiritu, non potest introire regnum cælorum.

III. Si Deus abrogauerit circumcisionem, erit mutabilis: sed non est mutabilis: Ergo. Resp. Si Deus circumcisionem hoc fine instituisset, vt esset perpetuum ecclesiæ sacramentum, & nihilo tamen minus abrogasset eandem, vtique esset mutabilis; sed instituta fuit ad certum tempus pædagogiæ & pupillatus Iudæorum, quo transacto cessare debuit. E. Deus non mutabilis, sed constans est in suis consiliis.


### Of the Paschal Lamb


### Q. XXXII. What is the paschal lamb?

The paschal lamb was a later sacrament of the old testament, by which God, through a whole and yearling lamb, consecrated by the word of institution, slaughtered, roasted, and eaten by the Israelites and legally clean proselytes, prefigured the Messiah, who was to be killed for the sins of the human race, for the sake of exciting and confirming faith in him, and obtaining the remission of sin and of the destructive plague.

Obs. I. Pascha, and the paschal lamb, is said from the Hebrew word פסח, which denotes passing over, passing through, or leaping over, from the passing over of the destroying angel, who on that night, which followed immediately upon the institution of the paschal lamb, struck the firstborn of the Egyptians, but passed over the houses of the Israelites, and spared them, having seen the blood of the paschal lamb on the threshold, Ex. 12:13.

Obs. II. Pascha in biblical usage signifies 1) the paschal lamb, Ex. 12:21, 2 Chron. 35:16, Mk. 14:12, whose antitype is Christ, 1 Cor. 5:7, Christ our passover, sacrificed for us, where Christ is called the passover metaphorically; 2) the paschal feast, together with the sacrifices connected with the paschal lamb, Ex. 34:25, Lev. 23:5; 3) the sacred action by which this sacrament of the old testament was administered, Ex. 12:43.

Latin:

Agnus paschalis fuit sacramentum veteris testamenti posterius, quo Deus per agnum integrum & anniculum, verbo institutionis consecratum, mactatum, assatum, & ab Israëlitis atque proselytis legaliter mundis, manducatum, Messiam, pro peccatis humani generis occidendum, præfigurauit, ad fidem in hunc excitandam & confirmandam, remissionemque peccati & plagæ exitialis impetrandam.

Obs. I. Pascha, & agnus paschalis dicitur a voce Hebræa פסח, quæ notat præteritionem, transitum, aut transultum, a transitione angeli vastatoris, qui nocte illa, proxime institutionem agni paschalis secuta, Ægyptiorum primogenita percussit, Israëlitarum vero domos transiliuit, iisque pepercit, conspecto in limine sanguine agni paschalis, Exod. XII, 13.

Obs. II. Pascha in vsu biblico significat 1) agnum paschalem, Exod. XII, 21. 2 Paral. XXXV, 16. Marc. XIV, 12. cuius antypus est Christus, 1 Cor. V, 7. Pascha nostrum, pro nobis immolatum, est Christus, vbi Christus vocatur pascha metaphorice; 2) festum paschale, vna cum sacrificiis, cum agno paschali connexis, Exod. XXXIV, 25. Leu. XXIII, 5; 3) actionem sacram, qua hoc sacramentum vet. testam. administrabatur, Exod. XII, 43.


### Q. XXXIII. Who instituted the sacrament of the paschal lamb?

God, by his own authority, instituted and ordained the sacramental action concerning the paschal lamb, to be duly handled and eaten.

Prob. We learn that God himself ordained the paschal lamb to be handled and eaten with certain rites from Ex. 12:1 ff., where the proper seat of this doctrine is.

Latin:

Actionem sacramentalem circa agnum paschalem, rite tractandum & manducandum, auctoritate sua instituit & ordinauit Deus.

Prob. Deum ipsum agnum paschalem certis ritibus tractandum comedendumque ordinasse, discimus ex Exod. XII, 1. seqq. vbi propria huius doctrinæ sedes est.


### Q. XXXIV. Who were the ministers of this sacrament?

The ministers for the promulgation of the divine institution of this sacrament were Moses and Aaron . But the ministers of the slaughtering and roasting of the paschal lamb were partly the fathers of families of the Israelite nation , and partly the Levites .

Proof a. From Exod. XII, 21. Where Moses says: "Take for yourselves flocks according to your families, and slaughter the Passover." The people's obedience is added, v. 28. "And the children of Israel went away, and as the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

1) From Exod. XII, 6. "The whole assembly of Israel shall slaughter the lamb between the evenings." Therefore, every head of a household in Egypt, where the Levitical priesthood was not yet ordained, could slaughter the paschal lamb.

2) Deut. XVI, 2. God addresses the entire Israelite people: "You shall slaughter the Pesach to the Lord your God." From this we gather that the right to slaughter and offer the paschal lamb belonged to every head of a household of the Israelite nation not only before, but also after the establishment of the Mosaic polity.

Proof c. 1) From 2 Paral. XXX, 1. The Levites were in charge of the slaughter of the paschal lambs: Conf. c. XXXV, 6. 11. The Levites slaughtered the Passover, and removed the skins.

2) From Esdr. VI, 18. The priests and Levites purified themselves, to make the Passover. Here we note: a) That "Passover" does not only denote the paschal lamb, but also other sacrifices that were made during the days of unleavened bread, and were connected with the paschal lamb: b) Heads of households, suffering from legal uncleanness, resigned their right to the priests and Levites: c) Heads of households, for the greater joy of public solemnity, brought in the priests and Levites, as companions in sacred labors.

Question XXXV.

What was the earthly and heavenly matter of this sacrament? The earthly matter was a whole and perfect lamb, a male, one year old, taken from the common flock of sheep, and sometimes also of goats (a)).

Proof a. From Exod. XII, 5. "Your animal shall be a whole male, a year old: You shall take it from the lambs, or from the young goats." Here we observe: 1) That the Israelites for the most part slaughtered a lamb; for it more clearly foreshadowed Christ, the most innocent lamb, who takes away the sins of the world, Io. I, 29. But if a lamb was lacking, a young goat was used; for it is called by the generic name שֶׂה, "animal," which denotes a small animal, and could be taken from different species of smaller animals, from the flock of sheep, or of goats. 2) That the lamb used was whole and perfect, i.e., without blemish, not lame, not scabby, etc. 3) That it had to be a year old, which was either about to complete its first year of age, or had completed it, but had not excelled so much as to be considered two years old. Furthermore, a lamb that was less than eight days old from its birth was not used.

Proof b. The heavenly matter was Christ, to be sacrificed for the sins of the entire human race that had fallen into sin, concerning whom Paul, 1 Cor. V, 7. "For Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed for us."

Question XXXVI.

What was the union of the heavenly and earthly matter? The union of the earthly and heavenly lamb, according to the nature of the Old Testament, was a σχήμα τυπικὸν, a typical figure to an antitype; for by it Christ, to be crucified and killed, was prefigured, and was signified to the fathers as morally present, but was not exhibited, as to both natures, substantially.

Proof a. By the paschal lamb, Christ, the heavenly lamb, who takes away the sins of the world, Io. I, 19., was typically represented, with all His merit, for the salvific enjoyment of those who partake. Therefore, the Messiah was personally present, as the eternal Son of God; but as to His flesh, He was present in

PART III. SECT. of the Passover sacrament not substantially, but morally, by reason of the divine decree, the promise, and the efficacy of the merit to be performed by Himself. For the meritorious cause, before it actually exists, by the value of its foreknown merit can move the will of the efficient cause: In which respect the Lamb is said to be slain from the foundation of the world, Apoc. XIII, 8.

Latin:

Ministri promulgandæ institutionis diuinæ huius sacramenti fuerunt Moses & Aaron . Ministri autem mactationis & affationis agni paschalis partim patres familias gentis Israëliticæ , partim Leuitæ fuerunt.

Prob. a. Ex Exod. XII, 21. Vbi Moses dicit: Accipite vobis pecora per familias vestras, & immolate pascha. Subiungitur populioblequium, v. 28. Et abierunt filii Ifraël, & quemadmodum præceperant Mose & Aaron, sic fecerunt.

Prob. b. 1) Ex Exod. XII, 6. Ma&abunt agnum omnis cœtus Ifraëlis inter vesperas. E. quiuis paterfamilias in Ægypto, vbi sacerdotium Leuiticum nondum ordinatum erat, agnum paschalem mactare potuit.

2) Deut. XVI, 2. Deus vniuersum populum Ifraëliticum alloquitur: Ma&abis Pesach Iehouæ Deo tuo. Ex quo colligimus, ius mactandi & affandi agnum paschalem fletille penes quemuis patremfamilias gentis Ifraëliticæ non ante folum, sed & post constitutam poliliam Mofaicam.

Prob. c. 1) Ex 2 Paral. XXX, 1. Leuitæ erant super ma&atione agnorum paschalium: Conf. c. XXXV, 6. 11. Leuitæ immolarunt pascha, & detraxerunt pelles.

2) Ex Esdr. VI, 18. Sacerdotes & Leuitæ purificarunt se, ad faciendum pascha. Vbi notamus: a) Quod pascha non notet tantum agnum paschalem, sed & alia sacrificia, quæ diebus azymorum fiebant, & cum agno paschali connexa erant: b) Patresfamilias, immunditia legali laborantes, ius suum resignarunt sacerdotibus & Leuitis: c) Patresfamilias ad maiorem lætitia publicæ solemnitatem coadhibuerunt sacerdotes & Leuitas, velut sacrorum laborum comites.

Quæst. XXXV. Quænam fuit materia terrena & cælestis huius sacramenti?

Materia terrena erat agnus integer & perfectus, masculus, vnius anni, ex communi grege ouium, & interdum etiam caprarum fumtus a). Materia cælestis fuit Christus, pro peccatis totius mundi immolandus b).

Prob. a. Ex Exod. XII, 5. Pecus integra, mascula, filia anni erit vobis: De agnis, vel de hædis sumetis. Vbi obs. 1) Quod Ifraëlitæ vt plurimum mactauerint agnum; quippe qui luculentius adumbrabat Christum, agnum innocentissimum, tollentem peccata mundi, Io. I, 29. At deficiente agno adhibebatur hædus; dicitur enim nomine generico שֶׂה, pecus, quod notat paruum pecudem, & potuit sumi ex diuersis minorum pecudum speciebus, de grege ouium, aut caprarum. 2) Quod agnus adhibitus sit integer & perfectus, i. e. vitio carens, non claudicans, non scabiolus &c. 3) Quod debuerit esse anniculus, qui annum ætatis primum vel mox impleturus erat, vel impleuerat, non tamen ita excellerat, vt pro bimo haberi potuerit. Ceterum non vfurpabatur agnus, qui infra octauum ab ortu suo diem erat.

Prob. b. Materia cælestis fuit Christus, immolandus pro peccatis vniuersi generis humani in peccatum prolapsi, de quo Paullus, 1 Cor. V, 7. Pascha nostrum pro nobis oblatum est Christus.

Quæst. XXXVI. Qualis erat vnio materiæ cælestis & terrestris?

Vnio agni terrestris & cælestis, iuxta naturam veteris testamenti, erat σχήμα τυπικὸν, typi ad antitypum; quippe qua Christus crucifigendus & occidendus præfigurabatur, & significabatur patribus præsens moraliter, non exhibebatur, quoad vtramque naturam, substantialiter.

Prob. a. Agno paschali typice repræsentabatur Christus agnus cælestis, tollens peccata mundi, Io. I, 19. cum omni ipsius merito, ad salutarem participantium fruitionem. Erat igitur præsens Messias personaliter, vt æternus Dei filius; qua carnem autem præsens erat in

PARS III. SECT. sacramento Paschah non substantialiter, sed moraliter, ratione divini decreti, promissionis & efficaciae meriti, a se praestandi. Causa quippe meritoria, antequam realiter existat, valore meriti sui praecogniti voluntatem causae efficientis movere potest: Quo respectu agnus ab origine mundi occisus dicitur, Apoc. XIII, 8.


### Quest. XXXVII. What was the form of this sacrament?

The form of this sacrament consisted a) in the timely selection of a perfect lamb, b) in the bloody slaughter, c) in the roasting, d) in the total consumption, e) in the repetition of the words of institution.

Proof a. The lamb was taken from the common flock on the tenth day of the month Nisan, and was kept until the fourteenth day of this month, Exod. XII, 3, 6. Thus, the segregation took place four days before the lamb was slaughtered, 1) so that the heads of families could inquire more solicitously into the perfection and requirements of that lamb, and observe whether it labored under any defect: 2) so that from the daily sight (or even the bleating) of that lamb, they might take the opportunity to converse among themselves about their wonderful liberation from Egypt, and the future redemption through the Messiah.

Proof b. The lamb was slaughtered between the two evenings, Exod. XII, 5, the first of which began from the exact third hour after noon, which was called the ninth by the Hebrews; when the sun, a large part of the day having passed, inclines toward setting, the other evening is the eleventh hour exactly. That whole interval is called by the phrase of Scripture between the two evenings. At the same point of time, Christ, the antitypical lamb, willed to die. The slaughter did not take place without αἱματεκχυσίᾳ (shedding of blood), because without it there is no remission of sin, Hebr. IX, 22. Wherefore the slaughter of the lamb prefigured the shedding of the blood of Christ.

Proof c. The lamb was eaten not raw, not boiled in water, but roasted with fire, Exod. XII, 9. Christ was prefigured as about to be roasted; partly by the fire of divine wrath toward the sins which He took upon Himself, partly by the fire of His own love toward us who were to be redeemed.

Proof d. That the whole lamb was to be eaten, Moses teaches, Exod. XII, 9. It was signified that the whole Messiah was to be eaten both spiritually and sacramentally.

Proof e. God sanctioned this sacrament with the word of institution, Exod. XII, 11. This Passover shall be to Jehovah, and He commanded that these words also be used in the progress of time, so that this rite might be distinguished from other similar non-sacramental acts, Exod. XII, 27.

Latin:

Forma huius sacramenti consistebat a) in tempestiva agni perfecti selectione, b) cruenta mactatione, c) assatione, d) totali manducatione, e) verborum institutionis repetitione.

Prob. a. Sumebatur agnus de communi grege, die decimo mensis Nisan, & custodiebatur usque in diem decimum quartum huius mensis, Exod. XII, 3, 6. Fiebat itaque segregatio quatriduo, antequam agnus mactaretur, 1) ut patresfamilias eo follicitius in perfectionem & requisita agni illius inquirere, & observare possent, num defectu quodam laboraret: 2) ut ex quotidiano illius agni aspectu (vel etiam clamore) ansam caperent, inter se colloquendi de admiranda liberatione sua ex Aegypto, & futura redemptione per Messiam.

Prob. b. Mactabatur agnus inter duas vesperas, Exod. XII, 5. quarum prima incepit ab exacta hora tertia pomeridiana, quae Hebraeis nona dicebatur; quando sol, decursa magna diei parte, ad occasum vergit, altera vespera est hora undecima exacta. Totum illud intervallum phrasi scripturae dicitur inter duas vesperas. Eodem temporis articulo mori voluit Christus, agnus antitypicus. Non fiebat mactatio sine αἱματεκχυσίᾳ, quia sine illa non fit peccati remissio, Hebr. IX, 22. Quare mactatio agni praefiguravit effusionem sanguinis Christi.

Prob. c. Comedebatur agnus non crudus, non coctus aqua, sed assatus igne, Exod. XII, 9. Praefigurabatur Christus assandus; partim igne irae divinae erga peccata, quae in se suscepit, partim igne amoris sui erga nos redimendos.

Prob. d. Totum agnum fuisse comedendum, docet Moses, Exod. XII, 9. Significabatur, totum Messiam tum spiritualiter, tum sacramentaliter edendum esse.

Prob. e. Deus verbo institutionis hoc sacramentum tanciuit, Exod. XII, 11. Pascha hoc erit Iehovae, ac iussit his verbis etiam progressu temporis uti, ut distingueretur ritus hic ab aliis similibus actibus non sacramentalibus, Exod. XII, 27.


### Quest. XXXVIII. Who were admitted to the eating of the paschal lamb?

Israelites were admitted, both males and females a), free from impurity b), possessing the use of reason c), servants also, and circumcised proselytes d).

Proof a. All the congregation of Israel shall keep it (the Passover) Exod. XII, 47. Therefore, females were not excluded, who, although they were not circumcised, were nevertheless partakers of the covenant of grace.

Proof b. From Num. IX, 11. Speak to the children of Israel, saying: When any man shall be unclean by reason of a dead body, or be in a journey afar off, among you or your generations; yet he shall keep the Passover unto Jehovah. But in the second month on the fourteenth day between the evenings they shall keep it. From which we gather that females, laboring under menstrual blood, were not admitted to the feast of the paschal lamb. But that King Hezekiah admitted the unclean to the celebration of the Passover (contrary to the law, Num. IX, 10), that was done by a singular dispensation of God, 2 Chron. XXX, 20.

Proof c. Children, in whom the use of reason had manifested itself, so that they could say: What (does this) service mean to you? Exod. XII, 26, were present at the celebration of the Passover; the rest were barred.

Prob. d. 1) From Exod. XII, 43. 44. Every son of a foreigner shall not eat of it; but as for every servant of a man, a purchase of silver, if you circumcise him, then he shall eat of it.

2) From Exod. XII, 48. 49. But if a stranger shall sojourn with you, and shall desire to perform the Pesach of Jehovah, every male of his shall be circumcised; and then he shall approach to perform it, and he shall be as a native of the land; but any uncircumcised person shall not eat of it.

Latin:

Admittebantur Israelitae, tam mares, quam feminae a), impuritatis expertes b), usu rationis pollentes c), servi quoque, & proselyti circumcisi d).

Prob. a. Omnis coetus Israelis facient illud (pascha) Exod. XII, 47. Non igitur excludebantur feminae, quae, licet circumcisae non essent, foederis tamen gratiae erant consortes.

Prob. b. Ex Num. IX, 11. Loquere ad filios Israelis dicendo: Quum vir quis fuerit immundus ob animam, aut in via longinqua, vobis aut generationibus vestris; faciet tamen Pasch Iehovae. Sed in mense secundo in quarto decimo die inter vesperas facient. Ex quo colligimus, feminas, sanguine menstruo laborantes, non fuisse admissas ad epulum agni paschalis. Quod autem rex Ezechias admisit immundos ad celebrationem paschalis (contra legem, Num. IX, 10.) id factum est singulari Dei dispensatione, 2 Paral. XXX, 20.

Prob. c. Liberi, in quibus usus rationis se exsererat, ut dicere possent: Quid (sibi vult) altus hic vobis? Exod. XII, 26. intererant celebrationi paschatis, reliqui arcebantur. paschatis, reliqui arcebantur. paschatis, reliqui arcebantur.

Omnis filius alienigena non comedet de eo; quantum autem ad omnem seruum viri, emtionem argenti, si circumcidetis eum, tum comedet de eo.

2) Ex Exod. XII, 48. 49. Quod si peregrinabitur tecum peregrinus, & voluerit facere Pesach Iehouae, circumcidetur ei omnis masculus; & tunc accedet ad faciendum illud, eritque sicut incola terrae; sed vllus praeputiatus non comedet de eo.


### Quest. XXXIX. What was the end of the paschal lamb?

The primary end was the confirmation of federal grace and faith in the coming Messiah . The secondary ends were: bodily liberation from the striking angel , the miraculous commemoration of the leading out from Egyptian servitude , and the certification of future defense and protection .

Prob. a. From Heb. XI, 28. By faith Moses kept the passover, and the shedding of blood. The slaughter of the paschal lamb was a notable figure of the Lamb of God to be slaughtered for us, Jo. I, 29. 1 Cor. V, 7. Rev. XIII, 8. and the profusion of blood shadowed forth the shedding of the blood of Christ, by whose virtue we escape the slaughter of the destroying angel, obtaining through Christ’s blood the remission of sins, Eph. I, 7. Thus, therefore, Moses celebrated the passover with the people of God by faith, so that he might more and more excite and confirm faith in the Messiah, the immaculate Lamb of God.

Prob. b. From Exod. XII, 22. Jehovah will pass through to strike Egypt, and when He shall see the blood upon the lintel and upon the two doorposts, Jehovah will pass over the door, and will not permit the striker to come into your houses to strike you.

Prob. c. From Exod. XII, 14. This day shall be for you for a memorial. This was the end of the passover, that the Israelites, eating the paschal lamb, might ruminate upon the incomparable benefit of the admirable liberation from Egypt, where they were pressed by the yoke of servitude.

Prob. d. Whoever God, the best and greatest, had afforded aid to the Israelites in the most turbulent times in Egypt, His help is to be seriously implored and certainly expected in every adversity.

Latin:

Finis primarius fuit gratiae foederalis & fidei in venturum Messiam confirmatio . Secundarii fines fuerunt: liberatio corporalis ab angelo percussore , miraculosa eductionis ex seruitute Aegyptiaca commemoratio , futurae defensionis ac protectionis certificatio .

Prob. a. Ex Hebr. XI, 28. Moses fide fecit pascha, & effusionem sanguinis. Mactatio agni paschalis erat insignis agni Dei pro nobis mactandi figura, Io. I, 29. 1 Cor. V, 7. Apoc. XIII, 8. & profusio sanguinis adumbrabat effusionem sanguinis Christi, cuius virtute effugimus angeli vastatoris caedem, consequentes per Christi sanguinem remissionem peccatorum, Eph. I, 7. Ita ergo per fidem celebrauit Moses pascha cum populo Dei, vt fidem in Messiam, agnum Dei immaculatum, magis magisque excitaret & confirmaret.

Prob. b. Ex Exod. XII, 22. Transibit Iehouah ad percutiendum Aegyptum, cumque viderit sanguinem super superliminari, & super duobus postibus, praeteribit Iehouah praeter ostium, & non permittet percussori, venire ad domos vestras ad vos percutiendum.

Prob. c. Ex Exod. XII, 14. Erit iste dies vobis in memoriam. Hic erat finis paschatis, vt Israelitae, edentes agnum paschalem, ruminarentur incomparabile beneficium adinirandae liberationis ex Aegypto, vbi seruitutis iugo premebantur.

Prob. d. Quicunque Deus opt. max. opem praestiterat Israelitis turbulentissimis in Aegypto temporibus, illius subsidium in omni aduersitate serio implorandum & certo expectandum est.


### Quest. XL. Was the paschal lamb a sacrifice?

The paschal lamb was not a sacrifice, strictly so called; yet analogically it can be so called.

Obs. I. A sacrament is one thing, a sacrifice another. In a sacrament, God offers and confers grace to men: In sacrifices, men offer a gift to God, to obtain His grace.

Obs. II. The paschal lamb is not to be confused with the paschal sacrifices: 1) Because the Pesach was only a lamb; but the paschal sacrifices were sheep and oxen, Deut. XVI, 1. 2) The Pesach was the object of the evening slaughter, or between the two evenings on the 14th day of the month Nisan from the ninth hour to the eleventh hour exactly; but sheep and oxen were used for paschal sacrifices on the days of unleavened bread: 3) the paschal lamb was slaughtered by the head of the household in individual houses; but those paschal victims were not slaughtered except by the priests, with the Levites skinning the sacrificial cattle.

Prob. 1) No sacrifice, strictly so called, could be made in Egypt, because of the abominations of the Egyptians, Exod. VIII, 26. 2) Every sacrifice, strictly so called, was performed by a priest at the altar, with a sacrificial rite which the delineation of the Levitical priesthood prescribes: The paschal lamb was ordinarily slaughtered not by a priest, but by the head of the household, Exod. XII, 4. and not on a solemn altar, but in private houses.

3) If the paschal lamb was a sacrifice properly so called, it was either mincha (מנחה) or zebach (זבח).

It was not mincha, because that was a meal-offering, consisting of fine flour, and cakes and fruits with salt, wine, and oil, partly burned, partly destined for the priest, Levit. II. Num. XV. But the lamb, a living animal, was not such. Nor was it zebach strictly so called; because it was neither a burnt-offering, nor a sacrifice for sin and guilt, nor a peace-offering: It was not a burnt-offering; because the whole lamb was not burned; nor a sacrifice for sin, because the sins of the people were not laid upon it; nor a peace-offering, because it was not eaten by the priests in the holy court itself. Therefore, it is not zebach, under the special notion of sacrifice, although it may be called zebach under the notion of slaughter.

There is an antithesis of most Papists, asserting that the paschal lamb was a sacrifice properly so called. They rely on the following arguments:

I. Whatever was a type of the sacrifice of Christ, that was a sacrifice properly so called: The Passover was, etc. Therefore. The major premise is evident: because it is necessary that the antitype correspond to the type, either in every way, or appropriately, or respectively. It is not necessary for the type to correspond to the antitype in special requirements, since the former agrees with the latter not absolutely and simply, but in a certain respect, and thus a type of a sacrifice is not necessarily a sacrifice. For the slaughter of the red heifer, Num. XIX. 2. also figures the bloody slaughter of Christ, Hebr. IX, 3. yet it was not a sacrifice.

II. The paschal lamb is called zebach (זבח), Exod. XII, 27. Therefore, it is a sacrifice. Resp. It is called zebach not because it was a sacrifice properly so called, but with the word zebach taken more generally, so that the sense is: The slaughter of the passing over, because this slaughter was instituted when the Lord was passing, and so that He might pass. And thus the Holy Spirit uses the word zebach in 1 Sam. XVIII, 24. ch. XVI, 3. 1 Kings I, 9. for slaughter; whence it is even used for the killing of men, Is. XXXIV, 6. The same is answered to that in Mark XIV, 12. πάσχα θύειν. For θύειν does not always denote sacrificial slaughter: as in Matt. XXII, 4. Luke XV, 23. Acts X, 13.; in which places θύειν is used for preparatory acts for a feast, or food, outside of any sacrificial respect.

Instance: Although the word zebach may broadly signify any slaughter, yet you will not easily find zebach used otherwise than for a sacrifice, especially in this place where a special relation to God is insinuated, לזבח, Exod. XII, 27. Resp. Although the application of zebach to a victim is more frequent in the scriptures; yet that is not necessarily so by reason of the root, which denotes slaughter; or for a feast, or for a sacrifice; but by reason of the material placement. In that amplification, therefore, we understand the words of Moses, Exod. XII, 27. although we admit that the feast of the paschal lamb was most holy and most singular, which we concede can be called a sacrifice analogically, on account of the solemn slaughter and the shedding of blood.

III. Every external act, defined by the word of God, in which some sensible and permanent thing is consecrated to God alone, and is actually offered for a sweet-smelling savor, is a sacrifice: But the paschal lamb, etc. Therefore. Resp. Something is consecrated to God, either as a formal term, or as a final term. The paschal lamb is entirely celebrated for the use of man, who is the formal term to which this sacrament is directed. Quæst.

Latin:

Agnus paschalis non fuit sacrificium, proprie dictum; analogice tamen ita dici potest.

Obs. I. Aliud est sacramentum, aliud sacrificium. In sacramento Deus offert & confert gratiam hominibus: In sacrificiis offerunt homines munus Deo, ad consequendam eius gratiam.

Obs. II. Agnus paschalis cum sacrificiis paschalibus non est confundendus: 1) Quia Pesach tantum agnus erat; at sacrificia paschalia oues & boues, Deut. XVI, 1. 2) Pesach erat obiectum mactationis vespertinae, seu inter duas vesperas die 14. mensis Nisan ab hora nona ad vndecimam exactam; oues autem & boues pro sacrificiis paschalibus vsurpabantur in diebus azymorum: 3) agnus paschalis mactabatur a patrefamilias in singulis domibus; at victimae illae paschales non, nisi a sacerdotibus, excoriantibus pecora sacrificialia Leuitis, mactabantur.

Prob. 1) Nullum sacrificium, proprie dictum, potuit fieri in Aegypto, propter abominationes Aegyptiorum, Exod. VIII, 26. 2) Omne sacrificium, proprie dictum, peractum est a sacerdote in altari, ritu sacrificiali, quem leuitici sacerdotii delineatio praescribit: Agnus paschalis ordinarie non a sacerdote, sed patrefamilias est mactatus, Exod. XII, 4. neque in altari solemni, sed in priuatis aedibus. folemni, sed in priuatis ædibus.

3) Si agnus paschalis fuit sacrificium proprie dictum, vel fuit מנחה, vel זבח.

Non mincha, quia illud erat sacrificium dapale, constans ex farina munda, & placentis & frugibus cum sale, vino & oleo, partim combustum, partim sacerdoti destinatum, Levit. II. Num. XV. Sed tale non fuit agnus, animal vivum. Neque etiam zebach stricte dictum; quia neque holocaustum, neque sacrificium pro peccato & delicto, neque hostia pacifica erat: Non erat holocaustum; quia totus agnus non comburebatur; neque sacrificium pro peccato, quia peccata populi illi non imponebantur; neque hostia pacifica, quia non a sacerdotibus in ipso atrio sancto comedebatur. E. non est זבח, sub notione speciali sacrificii, licet possit appellari זבח sub notione mactationis.

Antithesis est plerorumque Pontificiorum, afferentium, agnum paschalem fuisse sacrificium proprie dictum. Qui sequentibus innituntur argumentis:

I. Quidquid fuit typus sacrificii Christi, illud fuit sacrificium proprie dictum: Pascha fuit &c. Ergo. Maior constat: quia necesse est, ut antitypus respondeat typo, sive ab omni, sive accommodam, sive respectivam. Non necesse est typum antitypo in specialibus requisitis respondere, siquidem ille cum hoc convenit non absolute & simpliciter, sed certo respectu, adeoque typus sacrificii non necessario est sacrificium. Nam & mactatio vaccæ rufæ, Num. XIX. 2. figurat cruentam Christi mactationem, Hebr. IX, 3. neque tamen fuit sacrificium.

II. Agnus paschalis dicitur זבח, Exod. XII, 27. E. est sacrificium. Resp. Dicitur זבח non quod fuerit sacrificium proprie dictum, sed voce זבח generalius sumta, ut sensus sit: Mactatio transitus est, quia mactatio hæc instituebatur, cum transiret Dominus, & ut transiret. Atque ita vocem זבח usurpat Spiritus S. 1 Sam. XVIII, 24. cap. XVI, 3. 1 Reg. I, 9. pro mactatione; unde etiam de cæde hominum usurpatur, Es. XXXIV, 6. Idem respondetur ad illud Marc. XIV, 12. πάσχα θύειν. Neque enim θύειν semper notat mactationem sacrificialem: vt Matth. XXII, 4. Luc. XV, 23. Act. X, 13.; in quibus locis τὸ θύειν usurpatur de actibus præparatoriis ad convivium, aut cibum, extra omnem respectum sacrificialem.

Instantia: Licet verbum זבח late significet quamlibet mactationem, non tamen facile reperias זבח aliter, quam de sacrificio usurpatum, præsertim h. l. vbi specialis ad Deum relatio insinuatur, לזבח, Exod. XII, 27. Resp. Licet fainosior sit in scripturis applicatio זבח ad victimam; id tamen non est necessario, ratione radicis, quæ notat mactationem; vel ad epulum, vel ad sacrificium; sed ratione positus materialis. In illa igitur ampliatione intelligimus verba Mosis, Exod. XII, 27. quamvis fateamur, epulum agni paschalis fuisse sanctissimum & singularissimum, quod analogice sacrificium dici posse, concedimus, ob solemnem mactationem, & sanguinis effusionem.

III. Omnis actus externus, verbo Dei definitus, in quo soli Deo res aliqua sensibilis & permanens consecratur, & actu offertur in odorem quietis, est sacrificium: Atqui agnus paschalis &c. Ergo. Resp. Consecratur aliquid Deo, vel vt termino formali, vel vt termino finali. Agnus paschalis totus celebratur in vsum hominis, qui huius sacramenti terminus formalis ad quem est.


### XLI. Was the sacramental action occupied about the paschal lamb necessary?

The sacrament of the paschal lamb was necessary, by necessity of precept and of means. Prob. God instituted and commanded the eating of the paschal lamb, Exod. XII. Therefore, it is necessary by necessity of precept. The neglected eating of the paschal lamb brought condemnation.

Exod. 11:15. It was observed and saved, and indeed was necessary by a necessity not only of precept, but also of means.

Question 42. What circumstances must be observed for a fuller understanding of the sacrament of the paschal lamb?

In order that we may more fully understand this sacrament, the circumstances of place a) and of time b) must be observed.

Proof a. The place of the celebrated Passover was either extraordinary or ordinary. The first extraordinary one was Egypt, and specifically the house of each head of a household, Exod. 12:46; the second was the desert of Sinai, Num. 9:2; the third was Gilgal, Josh. 5:10. The ordinary one was Jerusalem; for it was that place which God had chosen to place His name there, Deut. 16:5-6. By that express designation of place, 1) elective worship was prevented, 2) harmony among the confessors of the one true religion was fostered, 3) the sacrifice of the Messiah, to be offered in the city of Jerusalem, was prefigured. Outside this place, however, the Hebrews, being exiles and dispersed, celebrated the Passover indeed as a memorial, but not as a public and solemn festival.

Proof b. The time of this sacrament is one thing for its institution, another for its administration, and another for its abrogation. The time of institution falls in the year of the world 2513, according to the calculation of D. Calovius. See his Biblical Chronicle, fol. 80.
