6) Whoever eat the body of Christ without the mouth of faith, they eat the body of Christ with the mouth of the body: But unworthy communicants &c. 1 Cor. XI, 26. Therefore. The minor premise is evident; because the unworthy do not have the mouth of faith.

7) Against which, as an object, one sins by eating and drinking, which is done by the mouth of the body; that is also eaten and drunk by the mouth of the body: But against the body and blood of Christ, as an object, one sins by eating and drinking, which is done by the mouth of the body. Therefore.

8) Antiquity believed in the oral eating of the body and the drinking of the blood of Christ. TERTULL. de resurrect. carn. c. 8. says: The flesh feeds on the body and blood of Christ, so that the soul also may be fattened by God. CHRYSOST. hom. XXIX. in 2 Corinth. Our mouth has attained no common honor, receiving the dominical body. And notable are the words of AMBROSE to Theodosius: With what rashness will you receive with your mouth the cup of the precious blood, when by the fury of your words blood has been unjustly shed.

You say: I. Whatever sacramental eating is not instituted by Christ, that is not to be brought forward: But oral sacramental eating &c. Therefore. The minor premise is proven: because the eating of the body and blood, which is done by the mouth, is a Capernaitic butchery of human flesh, John VI, 52, 63, and a cyclopean ἀνθρωποφαγία (anthropophagy).

Resp. i) One must distinguish between oral eating that is physical, or natural, and hyperphysical, or supernatural. The physical eating of human flesh is a cyclopean ἀνθρωποφαγία (anthropophagy), which we do not bring forward; but we believe that sacramental eating is indeed oral, in that it is done by the mouth as by an organ, but supernatural, mystical, incomprehensible, known to God alone; since it takes place without injury to the body of Christ, existing unextendedly and indivisibly in the Holy Supper. 2) The Capernaites believed, a) that Christ was a mere man; but we are fed with the flesh of Christ θεανθρώπης. b) They believed that the flesh of Christ was to be eaten immediately and naturally: but we assert that the flesh of Christ in the Holy Supper is truly and really eaten indeed by the mouth of the body, but mediately, through the blessed bread as mediator, and supernaturally, since concerning this supreme mystery we hold views that are not natural, not vulgar, not Capernaitic. Instance: There is no proper, true and real eating that is not physical. Reply: Just as there is a proper, true and real generation of the Son of God from the substance of the Father, which nevertheless is not physical: so there is an eating of the body of Christ that is proper, true and real, which nevertheless is not natural.

II. Whatever body is eaten by the mouth, that is eventually consumed: But the body of Christ is not consumed, because it is incorruptible: Therefore, it is not eaten by the mouth. Resp. 1) Whatever body is physically eaten, that is consumed; I concede: But the body of Christ in the Holy Supper is eaten supernaturally. 2) A whale devoured Jonah, yet it did not consume him.

III. If the body of Christ were eaten properly and orally, it would certainly be crushed by the teeth and cast into the stomach: The consequent is absurd: Therefore, so is the antecedent. Resp. 1) I deny the consequence, because the body of Christ is eaten not only in a natural or vulgar way, but in a supernatural and mystical way. 2) Distinguish between the universal and the particular requirement of eating. If all food had to be crushed by the teeth, toothless old women and infants would not truly eat. 3) If someone has received food into the mouth and swallowed it, but nausea or weakness of strength prevents him from sending it down into the stomach, and before it has arrived there, he is forced to cast it out through vomiting; he truly eats the food, even though he has not passed it into the stomach. 4) The body of Christ is not natural food, destined for the natural digestion and nutrition of man, to which the passing of food into the stomach is solely directed, but it is supernatural, heavenly, and in a certain respect spiritual food.

IV. Whatever food is heavenly and spiritual, that is not eaten by the mouth of the body: But the body of Christ is: Therefore. Resp. 1) I deny the major. For the word of the Gospel is also spiritual food, and yet it is perceived by the bodily ears. 2) Heavenly and spiritual food is not eaten by the mouth of the body in a natural and vulgar way, yet it is eaten in a supernatural way. 3) The body and blood of Christ is spiritual food and drink, not simply by reason of its essence, as if the body of Christ were changed into a spirit; for that conflicts with the truth of human nature; but comparatively and in a certain respect: a) In opposition to vulgar and natural food; because sacramental food is not gross and physical, but mystical and supernatural: b) By reason of its qualities; because the body of Christ is glorified and majestic, and thus endowed with spiritual gifts: c) By reason of its effect; because it nourishes us unto spiritual life, and confers heavenly spiritual benefits.

V. If the eating of the body of Christ, which takes place in the Holy Supper, is real and proper; it will be either corporal or spiritual: But it is not corporal; because it does not take place in a corporal, i.e., natural and vulgar, way. Therefore, it is spiritual, and takes place by the mouth of faith. Resp. A third option is given, namely, supernatural, mystical, and incomprehensible. For just as the conception of Christ in the womb of Mary is true and proper, yet by reason of the mode it is neither natural and vulgar, nor merely spiritual, which takes place through faith: so the eating of the body of Christ in the Holy Supper, by reason of the mode, is not corporal, i.e., vulgar and natural, nor merely spiritual, which takes place through faith; although in a certain respect it can be called corporal, by reason of the organ, because it takes place by the mouth of the body; and spiritual, insofar as spiritual is opposed to natural and gross. Conf. D. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 1242.

VI. Whoever sits alive at the table, his body could not be eaten by the disciples: But Christ &c. Therefore. Resp. Christ sat at the table naturally, and yet through his omnipotent power, having multiplied the presence of his body, he gave his body to the disciples to be eaten sacramentally.

VII. If the blood of Christ is drunk by the mouth of the body, then the new testament of Christ must also be drunk by the same: The consequent is absurd: Therefore, the antecedent is as well. The consequence is proved from Luke 22:20, where Christ, instituting the supper, says: This cup is the new testament in my blood. Therefore, if the blood of Christ is drunk by the mouth, the N.T. will be drunk by the same. Resp. Distinguish between real and usual predication. Matthew and Mark employ real predication when they describe the other species of this sacrament: This is my blood of the N.T. Luke and Paul use usual predication: This cup is the N.T. in my blood, which is poured out for you. Christ commands to drink the blessed [cup], encompassing wine and blood, concerning which He predicates this use, that it becomes the N.T. in His blood, i.e., a medium of grace and peace, not by reason of the wine, but in respect of the blood.

VIII. Whatever manducation of the body of Christ is useless, that is not to be brought forward: But oral manducation of the body of Christ, etc. Therefore. The minor is proved from John 6:63: The flesh profiteth nothing. I answer with the words of CYRIL, lib. IV in John, c. 23: The flesh of other men indeed (ψιλὴν) truly profiteth nothing: But the flesh of Christ, because the only-begotten Son of God dwells in it, alone can vivify. Therefore these words are premised: It is the spirit that vivifieth, i.e., the principle, source, and origin of vivification is the spirit, or that spiritual nature in Christ. Whence the flesh of a mere man, naturally eaten, or Capernaitically torn to pieces, profiteth nothing. There are those who think that by flesh in the cited place is denoted the carnal intellect, or the prudence of the flesh, Rom. 8:6, so that the sense here is: carnal thoughts about this great mystery profit nothing.

IX. If oral manducation of the body of Christ were profitable, it would also be salutary to the unworthy. Resp. 1) Even the word of the gospel, nay, the very death and shedding of the blood of Christ, do not profit the infidels; are they therefore never simply profitable? 2) Spiritual manducation of the body of Christ, joined with oral manducation, profits more than without it: It profits, I say, toward a closer union of us with Christ. Quest.

Latin:

Corpus & sanguis Christi in legitimo sacrae coenae vsu a communicantibus non tantum ore fidei, sed etiam ore corporis accipiuntur, eduntur & bibuntur. Obs.

I. Comestio formaliter est rei, sub ratione cibi oblatae, per os intra corpus receptio, ad hominis alimoniam. Obs.

II. Manducatio triplex est: Alia est naturalis, alia spiritualis, alia sacramentalis. Illa fit ore corporeo, & instituta est ad nutritionem & refectionem virium naturalium: ista fit ore fidei, & gustat Christum cum omnibus meritis & beneficiis ipsius, in euangelio oblatis, ad refectionem animae & conscientiae: hac fieri potest ore corporis, sed modo supernaturali, ad spiritualem refectionem. Obs.

III. Differunt manducatio spiritualis, & sacramentalis. Illa est omnium temporum; haec est N. T. propria. Illa etiam extra coenam: haec tantum in ipsa coena locum habet. Illa etiam fieri potest absque symbolis; haec duntaxat mediantibus symbolis externis peragitur. Illa prodest semper ad salutem: haec interdum fit etiam ad iudicium. Illa apprehendit totum Christum cum omnibus ipsius beneficiis; haec tantum corpus Christi in & sub pane. Illa est metaphorica; haec propria proprietate grammatica, licet non proprietate physica. Obs.

IV. Dist. inter manducationem oralem physicam, siue naturalem, & hyperphysicam, siue supernaturalem. Illa est, qua cibus ore sumtus demittitur in aluum, concoquitur & eiicitur: Haec est, qua cibus oblatus quidem per os intra corpus recipitur, sed non modo naturali concoquitur & eiicitur. Comederunt angeli, Gen. XVIII, 8. & Christus post resurrectionem, Luc. XXIV, 42. quae tamen manducatio non fuit ordinis naturalis, neque modo naturali cibus fuit concoctus. Sed sicut aliter terra absumit aquam, aliter sol: ita quoque non physica ratione cibus ille est concoctus. Manducationem propriam supernaturalem in oeconomicam, & sacramentalem subdistinguit D. DANNHAVER in hodof. phanom. X. p. 1233. Obs.

V. Sacramentalis manducatio & bibitio est vna & indiuisa actio, qua simul eodem momento & panem eucharisticum, eique sacramentaliter vnitum corpus Christi comedimus, idemque vinum & cum eo sacramentaliter vnitum sanguinem Domini ex calice eucharistico haurimus. Sed vnius illius manducationis & bibitionis illius duplex est modus. Nam licet vno & eodem organo sumatur res terrena & coelestis, non tamen eodem modo. Panis & vinum ore accipiuntur immediate & naturaliter, corpus & sanguis Christi mediate & supernaturaliter. Declarari potest per similia. In infantem baptizandum immediate effunditur aqua, mediate Spiritus S. Immediate acceperunt discipuli halitum oris Christi, quo illos afflauit, mediate Spiritum S. Filium Mariae virginis immediate viderunt Apostoli oculis corporeis, manibusque contrectarunt; mediate viderunt & contrectarunt Verbum vitae, 1 Io. I, 1. ob vnionem personalem. Immediate deglutivit balaena corpus Ionae, mediate animam ob vnionem naturalem. Ita in legitimo eucharistiae vsu immediate edimus & bibimus panem & vinum benedictum, mediate corpus & sanguinem Christi ob vnionem sacramentalem.

Probatur assertum: 1) Quidquid eadem comestione cum pane benedicto editur, illud ore corporis comeditur: Atqui corpus Christi &c. E. Minor probatur, quia vnicum numero

verbum, EDITE, de pane & corpore simul praedicatur. E. vna tantum significatione gaudebit in eadem propositione. Aut igitur solam comestionem oralem, aut solam spiritualem, aut utramque simul significabit. Si illam: E. & panis & corpus Christi simul ore comedetur, quod volumus. Si istam: Igitur in panem simul credemus, quod est idololatricum. Si utramque simul: E. vna vox, eodem loco, eodemque propositionis membro duplicem habebit sensum litteralem, quod est falsum.

2) Verbum, EDITE, coniunctum cum τῷ ACCIPITE, in propositione conuivali significat proprie. Atqui τὸ EDITE hoc loco coniunctum est cum τῷ ACCIPITE, in propositione conuivali. E. τὸ EDITE hoc loco sumitur proprie. Sed omnis comestio propria est oralis.

3) Quaecunque in eodem sacramento, eademque in actione sunt vnita sacramentaliter, illa eodem quoque organo accipiuntur. Iam vero in vsu S. coenae panis & corpus Christi, vinum & sanguis Christi vnita sunt sacramentaliter. E. eodem quoque organo in vsu sacramenti panis & corpus, vinum & sanguis Christi accipiuntur. Maior constat: quia vna & indiuisa actio non potest duplici instrumento fieri.

4) Omnis manducatio, bibitioni contradistincta, est manducatio oralis: Atqui manducatio sacramentalis bibitioni est contradistincta. E. Maior constat: quia manducatio spiritualis, quae fit ore fidei, a bibitione spirituali non differt.

5) Quicunque distincte edunt corpus Christi cum pane benedicto, & distincte bibunt sanguinem Christi cum vino benedicto, illi edunt corpus, & bibunt sanguinem Christi ore corporis: Atqui communicantes &c. E. Maior constat: quia manducatio & bibitio spiritualis respicit totum Christum cum omnibus ipsius beneficiis. E. illa manducatio, qua distincte corpus Christi cum pane benedicto comeditur, & bibitio, qua distincte sanguis Christi cum vino benedicto bibitur, non est manducatio & bibitio mere spiritualis, quae fiat ore fidei.

6) Quicunque edunt corpus Christi fine ore fidei, illi edunt corpus Christi ore corporis: Atqui communicantes indigni &c. 1Cor. XI, 26. E. Minor constat; quia indigni os fidei non habent.

7) Contra quod, tanquam obiectum, esu & potu, qui fit ore corporis, peccatur, illud etiam ore corporis comeditur atque bibitur: Atqui contra corpus & sanguinem Christi, tanquam obiectum, esu & potu, qui fit ore corporis, peccatur. Ergo.

8) Oralem manducationem corporis & bibitionem sanguinis Christi pia credidit antiquitas. TERTULL. de resurrect. carn. c. 8. inquit: Caro corpore & sanguine Christi vescitur, vt & anima de Deo saginetur. CHRYSOST. hom. XXIX. in 2 Corinth. Non vulgarem honorem consecutum est os nostrum, accipiens corpus dominicum. Et nota sunt verba AMBROSII ad Theodosium: Qua temeritate ore tuo poculum sanguinis pretiosi percipies, quando furore verborum tuorum iniuste effusus est sanguis.

Dicis: I. Quaecunque manducatio sacramentalis a Christo non est instituta, illa non est afferenda: Atqui manducatio sacramentalis oralis &c. Ergo. Minor probatur: quia manducatio corporis & sanguinis, quae fit ore, est Capernaitica laniena carnis humanae, Io. VI, 52. 63. & cyclopica ἀνθρωποφαγία.

Resp. i) Distinguendum inter manducationem oralem physicam, siue naturalem, & hyperphysicam, siue supernaturalem. Manducatio physica carnis humanae est cyclopica ἀνθρωποφαγία, quam nos non afferimus; sed credimus, sacramentalem manducationem esse quidem oralem, qua fit ore, velut organo, sed supernaturalem, mysticam, incomprehensibileem, solique Deo cognitam; quippe quae fit fine laesione corporis Christi, inextense & indiuisibiliter existentis in S. coena. 2) Capernaitae putabant, a) Christum esse nudum hominem; nos autem pascimur carne Christi θεανθρώπης. b) Putabant, carnem Christi comedendam esse immediate & naturaliter: nos autem asserimus, carnem Christi in S. cœnæ vere & realiter quidem comedi ore corporis, sed mediate, mediante pane benedicto, & supernaturaliter, siquidem de hoc summo mysterio non naturalia, non vulgaria, non Capernaitica sentimus. Instantia: Non datur comestio propria, vera & realis, quæ non sit physica. Resp. Sicut datur propria, vera & realis generatio Filii Dei ex substantia Patris, quæ tamen non est physica: ita datur comestio corporis Christi propria, vera & realis, quæ tamen non est naturalis.

II. Quodcunque corpus comeditur ore, illud tandem absumitur: Atqui corpus Christi non absumitur, quia est incorruptibile: E. non comeditur ore. Resp. 1) Quodcunque corpus physice comeditur, illud absumitur; concedo: At corpus Christi in S. cœna comeditur supernaturaliter. 2) Balæna deuorauit Ionam, neque tamen absumsit eundem.

III. Si corpus Christi proprie & oraliter comederetur, vtique dentibus comminuere-tur, & in stomachum deiiceretur: Consequens est absurdum: E. & antecedens. Resp. 1) Neg. consequentiam, quia corpus Christi non modo naturali, aut vulgari, sed supernaturali & mystico editur. 2) Dist. inter requisitum manducationis vniuersale, & particulare. Si omnis cibus dentibus esset comminuendus, anus edentulæ & infantes non vere comederent. 3) Si quis cibum ore receperit, & deglutierit, nausea tamen, vel virium imbecillitate eum in ventriculum demittere impediat, sed antequam eo peruenerit, per vomitum cogatur effundere; vere cibum comedit, licet in ventriculum non traiecerit. 4) Corpus Christi non est cibus naturalis, destinatus ad concoctionem & nutritionem hominis naturalem, ad quam vnice directa est cibi in ventriculum traiectio, sed est cibus supernaturalis, cœlestis, & certo respectu spiritualis.

IV. Quicunque cibus est cœlestis & spiritualis, ille non comeditur ore corporis: Atqui corpus Christi: E. Resp. 1) Neg. Mai. Nam verbum euangelii est etiam cibus spiritualis, & tamen percipitur auribus corporeis. 2) Cibus cœlestis & spiritualis non comeditur ore corporis modo naturali & vulgari, attamen modo supernaturali. 3) Corpus & sanguis Christi est cibus & potus spiritualis, non simpliciter ratione essentiæ, quasi corpus Christi inu-tatum sit in spiritum; id enim pugnat cum veritate humanæ naturæ; sed comparate & certo respectu: a) In oppositione ad cibum vulgarem & naturalem; quia cibus sacramentalis non est crassus & physicus, sed mysticus & supernaturalis: b) Ratione qualitatum; quia corpus Christi est glorificatum & maiestaticum, adeoque spiritualibus dotibus præditum: c) Ratione effectus; quia nos alit ad vitam spiritualem, & confert beneficia spiritualia cœlestia.

V. Si manducatio corporis Christi, quæ fit in S. cœna, est realis & propria; aut corporalis erit, aut spiritualis: Sed non est corporalis; quia non fit modo corporali, i. e. naturali & vulgari. E. est spiritualis, & fit ore fidei. Resp. Datur tertium, scil. supernaturalis, mystica & incomprehensibilis. Sicut enim conceptio Christi in vtero Mariæ est vera & propria, neque tamen ratione modi est naturalis & vulgaris, neque etiam mere spiritualis, quæ fit per fidem: ita manducatio corporis Christi in S. cœna, ratione modi, non est corporalis, i. e. vulgaris & naturalis, neque mere spiritualis, quæ fit per fidem; quamuis certo respectu dici possit corporalis, ratione organi, quia fit ore corporis; & spiritualis, quatenus spirituale opponitur naturali & crasso. Conf. D. DANNHAV. in hodof. p. 1242.

VI. Quicunque viuus assedit mensæ, illius corpus a discipulis comedi non potuit: Atqui Christus &c. E. Resp. Christus assedit mensæ naturaliter, & tamen per omnipotentem virtutem multiplicata corporis sui præsentia discipulis corpus suum comedendum dedit sacramentaliter. omnipotente suam virtutem multiplicata corporis fui præfentia discipulis corpus suum comedendum dedit sacramentaliter.

VII. Si ore corporis bibitur sanguis Christi, etiam eodem bibetur novum testamentum Christi: Consequens est absurdum: E. & antecedens. Consequentia probatur ex Luc. XXII, 20. ubi Christus, cœnam instituens, dicit: Hoc poculum est novum testamentum in meo sanguine. E. si ore bibitur sanguis Christi, eodem bibetur N. T. Resp. Dist. inter prædicationem realem, & usualem. Matthæus & Marcus adhibent prædicationem realem, cum alteram huius sacramenti speciem describunt: Hoc est sanguis meus N. T. Lucas & Paullus utuntur prædicatione usuali: Hoc poculum est N. T. in meo sanguine, quod pro vobis effunditur. Christus bibere iubet benedictum, complectens vinum & sanguinem, de quo prædicat hunc usum, quod fit N. T. in sanguine suo, i. e. medium gratiæ & pacis, non ratione vini, sed respectu sanguinis.

VIII. Quæcunque manducatio corporis Christi est inutilis, illa non est afferenda: Atqui oralis manducatio corporis Christi &c. E. Minor probatur ex Io. VI, 63. Caro nil prodest. Respondeo verbis CYRILLI libr. IV. in Io. c. 23. Caro quidem ceterorum hominum (ψιλὴν) quidquam vere non prodest: Caro autem Christi, quia in ipsa unigenitus Dei Filius habitat, sola vivificare potest. Ideo præmittuntur hæc verba: Spiritus est, qui vivificat, h. e. principium, fons & origo vivificationis est spiritus, seu spiritualis illa in Christo natura. Vnde caro meri hominis, naturaliter manducata, aut capernaitice dilaniata, nil prodest. Sunt, qui per carnem l. c. denotari censent carnalem intellectum, vel prudentiam carnis, Rom. VIII, 6. vt hic fit sensus: cogitationes carnales de hoc tanto mysterio nil prosunt.

IX. Si oralis manducatio corporis Christi prodesset, etiam indignis esset salutaris. Resp. 1) Etiam verbum euangelii, immo ipsa mors & effusio sanguinis Christi, infidelibus non prosunt; nunquam igitur simpliciter non prosunt? 2) Spiritualis manducatio corporis Christi, coniuncta cum orali manducatione, plus prodest, quam sine illa: Prodest, inquam, ad arctiorem nostri cum Christo coniunctionem.


### XVII. To which guests is the H. Supper to be offered?

The H.

Supper is to be offered to Christian men a), who are willing and able to eat and drink b), and to discern this mystical food, and to examine themselves, and to proclaim the death of the Lord c). Prob. a. The guests of the first supper were the Apostles, who represented adult faithful Christians. Therefore, the guests of this mystical feast are not Pagans, Turks, Jews, and not even catechumens not yet baptized; because baptism is as it were the door to the church, whose proper goods are the sacraments. Prob. b. They are not guests who are destitute of the faculty of eating and drinking. Therefore, the H.

Supper is not to be offered to dead men, nor to those abstainers who cannot taste even a drop of wine; but they are to be well instructed concerning spiritual manducation and drinking, of which AUGUSTINE says: believe and you have eaten.

Prob. c. They are welcome guests in whom there is both the will and the power to recognize the dignity of this most august feast and to discern it from common food, to examine themselves according to the law and the gospel, and to proclaim the death of the Lord with a grateful mind. Therefore, the following are excluded: 1) Notorious sinners, whose crimes, e.g., adulteries, fornications, thefts, blasphemies, and scandals given are manifest, as long as they indulge in sins and do not perform serious repentance. But the church does not judge concerning occult matters, but commits them to the judgment of the omniscient God. Hence hypocrites, although they are unworthy of the H. Supper, and thus deserve to be excluded, are nevertheless not excluded by the church, because by the hypocrisy with which they feign piety, they are not constant to the church. But notorious sinners are kept away, for the reason that they do not wish to examine themselves properly. 2) Heretics, erring in the foundation of the faith and overturning the substantials of this sacrament, who, entangled in gross error, neither wish nor are able to examine themselves. 3) Infants, who by reason of their age cannot announce the death of the Lord and examine themselves. 4) Those possessed by the devil, who are perpetually harassed by this enemy. 5) The insane, or those delirious from disease, who are perpetually stirred by madness. But, if those possessed are sometimes free from the attack of the devil, and the insane have certain lucid intervals of sanity, they are to be admitted to this sacred banquet, so that they may be refreshed by the most divine goods which are conferred in the Holy Supper. As regards the deaf and the mute, we follow the counsel of LUTHER: If signs of desire and repentance are present, the mute and the deaf should not be kept away from the altar. For communicants are not considered worthy unless they are penitent and faithful, who have laid the foundations of the saving faith, as much as suffices for obtaining salvation. And it is fitting that they be communicants not only of a proven faith, but also of a proven life. Hence the deacon in the primitive church proclaims to them: Holy things for the holy!

Latin:

Porrigenda est S. cœna hominibus christianis a), qui edere & bibere b), & cibum hunc mysticum diiudicare, seque ipsos probare, ac mortem Domini annuntiare volunt & possunt c).

Prob. a. Conuiuæ primæ cœnæ fuere Apostoli, qui repræsentarunt fideles Christianos adultos. Non ergo conuiuæ mystici huius epuli sunt Pagani, Turcæ, Iudæi, ac ne catechumeni nondum non baptizati; quia baptismus est velut ianua ad ecclesiam, cuius propria bona sunt sacramenta.

Prob. b. Non sunt conuiuæ, qui edendi, bibendique facultate sunt destituti. Non igitur porrigenda est S. cœna hominibus mortuis, nec illis abstemiis, qui ne guttulam quidem vini degustare possunt; fed illi de spirituali manducatione & bibitione bene erudiendi sunt, de qua AVGVSTINVS inquit: crede & manducasti.

Prob. c. Grati conuiuæ, quos penes est tum voluntas, tum potestas, augustissimi huius conuiuij dignitatem agnoscendi & a cibo vulgari discernendi, iuxta legem & euangelium se ipsos probandi, & mortem Domini grato animo annuntiandi. Excluduntur igitur 1) peccatores notorii, quorum crimina, v. gr. adulteria, scortationes, furta, blasphemiæ & data scandala sunt manifesta, quamdiu peccatis indulgent, nec seriam pœnitentiam agunt. De occultis autem non iudicat ecclesia, sed Dei omnscii iudicio eos committit. Hinc hypocritæ, licet S. cœna sint indigni, adeoque excludi mereantur, non tamen excluduntur ab ecclesia, quia per hypocrisin, qua pietatem præ se ferunt, ecclesiæ non constant. Notorii autem peccatores arcentur, ideo, quod se rite probare nolunt. 2) Haeretici, in fundamento fidei errantes & substantialia huius sacramenti euertentes, qui crasso errore impliciti seipsos probare nec volunt, nec possunt. 3) Infantes, qui per aetatem mortem Domini annuntiare & seipsos probare nequeunt. 4) Obsessi a diabolo, qui perpetuo ab hoc hoste infestantur. 5) Furiosi, siue ex morbo delirantes, qui perpetuo concitantur furore. At, si obsessi aliquando immunes sint ab impetu diaboli, & furiosi lucida quaedam habeant amentia interualla, admittendi sunt ad sacrum hoc epulum, ut diuinissimis bonis, quae in sacra coena conferuntur, reficiantur. Quod attinet ad surdos & mutos, sequimur consilium LUTHERI: Si adsunt signa desiderii & paenitentiae, mutus & surdus non arceatur ab altari. Neque enim digni censentur communicantes, nisi paenitentes & fideles, qui fundamenta fidei saluificae, quantum saluti consequendae sufficit, posuere. Nec probatae tantum fidei, sed & probatae vitae, decet esse communicantes. Hinc diaconus in primitiua ecclesia eos acclamat: Sancta sanctis!


### Q. XVIII. Do hypocrites and unworthy communicants receive the body and blood of Christ in the use of the Holy Supper?

Hypocrites and all the unworthy, in the use of the Holy Supper, take the true body and blood of Christ: yet in such a way that they perceive neither consolation nor life from it, but rather that this taking yields to them for judgment and condemnation, if they are not converted and do penance. Obs.

Unworthy guests are not those who are weak in faith, faint-hearted, or troubled Christians. For the Supper of the Lord was instituted primarily for those weak in faith, yet penitent, so that they might perceive from it true consolation and the confirmation of their weak faith; but those are unworthy who approach the Supper of the Lord without true repentance, and contrition, and true faith, and without the purpose of amending their life.

Prob. 1) From 1 Cor. XI, 27. 29. Whoever shall have eaten this bread, or drunk the cup of the Lord unworthily: shall be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord. For he who eats and drinks unworthily, eats and drinks judgment to himself, in that he does not discern the body of the Lord. From which apostolic words we gather: Whoever, by unworthily eating the blessed bread and drinking the cup of the Lord, become guilty of the body and blood of Christ himself; they truly and really receive the body and blood of Christ in the Holy Supper: But unworthy communicants do so &c. Therefore.

You say: Guilt is contracted by the unworthy, not by unworthily eating the body of Christ itself, or unworthily drinking the blood; but by approaching the Holy Supper, by profaning the sacred symbols, and by treating them irreverently, insofar as the unworthy, with the profane impiety of their heart, do not even esteem the symbols worthily; just as he is considered guilty of lese-majesty who tears up and tramples upon a royal decree, even if he does not touch the king substantially.

Resp. 1) The unworthy do not become guilty of some act, and by drinking unworthily, which cannot happen unless the object to be eaten and drunk is presupposed, in which they sin. They become unworthy by not discerning the Lord's body; therefore this is exhibited to them to be eaten. 2) The comparison is dissimilar. For bread and wine is not a naked sign of the body and blood, like the decree of an absent king; but rather an instrument and vehicle by which the body of the Lord is conferred upon us. And he who tears up the king's decree does not touch the substance of the king himself; but only his majesty, office, and authority. Hence also he is never said to become guilty of the king himself, but of the royal majesty. But he who communicates unworthily is said to become guilty of the substance, guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.

2) From 1

Cor. X, 16. Whoever receives the blessed bread, by which the body of Christ is communicated, and partakes of the cup of the Lord, they also become partakers of the body and blood of the Lord: But unworthy communicants in the S. supper &c.

E. 3) From the reception of the entire sacrament. Whoever receives the entire sacrament of the eucharist, they receive not only the earthly thing, but also the heavenly. But unworthy communicants &c. The minor is proven: because faith does not constitute the essence of the sacrament, nor does it contribute to its integrity, but the integrity of the sacrament depends on the institution of Christ.

The antithesis is that of the Anabaptists and Schwenckfeldians, who deny that unworthy communicants receive the body and blood of Christ in the S. supper.

Their arguments are:

I. Whoever eats the body of Christ, they are spiritually vivified, Jo.

VI, 54: Hypocrites are not spiritually vivified: for they are destitute of faith, without which there is no spiritual life: Therefore. Resp.

The body of Christ is always vivifying in the first act; but in the second act hypocrites are not vivified by it; because they impede the operation of the body of Christ by their malicious hypocrisy.

II. If Christians cannot simultaneously drink the cup of the Lord and of demons, it follows that hypocrites cannot receive the body and blood of Christ: The antecedent is true, as Paul testifies 1 Cor. X, 20: Therefore also the consequent.

The consequence is proven; because hypocrites persuade themselves that they can approach the holy synaxis, and yet at the same time take part in feasts which the Gentiles had prepared from foods which they had sacrificed to their gods, or from idolothytes.

Resp.

The Apostle speaks of right, not of fact; but now the question is about the thing itself.

III. Christ and Belial cannot be together in the same man, as Paul testifies 2 Cor VI, 15. E. the body of Christ cannot be received by infidels.

The reason for the consequence is: because the devil dwells and works in infidels.

Resp.

Distinguish between the participation of the body and blood of Christ, and gracious indwelling. Hypocrites are indeed made partakers of the body and blood of Christ, but to judgment, because of the lack of faith: And therefore Christ does not graciously dwell in them.

IV. Whoever does not rightly use the sacrament of the supper, they do not receive the body and blood of Christ: Hypocrites do not rightly use the sacrament of the supper: E.

The major is evident: because outside of sacramental use the sacrament is not given.

Resp.

Distinguish between the formal use of the sacrament, and the final, or salutary use. Outside of formal use the sacrament is not given: but hypocrites do not obtain the salutary end and fruit, because to obtain this, besides the sacramental manducation, which is done by the mouth of the body, spiritual manducation is also required, which is done by the mouth of faith.

V. Infidels reject Christ: Therefore they do not receive his body in the S. supper.

Resp. Just as infidels receive the word of God with their bodily ears, which they nevertheless reject with their heart: so the same, using the S. supper externally, receive the body of Christ to judgment, because they do not receive Christ with true faith.

They receive with the mouth what they reject with the heart: because they do not reject Christ orally, but morally.

VI. The impious are dogs and swine, and therefore not worthy that the body and blood of Christ should be offered to them, Matth.

VII, 6. Resp.

1) The notoriously impious are to be clearly barred from the use of the supper; but hypocrites feign piety, no differently than Judas Iscariot, who was admitted by Christ to the S. supper.

This is what Luke clearly records. When he had recited the words of institution, he adds c. XXII, 21. But behold, the hand of him who betrays me is with me at the table.

2) The impious are not worthy of the sun and daily bread, upon whom, however, the heavenly Father confers many benefits.

VII. We being many are one bread and one body, since we all partake of one bread: Infidels are not one body with the faithful: E. they do not [partake] of the body of Christ with them.

partake. Resp. 1) That infidels participate in the one eucharistic bread, which is the communion of the body of Christ, is certain. 2) The major premise speaks of the mystical body, which is the church, which is either visible, the assembly of Christians, in which hypocrites are mixed with the faithful, or is invisible, by reason of faith & election. Hypocrites belong to the visible body of the church.

Latin:

Hypocritae omnesque indigni, in vsu S. coenae verum corpus, & sanguinem Christi sumunt: Ita tamen, ut nec consolationem, nec vitam inde percipiant, sed potius ut illa sumtio ipsis ad iudicium & condemnationem cedat, si non conuertantur & paenitentiam agant.

Obs. Indigni conuiuae non sunt infirmi in fide, pusillanimes, aut perturbati Christiani. Coena enim Domini in primis propter infirmos in fide, paenitentes tamen, instituta est, ut ex ea veram consolationem & imbecillis fidei suae confirmationem percipiant; sed indigni sunt, qui sine vera paenitentia, & contritione, & vera fide, & absque proposito vitam emendandi ad coenam Domini accedunt.

Prob. 1) Ex 1 Cor. XI, 27. 29. Quisquis comederit panem hunc, aut biberit poculum Domini indigne: Reus erit corporis & sanguinis Domini. Qui enim comedit & bibit indigne, iudicium sibi ipsi comedit & bibit, eo, quod non discernit corpus Domini. E quibus verbis apostolicis colligimus: Quicunque indigne manducando panem benedictum, & bibendo poculum Domini, rei fiunt ipsius corporis & sanguinis Christi; illi in S. coena vere & realiter accipiunt corpus & sanguinem Christi: Atqui indigni communicantes &c. Ergo.

Dicis: Reatus ab indignis contrahitur, non ipsum corpus Christi indigne manducando, aut sanguinem indigne bibendo; sed ad S. coenam accedendo, symbola sacra profanando, & irreuerenter tractando, quatenus indigni profana cordis impietate ne symbola quidem condigne aestimant; prout laese maiestatis reus censetur, qui diploma regium proscindit & conculcat, etsi regem substantialiter non attingat.

Resp. 1) Indigni non fiunt rei alicuius actus, & bibendo indigne, quod fieri nequit, nisi praesupponatur obiectum manducandum, & bibendum, in quod peccant. Fiunt indigni, non discernendo dominicum corpus; ergo hoc illis manducandum exhibetur. 2) Simile est dissimile. Nam panis & vinum non est nudum signum corporis & sanguinis, prout diploma regis absentis; sed vna organum & vehiculum, quo corpus Domini nobis confertur. Nec proscindens diploma regis ipsam substantiam regis attingit; sed solum maiestatem, officium & auctoritatem illius. Hinc etiam nunquam dicitur reus ipsius regis fieri, sed maiestatis regiae. At indigne communicans dicitur reus substantiae fieri, reus corporis & sanguinis domini.

2) Ex 1

Cor. X, 16. Quicunque panem benedictum, quo communicatur corpus Christi, accipiunt, & calicem Domini participant, illi etiam corporis & sanguinis Domini participes fiunt: Atqui comituae indigni in S. coena &c.

E. 3) Ex integri sacramenti perceptione. Quicunque integrum sacramentum eucharistiae accipiunt, illi non tantum rem terrenam, sed & coelestem accipiunt. Atqui indigni conuinae &c. Minor probatur: quia fides non constituit essentiam sacramenti, nec ad eius integritatem facit, sed dependet integritas sacramenti ab institutione Christi.

Antithesis est Anabaptistarum & Schwenckfeldianorum, negantium, indignos comiuas corpus & sanguinem Christi in S. coena accipere.

Quorum argumenta sunt:

I. Quicunque comedunt corpus Christi, illi spiritualiter viuificantur, Io.

VI, 54: Hypocritae spiritualiter non viuificantur: destituuntur enim fide, fine qua non est vita spiritualis: Ergo. Resp.

Corpus Christi semper est viuificum actu primo; actu secundo autem ab eodem non viuificantur hypocritae; quia operationem corporis Christi malitiosa sua hypocrisi impediunt.

II. Si Christiani non possunt simul bibere calicem Domini & daemoniorum, sequitur, quod hypocritae non possint accipere corpus & sanguinem Christi: Antecedens est verum, teste Paullo 1 Cor. X, 20: Ergo & consequens.

Consequentia probatur; quia hypocritae sibi persuadent, se posse adire sacram synaxin, & tamen simul interesse conuiuiis, quae parauerat gentiles ex cibis, quos diis suis sacrificauerant, siue ex idolothytis.

Resp.

Apostolus loquitur de iure, non de facto; iam autem quaeritur de re ipsa.

III. Christus & Belial non possunt simul in eodem esse homine, teste Paullo 2 Cor VI, 15. E. corpus Christi non potest recipi ab infidelibus.

Ratio consequentiae est: quia in infidelibus habitat & operatur diabolus.

Resp.

Dist. inter participationem corporis & sanguinis Christi, & gratiosam inhabitationem. Hypocritae redduntur quidem participes corporis & sanguinis Christi, sed ad iudicium, ob defectum fidei: Ideoque Christus gratiose in ipsis non habitat.

IV. Quicunque non recte vntuntur sacramento coenae, illi corpus sanguinemque Christi non accipiunt: Hypocritae non recte vtuntur sacramento coenae: E.

Maior constat: quia extra vsum sacramentalem non datur sacramentum.

Resp.

Dist. inter vsum sacramenti formalem, & finalem, siue salutarem. Extra vsum formalem non datur sacramentum: sed salutarem finem & fructum non obtinent hypocritae, quia ad hunc obtinendum praeter manducationem sacramentalem, quae fit ore corporis, requiritur etiam manducatio spiritualis, quae fit ore fidei.

V. Infideles reiiciunt Christum: Ergo corpus ipsius in S. coena non accipiunt.

Resp. Sicut infideles verbum Dei auribus corporeis accipiunt, quod tamen corde reiiciunt: ita iidem vtentes externe S. coena, corpus Christi accipiunt ad iudicium, quia vera fide Christum non recipiunt.

Ore accipiunt, quod corde respuunt: quia non oraliter, sed moraliter Christum reiiciunt.

VI. Impii sunt canes & porci, adeoque non digni, quibus corpus & sanguis Christi porrigatur, Matth.

VII, 6. Resp.

1) Notorie impii ab vsu coenae plane arcendi sunt; sed hypocritae pietatem simulant, haud secus ac Iudas Iuchariotes, qui a Christo ad S. coenam admissus est.

Id quod clare memorat Lucas. Cum recitasset verba institutionis, addit c. XXII, 21. Veruntamen ecce manus prodentis me mecum est in mensa.

2) Impii non sunt digni sole & pane quotidiano, in quos tamen Pater coelestis multa beneficia confert.

VII. Vnus panis & vnum corpus multi sumus, quoniam de vno pane omnes participamus: Infideles non sunt vnum corpus cum fidelibus: E. non de corpore Christi cum illis Christi cum illis

participant. Resp. 1) Infideles de vno pane eucharistico, qui est κοινωνία corporis Christi, participare, certum est. 2) Maior loquitur de corpore mystico, quod est ecclesia, quae vel est visibilis, coetus Christianorum, in quo hypocritae fidelibus sunt mixti, vel est invisibilis, ratione fidei & electionis. Ad corpus ecclesiae visibile pertinent hypocritae.


### XIX. Is the sacrament of the supper to be offered to the laity under both species?

Not only to the clergy, but also to the laity is the sacrament of the supper to be offered under both species.

Prob. 1) Whoever were commanded by Christ in the institution of the eucharist to eat the blessed bread, the same were also commanded to drink the blessed wine: But all the Apostles, and in their name all adult believers, were commanded by Christ in the institution of the eucharist to eat the blessed bread. Therefore, all the Apostles, and in their name all adult believers, were commanded to drink the blessed wine. The major premise is clear: for to the same ones to whom Christ said: Eat, he likewise said: Drink. Nay, he even expressly added: Drink ye all of this! Matt. XXVI, 27. The truth of the minor premise concerning the Apostles is evident: For to all these the Lord says: Take, drink. Mark adds, ch. XIV, 23, they all drank of it. It is also evident concerning all adult believers. The Apostles, whom Christ commanded to eat and drink, represented either only the clergy, or both the clergy and the laity. But not only the clergy; because thus no Christian layman would have to receive the sacrament of the supper, either under one or under both species: Therefore, they represented all adult believers, whom Christ under the name of the Apostles commanded to eat the consecrated bread and drink the consecrated wine .

I. Communion under both species was indeed instituted by Christ, but not commanded. Not everything that God instituted, he commanded to all. God instituted marriage through imperative words, yet he did not command it to all. Resp. Although institution and divine command differ; if, however, the persons for whom the institution was made are added, the institution is equal to a command, especially if it is done through imperative words, such as are here: Eat! Drink! For marriage also is not only instituted by God, but also commanded to all persons who are fit for marriage, and do not have the gift of continence, to avoid fornication and all impurity.

II. The Apostles were commanded to eat, as were all the faithful, but in being commanded to drink, they represented only the priests. Resp. a) If Christ had regarded the Apostles in another respect when he said: Eat: certainly he himself, or Paul, repeating the dominical institution, 1 Cor. XI, would have at least made a slight indication of that double respect. b) Christ in the first eucharist did not regard the Apostles as priests, but as communicants.

Prob. 2) Paul repeats the words of the institution, 1 Cor. XI, 23, where he exhorts all who can prove themselves to eat of this bread and drink of this cup, v. 28.

Prob. 3) The same Apostle 1 Cor. X, 14, says: Wherefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry. I speak as to wise men; judge ye what I say. The cup of blessing, which we bless, we say, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? Where note: 1) That Paul addresses all the faithful Corinthians, as much those teaching as those learning, and dissuades them by an argument (among others) taken from the communion of the entire supper. 2) That he himself distinguishes the blessed cup from the broken bread, calling the former the κοινωνία [communion] of the blood, and the latter that of the body of Christ.

The antithesis is that of the Papists, who decree that the blessed cup is not to be offered to the laity.

Who rely on the following arguments:

I. Whoever receives the blood of Christ under the consecrated bread, to them the blessed wine is not to be offered: But the laity &c. Therefore. The major is proven: because those who have received the blood of Christ under the blessed bread have no need to receive the blood of Christ under another symbol. The minor is evident: since Christ’s body is not bloodless. Resp. 1) If this argument is valid, it can be inferred that not even to the clergy should the blessed wine be offered, since they too receive the body of Christ full of blood under the blessed bread. 2) Distinguish between the natural union of the body and blood of Christ, and the sacramental union of the body and blood of Christ under distinct symbols, instituted by Christ. If you look at the natural union, the body of Christ is never without blood, and the blood is never without the body of Christ; yet if you consider the sacramental union, it pleased the Savior to give and distribute to us His body under a distinct symbol, and His blood under a distinct symbol, the former for eating, the latter for drinking. But we ought not to be wise beyond that which is written and instituted by Christ, 1 Cor. IV, 7.

II. Whoever has approved the celebration of the Holy Supper under one kind both by words and by deeds, he did not will that the same must necessarily be celebrated under both kinds: But Christ &c. Therefore. The minor is proven. Christ approved the celebration of the Holy Supper under one kind by words, John VI, 50. seq., where He promises eternal life four times to those who eat His flesh, with no mention made of drinking. 2) He approved the celebration of the Holy Supper under one kind by deed, Luke XXIV, 30, where Christ offered the sacrament to two disciples at the inn in Emmaus under the sole species of bread.

Resp. In John VI, it is a matter of spiritual eating: in Luke XXIV, it is a matter of the common breaking of bread, or a charitable meal, not a Eucharistic one. For the same words are read concerning the feeding of the people, Matt. XIV, 19, Mark VI, 41. Grant that Luke XXIV is to be understood as the celebration of the Holy Supper; yet the positing of one will not be the exclusion of the other. The breaking of bread does not exclude the distribution of wine.

III. There are abstainers who cannot taste even a single drop of wine. To these the sacrament of the supper must be exhibited under one kind. Resp. 1) Those abstainers are few and rare, in consideration of whom the blessed wine is not to be snatched away from all the laity. 2) Abstainers are to be well instructed, so that by true faith they may spiritually eat and drink Christ, with all His benefits.

IV. The Catholic Church has approved communion under one kind not without grave causes; namely, a) because in all places there is not an abundance of wine: b) because reverence for the sacrament is to be feared, if a single drop should fall into a beard, on clothing, or on the ground: c) yet it has meanwhile granted a wiping cup. Resp. a) In every place there is as much abundance of wine as is required for the celebration of the Holy Supper. b) The blessed cup, outside the use of drinking, is not the κοινωνία [communion] of the blood of Christ. c) The wiping cup is a common cup, not a blessed cup.

Latin:

Non tantum clericis, sed etiam laicis sacramentum cenae sub utraque specie porrigendum est.

Prob. 1) Quicumque a Christo in institutione eucharistiae iussi sunt edere panem benedictum, iidem etiam iussi sunt bibere vinum benedictum: Atqui Apostoli omnes, & sub eorum nomine fideles adulti omnes, a Christo in institutione eucharistiae iussi sunt edere panem benedictum. E. Apostoli omnes, & sub eorum nomine fideles adulti omnes, iussi sunt bibere vinum benedictum. Maior claret: iisdem enim, quibus Christus dixit: Edite, similiter dixit: Bibite. Quin expresse etiam adiecit: Bibite ex hoc omnes! Matth. XXVI, 27. Veritas minoris de Apostolis patet: His enim omnibus Dominus ait: Accipite, bibite. Addit Marcus c. XIV, 23. biberunt ex hoc omnes. Patet etiam de fidelibus adultis omnibus. Apostoli, quos Christus iussit edere & bibere, repraesentarant vel tantum clericos, vel tam clericos, quam laicos. At non tantum clericos; quia sic nullus laicus christianus accipere deberet sacramentum cenae, vel sub una, vel sub utraque specie: E. repraesentarant fideles adultos omnes, quos Christus sub nomine Apostolorum iussit edere panem consecratum & bibere vinum consecratum .

Dicis: I. Communio sub utraque specie a Christo quidem est instituta, sed non praecepta. Non omnia, quae Deus instituit, omnibus mandauit. Matrimonium Deus per verba imperantia instituit, neque tamen omnibus mandauit. Resp. Licet institutio & mandatum diuinum differant; si tamen addantur personae, ob quas institutio facta est, institutio mandato par est, in primis si fiat per verba imperantia, qualia hic sunt, edite! bibite! Nam & matrimonium a Deo non tantum institutum, sed etiam mandatum est omnibus personis, quae ad coniugium sunt aptae, & continentiae donum non habent ad vitandum scortationem, & omnem impuritatem.

II. Apostoli iussi edere, fideles omnes, sed iussi bibere, solos sacerdotes repraesentarant. Resp. a) Si Christus alio respectu Apostolos intuitus esset, cum diceret: Edite: vtique ipse, vel Paullus, institutionem dominicam repetens, 1 Cor. XI. saltem leue duplicis illius respectus indicium fecisset. b) Christus in prima eucharistia Apostolos non respexit vt sacerdotes, sed vt communicantes.

Prob. 2) Paullus repetit verba institutionis, 1 Cor. XI, 23. ubi omnes, qui se probare possunt, adhortatur, vt edant ex hoc pane, & bibant ex hoc poculo, v. 28.

Prob. 3) Idem Apostolus 1 Cor. X, 14. ait: Quapropter, dilecti mei, fugite ab idololatria. Tanquam prudentibus dico: Iudicate vos, quod dico. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nedicimus, nonne est communicatio sanguinis Christi? Vbi obs. 1) Quod Paullus compellet omnes Corinthios fideles, tam docentes, quam discentes, eosque dehortetur argumento (inter alia) sumto ab integræ cœnæ communione. 2) Quod ipse distinguat poculum benedictum a pane fracto, illud sanguinis, hunc corporis Christi κοινωνίαν vocans.

Antithesis est Pontificiorum, statuentium, laicis poculum benedictum non esse porrigendum.

Qui sequentibus innituntur argumentis:

I. Quicunque sub pane consecrato sanguinem Christi accipiunt, illis vinum benedictum non est porrigendum: Atqui laici &c. E. Maior probatur: quia, qui sub pane benedicto sanguinem Christi acceperunt, non opus habent, vt sub alio symbolo sanguinem Christi accipiant. Minor constat: quoniam Christi corpus non est exsangue. Resp. 1) Si hoc argumentum validum est, inferri potest, ne clericis quidem vinum benedictum esse porrigendum, cum etiam illi sub pane benedicto corpus Christi sanguinis plenum accipiant. 2) Dist. inter vnionem naturalem corporis & sanguinis Christi, & inter vnionem sacramentalem corporis & sanguinis Christi sub distinctis symbolis, a Christo institutis. Si spectes vnionem naturalem; corpus Christi nunquam est sine sanguine, & sanguis nunquam est sine corpore Christi; attamen si consideres vnionem sacramentalem, placuit Saluatori, sub distincto symbolo corpus suum, & sub distincto symbolo sanguinem suum, illud ad edendum, huic ad bibendum nobis dare & distribuere. Non debemus autem sapere vltra id, quod scriptum & a Christo institutum est, 1 Cor. IV, 7.

II. Quicunque & verbis, & factis approbauit celebrationem S. cœnæ sub vna specie, ille noluit eandem necessario sub vtraque specie esse celebrandam: Atqui Christus &c. E. Minor prob. Christus celebrationem S. cœnæ sub vna specie verbis approbauit, Io. VI, 50. seq. vbi quater promittit vitam æternam carnem suam manducantibus, nulla facta potationis mentione. 2) Facto autem approbauit celebrationem S. cœnæ sub vna specie, Luc. XXIV, 30. vbi Christus duobus discipulis in hospitio Emauntico sub sola specie panis sacramentum porrexit.

Resp. Io. VI. agitur de manducatione spirituali: Luc. XXIV. agitur de fractione panis vulgari, aut refectione caritatiua, non eucharistica. Eadem quippe verba leguntur de cibatione populi, Matth. XIV, 19. Marc. VI, 41. Fac, Luc. XXIV. intelligendam esse celebrationem S. cœnæ; vnius tamen positio non erit alterius exclusio. Fractio panis non excludit distributionem vini.

III. Dantur abstemii, qui ne vnam quidem guttulam vini gustare possunt. His sacramentum cœnæ sub vna specie exhibendum est. Resp. 1) Abstemii illi sunt pauci & rari, quorum intuitu non omnibus laicis furripiendum est vinum benedictum. 2) Abstemii bene erudiendi sunt, vt vera fide spiritualiter edant, bibantque Christum, cum omnibus ipsius beneficiis.

IV. Ecclesia catholica non fine grauibus caussis communionem sub vna specie approbauit; sc. a) quia non in omnibus locis datur copia vini: b) quia metuenda est irreuerentia sacramenti, si vna guttula in barbam, vestem aut terram decideret: c) concessit tamen interim poculum absterforium. Resp. a) Vbiuis locorum tanta habetur copia vini, quanta ad celebrationem S. cœnæ requiritur. b) Poculum benedictum, extra vsum bibitionis, non est κοινωνία sanguinis Christi. c) Poculum absterforium est poculum vulgare, non poculum benedictum.


### XIX. Is the sacrament of the supper to be offered to the laity under both species?: Quest. XX. What is the end of the Eucharist?

Quest. XX. What is the end of the Eucharist?

The end of the Eucharist is: a) the remembrance and proclamation of the passion and death of Christ, which is performed by faith and thanksgiving: b) the sealing of evangelical grace: c) the mutual love of those communicating.

Christ, the institutor of the Holy Supper, says in Luke ch. XXII, 19: Do this in remembrance of me. Paul, repeating these words, 1 Cor. XI, 24. 25. adds, v. 26: For as often as you eat this bread, and drink of this cup, you proclaim the Lord's death till he comes. The remembrance and proclamation of Christ's death is made by true faith, by which we weigh and believe that he offered his own body, which he holds out to us to be eaten with the blessed bread in the Holy Supper, as a victim for us on the altar of the cross, and that he offered his own blood, which he exhibits to us to be drunk in the blessed cup, for us, that he might obtain for us the grace of God and the remission of sins. And thus the application of faith, insofar as it is directed toward the body of Christ, delivered to death for us, is called the spiritual eating of the body of Christ, and insofar as it is directed toward the blood of Christ, shed for us, it is called the spiritual drinking of the blood of Christ, of both of which see John VI, 35. ff.

Without this spiritual eating, the oral eating does not receive the saving fruit of the Eucharist: because all spiritual benefits are received by faith.

Meanwhile, however, the oral eating of the body of Christ is a means promoting the spiritual eating and enjoyment of Christ: just as the bodily reception of the divine word into the ears is a means promoting the spiritual knowledge of the mind, cf. D. CHRIST. FRANCKIE E. AW. p. 562. Prob. b. To this end Christ holds out to us his body to be eaten, and his blood to be drunk, so that evangelical grace, or divine grace promised and offered to us in the Gospel, may be applied to us individually and sealed: This is what becomes known more fully to us as we ponder the acts of the applying grace.

God promised, through regenerating grace, to give faith to all, Acts XVII, 31. Which regenerating grace, and its effect, namely faith, God confirms, strengthens, and increases through the eucharistic sacrament. For he who receives the body and blood of the Lord, he can most firmly establish that the evangelical promise pertains to him individually. For he receives here and now the body of Christ, held out to him individually, the Lord himself saying: Take, eat, this is my body which is given for you.

Then, through justifying grace, God forgives the sins of the reborn, and imputes the righteousness of Christ: Which justifying grace and remission of sins is sealed by the sacrament of the Supper. For when we receive in the sacrament of the Supper that very body of Christ, which was delivered to death for us, and that very blood, which was shed for us for the remission of sins, we are thereby made most certain, as by a seal of the New Testament, that the remission of sins, obtained for us who believe in Christ by the delivery of the body and the shedding of the blood of Christ, has been granted and applied. Through indwelling grace God unites himself graciously with us, which mystical union is rendered closer and firmer through the eating of the body and the drinking of the blood of Christ.

He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, abides in me, and I in him, says Christ, John VI, 56. Truly it is an indication of ineffable love that Christ, not content to have dwelt in us spiritually through faith, comes to us furthermore in his body and blood through a special approximation, and thus joins himself to our body, just as to our soul. Through renewing grace, spiritual powers are conferred upon us, so that we may bear the fruits of righteousness.

In the Holy Supper we are more closely united to Christ, just as to a vine, so that in him, as branches, we may bear more abundant fruit, John XV, 5. Through preserving grace we are kept from sins, and refreshed by consolation.

The sacrament of the Supper is a medicine against daily sins, in the judgment of AMBROSE, L. V. de Sacram. c. 4. And just as a complete refreshment, or nutrition of bodies, consists of food, which is dry nourishment, and drink, which is moist nourishment: So in the Eucharist Christ is proposed to us as food and as drink, lest we think anything is lacking to us for our complete sustenance, or spiritual nutrition, in the opinion of AUGUSTINE, tract.

XXV. in Ioann. Through glorifying grace, blessed immortality is conferred upon us, the symbols or pledges of which are the body and blood of the Lord, mini, taken in the H. Supper. He who eats my flesh, and drinks my blood, lives forever, says the Savior, John VI, 54. We have here the body of the Lord, as the root of the resurrection, says ATHANASIUS in Theodoret, Book I, ch. 22.

Prob. ch. Through the holy supper, being united to Christ the head, they are also united among themselves, as members of a mystical body, and thus the eucharist is the foundation of charity between us and our neighbor. Paul reaches this end of the H. Supper when he says in 1 Cor. X, 17: Because we being many are one bread, and one body: For we all partake of one bread. Whence it is also a mark of ecclesiastical communion, and a token of that church with which we communicate in faith.

The antithesis is that of the Socinians, Arminians, and Anabaptists, who deny that faith is confirmed through the eucharist, but maintain that it is only a ceremony, instituted in commemoration of the death of the Lord. Their arguments are: I. The eating of bread and drinking of wine can work nothing in the mind of man: Therefore, it cannot confirm faith in the mind. Resp. The eating and drinking of common food can work nothing in the mind of man; but the eating of the body of Christ, and the drinking of the blood of Christ, is the nourishment of the soul, and the firmament of faith.

II. The H. Supper was instituted for the commemoration of the death of Christ: Therefore, not for the confirmation of faith. Resp. That commemoration is not bare, but ἐνεργητικὴ [energetic], joined with a fiducial application.

III. It is possible that someone may approach the H. Supper with firm faith: Therefore, his faith is not confirmed through the H. Supper. Resp. No faith is so firm that it does not receive increments, or that it does not sometimes waver. The Apostles, confirmed in faith, sought a more abundant confirmation; Luke XVII, 5. And to Abraham, the father of believers, circumcision was a seal of the righteousness of faith, Rom. IV, 11.

Latin:

Quæst. XX. Quis est finis eucharistiæ?

Finis eucharistiæ est: a) recordatio & annuntiatio passionis & mortis Christi, quæ fide & gratiarum actione peragitur: b) gratiæ euangelicæ obsignatio: c) mutuæ communicantium dilectio.

Christus, institutor S. coenae, apud Lucam c. XXII, 19. inquit: Hoc facite in mei recordationem. Quae verba repetens Paullus, 1 Cor. XI, 24. 25. addit, v. 26. Quotiescunque enim comederitis panem hunc, & ex hoc poculo biberitis, mortem domini annuntiate, donec venerit.

Fit recordatio & annuntiatio mortis Christi vera fide, qua expendimus & credimus, quod corpus suum, quod cum pane benedicto in S. coena nobis comedendum porrigit, victimam pro nobis obtulerit in ara crucis, & quod sanguinem suum, quem in benedicto poculo nobis bibendum exhibet, pro nobis obtulerit, vt gratiam Dei & remissionem peccatorum nobis impetraret. Atque ita applicatio fidei, quatenus fertur in corpus Christi, pro nobis in mortem traditum, dicitur manducatio spiritualis corporis Christi, & quatenus fertur in sanguinem Christi pro nobis effusum, dicitur spiritualis bibitio sanguinis Christi, de qua vtraque vid. Io. VI, 35. seqq. Sine hac spirituali manducatione oralis manducatio salutarem eucharistiae fructum non capit: quia omnia beneficia spiritualia recipiuntur fide.

Interim tamen oralis manducatio corporis Christi est medium promouens spiritualem manducationem & fruitionem Christi: sicut corporalis receptio verbi diuini intra aures est medium promouens cognitionem mentis spiritualem, conf. D. CHRIST. FRANCKIE E. AW. p. 562. Prob. b. Eum in finem nobis Christus corpus suum comedendum, & sanguinem suum bibendum porrigit, vt gratia euangelica, siue gratia diuina in euangelio nobis promissa & oblata, applicetur nobis in indiuiduo & obsignetur: Id quod pensitantibus nobis actus gratiae applicatricis innotescit vberius.

Promisit Deus, per gratiam regenerantem omnibus dare fidem, Act. XVII, 31. Quam gratiam regenerantem, eiusque effectum, scil. fidem, Deus confirmat, roborat, auget per sacramentum eucharisticum. Etenim qui accipit corpus & sanguinem Domini, ille firmissime statuere potest, promissionem euangelicam ad se in indiuiduo pertinere. Accipit quippe hic & nunc corpus Christi, sibi in indiuiduo porrectum, ipso Domino dicente: Accipe, ede, hoc est corpus meum pro te traditum.

Deinde per gratiam iustificantem Deus renatis peccata remittit, & iustitiam Christi imputat: Quae gratia iustificans & remissio peccatorum sacramento coenae obsignatur. Nam quando illud ipsum corpus Christi, quod pro nobis in mortem traditum est, & illum ipsum sanguinem, qui pro nobis fusus est in remissionem peccatorum, accipimus in sacramento coenae, inde tanquam sigillo N. T. maxime certi reddimur, remissionem peccatorum traditione corporis & effusione sanguinis Christi partam nobis, qui in Christum credimus, donatam & applicatam esse. Per gratiam inhabitantem Deus se nobiscum gratiose vnit, quae vnio mystica per manducationem corporis & bibitionem sanguinis Christi arctior & firmior redditur.

Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, in me manet, & ego in ipso, ait Christus, Io. VI, 56. Profecto ineffabilis caritatis indicium est, quod Christus, non contentus habitasse in nobis spiritualiter per fidem, insuper corpore & sanguine suo per specialem approximationem ad nos veniat, & sic corpori pariter, ac animae nostrae se coniungat. Per gratiam renouantem conferuntur nobis vires spirituales, vt feramus fructus iustitiae.

In S. coena arctius vnimur Christo, veluti viti, vt in eo, tanquam palmites, fructum copiosiorem feramus, Io. XV, 5. Per gratiam conseruantem a peccatis preseruamur, & consolatione reficimur.

Sacramentum coenae est medicina contra peccata quotidiana, iudice AMBROSIO L. V. de Sacram. c. 4. Et quemadmodum integra refectio, seu nutritio corporum cibo, qui est alimentum siccum, & potu, qui est alimentum humidum, constat: Ita in eucharistia proponitur nobis Christus, vt esca & vt potus, ne deesse nobis quidquam putemus ad integram alimoniam nostram, siue nutritionem spiritualem, censente AVGVSTINO tract.

XXV. in Ioann. Per gratiam glorificantem beata nobis confertur immortalitas, cuius symbola aut pignora sunt corpus & sanguinis Domini, mini, sumta in S. cœna. Qui edit carnem meam, & bibit sanguinem meum, viuit in æternum, ait Saluator Io. VI, 54. Corpus Domini nos hic habemus, tanquam radicem resurrectionis, inquit ATHANASIVS apud Theodor. L. I. c. 22.

Prob. c. Per sacram cœnam capiti Christo vniti, etiam inter se, velut membra corporis mystici, vniuntur, adeoque eucharistia est fundamentum caritatis inter nos & proximum nostrum. Hunc finem S. cœnæ attingit Paullus, cum 1 Cor. X, 17. ait: Quia vnus panis, vnum corpus multi sumus: Omnes enim ex vno pane participamus. Vnde etiam est nota communionis ecclesiasticæ, & tessera illius ecclesiæ, cum qua in fide communicamus.

Antithesis est Socinianorum, Arminianorum, & Anabaptistarum, negantium, fidem per eucharistiam confirmari, sed statuentium, ipsam tantum esse cærimoniam, institutam in commemorationem mortis Domini. Quorum argumenta sunt: I. Esus panis & potus vini in animo hominis nihil operari potest: E. non potest in animo confirmare fidem. Resp. Esus & potus vulgaris in animo hominis nihil operari potest; at esus corporis Christi, & potus sanguinis Christi est nutrimentum animæ, & firmamentum fidei.

II. Instituta est S. cœna propter commemorationem mortis Christi: E. non propter confirmationem fidei. Resp. Commemoratio illa non est nuda, sed ἐνεργητικὴ, cum fiduciali applicatione coniuncta.

III. Fieri potest, vt quis firma fide accedat ad S. cœnam: E. illius fides per S. cœnam non confirmatur. Resp. Nulla fides tam firma est, quæ non incrementa capiat, aut quæ non aliquando vacillet. Apostoli, in fide confirmati, vberiorem expetebant confirmationem; Luc. XVII, 5. Et Abrahamo, credentium patri, circumcisio erat sigillum iustitiæ fidei, Rom. IV, 11.


### XIX. Is the sacrament of the supper to be offered to the laity under both species?: Quest. XXI. Is the mass a sacrifice properly so called?

Quest. XXI. Is the mass a sacrifice properly so called?

The mass is not a sacrifice, properly so called, propitiatory, for the sins of the living and the dead.

Obs. I. There is a distinction between the Christian mass and the superstitious or idolatrous one. The former is the legitimate celebration of the H. Supper: The latter is defined by the Papists as an unbloody sacrifice of the N. T., propitiatory and satisfactory, in which a priest properly so called and the sole communicant, upon an altar properly so called, offers to the heavenly Father the same Christ, and the same host, which was offered on the cross, under the species of bread and wine, for the sins, punishments, satisfactions, and other necessities of the living and the dead, not yet fully purged in purgatory.

Obs. II. The name of sacrifice is taken either improperly or properly. It is taken improperly 1) for every work that is done so that we may adhere to God in a holy society, related to that end by which we can be truly blessed, as AUGUSTINE speaks, Book X, de C. D. ch. 6. 2) for the worship of the N. T. and the preaching of the gospel, Rom. XV, 16. Phil. II, 17. 3) for beneficence and offices of charity toward one's neighbor, Phil. IV, 8. Hebr. XIII, 16. 4) for prayers and thanksgivings directed to God, Hebr. XIII, 16. Apoc. V, 8. A sacrifice properly so called is either מנחה [minchah], an oblation from inanimate things, both solid, e.g., from bread, salt, incense, and liquid, which were called libations: or it is זבח [zebach], a bloody sacrifice, by which, by divine command, living things are immolated in honor of God. We do not deny that the mass, or the celebration of the eucharist, can be called a sacrifice improperly; because 1) it is a work that is done so that we may adhere to God in a holy society: 2) it is a part of the worship of the N. T., not the last: 3) formerly, when the eucharist was celebrated, gifts were accustomed to be offered which would go to the use of the ministers of the church and the poor: 4) it is joined to the H. the administration of the Supper with prayers and thanksgivings: 5) is instituted in memory of the sacrifice of Christ offered on the altar of the cross.

Obj. III. A distinction must be made between a sacrifice taken materially and formally. If we take it materially, in the Eucharist there is the same sacrifice in number as that which was on the cross, or the thing and substance are absolutely the same; the same, I say, victim or host. But if we take it formally, or for the act of sacrificing, then, even if it is one and the same victim in number, yet it is not the same action or immolation that takes place in the Eucharist as the immolation that was performed on the cross. For on the cross, the offering was made through the true passion and death of a living thing immolated, without which a sacrifice properly so-called can in no way exist; but in the Eucharist, the offering is made through prayers and through the commemoration of the death, or of the sacrifice offered on the cross.

Proof of our assertion: 1) Whatever animate thing is properly sacrificed is killed and destroyed by death: The animate body of Christ is not killed in the mass, nor is it destroyed by death: Therefore, the body of Christ is not properly sacrificed in the mass. The major is clear from the nature of a sacrifice properly so-called. The minor is clear from the testimony of Paul, Rom.

VI, 9. 2) That sacrifice which must be repeated is imperfect and argues an imperfect priesthood: The sacrifice of Christ is neither imperfect, nor does it argue an imperfect priesthood: Therefore, it must not be repeated. The major and minor are evident from Heb. VII, 27; ch.

IX, 25, 26. 3) If the mass were a sacrifice properly so-called, it would have been instituted by Christ at the last supper. But it was not instituted therein. Therefore, it is not a sacrifice properly so-called. The reason for the consequence is: because according to the Papists, the mass does not differ from the Eucharist regarding the thing itself: however, the Eucharist was only instituted at the last supper. The consequent is proven: because the institution of a sacrifice properly so-called, by which an animate thing is offered, implies a command to slaughter that which is to be offered.

But no command concerning the slaughtering of Christ is contained in the institution of the Supper, neither explicitly nor implicitly. 4) According to the mind of the adversaries, the mass is an unbloody sacrifice. From which we conclude: No propitiatory sacrifice, properly so-called, is made without blood, Heb. IX, 22. But the mass-sacrifice is made without blood.

Therefore, it is not a propitiatory sacrifice, properly so-called. 5) No sacrament can be a sacrifice: The Eucharist is a sacrament. Therefore. The major is proven: because in sacraments God offers and confers His grace to men; but in sacrifices, men offer certain gifts to God . The antithesis is that of the Papists, who maintain that Christ is sacrificed in the mass properly, but in an unbloody manner. Their stronger arguments are: I. If the sacrifice of the new testament must be daily and universal, it follows that the mass-sacrifice is not to be called into doubt (for this is daily and universal): The antecedent is true, by the witness of Malachi ch. I, 11. Therefore, the consequent is also.

Resp. The cited passage is not understood as an expiatory sacrifice, properly so-called, but a spiritual sacrifice, namely a spiritual sacrifice, namely a spiritual sacrifice,

namely the preaching of the gospel in the whole world, Rom. XV, 16. a sacrifice of charity, or of beneficence, a sacrifice of prayers and a host of praise.

II. Whoever is a priest in the manner of Melchizedek, his office is to be performed by offering bread and blood: But Christ &c. Hebr. V, 6. Therefore. The major is proved: because Melchizedek is said to have sacrificed and offered bread and wine to Abraham, Gen. XIV, 18. Resp. 1) Melchizedek did not sacrifice, but brought bread and wine to refresh Abraham and his soldiers. 2) Christ sacrificed once, and immolated himself on the altar of the cross, Hebr. IX, 12.

Instance: But the sacrifice of Christ must be eternal; because he is a priest in the manner of Melchizedek forever. Resp. The sacrifice of Christ performed on the altar of the cross is eternal, not on account of perennial reiteration, but on account of perpetual value, Hebr. X, 10.

III. No true religion can be without a constant and perennial sacrifice. But the Christian religion is a true religion. Therefore. The major is proved because the Israelite religion was not without daily sacrifices: Nay, even the gentiles sacrificed. Resp. 1) The Christian religion relies on the sacrifice of Christ, which, as to value, is eternal, Hebr. X, 14. 2) The Christian religion is exercised by daily eucharistic sacrifices, or hosts of praise and prayers.

Latin:

Quæst. XXI. Estne missa sacrificium proprie dictum?

Missa non est sacrificium, proprie dictum, propitiatorium, pro peccatis viventium & mortuorum.

Obs. I. Dist. est inter missam christianam, & superstitiosam, siue idololatricam. Illa est legitima S. cœnæ celebratio: Hæc a Pontificiis definitur, quod sit sacrificium incruentum N. T. propitiatorium & satisfactorium, in quo sacerdos proprie dictus & solus communicans, super altari proprie dicto, Patri cælesti eundem Christum, eandemque hostiam, quæ in cruce fuit oblata, sub specie panis & vini, pro viuorum ac mortuorum, purgatorio nondum plene purgatorum, peccatis, pœnis, satisfactionibus, aliisque necessitatibus, offert.

Obs. II. Nomen sacrificii accipitur vel improprie, vel proprie. Improprie accipitur 1) pro omni opere, quod agitur, vt sancta societate inhæreamus Deo, relato ad illum finem, quo vere beati esse possumus, vt AVGVSTINVS loquitur, L. X. de C. D. c. 6. 2) pro cultu N. T. & prædicatione euangelii, Rom. XV, 16. Phil. II, 17. 3) pro beneficentia & officiis caritatis erga proximum, Phil. IV, 8. Hebr. XIII, 16. 4) pro precibus & gratiarum actionibus ad Deum directis, Hebr. XIII, 16. Apoc. V, 8. Proprie dictum sacrificium est vel מנחה, oblatio ex rebus inanimatis, cum solidis, verb. gr. ex pane, sale, thure, tum liquidis, quæ libamenta dicebantur: vel est זבח, sacrificium sanguineum, quo ex mandato diuino res animatæ in honorem Dei immolantur. Missam, siue celebrationem eucharistiæ, improprie posse sacrificium dici, non negamus; quia 1) est opus, quod agitur, vt sancta societate Deo inhæreamus: 2) est pars cultus N. T. non vltima: 3) olim cum celebraretur eucharistia, offerri solebant dona, quæ cederent in vsum ministrorum ecclesiæ & pauperum: 4) coniuncta est S. cœnæ administratio cum precibus & gratiarum actionibus: 5) est instituta in memoriam sacrificii Christi in ara crucis oblati.

Obs. III. Distinguendum est inter sacrificium materialiter, & formaliter sumtum. Si materialiter sumamus, in eucharistia idem numero sacrificium est, quod fuit in cruce, sive res & substantia prorsus eadem; eadem, inquam, victima, sive hostia. Si vero accipiamus formaliter, sive pro actu sacrificandi, tum, etiamsi sit victima una et eadem numero, non tamen eadem actio, sive immolatio est, quæ fit in eucharistia, cum immolatione, quæ in cruce peracta fuit. Nam in cruce facta est oblatio per veram rei vivæ immolatæ passionem & mortem, absque qua sacrificium proprie dictum nullo modo esse potest; in eucharistia vero fit oblatio per preces, & per commemorationem mortis, sive sacrificii in cruce oblati.

Prob. Assertio nostra: 1) Quæ res animata proprie sacrificatur, ea occiditur & per mortem destruitur: Corpus Christi animatum in missa non occiditur, neque per mortem destruitur: E. corpus Christi in missa proprie non sacrificatur. Maior liquet ex natura sacrificii proprie dicti. Minor claret testimonio Pauli, Rom. VI, 9.

2) Quod sacrificium repeti debet, illud est imperfectum & arguit sacerdotium imperfectum: Christi sacrificium nec est imperfectum, nec sacerdotium arguit imperfectum: E. repeti non debet. Maior & minor patet ex Hebr. VII, 27. c. IX, 25. 26.

3) Si missa esset sacrificium proprie dictum, esset institutum a Christo in vltima cœna. Sed in ea institutum non est. E. non est sacrificium proprie dictum. Ratio consequentia est: quia iuxta Pontificios missa ab eucharistia non differt, quoad rem: eucharistia autem in vltima cœna demum fuit instituta. Consequens probatur: quia institutio sacrificii proprie dicti, quo res animata offertur, importat mandatum de mactando eo, quod offerendum est. De Christo autem mactando nullum in institutione cœnæ mandatum, neque explicite neque implicite continetur.

4) Ex mente aduersariorum missa est sacrificium incruentum. Ex quo colligimus: Nullum sacrificium propitiatorium, proprie dictum, fit sine sanguine, Hebr. IX, 22. At sacrificium missaticum fit sine sanguine. E. non est sacrificium propitiatorium, proprie dictum.

5) Nullum sacramentum potest esse sacrificium: Eucharistia est sacramentum. Ergo. Maior probatur: quia in sacramentis Deus gratiam suam hominibus offert & confert; in sacrificiis autem homines quædam munera Deo offerunt . Antithesis est Pontificiorum, statuentium, Christum in missa proprie, sed modo incruento sacrificari. Quorum argumenta potiora sunt: I. Si sacrificium noui testamenti debet esse quotidianum & vniuersale, sequitur, quod sacrificium missaticum in dubium non fit vocandum (nam hoc est quotidianum & vniuersale): Antecedens est verum, teste Malachia c. I, 11. Ergo & consequens.

Resp. L. c. non intelligitur sacrificium expiatorium, proprie dictum, sed sacrificium spirituale, nempe sacrificium spirituale, nempe sacrificium spirituale,

nempe praedicatio evangelii in toto terrarum orbe, Rom. XV, 16. sacrificium caritatis, sive beneficentiae, sacrificium precum & hostia laudis.

II. Quicunque est sacerdos in morem Melchisedechi, illius officium offerendo panem & sanguinem est peragendum: Atqui Christus &c. Hebr. V, 6. Ergo. Maior probatur: quia Melchisedechus dicitur sacrificasse & obtulisse Abrahamo panem & vinum, Gen. XIV, 18. Resp. 1) Melchisedechus non sacrificavit, sed attulit panem & vinum ad reficiendum Abrahamum & ipsius milites. 2) Christus semel sacrificavit, & immolavit seipsum in ara crucis, Hebr. IX, 12.

Instantia: Sed sacrificium Christi debet esse aeternum; quia est sacerdos in morem Melchisedechi aeternum. Resp. Sacrificium Christi in ara crucis peractum, est aeternum, non ob perennem reiterationem, sed ob perpetuum valorem, Hebr. X, 10.

III. Nulla vera religio potest esse sine sacrificio constanti & perenni. Atqui Christiana religio est vera religio. E. Maior prob. quia religio Israelitica non erat sine sacrificiis quotidianis: Quin immo gentiles sacrificaverunt. Resp. 1) Religio Christiana nititur sacrificio Christi, quod, qua valorem, aeternum est, Hebr. X, 14. 2) Religio Christiana exercetur quotidianis sacrificiis eucharisticis, sive hostiis laudis & precum.


### XIX. Is the sacrament of the supper to be offered to the laity under both species?: S I G H

S I G H.
