Common and more remote signs, although they do not seem to signify the time of judgment, nevertheless, by the institution and intention of God, they do signify and ought to warn Christians that some solemn judgment is to be expected, by virtue of divine justice and the truth of the predictions. But the difference of the more proximate, or proper signs, is such that some precede the judgment by a longer interval, others by a shorter: which therefore do not themselves signify a determinate certain time.

Prob. The signs which precede the last day by either a longer or shorter interval are: 1) Security and wicked impiety, Matt. XXIV, 37, 38. Conf. 2 Pet. III, 3, 4. 2) Multiplication of heresies, Matt. XXIV, 11. 2 Pet. III, 4. 3) Disturbance of the whole world by wars, seditions, pestilential diseases, earthquakes, Luke XXI, 9, 10. 4) Notable inclination of the Roman monarchy, Dan. II, 31. seqq. 5) Revelation of the Anti-Christ, 2 Thess. II, 3. 6) Prodigious eclipses, falling of stars from heaven, and horrendous tempests, Matt. XXIV, 29. There are those who explain the words of Christ mystically concerning the notable mutation of the church, concerning the obscuration of heavenly doctrine, and the ἀποστασίᾳ of the doctors of the church. See D. IO. ADAM OSIANDER, Colleg. Systemat. P. VI. page 278. Others persuade that the literal sense should not be abandoned. See CALOVIUS, Bibl. Illustrat. in h. l. fol. 420. (*).

IV. Question IV. Who will be the oecumenical, or universal, judge? Universal judgment over all men and angels, by reason of majesty, authority, power, and decree, belongs to the whole Holy Trinity. By economy, however, or the singular dispensation of God, Christ will be the visible judge in his assumed humanity, and thus he will perform the office of judge not only according to his divine, but also his human nature.

Prob. a. 1) The function of universal judgment is an action ad extra, common to the whole Holy Trinity.

Whence the Hieropsaltes says, Ps. IX, 8. Jehovah has prepared his throne for judgment.

2) God the Father, as the Ancient of Days, sits to judge, Dan. VII, 9. Who has destined to judge the world in righteousness by one man, Acts XVII, 31. who also gave judgment to the Son of Man, John V, 22.

3) The Holy Spirit is called the Spirit of judgment, Is. IV, 4. who just as he contends with men in this life, Gen. VI, 3. and convicts them of their sins, John XIV, 8: so the power of judging on the last day, and of inwardly convincing the hearts of men, belongs to him.

Prob. b. The oecumenical judgment will be a visible act, the judge of which will be obvious and exposed to the eyes of all men. Although the body of Christ, by virtue of its glorified state, is invisible; yet by economy, or the singular disposition of God, it will come to pass that Christ the judge will appear visibly in his glorified body.

The angels, conspicuous in the form of two men, pointed out the visible advent of Christ to judgment, Acts I, 11. Ye men of Galilee, why stand ye looking into heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, in the manner you saw him going into heaven. The Savior himself says more clearly, Matt. XXIV, 30. Then shall appear the sign of the Son of Man: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Man, coming in the clouds of heaven, with power and glory.

God the Father is not going to judge the world in a visible form; but Christ, in human form, clearly to be seen, will promulgate the definitive sentence of the omnipotent and omniscient God concerning all men with a sonorous voice, and will immediately command the promulgated sentence to be executed. Prob. c. From John V, 22, 27. For neither does the Father judge anyone, but has given all judgment to the Son; because he is the Son of Man.

We learn from this oracle that the ἐξουσία, or judicial power, does not belong to the human nature of Christ by itself, but communicatively. For the particle ὅτι, because, is not αἰτιολογική, or causal, since the human nature is not the cause from which the judicial power depends; but it is ἐπιστημονική καὶ δεικτική, showing and determining the nature to which the judicial power is communicated by virtue of the personal union.

You say: Christ says, John XII, 47. And if anyone hears my words, yet does not believe: I do not judge him: for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.

Resp. These words of Christ are to be understood concerning the first humble advent of Christ, in which Christ came as a priest, to offer himself for the sins of the world, and as a teacher, to preach the gospel: but the other advent of Christ will be most splendid in majesty, in which, as universal King, he will judge all men.

Latin:

Resp. Infideles dicuntur iudicari ratione decreti & iudicii in verbo diuino de ipsis manifestati; at huius iudicii solennis promulgatio & exsecutio differtur in diem mundi vltimum. Credentes non veniant in iudicium condemnationis, licet iudicio comparitionis & discussionis non sint exemti

IV. Cui promulgatur sententia definitiua in hora mortis, illi non est promulganda in die mundi nouissimo, (neque enim probabile est eandem sententiam bis a iudice cœlesti latum iri): Atqui sententia definitiua absolutoria, aut condemnatoria promulgatur in hora mortis: Ergo. Minor patet: quia animæ a corpore solutæ e vestigio assignatur paradisus cœlestis aut infernus, Luc. XVI. Resp. Dist. inter iudicium particulare, & vniuersale. Illud cuiuis seorsim in hora mortis subeundum est: hoc publicabitur in extremo mundi die, vt tum iustitia Dei ab omnibus palam agnoscatur & celebretur, tum totus homo, constans ex anima & corpore, iudicetur & reportet, prout gessit in corpore, siue bonum, siue malum, 1 Cor. IV, 5.

III. An aduentum Domini signa quædam antecedent, e quibus cognosci potest, quando dies nouissimus venturus sit?

Ex voluntate & ordinatione Dei antecedent diem supremum signa diuinitus revelata, e quibus magnum illum diem appropinquare, cognoscere licet.

Obs. Distinguuntur signa prognostica diei nouissimi in remota, siue communia, & propinqua, siue propria. Illa sæculo non vno contingunt, ac sæpe recurrunt aut continuantur. Hæc sunt, quæ propius demum accedente iudicio, non autem æque prioribus sæculis conspicienda sunt. Signa communia & remotiora, licet tempus iudicii non significare videantur, tamen ex instituto & intentione Dei significant & Christianos monere debent, quod iudicium aliquod solemne sit exspectandum, ex vi iustitiæ diuinæ ac veritate prædictionum. Propinquiorum vero, seu propriorum signorum ea differentia est, vt aliqua longiore intervallo, aliqua breuiore, antecedant iudicium: quæ proinde nec ipsa certum tempus determinate significant.

Prob. Signa, quæ diem extremum vel longiore, vel breuiore interuallo antecedunt, sunt: 1) Securitas & nefanda impietas, Matth. XXIV, 37. 38. Conf. 2 Petr. III, 3. 4. 2) Hæresium multiplicatio, Matth. XXIV, 11. 2 Petr. III, 4. 3) Totius orbis per bella, seditiones, pestiferos morbos, terræ motus conturbatio, Luc. XXI, 9. 10. 4) Insignis Romanæ monarchiæ inclinatio, Dan. II, 31. seqq. 5) Anti-Christi reuelatio, 2 Thess. II, 3. 6) Prodigiosæ eclipses, lapsus stellarum de cælo, & horrenda tempestates, Matth. XXIV, 29. Sunt, qui verba Christi exponunt mystice de insigni mutatione ecclesiæ, de obfuscatioe doctrinæ cœlestis, & ἀποστασίᾳ doctorum ecclesiæ. Vid. D. IO. ADAM OSIANDRI colleg systemat. P. VI. pag. 278. Alii suadent, non deserendum esse sensum litteralem. Vid. CALOVII bibl. illustrat. in h. l. fol. 420. (*).

IV. Quaest. IV. Quis erit iudex oecumenicus, sive universalis? Iudicium universale in omnes homines, angelosque, ratione maiestatis, auctoritatis, potestatis et decreti, toti SS. Trinitati competit . Per oeconomiam tamen, sive dispensationem Dei singularem, Christus visibilis in assumpta humanitate, et immediatus iudex erit , atque adeo functurus est officio iudicis non tantum secundum divinam, sed et humanam naturam .

Prob. a. 1) Functio iudicii universalis est actio ad extra, toti SS. Trinitati communis.

Ex quo Hieropsaltes inquit, Ps. IX, 8. Iehouah ad iudicium praeparavit thronum suum.

2) Deus Pater, ut antiquus dierum, sedet ad iudicandum, Dan. VII, 9. Qui destinavit per unum virum orbem in iustitia iudicare, Act. XVII, 31. qui etiam iudicium filio hominis dedit, Io. V, 22.

3) Spiritus S. audit Spiritus iudicii, Es. IV, 4. qui sicut in hac vita cum hominibus contendit, Gen. VI, 3. et peccata eorum arguit, Io. XIV, 8: ita potestas iudicandi in novissimo die, et intus convincendi cor la hominum ei competit.

Prob. b. Iudicium oecumenicum erit actus visibilis, cuius iudex omnium hominum oculis obvius et expositus erit. Quamvis autem corpus Christi, vi status glorificati, sit invisibile; per oeconomiam tamen, seu singularem Dei dispositionem fiet, ut iudex Christus visibiliter in corpore suo glorificato appariturus sit.

Visibilem Christi adventum ad iudicium indigitatum iuerunt angeli, duorum virorum forma conspicui, Act. I, 11. Viri Galilaei, quid statis suspicientes in caelum? Hic Iesus, qui sublatus est a vobis in caelum, sic veniet, quemadmodum vidistis ipsum euntem in caelum. Clarius ipse Servator inquit, Matth. XXIV, 30. Tunc apparebit signum filii hominis: et tunc plangent omnes tribus terrae, et videbunt filium hominis, venientem in nubibus caeli, cum virtute et gloria.

Deus Pater in forma visibili non iudicaturus est orbem terrarum; sed Christus in forma humana aperte conspiciendus sententiam definitivam Dei omnipotentis et omniscii de omnibus hominibus sonora voce promulgabit, promulgatam confestim executioni mandabit. Prob. c. Ex Io. V, 22. 27. Neque enim Pater iudicat quemquam, sed iudicium omne dedit Filio; quia filius hominis est.

Discimus ex hoc oraculo, quod ἐξουσία, sive potestas iudiciaria non competat naturae humanae Christi per se, sed communicative. Neque enim particula ὅτι, quia, est αἰτιολογική, sive causalis, siquidem humana natura non est causa, a qua potestas iudiciaria dependet; sed est ἐπιστημονική καὶ δεικτική, monstrans et determinans naturam, cui potestas iudiciaria vi unionis personalis est communicata.

Dicis: Christus inquit, Io. XII, 47. Et si quis mea audiverit verba, non tamen crediderit: Ego non iudico ipsum: non enim veni, ut iudicem mundum, sed ut salvem mundum.

Resp. Verba haec Christi intelligenda sunt de primo Christi adventu humili, quo Christus veniebat ut sacerdos, pro peccatis mundi se oblaturus, et ut doctor, evangelium praedicaturus: alter autem adventus Christi erit maiestate splendidissimus, quo, ut Rex universalis, omnes homines iudicaturus est.


### Question VI

V. Question V. What will the advent of Christ to judgment be like?

The advent of Christ the judge will be public and most glorious by far, terrible to the impious, and most desired by the pious.

Prob. and the destruction of the Antichrist, 2 Thess. II, 8. the marvelous changes of the celestial bodies, Matt. XXIV, 29.

Luke XXI, 25.

Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear: and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and glory.

The advent of Christ will be glorious, because He will come with power and glory, i.e., with the glory of omnipotence, omniscience, justice, and omnipresence. And therefore they will see the sign of the Son of Man, by which we understand the splendor of Christ’s body joined with the light of the cloud. This splendor will be terrible to the impious: consequently they will mourn, i.e., they will strike their breasts, tremble in their limbs, and pour forth complaints mixed with tears. To the pious, the advent of Christ will be most desired: for they will see the Son of Man, their brother, Goel [Redeemer], and their mystical head, to whom they were grafted through faith, as spiritual members.

Quest. VI. Who will be the ministers of the ecumenical judge?

The ministers of the heavenly judge appearing in the clouds of heaven will be partly angels, as companions, trumpeters, and executors of His very sentence, and partly apostles and other holy men, as assessors, witnesses, and approvers of the judgment passed by Christ.

Proof a.

The office of the angels on the last day will be: 1) to accompany the arriving judge honorably, Matt. XXIV, 31. and XXV, 31. 2) to manifest the advent of Christ with a loud voice and blown trumpets, ibid. cf. 1 Thess. IV, 16. 3) to execute the will of Christ by gathering and segregating men, Matt. XXIV, 31. Matt. XIII, 41.

Proof b.

In the entire choir of assessors, the apostles will excel, Matt. XIX, 28. Then all the elect patriarchs, prophets, martyrs, and the remaining saints will sit, 1 Cor. III, 2. 3. who will judge the world, not by promulgating a definitive sentence, but by sitting, testifying, approving, and presenting themselves as examples of repentance and faith.

Obs.

All men, and thus even the saints, must be presented before the tribunal of Christ, but soon to be caught up into the air to meet Christ, and together with Christ and the apostles, who as the leaders and principal assessors will be closest to Christ the judge, they are to judge the world. See GERHARD, loc. de extremo iudicio §. 43. fol. 75.

Quest. VII. What cause impelled God to the universal judgment?

The internal impulsive cause is remunerative and vindictive justice. The external impulsive causes are partly the merit of Christ apprehended by faith, partly sins, and primarily the final impenitence of the men to be judged.

Proof a. From 2 Thess. I, 6. It is just with God to repay affliction to those who afflict you; but to you who are afflicted, relief with us, at the revelation of the Lord Jesus from heaven with the angels of His power.

Proof b. The merit of Christ, apprehended by faith, moves God to the judgment of absolution, because by the same God we have been reconciled, Rom. V, 10. Proof c.

We must all be manifested before the tribunal of Christ, so that each may receive what was done through the body, according to what he did, whether good or evil, 2 Cor. V, 10. The evils which each one committed in the body move God to wish him to be manifested before the tribunal of Christ, to receive just punishments in the body.

Proof d. From John XII, 48. Where Christ says: He who rejects me, and does not receive my words, has one who judges him: the word that I have spoken, that will judge him on the last day.

Which is the same as if He had said, that the unbelief (ἀπιστίαν) by which the gospel of Christ is despised moves the heavenly judge to condemn the stubborn despiser of the gospel in the final judgment.

Latin:

V. Quaest. V. Qualis erit adventus Christi ad iudicium?

Aduentus Christi iudicis erit publicus et longe gloriosissimus, impiis terribilis, piis exoptatissimus.

Prob. destructioque Antichristi, 2 Thess. II, 8. mirabiles mutationes corporum caelestium, Matth. XXIV, 29.

Luc. XXI, 25.

Tunc apparebit signum filii hominis: & tunc plangent omnes tribus terrae, & videbunt filium hominis venientem in nubibus caeli cum virtute & gloria.

Gloriosus erit aduentus Christi, quia veniet cum virtute & gloria, scil. cum gloria omnipotentiae, omniscientiae, iustitiae & omnipraesentiae. Ideoque videbunt signum filii hominis, per quod splendorem corporis Christi coniunctum cum luce nubis intelligimus. Hic splendor impiis erit terribilis: proinde plangent, i. e. ferient pectora, trement artubus, querelas lacrymis mixtas fundent. Piis aduentus Christi erit exoptatissimus: nam videbunt filium hominis, fratrem, Goelem, & caput suum mysticum, cui per fidem, velut membra spiritualia, fuerunt insiti.

Quaest. VI. Quinam erunt iudicis oecumenici ministri?

Iudicis coelestis in nubibus coeli apparentis ministri erunt partim angeli, tanquam comites, buccinatores & exsecutores ipsius sententiae , partim apostoli, alique sancti homines, tanquam assessores, testes & comprobatores iudicii a Christo lati .

Prob. a.

Angelorum officium in nouissimo die erit: 1) aduenientem iudicem honorifice comitari, Matth. XXIV, 31. & XXV, 31. 2) alta voce & inflatis tubis aduentum Christi manifestare, ib. conf. 1 Thess. IV, 16. 3) voluntatem Christi exsequi, homines congregando & segregando, Matth. XXIV, 31. Matth. XIII, 41.

Prob. b.

In vniuerso assessorum choro praeminebunt apostoli, Matth. XIX, 28. Deinde assidebunt omnes electi patriarchae, prophetae, martyres & reliqui sancti, 1 Cor. III, 2. 3. qui iudicabunt mundum, non definitiuam sententiam promulgando, sed assidendo, testificando, approbando, & se ipsos velut exempla poenitentiae & fidei sistendo.

Obs.

Omnes homines, adeoque etiam sancti, coram tribunali Christi sunt sistendi, sed mox in occursum Christi rapiendi in aerem, ac vna cum Christo & apostolis, qui velut primores & praecipui assessores Christo iudici erunt proximi, mundum sunt iudicaturi. Vid. GERHARD, loc. de extremo iudicio §. 43. fol. 75.

Quaest. VII. Quae causa impulit Deum ad iudicium vniuersale?

Causa impulsiva interna est iustitia remuneratoria & vindicatiua . Causa impulsiva externa sunt partim meritum Christi fide apprehensum , partim peccata , & in primis finalis impoenitentia hominum iudicandorum.

Prob. a. Ex 2 Thess. I, 6. Iustum est apud Deum, retribuere affligentibus vos afflictionem; at vobis, qui affligimini, recreationem nobiscum, in reuelatione Domini Iesu de caelo cum angelis potentiae ipsius.

Prob. b. Meritum Christi, fide apprehensum, mouet Deum ad iudicium absolutionis, quia eodem Deo reconciliati sumus, Rom. V, 10. Prob. c.

Omnes nos manifestari oportet coram tribunali Christi, vt reportet quilibet ea, quae per corpus facta, prout ea fecit, siue bonum, siue malum, 2 Cor. V, 10. Mala, quae quisque gessit in corpore, mouent Deum, vt velit eum manifestari coram tribunali Christi, ad reportandas iustas in corpore poenas.

Prob. d. Ex Io. XII, 48. Vbi Christus dicit: Qui spernit me, & non accipit verba mea, habet, qui iudicet ipsum: verbum, quod locutus sum, illud iudicabit illum in extremo die.

Quod idem est, ac si dixisset, ἀπιστίαν, qua contemnitur euangelium Christi, mouere iudicem coelestem ad condemnandum in iudicio extremo pertinacem euangelii contemtorem.


### Q. VIII. Who are to be judged?

All men are to be judged, the pious and the wicked a), the living and the dead b), and besides these, the evil angels c).

Proof a. 1) From Rom. XIV, 10. We shall all stand before the judgment seat of Christ.

2) From 2 Cor. V, 10. We must all be made manifest before the judgment seat of Christ.

Proof b. From 2 Tim. IV, 1. Christ is to judge the living and the dead. By the phrase of Scripture, all men to be judged are divided into the living and the dead. By the living are designated those men whom the last day will find alive; by the dead are understood those who, having previously finished their life, are resurrected on the last day of the world, so that they may be stationed before the tribunal.

Proof c. From 2 Pet. II, 4. God did not spare the angels who sinned, but casting them into hell, delivered them into chains of darkness, to be kept for judgment. Compare Epist. Jude v. 6. Demons, indeed, were adjudged to eternal punishments immediately from their fall: but the completion will be added to them on the pantocritic day, on which the chains of darkness will be tightened more strictly—which, with God permitting, are still sometimes loosened for them—but after the day of universal judgment, no power of wandering out of hell will be granted to them by God.

Latin:

Iudicandi sunt omnes homines, pii & mali a), viui & mortui b), & praeter hos angeli mali c).

Prob. a. 1) Ex Rom XIV, 10. Omnes fitemur coram tribunali Christi.

2) Ex 2 Cor. V, 10. Omnes manifestari oportet coram tribunali Christi.

Prob. b. Ex 2 Tim. IV, 1. Christus iudicaturus est viuos & mortuos. Phrasi scripturae omnes homines iudicandi diuiduntur in viuos & mortuos. Per viuos designantur illi homines, quos extremus dies viuos deprehendet, per mortuos intelliguntur, qui antea vita functi, nouissimo mundi die resuscitantur, vt ad tribunal sistantur.

Prob. c. Ex 2 Petr. II, 4. Deus angelis, qui peccarunt, non pepercit, sed eas catenis tenebrarum in tartarum detrudens, tradidit in iudicium asseruatos. Confer. Epist. Iud. v. 6. Daemones quidem statim a lapsu poenis aeternis sunt adiudicati: at complementum iisdem addetur in die pantocritico, quo arctius constringentur catenae tenebrarum, quae, permittente Deo illis adhuc interdum laxantur, at post diem vniuersalis iudicii nulla ipsis potestas ex inferno euagandi a Deo concedetur.


### Q. IX. What will be judged in men and fallen angels?

In men, both faith and unbelief a) will be judged, as well as the effects of faith and unbelief, namely, good and evil works, internal and external b); in evil angels c).

Proof a. Men will be judged immediately from faith and unbelief. For in John III, 18, Christ says: He who believes in Him is not judged (with the judgment of condemnation); but he who does not believe has already been judged (by the decree of God).

Proof b. Since good works are the fruits and τεκμήρια (proofs) of faith, and evil works are the effects and testimonies of unbelief, the works of men will also be judged, Matt. XXV, 35. (*) To which must also be referred the words of men, Matt. XII, 36, and the thoughts and secrets of hearts, Rom. II, 16; 1 Cor. IV, 5.

Proof c. From the Epistle of Jude, v. 6. The evil angels will be judged, because they did not keep their origin (original righteousness), but left their own habitation (they lost their glorious state by their own fault). By which words their ἀποστασία (apostasy) is graphically described. Question

Latin:

Iudicabuntur in hominibus tum fides & infidelitas a), tum effecta fidei & infidelitatis, scilicet opera bona & mala, interna & externa b), in angelis malis c).

Prob. a. Immediate iudicabuntur homines ex fide & infidelitate. Nam Io. III, 18. inquit Christus: Qui credit in ipsum, non iudicatur (iudicio condemnationis); qui autem non credit, iam iudicatus est (vi decreti diuini).

Prob. b. Cum bona opera sint fructus & τεκμήρια fidei, mala opera autem effectus & testimonia infidelitatis, diiudicabuntur etiam hominum opera, Matth. XXV, 35. (*) quo referenda etiam sunt hominum verba, Matth. XII, 36. cogitata & cordium secreta, Rom. II, 16. 1 Cor. IV, 5.

Prob. c. Ex ep. Iud. v. 6. Iudicabuntur angeli mali, quia non tenuerunt suam originem (originalem iustitiam), sed reliquerunt proprium domicilium (amiserunt sua culpa statum gloriosum). Quibus verbis eorum ἀποστασία graphice describitur.


### X. According to what norm will the pronouncement be made on the last day?

Believers and unbelievers will be judged according to the rule of the divine word a). To the faithful and pious men, eternal joy will be decreed according to the gracious norm of the Gospel b). To the unbelievers, eternal death will be decreed according to the law, illuminated by the light of the Gospel c).

Proof a. Speaking generally, the norm of the final judgment is the word of God. The word that I have spoken, that will judge him in the last day, says Christ, John XII, 48. Proof b.

Those who are saved only by the Gospel, to them salvation will be adjudged on the last day by the Gospel: But believers are saved only by the Gospel (not by the law, from which there is no blessing and justification, Gal. III, 11, 19). Therefore. Proof c.

From Rom. II, 12. As many as have sinned in the law shall be judged by the law. Since, however, the law alone and considered by itself is ignorant of Christ, and does not formally argue against unbelief in Christ, it is necessary that it be illuminated by the light of the Gospel. You say:

I. All men seem to be judged according to the Gospel. For Paul says, Rom. II, 16. In the day when God shall judge the secrets of men, according to my gospel, by Jesus Christ.

Resp. The judgment is said to be future according to the Gospel not simply, as if threats and even punishments pertained to the Gospel, but in a certain respect: 1) because eternal life will be adjudged to the elect, according to the Gospel: 2) because the unbelief which is directed toward Christ is declared in the Gospel, insofar as in it is shown the object, the righteousness and merit of Christ, which the infidels reject, even if ἀπισία (unbelief), considered generically, is argued in the law, as a sin against the first commandment, and thus condemnation redounds from the law: 3) because we are taught that the judgment is to be instituted by Christ, not through the law, but through the Gospel. You say:

II. Whoever are sinners are to be judged according to the norm of the law: But all men &c. 1 Kings VIII, 46. Therefore.

Resp. Whoever are sinners not justified are to be judged according to the norm of the law. But believers are justified, and absolved from guilt and punishment, by the fact that they have accepted the satisfaction of Christ, offered in the Gospel, and have interposed this surety for themselves. You say:

To question II. The reason is situated in this: since love toward other men, even those of the lowest sort, is the first of all virtues which are contained in the second table, and the fulfillment of the whole law, Rom. XIII, 10. And love toward men that is not feigned is a document of love toward God, 1 John IV, 20, 21. To question III. 1)

To question III. 1) It would have been too long, indeed, if Christ had wished to enumerate every single part of duty by counting them up one by one. It was enough to have named one as an example of all, and that one, indeed, which was most of all accommodated to the time. The times were most difficult, which in the first place demanded compassion and liberality as necessary, because of the abundance of those who, having professed the name of Christ, were in need of all things. 2) Christ proceeds from more special examples to a general rule, v. 40. 3) In those things which are brought forward for the sake of example, there is great force of argumentation, not only from species to genus, but also from the lesser to the greater: If the Judge will punish so severely those who did not bring aid to the miserable; what is not to be feared by those who neither profited others, and by cruel savageness harmed many! savageness harmed many! savageness harmed many! savageness harmed many!

You say: III. Whoever are judged according to works, they are judged according to the law (because not the gospel, but the law is the doctrine of works): But the pious Matth. XXV, 34. 35. E. Resp. Whoever are judged proximately and immediately according to works, they are judged according to the law; I concede: But the pious are proximately and immediately judged according to faith, the fruits of which are good works, whose directive principle is the law, [and whose] productive [principle] is the gospel.

Q. XI. In what does the extreme judgment formally consist?

The process of the extreme judgment formally consists a) in the most accurate cognition of the cause, according to the law and the gospel: b) in the pronouncement of the sentence: c) in the execution of the sentence passed. Prob. a.

From Rom. XIV, 10. 12. We shall all be placed before the tribunal of Christ. And each of us will render an account of himself to God, and thus the heavenly judge will know the cause of each, and indeed the cause of the faithful man, according to the gospel; the cause of the infidel, according to the law.

Prob. b. Christ will promulgate the decretory sentence by addressing first the elect: Come! then the reprobate: Go! &c. Matth. XXV, 34. 41.

Prob. c. Execution will follow the promulgated sentence immediately: And they will go (the unjust) into eternal punishment, but the just into eternal life, Matth. XXV, 46.

Q. XII.

How is the judgment of Christ distinguished by reason of form or process? The judgment of Christ, by reason of process, is distinguished into the judgment of discussion and of retribution. In the judgment of discussion, the cause of all men, as well of the just as of the unjust, will be known, and the evil works of the unjust will be accurately examined and made public. In the judgment of retribution, the sentence suitable to each will be pronounced, which will be twofold: of approbation, or absolution, by which eternal life will be assigned and conferred upon the elect, and of reprobation, or condemnation, by which the reprobate will be banished into eternal fire.

Q. XIII. Will the sins of the faithful also be examined and made public on the day of the extreme judgment?

That the individual sins of the faithful will be specifically examined and made public by Christ on the last day is not probable.

Prob. 1) From the divine promise. God has promised that He wills to blot out our sins, as clouds, Is. XLIV, 22. to cast them behind His back, Is. XXXVIII, 17. to sink them into the depth of the sea, Mic. VII, 19. so that He no longer remembers them, Is. XLIII, 17. But those things which God does not will to remember, He does not make public. 2) From the immutability of God. The will of God is immutable, Mal. III, 6. Since, therefore, God has forgiven the sins of the faithful in this life, it is improbable that He will recall the forgiven sins to a rigid examination in the other life. 3) From the affection of the judge. Christ will come to judgment as our redeemer, Luke XXI, 28. Who presents to Himself a glorious church, not having spot, or wrinkle, or any such thing, Eph. V, 27: He will not reveal the spots of the saints. Antith. This is [the position] of the Papists, who maintain that in the judgment of discussion the sins of the elect will be examined and made public by Christ.

Who object: I. The day will make it manifest, because it will be revealed by fire; and the work of each one will be made manifest, 1 Cor. III, 12. Resp. In that place, the last day is not understood, but the day of temptation, by which the teacher VII. The falls of the pious are recorded in the holy scriptures: doctor of the church, who has built upon the foundation of faith, hay and stubble, or useless and erroneous dogmas, being placed in extreme danger, or the agony of life, is examined, tested, and finally saved through fire. The last day is not a day of probation, but of retribution.

II. Whoever shall bring all good and evil works into judgment, he shall examine and publish the evil works of the pious: But the heavenly judge, etc. Resp. All the thoughts, words, and works of men are said to be manifested not collectively, just as if all the sins of both the pious and the impious were to be revealed; but distributively, because the good works of the pious, and the evil works of the impious, perpetrated secretly without witnesses and arbiters, are to be brought into the clear light, as may be gathered from the judicial process, Matt. XXV. 31. seqq.

III. Whoever has spoken idle words, they shall render an account of them, Matt. XII, 36. But the reborn, etc. Resp. Whoever has spoken idle words, and has not received remission for them, shall render an account of them. But for the elect, sins are forgiven in this life.

IV. All men shall be set before the tribunal of Christ, and shall render an account of themselves, Rom. XIV, 10. 12. Therefore, the sins of all men shall be examined and published. Resp. I deny the consequence. For all men shall render an account of themselves either according to the evangelical ἐπίσκεψιν (visitation/examination), or according to the rigor of the law. The elect shall be judged according to the gospel, and thus they shall not come into judgment, neither of legal discussion, nor of condemnation.

V. If all books are to be opened on the last day, and men are to be judged from them; then certainly the book of conscience shall also be opened to undergo examination: The antecedent is true, Apoc. XX, 12. Therefore, the consequent is also. Resp: On the last day the books of life, or of the gospel, and the books of death, or of the law, shall be opened, and they shall be judged, the faithful from the book of the gospel, the unfaithful from the book of the law.

VI. Those whose sins Christ shall not examine on the day of universal judgment, He shall judge with the case unheard: But He shall judge no one with the case unheard. Therefore. The major is evident: since it is the duty of the judge, without respect of persons (προσωποληψίᾳ), to discuss and examine the good and evil works of all. Resp. It is the duty of a terrestrial judge to discuss and examine the works of all according to acts and proofs; but the heavenly judge needs neither acts nor proofs, but looks into all things most deeply, and thus knows who are His, 2 Tim. II, 19.

Therefore, they shall also be published on the last day. Resp. They are recorded in the holy scriptures for the sake of those living in the time of grace, both so that they may carefully decline from sins, and so that the fallen themselves may be converted, and conceive in their minds the hope of remission. But on the last day there is no time of grace, but a time of judgment, nor is there then any return open to saving repentance. Quaest.

Latin:

Iudicabuntur fideles & infideles secundum regulam verbi diuini a). Fidelibus atque piis hominibus decernetur æternum gaudium iuxta gratiosam euangelii normam b). Infidelibus decernetur æterna mors iuxta legem, lumine euangelii collustratam c).

Prob. a. Generatim loquendo norma iudicii extremi est verbum Dei. Sermo, quem locutus sum, ille iudicabit eum in die nouissimo, ait Christus, Io. XII, 48.

Prob. b. Qui ex euangelio tantum saluantur, illis ex euangelio salus in die nouissimo adiudicabitur: Atqui fideles tantum ex euangelio saluantur (non ex lege, ex qua non est benedictio & iustificatio, Gal. III, 11. 19.) Ergo.

Prob. c. Ex Rom. II, 12. Quotquot in lege peccauerunt, per legem iudicabuntur. Cum autem lex sola & per se considerata ignoret Christum, nec incredulitatem in Christum formaliter arguat, necesse est, vt lumine euangelii collustretur.

Dicis: I. Omnes homines videntur iudicandi secundum euangelium. Nam Paullus inquit, Rom. II, 16. In die, quando iudicabit occulta hominum Deus, iuxta euangelium meum, per Iesum Christum.

Resp. Iudicium secundum euangelium futurum dicitur non simpliciter, quasi ad euangelium pertineant comminationes etiam atque supplicia, sed secundum quid: 1) quia electis adiudicabitur vita æterna, secundum euangelium: 2) quia incredulitas, quæ in Christum fertur, in euangelio declaratur, quatenus in eodem monstratur, obiectum, Christi iustitia & meritum, quod infideles respuunt, etsi ἀπισία, generice considerata, arguatur in lege, vt peccatum contra primum præceptum, atque adeo ex lege damnatio redundet: 3) quia iudicium instituendum esse a Christo, non per legem, sed per euangelium docemur.

Dicis: II. Quicunque sunt peccatores, secundum normam legis sunt iudicandi: Atqui omnes homines &c. 1 Reg. VIII, 46. E. Resp.

Quicunque sunt peccatores non iustificati, secundum normam legis sunt iudicandi. At fideles sunt iustificati, atque absoluti a culpa & pœna, eo, quod satisfactionem Christi, in euangelio oblatam, acceptarunt, & hunc vadem pro se interposuerunt. Dicis:

Ad quæst. II. Ratio in eo sita est: quoniam amor in alios homines, immo infimæ sortis, est prima omnium virtutum, quæ tabula II, continentur, ac legis vniuersæ complementum, Rom. XIII, 10. Et amor in homines non fucatus est documentum amoris in Deum, 1 Io. IV, 20. 21.

Ad quæst. III. 1) Nimis profecto longum fuisset, si Christus singulas officii partes voluisset annumerando percensere. Satis erat, vnam instar omnium nominasse, & eam quidem, quæ omnium maxime erat tempori adcommodata. Erant difficillima tempora, quæ in primis miserationem ac liberalitatem necessariam postulabant, propter copiam eorum, qui, nomen Christi professi, omnium rerum indigentes erant. 2) Christus ab exemplis specialioribus ad regulam generalem progreditur, v. 40. 3) Quæ exempli caussa proferuntur, in iis magna vis est argumentationis, non modo a specie ad genus, verum etiam a minori ad maius: Si Iudex tam seuere animaduertet in eos, qui miseris opem non tulerunt; quid non metuendum erit illis, qui nec profuerunt aliis, & crudeli fænitia multis nocuerunt! fæuitia multis nocuerunt! fæuitia multis nocuerunt! fæuitia multis nocuerunt!

Dicis: III. Quicunque iudicantur secundum opera, illi iudicantur secundum legem (quia non evangelium, sed lex est doctrina operum): Atqui pii Matth. XXV, 34. 35. E. Resp. Quicunque proxime & immediate iudicantur secundum opera, illi iudicantur secundum legem; concedo: At pii proxime & immediate iudicantur secundum fidem, cuius fructus sunt bona opera, quorum principium directivum est lex, productivum est evangelium.

Quaest. XI. In quo formaliter consistit iudicium extremum?

Processus extremi iudicii formaliter, consistit a) in accuratissima causae cognitione, secundum legem & euangelium: b) in sententiae pronuntiatione: c) in sententiae latae exsecutione. Prob. a.

Ex Rom. XIV, 10. 12. Omnes sistemur coram tribunali Christi. Et quilibet nostrum de seipso rationem reddet Deo, adeoque iudex coelestis cuiuslibet caussam cognoscet, & quidem hominis fidelis caussam, secundum euangelium; infidelis caussam, secundum legem.

Prob. b. Christus sententiam decretoriam promulgabit compellando primum electos: Venite! deinde reprobos: Ite! &c. Matth. XXV, 34. 41.

Prob. c. Sententiam promulgatam et illico sequetur exsecutio: Et ibunt (iniusti) in poenam aeternam, iusti vero, in vitam aeternam, Matth. XXV, 46.

Quaest. XII. Quomodo ratione formae, aut processus, iudicium Christi distinguitur?

Iudicium Christi, ratione processus, distinguitur in iudicium discussionis, & retributionis. Iudicio discussionis omnium hominum, tam iustorum, quam iniustorum cognoscetur caussa, & iniustorum mala opera accurate examinata publicabuntur. Iudicio retributionis pronuntiabitur sententia cuique conueniens, quod erit duplex: approbationis, siue absolutionis, quo electis assignabitur & conferetur vita aeterna, & reprobationis, seu condemnationis, quo reprobi ablegabuntur in ignem aeternum.

Quaest. XIII. An etiam fidelium peccata in die iudicii extremi examinabuntur & publicabuntur?

Singula fidelium peccata in die nouissimo speciatim a Christo examinatum & publicatum iri, non est probabile.

Prob. 1) A promissione diuina. Promisit Deus, se velle peccata nostra delere, ut nebulas, Es. XLIV, 22. proiicere post tergum, Es. XXXVIII, 17. demergere in profundum maris, Mich. VII, 19. vt eorum non amplius recordetur, Es. XLIII, 17. Sed quorum Deus non vult recordari, ea non publicat. 2) Ab immutabilitate Dei. Voluntas Dei est immutabilis, Mal. III, 6. Quoniam itaque Deus in hac vita fidelibus peccata remisit, improbabile est, eundem peccata remissa in altera vita ad rigidum examen reuocaturum esse. 3) Ab affectu iudicis. Veniet Christus ad iudicium, vt noster redemtor, Luc. XXI, 28. Qui sistit sibi ecclesiam splendidam, non habentem maculam, aut rugam, aut quidquam talium, Eph. V, 27: maculas sanctorum non propalabit. Antith. fis est Pontificiorum, statuentium, iudicio discussionis peccata electorum a Christo examinatum & publicatum iri.

Qui obiiciunt: I. Dies manifestabit, quia per ignem reuelabitur; & opus vnius cuiusque manifestum fiet, 1 Cor. III, 12. Resp. L. c. non intelligitur dies nouissimus, sed dies tentationis, quo doctor ecclesiae, qui super fundamentum fidei, foenum & stipulas, seu dogmata inutilia & erronea superstruxit, constitutus in summo periculo, aut agone vitae, per ignem, examinatur, probatur & tandem salvatur. Dies novissimus non est dies probationis, sed retributionis.

II. Quicunque omnia opera bona & mala adducet in iudicium, ille mala opera piorum examinabit & publicabit: Atqui iudex coelestis &c. Resp. Omnia hominum cogitata, verba & opera dicuntur manifestari non collective, prorsus ac si omnia tam piorum, quam impiorum peccata sint revelanda; sed distributive, quod piorum bona opera, impiorum mala opera, fine testibus & arbitris clam perpetrata, in claram lucem protrahenda sint, uti colligere licet e processu iudiciali, Matth. XXV. 31. seqq.

III. Quicunque locuti sunt verba otiosa, de illis reddent rationem, Matth. XII, 36. Atqui renati &c. Resp. Quicunque locuti sunt verba otiosa, & eorum non acceperunt remissionem, de illis reddent rationem. At electis peccata in hac vita sunt remissa.

IV. Omnes homines sistentur coram tribunali Christi, & reddent rationem de seipsis, Rom. XIV, 10. 12. E. omnium hominum peccata examinabuntur & publicabuntur. Resp. Neg. consequ. Nam omnes homines reddent rationem de seipsis vel secundum ἐπίσκεψιν evangelicam, vel secundum rigorem legis. Electi iudicabuntur secundum evangelium, adeoque non venient in iudicium, neque discussionis legalis, neque condemnationis.

V. Si aperiendi sunt in die novissimo omnes libri, & ex iis homines iudicandi; utique & liber conscientiae ad examen sustinendum aperietur: Antecedens est verum, Apoc. XX, 12. E. & consequens. Resp: Aperientur in die novissimo libri vitae, sive evangelii, & libri mortis, sive legis, atque iudicabuntur, fideles ex libro evangelii, infideles ex libro legis.

VI. Quorum peccata Christus in die pantocritico non examinabit, illos iudicabit inaudita causa: At neminem iudicabit inaudita causa. E. Maior patet: quoniam iudicis est, sine προσωποληψίᾳ, bona & mala opera omnium discutere & examinare. Resp. Iudicis terrestris est, omnium opera secundum acta & probata discutere & examinare; at iudex coelestis neque actis, neque probatis indiget, sed omnia penitissime inspicit, adeoque novit, qui sint sui, 2 Tim. II, 19.

VII. Lapsus piorum in sacras litteras sunt relati: E. & in novissimo die publicabuntur. Resp. Sunt in sacras litteras relati, propter viventes tempore gratiae, tum ut peccata follicite declinent, tum ut ipsi lapsi convertantur, & spem remissionis animis concipiant. At in novissimo die non est tempus gratiae, sed tempus iudicii, neque ad salutarem poenitentiam tum patet reditus.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?

The principal end of the extreme judgment is the glory of the heavenly judge a). The less principal end is the introduction of the elect into the kingdom of glory, and the actual casting of the reprobate into eternal fire b).

Prob. a. From 2 Thess. I, 10. The Lord shall come, that He may be glorified in His saints. Christ shall be glorified in the saints: 1) because He shall communicate eternal glory to them, as to His own members: 2) because He shall be glorified by them not without the highest admiration. For on that great day the admirable remunerative and vindicatory justice of the heavenly judge shall shine forth most clearly, conjoined with ineffable mercy, wisdom, and power. 5. The final judgment is the introductory means for admitting the pious into blessedness, and for thrusting the impious into eternal torments. Q. XV. Is the millennial kingdom of Christ, conspicuous for the extraordinary knowledge of divine mysteries, holiness, and earthly happiness of those who are considered to be about to live in it, to be expected before the coming of Christ to the final judgment? The millennial kingdom of Christ, most conspicuous and most flourishing in the extraordinary knowledge of divine mysteries, holiness of life, and earthly happiness of those who are considered to be about to live in it, is not to be expected by the children of God in these lands. This is the antithesis of 1) The Jews, who so corrupted the prophecies of the holy prophets concerning the most ample kingdom of the Messiah, that they believed it would be splendid with a certain pomp and earthly glory, that the Jewish religion would be propagated far and wide, and that the nations adverse to it would be destroyed.

To this pertains what the Pharisees asked of Christ in Luke 17:20: When would the kingdom of God come? Concerning the dreams of the Jews of today, see Buxtorf, in synagog. iudaic. c. 36, p. 645 ff.

2) Cerinthus, contemporary with the Apostles themselves, or at least with John, partly addicted to Judaism and circumcised, who, since he was born for his belly, dared to measure the millennial kingdom of Christ by the pleasures of the flesh, as witnessed by Dionysius of Alexandria in Eusebius, hist. eccl. book 3, c. 28.

3) Papias, bishop of Hierapolis, σφόδρα μικρῷ τὸν νοῦν, i.e., of a judgment not very refined, and a lover of unwritten traditions, who defined the millennial kingdom by the holy delights of the soul, and then by the pleasures of the body, but lawful ones.

He was followed by Tertullian, Lactantius, Apollinaris, Coracion, and especially Nepos the Egyptian. Cf. Gerhard, Loci theol. de consummat. sæculi § 67. But indeed, the most learned fathers, Dionysius of Alexandria, Jerome, Augustine, and others, refuted the fable of such a millennial kingdom of Christ. See Philastrius, hæref. 59; Epiphanius, hæref. 77.

4) As the papacy grew strong, the millennial kingdom was defended by Joachim, Abbot of Fiore, Ubertinus de Casali, and the Bishop of Chiemsee, author of the book which is called Onus Ecclesiæ , concerning which see Flacius in catal. testium veritatis , book 18, p. 1795.

5) The Fanatics and Anabaptists, concerning whose frenzies Phil. Melanchthon wrote in Opp. vol. 1: The Anabaptists affirm that it is necessary that before the last day such a kingdom of Christ exist on earth, in which the pious rule, and oppress and destroy all impious kings.

6) Caspar Schwenckfeld, who, having awaited a certain new kingdom of Christ, in his published book de triplici hominum vita , c. 43, intending to distinguish his opinion from the Cerinthian and Anabaptist, argues thus: Our opinion is, therefore, that we hope that the Lord and Head of the Church, Christ Jesus, will yet spread his heavenly kingdom with power, Spirit, and blessing over us poor ones, gather the scattered children of God in the Holy Spirit, yes, beget many of them through the Word of Truth, and let his knowledge and glory shine forth more brightly, so that he will endow the Church and its members with more grace, light, and understanding, and richer spiritual gifts, so that also men will be more zealous, more spiritual, more pious, and more godly. Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombast von Hohenheim, from the Hermitage of the Swiss, born of a noble family, commonly called Paracelsus, pressed his thumb to this, who asserted that a golden age was still inflating, which he also called the age of the Holy Spirit.

Valentin Weigel followed Schwenckfeld and Theophrastus; he was pastor of Tzschocha near Freiberg in Meissen, and, having assumed the name Ulrich Wegweiser of Utopia and published a book on the wondrous work, he established three ages: I. of the Father, who drowned his enemies in a flood of water; II. of the Son, who destroyed his enemies in a flood of blood; III. of the Holy Spirit, who will blot out his adversaries in a flood of fire.

Furthermore, dreams about the millennial kingdom of Christ have been approved by HENRICUS NICOLAI, ESAIAS STIFELIUS, EGIDIUS GUTMANN, EZECHIEL METH, DAVID GEORGIUS, JACOB BOEHME, the shoemaker of Görlitz, the brethren of the Rosy Cross, QUIRINUS KUHLMANN, CHRISTIANUS HOURGIUS, JOH. GUIL. PETERSENIUS, Quakers, and many others by far.

Cf. PFEIFER’S Antichiliasm, and D. NEUMANN’S Antichiliastic disputation. ΕΚΘΕΣΙΣ (Exposition).

Latin:

Finis iudicii extremi principalis est gloria iudicis coelestis a). Finis minus principalis est electorum introductio in regnum gloriae, & reproborum abiectio actualis in ignem aeternum b).

Prob. a. Ex 2 Thess. I, 10. Veniet Dominus, ut glorificetur in sanctis suis. Glorificabitur Christus in sanctis: 1) quia ipsis, tanquam suis membris, perennem gloriam communicabit: 2) quia ab ipsis non fine summa admiratione glorificabitur. Etenim magno illo die clarissime emicabit admiranda iudicis coelestis iustitia remuneratoria & vindicativa, cum ineffabili misericordia, sapientia & potentia coniuncta. 5. Extremum iudicium est medium isagogicum immittendi pios in beatitudinem, & detrudendi impios in æternos cruciatus. Quæst. XV. An regnum Christi millenarium, eximia mysteriorum diuinorum cognitione, sanctitate, terrenaque felicitate eorum, qui in eodem victuri esse censentur, conspicuum ante aduentum Christi ad iudicium extremum expectandum est? Regnum Christi millenarium, eximia mysteriorum diuinorum cognitione, sanctitate vitæ, terrenaque felicitate eorum, qui in eodem victuri esse censentur, maxime conspicuum, florentissimumque, filiis Dei in his terris non est expectandum. Antithesis est 1) Iudæorum, qui sanctorum prophetarum vaticinia de amplissimo Messiæ regno ita deprauarunt, vt illud pompa quadam, & terrena gloria splendidum futurum, religionem iudaicam longe lateque propagandam, gentes autem ei aduersas destruendas crederent.

Quo pertinet, quod Luc. XVII, 20. Pharisæi ex Christo quæsierunt: quando futurum esset regnum Dei? De hodiernorum Iudæorum somniis BVTORF. in synagog. iudaic. c. XXXVI. p. 645. seqq.

2) Cerinthi, ipsis Apostolis, aut saltem Ioanni, coæui, Iudaismo ex parte addicti, & circumcisi, qui cum esset abdomini natus, regnum Christi millenarium voluptatibus carnis metiri ausus est, teste DIONYSIO ALEXANDRINO apud Eusebium, libr. III. hist. eccl. c. XXVIII.

3) Papiæ, Hieropolitani præsulis, σφόδρα μικρῷ τὸν νοῦν, i. e. iudicii non admodum exasciati, & traditionum non-scriptarum amatoris, qui regnum millenarium sanctis animæ deliciis, tum oblectamentis corporis, sed licitis, definivit.

Secuti ipsum sunt TERTULLIANVS, LACTANTIVS, APOLLINARIVS, CORACION, & in primis NEPOS Ægyptius. Conf. GERHARD. LL. theol. de consummat. sæculi §. 67. At vero fabulam de eiusmodi regno Christi millenario confutarunt patres doctissimi, DIONYSIVS Alexandrinus, HIERONYMVS, AVGVSTINVS & alii.

Vid. PHILASTR. hæref. LIX. EPIPH. hæref. LXXVII. 4) Inualefcente papatu regnum millenarium defenderunt IOACHIMVS, Abbas Florensis, VBERTINVS de Casali, & Episcopus Chemenfis, auctor libri, qui vocatur onus ecclesiæ, de quo vid. FLACIVS in catal. testium veritatis, libr. XVIII. p. 1795.

5) Fanaticorum & Anabaptistarum, de quorum furoribus PHIL. MELANCHTHON tom. I. Opp. scripsit: Anabaptistæ affirmant, oportere ante nouissimum diem in terris regnum Christi tale exsistere, in quo pii dominentur, & omnes reges impios opprimant & deleant.

6) CASP. SCHWENCKFELDII, qui nouum quoddam Christi regnum prællolatus, edito libro de triplici hominum vita, c. XLIII, sententiam suam a Cerinthiana & Anabaptistica distincturus, ita disserit: Unsere Meynung, ist also, daß wir hoffen, daß der Herr und das Haupt der Kirchen, Christus Jesus, werde noch sein himmlisches Reich mit Kraft, Geist und Seegen über uns Arme ausbreiten, die zerstreuten Kinder Gottes im heiligen Geist versammlen, ja derer viel durch das Wort der Wahrheit erzeugen, und seine Erkänntniß und Herrlichkeit heller herfür lassen dringen, daß er mit mehr Gnade, Licht und Verstand, und reichern geistlichen Gaben die Kirche und derselben Glieder werde begaben, daß auch die Menschen eifriger, geistlicher, frömmer und gottseliger seyn werden.

Huic pollicem pressit PHILIPPVS AVREOLVS THEOPHRASTVS BOMBAST ab HOHENHEIM, ex Eremo Heluetiorum, nobili familia oriundus, vulgo dictus PARACELSVS, qui asseruit, inflare adhuc aureum sæculum, quod etiam vocauit faculum Spiritus S. Schwenckfeldium & Theophrastum secutus est VALENTINVS WEGELIVS, pastor Tzschopensis prope Freibergam in Misnia, qui assumto nomine Vdalrici Wegweisers Vtopiensis, & edito libro de opere mirabili, tria constituit sæcula: I. Patris, qui hostes suos submersit diluuio aqueo: II. Filii, qui inimicos suos perdidit diluuio sanguineo: III. Spiritus S. qui aduersarios suos delebit diluuio igneo.

Ceterum somnia de regno Christi millenario approbarunt HENRICVS NICOLAI, ESAIAS STIFELIVS, EGIDIVS GVTMANN, EZECHIEL METH, DAVID GEORGIVS, IACOB BOEHME, sutor Gorlicensis, fratres roseæ crucis, QVIRINVS KVHLMANN, CHRISTIANVS HOVRGIVS, iò. GVIL. PETERSENIVS, Quackeri & alii longe plurimi.

Conf. PFEIFERI antichiliasmum, & D. NEVMANNI disput. antichiliast. ΕΚΘΕΣΙΣ.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: Obs

Obs.

I. The false dogma concerning the kingdom of Christ is commonly called chiliasm, from the Greek word χιλιας, or χιλιαδες, a thousand; AUGUSTINE, in De haeresibus ad Quodvultdeum, ch. 8, translates [it] Milliaflas; elsewhere, in L. XX. de C. D. [De Civitate Dei], Millarios; PHILASTRIUS, in Heresies LIX, Chilionetitas.

They are called Millenarii by ISIDORE, L. VIII. de etymol.

Obs. II. Chiliasts do not cherish one single opinion concerning the blessed millennium in these lands.

For which reason D. AFFELMANN, in Heptad. quaest., reduced the Chiliasts to five classes.

I. It is that of those who write that Christ will return corporally before the last day, and will establish such a kingdom on this earth.

II. Those who restrict it more specifically to the land of Canaan, into which they say the Jews are to be brought back.

III. Those who claim the happiness of some millennium only for the martyrs who are to be resurrected before the final day.

IV. Those who understand a spiritual happiness, and refer it to the destruction of the Anti-Christ, the extinction of the Turk, the overthrow of heretics, the ceasing of persecutions, and the catholic evangelical church.

V. Those who interpret that happiness both spiritually and corporally, and promise it to us as great as it was in paradise before the fall, before the final judgment.

Obs. III. Some Theologians distinguish Chiliasm into gross, or Cerinthian, and subtle, or Papian.

The former measures the blessed millennium by illicit pleasures of the flesh; the latter by delights of both body and soul that are licit and honest. See

D.

HANNEKEN, de moribus regni Christi §.

6. Others, however, prefer a trichotomy, who distinguish between gross, subtle, and most subtle Chiliasm.

Gross is Cerinthian, subtle is Papian, most subtle is Schwenckfeldian and Weigelian; although they do not agree in everything even here. In this, however, the Chiliasts conspire: a) that they establish with great consensus that there will be a greater illumination of the Holy Spirit and a more excellent knowledge of divine mysteries in the millennial kingdom than in this spiritual kingdom of grace: b) that the members of the chiliastic kingdom will be perfectly holy: c) that, with afflictions ceasing, peace and earthly happiness in that most blessed millennium will be most pleasant and most abundant: and therefore the martyrs will rise again, so that, since they endured such dire tortures in these lands, they may be rendered partakers of that earthly prosperity: d) that the conversion of the Jews in the most prosperous millennium will be so solemn, clear, and illustrious that it deserves to be called universal: e) that the death of the Roman Anti-Christ and his total excision will undoubtedly come to pass.

We shall weigh each of these with an impartial estimation of mind. ΒΕΒΑΙΩΣΙΣ (Confirmation).

We prove the assertion.

I. We say from the God-breathed Word that the kingdom of Christ is threefold.

For the kingdom of Christ is either the kingdom of power, or of grace, or of glory. The millennial kingdom is neither the kingdom of power, nor of grace, nor of glory.

It is not the kingdom of power; because in it, the subjects of Christ are not only all creatures, but all men, both pious and impious, and even the evil spirits themselves. But these are not said to be in the millennial kingdom.

Nor is this the kingdom of grace. For a) the kingdom of grace is already present; but the chiliastic kingdom as it is expected to be in the future. b) The kingdom of grace is spiritual, not secular, and therefore not to be estimated by earthly happiness, John 18:36, inasmuch as it does not come μετὰ παρατηρήσεως, with observation, i.e., μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας, with much outward show, with royal splendor, riches, and triumph, such as the Pharisees expected, and as the Jews still expect today, as GROTIUS explains, but it is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit, Rom. 14:17. But the millennial kingdom, according to the opinion of the Chiliasts, is conspicuous for the external splendor of earthly happiness. Nor is it the kingdom of glory: because this is eternal, not to be defined by a span of a thousand years. We conclude: Whatever kingdom is neither the kingdom of power, nor the kingdom of grace, nor the kingdom of glory, that is not the true kingdom of Christ, but is a being of reason, and a dream of waking men: But the chiliastic kingdom is neither, etc. Therefore.

II. In the millennial kingdom there cannot be a greater illumination of the Holy Spirit than there was in the kingdom of grace in the times of the Apostles: But the θεογνωσία (knowledge of God) in the kingdom of grace in the times of the Apostles was imperfect. Therefore. The major is established; because the Apostles were men θεόπνευστοι (God-breathed), 2 Pet. 1:21, who most wisely expounded the way to heaven. The minor is evident from 1 Cor. 13:9, 10. We know in part, and we prophesy in part: but when that which is perfect is come, then that which is in part shall be done away. For now we see through a glass in a riddle, but then face to face. The Apostle gives the reason for the imperfect knowledge of God in 2 Cor. 5:6, 7. While we dwell in the body, we are absent from the Lord: for we walk by faith, not by sight (appearance). For which reason Paul says that he is not made perfect, Phil. 3:12.

III. The citizens of the millennial kingdom cannot excel in a more perfect holiness than that with which the Apostles were endowed: But these were endowed with an imperfect holiness; of which imperfection the Apostles themselves complain. Paul, Rom. 7: 18. I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, dwelleth no good thing. For to will is present with me; but how to perform that which is good I find not. John, 1 ep. 1:8. If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. James, ep. c. 3:2. In many things we offend all. As long as men shall behold this light on this earth, they are to pray: Lord, forgive us our debts! Matt. 6. Therefore, on this earth, until the day of the final judgment, perfectly holy men will not live.

IV. Christ teaches, Matt. 13:30, that it will come to pass that the tares shall grow together with the wheat until the harvest, and he understands by the tares the children τοῦ πονηροῦ, i.e., of the devil, by the wheat, or good seed, the children of the kingdom, by the harvest the end of the world, and asserts that the reapers, or angels, will finally gather the tares at the harvest and burn them with fire. Therefore. The field of the church before the conflagration of the world will not be devoid of tares, but the segregation of the evil goats from the holy sheep will take place finally on the day of the final judgment, Matt. 25:32.

V. Whoever in this world are subject to many afflictions and persecutions, they cannot promise themselves perpetual halcyon days on this earth; But all the beloved children of God, etc. The minor is proved from John 16:33. These things I have spoken unto you, that in me ye might have peace; in the world ye shall have tribulation. By these afflictions all the pious are chastised in this life before they are transferred into heavenly glory. The words of the Holy Spirit are clear, Heb. 12:6. Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth: and scourgeth every son whom he receiveth. 2 Tim. 3:12. All that will live godly in Christ Jesus shall suffer persecution. Acts 14:22. Through much tribulation we must enter into the kingdom of heaven.

VI. The state of the church, or of the kingdom of Christ, toward the end of the world, on account of the most corrupt morals of the impious, and the most bitter afflictions of the pious, will be most turbulent and most sorrowful. Therefore the kingdom of Christ toward the end of the world will not flourish or stand out in eminent holiness and earthly happiness. The Apostles confirm the antecedent; Paul, 2 Tim. III, 1. This know also, that in the last days perilous times shall come. For men shall be lovers of their own selves, covetous, boasters, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God, covetous, boasters, lo-

...headstrong, arrogant, blasphemous, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, profane, devoid of charity, truce-breakers, slanderers, intemperate, fierce, not lovers of the good, traitors, headlong, puffed up, lovers of pleasures more than lovers of God, having a form of godliness but denying its power: and turn away from these! Peter, 2 ep. III, 3. Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last of the days mockers, who shall walk according to their own lusts, and shall say: Where is the promise of his coming? Jude v. 17. But you, beloved, remember the words which were spoken before by the Apostles of our Lord, Jesus Christ: for they told you that in the last time there shall be mockers, who shall walk according to their own lusts in impiety. But if the face of the last times shall be so foul and so sad, then surely the kingdom of Christ in that stretch of time will flourish neither by the holiness of many men nor by the earthly happiness of a few elect.

VII. That the solemn advent of Christ, contrasted with the daily advent of grace, is only twofold—and indeed the former humble, the latter sublime and majestic—is evident from the sacred letters and the more ancient symbols. Paul says explicitly in Heb. IX, 28: Christ, having been offered once to bear the sins of many, shall appear a second time without sin to those who wait for him for salvation. That this second advent shall be visible and conspicuous in the clouds is clear from Acts I, 11; Matt. XXIV, 30; immediately joined with the resurrection of the dead, the final judgment, and the consummation of the age, Matt. XXIV, 27; ch. XXV, 31; 2 Thess. I, 7. Concerning which the Apostolic symbol testifies in the clearest words: From whence he shall come to judge the living and the dead. If Christ shall appear in his second majestic advent in the clouds for the purpose of resurrecting the dead, judging them, and consuming this world, he does not come to establish a millennial kingdom in this world: The antecedent is true; and the consequent [follows].

VIII. At the same time that all impious, unjust, and reprobate men shall rise again, at that same time all pious, just, and elect men—and thus also all pious martyrs—are to rise again: But on the last day all impious men, etc. Therefore. The minor is clear: because Christ most openly teaches the simultaneous resurrection of the pious and the impious, John V, 28: The hour is coming (it will come as certainly as if it were present) in which all who are in the tombs shall hear his voice, and shall come forth; those who have done good, unto the resurrection of life, but those who have done evil, unto the resurrection of judgment. Cf. Dan. XII, 2. That this universal and simultaneous resurrection is to happen on the last day, the Savior affirms in John VI, 40: This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life, and I will raise him up on the last day. Cf. John XI, 24; ch. XII, 48; Acts XVII, 31.

IX. That souls which receive the retribution of a most splendid reward for temporal affliction in heaven are sent back by God from heaven into bodies for the sake of earthly happiness is incredible: But the reborn souls, released from their bodies, along with all pious men, and especially the martyrs, etc. Therefore. The major is established: because earthly happiness is in many parts less than heavenly rewards. But if God were to send back souls enjoying heavenly rewards into bodies living on these earths, their blessed state would not be advanced to something greater, but would be diminished by an immense amount. The minor is clear from the words of Christ, Matt. V, 12: rejoice and be glad, for your reward shall be abundant in heaven: there is the crown of righteousness, 2 Tim. IV, 8.

X. True Christians at every moment watch for their salvation, for the reason that they expect the sudden and unknown advent of Christ for judgment: Therefore, true Christians do not expect a blessed millennium that would precede the final judgment. The antecedent is proven from the clear words of the Savior, Mark XIII, 31: Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words... will not pass away. But of that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels who are in heaven, nor the Son, but the Father. Watch, stay awake and pray, for you do not know when the time will be.

But if Christ is to come to judgment only after a millennium: what need is there for such a grave exhortation to consider the extreme judgment of Christ, and to weigh it without omitting anything? According to the mind of the Savior, the day of the final judgment should be unknown to us. But if the universal judgment is to be held after a millennium, which is thought not to have begun even today, it is most exactly certain to us that Christ will not come to judgment within the course of many years.

XI. The hypothesis concerning the millennial kingdom of Christ does not kindle piety, but extinguishes it, or at the very least slows its course.

For a) through the Chiliastic hypothesis, men are turned away from the desire for heavenly and spiritual goods, which desire is nevertheless that of true Christians, Rom. VIII, 23. Phil. III, 20. b) The Chiliastic opinion fosters the security of men who think nothing, or little, of the final judgment. For, fascinated by this opinion once it is accepted, they persuade themselves that the advent of Christ is very far off, and therefore that one must live for the day. c) Through the Chiliastic opinion, an opportunity is provided to men greedy for novelty, and more apt for disturbing things than for managing them, to incite rebellion against the ordinary magistracy. This perverse opinion in the previous century excited and raised the spirits of the rustics to refuse the authority of the magistrate.

Latin:

Obs.

I. Falsum de regno Christi dogma vulgo appellatur chiliasmus, ex græca voce χιλιας, vel χιλιαδες, mille, Chiliastas AVGVSTINVS de hæres. ad Quod vult Deum, c. 8. vertit Milliaflas alibi L. XX. de C. D. Millarios, PHILASTRIvs hæres. LIX. Chilionetitas.

Mille-narii dicuntur ab ISIDORO L. VIII. de etymol.

Obs. II. Chiliastæ de beato in his terris millennio non vnam fouent sententiam.

Qua de causa D. AFFELMANNVS in heptad. quæst. Chiliastas ad quinque classes reduxit.

I. Eorum est, qui Christum corporaliter ante diem nouissimum rediturum scribunt, & in hac terra tale regnum institururum.

II. Qui specialius ad terram Canaan restringunt, in quam Iudæos reducendorum dicunt.

III. Qui solis martyribus ante extremum diem resuscitandis millenarii alicuius felicitatem vindicant.

IV. Qui spiritualem felicitatem intelligunt, eamque ad deletum Anti-Christum, exstinctum Turcam, euersos hæreticos, cessantes persecutiones & ec-clesiam catholicæ euangelicam referunt.

V. Qui & spiritualiter & corporaliter felicitatem eam interpretantur, illamque tantam nobis, quanta ante lapsum in paradiso fuit, ante extremum iudicium pollicentur.

Obs. III. Nonnulli Theologi Chiliasmum in crassum, siue Cerinthiacum, & subtilem, siue Papiensem distinguunt.

Ille beatum millennnium voluptatibus carnis illicitis; hic deliciis tam corporis, quam animi licitis & honestis metitur. Vid.

D.

HANNEKEN. de moribus regni Christi §.

6. Alii autem placet τριχοτομια, qui distinguunt inter Chiliasmum crassum, subtilem, & subtilissimum.

Crassus est Cerinthianus, subtilis Papienfis, subtilissimus Schwenck-feldianus, & Weigelianus; quamuis neque hic per omnia consentiant. In hoc tamen Chi-liastæ conspirant: a) quod magno consensu statuunt, maiorem Spiritus S. illuminationem, & excellentiorem mysteriorum diuinorum cognitionem fore in regno millenario, quam in hoc spirituali gratiæ regno: b) Membra regni chiliastici fore perfecte sancta: c) Cessan-tibus afflictionibus, pacem & felicitatem terrenam in perbeato isto millennio iucundissimam, vberrimamque futuram esse: ideoque resurrecturos esse martyres, vt, cum in his terris tam diros sustinuerint cruciatus, illius terrestris prosperitatis reddantur compotes: d) Conuersio-nem Iudæorum in prosperrimo millennio adeo solemnem, luculentam & illustrem fore, vt vniuersalis dici mereatur: e) Anti-Christi Romani interitum, & excisionem totalem indabi-tato futuram.

Quæ singula æqua animi æstimatione pensitaturi sumus. ΒΕΒΑΙΩΣΙΣ.

Probamus assertum.

I. Regnum Christi triplex esse, e verbo Θεοπνευςω dicimus.

Etenim regnum Christi est vel regnum potentia, vel gratia, vel gloria. Regnum millena-rium neque regnum potentiæ, neque gratiæ, neque gloriæ est.

Non est regnum pote tiæ; quia in illo subditi Christi sunt cum omnes creaturæ, tum cuncti homines, tam pii, quam impii, quin ipsi etiam cacodæmones. At hi non dicuntur esse in regno millenario.

Neque hoc est regnum gratiæ. Nam a) regnum gratiæ iam præsens est; at regnum chiliasticum vt futurum exspectatur. b) Regnum gratiae est spirituale, non saeculare, atque adeo terrena felicitate non aestimandum, Io. XVIII, 36. quippe quod non venit μετὰ παρατηρήσεως, cum observatione i. e. μετὰ πολλῆς φαντασίας, cum regio splendore, divitiis triumpho, qualia exspectabant Pharisaei, & nunc quoque iudaei exspectant, exponente GROTIO, sed est iustitia, pax & gaudium in Spiritu S. Rom. XIV, 17. At regnum millenarium, Chiliastarum sententia, est externo splendore terrenae felicitatis conspicuum. Neque est regnum gloriae: quia hoc est aeternum, non spatio mille annorum definiendum. Colligimus: Quodcunque regnum neque est regnum potentiae, neque regnum gratiae, neque regnum gloriae, illud non est verum Christi regnum, sed est ens rationis, & somnium hominum vigilantium: Atqui regnum chiliasticum neque est &c. E.

II. In regno millenario non potest esse maior Spiritus S. illuminatio, quam fuit in regno gratiae temporibus Apostolorum: Atqui θεογνωσία in regno gratiae temporibus Apostolorum fuit imperfecta. E. Maior constat; quia Apostoli fuerunt viri θεόπνευστοι, 2 Petr. I, 21. qui viam ad coelum sapientissime exposuerunt. Minor patet ex 1 Cor. XIII, 9, 10. Ex parte cognoscimus, & ex parte prophetamus: quando vero venerit perfectum, tunc, quod ex parte est, abrogabitur. Videmus enim nunc per speculum in aenigmate, tunc vero a facie ad faciem. Rationem imperfectae Deo notitiae reddit Apostolus 2 Cor. V, 6, 7. Dum habitamus in corpore, peregrinamur a Domino: per fidem enim ambulamus, non per speciem (conspectum). Qua de caussa Paullus dicit, se non esse consummatum, Phil. III, 12.

III. Ciues regni millenarii non possunt perfectiori eminere sanctitate, quam qua praediti fuerunt Apostoli: At hi praediti fuerunt sanctitate imperfecta; de qua imperfectione ipsimet Apostoli conqueruntur. Paullus Rom. VII, 18. Noui, quod non habitet in me, hoc est in carne mea, bonum. Velle enim, adiacet mihi; sed operari bonum, non inuenio Ioannes, 1 ep. I, 8. Si dixerimus, quod peccatum non habeamus, nos ipsos seducimus, & veritas non est in nobis. Iacobus, epist. c. III, 2. Saepe labimur omnes. Quamdiu in his terris homines hanc lucem intuebuntur, precaturi sunt: Domine, remitte nobis debita nostra! Matth. VI. Ergo in hac terra, vsque ad diem extremi iudicii, non viuent homines perfecte sancti.

IV. Docet Christus, Matth. XIII, 30. futurum esse, vt zizania una cum tritico crescant, vsque ad messem, & intelligit per zizania filios τοῦ πονηροῦ, i. e. diaboli, per triticum, siue bonum semen, filios regni, per messem consummationem seculi, atque asserit, messores, siue angelos, demum in messe collecturos esse zizania, atque igne combusturos. E. Ager ecclesiae ante conflagrationem mundi non erit expers zizaniorum, sed segregatio malorum hircorum a sanctis ouibus fiet demum in die extremi iudicii, Matth. XXV, 32.

V. Quicunque in hoc mundo plurimis afflictionibus & persecutionibus subiacent, illi perpetua in his terris halcyonia sibi promittere nequeunt; Atqui omnes dilecti filii Dei, &c. Minor prob. ex Io. XVI, 33. Haec locutus sum vobis, vt in me pacem habeatis; in mundo afflictionem habetis. His afflictionibus omnes pii castigantur prius in hac vita, quam in gloriam coelestem transferuntur. Perspicua sunt verba Spiritus S. Hebr. XII, 6. Quem diligit Dominus, corrigit: castigat autem omnem filium, quem suscipit. 2 Tim. III, 12. Omnes, qui volunt pie viuere in Christo Iesu, persecutiones patientur. Act. XIV, 22. Per multas afflictiones oportet nos ingredi in regnum coelorum.

VI. Status ecclesiae, siue regni Christi sub finem mundi propter mores impiorum corruptissimos, & afflictiones piorum acerbissimas, erit turbulentissimus atque tristissimus. Ergo regnum Christi sub finem mundi eximia sanctitate, terrenaque felicitate non florebit, aut eminebit. Antecedens confirmant Apostoli; Paullus, 2 Tim. III, 1. Hoc vero scito, quod in extremis diebus instabunt tempora difficilia. Erunt enim homines sui amantes, auari, fastuosi, fui amantes, auari, fa-

stuosi, superbi, blasphemi, parentibus inobedientes, ingrati, profani, caritatis expertes, fœdifragi, calumniatores, intemperantes, immites, bonum non amantes, proditores, præcipites, inflati, voluptatum magis, quam Dei amantes, habentes speciem pietatis, virtutem vero eius abnegantes: & hos auersare! Petrus, 2 ep. III, 3. Hoc primo agnoscentes, quod venturi sint in extremate dierum empactæ, qui secundum proprias concupiscentias ambulaturi, & dicturi sunt: Vbi est promissio aduentus ipsius? Iudas v. 17. Vos vero, dilecti, mementote verborum, quæ pridem dicta sunt ab Apostolis Domini nostri, Iesu Christi: dixerunt enim vobis, quod in extremo tempore futuri sint illusores, qui iuxta suas ipsorum concupiscentias ambulaturi impietatem. Quod si vltimorum temporum tam tetra, tamque tristis erit facies, vtique regnum Christi eo temporum tractu nec plurimorum hominum sanctitate, nec paucorum electorum terrena felicitate florebit.

VII. Aduentum Christi solemne quotidiano gratiæ aduentui contradistinctum, esse tantum geminum, & quidem priorem humilem, posteriorem sublimem & maiestaticum, e sacris litteris, & antiquioribus symbolis patelcit. Paullus diferte dicit Hebr. IX, 28. Christus semel oblatus ad perferendum multorum peccata, ex deuteres, secunda vice sine peccato videbitur ipsum exspectantibus in salutem. Secundum illum aduentum fore visibilem & conspicuum in nubibus, liquet ex Act. I, 11. Matth. XXIV, 30. immediate coniunctum cum mortuorum resurrectione, extremo iudicio, & consummatione sæculi, Matth. XXIV, 27. c. XXV, 31. 2 Thess. I, 7. De quo testatur symbolum Apostolicum verbis clarissimis: Vnde venturus est, iudicare viuos & mortuos. Si Christus eo fine aduentu suo secundo maiestatico in nubibus apparebit, vt mortuos resuscitet, iudicet, & hunc mundum consummet; non venit ad constituendum in hoc mundo regnum millenarium: Antecedens est verum: E & consequens.

VIII. Quo tempore omnes homines impii, iniusti & reprobi resurgent, eodem tempore simul omnes pii, iusti & electi, adeoque etiam omnes pii martyres resurrecturi sunt: Atqui in die nouissimo omnes homines impii &c. Ergo. Minor claret: quia simultaneam piorum & impiorum resurrectionem Christus apertissime docet, Io. V, 28. Venit hora (æque certo veniet, ac si in præsenti adesset) in qua omnes, qui in monumentis sunt, audient vocem eius, & prodibunt, qui bona fecerunt, in resurrectionem vitæ, qui vero mala fecerunt, in resurrectionem iudicii. Conf. Dan. XII, 2. Quod hæc resurrectio vniuersalis & simultanea futura fit in die nouissimo, affirmat Saluator Io. VI, 4. Hæc est voluntas eius, qui misit me, vt omnis, qui videt Filium, & credit in ipsum, habeat vitam æternam, & resuscita-bo illum in nouissimo die. Conf. Io. XI, 24. c. XII, 48. Act. XVII, 31.

IX. Quæ animæ retributionem præmii splendidissimi pro temporali afflictione accipiunt in cœlo, illas e cœlo ad consortium terrenæ felicitatis a Deo corporibus denuo immitti, incredibile est: Atqui animæ renatæ, a corporibus solutæ, cum omnium hominum piorum, tum inprimis martyrum &c. Ergo. Maior constat: quia felicitas terrena multis partibus minor est præmiis cœlestibus. Quod si Deus animas fruentes præmiis cœlestibus, denuo immitteret corporibus in his terris degentibus, beatus earum flatus non proueheretur in maius, sed immane quantum imminueretur. Minor claret verbis Christi, Matth. V, 12. gaudete & exsultate, quoniam merces vestra copiosa erit in cœlis: ibi est corona iustitiæ, 2 Tim. IV, 8.

X. Veri Christiani quouis momento in salutem suam vigilant, propterea, quod fubitaneum, & sibi ignotum aduentum Christi ad iudicium exspectant: E. veri Christiani beatum millennium, quod extremum iudicium antecedat, non exspectant. Antecedens probatur e perspicuis Saluatoris verbis, Marc. XIII, 31. Cœlum & terra transibunt: verba autem mea non transibunt. De die tamen ista, & hora nemo scit, neque angeli, qui in caelo, neque Filius, sed Pater. Videte, vigilate & orate, non enim scitis, quando tempus futurum sit.

Quod si post millennium demum venturus est Christus ad iudicium: quid opus est tam gravi adhortatione ad iudicium Christi extremum considerandum, & nullo praetermisso depensandum? Ex mente Salvatoris dies extremi iudicii nobis ignotus esto. At, si post millennium, quod hodie nondum coepisse putatur, iudicium universale habebitur, exactissime nobis constat, intra decursum plurimorum annorum Christum ad iudicium non esse venturum.

XI. Hypothesis de regno Christi millenario pietatem non accendit, sed exstinguit, aut certe cursum eius sufflaminat.

Nam a) per hypothesin Chiliasticam homines avertuntur a desiderio bonorum caelestium & spiritualium, quod desiderium tamen est verorum Christianorum, Rom. VIII, 23. Phil. III, 20. b) Alit opinio Chiliastica securitatem hominum, de extremo iudicio aut nihil, aut parum cogitantium. Sublata quippe hac opinione fascinati, sibi persuadent, adventum Christi longissime abesse, adeoque in diem esse vivendum. c) Per opinionem Chiliasticam hominibus novitatis avidis, & rebus turbandis, quam gerendis, aptioribus subministratur occasio ad rebellionem concitandam adversus ordinarium magistratum. Haec perversa opinio superiori saeculo animos rusticorum ad detrectandum magistratum imperium excitavit & erexit.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: Dissolution

DISSOLUTION

The Chiliasts object.

I. That the Apostle John most openly teaches the millennial kingdom of Christ, Apoc. XX, 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. & 8. whose words are most worthy of being remembered.

Afterward I saw an angel descending from heaven, who had the key of the abyss, and a great chain in his hand. He seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan: and bound him for a thousand years: and cast him into the abyss, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, so that he would not seduce the nations anymore, until the thousand years were completed. But afterward he must be released for a little time.

Furthermore, I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given to them: and also the souls of those beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of God, and who did not worship the beast, nor his image, and they reigned with Christ for a thousand years. But the rest of the dead did not live again, until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection. Blessed and holy is he who has a part in the first resurrection. For over these the second death has no power: but they will be priests of God, and of Christ, and will reign with him for a thousand years. But when the thousand years have been completed, Satan will be released from his custody, and will go out to seduce the nations.

Resp.
