1) Because the apocalyptic book is prophetic, full of both most abstruse prophetic visions and allegorical and quasi-enigmatic forms of speech, and difficult to understand, it must therefore be explained according to the analogy of faith, built upon clear and perspicuous passages of Scripture (*).

2) The Chiliasts cannot clearly [prove] from the cited passage to show in detail the solemn advent of Christ for the establishment of a millennial kingdom, in which, a) men live endowed with perfect θεογνωσίᾳ [knowledge of God], excelling in consummate holiness, and enjoying earthly happiness, b) the martyrs rise again, c) all Jews are converted, & d) under the beginning of which the Anti-Christ is overthrown.

Furthermore, that we may perceive the mind of the Apostle more deeply, we shall first give a succinct paraphrase of the words adduced, then we shall briefly respond to those things which are objected.

The words of John are: Καὶ εἶδον, & I saw (the Apostle indicates the order of the visions, not the order of the events) an angel (to wit, the uncreated one, Christ, who alone crushes, binds, and abolishes Satan, according to Gen. III, 15. Luke XI, 22. Heb. II, 14) descending from heaven (manifesting himself in a singular manner, and exerting his power by a certain miraculous work: for to descend from heaven is frequently said in Holy Scripture κατ’ ἀνθρωποπάθειαν [according to human mode of speech] concerning the most omnipresent God, when He manifests the presence of His power and grace by some singular work; see Gen. XI, 5. c. XVIII, 21.) who had the key of the abyss, and a great chain in his hand (the key is a symbol of authority, Apoc. I, 18. the abyss denotes hell: but the great chain symbolically designates both the prevailing power of Christ, and the subjection and punishment of the devil, Cf. 2 Pet. III, 4. Jude v. 6.): He laid hold of the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan (John proceeds gradually, and teaches, a) that Satan was laid hold of, who was then seducing both Gentiles and Jews, through paganism and idolatry, as well as through manifold heresies.

On account of this, Christ then, both immediately and through the Apostles, attacked and conquered him with great force) and bound him (He teaches b) the binding of Satan, or his restraint, because he was drawn back and checked from the horrible seduction of the nations, lest he rage so freely and at his own will. However, the binding is understood not as absolute, but as limited; for even to a bound dog is given some space, within which he can rage, harm, and bite), and cast him into the abyss (The Apostle teaches c) the precipitation of Satan into the abyss. Now Satan is said to be cast into the abyss when public dominion is taken away from him. Which happened at that time when the shrines of the pagans were destroyed, the altars torn down, and the magic books burned), and shut him up, and set a seal upon him (He teaches now d) the sealing of Satan, by which the license to go out, to wander, and to harm was taken away from him) that he should not seduce the nations (with violent and tyrannical seduction, through kings and gentile emperors, devoted to idolatry, who had persecuted the church by warlike assault, and had hindered the public preaching of the gospel) until the thousand years should be finished (There are those who take this number indefinitely, for a great interval of time; others wish for a definite millennial time to be expressed; since it does not seem likely that John would say χίλια ἔτη [thousand years] six times, and four times indeed with the article, τὰ χίλια ἔτη.

Nor yet is it permitted to define the epoch of a thousand years by some mathematical point. But if, therefore, we cannot precisely determine the year, it suffices for us to point out the age of the satanic binding and loosing.

Wherefore, the beginning of the satanic binding [was] in the IV century, with Constantine the Great holding power, but the beginning of the diabolical loosing [was] in the XIV century, in which the Ottoman kingdom was erected. The sharpest censors think they have found a defense far more firm, indeed almost the only one, upon which their whole opinion rests. If there were any millennium, 1) still to be expected, 2) such as those dreamers have already seen, 3) of such moment, and to be valued so highly, that it should be held in no low place among the dogmas of the Christian faith (inasmuch as PETERSEN, and many others, have fought for this cause as for hearth and home): it is surely far removed from all likelihood that other sacred writers, and above all our Jesus, and His Legates also, should have passed over a matter so fruitful, indeed absolutely necessary to be known, in silence; and that not even one of them should have left anything written most openly and most plainly about it. began to be raised, we are persuaded that it has happened). Afterwards, however, it is necessary that he be released for a short time (just as the apprehension, binding, precipitation, and observation of Satan happened gradually: so also the release of the same has its own stages. For although the beginning of the release falls in the XIV century, yet the devil began to wander and rage most in the XV century, when Constantinople, the seat of the eastern Emperors, was occupied by Mahomet II, who gave an example of cruelty more than Stygian).

Latin:

ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ

Obiiciunt Chiliastae.

I. Apostolum Ioannem regnum Christi millenarium apertissime docere, Apoc. XX, 1. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. & 8. cuius verba memoratu sunt dignissima.

Postea vidi angelum descendentem e caelo, qui habebat clavem abyssi, & catenam magnam in manu sua. Hic comprehendit draconem, serpentem antiquum, qui est diabolus & Satanas: vinxitque eum mille annos: coniecitque eum in abyssum, & conclusit eum, & super eo obsignavit, ut non seduceret gentes amplius, usque dum consummarentur mille anni. Postea vero oportet illum solui exiguum tempus.

Vidi porro thronos, consederuntque super iis, & iudicium datum est illis: animas etiam securi percussorum propter testimonium Iesu, & propter verbum Dei, & qui non adoraverunt bestiam, neque imaginem eius, & regnarunt cum Christo mille annos Reliqui vero mortuorum non revixerunt, donec consummarentur mille anni. Haec est resurrectio prima. Beatus & sanctus est, qui habet partem in resurrectione prima. Super hos enim mors altera non habet potestatem: sed erunt sacerdotes Dei, & Christi, & regnabunt cum illo mille annos. Quando autem consummati fuerint mille anni, solvetur Satanas e custodia sua, & exibit ad seducendum gentes.

Resp.

1) Quia liber apocalypticus est propheticus, tum abstrusissimis visionibus propheticis, tum allegoricis, & quasi aenigmaticis loquendi formulis plenus, intellectu difficilis, ideo secundum analogiam fidei, claris & perspicuis scripturae locis superstructam, exponendus est (*).

2) Non possunt Chiliastae e loco citato luculenter culenter ostendere solemnem Christi adventum ad constituendum regnum millenarium, in quo, a) vivant homines perfecta θεογνωσίᾳ præditi, consummata sanctitate eminentes, terrenaque felicitate gaudentes, b) resurgant martyres, c) convertantur omnes Iudæi, & d) sub cuius primordium Anti-Christus euertatur.

Ceterum, vt mentem Apostoli penitius perspiciamus, primum succinctam verborum adductorum dabimus paraphrasin, deinde ad ea, quæ obiiciuntur, breuiter respondebimus.

Verba Ioannis sunt: Καὶ εἶδον, & vidi (indicat Apostolus ordinem visionum, non ordinem euentuum) angelum (scil. increatum, Christum, qui solus Satanam conterit, ligat, abolet, iuxta Genes. III, 15. Luc. XI, 22. Hebr. II, 14). descendentem de cælo (singulari se ratione manifestantem, & opere quodam miraculoso suam vim exerentem: nam descendere de cælo frequenter in S. litteris κατ’ ἀνθρωποπάθειαν de Deo omnipræsentissimo dicitur, cum præsentiam potentiæ & gratiæ singulari quodam opere manifestat; vid. Gen, XI, 5. c. XVIII, 21.) qui habebat clauem abyssi, & catenam magnam in manu sua (clauis est symbolum imperii, Apoc. I, 18. abyssus notat infernum: catena autem magna symbolice designat tum præualidam Christi potentiam, tum diaboli subiectionem & pœnam, Conf. 2 Petr. III, 4. Iud. v. 6.): Hic comprehendit draconem, serpentem antiquum, qui est diabolus & Satanas (Gradatim procedit Ioannes, & docet, a) Satanam esse comprehensum, qui tum per paganismum & idololatriam, tum per multiplices hæreses, tam ethnicos, quam Iudæos seducebat.

Id propter Christus tum immediate, tum per Apostolos magno impetu eum inuasit & vicit) vinxitque illum (Docet b) ligationem Satanæ, siue eius coërcitionem, quia ab horrenda gentium seductione retractus, cohibitusque fuit, ne adeo libere, & pro arbitratu delæuiret. Intelligitur autem ligatio non absoluta, sed limitata; nam & cani ligato datur aliquod spatium, intra quod furere, lædere & mordere potest), coniecitque eum in abyssum (Docet Apostolus c) præcipitationem Satanæ in abyssum. Dicitur autem Satanas in abyssum conici, cum illi publicum dominium adimitur. Quod contigit eo tempore, quo delubra paganorum sunt destructa, altaria diruta, & libri magici combusti), & conclusit eum, & super eo obsignauit (Docet iam d) obsignationem Satanæ, qua ipsi ademta est licentia exeundi, vagandi & nocendi) ne seducat gentes (seductione violenta & tyrannica, per reges & imperatores gentiles, idololatriæ deditos, qui bellica oppugnatione ecclesiam persecuti erant, & publicam euangelii prædicationem impedierant) vsque dum consummarentur mille anni (Sunt, qui hunc numerum indefinite sumunt, pro magno temporis interuallo; alii definite millenarium quoddam tempus expressum volunt; cum non videatur verisimile, Ioannem sexies dicturum χίλια ἔτη mille annos, & quater quidem cum articulo, τὰ χίλια ἔτη.

Neque tamen epocham mille annorum puncto quodam mathematico definire licet. Quod si itaque non præcise annum, tus est, possumus determinare, sufficit nobis, ligationis & solutionis satanicæ sæculum commonstrare.

Quocirca ligationis satanicæ primordium sæculo IV. rerum potiunte Constantino M., solutionis autem diabolicæ initium sæculo XIV. quo Ottomanicum regnum erigi fenfores acerrimi putant se reperisse præsidium longe firmissimum, immo fere vnicum, quo tota nititur ipsorum opinio. Si quod esset millennium, 1) adhuc exspectandum, 2) tale futurum, quale illi somniantes iam viderunt, 3) tam momentum, tantique faciendum, vt in dogmatibus Christianæ fidei haud infimo loco habendum esset (quando quidem PETERSENIVS, plures alii, pro hac causa, tanquam pro aris & focis propugnarunt): longe profecto ab omni veri similitudine remotum est, alios scriptores sacros, in primisque Iesum nostrum, eius etiam Legatos, rem adeo fructuosam, immo prorsus scitu necessariam, silentio transiisse; ac ne vnum quidem eorum apertissime planissimeque de ea scriptum aliquid reliquisse. erigi cœpit, contigisse persuasi sumus). Postea vero oportet eum solui exiguum tempus (sicut comprehensio, ligatio, præcipitatio & obseruatio Satanæ gradatim facta est: ita & solutio eiusdem suos habet gradus. Quamuis enim initium solutionis incidat in sæculum XIV. maxime tamen euagari & furere cœpit diabolus sæculo XV. quo Constantinopolis sedes Imperatorum orientalium occupata est a Mahomete II. qui crudelitatis plusquam stygia exemplum dedit).


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: I saw furthermore thrones, and they sat upon them

I saw furthermore thrones, and they sat upon them.

(John had beheld the turbulent state of the athletes of Christ, now he sees their state as more blessed: he sees those sitting upon thrones, i.e., reigning and enjoying peace), and judgment was given to them (by which, in approving the judgment of Christ, they disapprove and condemn gentile idolomania, Matt. XIX, 28.), and the souls of those beheaded on account of the testimony of Jesus, and on account of the word of God, and who had not adored the beast, nor its image, and had not received its character upon their forehead, and upon their hand: who lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years (The Apostle cast the eyes of his mind into the heaven of glory, and there in spirit he saw the martyrs and confessors of the gospel of Christ.

Concerning the souls of the martyrs he says: ἔζησαν, they lived, not ἀνέζησαν, they lived again; for since they are immortal, they always live, but they do not rise again from death, nor do they revive. The confessors did not adore the beast and its image, they did not venerate the Anti-Christ, and not even in an image did they worship him. The character upon the forehead denotes the most Anti-Christian profession, the character upon the hand denotes prompt obedience in the works of the flesh. These lived and reigned in the kingdom of glory, never to depart from the state of glory, within this chiliad, and while it runs in the kingdom of grace.

The rest of the dead, however, did not live again, until the thousand years were completed (The rest of the dead are the spiritually dead, who did not live again through conversion to Christ, as long as that fatal millennium lasts).

This is the first resurrection (from the death of sin). Blessed and holy is he who has a part in the first resurrection (who, converted to Christ through true faith, persists in the state of grace to the end). For over these the second death has no power, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and shall reign with him for a thousand years (The first death is the privation of the life of grace, the second death is the privation of the life of glory, or eternal condemnation: Spiritual priests are men reborn, justified, and renewed, who offer eucharistic sacrifices to God: Spiritual kings are those who through faith conquer the world, the devil, and the flesh, and dominate sin).

And when the thousand years have been completed, Satan shall be released from his prison, and shall go out, to seduce the nations. (Just as Satan was bound in his sons and organs; so now, released, he has in turn overcome the church of Christ among the nations, with the foulest idolatry recalled).

Latin:

Vidi porro thronos, confederuntque super iis.

(Conspexerat Ioannes statum athletarum Christi turbulentum, iam videt statum eorum beatiorem: videt sedentes super thronos, i. e. regnantes & pace fruentes), & iudicium datum est illis (quo iudicium Christi approbando gentilem idolomaniam improbant & condemnant, Matth. XIX, 28.), & animas securi percussorum propter testimonium Iesu, & propter verbum Dei, & qui non adorauerant bestiam, neque imaginem eius, & non acceperant characterem eius super frontem suam, & super manum suam: qui vixerunt & regnarunt cum Christo mille annos (Coniecit Apostolus oculos mentis in cœlum gloriæ, ibique in spiritu vidit martyres & confessores euangelii Christi.

De animabus martyrum dicit: ἔζησαν, vixerunt, non ἀνέζησαν, reuixerunt; cum enim immortales sint, semper viuunt, non autem a morte resurgunt, aut reuiuiscunt. Confessores non adorauerunt bestiam & imaginem eius, non Anti-Christum venerati sunt, ac ne in imagine quidem eum coluerunt. Character super frontem notat professionem Anti-Christianissimam, character super manum notat promptum in operibus carnis obsequium. Hi vixerunt & regnarunt in regno gloriæ, nunquam decessuri e statu gloriæ, intra hanc chiliada, & dum illa in regno gratiæ decurrit. Vid. Apoc. III, 12. Regnare significat felicissime agere, & bene beateque viuere, neque amplius seruituti illi probrosæ peccati & mundi subesse.

Reliqui vero mortuorum non reuixerunt, donec consummarentur mille anni (Reliqui mortuorum sunt spiritualiter mortui, qui non reuixerunt per conuersionem ad Christum, quamdiu illud fatale millennium durat).

Hæc est resurrectio prima (e morte peccati). Beatus & sanctus, qui habet partem in resurrectione prima (qui ad Christum conuersus per veram fidem in statu gratiæ ad finem persistit). Super hos enim mors altera non habet potestatem, sed erunt sacerdotes Dei & Christi, & regnabunt cum illo mille annos (Mors prima est priuatio vitæ gratiæ, mors secunda est priuatio vitæ gloriæ, siue æterna condemnatio: Sacerdotes spirituales sunt homines renati, iustificati & renouati, qui Deo sacrificia eucharistica offerunt: Reges spirituales sunt, qui per fidem vincunt mundum, diabolum & carnem, atque dominantur peccato).

Et cum consummati fuerint mille anni, soluet Satanas de carcere suo, & exibit, vt seducat gentes. (Vti ligatus fuit Satanas, in filiis & organis suis; ita nunc solutus vicissim gentibus debellauit ecclesiam Christi, fœdissima idololatria reuocata).


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: We note the epoch of the following millennium

We note the epoch of the following millennium.

Constantine the Great, in the year of Christ 312, with the sign of the cross seen in the sky, with the inscription: ἐν τούτῳ νίκῃ, carried off victory from his enemies, and converted to Christianity, gave peace to the church; which year, therefore, the fathers call the most happy year of the church: on the contrary, in the year of Christ 1307, Michael IX, Emperor of the Greeks, was conquered and defeated, so that you can call it an unlucky and fatal year for the whole east. Conf. D. NEVNANNI disput. II. Antichiliaft. §. 9. Its observation and sealing was done in the V century, in which that ecumenical council of Chalcedon was celebrated, namely in the year 453, in which paganism was not only exterminated, but also heresies were reprobated.

1) The souls of the beheaded lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years: Therefore Christ will establish a millennial kingdom with his saints in these lands. Resp. a) The souls lived, they did not live again, not in these lands, but in heaven. b) To reign does not denote a terrestrial, visible, and corporeal kingdom; but a heavenly, invisible, and spiritual one, which does not consist in temporal happiness, but in eternal beatitude. For to reign with John signifies, superto act most blessedly having overcome the enemies, in which sense this word is also used by Paul .

You say: 2) In the millennium, which begins in the 4th century and ends in the 14th century, Satan was not bound; because a) Julian the apostate ascended the imperial throne in the same century, and b)

XIV. Satan was not bound; because a) Julian the apostate ascended the imperial throne in the same century, and b) various heresies (Arian, Pelagian, Photinian, and many others) grew like tares, which Satan sows.

Response: a) In the 4th century Satan was bound, in the 5th century he was shut up. God, most just, moved by the causes of Satan, loosened for a time the chain with which he was bound, so that his chattel, Julian, might ascend the throne; but it was a small cloud, passing easily. With him dead, no pagan Emperor was crowned within the course of that millennium.

The binding of Satan is limited, not absolute.

Satan is bound, so that he may not seduce the nations with violent and tyrannical seduction; the seduction of heretics is not so much violent as it is fraudulent. AUGUSTINE used this distinction, he narrates in Ps. IX. The first persecution of the church was violent, when with proscriptions, tortures, and slaughters, Christians were forced to sacrifice.

The second persecution is fraudulent, which is carried out through heretics and false brethren. The third, in the time of the Antichrist, is both violent and fraudulent, having force in the empire and deceit in miracles. John speaks of the first, not of the second.

Then there are other general persecutions of the church, stirred up by pagans, and some special disturbances, which the devil brings about, sometimes with the word through heretics, sometimes with the sword through tyrants. The text in the Apocalypse speaks of these again, and the fulfillment itself has confirmed it; nor is Satan said to be bound ἁπλῶς & ὁλικῶς, simply and absolutely, but κατὰ τὶ & προσδιορισικῶς, in a certain respect and specifically, namely in respect of the seduction of the nations. For the text holds thus: And he cast him into the abyss, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should not seduce the nations (to wit, to persecute Christians atrociously, in the ancient manner).

That which is evident even from this, because it is said shortly after, v. 9, that Satan, after those thousand years of his binding, having been released from his prison, is again to seduce the nations, or peoples, συναγαγεῖν αὐτὲς εἰς πόλεμον, to gather them together to battle, where it is most manifest that what Satan is said to be about to do after the release, he must have ceased to do at the time of the release.

The blessed HUNNIUS illustrates the matter with a most convenient similitude, in disp. de regno Christi

§. 75. Just as, when it is read in Judg. III, that after Eglon, King of the Moabites, was killed by Ehud, there followed a peace of 80 years, it is not understood simply in respect of all the enemies of the Israelite nation equally; but by reason of the Moabites, concerning whom it is specifically discussed there; so also, when it is written that Satan is bound, it is to be understood not simply, but in a certain respect, namely in respect of the nations, previously under pagan rule, and thus in respect of the impression of the nations upon the church of Christ: Just as John clearly explains his prophecy, adding: that he should not seduce the nations anymore. For that a time should be expected in this world in which Satan is plainly no longer stirring up trouble against Christians is absurd, and contrary to the prediction of the sacred scriptures.

You say: 3) The millennium, which begins in the 4th century and ends in the 14th century, was not lacking in violent seduction.

For the Ostrogoths, Huns, Vandals, and other peoples, during the course of that millennium, poured themselves into Italy, and raged cruelly against the followers of true Christian doctrine.

Response: Perpetual peace is an excellent good not of human travelers, but of the blessed. The barbarian nations either embraced the Catholic faith or adhered to Arianism, with Paganism rejected.

You say: 4) The release of Satan lasts for a short time.

See Apoc. XX, 3. The release of Satan from the founding of the Ottoman kingdom does not last for a short time: for it has already lasted for the course of three centuries, and more than this.

Therefore, that in the Apocalypse of John is not understood [as this].

Response: A short and small time is left to Satan, whether it be compared with the thousand years past, or with all the past time in which he has variously stirred up trouble among the nations from the beginning of the world.

Satan, or finally with eternity itself, in whose view a thousand years are no different than one day, Ps. XC, 5.

II. Chiliasts call upon Dan. II, 44 ff., compared with 35, for support, where Daniel, about to expound the dream of Nebuchadnezzar, says: "But in the days of these kingdoms shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall not be destroyed for ages, and his kingdom shall not be left to other people: it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, but it shall stand for ages. Forasmuch as thou sawest that the stone was cut out of the mountain without hands, and that it brake in pieces the iron, the brass, the clay, the silver, and the gold, v. 35. And the stone that smote the image became a great mountain, and filled the whole earth." From this prophetic oracle, the Chiliasts argue: Whatever kingdom is spiritual, filling the whole earth and crushing the remaining kingdoms, that is neither the kingdom of grace nor the kingdom of glory, but some intermediate kingdom, etc., the millennial kingdom of Christ: But the kingdom of Christ, predicted by Daniel, etc. The major premise is established: because 1) the kingdom of grace indeed fills the whole earth, but it does not crush or consume the remaining kingdoms: 2) The kingdom of glory fills heaven, not the earth: Resp. to 1) The kingdom of grace is entirely what is understood by Daniel, which fills the whole earth through the preaching of the Gospel, Col. I, 23. This crushes and consumes the remaining kingdoms, not through corporal desolation, but through spiritual subjugation: it does not abolish polities, but subjects Kings and citizens to Christ, so that they may kiss this Son of God, Phil. II, 12. 2) The kingdom predicted by Daniel cannot be the millennial kingdom. For that is eternal; this, once a thousand years have elapsed, is finished: that crushes and consumes all remaining kingdoms; but the millennial kingdom will not crush the kingdom of Gog and Magog, Rev. XX, 8.

You say: The spiritual kingdom of Christ is not eternal. For it is terminated by the consummation of the age, when Christ shall deliver the kingdom to the Father. Resp. The consummation of the age will not terminate the substance of the kingdom of Christ, but the mode of governance through the Word and sacraments.

III. Chiliasts strive to establish the millennial kingdom of Christ from Dan. VII, 26. 27. "After the judgment he shall sit, and his dominion shall be taken away to be destroyed and overturned, even to the end. But the kingdom and dominion, and the majesty of the kingdoms under all the heavens shall be given to the most holy people: Whose kingdom is the kingdom of the age, and all dominions shall worship him, and shall obey him." The Chiliasts argue: Whatever kingdom shall be given to the most holy people under heaven, the fourth monarchy having been destroyed, that is neither the kingdom of grace nor the kingdom of glory, but the millennial kingdom of Christ. But the kingdom in Daniel, promised by the angel, shall be given to the most holy people, and indeed under heaven, the Roman monarchy having been destroyed: Therefore. The major premise is established: because that kingdom, which shall be given to the most holy people under heaven, cannot be the kingdom of glory, because this is not given under heaven, but in heaven: nor the kingdom of grace; since this is given while the Roman monarchy is flourishing and thriving. Therefore, some intermediate kingdom (to wit, the millennial) is understood in Daniel. Resp. The kingdom of glory is understood in Daniel, which shall indeed be conferred upon the most holy people under heaven, but shall be consummated in the heavenly fatherland. For the spiritual kingdom of Christ is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit, Rom. XIV, 17; which is begun under heaven, but consummated in heaven. But the millennial kingdom cannot be understood in Daniel. For the kingdom, of which mention is made in Daniel, viewed consummatively, shall be given after the final judgment, all earthly kingdoms having been destroyed, and it shall endure for eternity: which predicates certainly do not fit the millennial kingdom in the least.

Quest. XVI. Is a universal, or at least an illustrious and notable conversion of the Jews to be expected toward the end of the world?

Although the approach to repentance and faith in Christ is not closed to the Jews by an absolute decree of God a), and many of them from the apostolic age onward in the course of time ...when they have returned into favor with God b): nevertheless, a universal, or at any rate an illustrious and solemn conversion of them toward the end of the world is not to be expected c).

There is an antithesis from 1) many Fathers, 2) most Papists, 3) certain Reformed, 4) some of our own theologians, 5) Chiliasts, to adduce the lengthy words of all of whom is superfluous. Let it suffice for the present to have cited one, HOBURG, in his *Mystical Postils*, Dom. Iudic. p. 456, writing: "I fear that no people under the sun dishonors you more than your very Christians: therefore you will also finally dishonor them again, and will again look upon, have mercy on, and accept the blind Jews, who formerly out of blind ignorance and untimely zeal dishonored you." In his *Apologia Prætoriana*, the same mystic says on p. 282: "We hold that before the Last Day the Jews will be converted, the Gentiles will come into the fellowship of the Church, and that before this happens, the sectarian Babel-nature of the Christians will fall, and before this occurs, no Last Day is to be hoped for."

EXPOSITION.

Obs. I. A distinction must be made between the universal and simultaneous conversion of the Jews, and their particular and successive conversion. That universality is viewed either *haplōs*, and simply, and embraces all Jews whatsoever who are, have been, or will be; or it is considered *kata ti*, and in a certain respect; in which sense it denotes the greatest part of the Jews entering into the assembly of Christ all at once.

Obs. II. The successive and particular conversion of the Jews is sometimes solemn, notable, and clear; sometimes it is less solemn, private, and thus as it were obliterated. The former happens more rarely; the latter can be expected daily.

CONFIRMATION.

Proof a. From Rom. XI, 1. 2. "Has God rejected his people? Far be it. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God has not rejected his people whom he foreknew." The Apostle teaches that the Jews have not been rejected from grace by an absolute decree of God or by irreconcilable hatred, but that the cause of the rejection of many Jews is their final impenitence and *apistia* [unbelief]. But those Jews whom God foreknew would believe in Christ, he did not reject. Wherefore the Jewish nation has not been rejected out of mere hatred of God or an absolute decree.

Proof b. Both the Sacred Scriptures and ecclesiastical histories speak of the fact that from the apostolic age onward, very many Jews have been converted. When the Apostle Peter preached the gospel of Christ, three thousand Jews were converted, Acts II, 41. At another time, almost countless thousands embraced the worship of Christ, Acts XXI, 20. In succeeding times, this multitude of believing Jews increased. Cf. *Magdeburg Centuries*, Cent. VI; OSIANDER, *Centuries*, V, book I, c. 34; Cent. VI, book IV, c. 4; Cent. VII, book II, c. 7.

Proof c. That a universal conversion of the Jews is not to be expected, we demonstrate I. From the most clear testimony of the Apostle Paul, which we read in 1 Thess. II, 15. 16. "The Jews killed the Lord Jesus, and persecuted their own prophets, and us (the Apostles), and they do not please God, and are opposed to all men, who hinder us from speaking to the Gentiles that they might be saved, so as to fill up their sins always; for wrath has come upon them *eis telos*, even to the end." Regarding the phrase *eis telos*, THEOPHYLACT says: "It is not given," he says, "that a return, as once from captivity, and a turning back to the land of promise is to be hoped for, but the wrath of God has come upon them *eis telos*, that is, the wrath of God is to remain upon them forever." From the Pauline utterance, there is born for us a most valid argument: Whoever, on account of the Lord Jesus most cruelly slain, and his Prophets and Apostles most harshly treated, have provoked upon themselves eternal wrath and a curse, the universal conversion of them is not to be expected: But the Jews, etc.

Therefore. You say: If this argument is valid, not even one Jew will enter the Church of Christ. I reply: That from the nation of the Israelites, who crucified the Lord Jesus, one or another is converted, this the Apostle calls a mystery, Rom. XI, 25.

II. There is no certain hope for us of a universal conversion of the Jews; because a threefold curse presses upon them: a) general, Deut. XXVII, 26. Cursed be he that confirmeth not the words of this law to do them; and all the people shall say: Amen! Because the Jews do not perform all the words of the law, they are subject to the Mosaic curse. From this curse they could be freed, if they believed in Christ the redeemer, of whom Paul says: Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: For it is written: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree; that the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith, Gal. III, 13. But the blinded Jews reject Christ the liberator: Therefore they remain subject to the Mosaic curse. b) A special and proper curse, voluntarily drawn upon themselves by these words: His blood be on us and on our children, Matth. XXVII, 25. The Jews committed the most grievous sin of all, by crucifying the Lord of glory, and to this sin they added so horrible a curse: Who then can be induced to believe in the future conversion of all, or at least of very many Jews? c) The curse of Christ, pronounced through the mouth of David, presses upon the Jews, Ps. CIX, 24. seqq. Let their eyes be darkened, that they may not see; and bow down their back alway. Pour out thine indignation upon them, and let thy wrathful anger take hold of them. Let their habitation be desolate. Let there be no dweller in their tents. For they persecute him whom thou hast smitten; and they talk to the grief of those whom thou hast wounded. Add iniquity unto their iniquity: and let them not come into thy righteousness. Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous. This curse of the Messiah is not a bolt from the blue, but truly denounces an everlasting punishment upon the Jews. Cf. Ps. CIX, 17.

Latin:

Epocham millennii sequentem notamus.

Constantinus M. anno Christi CCCXII. signo crucis in cœlo conspecto, cum epigraphe: ἐν τούτῳ νίκῃ, victoriam ab hostibus reportauit, & conuersus ad christianismum, pacem ecclesiæ dedit; quem proinde annum ecclesiæ felicissimum patres appellant: contra, anno Christi MCCCVII. Michaël IX. Græcorum Imperator, victus & debellatus est, vt annum infaustum & fatalem totius orientis dicere possis. Conf. D. NEVNANNI disput. II. Antichiliaft. §. 9. Obseruatio & obsignatio eius facta est sæculo V. quo œcumenicum illud Chalcedonense concilium celebratum est, nempe anno CCCCLIII. quo paganismus non tantum exterminatus est, sed & hæreses reprobatæ sunt.

1) Anima decollatorum vixerunt & regnauerunt cum Christo mille annos: Ergo Christus cum sanctis suis in his terris regnum millenarium constituet. Resp. a) Animæ vixerunt, non reuixerunt, non in his terris, sed in cœlo. b) Tò regnare non notat regnum terrestre, visibile & corporale; sed cœleste, inuisibile & spirituale, quod non in felicitate temporali, sed in æterna beatitudine consistit. Nam regnare apud Ioannem significat, superatis hostibus beatissime agere, quo sensu etiam a Paulo haec vox usurpatur .

Dicis: 2) In millennio, quod incipit saeculo IV. & terminatur saec.

XIV. non ligatus fuit Satanas; quia a) Iulianus apostata thronum imperatorium conscendit, eodem saeculo, & b) variae haereses (Ariana, Pelagiana, Photiniana, plures aliae) zizaniorum more, quae Satanas seminat, creverunt.

Resp. a) Saeculo IV. ligatus est Satanas, saec. V. obseratus. Deus iustissimus motus caussis Satanae catenam, cui illigatus erat, ad tempus laxauit, vt eius mancipium, Iulianus thronum conscenderet; at nubecula fuit, facile transiens. Eo defuncto, nullus ethnicus Imperator corona redimitus fuit, intra decursum illius millennii.

Ligatio Satanae est limitata, non absoluta.

Ligatus est Satanas, ne seducat gentes, seductione violenta & tyrannica; haereticorum seductio non tam violenta, quam fraudulenta est. Vsus est hac distinctione AVGVSTINVS, enarrat. in Ps. IX. Prima persecutio ecclesiae violenta fuit, cum proscriptionibus, tormentis, caedibus, Christiani ad sacrificandum cogerentur.

Altera persecutio fraudulenta est, quae per haereticos & falsos fratres agitur. Tertia, Antichristi tempore, & violenta, & fraudulenta est, vim habens in imperio, dolum in miraculis. De prima loquitur Ioannes, non de secunda.

Deinde aliae sunt persecutiones ecclesiae generales, ab ethnicis motae, aliquae speciales quaedam turbae, quas cum verbo, per haereticos, tum ferro, per tyrannos, dat diabolus. De illis iterum loquitur textus in Apocalypsi, ipsumque complementum id confirmauit; neque ἁπλῶς & ὁλικῶς, simpliciter & absolute ligatus dicitur Satanas, sed κατὰ τὶ & προσδιορισικῶς, secundum quid, & certo respectu, nimirum respectu seductionis gentium. Sic enim habet textus: Et coniecit eum in abyssum, concludit eum, & super eo obsignauit, ne seducat gentes (ad persequendum scil. atrociter Christianos, more pristino).

Id quod vel inde patet, quia mox dicitur, v. 9. quod Satan, post annos illos mille suae ligationis ex suo carcere solutus, iterum seducturus sit gentes, seu populos, συναγαγεῖν αὐτὲς εἰς πόλεμον, ad congregandum eos in praelium, vbi manifestissimum est, quae post solutionem moliturus dicitur Satanas, ea tempore solutionis illum intermittere debuisse. Conuenientissima similitudine rem illustrat B.

HVNNIVS, in disp. de regno Christi §. 75. Quemadmodum, quando Iudic.

III. legitur, post Eglonem, Moabitarum Regem, ab Ehud occisum, secutam esse pacem 80. annorum, non id simpliciter, respectu omnium pariter hostium gentis Israeliticae intelligitur; sed ratione Moabitarum, de quibus illic specifice disseritur; sic quoque, cum Satanas ligatus esse scribitur, id non simpliciter, sed secundum quid intelligendum est, videlicet respectu gentium, sub imperio prius ethnico, atque sic respectu impressionis gentium in ecclesiam Christi: Sicut manifeste vaticinium suum explicat Ioannes, addens: vt non seducat amplius gentes. Nam vt exspectetur in hoc mundo tempus, quo plane non amplius tumultuetur aduersus Christianos Satanas, absurdum est, & sacrarum litterarum praedictioni contrarium.

Dicis: 3) Millennium, quod incipit saec.

IV. & terminatur saec. XIV, non caruit seductione violenta. Nam Ostogothi, Hunni, Vandali, & alii populi, decurrente illo millennio, se effuderunt in Italiam, & in verae doctrinae christianae sectatores crudeliter saeuierunt.

Resp. Pax perpetua non hominum viatorum, sed beatorum eximium bonum est. Barbarae gentes vel catholicam amplexae sunt fidem, vel Arianismo adhaeserunt, Paganismo reiecto.

Dicis: 4) Solutio Satanae durat modico tempore.

Vid. Apoc. XX, 3. Solutio Satanae a fundatione regni Ottomannici non durat modico tempore: duravit enim iam trium saeculorum decursu, & hoc amplius.

E. illa in Apocalypsi Ioannae non intelligitur.

Resp. Modicum & exiguum tempus Satanae relictum est, siue conferatur cum annis mille praeteritis, siue cum omni tempore praeterito, quo inde ab origine mundi inter gentes varie tumultuatus est

Satanas, siue denique cum ipsa æternitate, cuius intuitu chilias vna, non secus, ac vna dies est, Pf. XC, 5.

II. Chiliaftæ in subsidium vocant Dan. II, 44. sqq. collat. cum 35. vbi Daniel somnium Nebucadnezaris expositurus, inquit: Sed in diebus regnum horum surgere faciet Deus, cælorum regnum, quod in sæcula non perdetur, & regnum eius populo alii non permittetur: conteret & consumet omnia ista regna, ipsum autem stabit in sæcula. Propterea, quod vidisti, quod de petra excisus est lapis, non per manus, & contriuit ferrum, æs, argillam, argentum & aurum, v. 35. Et lapis, qui percussit statuam, effectus est in montem magnum, & impleuit omnem terram. Ex hoc oraculo prophetico Chiliaftæ argumentantur: Quodcunque regnum est spirituale, implens omnem terram & comminuens reliqua regna, illud neque regnum gratiæ, neque regnum gloriæ est, sed intermedium aliquod regnum, &c. regnum Christi millenarium: Atqui regnum Christi, a Daniele prædictum &c. Maior constat: quia 1) regnum gratiæ quidem implet omnem terram, sed non comminuit, aut consumit reliqua regna: 2) Regnum gloriæ implet cœlum, non terram: Resp. ad 1) Omnino intelligitur a Daniele regnum gratiæ, quod prædicatione euangelii implet omnem terram, Col. I, 23. Hoc conterit & consumit reliqua regna, non per desolationem corporalem, sed subiugationem spiritualem: non abolet politias, sed Reges & ciues Christo subiicit, vt hunc Filium Dei osculentur, Phil. II, 12. 2) Regnum a Daniele prædictum non potest esse regnum millenarium. Nam illud est æternum; hoc, elapsis mille annis, finitur: illud omnia reliqua regna conterit & consumit; regnum autem millenarium regnum Gogi & Magogi non comminuet, Apoc. XX, 8.

Dicis: Regnum Christi spirituale non est æternum. Nam terminatur consummatione sæculi, vbi Christus Patri tradet regnum. Resp. Consummatio sæculi non terminabit substantiam regni Christi, sed modum regiminis per verbum & sacramenta.

III. Regnum Christi millenarium Chiliaftæ stabilire nituntur ex Dan. VII, 26. 27. Post iudicium sedebit, & dominium eius auferent ad perdendum & euertendum, vsque ad finem. Regnum vero & dominium, & maiestas regnorum sub omnibus cœlis dabitur populo sanctissimo: Cuius regnum est regnum sæculi, & omnia dominia colent eum, & obedient ei. Arguunt Chiliaftæ: Quodcunque regnum populo sanctissimo sub cœlo dabitur, destructa monarchia quarta, illud neque regnum gratiæ, neque regnum gloriæ est, sed regnum Christi millenarium. At regnum apud Danielem, ab angelo promissum, dabitur populo sanctissimo, & quidem sub cœlo, monarchia Romana destructa: E. Maior constat: quia regnum illud, quod populo sanctissimo dabitur sub cœlo, non potest esse regnum gloriæ, quia hoc non sub cœlo; sed in cœlo datur: neque regnum gratiæ; quoniam hoc datur, monarchia Romana vigente & florente. E. Regnum aliquod intermedium (scil. millenarium) apud Danielem intelligitur. Resp. Intelligitur apud Danielem regnum gloriæ, quod populo sanctissimo sub cœlo conferetur quidem, in cœlesti autem patria consummabitur. Nam regnum Christi spirituale est iustitia, pax & gaudium in Spiritu S. Rom. XIV, 17; quod sub cœlo inchoatur, in cœlo autem consummatur. Regnum vero millenarium apud Danielem intelligi nequit. Nam regnum, cuius apud Danielem fit mentio, consummatiue spectatum, dabitur post extremum iudicium, destructis omnibus regnis terrenis, & durabit in æternum: quæ certe prædicata regno millenario minime conueniunt.

Quæst. XVI. Estne Iudæorum vniuersalis, aut certe illustris & notabilis conuersio sub finem mundi exspectanda?

Quamuis Iudæis aditus ad pœnitentiam & fidem in Christum absoluto Dei decreto non sit præclusus a), multique eorum inde ab æuo apostolico successu temporis poris cum Deo in gratiam redierint b): vniuerfalis tamen eorum, aut certe illuftris & folemnis conuerfio fub finem mundi non eft exspectanda c).

Antithefis eft 1) multorum Patrum, 2) plerorumque Pontificiorum, 3) quorundam, Reformatorum, 4) nonnullorum ex noftratibus Theologis, 5) Chiliaftarum, quorum omnium prolixa adducere verba, fuperuacuum eft. Sufficiat in præfenti, vnum citaffe HOBVRGIVM, in poftillis myfticis, Dom. Iudic. p. 456. fcribentem: Ich fürchte, daß kein Volk unter der Sonne dich mehr unehre, als eben deine Christen: Daher du sie auch endlich wieder unehren, und die blinden Juden, welche vorzeiten aus blinder Unwissenheit und unzeitigem Eifer dich verunehret haben, wirst wieder ansehen, erbarmen und annehmen. In Apologia Prætoriana idem Mysticus inquit p. 282. Wir halten dafür, daß vor dem jüngsten Tage die Juden werden bekehret, die Heiden zur Gemeinschaft der Kirchen kommen, und daß zuvor der Christen ihr sectisch Babel-Wesen fallen werde, und ehe dieses nicht geschicht, ist kein jüngster Tag zu hoffen.

E K Θ E Σ I Σ.

Obf. I. Distinguendum eft inter Iudæorum conuerfionem vniuerfalem & fimultaneam, & eorundem conuerfionem particularem ac fucceffiuan. Vniuerfalitas illa viciffim vel ἁπλῶς, & fimpliciter fpectatur, & omnes omnino Iudæos complectitur; qui funt, fuerunt aut erunt: vel κατὰ τὶ, & fecundum quid confideratur; quo fenfu maximam Iudæorum partem notat, fimul ac femel in cœtum Chrifti introëuntem.

Obf. II. Succeffina ac particularis Iudæorum conuerfio aliquando eft folemnis, notabilis ac luculenta: aliquando eft minus folemnis, priuata, adeoque velut oblitterata. Illa rarius contigit, hæc quotidie exspectari poteft.

B E B A I Ω Σ I Σ.

Prob. a. Ex Rom. XI, 1. 2. Num reprobauit Deus populum fuum? Abfit. Nam etiam ego fum Ifraëlita, ex femine Abrahami, tribus Beniaminis. Non reprobauit Deus populum fuum, quem præfciuit. Docet Apoftolus, Iudæos non ex abfoluto Dei decreto, aut odio irreconciliabili, effe a gratia reiectos, fed cauffam reprobationis effe multorum Iudæorum finalem impoenitentiam & ἀπισίαν. Illos autem Iudæos, quos Deus præfciuit, in Chriftum effe credituros, non reiecit. Quare gens Iudaica non ex mero Dei odio, aut abfoluto decreto reiecta eft.

Prob. b. Inde ab æuo apoftolico Iudæos longe plurimos conuerfos effe, tum facræ litteræ, tum hiftoriæ ecclefiasticæ loquuntur. Apoftolo Petro euangelium Chrifti prædicante, ter mille Iudæi conuerfi funt, Act. II, 41. Alio tempore millia fere innumera Chrifti cultum amplexa funt, Act. XXI, 20. Procedentibus temporibus hæc credentium Iudæorum multitudo aucta eft. Conf. Hiftoriam Magdeb. Centur. VI. OSIANDRI Centur. V. libr. I. c. 34. Centur. VI. libr. IV. c. 4. Centur. VII. libr. II. c. 7..

Prob. c. Vniuerfalem Iudæorum conuerfionem non effe exspectandam, demonstramus I. E clariffimo Apoftoli Paulli teftimonio, quod legimus 1. Theff. II, 15. 16. Iudæi Dominum Iefum occiderunt, & proprios Prophetas, & nos (Apoftolos) perfecuti funt, & Deo non placent, & omnibus hominibus aduerfantur, qui obfiftunt nobis, ne loquamur gentibus, quo falui fiant, vt expleant peccata fua femper; vnde peruenit in illos ira εἰς τέλος, vfque ad finem. De voce, eis τέλος, THEOPHYLACTVS: Non datur, inquit, vt quondam ex captiuitate reditus, & ad terram promiffionis peruertus fit fperandus, fed in finem vfque in hos ira Dei peruenit, id eft, femper in hos permanfura eft Dei ira. Nafcitur nobis ex effato Paullino argumentum validissimum: Quicunque ob Dominum Iesum crudelissime occisum, & suos Prophetas atque Apostolos asperrime tractatos, iram & maledictionem in se perpetuam concitarunt, illorum conversio universalis expectanda non est: Atqui Iudæi ...&c.

E. Dicis: Si hoc argumentum validum est, ne unus quidem Iudæus ecclesiam Christi ingredietur. Resp. Quod ex natione Israelitarum, qui Dominum Iesum crucifixerunt, unus & alter convertitur, hoc vocat Apostolus μυστήριον, Rom. XI, 25.

II. Non est nobis certa spes universalis Iudæorum conversionis; quia illos triplex premit maledictio: a) generalis, Deut. XXVII, 26. Maledictus, qui non stabiluerit verba legis huius, ad faciendum illa; dicetque omnis populus: Amen! Quia Iudæi non faciunt omnia verba legis, maledictioni Mosaicæ sunt subiecti. Ab hac maledictione possent liberari, si crederent in Christum redemptorem, de quo Paullus ait: Christus nos redemit a maledictione legis, factus pro nobis maledictio: Scriptum namque est: Maledictus omnis, qui pependerit super ligno; ut in gentes benedictio Abrahami fieret in Christo Iesu; ut promissionem Spiritus acciperemus per fidem, Gal. III, 13. Atqui occæcati Iudæi Christum liberatorem repudiant: Ergo maledictioni Mosaicæ subiecti manent. b) Maledictio specialis & propria, sponte attracta verbis illis: Sit sanguis eius super nos & filios nostros, Matth. XXVII, 25. Commiserunt Iudæi peccatum omnium gravissimum, Dominum gloriæ crucifigendo, & huic peccato tam horrendam maledictionem adiecerunt: Ecquis igitur adduci potest, ut credat, omnium, aut certe plurimorum Iudæorum futuram conversionem? Premit Iudæos c) maledictio Christi per os Dauidis prolata, Ps. CIX, 24. seqq. Obscurentur oculi eorum, ut non videant; & lumbos eorum iugiter concute. Effunde iram tuam super eos, & excandescentia indignationis tuæ assequatur eos. Sit habitatio eorum devastata. In tentoriis eorum ne sit habitans. Quia quem tu percussisti, illi persecuti sunt; & super dolore confessorum tuorum nungantur. Da iniquitatem super iniquitatem illorum, & ne perveniant ad iustitiam tuam. Deleantur e libro vitarum, & cum iustis ne scribantur. Hæc maledictio Messiæ non est fulmen e pelvi, sed Iudæis perennem pœnam ex vero denuntiat. Conf. Ps. CIX, 17.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: III. Whoever frowardly and stubbornly reject the means of grace and salvation, the universal, or at least notable, conversion of them is…

III. Whoever frowardly and stubbornly reject the means of grace and salvation, the universal, or at least notable, conversion of them is not to be hoped for: But the Jews, etc. Therefore.

The major premise is open to no one. For when a profane man contemns the instruments, or means of the Holy Spirit, and is unwilling to hear the word of God, no injury is done to him if he is not illuminated by the Holy Spirit, but is left in the darkness of his own infidelity, and perishes. Concerning this matter it is written thus: How often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Matth. XXIII, 37. says the Formula of Concord, p. 627. The minor premise also is free from all doubt.

For the Jews, from many ages past, even unto this day in which we live, refuse to read the writings of the Evangelists and Apostles, and rarely even unfold the monuments of the Prophets, content with the knowledge of the Pentateuch; they esteem Talmudic fables most highly, retain circumcision, and detest baptism, mock the sacrament of the Supper, and so loathe the preaching of the gospel that the temples of the Christians are loathsome to them, and they instill and imprint upon their children in the first flower of tender age such a hatred of Christians that they refuse to associate familiarly with the children of Christians. Cf. Buxtorf, Synagoga Judaica, cap. III, p. 152.

For which reason the hope of a universal conversion of the Jews falls away. IV.

Whoever burn with such immense hatred against Jesus, the author of salvation, that they vomit forth dire blasphemies against him with profane mouth, the notable conversion of them is by no means to be hoped for: But the Jews, etc. Therefore. St. Paul confirms the major premise, 1 Cor. XVI, 22. If any man love not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be Anathema, Maran Atha! Experience itself establishes the minor premise. For the Jews are accustomed in their synagogues to call our Jesus Thalui, and the deeds of his name his mention, to add: let his name and memory be blotted out ! and to spit on the ground, as BVXTORFFIUS testifies l. c. p. 167. But who would persuade himself that that stubbornly impious nation, which assails the most holy name of Jesus with wicked slanders, will be illuminated and converted by the grace of the Holy Spirit?

V. Whoever are cast out of the kingdom of God by the most just divine judgment for their persistent ἀπιστίαν and excluded from the heavenly supper, their solemn conversion is not to be expected: But the Jews &c. The minor premise is established by the words of Christ Matthew VIII, 11. 12. Many will come from the east and west, and will recline with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven. But the sons of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness. And Luke XIV, 24. I say to you, that none of those men (Jews), who were invited, will taste my supper.

VI. That the generation of circumcised Jews will not pass away until all things are fulfilled, Christ himself enumerated among the signs of the last judgment, Luke XXI, 32. . Therefore, so great a multitude of Jews will not be aggregated to the Christian church before the last day of judgment, that all Israel can be said to be converted. The Savior's discourse l. c. is about this very generation, which is distinguished from the uncircumcised Gentiles by the rite of circumcision. But, if either all, or most Jews, with circumcision abrogated, were baptized, this Jewish nation would not remain, but would become Christian, and thus its existence would not be a prognostic sign of the imminent last day.

But the Savior wished to teach us something else by the cited words. VII. The Jewish people will remain an outcast from the Israelite kingdom, a perpetual fugitive and wanderer, until the end of the world: Therefore, their catholic and simultaneous conversion is not to be hoped for. The consequence is solid: because the Jewish nation is dispersed through the vastest parts of the world, Europe, Asia, and Africa, and therefore so many myriads of Jews cannot be converted simultaneously and at once by the ordinary means of grace, the word and sacraments, but many centuries will flow by before all are called to the church, illuminated, and converted. The antecedent is clear from the prophecy of the Prophet Daniel, c. IX, 27. Until the consummation and the decreed will be poured out upon the desolation (the wrath of God), and the prediction of Christ, Matthew XXIII, 38. Behold, your house is left to you desolate: and Luke XXI, 24. For they will fall by the edge of the sword (those who are in Judea) and will be led captive among all nations; and Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled. But the fulfillment of the times of the Gentiles is rightly extended by CHRYSOSTOM to the consummation of the age, in the judgment of the blessed CALOVIUS in bibl. illustr. in h. l. fol. 673. and Matthew XXI, 43. The kingdom of God will be taken from you, and given to a nation producing its fruits.

VIII. In whatever nation blindness is to last perpetually, its conversion is not to be hoped for, except a particular one: But in the Jewish nation &c. Therefore. The minor premise is proven by the words of Christ, Matthew XXIII, 14, 15. The prophet Isaiah is fulfilled in the Jews, who says: By hearing you will hear, and will not understand; and seeing you will see, and will not perceive. For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have heard heavily, and their eyes they have closed, lest perhaps they should see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and convert themselves, and I should heal them. Paul supports this, saying, Rom. XI, 25. ἡ πώρωσις, hardening has happened to Israel in part, until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in. But the entry of the Gentiles into the Christian church will last until the consummation of the age; because a) Christ connects the promulgation of the gospel among the Gentiles with the consummation of the age connects the dregs, Matt. 28:19, 20; and b) πλήρωμα καιρῶν τῶν ἐθνῶν, the fullness of the times of the Gentiles, he connects with the last day, Luke 21:24. E. And the hardening of certain Jews, and the conversion of some, will consist until that time.

IX. Whatever people God foreknew would believe in Christ, He did not reject, but converted and elected, Rom. 11:2. But He foreknew that some would believe in Christ: Therefore. The minor is clear: because election is made κατὰ πρόγνωσιν (according to the foreknowledge) of faith, 1 Pet. 1:2; 2 Thess. 2:13. But faith is not of all, 1 Thess. 3:2, and election is of the few, Matt. 20:16.

X. Whatever Jews do not remain in unbelief, they are received into the kingdom of grace, Rom. 11:23. But there are few Jews who do not remain in unbelief. E. The minor is clear: because not all believe the gospel, Rom. 10:16, nor are all who are of Israel, Israel, Rom. 9:6.

XI. The Jews to be converted are described as λείμματα, a remnant, Rom. 11:5; as λοιποὶ, the rest, v. 7; as τινὲς ἐξ αὐτῶν, some of them, v. 14. In Hebrew they are called שְׁאָר, פְּלֵיטָה, שְׁאֵרִית, Is. 10:20; ch. 11:11; Mic. 2:12; ch. 5:2, 3. They are emphatically delineated as the tithes selected from the fruits, Is. 6:13. They shall be as grains of wheat, separated from the chaff, Amos 9:9. Nay, even as the ears of some sheep torn away, which are snatched from the mouth of the lion, ch. 3:12. Therefore, the conversion of the Jews is not universal, not notable, and illustrious, but particular.

XII. Holy Scripture delineates for us the last times as horrible, as full of hypocrites and heretics, 2 Tim. 3:1; Matt. 24:24; Luke 18: 8. Therefore, in the last times of the world, not even an illustrious or notable conversion of the Jews is to be hoped for.

XIII. Just as the πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν, the fullness of the Gentiles, enters the church of Christ not all at once, but successively, sparsely, and step by step: So also πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ, all Israel, or the entire assembly of the elect Jews, is aggregated to the Christian church not all at once, but successively. For the Apostle Paul says, Rom. 11:25, 26: Hardening in part has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles comes in; and so all Israel will be saved.

XIV. Whatever conversion and justification is made through the merit of Christ, apprehended by true faith, that is for all times, and not to be restricted to the end of the age: But the conversion of the Jews, etc. Therefore. The minor is proved from Rom. 11:26, where the Apostle says: All Israel will be saved, as it is written: The deliverer will come out of Zion, and will turn away ungodliness from Jacob. These words are taken from Is. 59:20, where the prophet speaks of the advent of Christ in the flesh, since He is said to come out of Zion, that is, out of the afflicted church of the Jews, to redeem Jacob, that is, the Israelites, from sin. As, therefore, the redemption of Christ is valid at all times: So also for the Israelites, at no time is the access to this deliverer closed.

XV. Whatever conflicts with the nature of the divine testament and covenant, that, saving the justice of God, cannot be asserted: But that the people of God should be forsaken for so many intervals of time, and converted only toward the end of the world, conflicts with the divine covenant. For this is the testament of God, that He wills to take away their sins, Rom. 11:27; Jer. 31: 31. But the taking away of sins comes through faith in Jesus Christ unto all who believe, Rom. 3:22. Now, how will the divine covenant stand with the whole people of God, which will be to save the whole people so late, namely, toward the end of the world?

XVI. Whatever conversion Paul, in Rom. 11:25, brings forward to suppress the pride of the Gentiles, he understood not concerning the time immediately preceding the last day, but primarily concerning the present and the subsequent interval of times: But the conversion of the Jews, etc. Therefore. Dannhauer solidly confirms the major: It does not follow: You Romans ought to put on your crests, and not oppress the Jews: because after the passage of seventeen centuries they will still be converted in great numbers. They would have replied: let these things be said to those Romans who are to live then; what is it to us, the latest of men? Whom, just as we do not know, so we cannot despise. XVII.

The hypothesis of the adversaries, who maintain that the conversion of the Jews will only happen around the end of the world, obscures and overturns the doctrine of the universal grace of God. For the paternal heart of God, universally and equally merciful to all, is laid bare. Is it concluded equally, if the late rain of divine grace, and only in the evening of the world, sparingly distills dews upon a few, while others are excluded by an absolute decree?

Latin:

III. Quicunque media gratiæ & salutis proterve & pertinaciter reiiciunt, illorum universalis, aut certe notabilis conversio non est speranda: Atqui Iudæi &c.

E. Maior nemini non aperta est. Nam cum homo profanus instrumenta, seu media Spiritus S. contemnit, neque verbum Dei audire vult, non fit illi iniuria, si a Spiritus S. non illuminetur, sed in tenebris infidelitatis suæ relinquatur, ac pereat. De hac re sic scriptum extat: Quoties volui congregare filios tuos, quemadmodum gallina congregat pullos suos sub alas, & noluistis! Matth. XXIII, 37. ait Form. Concord. p. 627. Minor etiam omni vacat dubio.

Iudæi quippe a multis retro lapsis sæculis, usque in hunc, quo vivimus, diem, renuunt legere scripta Evangelistarum & Apostolorum, raro etiam evoluunt monumenta Prophetarum, contenti notitia Pentateuchi, fabulas Talmudicas maximi æstimant, retinent circumcisionem, & detestantur baptismum, rident sacramentum cœnæ, prædicationem evangelii adeo fastidiunt, vt templa Christianorum ipsis sordeant, liberis suis in primo tenerrimæ ætatis flore odium Christianorum instillant & imprimunt, vt cum liberis Christianorum familiariter versari recusent. Conf. BUXTORFII synagog. iudait. cap. III. p. 152. Quam ob rem spes de universali Iudæorum conversione decollat.

IV. Quicunque tam immani odio adversus Iesum, salutis auctorem, ardent, vt diras in ipsum blasphemias ore profano evomant, illorum insignis conversio minime speranda est: Atqui Iudæi &c. Ergo. Maiorem confirmat S.

Paullus, 1 Cor. XVI, 22. Si quis non amat Dominum Iesum Christum, sit Anathema, Maran Atha! Minorem stabilit ipsa experientia. Consueverunt quippe Iudæi in synagogis suis Iesum nostrum vocare Thalui, & facta nominis ipsius mentione, subiicere: deleatur nomen & memoria eius ! & in terram exspuere, teste BVXTORFFIO l. c. p. 167. Ecquis autem sibi persuadeat, nationem illam præfracte impiam, quæ sanctissimum Iesu nomen nefandis conviciis proscindit, gratia Spiritus S. illuminatum & conversum iri?

V. Quicunque iustissimo iudicio diuino ob pertinacem ἀπιστίαν regno Dei eiiciuntur & a cœna cœlesti excluduntur, illorum solemnis conversio non est exspectanda: Atqui Iudæi &c. Minor constat e verbis Christi Matth. VIII, 11. 12. Multi ab oriente & occidente venient, & accumbent cum Abrahamo, Isaac & Iacobo in regno cœlorum. Filii vero regni eiicientur in tenebras exteriores. Et Luc. XIV, 24. Dico vobis, quod nemo virorum istorum (Iudæorum), qui vocati fuerunt, gustaturus sit meam cœnam.

VI. Quod generatio Iudæorum circumcisorum non sit transitura, donec omnia fiant, Christus ipse signis extremi iudicii annumerauit, Luc. XXI, 32. . E. tanta multitudo Iudæorum ante extremum iudicii diem christianæ ecclesiæ non aggregabitur, vt omnis Israël conversus esse dicatur. Sermo est Saluatori l. c. de hac ipsa generatione, quæ a gentibus præputiatis ritu circumcisionis discernitur. At, si aut omnes, aut plerique Iudæi, circumcisione abrogata, baptizarentur, non maneret hæc natio iudaica, sed euaderet christiana, atque adeo non foret eius exsistentia signum prognosticum imminentis extremi diei.

Aliud autem Saluator verbis citatis nos condocefacere voluit. VII. Populus iudaicus vsque ad finem mundi relinquetur extorris regno Israëlitico, profugus perpetuus & vagabundus: E. illius conversio catholica & simultanea non est speranda. Consequentia est solida: quia natio iudaica per amplissimas orbis partes Europam, Asiam, & Africam dispersa est, adeoque per ordinaria gratiæ media, verbum & sacramenta, simul & semel converti nequeunt tot Iudæorum myriades, sed multa sæcula præterfluent, priusquam omnes ad ecclesiam vocentur, illuminentur & convertantur. Antecedens liquet ex vaticinio Prophetæ Danielis, c. IX, 27. Vsque ad consummationem & decisum stillabit super deuastationem (ira Dei), & prædictione Christi, Matth. XXIII, 38. Ecce relinquetur vobis domus desolata: & Luc. XXI, 24. Cadent namque ore gladii (qui in Iudæa sunt) & captiuabuntur inter omnes gentes; tandemque Hierosolyma erit conculcata a gentibus, vsque dum implebuntur tempora gentium. At impletio temporum gentium recte a CHRYSOSTOMO ad consummationem sæculi extenditur, iudice b. CALOVIO in bibl. illustr. in h. l. fol. 673. & Matth. XXI, 43. Auferetur a vobis regnum Dei, & dabitur genti facienti fructus eius.

VIII. In quacunque natione occæcatio perpetuo duratura est, illius conversio non, nisi particularis, speranda est: Atqui in natione iudaica &c. E. Minor probatur verbis Christi, Matth. XXIII, 14, 15. Completur in Iudæis propheta Esaiæ, qui dicit: Auditu audietis, & non intelligetis; & videntes videbitis, & non cernetis. Incrassatum est enim cor populi huius, & auribus grauiter audiuerunt, & oculos suos occluserunt, ne forte videant oculis, & auribus audiant, & corde intelligant, & convertant se, & sanem illos. Suffragatur Paullus, inquiens, Rom. XI, 25. ἡ πώρωσις, obduratio ex parte Israëli contigit, donec plenitudo gentium ingrediatur. At introitus gentium in ecclesiam christianam durabit vsque ad consummationem sæculi; quia a) Christus promulgationem euangelii inter gentes cum consummatione fæculi coniungit, Matth. XXVIII, 19. 20. & b) πλήρωμα καιρῶν τῶν ἐθνῶν, impletionem temporum gentium cum extremo die connectit, Luc. XXI, 24. E. & induratio quorundam Iudæorum, & quorundam conuersio eo vsque consistet.

IX. Quemcunque populum Deus præsciuit crediturum in Christum, illum non repulit, sed conuertit & elegit, Rom. XI, 2. At aliquos præsciuit credituros in Christum: Ergo. Minor liquet: quia electio fit κατὰ πρόγνωσιν fidei, 1 Petr. I, 2. 2 Thess. I, 13. Sed fides non est omnium, 1 Thess. III, 2. & electio est paucorum, Matth. XX, 16.

X. Quicunque Iudæi non permanent in incredulitate, illi recipiuntur in regnum gratiæ, Rom. XI, 23. At pauci Iudæi sunt, qui non permanent in incredulitate. E. Minor claret: quia non omnes credunt euangelio, Rom. X, 16. nec omnes, qui sunt ex Israël, sunt Israël, Rom. IX, 6.

XI. Iudæi conuertendi describuntur vt λείμματα, reliquiæ, Rom. XI, 5. vt λοιποὶ, reliqui, v. 7. vt τινὲς ἐξ αὐτῶν, nonnulli ex illis, v. 14. Hebraice dicuntur שְׁאָר, פְּלֵיטָה, שְׁאֵרִית, Es. X, 20. c. XI, 11. Mich. II, 12. c. V, 2. 3. Emphatice delineantur vt decimæ ex frugibus delectæ, Es. VI, 13. Erunt vt grana tritici, a paleis segregata, Amos IX, 9. Quinimo velut auriculæ ouis alicuius discerptæ, quæ ex ore leonis eripiuntur, c. III, 12. Ergo Iudæorum conuersio non est vniuersalis, non notabilis, & insignis, sed particularis.

XII. Scriptura Sacra delineat nobis tempora vltima, vt horrenda, vt hypocritarum & hæreticorum plena, 2 Tim. III, 1. Matth. XXIV, 24. Luc. XVIII, 8. Ergo vltimis mundi temporibus ne illustris quidem, aut notabilis Iudæorum conuersio speranda est.

XIII. Quemadmodum πλήρωμα τῶν ἐθνῶν, plenitudo gentium ecclesiam Christi ingreditur non simul & semel, sed successiue, sparsim & pedetentim: Ita & πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ, omnis Israël, siue vniuersus electorum Iudæorum cœtus non simul & semel, sed successiue ecclesiæ Christianæ aggregatur. Dicit enim Apostolus Paullus, Rom. XI, 25. 26. Obduratio ex parte Israëli contigit, donec plenitudo gentium ingrediatur; & sic totus Israël saluabitur.

XIV. Quæcunque conuersio & iustificatio fit per meritum Christi, vera fide apprehensum, illa est omnium temporum, nec ad finem sæculi restringenda: Atqui conuersio Iudæorum &c. Ergo. Minor probatur ex Rom. XI, 26. vbi Apostolus inquit: Totus Israel saluabitur, sicut scriptum est: Veniet ex Sion liberator, & auertet impietatem a Iacobo. Verba hæc fumta sunt ex Es. LIX, 20. vbi propheta loquitur de aduentu Christi in carnem, siquidem ex Sion, id est, ex afflicta Iudæorum ecclesia venire dicitur, ad redimendum Iacobum, id est, Israëlitas, a peccato. Sicut igitur redemtio Christi omnibus temporibus est valida: Ita & Israëlitis nullo non tempore aditus ad hunc liberatorem patet.

XV. Quidquid pugnat cum natura testamenti & fœderis diuini, illud, salua iustitia Dei, afferi nequit: At populum Dei per tot temporum interualla deferi, & sub finem mundi demum conuerti, pugnat cum fœdere diuino. Nam hoc est testamentum Dei, quod peccata ipsorum auferre velit, Rom. XI, 27. Ier. XXXI, 31. Venit autem ablatio peccatorum per fidem Iesu Christi in omnes, qui credunt, Rom. III, 22. Iam quomodo fœdus diuinum constabit cum toto populo Dei, quod tam fero, scilicet sub finem mundi, toti populo saluare erit?

XVI. Quæcunque conuersionem Paullus ad Rom. XI, 25. adducit, ad supprimendam gentilium superbiam, illam non de tempore extremum diem proxime anteceffuro, sed de præsente imprimis, & subsequente temporum interuallo intellexit: At conuersionem Iudæorum &c. Ergo. Maiorem DANNHAVERVS folide confirmat: Non sequitur: Vos Romani debetis ponere cristas, & Iudæos non opprimere: quia post septendecim sæculorum decursum illi adhuc magno numero convertentur. Regesturi fuissent: illis haec dicantur Romanis, qui tunc victuri sunt; quid ad nos novissimi hominum? quos ut non novimus, ita nec contemnere possumus. XVII.

Hypothesis adversariorum, statuentium, Iudaeorum conversionem circa finem mundi demum futurum esse, obscurat et evertit doctrinam de universali Dei gratia. Nam cor Dei paternum in omnes universaliter et ex aequo misericors denudatur. Concluditur ex aequo, si gratiae divinae imber ferotinus tantum, et in vespera mundi largus, in priore saeculorum orbe rores parce destillat in paucos aliquot, aliis absoluto decreto exclusis?


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ (Dissolution) The doubters object: I. from Zechariah

ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ (Dissolution).

The doubters object: I. from Zechariah.

XIV, 6. 7. And it shall be in that day: there shall be no light; but splendors and condensation. And it shall be one day, which shall be known to Jehovah, not day, nor night; because about the time of evening there shall be light. If there shall be light about the time of evening, in Judea (of which the Prophet Zechariah speaks), undoubtedly the Jews will be illuminated and converted toward the end of the world: The antecedent is true: and the consequent.

Resp. (Response.)

1) Dr. Sebastian Schmid, in the Latin Bible which he edited, intending to show the summary of chapter XIV and its parts, writes: This chapter contains a significant change of affairs under the New Testament.

Its parts are four. I. There is the devastation of Jerusalem by the nations, from v. 1. II. The preaching of the Gospel after the ascension of Christ in Judea, from v. 12, also the conversion of the Gentiles through preaching, from v. 9. III. The punishment of the enemies of Jerusalem, or the church, from v. 12. IV. The breath of Jerusalem and the church of the Gentiles, from v. 16. From these it is clear that the Prophet’s discourse is not simply about the final times, which will immediately precede the end of the world, but about the time following the ascension of Christ (v. 4.) and preceding the conversion of the Gentiles through the preaching of the Gospel (v. 9.). Therefore, the sense of the Prophet’s words is: Christ having been raised to heaven, in Judea (where there will be a meager light of faith), the Gospel will be preached by the Apostles, so that even toward evening, i.e., in the time of the N.T., a richer light of saving knowledge may shine upon the Jews. Evening, speaking physically, is the last hour of the day, or its end.

Hence, speaking allegorically, the time of the N.T. is evening. For the Apostle John said: We know that it is the last hour (even now it has begun), and Paul, 1 Cor.

X, 11. Upon us the ends of the ages have come. 2) Dr.

Calovius in Bibl. Illustr. fol. 1031, explains this prophetic passage somewhat more generally, saying: Others think that the vicissitudes of the church are designated here in general, and that no time in particular is looked to: such as the three major vicissitudes found in the ecclesiastical history of the New Testament. The first, when there was darkness under the ten persecutions of the tyrants, but toward the evening of those calamities, in the time of Constantine the Great, light arose.

The second, when darkness in turn encroached from the faction of the Arians and other heretics, which however was dispelled, light having arisen in the church, until for the third time under the Anti-Christ darkness was made again: where, however, there was a day that was neither day nor night: because it had some light, due to some part of the catechism left behind, and the evangelical light shining solidly through the confession of the witnesses of the truth: until toward the evening of the world a fuller light shone forth at the time of the evangelical reformation.

II. From Hos. III, 4. 5. For the children of Israel shall sit many days; without a King, and without a Prince, and without a sacrifice, and without a statue, and without an ephod, and without theraphim. Afterward the children of Israel shall return, and seek Jehovah their God, and shall come with fear to Jehovah, and to his goodness in the extremity of days.

An argument is born from the words of Hosea: Whoever shall return to Jehovah in the extremity of days, their universal conversion is to be hoped for toward the end of the world: But the Israelites &c. Therefore.

The major is evident: because the extremity of days is the time immediately preceding the end of the world. Resp. by denying the major. For 1) the Prophet does not speak of all Israelites, but only of the ten tribes of Israel, who in the time of Jeroboam had separated themselves from the Judeans, and over a long lapse of time had lived in a most afflicted state without a king and without divinely instituted worship. Their return to Jehovah is not a universal conversion of the entire Israelite people. 2) The phrase "extremity of days" used in the scriptures designates either the very time of the arrival of the Messiah, or the entire time after Christ was exhibited, up to the consummation of the age. Conf. Isa. II, 2. Joel II, 28. Mic. IV, 1. Acts II, 17. Heb. I, 2. See, if you please, B. Calovius, Biblia illustrata, part II, O.T., fol. 720; the same, part II, N.T., fol. 1107. Whatever, therefore, Hosea says will happen בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים, in the extremity of days, he signified that it would happen either during the very arrival of Christ in the flesh, or throughout the time of the New Testament. For which reason, from the prophecy of Hosea, the particular and successive conversion of the Israelites is rightly inferred, but not a universal and simultaneous one. The chief glory of the successive conversion of the Israelites, however, must be left to the apostolic age; although we do not deny that after the death of the Apostles, not a few Israelites were converted to Christ sporadically and successively.

Latin:

ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ.

Obiiciunt diffidentes: I. ex Zachar.

XIV, 6. 7. Erit vero in die illo: non erit lux; sed splendores et condensatio. Eritque dies unus, qui notus erit Iehovae, non dies, nec nox; quia circa tempus etiam vesperae erit lux. Si circa tempus vesperae erit lux, in Iudaea, (de qua Propheta Zacharias loquitur) haud dubie Iudaei sub finem mundi illuminabuntur et convertentur: Antecedens est verum: et consequens.

Resp.

1) D. Sebastianus Schmidius in latinis bibliis, quae edidit, summam capitis XIV. eiusque partes ostensurus, scribit: Habet hoc caput insignem rerum sub novo testamento mutationem.

Partes eius quatuor. I. Est Hierosolymae per gentes devastatio, a v. 1. II. Evangelii post ascensionem Christi in Iudaea praedicatio, a v. 12. etiam gentilium per praedicationem conversio, a v. 9. III. Poena hostium Hierosolymae, seu ecclesiae, a v. 12. IV. Hierosolymae et ecclesiae gentium flatus, a v. 16. Ex his patet, non esse sermonem Prophetae de temporibus simpliciter ultimis, finem mundi proxime antegressuris, sed de tempore ascensionem Christi insequente, (v. 4.) et gentilium per praedicationem evangelii conversionem antecedente (v. 9.). Sensus itaque verborum Prophetae est: Christo in coelum evecto, in Iudaea (ubi exigua lux fidei erit), praedicabitur ab Apostolis evangelium, vt etiam circa vesperam, i. e. tempore N. T. Iudaeis vberior salutiferae cognitionis lux affulgeat. Vespera, physice loquendo, est hora vltima diei, vel huius terminus.

Proinde ἀλληγορικῶς loquendo, tempus N. T. est vespera. Apostolus quippe Ioannes aiebat: Cognoscimus, quod extrema hora fit (etiam nunc coeperit), et Paulus, 1 Cor.

X, 11. In nos fines saeculorum occurrerunt. 2) D.

Calovius in bibl. illustr. fol. 1031. hunc locum propheticum aliquando generalius explicat, dicens: Alii in genere vices ecclesiae hic designari censent, nullum vero in specie tempus respici: quales vicissitudines trinae potiores in historia ecclesiastica novi testamenti reperiuntur. Prima cum tenebrae fuere sub decem persecutionibus tyrannorum, sub vesperam autem calamitatum illarum tempore Constantini M. lux orta est.

Altera, cum tenebrae vicissim ingruerunt a factione Arianorum, et aliorum haereticorum, quae tamen discussae, exorta luce in ecclesia, usque dum tertio sub Anti-Christo tenebrae factae sint denuo: ubi tamen dies fuit, quae neque dies, neque nox: quia aliquid lucis habuit, ob relictam aliquam partem catecheseos, et solide micantem per testium veritatis confessionem lucem evangelicam: donec sub mundi vesperam lux plenior effulgerit tempore reformationis evangelicae.

II. Ex Hos. III, 4. 5. Dies multos sedebunt filii Israëlis; non Rex, et non Princeps, et non sacrificium, et non statua, et non ephodum, et non theraphim. Dein reuertentur filii Israelis, et quaerent Iehouam Deum suum, et cum timore venient ad Iehouam, et ad bonum eius in extremitate dierum.

Nalcitur e verbis Hoseae argumentum: Quicunque in extremitate dierum reuertentur ad Iehouam, illorum uniuersalis conuersio sub finem mundi speranda est: Atqui Israëlitae &c. Ergo.

Maior est evidens: quia extremitas dierum est tempus mundi finem proxime antecedens. Resp. negando mai. Nam 1) non loquitur Propheta de omnibus Israëlitis, sed tantum de decem tribubus Israëlis, qui tempore Ieroboami se a Iudæis segregauerant, & longo temporum tractu in statu afflictissimo absque rege, & cultu diuinitus instituto vixerant. Horum reditus ad Iehouam non est vniuersalis totius populi Israëlitici conuersio. 2) Extremitas dierum phrasi in scripturis vsitata designat aut tempus ipsum aduentus Messiæ, aut vniuersum tempus post exhibitum Christum, vsque ad consummationem sæculi. Conf. Es. II, 2. Ioel. II, 28. Mich. IV, 1. Act. II, 17. Hebr. I, 2. Vide, fis, B. Calovii biblia illustrata part. II. V. T. fol. 720. idem part. II. N. T. fol. 1107. Quidquid igitur Hoseas futurum dicit בְּאַחֲרִית הַיָּמִים, in extremitate dierum, illud aut sub ipsum Christi in carnem aduentum, aut toto noui testamenti tempore euenturum esse, significauit. Quam ob rem ex prophetia Hoseæ recte colligitur Israëlitarum conuersio particularis & successiua, non autem vniuersalis & simultanea. Præcipua autem successiuæ Israëlitarum conuersionis gloria æuo apostolico relinquenda est; quamuis non diffiteamur, post obitum Apostolorum Israëlitas haud paucos ad Christum sparsim & successiue conuersos esse.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: III. From Rom. XI, 26. Καὶ ὅτω πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται, And so all Israel shall be saved, scil. until the fullness of the Gentiles has entered…

III. From Rom. XI, 26. Καὶ ὅτω πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται, And so all Israel shall be saved, scil. until the fullness of the Gentiles has entered in, ver. 25.

From which words of the Apostle an argument can be formed: He who says that all Israelites will be saved after the conversion of the Gentiles is completed, by this very fact asserts that all Jews will be converted to Christ toward the end of the world: But Paul &c. Therefore. Resp. by denying the minor. For 1) if, according to the mind of many interpreters, you take "all Israel" to mean the spiritual assembly of Israel, gathered from Jews and Gentiles, according to the Pauline phrase, Rom. II, 28; ch. IX, 6; Gal. VI, 16, and the connection of this chapter, which deals with the contention of both peoples in being saved, v. 11, 12, 13, 14, 21, 23, those who disagree will never prove a universal conversion of the Jews from the cited passage. But if you understand Israel according to the flesh (because both the use of that word in the preceding verses and the opposition of the "fullness" of the Gentiles seem to demand it): yet not all Israel according to the flesh in a reduplicative sense, insofar as it enjoys carnal generation, but in a specificative sense, which is at the same time truly Israel through faith, or who has been reborn by the Holy Spirit and elected, is to be understood. Wherefore the Pauline proposition is universal, not absolutely, but limitedly.
