The limitation is had in this chapter XI of Romans, v. 2: God has not rejected His people whom He foreknew; likewise v. 5: If therefore even at the present time a remnant has been made according to the election of grace; and also v. 23: They indeed also (the Israelites) if they do not persist in unbelief, shall be grafted in. Wherefore, with the limitation added, this sense emerges: All Israel, whom God foreknew would believe in Christ, shall be saved: or, all Israel, elected to eternal life, shall be saved; or, all Israelites who do not persist in unbelief shall be saved. But from this it is not permitted to conclude: the entire nation of Israelites, or the greatest part of the Jews, will be converted; since it is certain that there is neither faith of all, nor election of many. 2) The particle ἄχρις ὅ, "until," or "up to," does not always denote the cessation or end of something, but frequently in affirmative propositions denotes continuation, so that it is equivalent to "always." Compare Ps. CX, 1; Ps. CXXIII, 2; Matt. XXVIII, 20; 1 Cor. XV, 25; 1 Tim. IV, 13. Wherefore the mind of the Apostle is: As long as the conversion of the Gentiles is continued, and their entry into the church: so long will the Jews be converted successively. But the conversion of the Gentiles will be continued throughout the entire time of the New Testament: Therefore also that of the Jews.

Latin:

III. Ex Rom. XI, 26. Καὶ ὅτω πᾶς Ἰσραὴλ σωθήσεται, Et sic omnis Israël saluabitur, scil. donec plenitudo gentium introiuerit, vers. 25.

E quibus verbis Apostoli formari potest argumentum: Qui dicit, omnes Israëlitas post impletam gentium conuersionem saluatum iri, is hoc ipso asserit, omnes Iudæos sub finem mundi ad Christum conuersum iri: Atqui Paulus &c. Ergo. Resp. neg. min. Nam 1) si, ex mente multorum interpretum, omnem Israëlem accipias de cœtu Israëlis spirituali, ex Iudæis & gentilibus collecto, iuxta phrasin Paulinam, Rom. II, 28. c. IX, 6. Gal. VI, 16. & συνάφειαν huius capitis, quod de vtriusque populi in saluando contentione agit, v. 11. 12. 13. 14. 21. 23. diffidentes e loco citato vniuersalem Iudæorum conuersionem nunquam probabunt. Sin autem intelligas Israëlem secundum carnem (quia id tum illius vocis vsus in antecedentibus, tum oppositio πληρώματος gentium postulare videtur): non tamen omnis Israël secundum carnem in sensu reduplicatiuo, quatenus carnali generatione gaudet, sed specificatiuo, qui simul vere est Israël per fidem, siue qui a Spiritu S. renatus, & electus est, intelligendus est. Quare propositio Paullina est vniuersalis, non absolute, sed limitate. Limitatio habetur in hoc ipite XI. Rom. v. 2. Non reprobauit Deus populum suum, quem præsciuit; it. v. 5. Si ergo etiam in præsenti tempore reliquiæ secundum electionem gratiæ factæ sunt; nec non v. 23. Illi vero etiam (Israëlita) si non permanserint in incredulitate, inferentur. Quare limitatione adiecta; hic emergit sensus: Omnis Israël, quem Deus præsciuit crediturum esse in Christum, saluabitur: vel, omnis Israël, ad vitam æternam electus, saluabitur; vel, omnes Israëlita, qui non permanent in incredulitate, saluabuntur. At exinde concludere non licet: vniuersa Israëlitarum natio, vel maxima pars Iudæorum, conuertetur; cum constet, nec fidem omnium, nec electionem multorum esse. 2) Particula ἄχρις ὅ, donec, siue vsque, non semper desitionem aut finem alicuius rei, sed frequenter in propositionibus affirmatiuis continuationem, vt æquipolleat τῷ semper, denotat. Confer, Ps. CX, 1. Ps. CXXIII, 2. Matth. XXVIII, 20. 1 Cor. XV, 25. 1 Tim. IV, 13. Quocirca mens Apostoli est: Quamdiu continuabitur conuersio gentium, & horum introitus in ecclesiam: tamdiu successiue conuertentur Iudæi. At gentilium conuersio continuabitur toto noui testamenti tempore: Ergo & Iudæorum.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: IV. You say: There will be no mystery if certain Israelites, who believe in the gospel, are saved, when nevertheless the Apostle expressly…

IV. You say: There will be no mystery if certain Israelites, who believe in the gospel, are saved, when nevertheless the Apostle expressly calls it a mystery, Rom. XI, 25.

The successive and particular conversion of the Jews, since it is a most well-known thing, does not deserve to be distinguished by the name of a mystery.

Resp. A mystery, as scripture indicates, is a dogma hidden and so sublime, that it exceeds the grasp of reason, that it exceeds the grasp transcends reason, nor is it understood, except from divine revelation.

Now, indeed, it transcends the grasp of our reason that the doors of divine grace should remain open until the end of the age to the Jews, who killed Christ, the author of salvation, and held the means of salvation in contempt. This is something we would not have perceived, had God not revealed it to us. The mystery therefore remains, even though it has become known to us through revelation.

Quest. XVII. Will the great Anti-Christ be so defeated by a certain majestic advent of Christ that he is overthrown before the millennial kingdom of Christ is established?

EXPOSITION

Obs.

I. The word, Anti-Christ, is accepted in the sacred code in two ways: a) Generally, for any heretics who disseminate false doctrines, and those opposing the doctrine of Christ, and who stubbornly defend them.

Of whom St. John says: Even now, he says, there are many Anti-Christs, 1 ep. ch. II, 18. who are commonly called little Anti-Christs: b) Specifically and preeminently for that notable adversary of Christ, described in 2 Thess. II, 3. sqq., whom, for the sake of distinction, we call the great Anti-Christ.

Obs.

II. A distinction must be made between the eastern Anti-Christ, or Mahomet, who, sitting outside the temple of God, wishes it to be utterly destroyed: and the western Anti-Christ, or the Roman Pontiff, who sits in the temple of God, 2 Thessal. II, 4. i.e., rules in the midst of the church, which he does not wish to be completely destroyed, like Mahomet, but governed by himself with monarchical power. At present, we are dealing with the ruin of the western Anti-Christ, sitting in the temple of God.

The antithesis is that of the Chiliasts, who maintain that the Anti-Christ will be destroyed by a certain majestic advent of Christ before the millennial kingdom of Christ is established, so that the church, within that blessed millennium, may enjoy the most pleasant tranquility.

Asserts this very thing CHRISTIAN HOBVRG. in apol. Praetoriana, p. 287.

The Great Prince Michael will arise and save his people, overthrow the Anti-Christ, bind Satan, and make his kingdom in the world glorious for a short time known to him. Then, after the destruction of the fourth monarchy, the fifth shall be set up by the arrival of the Lord Christ, when all kings, princes, and potentates shall lay down their rule and offices, and no one shall let themselves be called masters anymore.

And QVIRINVS KVHLMANNVS, in the book which he entitled: Neubegeisterter Böhm, ch. XIV.

The very last time will soon dawn, and open all mysteries, because the restoration of all things draws near. All world-empires will fall as soon as it dawns at midnight. The Papacy, Turkdom, along with all sects and religions, will then reach their certain end.

Afterwards he shall appear again with Noah, Moses, and Elias, and Elias will give fire-signs in the world as a sign. The breaking of the great city of Babel, of confused Christendom, stands at the door; all sects shall soon be terrified. In a short time, the Anti-Christ, together with the beast, the whore, and the false prophets, will be discovered and stabbed by a youth.

A great king and ruler of the earth will be born a little after the noon of the sixth day; great heroes are around him, prophets prophesy of him, and his splendor rises from the rising to the setting [of the sun]. The conversion of the Turks, Jews, and Heathens is to be expected immediately. The mystery of the Jesus-Monarchy or Kingdom of God will be completed at seventeen o'clock, and there will be thereafter a tabernacle of God with men.

Objection III. Our discourse is not concerning the ruin or partial fall of the Anti-Christ, but concerning the total one. The authority and power of the Anti-Christ has indeed fallen in many places; yet he will retain some dominion, which he arrogated and took to himself over the church of Christ, until the day of the final judgment, although it has been broken and diminished.

Latin:

IV. Dicis: Nullum erit mysterium, si quidam Israëlita, qui euangelio credunt, saluentur, cum tamen Apostolus diserte mysterium appellet, Rom. XI, 25.

Successiua & particularis Iudæorum conuersio, cum sit res notissima, nomine mysterii insigniri non meretur.

Resp. Mysterium, scriptura indice, est dogma reconditum & adeo sublime, vt captum rationis sublime, vt captum rationis transcendat, nec, nisi ex revelatione divina, intelligatur.

Iam vero captum rationis nostrae transcendit, quod Iudaeis, qui Christum salutis auctorem occiderunt, & media salutis despicatui habuerunt, fores gratiae divinae usque ad consummationem saeculi pateant. Id quod perspectum non haberemus, nisi Deus nobis id revelasset. Manet ergo mysterium, licet nobis ex revelatione innotuerit.

Quaest. XVII. An Anti-Christus magnus, adventu quodam Christi maiestatico, sic debellabitur, ut evertatur prius, quam regnum Christi millenarium constituatur?

ΕΚΘΕΣΙΣ

Obs.

I. Vox, Anti-Christus, in sacro codice bifariam accipitur: a) Generatim, pro quibusuis haereticis, qui falsas, & doctrinae Christi aduersantes doctrinas disseminant, easque pertinaciter propugnant.

De quibus S. Ioannes: Etiam nunc, inquit, Anti-Christi multi sunt, 1 ep. c. II, 18. qui vulgo dicuntur Anti-Christi parui: b) Speciatim & κατ' ἐξοχὴν pro insigni illo Christi aduersario, 2 Thess. II, 3. sqq. descripto, quem differentiae caussa, Anti-Christum magnum vocamus.

Obs.

II. Distinguendum est inter Anti-Christum orientalem, siue Mahometum, qui, sedens extra templum Dei, hoc plane vult conuulsum: & inter Anti-Christum occidentalem, siue Pontificem Romanum, qui sedet in templo Dei, 2 Thessal. II, 4. h. e. in media ecclesia dominatur, quam non vult penitus destructam, vt Mahometus, sed a se potestate monarchica gubernatam. In praesenti agimus de ruina Anti-Christi occidentalis, sedentis in templo Dei.

Antithesis est Chiliastarum, statuentium, Anti-Christum maiestatico quodam Christi adventu deletum iri prius, quam millenarium Christi regnum constituatur, vt ecclesia, intra beatum illud millennium, iucundissima tranquillitate perfruatur.

Asserit hoc ipsum CHRISTIAN HOBVRG. in apol. Praetoriana, p. 287.

Der Groß-Fürst Michael wird sich ausmachen und sein Volk erretten, den Anti-Christ stürzen, den Satan binden, sein Reich in der Welt eine kurze Zeit ihm bekannt herrlich machen. Da soll alsdenn nach Verstörung der vierten Monarchie die fünste durch des Herrn Christi Ankunst angerichtet werden, da alle Könige, Fürsten und Gewaltigen ihre Herrschast und Aemter niederlegen, und keine sich mehr Herren nennen lassen sollen.

Et QVIRINVS KVHLMANNVs, in libro, quem inscripsit: Neubegeisterter Böhm, cap. XIV.

Die allerletzte Zeit wird bald anbrechen, und erössnen alle Verborgenheiten, weil die Wiederbringung aller Dinge herzu nahet. Alle Welt-Reiche werden fallen, so bald es in Mitternacht taget. Das Pabstthum, Türkenthum, nebst allen Secten und Religionen erlangen alsdenn ihre gewisse Endschast.

Darnach soll wieder erscheinen mit Noah, Moses und Elias, und wird Elias Feuer-Zeichen in der Welt zum Zeichen geben. Die Zerbrechung der großen Stadt Babel, der verwirrten Christenheit, stehet vor der Thür, alle Secten sollen bald entsetzet werden. Es wird in kurzem der Anti-Christ samt dem Thiere, der Huren und falschen Propheten von einem Jünglinge entdecket und erstocket werden.

Ein großer König und Beherrscher des Erdreichs wird ein wenig über den Mittag des sechsten Tages gebohren, große Helden sind um ihn, Propheten weissagen von ihm, und sein Glanz gehet auf, vom Ausgang bis zum Niedergang. Der Türken, Jüden und Heyden Bekehrung ist stracks zu erwarten. Das Geheimniß der Jesus-Monarchie oder Reiches Gottes werden vollendet um sieben und zehen Uhr, und wird seyn hernach eine Hütte Gottes bey den Menschen.

Obiectio III. Non est nobis sermo de ruina, vel lapsu Anti-Christi partiali, sed de totali. Cecidit quidem multis locis auctoritas & potestas Anti-Christi; aliquod tamen dominium, quod in ecclesiam Christi sibi arrogauit & sumpsit, retinebit, vsque ad diem extremi iudicii, quamuis illud fractum & imminutum sit.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: BEBAIΩΣIΣ (Confirmation) We prove our assertion from the classic passage 2 Thess. II, 8

BEBAIΩΣIΣ (Confirmation) We prove our assertion from the classic passage 2 Thess. II, 8.

Then shall that wicked one be revealed (ἀποκαλυφθήσεται), whom the Lord shall consume (ἀναλώσει) with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy (καταργήσει) with the brightness of his coming (τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ).

In which words the Apostle speaks of three cases befalling the Anti-Christ. a) He describes the ἀποκάλυψιν, or revelation of the Anti-Christ, which happened many centuries ago through the witnesses of the truth, primarily through LUTHER and his assistants, who observed the waxing dominion of the Roman Bishop and detected his cunning machinations. b) ἀνάλωσιν, the consumption made gradually, through the word of God and the ministry of Luther and other faithful teachers, who wore away or diminished the authority of the Roman Pontiff, not in one moment, but little by little and successively, just as the Anti-Christ was not raised to such dignity in one moment, but little by little. c) Κατάργησιν, the abolition: Κατάργησις, in this place, opposed to ἀναλώσει, designates the total destruction of the Anti-Christ. Christ will abolish his great adversary τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, by the appearance of his coming, durch die Erscheinung seiner Zukunft. The word ἐπιφάνεια, as often as it is used concerning Christ, denotes either his former or his latter solemn and visible coming. Compare 1 Timothy VI, 14; 2 Tim. IV, 1. Moreover, παρουσία, when it is used concerning the coming of Christ, denotes nothing but the glorious one, as DANNHAVER says, p. 804. We note further that the Apostle Paul, in both epistles written to the Thessalonians, deals with the coming of Christ to judgment. Cf. 1 Thess. I, 10; chap. II, 19; chap. III, 13; chap. IV, 4; chap. V, 1; 2 Thess. I, 7; chap. II, 1, 2, 8. From which arises this argument: He whom Christ will destroy by his solemn, visible, and glorious coming to judgment, the destruction of him will not precede the coming of Christ by a whole millennium; But Christ will destroy the great Anti-Christ, etc. Therefore.

II. At the same time that the devil shall be cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, at that same time the Anti-Christ and his helpers shall rush headlong into hell-fire: But the devil shall be cast into the lake of fire and brimstone on the day of the final judgment: Therefore.

The major is proved, because, as in seduction, so also in punishment, the devil, the beast, and the false prophet are joined, Rev. XX, 10. Καὶ ὁ διάβολος, ὁ πλανῶν αὐτούς, ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ θείου, ὅπε τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, καὶ βασανισθήσονται ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. And the devil, who was deceiving them, was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where the beast and the false prophet are, and they shall be tormented day and night for ever and ever. We note in the present case, in the words of the Apostle saying: ὅπε τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, no verb has been added, and thus ἐβλήθη is to be repeated from the preceding clause, by which the beast and the false prophet were cast. For ὅπε also sometimes signifies motion to a place. But if the substantive verb is to be understood, it can conveniently be added, εἰσὶ, they are, so that the sense may be: where the beast and the false prophet are together, and together undergo eternal torments. Very many have contracted the two propositions of this text into one, in this way: where both the beast and the false prophet shall be tormented. Thus the Vulgate, the Dutch, VATABLUS, ERASMUS; PAGNINUS, MARLORATUS, ERASMUS SCHMIDIUS. ERASMUS; PAGNINUS, MARLORATUS, ERASMUS SCHMIDIUS. You say: The verb ἦσαν, "they were," can be understood. For LUTHER translates it thus: "Da das Thier und der falsche Prophet war" [When the beast and the false prophet were]. This exposition rests on a certain foundation; because ch.

XIX. of the Apocalypse deals with the destruction of the Anti-Christ, but chapter XX with the millennial kingdom.

Therefore, the ruin of the Anti-Christ precedes the millennial kingdom. Resp. It is better to understand εἰσὶ, "they are," than ἦσαν, "they were," because the devil and the beast are joined in punishment.

Most conveniently, however, the verb ἐβλήθη [was cast] is repeated. For this reason, the words of the Apostle do not necessarily imply a preceding casting of the Anti-Christ into hell, but note a simultaneous public condemnation, so that at the same time that the devil was cast into hell by Christ the judge, the Anti-Christ was also cast into that abyss. Mention of the casting of the beast, or Anti-Christ, into hell was indeed made in chapter XIX, but that is repeated in this chapter, and joined with the punishment of the devil, so that it may be indicated that the devil and the Anti-Christ will be publicly condemned by Christ the judge at one and the same time on the last day.

III. As long as tares exist in the field of the church, so long will the Anti-Christ endure.

But tares will exist in the field of the church until the harvest, or until the consummation of the age. Therefore.

The major premise is certain: because the Anti-Christ is the most pernicious of the tares, he is υἱὸς τοῦ πονηροῦ, the son of that evil one.

The minor premise is clear from Matth.

XXIII, 30.39. IV. The genuinely orthodox Theologians agree with us.

D. LUTHER says, in Ps. CX. tom. Ien. "Allein der jüngste Tag soll das Pabstthum zerstören" [Only the last day shall destroy the Papacy].

D. GERHARD in Anti-Christiasino page 304. The ἀνάλωσις [consumption] and κατάργησις [abolition] of the Anti-Christ are distinguished by reason of time and instrument: For the Apostle predicts that the former will happen by the spirit of Christ's mouth before the last day, but the latter by the brightness of the glorious coming of Christ on the day of judgment.

D. CALOV in bibliis illustr. in Apocal. fol. 1911. No century has been without heresy so far, nor will there be one, since the Anti-Christ, the worst of heretics, is to endure until the end of the world.

D. CLUVER, Comment. in Apocal. p. 314. That the Anti-Christ and his false prophet are apprehended alive, and are seized for punishment, is a sufficiently clear indication that the tyranny of the Pope will not perish entirely until the Lord himself destroys it by the glorious manifestation of his coming, just as Paul speaks, 2 Thess.

II, 8. And John agrees; because the appearance and manifestation of the coming of the Lord is always understood as his final coming. D. KROMAYER, Comment. in Apocal. p 433. Kingdoms have fallen away from the obedience of the Roman see, and more will fall away, until the Son of God by his final coming utterly abolishes τὸν ἄνομον [the lawless one].

D. DANNHAUER, in Anti-Christosophia page 253. The term of the Anti-Christ's duration reaches the final judgment.

You say: D. DANNHAUER writes in Anti-Christosophia p. 421. It is nothing strange or singular if the Roman synagogue perishes on the last day, when the whole world will return to nothing.

Resp. In that same place, the most consummate Theologian speaks precisely of the city of Rome, and its destruction, not of the destruction of the entire Anti-Christian kingdom.

Latin:

BEBAIΩΣIΣ Assertionem nostram, probamus ex dicto classico 2 Thess. II, 8.

Tunc reuelabitur (ἀποκαλυφθήσεται) iniquus, quem Dominus consumet (ἀναλώσει) spiritu oris sui, & abolebit (καταργήσει) apparitione aduentus sui (τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ).

Quibus verbis Apostolus de tribus Anti-Christo obtingentibus casibus loquitur. a) Describit Anti-Christi ἀποκάλυψιν, siue reuelationem, quae contigit multis retro lapsis saeculis per testes veritatis, in primis per LVTHERVM, & eius paraestatas, qui inualescentem Episcopi Romani dominatum obseruarunt, eiusque machinamenta callida detexerunt. b) ἀνάλωσιν, consumtionem gradatim factam, per verbum Dei, & ministerium Lutheri, aliorumque fidelium doctorum, qui auctoritatem Pontificis, Romani attriuerunt, vel imminuerunt, non vno momento, sed paullatim & successiue, sicut Anti-Christus non vno momento, sed paullatim ad tantam dignitatem euectus est. c) Κατάργησιν, abolitionem: Κατάργησις, h. l. ἀναλώσει opposita, designat totale Anti-christi excidium. Abolebit Christus magnum suum aduersarium τῇ ἐπιφανείᾳ τῆς παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, apparitione aduentus sui, durch die Erscheinung seiner Zukunft. Vox, ἐπιφάνεια, quoties de Christo adhibetur, toties vel priorem, vel posteriorem eius aduentum solemne atque visibilem denotat. Confer, 1 Timoth. VI, 14. 2 Tim. IV, 1. Παρουσία autem, cum de aduentu Christi vsurpatur, non, nisi gloriosum, denotat, dicente DANNHAVERO, p. 804. Notamus insuper, Apostolum Paullum in vtraque epistola ad Thessalonicenses scripta, agere de aduentu Christi ad iudicium. Conf. 1 Thess. I, 10. cap. II, 19. cap. III, 13. cap. IV, 4. cap. V, 1. 2 Thess. I, 7. cap. II, 1. 2. 8. E quibus nascitur hoc argumentum. Quem Christus solemni, visibili & glorioso aduentu suo ad iudicium destruet, illius destructio integrum millennium non antecedet aduentum Christi; Atqui Anti-Christum magnum Christus &c. Ergo.

II. Quo tempore diabolus coniicietur in stagnum ignis & sulphuris, eodem Anti-Christus, & adiutores eius in ignem infernalem praecipites ruent: Atqui diabolus coniicietur in stagnum ignis & sulphuris in die extremi iudicii: Ergo.

Maior probatur, quia, vt in seductione, ita & in poena coniunguntur diabolus, bestia & pseudo-propheta, Apoc. XX, 10. Καὶ ὁ διάβολος, ὁ πλανῶν αὐτούς, ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν λίμνην τοῦ πυρὸς καὶ θείου, ὅπε τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, καὶ βασανισθήσονται ἡμέρας καὶ νυκτὸς εἰς τοὺς αἰῶνας τῶν αἰώνων. Diabolus autem, qui seducebat eos, coniectus est in stagnum ignis & sulphuris, vbi bestia & pseudo-propheta, & cruciabuntur dies & noctes in saecula saeculorum. Notamus in praesenti, verbis Apostoli, dicentis: ὅπε τὸ θηρίον καὶ ὁ ψευδοπροφήτης, nullum adiectum esse verbum, adeoque e praecedenti cominate repetendum ἐβλήθη, quo bestia & pseudo-propheta coniectus est. Nam & τὸ ὅπε interdum motum ad locum significat. Quod si autem intelligendum sit verbum substantiuum, commode adiici potest, εἰσὶ, sunt, vt sensus sit: vbi bestia & pseudo-propheta simul sunt, & vna aeternos cruciatus subeunt. Plurimi duas huius textus propositiones in vnam contraxerunt, hoc modo: vbi & bestia & pseudo-propheta cruciabuntur. Sic Vulgatus, Belga, VATABLVS, ERASMUS; PAGNINVS, MARLORATUS, ERASMUS SCHMIDIVS. ERASMUS; PAGNINVS, MARLORATUS, ERASMUS SCHMIDIVS. Dicis: Subintelligi potest verbum: ἦσαν, erant. Nam sic vertit LUTHERVS: Da das Thier und der falsche Prophet war. Nititur hæc expositio certo fundamento; quia c.

XIX. Apocal. agitur de excidio Anti-Christi, capite autem XX. de regno millenario.

Ergo ruina Anti-Christi regnum millenarium antecedit. Resp. Melius subintelligitur εἰσὶ, sunt, quam ἦσαν, erant, quia diabolus & bestia in pœna coniunguntur.

Commodissime autem verbum ἐβλήθη repetitur. Quam ob rem verba Apostoli non necessario inferunt præcedaneam Anti-Christi coniectionem in infernum, sed notant simultaneam condemnationem publicam, vt eodem tempore, quo diabolus a Christo iudice in infernum præcipitatus est, etiam Anti-Christus in illud barathrum coniectus fit. Iniecta quidem est etiam capite XIX. mentio præcipitationis bestiæ, sive Anti-Christi in infernum, sed illa hoc capite repetitur, & cum pœna diaboli coniungitur, vt indicetur, diabolum & Anti-Christum vno eodemque tempore a Christo iudice in nouissimo die publice condemnatum iri.

III. Quamdiu exsistent zizania in agro ecclesiæ, tamdiu durabit Anti-Christus.

At zizania exsistent in agro ecclesiæ vfque ad messem, sive ad consummationem sæculi. Ergo.

Maior constat: quia Anti-Christus est zizaniorum perniciosissimum, est υἱὸς τοῦ πονηροῦ, filius illius mali.

Minor liquet ex Matth.

XXIII, 30.39. IV. Consentiunt nobiscum Theologi γνησίως orthodoxi.

D. LUTHERVS ait, in Ps. CX. tom. Ien. Allein der jüngste Tag soll das Pabstthum zerstören.

D. GERHARDVS in Anti-Christiasino pag. 304. Anti-Christi ἀνάλωσις & κατάργησις temporis & organi ratione distinguuntur: Illam enim futuram prædicit Apostolus spiritu oris Christi ante diem nouissimum, hanc vero claritate gloriosi aduentus Christi in die iudicii.

D. CALOVIVS in bibliis illustr. in Apocal. fol. 1911. Nullum hactenus sæculum sine hæresi fuit, nec futurum est, quum Anti-Christus hæreticorum pessimus vsque ad finem mundi duraturus sit.

D. CLVVERVS, Comment. in Apocal. p. 314. Quod Anti-Christus & pseudo-propheta eius vivi apprehenduntur, & ad supplicium rapiuntur, luculentum satis indicium est, non perituram tyrannidem Pontificis omnino, donec ipse dominus eam destruat gloriosa illustratione aduentus sui, sicut Paullus loquitur, 2 Thess.

II, 8. & Ioannes consentit; quia apparitio & illustratio aduentus Domini semper accipitur de eius aduentu postremo. D. KROMAYERVS, Comment. in Apocal. p 433. Regna defecerunt ab obedientia sedis Romanæ, pluraque deficient, donec Filius Dei aduentu suo vltimo τὸν ἄνομον prorsus aboleat.

D. DANNHAVERVS, in Anti-Christosophia pag. 253. Durationis terminus Anti-Christi attingit nouissimum iudicium.

Dicis: D. DANNHAVERVS scribit in Anti-Christosophia p. 421. Nihil mirum, aut singulare, si Romana synagoga in nouissimo die pessum eat, quo totus mundus in nihilum redibit.

Resp. Loquitur ibidem Theologus consummatissimus præcise de vrbe Romana, eiusque interitu, non de excidio totius regni Anti-Christiani.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ [Resolution]

ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ [Resolution].

The opponents object: I. The Apostle John saw the casting of the Anti-Christ into the lake of fire first, Apoc.

XIX, than the blessed millennium, in which Satan was bound, Apoc. XX. Therefore.

The Anti-Christ will perish before the millennial kingdom is established. Resp. Distinguish between the order of the visions and the event.

It is customary for the prophets that what they relate in a later place does not always happen at a later time. Isaiah ch.

VII, 14. ch. IX, 6. deals with the birth of Christ, and ch. XLV, 1. finally with Cyrus, who preceded the birth of Christ by a long interval of time.

II. Long before the rise of the blessed millennium, an angel from heaven cried out with a great voice and power: Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird, Apoc. XVIII, 2. E. The ruin of the Anti-Christ precedes the blessed millennium. Resp. 1) By Babylon the great, Rome is denoted on account of its similar tyranny and similar end. Some interpreters wish the bodily destruction of the city of Rome to be indicated. Hugo Grotius says: That angel announces the consequences, the burning of Rome (concerning which Apoc. XVII, 16.), with a certain explanation of the things said before. Just as the devastation of ancient Babylon is predicted not once, but more often in Isaiah and Jeremiah, 2) Others wish for a spiritual understanding of Babylon, or the ruin of the Anti-Christian kingdom, and that it is not total, but partial, which precedes the final coming of Christ to the solemn judgment, there is no doubt. Let us listen to our Calovius commenting on this passage thus: Babylon has fallen, as regards the public manifestation of its ruin, and the decline of its authority under Emperor Frederick II, who declared that there were many Anti-Christs among the Romanists. It fell under Philip, King of the Gauls, who wrote to Boniface VIII in this manner: Philip, by the grace of God, King of the Gauls, to Boniface, acting as supreme pontiff, little or no greeting! Let your great fatuity know that in temporal matters we are subject to no one, and that the collation of churches and prebends pertains to us by royal right, etc.; but we consider those who believe otherwise to be fools and senseless. It fell under Emperor Louis IV, who publicly declared the Roman Pontiff to be the Anti-Christ. It fell among the eastern churches, which, to the Roman Pontiff demanding obedience, responded thus: We firmly believe in your supreme power over your subjects, but we cannot tolerate your supreme pride, we cannot satisfy your supreme avarice; the devil be with you, because the Lord is with us. What? That even today the Greek church, on the Lord's day of Lent, publicly excommunicates the Roman Pontiff every year as a heretic. It fell, attacked, shattered, and diminished by the spiritual arms of the blessed Martin Luther, the most valiant athlete of Christ, so that very many churches detest the Anti-Christian doctrine of the Roman Pontiff.

III. The kingdom is delivered to the holy people of God after the Anti-Christ is condemned, Dan. VII, 26. E. The millennial kingdom of Christ precedes the ruin of the Roman Pontiff. Resp. In the cited place, it is not a question 1) of the millennial kingdom; but of the kingdom of glory. For it is called eternal, Dan. VII, 27, such as the Chiliastic kingdom is not. 2) Not of the western Anti-Christ, but of the eastern, whom St. John teaches will exist after the blessed millennium, Apoc. XX, 8.

Latin:

ΔΙΑΛΥΣΙΣ.

Obiciunt oi ἐξ ἐναντίας: I. Apostolus Ioannes præcipitationem Anti-Christi in stagnum ignis vidit prius, Apoc.

XIX. quam beatum millennium, quo Satanas ligatus fuit, Apoc. XX. E.

Anti-Christus pessum ibit prius, quam regnum millenarium constituatur. Resp. Dist. inter ordinem visionum, & euentum.

Solemne est prophetis, vt non semper posteriori tempore eueniat, quod posteriori loco enarrant. Esaias c.

VII, 14. cap. IX, 6. de Christi natalibus agit, & c. XLV, 1. demum de Cyro, qui longo temporum interuallo natales Christi antecessit.

II. Dudum ante exortum beatum millennium angelus e caelo virtute & voce magna clamauit: Cecidit, cecidit Babylon magna, & facta est habitaculum daemoniorum, & custodia omnis spiritus immundi, & custodia omnis auis immundae, & exosae, Apoc. XVIII, 2. E. ruina Anti-Christi beatum millennium antecedit. Resp. 1) Per Babylonem magnam denotatur Roma ob similem tyrannidem, & similem exitum. Nonnulli interpretes corporalem interitum vrbis Romae indigitatum volunt. Hugo Grotius ait: Ille angelus consequentia, incendium Romae (de quo Apoc. XVII, 16.) nuntiat, cum quadam ante dictorum explicatione. Sicut Babylonis veteris deuastatio non semel, sed saepius praedicitur apud Esaiam & Ieremiam, 2) Alii intellectum volunt spiritualem Babylonis, siue regni Anti-Christiani ruinam, eamque non totalem, sed partialem, quam praecedere aduentum Christi vltimum ad solemne iudicium, nullum est dubium. Auscultemus Calovium nostrum in h. l. ita commentantem: Cecidit Babylon, quoad manifestationem ruinae publicam, & occasum auctoritatis apud Fridericum II. Imperatorem, qui Anti-Christos multos Romanensibus inesse declarauit. Cecidit penes Philippum regem Galliarum, qui ad Bonifacium VIII. hunc in modum scripsit: Philippus, Dei gratia, Galliarum rex, Bonifacio, gerenti se pro summo pontifice salutem modicam, siue nullam! Sciat tua maxima fatuitas, in temporalibus nos alicui non subesse, ecclesiarum & praebendarum collationem ad nos iure regio pertinere &c. secus autem credentes fatuos & insipientes reputamus. Cecidit apud Ludouicum IV. Imperatorem, qui Pontificem Romanum pro Anti-Christo publice declarauit. Cecidit apud ecclesias orientales, quae Pontifici Romano obedientiam exigenti sic responderunt: Potentiam tuam summam erga subditos tuos firmiter credimus, superbiam tuam summam tolerare non possumus, auaritiam tuam summam satiare non valemus, diabolus tecum, quia Dominus nobiscum. Quid? quod hodieque ecclesia graeca, dominica quadragesima, Pontificem Romanum ceu haereticum quotannis publice excommunicat. Cecidit spiritualibus armis B. Martini Lutheri, fortissimi athletae Christi, oppugnata, quassata, & imminuta, ut plurimae ecclesiae Pontificis Romani doctrinam Anti-Christianam detestentur.

III. Sancto Dei populo traditur regnum post condemnatum Anti-Christum, Dan. VII, 26. E. regnum Christi millenarium ruinam Pontificis Romani antecedit. Resp. L. c. non agitur 1) de regno millenario; sed de regno gloria. Dicitur enim aeternum, Dan. VII, 27. quale non est regnum Chiliasticum. 2) Non de Anti-Christo occidentali, sed de orientali, quem post beatum millennium superfuturum esse docet S. Ioannes, Apoc. XX, 8.


### XIV. What is the end of the extreme judgment?: De Consvmmatione Mvndi. Quaest. XVIII. What is the consummation of the world?

DE CONSVMMATIONE MVNDI. Quaest. XVIII. What is the consummation of the world?

The consummation of the world is the action of the Triune God, by which He will destroy and annihilate with fire the whole machine of heaven and earth, and all created things, except for intelligent creatures, for the glory of His truth, power, and justice, and for the liberation of the elect of mankind. Obf.

I. By the world here is denoted the structure of heaven and earth, and of all created things, with the sole exception of creatures endowed with intellect, namely angels and men.

Obf. II. The consummation of the world is otherwise called the consummation of the age, Matt. XXVIII, 20. Behold! I am with you even unto the consummation of the age, where ἀιών, age, by metonymy added to the subject denotes the world .

For once the world is destroyed, time will end along with it. It is also called the conflagration of the world, from 2 Pet. III, 10. The end of all things, 1 Pet. IV, 7. Quest. XIX.

Does the conflagration of the world precede the ecumenical judgment? The conflagration of the world does not precede the final universal judgment, but follows it.

Proof: 1) Because the heavenly judge will come in the clouds, Matt. XXIV, 30. 2) Because, after the sentence has been pronounced, the pious will be caught up in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air, 1 Thess.

IV, 17. Quest. XX. Is the consummation of this world certainly to be?

The consummation of this universe is certainly to be.

Proof: 1) From the O.T. and indeed from Is. LI, 6. Lift up your eyes to the heavens, and look upon the earth beneath, for the heaven shall vanish away like smoke, and the earth shall wax old like a garment. See also Ps. CII, 26. 27. 2) From the N.T. Heaven and earth παρελεύσονται, shall pass away, Matt. XXIV, 35. As the word of God will endure through its effect; so heaven and earth shall pass away, and lose all their efficacy. The antithesis is that of certain Philosophers, Jews, and Epicureans, who maintain that the world is eternal.

They object:

I. Whatever is God’s dwelling-place, and his footstool, that will never perish (otherwise God would not have a dwelling-place): But heaven and earth is, etc.: Therefore. The minor is evident from Is. LXIV, 15. Resp. Heaven and earth are indeed called God’s dwelling-place and his footstool, after they have been created, for the reason that he manifests his presence in them; otherwise God, an independent and infinite Spirit, neither needs a dwelling-place, nor needs a footstool, since he dwells most sweetly in him-self.

II. God promises that seedtime and harvest, cold and heat shall never perish, Gen. VIII, 22. If seedtime and harvest, cold and heat shall never cease, the world is never to perish. Resp. The vicissitudes of seedtime and harvest, cold and heat shall not cease as long as the earth shall stand; but once this is destroyed, those mobile changes of things shall cease.

III. If the hills shall endure עולם for eternity, then the world shall endure for eternity: But the hills shall endure for eternity, as Moses testifies, Deut. XXXIII, 15. Therefore. Resp. Distinguish between the periodic עולם, and the absolute. Sometimes עולם denotes a long time, not an eternity devoid of an end.

IV. The world has stood unchanged through the course of so many centuries: Therefore it will never perish. Resp. Just as the world has stood unchanged through the course of so many centuries by the will of the Creator; so also it will perish by the will of the Creator.

Quest. XXI. Who will destroy the world? The triune God will dissolve the structure of heaven and earth. Proof: 1) The consummation of the world is an action ad extra, and therefore common to the whole Holy Trinity. 2) From Ps. CII, 26. 27. Thou, O Lord, didst lay the foundation of the earth; and the heavens are the work of thy hands. They shall perish; but thou shalt endure; and all of them shall wax old like a garment, as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed.

Latin:

DE CONSVMMATIONE MVNDI. Quaest. XVIII. Quid est consummatio mundi?

Consummatio mundi est actio Dei trinunius, qua is totam machinam caeli terraeque, & omnes res conditas, creaturis intelligentibus exceptis, igne destruet & annihilabit, in veritatis, potentiae & iustitiae suae gloriam, & electorum hominum liberationem.

Obs. I. Per mundum hic denotatur compages caeli & terrae, rerumque omnium creatarum, solis creaturis intellectu praeditis, nempe angelis & hominibus, exceptis.

Obs. II. Consummatio mundi alias vocatur consummatio saeculi, Matth. XXVIII, 20. Ecce! ego vobiscum sum vsque ad consummationem saeculi, vbi ἀιών, saeculum, per metonymiam adiuncti pro subiecto notat mundum . Destructo quippe mundo tempus una finietur.

Dicitur etiam conflagratio mundi, ex 2 Petr. III, 10. finis omnium, 1 Petr. IV, 7. Quaest. XIX. Num conflagratio mundi iudicium oecumenicum antecedit?

Conflagratio mundi extremum iudicium universale non antecedit, sed sequitur.

Prob. 1) Quia iudex coelestis veniet in nubibus, Matth. XXIV, 30. 2) Quia, post pronuntiatam sententiam, pii rapientur in nubes, in occursum Domini in aere, 1 Thess.

IV, 17. Quaest. XX. An certo futura est consummatio huius mundi?

Consummatio huius universi certo futura est.

Prob. 1) Ex V. T. & quidem ex Es. LI, 6. Tollite in coelum oculos vestros, & spectate ad terram desubter, nam coelum sicut sumus evanescet, & terra sicut vestis inveterascet. Vid. etiam Ps. CII, 26. 27. 2) Ex N. T. Coelum & terra παρελεύσονται, transibunt, Matth. XXIV, 35. Vt verbum Dei qua effectum suum perennabit; ita coelum & terra transibunt, & omnem suam efficaciam perdent. Antithesis est nonnullorum Philosophorum, Iudaeorum & Empaetarum, statuentium, mundum esse aeternum.

Qui obiiciunt:

I. Quidquid est Dei-domicilium, & scabellum pedum eius, illud nunquam interibit (alias Deus non haberet domicilium): Atqui coelum & terra est &c: Ergo. Minor constat ex Es. LXIV, 15. Resp. Coelum & terra dicuntur quidem Dei domicilium & scabellum pedum eius, postquam sunt condita, ideo, quod in iisdem suam praesentiam manifestat; caeteroqui Deus, Spiritus independens & infinitus, nec domicilio indiget, nec scabello indiget, cum habitet suavissime in seipso.

II. Proinifit Deus, sementem & messem, aestatem ac frigus nunquam peritura esse, Gen. VIII, 22. Si nunquam cessabunt sementis & messis, frigus & aestas, mundus nunquam periturus est. Resp. Non cessabunt vicissitudines sementis & messis, frigoris & aestatis, quamdiu stabit terra; at hac destructa, mobiles illae rerum vices cessabunt.

III. Si colles durabunt עולם in aeternum, & mundus in aeternum durabit: Atqui colles durabunt in aeternum, teste Mose, Deut. XXXIII, 15. E. Resp. Dist. inter עולם periodicum, & absolutum. Interdum עולם notat tempus longum, non aeternitatem finis expertem.

IV. Mundus tot saeculorum decursu stetit invariatus: E. nunquam interibit. Resp. Sicut mundus ex voluntate Creatoris tot saeculorum decursu stetit invariatus; ita & ex voluntate Creatoris interibit.

Quaest. XXI. Quis mundum destruet? Deus triunus compagem coeli terraeque dissoluet. Prob. 1) Consummatio mundi est actio ad extra, adeoque toti SS. Trinitati communis. 2) Ex Ps. CII, 26. 27. Deus nii, antea terram fundasti; & opus manuum tuarum sunt coeli. Illi peribunt; sed tu perstabis; & omnes sicut vestis veterascent, sicut vestem mutabis eos, & mutabuntur.


### Q. XXII. By what means will God destroy the world?

God will destroy the world by a true and proper fire a), but the power and nature of which is investigable by no mortal b).

Proof a. From 2 Peter III, 12. The heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements being burnt shall melt. The fire which is kindled, so that the elements are not only burnt by it, but also melt, must be a true fire.

Proof b. The properties and powers of that fire, which will consume the whole machine of heaven and earth, escape the keenness of human wit. For that fire cannot be elemental, which will annihilate all things, and consume itself.

Latin:

Destruet Deus mundum igne vero & proprio a), sed cuius vis & indoles nulli mortalium est peruestigabilis b).

Prob. a. Ex 2 Petr. III, 12. Cæli igne accensi dissoluentur, & elementa combusta liquescent. Qui ignis accenditur, vt elementa eodem comburantur haud tantum, sed etiam liquescant, illum oportet esse verum ignem.

Prob. b. Proprietates & vires illius ignis, qui totam cæli terræque machinam absumet, aciem humani ingenii fugiunt. Nam non potest ignis ille esse elementaris, qui omnia annihilabit, & seipsum consumet.


### Q. XXIII. In what does

The consummation of the world consists formally not in the change or alteration of the qualities of this world, but in the total abolition or annihilation of the substance of the world.

Proof 1) Heaven and earth will perish in such a way that they will no longer be, Revelation XXI, 1. Therefore they will be utterly annihilated. For whatever is changed only according to qualities, still remains.

2) From 2 Peter III, 12. The elements being burnt by fire will melt. From which I gather: Whatever is composed of elements in such a way that it cannot exist without the elements, that, when the elements are abolished, will be reduced to nothing: But the world &c: Therefore.

3) From Revelation XX, 11. From the face of him who sat on the throne, heaven and earth fled away, and no place was found for them. That natural body for which no place is given, does not exist as to its substance: But for the perishing heaven and earth no place is any longer given. Therefore.

4) From Psalm CII, 26, 27. The heavens will perish, but you will remain. In the way that God remains, in that way heaven and earth do not remain: But God remains according to substance: Therefore heaven and earth do not remain according to substance.

There is an antithesis of certain Fathers and Scholastics, according to whose opinion the world will be changed as regards its qualities, so that it may be advanced into a better state, but its substance will not be annihilated. Who object:

I. The world will stand forever, Ps. CIV, 5. Therefore, it will not be annihilated. Resp. In the cited place, עולם denotes a long duration of time.

II. The schema of the world passes away, 1 Cor. VII, 31. Therefore, not the world itself. The reason for the consequence is: because σχῆμα is only an external figure. Resp. In the cited place, by σχῆμα is understood not the external figure of the world, but the external splendor of worldly things, such as is seen in food, drink, clothing, retinue, and buildings, which will not be changed for the better, but like a small cloud will pass away entirely.

III. Whatever is changed, like a garment, its substance does not perish: But the world &c. Ps. CII, 28. Therefore. The major premise is evident; because a garment is changed in such a way that the inner side becomes the outer. Resp. The words of David are these: They all shall grow old like a garment; as a garment Thou shalt change them. A garment growing old is eventually worn away, so that it is seen nowhere.

IV. Whatever is renewed, is not annihilated: But the world &c: Therefore. The minor premise is proved from Ps. CIV, 30. Thou shalt send forth Thy Spirit, and they shall be created, and Thou shalt renew the face of the earth. Resp. The Psalmist speaks of the annual renewal, which happens primarily in the spring time, not of the renewal which will take place at the end of the age.

Latin:

Consummatio mundi formaliter consistit non in qualitatum huius mundi mutatione, aut alteratione, sed in totali substantiæ mundi abolitione, aut annihilatione.

Prob. 1) Cœlum & terra ita peribunt, vt non amplius sint, Apoc. XXI, 1. E. penitus annihilabuntur. Nam quidquid tantum secundum qualitates mutatur, adhuc superest.

2) Ex 2 Petr. III, 12. Igne combusta elementa liquescent. Ex quo colligo: Quodcunque compositum ex elementis ita consistit, vt sine elementis exsistere nequeat, illud elementis abolitis in nihilum redigetur: Atqui mundus &c: E.

3) Ex Apoc. XX, 11. A conspectu eius, qui throno insidebat, fugit cælum & terra, & locus non est inuentus eis. Cuius corporis naturalis non datur locus, illud, quoad substantiam, non adest: Atqui cæli & terræ pereuntis non amplius datur locus. E.

4) E Ps. CII, 26. 27. Cæli peribunt, tu autem perstabis. Quo pacto Deus permanet, eo pacto cælum & terra non permanent: Atqui Deus permanet secundum substantiam: E. cœlum & terra non permanent secundum substantiam.

Antithesis est quorundam Patrum & Scholasticorum, ex quorum sententia mundus mutabitur, quoad qualitates, vt in meliorem prouehatur statum, sed eius substantia non annihilabitur. Qui obiiciunt:

I. Mundus stabit in æternum, Ps. CIV, 5. E. non annihilabitur. Resp. L. c. עולם notat diuturnum tempus.

II. Schema mundi transit, 1 Cor. VII, 31. E. non mundus ipse. Ratio consequentiæ est: quia σχῆμα est tantum externa figura. Resp. L. c. per σχῆμα non externa figura mundi, sed externus splendor rerum mundanarum intelligitur, qualis in cibo, potu, vestitu, comitatu & ædificiis conspicitur, qui non mutabitur in melius, sed instar nubeculæ penitus transibit.

III. Quidquid mutatur, vt vestimentum, illius substantia non perit: Atqui mundus &c. Ps. CII, 28. Ergo. Maior patet; quia vestimentum sic mutatur, vt latus interius fiat exterius. Resp. Verba Dauidis hæc sunt: Omnes sicut vestis veterascent; sicut vestem mutabis eos. Vestimentum veterascens deteritur tandem, vt nullibi conspiciatur.

IV. Quidquid renouatur, non annihilatur: Atqui mundus &c: E. Minor probatur ex Ps. CIV, 30. Emittes Spiritum tuum, & creabuntur, & renouabis faciem terræ. Resp. Hieropsaltes loquitur de annua renouatione, quæ in primis contingit tempore verno, non de renouatione, quæ fiet in fine sæculi.


### Q. XXIV. What is the end of the conflagration of the world?

The primary end of the conflagration of the world is the glory of God a). The secondary end is the liberation of the pious b).

Prob. a. The annihilation of the world testifies to the power of God, just as creation does, and the conflagration of created things is a manifestation of divine justice and wrath against sins.

See Deut. IV, 24. Prob. b. From Luke XXI, 28. When these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.

The consummation of this universe is for the pious the consummation of every temporal calamity.

SIGH.

I appear before thy tribunal, O most just God, seriously with sorrow and fear. I fear that I have offended thee, the most holy God, with my sins! I grieve that I have violated thy law by following the desires of the flesh! But if thou shouldst wish to call back all and each of my thoughts, words, and deeds to a rigid reckoning, I am a miserable man, and no hope of salvation is left to me. But I flee as a suppliant from the tribunal of justice to the throne of grace. O Jesus, heavenly judge, be propitious to me in the hour of judgment! Remember thy most ardent love for me! Remember thy blood shed for me! By the sight of which, absolve me from my sins, and cause that on the last day I may hear that joyful sentence: Come, thou blessed one!

PART IV.

Latin:

Finis primarius conflagrationis mundi est gloria Dei a). Secundarius finis est liberatio piorum b).

Prob. a. Annihilatio mundi testatur de potentia Dei, perinde, ac creatio, & conflagratio rerum conditarum est iustitiae atque irae divinae adversus peccata manifestatio.

Vid. Deut. IV, 24. Prob. b. Ex Luc. XXI, 28. Quando haec omnia incipiunt fieri, suspicite & attollite capita vestra; quia appropinquat liberatio vestra.

Consummatio huius universi piis est consummatio omnis temporalis calamitatis.

SVSPIRIVM.

Compareo coram tribunali tuo, o Deus iustissime, serio cum dolore & timore. Timeo, quod te, Deum sanctissimum, peccatis meis offendi! Doleo, quod legem tuam violavi desideriis carnis obsecutus! Quod si cogitata, dicta, facta mea omnia & singula ad calculos rigide revocare velis, perii miser, nec ulla mihi spes salutis relicta est. Sed confugio supplex a tribunali iustitiae ad thronum gratiae. O Iesu, iudex coelestis, sis mihi propitius in hora iudicii! Memento amoris in me tui ardentissimi! Memento sanguinis tui pro me fusi! Cuius intuitu absolue me a meis peccatis, & fac, vt in die novissimo audiam laetam illam sententiam: Veni, benedicte!

PARTIS IV.


## 38 Of the Church


### Of the Church

Quest. I. Do men who are wayfarers, about to obtain eternal salvation, coalesce into one body? Men who are wayfarers, using the ordinary means of salvation, out of the gratuitous favor of God, on account of the merit of Christ, are gathered by the Holy Spirit into one sacred assembly, or mystical body, which is called the synthetic church, which, that we may consider it only now, a certain reason of method demands. Prob.

The law of accurate method demands, 1) that in dogmatic theology, men to be saved, considered individually, should be treated before they are considered collectively, because the collection presupposes the individuals: 2) We have hitherto weighed the general theological dogmas, by which both the common corruption of fallen men and the universal principles and means of salvation are explained. Now we descend to special dogmas, by which the peculiar duties of ministers of the church and hearers, of magistrate and subjects, of husbands and wives, of masters and servants are set forth. Whence some authors divide theology, just as other practical disciplines, into a common part and a proper part. In the common part, all men indifferently are taught the means of obtaining salvation: In the proper part, which has the likeness of a formed polity, the church and the hierarchical states are treated.

Conf. D. HILDEBRAND. in theol. dogmat. p. 25. Obj. I. Church is a word of Greek origin, and descends ἀπὸ τὸ ἐκκαλεῖν, from calling out, so that there is a certain kind of calling out, or an assembly of those called out from the promiscuous multitude of men.

For which reason the name of church denotes both separation, by the force of the particle, ἐκ, by reason of the term from which, and collection, by the force of the verb, καλεῖν, by reason of the term to which. The name of church owes its birth to the Athenians, among whom ἡ ἐκκλησία was an assembly of citizens, by the voice of a herald, the assembly of citizens of the republic, by the voice of a herald, of the republic cause, selected and called out from the rest of the crowd to hear the sentence of the senate; this is the most ancient acceptance of the name church.

Whence the sacred writers transferred it to a gathering of men who, by the voice of the heralds of the divine word, have been selected and called out from the profane crowd of impious men to hear God’s sentence concerning the attainment of salvation through Christ. Therefore, the term church from which is both the dregs of impious men and the state of sin and wrath; the term to which is the kingdom of God and the state of grace. Obj. II. The word, church, is ambiguous.

1) Church generally denotes any convened assembly. See Ps. XXVI, 4. 5. Acts XIX, 32. 39. Specifically, it denotes the congregation of the faithful, who are convened for the sake of religion, and for the sake of distinction from a profane assembly it is accustomed to be called the church of God, Acts XX, 28; the church of Christ, Matt. XVI, 18; the church of the saints, 1 Cor. XIV, 33. 2) Some ecclesiastical writers and Canonists apply the name of church to the place of sacred assemblies, or the temple, just as the Germans take the word Kirche (i.e., a house [κυριακή]) for the place of sacred assemblies. But in the sacred letters, this signification of church for the place of congregation does not occur. Whence ISIDORE OF PELUSIUM, book II, epist. 246, says: ἄλλο ἐσὶν ἐκκλησία καὶ ἄλλο ἐκκλησιαστήριον [another thing is the church and another the church-building]. It is indeed objected that Paul’s statement, 1 Cor. XI, 18, "When you come together in the church," i.e., in the temple. Resp. Church in that place denotes not the building, but the congregation of the people. For at that time there were no public temples for Christians.

Latin:

Quaest. I. An homines viatores aeternam salutem adepturi in unum coalescant corpus? Homines viatores, ordinariis salutis mediis utentes, ex gratuito Dei fauore, propter meritum Christi, colliguntur per Spiritum S. in unum coetum sacrum, sive corpus mysticum, quod vocatur ecclesia synthetica, quam vt nunc demum confideremus, certa exigit methodi ratio. Prob.

Lex accuratae methodi postulat, 1) vt in theologia dogmatica de hominibus saluandis singulatim pensitatis agatur prius, quam iidem considerentur collective, quia collectio singulos praesupponit: 2) Expendimus hactenus dogmata theologica generalia, quibus tum communis hominum lapsorum corruptio, tum universalia principia & media salutis explicantur. Nunc descendimus ad dogmata specialia, quibus officia peculiaria ministrorum ecclesiae & auditorum, magistratus & subditorum, maritorum & uxorum, dominorum & servorum exponuntur. Vnde nonnulli auctores theologiam aeque, ac alias disciplinas practicas, in partem communem, & propriam dispescunt. Parte communi homines indifferenter omnes media consequendae salutis docentur: In parte propria, quae factae politiae instar habet, de ecclesia & statibus hierarchicis agitur.

Conf. D. HILDEBRAND. in theol. dogmat. p. 25. Obs. I. Ecclesia est vox, origine graeca, & descendit ἀπὸ τὸ ἐκκαλεῖν, ab evocando, vt fit quaedam quasi evocatio, aut coetus evocatorum e promiscua hominum multitudine.

Quam ob rem nomen ecclesiae tum separationem, vi particulae, ἐκ, ratione termini a quo, tum collectionem, vi verbi, καλεῖν, ratione termini ad quem notat. Natales suos nomen ecclesiae debet Atheniensibus, apud quos ἡ ἐκκλησία erat coetus ciuium, praeconis voce, reipublicae cœtus ciuium, præconis voce, reipublicæ causa, ad audiendam senatus sententiam e reliqua turba selectus & euocatus; haec antiquissima est nominis ecclesiae acceptio.

Vnde sacri scriptores eam transtulerunt ad coetum hominum, qui voce praeconum verbi diuini ad audiendam Dei sententiam de consequenda per Christum salute selecti, & ex profana hominum impiorum turba euocati sunt. Proinde terminus ecclesiae a quo est tum hominum impiorum colluuies, tum status peccati & irae; terminus ad quem est regnum Dei & status gratiae. Obi. II. Vocabulum, ecclesia, ambiguum est.

1) Ecclesia generaliter quemuis conuocatum coetum denotat. Vide Ps. XXVI, 4. 5. Act. XIX, 32. 39. Specialiter notat congregationem fidelium, qui religionis causa conuocantur, & ad differentiam coetus profani vocari solet ecclesia Dei, Actor. XX, 28. ecclesia Christi, Matth. XVI, 18. ecclesia sanctorum, 1 Cor. XIV, 33. 2) Scriptores nonnulli ecclesiastici & Canonistae nomine ecclesiae infiguiunt locum sacrorum conuentuum, vel templum, quemadmodum Germani vocem Kirche (q. d. aedes κυριακή) pro loco sacrorum conuentuum accipiunt. At vero in sacris litteris haec significatio ecclesiae pro loco congregationis non occurrit. Vnde ISIDORUS PELVSIOTA libr. II. epist. 246. inquit: ἄλλο ἐσὶν ἐκκλησία καὶ ἄλλο ἐκκλησιαστήριον. Obiicitur quidem dictum Pauli, 1 Cor. XI, 18. Cum conuenitis in ecclesiam, i. e. in templum. Resp. Ecclesia l. c. non aedificium, sed populi congregationem denotat. Nam id temporis Christianis templa publica non fuerunt. Quaest.


### Quest. II. Why is the church called synthetic?

The synthetic church is the church taken collectively, consisting of teachers and hearers, joined by the bond of the same faith a), and it is called the synthetic church, in distinction from the representative church, which is a gathering of teachers solemnly assembled to decide questions concerning the doctrine of faith and the morals of Christians b).

Prob. a. The synthetic church is called ἀπὸ τῆς συνθέσεως [from the composition], from the collection or composition of all the living members of the church, which make one mystical body, which does not consist of mere eyes, or teachers, but also of hands and feet, or hearers.

Prob. b. The word, church, in the sacred code is sometimes taken by synecdoche of the whole for the part, for the gathering of teachers and legates of the church, who represent the synthetic church; and whatever they do in a public name by granted authority is held as ratified by the other members of the church, and is esteemed by all to be done or to have been done. Thus the word, church, is taken in Matt. XVIII, 16, where Christ says: "Tell it to the church," understanding the representative gathering of each synthetic church in a council, synod, or consistory. From which, however, the Papists cannot infer that one individual, e.g., the Roman Pontiff, can represent the church, since the name church is collective, and a collection is made of many.

Obs. The word, church, properly and exquisitely taken, denotes the gathering of true believers and saints. But when the signification of the word, church, is restricted to the gathering of teachers, that restriction is made by synecdoche of the whole for the part; conversely, when the signification of the word, church, is so amplified that it denotes a promiscuous gathering of the called, consisting of true believers and mixed-in hypocrites, that amplification is made by synecdoche of the part for the whole, by which there is attributed to the whole aggregate what properly belongs to the more important part; e.g., a heap consisting of grains of wheat and mixed-in chaff is called in common speech a heap of wheat, by denomination through synecdoche, taken from the more important part. synecdoche, taken from the more important part.

Latin:

Ecclesia synthetica est ecclesia collectiue sumta constans ex doctoribus & auditoribus, eiusdem fidei vinculo coniunctis a), & appellatur ecclesia synthetica, ad differentiam ecclesiae repraesentatiuae, quae est coetus doctorum, ad decidendum quaestiones de doctrina fidei & moribus christianorum solemniter congregatorum b).

Prob. a. Ecclesia synthetica dicitur ἀπὸ τῆς συνθέσεως, a collectione, vel compositione omnium viuorum ecclesiae membrorum, quae faciunt vnum corpus mysticum, quod non constat ex meris oculis, siue doctoribus, sed etiam manibus & pedibus, siue auditoribus.

Prob. b. Vox, ecclesia, in sacro codice interdum per synecdochen totius pro parte sumitur pro coetu doctorum & legatorum ecclesiae, qui ecclesiam syntheticam repraesentant, & quidquid iidem nomine publico ex potestate concessa gerunt, id a ceteris ecclesiae membris ratum habetur, atque ab omnibus geri, vel gestum aestimatur. Ita sumitur vocabulum, ecclesia, Matth. XVIII, 16. vbi Christus inquit: Dic ecclesiae, intelligens coetum repraesentatiuum cuiusque ecclesiae syntheticae in concilio, synodo aut consistorio. Ex quo tamen Pontificii colligere nequeunt, vnum indiuiduum v. gr. Pontificem Romanum posse ecclesiam repraesentare, cum nomen ecclesia sit collectiuum, & collectio fit plurium.

Obs. Vox, ecclesia, proprie & exquisite sumta, denotat coetum vere credentium & sanctorum. Cum autem significatio vocis, ecclesia, restringitur ad coetum doctorum, restrictio illa fit per synecdochen totius pro parte; contra cum significatio vocis, ecclesia, ita ampliatur; vt denotet coetum vocatorum promiscuum, constantem ex vere credentibus & admixtis hypocritis, illa ampliatio fit per synecdochen partis pro toto, qua toti aggregato tribuitur, quod parti potiori proprie competit, v. gr. aceruus constans ex granis tritici & admixta palea, populari sermone vocatur aceruus tritici, denominatione per synecdochen, a parte potiori sumta. synecdochen, a parte potiori sumta.


### Quaest. III. In how many ways is the term, synthetic church, understood?

The synthetic church is understood in two ways: a) κυρίως, strictly, properly, & precisely, for the assembly of men who are truly believing and holy, joined to Christ the head through faith, and constituting one mystical and living body: b) παχυλῶς, broadly & improperly, and by synecdoche for the assembly of the called, aggregated from those who are truly believing and holy, and the intermingled hypocrites and evil persons, who nevertheless profess the same faith.

Obs. I. Other authors teach that the term, church, is taken in two ways: a) for the assembly of τῶν κλητῶν, the called, who profess the same doctrine of faith and use the sacraments instituted by Christ: b) for the assembly of τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν, the elect, who believe in Christ with true faith. For the elect, the Augsburg Confession, Art. VIII, substitutes those who are truly believing and holy; because besides the elect, others, not elected to eternal life, are living members of the church, namely the πρόσκαιροι, who truly believe in Christ and are truly holy; and thus are genuine members of the church in that state, even though they are not elected to glory. Some therefore distinguish between the elect to grace and to glory. By the elect to grace, they understand all the regenerate, who either believe only for a time, or persevere in faith until the end of life. We, because of the ambiguity of the word, election, call the church strictly, properly, and principally so-called, with the Aug. Conf., the assembly of men who are truly believing and holy, or the assembly of the regenerate.

Obs. II. The assembly of the regenerate is called invisible by reason of its internal form (which is founded in justifying faith, by which the members are joined to Christ the head); but the promiscuous assembly of the called is visible by reason of its external form (which consists in the public society of the profession of the same faith).

Prob. a. That the church κυρίως, strictly, properly, & exquisitely so-called, is the assembly of those who are truly believing and holy, is evinced:

1) Because it is expressly called the church of the saints, 1 Cor. XIV, 33; a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for God's own possession, 1 Pet. II, 9. In the Apostles' Creed it is called the communion of saints: likewise the one holy, catholic church, which epithets and honorable encomiums belong primarily, in themselves, and properly to the church precisely accepted for the congregation of those who are truly believing and holy.

2) The church is a pure virgin and the bride of Christ, 2 Cor. XI, 2. Betrothed to Christ through faith, Hos. II, 20. Wherefore a man, devoid of faith, is not a true part of the church. It is also called the mother of the children of God, Gal. IV, 26. But we are children of God through faith in Christ Jesus, Gal. III, 26. Therefore the church is the mother of the faithful, not of hypocrites, not of the impious, not of heretics; it is the mother of the living, not of the dead.

3) Eph. IV, 16, the church is described as a spiritual body, which in its entirety, according to all the joints (by which it is compacted in the manner of one body), depends on Christ as from the head, i.e., through an influx, such as redounds from the head into the members, that it may receive from Him an increase suitable to the body, and that through charity. Whence it is gathered that all and only those are true members of the church properly so-called, who live from supernatural grace and the influx of Christ the head and His Spirit, and thus possess true faith, joined with charity.

4) The church is a spiritual kingdom, which is within us, Luke XVII, 21; it is the kingdom of Christ, which is not of this world, John XVIII, 39. Hence the church is a kingdom distinct from the kingdom of the devil. But it is certain that the impious are in the power of the devil and are members of the kingdom of the devil, as Paul teaches, Eph. II, 2, when he says: that the devil is effective in the unbelievers.

Wherefore since the church truly becomes the kingdom of Christ, [and] properly is the congregation of the saints. For the impious are ruled by the devil, and are captives of the devil, [and] are not ruled by the Spirit of Christ.

Conf. Apol. Aug. Conf. p. 147. Prob. b. Broadly, improperly, and less precisely, the church is called a gathering of the called, indiscriminately composed of true believers and saints, and mixed with hypocrites and the wicked, yet professing the same faith, who constitute one body of Christ, and one church in the manner in which a heap of wheat and mixed chaff are said to constitute one heap of wheat, the denomination being taken by synecdoche from the more worthy part.

For in this broader sense, the church is compared by John the Baptist to a threshing floor, containing both chaff and wheat, Matt. III, 12 .

Q. IV. What is the church strictly and properly so called? The church, strictly, properly, and precisely so called, is the assembly of true believers and saints, whom God, moved by mercy, in view of the merit of Christ, has called out from the impious dregs of the world and the state of sin to His kingdom and the state of grace by the ministry of the divine word, has regenerated, justified, and grafted into Christ the Redeemer, and together with other reborn persons, sanctifies and preserves them for the mutual edification and salvation of the whole body and of the individual members. Obs.

I. The church, κυρίως (properly) and strictly so called, can be described according to the received allegory, that it is the mystical or spiritual body, aggregated and united through faith from true believers and saints in Christ as the Head, from whom, through the ministry of the word and sacraments imparting influence, it draws life, sense, and motion, and with new members being born from time to time, it takes on an increase suitable to itself, for its own preservation and salvation.

Obs. II. We have described the church according to the proper and principal signification of the word "church," following the counsel of PHILIP MELANCHTHON, which he gave in the Apol. Aug. Conf. p. 146. Although hypocrites and the wicked are associates of this true church according to external rites, yet when the church is defined, it is necessary that it be defined as that which is the living body of Christ, and likewise that which is the church in name and in reality.

And there are many reasons for this. For it is necessary to understand what thing principally makes us living members of the church. If we define the church only as an external polity of good and bad men, people will not understand that the kingdom of Christ is the righteousness of the heart and the gift of the Holy Spirit, but will judge that it is only the external observation of certain cults and rites.

Q. V. How is the church strictly and properly so called divided? The church, strictly and properly so called, is divided into the militant and the triumphant.

The former is that in which reborn men, placed under the leadership and, as it were, the banner of Christ, fight in this life against Satan, the world, and carnal concupiscence . The latter is that in which the blessed, having finished their warfare and obtained victory over their enemies, rejoice and triumph with Christ in eternal life .

Prob. a. The church is called militant from the spiritual warfare or battle against the devil, the world, and the flesh; concerning which battle against Satan, Eph.

VI, 11, 1 Pet. V, 8, 9; against the world, 1 John V, 4; against the flesh, Rom. VII, 14, Gal. V, 17, it is treated. obtained victory over their enemies, rejoice and triumph with Christ in eternal life b).

Prob. b. The Church triumphant obtained its name from a spiritual triumph, or victory brought back from enemies, concerning which see Apoc. II, 10. c. IV, 4. VI, 5. Obs. The Church militant and triumphant differ, because in the former travelers live, in the latter the blessed: the former have a right to the thing, the latter a right in the thing: yet of both there is a sweet communion in the same right under one and the same head, Christ, Eph. I, 22. Hebr. XII, 23. The Papists add a Church suffering in purgatory, but without a solid foundation.

Latin:

Ecclesia synthetica bifariam accipitur: a) κυρίως, stricte, proprie & praecise, pro coetu hominum vere credentium & sanctorum, Christo capiti per fidem coniunctorum, unumque mysticum & vivum corpus constituentium: b) παχυλῶς, late & improprie, atque per synecdochen pro coetu vocatorum ex vere credentibus sanctisque, & admixtis hypocritis, ac malis, eandem tamen fidem profitentibus, aggregato.

Obs. I. Alii auctores docent, vocem, ecclesia, bifariam sumi: a) pro coetu τῶν κλητῶν, vocatorum, eandem doctrinam fidei profitentium, & sacramentis a Christo institutis utentium: b) pro coetu τῶν ἐκλεκτῶν, electorum, qui vera fide in Christum credunt. Pro electis Augustana Confessio artig. VIII. vere credentes & sanctos substituit; quia praeter electos alii, non electi ad vitam aeternam, viva ecclesiae membra sunt, nimirum πρόσκαιροι, qui vere in Christum credunt, vereque sancti sunt; adeoque ecclesiae genuina in eo statu membra, licet electi ad gloriam non sint. Distinguunt igitur nonnulli inter electos ad gratiam, & ad gloriam. Per electos ad gratiam intelligunt renatos omnes, qui vel ad tempus tantum credunt, vel in fide usque ad finem vita perseverant. Nos propter ambiguitatem vocis, electio, ecclesiam stricte, proprie & principaliter dictam, cum August. Conf. vocamus coetum hominum vere credentium & sanctorum, vel coetum renatorum.

Obs. II. Coetus renatorum dicitur ratione formae internae (quae fundatur in fide iustifica, qua Christo capiti membra iunguntur) invisibilis; coetus autem vocatorum promiscuus ratione formae externae (quae consistit in publica societate professionis eiusdem fidei) visibilis.

Prob. a. Ecclesiam κυρίως, stricte, proprie & exquisite dictam, esse, coetum vere credentium & sanctorum, evincitur:

1) Quia expresse dicitur ecclesia sanctorum, 1 Cor. XIV, 33. genus electum, regium sacerdotium, gens sancta, populus in peculium, 1 Petr. II, 9. In symbolo apost. vocatur communio sanctorum: item una sancta, catholica ecclesia, quae epitheta & honorifica encomia primo, per se & proprie conueniunt ecclesiae praecise acceptae, pro congregatione vere credentium & sanctorum.

2) Ecclesia est virgo pura & sponsa Christi, 2 Cor. XI, 2. Desponsata Christo per fidem, Hos. II, 20. Quare homo, expers fidei, non est vera pars ecclesiae. Appellatur etiam mater filiorum Dei, Gal. IV, 26. Sumus autem filii Dei, per fidem in Christo Iesu, Gal. III, 26. Ergo ecclesia est mater fidelium, non hypocritarum, non impiorum, non haereticorum; est mater vivorum, non mortuorum.

3) Eph. IV, 16. describitur ecclesia, tanquam corpus spirituale, quod totum secundum omnes iuncturas (quibus coagmentatum in ratione vnius corporis constituitur) dependet a Christo velut a capite, h. e. per influxum, qualis in membra a capite redundat, ab hoc ut incrementum capiat corpori conveniens, idque per caritatem. Vnde colligitur, eos omnes & solos esse vera membra ecclesiae proprie dictae, qui vivunt ex supernaturali gratia, & influxu Christi capitis, & Spiritus eius, adeoque vera fide, cum caritate coniuncta, pollent.

4) Ecclesia est regnum spirituale, quod intra nos est, Luc. XVII, 21. est regnum Christi, quod non est de hoc mundo, Io. XVIII, 39. Proinde ecclesia est regnum a regno diaboli distinctum. Certum est autem, impios in potestate diaboli, & membra regni diaboli esse, sicut docet Paullus, Eph. II, 2. cum ait: diabolum efficacem esse in incredulis. esse in incredulis.

Quare cum ecclesia vere fit regnum Christi, proprie est congregatio sanctorum. Nam impii reguntur a diabolo, & sunt captiui diaboli, non reguntur spiritu Christi.

Conf. Apol. Aug. Conf. p. 147. Prob. b. Late, improprie, minusque exquisite ecclesia dicitur coetus vocatorum promiscue ex vere credentibus, sanctisque, & admixtis hypocritis ac malis, eandem tamen fidem profitentibus, aggregatus, qui constituunt vnum Christi corpus, & vnam ecclesiam eum in modum, quo aceruus tritici & admixtae paleae dicuntur vnum aceruum tritici constituere, denominatione per synecdochen a potiori desumta.

Etenim hoc sensu latiori sumta ecclesia a Ioanne Baptista comparatur areae, paleas simul & triticum continenti, Matth. III, 12 .

Quaest. IV. Quid est ecclesia stricte & proprie dicta? Ecclesia stricte, proprie & exquisite dicta, est coetus vere credentium & sanctorum, quos Deus, motus misericordia, intuitu meriti Christi, ex impia mundi colluuie, statuque peccati ad regnum suum, statumque gratiae ministerio verbi diuini euocauit, regenerauit, iustificauit, & Christo redemptori inseuit, eosque vna cum aliis renatis sanctificat & conseruat, ad corporis totius, singulorumque membrorum mutuam aedificationem & salutem. Obs.

I. Potest ecclesia, κυρίως & proprie dicta, iuxta receptam allegoriam describi, quod fit corpus mysticum, siue spirituale, ex vere credentibus & sanctis in Christo, vt capite, per fidem aggregatum atque vnitum, a quo, mediante ministerio verbi & sacramentorum, influxum impertiente, vitam, sensum & motum trahit, & genitis subinde nouis membris, incrementum capit sibi conueniens, ad sui conseruationem & salutem.

Obs. II. Iuxta propriam & principalem vocis, ecclesia, significationem descripsimus ecclesiam ex PHILIPPI MELANCHTHONIS consilio, quod is dedit in Apol. Aug. Conf. p. 146. Quamquam hypocritae & mali sint socii huius verae ecclesiae, secundum externos ritus: tamen cum definitur ecclesia, necesse est eam definiri, quae est viuum corpus Christi, item quae est nomine & re ecclesia.

Et multae sunt causae. Necesse est enim intelligi, quae res principaliter efficiat nos viua membra ecclesiae. Si ecclesiam tantum definiemus, externam politiam esse bonorum & malorum, non intelligent homines, regnum Christi esse iustitiam cordis, & donationem Spiritus S., sed iudicabunt, tantum externam obseruationem esse certorum cultuum ac rituum.

Quaest. V. Quomodo diuiditur ecclesia stricte & proprie dicta? Ecclesia, stricte & proprie dicta, diuiditur in militantem, & triumphantem.

Illa est, in qua homines renati, sub Christi ductu & velut vexillo, contra Satanam, mundum & carnalem concupiscentiam constituti, in hac vita pugnant . Haec est, in qua beati, militia sua defuncti, & victoriam de hostibus nacti, cum Christo in vita aeterna gaudent & triumphant .

Prob. a. Ecclesia militans dicitur a spirituali militia, vel pugna aduersus diabolum, mundum & carnem; de qua pugna aduersus Satanam, Eph.

VI, 11. 1 Petr. V, 8. 9. aduersus mundum, 1 Io. V, 4. aduersus carnem, Rom. VII, 14. Gal. V, 17. agitur. hostibus nacti, cum Christo in vita æterna gaudent & triumphant b).

Prob. b. Ecclesia triumphans obtinuit nomen a spirituali triumpho, vel victoria ab hostibus reportata, de qua vide Apoc. II, 10. c. IV, 4. VI, 5. Obs. Ecclesia militans & triumphans differunt, quia in illa viatores, in hac beati vivunt: illorum est ius ad rem, horum ius in re: vtrorumque tamen in eadem iure suauis communio sub vno eodemque capite Christo, Eph. I, 22. Hebr. XII, 23. Pontificii addunt ecclesiam laborantem in purgatorio, sed sine solido fundamento.


### Q. VI. How manifold is the militant church?

The militant church is divided into the church of the Old and New Testament. The former was enclosed within the narrow borders of Judea, and as many as wished to learn the true worship of God and the way of obtaining eternal salvation before Christ was born, it behooved them to approach and be joined to the Israelitic people a): the latter is gathered to Christ from all languages and nations, with the voice of the gospel sounding everywhere. The former was not to endure perpetually, but was to be terminated by the advent of Christ: the latter is to endure as long as the fabric of the world shall stand (*). The former is surnamed Israelitic, the latter Christian. The former is more frequently called synagogue, the latter more often church b). Prob. a. The assembly of the faithful before Christ was born is called ἐκκλησία Ἰσραὴλ, Sirac. I, 15. Moses was ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, as Stephen testifies, Acts VII, 37. That this Israelitic church was restricted to the Jewish people, Moses teaches, Deut. IV, 8. Prob. b. Although the congregation of faithful Israelites, formed for the sake of religion, more frequently comes under the name of συναγωγῆς among the LXX interpreters and in the N. T., this is nevertheless not perpetual. For St. James in epistle II, 2, used the name synagogue for an assembly of Christians, saying: If anyone should enter εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν. Conf. Hebr. X, 25.

Latin:

Ecclesia militans diuiditur in ecclesiam veteris, & noui testamenti. Illa angustis Iudaeae limitibus fuit inclusa, & quotquot verum Dei cultum, & viam consequendae salutis aeternae discere voluerunt ante Christum natum, illos oportuit populo Israëlítico accedere & coniungi a): haec ex omnibus linguis & gentibus, voce euangelii vbique sonante, Christo colligitur. Illa non perpetuo durare, sed aduentu Christi terminari debuit: haec duratura est, quoad mundi machina stabit (*). Illa Israëlítica, haec christiana cognominatur. Illa frequentius synagoga, haec saepius ecclesia appellatur b). Prob. a. Coetus fidelium ante Christum natum dicitur ἐκκλησία Ἰσραὴλ, Sirac. I, 15. Moses fuit ἐν ἐκκλησίᾳ, teste Stephano, Actor. VII, 37. Ecclesiam isthanc Israëlíticam ad populum iudaicum restrictam fuisse, docet Moses, Deut. IV, 8. Prob. b. Quamvis fidelium Israëlitarum congregatio, religionis caussa facta, frequentius apud LXX. interpretes, & in N. T. συναγωγῆς nomine veniat, hoc tamen non est perpetuum. Nam S. Iacobus epist. II, 2. nomen synagoga pro coetu Christianorum vsurpauit, inquiens; Si quis ingrediatur εἰς συναγωγὴν ὑμῶν. Conf. Hebr. X, 25.


### Q. VII. How is the synthetic militant church of the Old and New Testament distinguished?

The synthetic militant church of both testaments is distinguished into universal and particular. The universal church is either absolutely or respectively universal. The absolutely universal church is a gathering consisting of the faithful of all places and times, whom God, from the beginning of the world, has called, still calls today, and will call until the consummation of the age, to the actual communion of spiritual goods through the proclamation of His word a). The church that is universal in a qualified sense and respectively is a gathering of all the faithful at the same time, wherever in the world they may be, persisting in one and the same internal communion of faith and charity b). A particular church is a gathering not of all, but of certain of the faithful called in a certain place to participate in salvation, and persisting in internal spiritual communion c).

Prob. a.
