Ratione qualitatis; propter doctrinam & fidem, quatenus eam fidem profitetur, quam semper vniuersitas credentium est professa: ratione quantitatis; ob diffusionem per vniuersum terrarum orbem; quatenus non perinde, atque ecclesia vet. test. ex peculiari quadam gente, vel natione, sed ex omnibus gentibus in vniuerso orbe colligitur. Quam notabilem distinctionem enucleatius exposituri auctores alii, distinguunt inter catholicismum internum, qui est fidei seu doctrinæ, & externum, qui est loci, temporis ac personarum. Doctrina vero & fides catholica dicitur, quæ ab omnibus omnino saluandis requiritur. Confer. D. SCHERZERI system. pag. 708. Alii obseruant, quod ecclesia interdum vocetur καθολικὴ prout opponitur hæresi, h. e. heterodoxis ecclesiis: interdum dicatur καθολικὴ in respectu & oppositione ad particulares ecclesias. Priori modo, quando ecclesia vocatur καθολικὴ, non idem est, ac vniuersalis; sed idem est, ac ecclesia vera & orthodoxa, & appellatur ita a doctrina catholica, i, e. orthodoxa Christi & Apostolorum doctrina, quæ, cum hæreses in ecclesia passim inualescerent, dicta est catholica, quatenus a Christo & Apostolis profecta, omnibus fidelibus commendata, atque vnanimi eorum consensu recepta & credita fuit. Hoc sensu etiam ecclesia particularis doctrinam catholicam, siue orthodoxam amplectens, dicitur catholica. Sic CONSTANTIVS Imperator ecclesiam Alexandrinam vocat catholicam, apud SOCRATEM Libr. II. c. 18. SOZOMENVS Callinicum appellat Episcopum catholicæ ecclesiæ, quæ in Pelusio est, Lib. II. c. 24. Posteriori modo, quando ecclesia dicitur καθολικὴ, nempe in ordine ad particulares ecclesias, idem est, quod vniuersalis ecclesia, & hoc modo ad ecclesiam catholicam non sufficit, quod Christi & Apostolorum doctrinam amplectatur, quia hanc etiam particularis ecclesia recipit, sed requiritur insuper ad catholicam ecclesiam, vt omnes credentes omnium locorum & temporum ambitu suo includat. Conf. D. HVLSEM. manuale in A. C. p. 258. & D. BECHMANNI instit. theol. p. 575. Alii annotant, quod ecclesiæ catholicismus primario & per se æstimandus sit ex consensu cum doctrina Prophetarum & Apostolorum, nec non conspiratione illa fidei, quam Deus vniformiter operatur in omnibus, qui ecclesiæ adhærent: secundario ex amplitudine locorum, & diffusione per omnes populos. Conf. D. IO. ADAMI OSIANDRI colleg. system. P. VII. p. 30. Nam ratione actualis diffusionis per omnia loca & populos, ne apostolica quidem & primitiua ecclesia fuit catholica, quamuis per omnes populos fuerit diffundenda, atque adeo parata omnes in sinum suum recipere, sine discrimine nationis, sexus aut status.

Ceterum catholicismus locorum, personarum ac temporum ecclesiæ noui test. proprietas est, & quidem totius, per quam differt ab ecclesia veteris test. quæ ad populum Iudaicum erat restricta, & a particularibus cœtibus quibusuis.

Prob. d. Apostolica dicitur ecclesia, partim quod plantata sit ab Apostolis, partim quod traditam ab Apostolis doctrinam salutis amplexa & superstructa sit super fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum, immo, angulari lapide existente, Iesu Christo, Eph. II, 20.


### Quæst. XXV. What is the church called broadly, improperly, & synecdochically?

The church, taken broadly, improperly, and synecdochically, is a promiscuous assembly of men, called to the kingdom of God and the participation of spiritual and heavenly goods by means of the ministry of the word, and consenting in the external profession of the same doctrine to the praise of God and the eternal salvation of the called themselves.

Observation I. PHIL. MELANCHTHON Part. III. Loc. theol. p. 116. describes the church taken broadly as a visible assembly of those embracing the gospel of Christ and rightly using the sacraments, in which God is effective through the ministry of the gospel and regenerates many to eternal life, in which assembly, however, there are many who are not reborn, but who consent to the same doctrine.

Observation II. A promiscuous assembly of the called is called the Christian church improperly, for the reason that it admits into its society hypocrites and the unholy, who are rotten, dead, and equivocal members of the church. Such a church is called synecdochical because the name of the church is attributed to a promiscuous assembly, consisting of the reborn and the intermixed non-reborn, by a synecdoche of the part for the whole, by which that which belongs to the true part is attributed to the whole assembly, composed of good and bad. Certainly, an assembly of men consisting of mere hypocrites and the unholy is a synagogue of Satan, and not the church of Christ. Therefore, the promiscuous assembly is called the church of Christ on account of the reborn and the elect, who are the more worthy and noble part of the church.

Observation III. A promiscuous assembly of the called is called the visible church: a) by reason of the external means by which it is gathered, which are the word and sacraments: b) by reason of the men dwelling in it: c) by reason of the external form and society, which consists in the use of means and external profession.

Question XXVI. What is the form of the church taken broadly?

The form of the church taken broadly consists in the consensus of the external profession of the same doctrine and the participation in the same sacraments.

Obj. A consenting profession of the same doctrine of faith is called the form of the external church, and, as D. Hülsemann teaches in Breviar. c. XVII. p. 71, it consists in the public society of the profession of the same faith, and its public exercise in preaching the authentic Word of God, and administering only those sacraments which were instituted by Christ.

Proof. Although in the church, taken broadly, the unholy are mingled with the holy; yet in the external profession of doctrine and the participation of the same sacraments, they must consent: This is what St. John teaches, 2 Ep. v. 10: "If anyone comes to you and does not bring this (evangelical) doctrine, do not receive him into your house (private: therefore much less into the house of God, the church, for the communion of the sacraments, which are the badge of faith), nor bid him greeting (therefore much less call him a brother in Christ), for he who says greeting to him shares in his works (of heterodoxy)."

Question XXVII.

Of what members does the church, taken broadly, consist? The church, taken broadly, consists of living and dead members, or holy men and hypocrites , among whom there is not only a civil society, but also an ecclesiastical one .

Proof a. 1) The pillars of the church, among whom was Peter, sometimes fall, Gal. II, 14. Therefore, the church of the called does not consist of merely holy persons.

2) The visible church, from the foundation of the world, has not been without hypocrites. In the church of Adam, there was Cain, a hypocrite and eventually a fratricide. In the church of Noah, there was the impious Ham. Abraham had Ishmael, the mocker of Isaac, in his church; Isaac had Esau, a profane man; Jacob had Reuben and Judah, who were incestuous; Simeon and Levi, who were murderers; Dinah, who was unchaste. Christ had in the company of His disciples Judas, a miser, a thief, and a traitor. That in the churches planted by the Apostles, the evil were mingled with the good, the Acts of the Apostles, the Pauline Epistles, and the Apocalypse of John teach.

3) The same is gathered from parables and the like, in which the church is compared to a threshing floor containing chaff and wheat together, etc. See above, Question III, Pr. b. To which add that the church is made the garden of God, Cant. IV, 12. In this garden are not only fruit-bearing trees, but also barren ones, Matt. III, 10; Luke XIII, 7. Indeed, just as one tree has some branches that are green and bear fruit, and others that are dry: so the church has some members that are green, bearing the fruit of good works, and others that are rotten and dead, luxuriating only in the leaves of words. The church is a vineyard, producing not only grapes but also wild grapes, Is. V, 4.

4) In the church there are men saying, "Lord, Lord," but not doing the will of the heavenly Father, Matt. VII, 21; having a form of godliness but denying its power, 2 Tim. III, 5; professing that they know God, but denying Him by their works, Tit. I, 16. Therefore, there are hypocrites in the church.

Proof b. Because hypocrites profess the same faith with their mouths and use the same sacraments.

The antithesis is that of the Novatians, Donatists, and Anabaptists, who deny that a group to which the unholy are mingled is a true church. Their arguments are:

I answer with the words of the Augsburg Confession, Art. VIII: Although the church is properly the congregation of saints, yet in this life many hypocrites and evil men are mingled with it. Certainly, the evil are in the church of the called, although they are not in the church of the regenerate and the elect.

II. In whatever assembly men do not conform themselves to the rule of Christ, that assembly is not a Christian church: But in that assembly in which hypocrites are found, men do not conform themselves &c: Therefore. Resp. 1) In that assembly where no men conform themselves to the rule of Christ, that assembly is not a Christian church; I concede. But we assert that the assembly of those called indiscriminately is called a Christian church by synecdoche, because its principal part conforms itself to the rule of Christ. Which synecdoche is customary for sacred writers. For Paul, at the beginnings of various epistles, calls the whole assembly, e.g., Roman, Corinthian, Ephesian &c. [by synecdoche]. AUGUSTIN, ep. to Paullinus, writes thus: It is the custom of scripture to speak of a part as if it were the whole. Just as the Apostle in his first epistle praises the Corinthians in parts, as if all were such, when some of them were praiseworthy.

III. Christ sanctified and cleansed the church with the washing of water by the word, so that he might present it to himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle, i.e., lacking vices and defects: Eph. V. 26. 27.

But that assembly in which the evil are mixed with the good does not lack vices: Therefore, that assembly is not the church of Christ.

Resp. The church militant in this life is cleansed, or regenerated and justified, just as it is sanctified inchoatively and continuatively; but the same, in the future life, having overcome its enemies, will be presented as triumphant, glorious internally and externally, not having spot or wrinkle, i.e., consummatively holy, immune from all sin and the remnants of sin. In this life, the church with all its members acknowledges its imperfection, praying daily from the Lord's Prayer: forgive us our debts! (*).

IV. Whatever church is entirely beautiful, in it there are no evil people: But the church of Christ &c.

Cant. IV, 7. Therefore. Resp. When the church is called the bride of Christ, entirely beautiful, then it is precisely understood as the assembly of the regenerate and the elect, which is beautiful with an imputed beauty, because it shines with the rays of the bridegroom Christ, and then with an inherent beauty, which is said to be entirely perfect, not by reason of degrees, since its members often fall through infirmity, but by reason of parts, because it strives that no divine precept be violated by determined malice. But we are dealing here with the church taken broadly, as it is an assembly of the called, using the preaching of the word and the sacraments.

V. Whoever are in the Christian church are its members and have the spirit of Christ, 1

Cor. X, 17. Rom. VIII, 9. Hypocrites are not members of the church, nor do they have the spirit of Christ. Resp. Whoever are in the invisible church, or the assembly of the regenerate and the elect, they are true and living members of the church, informed by the spirit of Christ. But in the visible church, or the assembly of the called, there are hypocrites and the unholy, who are dead members, and are called members by reason of external profession of faith, not by reason of internal union through faith with Christ. Instance: Hypocrites have no communion with the regenerate.

For what communion has light with darkness? 2 Cor. VI, 15. Therefore, by no reason do they belong to the church. Resp. Hypocrites have no internal communion with the regenerate; because they are not joined by the bond of saving faith to the head, Christ; yet they have with them in the church of the called an external communion, and that not only civil, such as exists in the Turkish empire between Muhammadans and Christians, but also ecclesiastical, on account of the consensus in the external profession of the same faith, and participation in the same sacraments.

VI. From whom true believers and the holy are commanded to separate themselves, with them they cannot constitute one church: But they are commanded [to separate] from unholy hypocrites &c. 2 Cor, VI, 17. Therefore. Resp.

Latin:

Ecclesia late, improprie & synecdochice accepta, est cœtus promiscuus hominum, ad regnum Dei & spiritualium ac cœlestium bonorum participationem, mediante verbi ministerio vocatorum, atque in externa eiusdem doctrinæ professione consentientium in Dei laudem & ipsorummet vocatorum salutem æternam.

Obs. I. PHIL. MELANCHTHON Part. III. Loc. theol. p. 116. describit ecclesiam late acceptam, quod sit cœtus visibilis amplectentium euangelium Christi & recte vtentium sacramentis, in quo Deus per ministerium euangelii est efficax, & multos ad vitam æternam regenerat, in quo cœtu tamen multi sunt non renati, sed de eadem doctrina consentientes.

Obs. II. Promiscuus vocatorum cœtus ecclesia Christiana improprie dicitur, ideo, quod intra societatem suam admittit hypocritas & non sanctos, qui sunt membra ecclesiæ putida, mortua & æquiuoca. Dicitur ecclesia synecdochice talis, quia cœtui promiscuo, constanti ex renatis, & admixtis non-renatis, nomen ecclesiæ tribuitur per synecdochen partis pro toto, qua toti cœtui, ex bonis & malis conflato, tribuitur id, quod veræ parti conuenit. Sane cœtus hominum constans ex meris hypocritis & non sanctis est synagoga Satanæ, & non ecclesia Christi. Promiscuus itaque cœtus vocatur ecclesia Christi, ob renatos & electos, qui sunt pars dignior & nobilior ecclesiæ.

Obs. III. Promiscuus vocatorum cœtus dicitur ecclesia visibilis: a) ratione mediorum externorum, quibus colligitur, suntque verbum & sacramenta: b) ratione hominum, in illa versantium: c) ratione externæ formæ & societatis, quæ in vsu mediorum & externa professione consistit.

Quæst. XXVI. Quæ est forma ecclesiæ late sumtæ?

Forma ecclesiæ late sumtæ, consistit in consensu externæ professionis eiusdem doctrinæ, & participatione de iisdem sacramentis.

Obi. Consentiens professio eiusdem doctrinae fidei, dicitur forma ecclesiae externae & docente D. Hvlsem. in breuiar. c. XVII. p. 71, consistit in publica societate professionis eiusdem fidei, & eiusque publici exercitii in praedicando verbum Dei authenticum, & administrando sola illa sacramenta, quae a Christo instituta sunt.

Prob. Quamuis in ecclesia, late dicta, sanctis admixti sint non sancti; in externa tamen doctrinae professione, & eorundem sacramentorum participatione consentire debent: Id quod docet S. Ioannes, 2 ep. v 10. Si quis venit ad vos, & hanc (euangelicam) doctrinam non affert, ne recipiatis eum, in domum (priuatam: ergo multo minus in domum Dei ecclesiam, ad communionem sacramentorum, quae sunt tessera fidei), nec aue (ergo multo minus fratrem in Christo appelletis) ei dixeritis, Qui enim illi dicit aue, communicat eius operibus (heterodoxiae).

Quaest. XXVII. Ex quibus membris constat ecclesia late sumta?

Ecclesia, late accepta, constat e membris viuis & mortuis, seu hominibus sanctis & hypocritis a), quos inter non tantum est societas ciuilis, sed etiam ecclesiastica b).

Prob. a. 1) Ecclesiae columnae, quas inter fuit Petrus, aliquando labuntur, Gal. II, 14. Ergo ecclesia vocatorum non constat ex meris sanctis.

2) Ecclesia visibilis inde ab orbe condito non caruit hypocritis. In ecclesia Adami erat Cain hypocrita, & tandem fratricida. In ecclesia Noachi erat impius Chaimus. Abrahamus Ismaelem, Isaaci illusorem, Isaacus Esauum, hominem profanum, Iacobus Rubenum & Iudam, incestuosos; Simeonem & Leui, homicidas; Dinam impudicam, in sua ecclesia habuit. Christus habuit in consortio discipulorum suorum Iudam auarum, furem & proditorem. In ecclesiis ab Apostolis plantatis malos bonis admixtos fuisse, docent acta apostolica, epistolae Paulinae & apocalypsis Ioannis.

3) Idem colligitur ex parabolis & similibus, in quibus ecclesia comparatur areae, paleas & triticum simul continenti, &c. Vid. supra Quaest. III, Pr. b. Quibus adde, quod ecclesia fit hortus Dei, Cant. IV, 12. In hoc horto sunt non solum arbores frugiferae, sed etiam steriles, Matth. III, 10. Luc. XIII, 7. Quin immo vt vna arbor alios ramos habet virides, & fructum ferentes, alios vero aridos: Sic ecclesia aliqua membra habet viridia, ferentia fructum bonorum operum, aliqua vero putrida, & emortua, verborum foliis duntaxat luxuriantia. Ecclesia est vinea, faciens non tantum vuas, sed etiam labruscas, Es. V, 4.

4) In ecclesia dantur homines, dicentes: Domine, Domine, sed non facientes voluntatem Patris caelestis, Matth. VII, 21. habentes speciem pietatis, virtutem vero eius abnegantes, 2 Tim. III, 5. confitentes, se nosse Deum, operibus vero abnegantes, Tit. I, 16. Ergo in ecclesia dantur hypocritae.

Prob. b. Quia hypocritae eandem fidem ore profitentur, iisdemque sacramentis vtuntur.

Antithesis est Nouatianorum, Donatistarum, & Anabaptistarum; negantium, illum coetum esse veram ecclesiam, cui admixti sunt non sancti. Quorum argumenta sunt:

I. Ecclesia est congregatio sanctorum. Ergo in illa minime dantur non sancti. Respondeo verbis August. confessionis artic. VIII. Quanquam ecclesia proprie fit congregatio sanctorum, tamen in hac vita multi hypocritae & mali admixti sunt. Nimirum mali sunt in ecclesia vocatorum, licet non sint in ecclesia renatorum & electorum.

II. In quo coetu homines se non conformant ad regulam Christi, ille coetus non est ecclesia Christiana: Atqui in illo coetu, in quo dantur hypocritae; homines se non conformant &c: Ergo. Resp. 1) In quo cœtu nulli homines se conformant ad regulam Christi, ille cœtus non est ecclesia Christiana; concedo. At nos asserimus, quod promiscua vocato rum cœtus dicatur ecclesia Christiana synecdoche, quia præcipua eius pars ad regulam Chri sti se conformat. Quæ synecdoche scriptoribus sacris vsitata est. Nam Paulus in initiis di versarum epistolarum totum cœtum, v. g. Romanum, Corinthiacum, Ephesinum &c. coin mac synecdoche AUGUSTIN. ep. ad Paullinum sic scribit: Mos est scriptura, ita loqui de parte, tanquam de toto. sicut Corinthios in primis epistola sua par tibus ita laudat Apostolus, tanquam omnes tales sint, cum essent laudabiles quidam eorum.

III. Christus sanctificauit & mundauit ecclesiam lauacro aquæ in verbo, ita, vt sisteret eam sibi splendidam ecclesiam, non habentem maculam, aut rugam, i. e. carentem vitiis & defectibus: Eph. V. 26. 27.

At cœtus ille, in quo mali bonis admixti sunt, non caret vitiis: E. cœtus ille non est ecclesia Christi.

Resp. Ecclesia militans in hac vita mundatur, siue regeneratur & iustificatur iuxta, atque sanctificatur inchoatiue & continuatiue; eadem autem in futura vi ta, superatis hostibus tanquam triumphans sistetur splendida interne & externe, non habens maculam aut rugam, h. e. consummatiue sancta, immunis ab omni peccato, & reliquiis pec cati. In hac vita ecclesia cum omnibus suis membris suam agnoscit imperfectionem, ex ora tione dominica quotidie precans; remitte nobis debita nostra! (*).

IV. Quæcunque ecclesia tota pulcra est, in illa non sunt mali: Atqui ecclesia Christi &c.

Cant. IV, 7. Ergo. Resp. Quando ecclesia dicitur sponsa Christi, tota pulcra, tunc præ cise intelligitur cœtus renatorum & electorum, qui est pulcer cum pulcritudine imputata, quia confulcat radiis sponsi Christi, tum pulcritudine inhærente, quæ tota perfecta dicitur, non ratione graduum, siquidem eius membra sæpe ex infirmitate labuntur, sed ratione par tium, quia eo annititur, ne vllum præceptum diuinum deffinata malitia violet. Nos au tem hic agimus de ecclesia late sumta, prout est cœtus vocatorum, prædicatione verbi & sa cramentis vtentiun.

V. Quicunque sunt in ecclesia Christiana, sunt eius membra & habent spiritum Christi, 1

Cor. X, 17. Rom. VIII, 9. Hypocritæ non sunt membra ecclesiæ, nec habent spiritum Christi. Resp. Quicunque sunt in ecclesia inuisibili, siue cœtu renatorum & electorum, illi sunt vera & viuâ ecclesiæ membra, spiritu Christi informata. At in ecclesia visibili, seu cœtu vocatorum, dantur hypocritæ & non sancti, qui sunt membra mortua, & dicuntur membra ratione externæ fidei professionis, non ratione internæ vnionis per fidem cum Christo. Instantia: Hypocritæ nullam habent communionem cum renatis.

Quia enim est com munio lucis cum tenebris? 2 Cor. VI, 15. Ergo nulla ratione pertinent ad ecclesiam. Resp. Hypocritæ cum renatis nullam habent communionem internam; quia vinculo fidei falaitice non capite Christo non sunt coniuncti; habent tamen cum iisdem in ecclesia vocatorum communionem externam, eamque non tantum ciuilem, qualis est in imperio Turcico inter Muhammedanos & Christianos, sed etiam ecclesiasticam, ob consensum in externa eiusdem fidei professione, & participationem de iisdem sacramentis.

VI. A quibus vere credentes & sancti iubentur se separare, cum iis non vnam possunt constituere ecclesiam: Atqui ab hypocritis non sanctis iubentur &c. 2 Cor, VI, 17. Ergo.


### Q. XXX

Resp. 1) A distinction is made between mental and local separation. Truly believing and holy people are commanded to separate themselves in mind and spirit from the impious, lest they follow their impurity or impiety; yet the impious can be in the church, like chaff in a heap of wheat. 2) We do not say that hypocrites constitute one church with true believers, but that the former adhere to the latter accidentally and beyond the intention of Christ, just as chaff adheres to wheat, yet they do not constitute one heap of wheat with it.

Quæst. XXVIII. In how many ways is the church taken in a broad sense, for a visible assembly of the called?

The visible church of the called is either true, or pure, or false, or impure. Proof. Just as it usually happens that, when hypocrites and the unholy are mixed with true believers and saints in one assembly, sometimes the former, and at other times the latter, stand out or prevail (and the saints are indeed considered to prevail when, by reason of doctrine, it is preached purely in public with harmful errors expelled, and also regarding the integrity of morals, when good examples of Christian virtues flourish, with vices suppressed; but the unholy prevail and stand out, by reason of morals indeed, when vices spread or reign with impunity, and by reason of doctrine, when false dogmas are publicly scattered and true doctrine and its confessors are oppressed): So then, the promiscuous assembly of the called is simply and absolutely called the church of Christ, or with an added encomium, a true and pure church, when the saints prevail by reason of doctrine and morals; but when the unholy, especially by reason of doctrine and public profession, stand out in the church, then that promiscuous assembly, aggregated from saints and the unholy, is not called the church absolutely, but in a certain respect, or with an addition, a false, impure, corrupt church. Confer D. BAYER in comp. theol. post. III. c. 13. p. 1006.

Quæst. XXIX. What is the true church?

The true, or pure, church (*) is an assembly of men in which all things that are necessary to be believed for salvation and to be done for the holiness of life are taught clearly from the Word of God, without the admixture of harmful errors, and the sacraments are duly administered according to the institution of Christ, and thus spiritual children are begotten, who are joined to Christ the head through true faith, and become one body in him.

Quæst. XXX. Is the true church of the called to be called one, holy, apostolic, and catholic?

The true visible church in a certain respect is one, holy, apostolic, and catholic. Proof. The true visible church, aggregated from the reborn and the elect and the mixed-in hypocrites, is 1) one, by external unity, on account of the profession of the same doctrine of faith, and because of the concord & ecclesiastical peace: but by internal unity, or that of saving faith and sincere charity, the reborn and the elect are joined, who are contained within the visible assembly of the called, which professes the true doctrine. 2) It is called holy; by a synecdoche of the part for the whole: because the better part, or the truly believing and holy, stand out and prevail in the true church. 3) It is apostolic: because the doctrine which is publicly set forth in it is built upon the foundation of the Apostles. 4) It is catholic, by reason of internal catholicity: because it professes the entire and uncorrupted catholic doctrine: but it is not catholic, if you look at external catholicity, for the reason that it does not embrace all who truly believe and are holy, since the children of God are also begotten in a corrupt church.

Latin:

Resp. 1) Distinguitur inter separationem mentalem, & localem. Vere credentes & sancti iubentur se separare mente & animo ab impiis, ne eorum impuritatem, aut impietatem sectentur; possunt tamen impii in ecclesia esse, vt paleæ in aceruo tritici. 2) Non dicimus, hypocritas cum vere credentibus vnam ecclesiam constituere, sed illos his per accidens & præter intentionem Christi adhærere, sicut paleæ adhærent tritico, neque tamen cum hoc vnum aceruum triticeum constituunt.

Quæst. XXVIII. Quotuplex est ecclesia late sumta, pro visibili cœtu vocatorum?

Ecclesia vocatorum visibilis est vel vera, siue pura, vel falsa, seu impura. Prob. Quem ad modum fieri assolet, vt, cum vere credentibus & sanctis admisceantur in vno cœtu hypocritæ & non sancti, aliquando illi, alias autem hi emineant aut præualeant (ac sancti quidem præualere censentur, cum ratione doctrinæ, quando ea expulsis erroribus noxiis pura publice prædicatur, tum quoad integritatem morum, quando exempla bona virtutum Christianarum vigent, suppressis vitiis; non sancti autem præualent & eminent, ratione morum quidem, quando vitia impune grassantur, aut regnant, ratione doctrinæ autem, quando falsa dogmata publice sparguntur, ac vera doctrina eiusque confessores opprimuntur): Ita tunc demum promiscuus vocatorum cœtus simpliciter & absolute ecclesia Christi, vel cum addito encomio, ecclesia vera & pura dicitur, quando sancti, ratione doctrinæ & morum præualent; quando autem non sancti, præsertim ratione doctrinæ & professionis publicæ in ecclesia eminent, tunc promiscuus ille cœtus, ex sanctis & non sanctis aggregatus, non dicitur ecclesia absolute, sed secundum quid, aut cum addito, ecclesia falsa, impura, corrupta. Confer. D. BAYER in comp. theol. post. III. c. 13. p. 1006.

Quæst. XXIX. Quid est ecclesia vera?

Ecclesia vera, seu pura (*), est cœtus hominum, in quo omnia, quæ ad salutem creditu, & ad vitæ sanctimoniam factu sunt necessaria, citra admixtos errores noxios, ex verbo Dei perspicue docentur, & sacramenta iuxta institutionem Christi rite administrantur, & sic filii spirituales gignuntur, qui per veram fidem Christo capiti coniunguntur, & in ipso vnum corpus fiunt.

Quæst. XXX. Estne ecclesia vocatorum vera dicenda vna, sancta, apostolica & catholica?

Ecclesia visibilis vera certo respectu est vna, sancta, apostolica, & catholica. Prob. Ecclesia visibilis vera ex renatis electisque, & admixtis hypocritis aggregata, est 1) vna, vnitate externa, propter professionem eiusdem doctrinæ fidei, atque ob concordiam & pacem ecclesiasticam: vnitate autem interna, seu fidei salvificae sinceraeque caritatis, coniuncti sunt renati & electi, qui in visibili vocatorum coetu, veram doctrinam profitente, continentur. 2) Sancta dicitur; per synecdochen partis pro toto: quia pars potior, siue vere credentes & sancti, eminent atque praevalent in ecclesia vera. 3) Apostolica est: quia doctrina, quae in ea publice ponat, Apostolorum fundamento est superstructa. 4) Catholica est, ratione catholicismi interni: quia doctrinam catholicam integram & incorruptam profitetur: non autem est catholica, si spectes catholicismum externum, propterea, quod non omnes vere credentes & sanctos complectitur, cum filii Dei etiam in ecclesia corrupta gignantur.


### Q. XXXI. Are there also heretics in the true church?

Manifest heretics do not stand out or prevail in the true church ). Occult heretics, however, can exist in the orthodox church ). But the same are not of the true church ).

Proof a. A church in which heretics dominate, and errors overturning the foundation of faith preponderate, is not true, pure, and orthodox, but false, impure, and corrupt.

Proof b. 1) From 1 Cor. XI, 19. "There must be also heresies among you, that they which are approved may be made manifest among you." It is not absolutely, but hypothetically necessary that there be heresies in the church, supposing, namely, the blindness of the intellect and the malice of the human will, along with the craftiness of the devil, which God permits so that the faithful may be tested, and those approved may be made known to all. 2) From Acts XX, 30. "Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them." Those heretics who arise from the true church certainly exist in it, although they lie hidden for a time.

Proof c. Heretics are not of the true church, for the reason that they are not its living members. For they lack saving faith, as the formal reason of the members of the church.

Latin:

Manifesti haeretici in ecclesia vera non eminent, aut praevalent ). Occulti tamen haeretici in ecclesia orthodoxa exsistere possunt ). At iidem non sunt de ecclesia vera ).

Prob. a. Ecclesia, in qua dominantur haeretici, & praeponderant errores, fundamentum fidei euertentes, non est vera, pura & orthodoxa, sed falsa, impura, & corrupta.

Prob. b. 1) Ex 1 Cor. XI, 19. Oportet haereses inter vos esse, vt qui probati, manifesti fiant inter vos. Non absolute, sed hypothetice necessarium est, in ecclesia esse haereses, supposita scil. coecitate intellectus & malitia voluntatis humanae, iuxta atque versutia diaboli, quas Deus permittit, vt fideles probentur, probati omnibus innotescant. 2) Ex Act. XX, 20. Ex vobis ipsis surgent viri, qui loquentur peruersa, vt abstrahant discipulos post se. Qui haeretici ex ecclesia vera exfurgunt, vtique in ea exsistunt, licet ad tempus lateant.

Prob. c. Haeretici non sunt de ecclesia vera, ideo, quod non sunt viua ipsius membra. Carent quippe fide saluifica, tanquam ratione formali membrorum ecclesiae.


### Q. XXXII. What is the false, or impure, church?

The false, or impure, church is an assembly of men in which the doctrine of faith from the Word of God is publicly proposed with errors and corruptions admixed, and the sacraments are indeed administered, but are not dispensed in the manner and for the end for which they were instituted by Christ. ) Observation.

The true and false church are here opposed to each other not contradictorily; in which sense a false church is one that is plainly not a church, e.g., an assembly of Muhammadans, ruining the entire true religion; but privatively, so that a false church is one that is falsified, vitiated, corrupted, and impure.

Latin:

Ecclesia falsa, siue impura, est coetus hominum, in quo doctrina fidei ex verbo Dei, admixtis erroribus & corruptelis, publice proponitur, & sacramenta quidem administrantur, sed non eo modo & fine, quo a Christo instituta sunt, dispensaantur. ) Obs.

Ecclesia vera & falsa hic sibi opponuntur non contradictorie; quo sensu falsa est ecclesia, quae plane non est ecclesia, v.g. coetus Muhammedanorum, totam religionem veram pessundans; sed priuatiue, vt ecclesia falsa sit falsata, vitiata, corrupta, impura.


### Q. XXXIII. What are the proper and infallible marks of the true visible church?

The proper marks of the true visible church, by which it is infallibly known to a Christian man skilled in the Sacred Scriptures, are the pure preaching of the divine Word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments. ) Observation

I. We are not speaking of the marks common to the true and false church, but of the marks and signs proper to the true church, by which its truth is so recognized that it can be distinguished from any false church whatsoever. The marks common to the true and false church are the preaching of the divine Word and the administration of the sacraments. But the marks proper to the true church are the pure preaching of the Word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments. Obj. II. The most proper mark of the true church is the pure proclamation of the Word, to which the legitimate dispensation of the sacraments is commonly joined, as being virtually included in the profession of the truth; a mark indeed proper, belonging only to the true church, but not to every one, nor always.

For the church existed at one time before Abraham without the ordinary choir of sacraments, and for forty years in the desert the church was without circumcision. For this reason, the pure preaching of the Word is a mark of the church πρώτως (primarily), or in the first place; the legitimate dispensation of the sacraments, as an appendix to the preached Word, is a mark of the same δευτέρως (secondarily), or in the second place.

Hence the use of the sacraments, e.g., of the Eucharist, is sometimes interrupted, namely in times of persecution, while the church nevertheless remains.

Obj. III. The marks of the true church already mentioned are marks of the visible church, or of the church taken as a gathering aggregated from true believers and hypocrites mixed in.

If it happens by God’s permission that the church, oppressed by the tyranny of persecutors, has no public exercise of religion, no public ministry by whose work it might publicly teach and profess the faith which the faithful have fixed in their hearts, then it will lie hidden, and by this very fact, that it lies hidden, it will have no sensible marks.

Therefore, these marks belong to the true church in a flourishing and free state, not in a corrupt and oppressed one.

Obj. IV. After churches were distracted into parts by schism, every visible church is particular.

Since, however, every particular church claims for itself the name of the true church, it began to be asked: which particular church is pure from corruptions?

The universal church, embracing all true believers and saints of all places, as it is invisible, so it cannot be distinctly known from certain signs and marks.

Obj. V. By the preaching of the Word is understood the public doctrine of faith, revealed in the Word of God, which must be known as to whether it is pure or impure from symbols and public confessions, published in the name of the whole church, or approved by the whole church, not from the opinions or writings of this or that doctor.

Furthermore, that preaching of the Word is called pure which does not involve corruptions and errors directly or indirectly overturning the foundation of the faith.

Those corruptions which are about the faith, and leave the foundation of the faith safe, do not make a church false and impure; however, there are diverse degrees of purity.

The purer and more sincere the doctrine is, the purer and more sincere is the church.

Obj. VI. When the pure preaching of the Word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments are called marks of the true church, this must be understood of marks from which the truth of the church can and ought to become known to a Christian man, to whom the infallibility of Holy Scripture is established.

To an infidel and pagan, however, the divinity and infallibility of the Scriptures must first be shown, before it can be demonstrated by certain marks which church, among those distracted by schism, is the true church.

It must be shown, however, from certain external κριτηρίοις (criteria), concerning which we treated in the Prolegomena, Q.

XXIX. Obj. VII. When the pure preaching of the Word is established as a mark of the true church, then the name of preaching is taken generally for the profession of doctrine, common to all members of the church, pastors and hearers alike, and for the public reading of biblical texts, which is like preaching, Acts 15:

21. Preaching, taken strictly, is an action proper to pastors rather than to the whole church, nor is it simply and absolutely necessary to the church, as the times of the most severe persecutions show, in which the church could be preserved through the mere reading of Scripture, without the public preaching of pure doctrine.

Question XIII. 1) By whatever means the church is gathered and preserved, by those same means it is known: But it is by the preaching of the word and the dispensation of the sacraments, etc. Therefore. The major premise is evident, because the principle of being is also the principle of knowing. We proved the minor premise above.

2) Whatever is better known than the church, and belongs to it alone and always, that is a genuine mark of the church: But the pure proclamation of the word is better known than the church, and belongs to it alone and always. Therefore. The major premise is clear: because every mark is better known than the thing marked. The minor premise is clear: because I cannot judge which is the true church, unless I first judge whether its public doctrine is revealed to be in conformity with the word of God.

3) Whatever is a mark of both true Christians and true doctors of the church, that same thing is a mark of the whole true church: But the pure proclamation of the divine word and its diligent observance is a mark of both true Christians and true doctors of the church: Therefore. The major premise is self-evident. For what makes a true member of the church, that also makes a true church; which is a congregation of true Christians. The minor premise is proved from the words of Christ, John 8:31: If you abide in my word, you are truly my disciples: and John 10:27: My sheep hear my voice. And just as false prophets are known by their corrupt doctrine; so true doctors are to be known by their pure doctrine.

4) Whatever were the marks of true churches in the time of the Apostles, those are still the marks of the true church: But the reception of apostolic or evangelical doctrine, and the right administration of baptism and the Holy Supper, were the marks of the churches in the time of the Apostles: Therefore they are still the marks of the church. The minor premise is evident from Acts 2:40, 41, 42, where Peter said: Save yourselves from this perverse generation. Those therefore who gladly accepted his word were baptized, so that there were added about three thousand souls. And they were adhering to the doctrine of the Apostles, and to the communion and the breaking of bread and prayers. If anyone here should ask: whence was it known in the time of the Apostles that the church was true and pure? by the force of this passage it must be answered: that this was known from the fact that it adhered to the doctrine of the Apostles, which was pure and without corruptions, and likewise that it received the sacrament of baptism and the Holy Supper without corruptions, just as the sacraments were administered by the Apostles.

5) That by which the true church is distinguished from the church of the malignant, that is the mark of the true church: But it is by the sincere preaching of the word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments that it is distinguished, etc. Therefore. The major premise is self-evident: because one thing is distinguished from another by its proper and essential marks. The minor premise is proved: for these two things a) formerly in the Old Testament distinguished the Israelite church from the pagans, Deut. 4:6; Ps. 147:19, 20; Gen. 17:10, 11; Exod. 12:48. b) The Arians were formerly distinguished from the orthodox in no other way than by doctrine. Wherefore TERTULLIAN says excellently, in his book De praescriptione adversus haereticos, c. 21: Those are true churches which hold what they received from the Apostles, and what the Apostles received from Christ, and Christ from God. But other churches, which were not instituted by the Apostles, yet, if they consist in the same faith, are to be considered no less apostolic, on account of the consanguinity of their doctrine.

The antithesis is that of the Papists, who deny that the pure preaching of the word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments are the proper marks of the true church, and substitute other tekmeria for it.

Their stronger arguments are: I. The marks of the true church are inseparable from it: The pure preaching of the word is not inseparable from the true church: Therefore. The major premise is evident: because the marks of the true church must be such that the true church can always be known from them. The minor premise is established by the examples of the Corinthians and the Galatians. In the church of the Corinthians, the resurrection was denied, 1 Cor. 15:12. In the church of the Galatians, the observance of the Mosaic law and justification by the works of the law were inculcated, Gal. 3. These were of the true church, but they could not be known from the pure preaching of the word, because this had ceased in them.

Resp. The purity of doctrine is to be judged from the public confession of the whole church. But in truth, the whole Corinthian church did not deny the resurrection of the dead. For Paul says expressly: How do some among you say, that there is no resurrection of the dead? Concerning the Galatians, the same Apostle says: There are some who trouble you; Gal. 1, 7. Furthermore, there are distinct degrees of purity; sometimes the word is preached more purely, sometimes less purely.

Latin:

Notae propriae ecclesiae visibilis verae, e quibus illa homini Christiano, sacrarum litterarum perito, infallibiliter innotescit, sunt pura verbi diuini praedicatio, & legitima sacramentorum administratio. ) Obs.

I. Non est nobis sermo de notis ecclesiae verae & falsae communibus, sed de notis & signis verae ecclesiae propriis, e quibus eius veritas ita cognoscitur, vt a qualibet ecclesia falsa discerni queat. Notae ecclesiae verae & falsae communes, sunt praedicatio verbi diuini, & administratio sacramentorum. At notae ecclesiae verae propriae sunt pura verbi praedicatio & legitima sacramentorum administratio. Obs. II. Propriissima verae ecclesiae nota est purum verbi praeconium, cui legitima sacramentorum dispensatio communiter adiungitur, tanquam virtualiter in professione veritatis inclusa, nota quidem propria, soli verae ecclesiae, sed non omni, nec semper competens.

Fuit enim aliquando ecclesia ante Abrahamum sine choragio sacramentorum ordinario, ac per XL. annos in deserto vacauit ecclesia circumcisione. Quam ob rem pura verbi praedicatio est nota ecclesiae πρώτως, siue primario; legitima sacramentorum dispensatio, tanquam verbi praedicati appendix, est nota eiusdem δευτέρως, & secundario.

Hinc sacramentorum vsus, v. gr. eucharistiae, quandoque intermittitur, tempore videlicet persecutionis, ecclesia nihilominus manente.

Obs. III. Notae verae ecclesiae iam memoratae sunt notae ecclesiae visibilis, siue ecclesiae funitae pro coetu, ex vere credentibus & admixtis hypocritis aggregato.

Si contingat Dei permissu, vt ecclesia persecutorum tyrannide oppressa, nullum habeat publicum religionis exercitium, nullum ministerium publicum, cuius opera fidem, quam cordibus infixam habent fideles, publice doceat & profiteatur, tum ipsa latebit, & hoc ipso, quod latet, notas sensibiles nullas habebit.

Competunt itaque hae notae verae ecclesiae in statu florente & libero, non corrupto & presso.

Obs. IV. Postquam ecclesiae per schisma distractae sunt in partes, quaelibet ecclesia visibilis particularis est.

Cum autem quaelibet ecclesia particularis sibi nomen verae ecclesiae vindicet, quaeri coepit: quaenam ecclesia particularis sit & pura a corruptelis?

Ecclesia vniueralis, omnes omnium locorum vere credentes & sanctos complectens, vt inuisibilis est, ita ex certis signis & notis distincte cognosci nequit.

Obs. V. Per praedicationem verbi intelligitur publica fidei doctrina, in verbo Dei revelata, quae vtrum pura, an impura debet cognosci debet ex symbolis & confessionibus publicis, totius ecclesiae nomine editis, vel a tota ecclesia approbatis, non ex opinionibus, aut scriptis huius, aut illius doctoris.

Ceterum pura dicitur praedicatio verbi, quae non inuoluit corruptelas & errores fundamentum fidei directe, aut indirecte euertentes.

Quae corruptelae sunt circa fidem, & fundamentum fidei saluum relinquunt, non faciunt ecclesiam falsam & impuram; sunt autem diuersi puritatis gradus.

Quo purior & sincerior est doctrina, eo purior & sincerior est ecclesia.

Obs. VI. Quando pura verbi praedicatio, & legitima sacramentorum administratio dicuntur notae verae ecclesiae, accipiendum id est de notis, ex quibus homini Christiano, cui infallibilitas S. scripturae constat, ecclesiae veritas innotescere possit et debeat.

Homini infideli autem & pagano prius scripturarum diuinitas & infallibilitas ostendenda est, quam quae inter ecclesias, schisinate distractas, vera ecclesia fit, certis quibusdam notis demonstrari possit.

Ostendenda autem ea est ex κριτηρίοις quibusdam externis, de quibus egimus prolegomeno III. quaest.

XXIX. Obs. VII. Quando pura verbi praedicatio nota verae ecclesiae statuitur, tum praedicationis nomen generaliter accipitur pro doctrinae professione, omnibus ecclesiae membris, pastoribus & auditoribus communi, ac pro publica textuum biblicorum lectione, quae est instar praedicationis, Act.

XV, 21. Praedicatio stricte accepta est pastorum potius actio propria quam totius ecclesiae, nec simpliciter & absolute ad ecclesiam necessaria, vt ostendunt tempora grauissimarum persecutionum in quibus per solam scripturae lectionem, absque publica purae doctrinae praedicatione ecclesia conseruari potuit.

Quaest. XIII. 1) Quibus mediis ecclesia colligitur & conservatur, ex iisdem cognoscitur: Atqui praedicatione verbi & dispensatione sacramentorum &c. Ergo. Maior patet, quia principium essendi est etiam principium cognoscendi. Minorem supra probavimus.

2) Quidquid est notius, quam ecclesia, ipsique soli ac semper competit, illud est genuina ecclesiae nota: Atqui purum verbi praeconium notius est, quam ecclesia, ipsique soli ac semper competit. Ergo. Maior liquet: quia omnis nota est notior notato. Minor claret: quia non possum iudicare, quae sit ecclesia vera, nisi prius iudicem, an publica ipsius doctrina verbo Dei revelata sit conformis.

3) Quidquid est nota cum verorum Christianorum, tum verorum doctorum ecclesiae, illud ipsum est nota totius verae ecclesiae: Atqui verbi divini purum praeconium & sedula observatio est nota, cum verorum Christianorum, tum verorum doctorum ecclesiae: Ergo. Maior per se manifesta est. Quod enim facit verum ecclesiae membrum, illud etiam facit ecclesiam veram; quae est congregatio verorum Christianorum. Minor probatur ex verbis Christi Io. VIII, 31. Si vos manseritis in sermone meo, vere mei discipuli estis: & Io. X, 27. Oues meae vocem meam audiunt. Et sicut ex praua doctrina pseudoprophetae cognoscuntur; ita ex pura doctrina veri doctores cognoscendi sunt.

4) Quae fuerunt notae verarum ecclesiarum tempore Apostolorum, illae adhuc sunt notae verae ecclesiae: Atqui receptio doctrinae apostolicae, sive evangelicae, baptismi & S. coenae recta administratio, ecclesiarum tempore Apostolorum notae fuerunt: Ergo adhuc sunt notae ecclesiae. Minor patet ex Act. II, 40. 41. 42. vbi Petrus dixit: Saluamini a generatione praua hac. Qui quidem igitur libenter acceptabant sermonem illius, baptizati sunt, ita ut addita sint de hac animae quasi ter mille. Erant vero adhaerentes doctrinae Apostolorum, & communioni & fractioni panis & orationibus. Hic si quis interrogauerit: vnde tempore Apostolorum cognitum fuerit, ecclesiam esse veram & puram? vi huius loci respondendum erit: hoc cognitum fuisse ex eo, quod adhaesit doctrinae Apostolorum, quae pura fuit, & sine corruptelis, item quod recepit sacramentum baptismi & S. coenae sine corruptelis, prout ab Apostolis administrata sunt sacramenta.

5) Per quae discernitur ecclesia vera ab ecclesia malignantium, illa sunt notae verae ecclesiae: Atqui per sinceram verbi praedicationem & legitimam sacramentorum administrationem discernitur &c. Ergo. Maior per se patet: quia per notas proprias & essentiales vna res ab altera discernitur. Minor probatur: Haec duo enim a) olim in V.T. ecclesiam Israëliticam discernebant a paganis, Deut. IV, 6. Ps. CXLVII, 19. 20. Gen. XVII, 10. 11. Exod. XII, 48. b) Ariani ab orthodoxis non aliter quondam discernebantur, quam doctrina. Quocirca praeclare inquit TERTVLLIANVS, libr. de praescript. aduersus haeres. c. 21. Illae sunt verae ecclesiae, quae tenent, quod ab Apostolis acceperunt, & quod Apostoli a Christo, & Christus a Deo. Aliae vero ecclesiae, quae non sunt institutae ab Apostolis, tamen, si in eadem fide consistant, non minus apostolicae reputandae sunt, propter consanguinitatem doctrinae.

Antithesis est Pontificiorum, negantium, puram verbi praedicationem & legitimam sacramentorum administrationem esse proprias verae ecclesiae notas, aliae eius τεκμήρια sub-stituentium.

Quorum potiora argumenta sunt: I. Notae verae ecclesiae ab hae sunt inseparabiles: Pura verbi praedicatio non est inseparabilis a vera ecclesia: Ergo. Maior patet: quia verae ecclesiae notae tales esse debent, vt ex illis semper cognosci possit vera ecclesia. Minor constat ex exemplis Corinthiorum & Galatarum. In ecclesia Corinthiorum negabatur resurrectio, 1 Cor. XV, 12. In ecclesia Galatarum inculcabatur observatio legis Mosaicae, & iustificatio per opera legis, Gal. III. Erant hae verae ecclesiae, sed ex pura verbi praedicatione non poterant cognosci, quia haec cessauerat in illis.

Resp. Puritas doctrinae diiudicanda est ex publica confessione totius ecclesiae. At vero tota ecclesia Corinthiaca non negauit resurrectionem mortuorum. Paullus enim expresse inquit: Quomodo dicunt quidam inter vos, non esse resurrectionem mortuorum? De Galatis inquit idem Apostolus: Sunt aliqui, qui vos conturbant; Gal. 1, 7. Ceterum sunt distincti gradus puritatis; aliquando magis, aliquando minus pure verbum praedicatur.


### Q. XXXIII. What are the proper and infallible marks of the true visible church?: II. Every true mark must be better known than the thing marked: The pure preaching of the word is not better known than the church…

II. Every true mark must be better known than the thing marked: The pure preaching of the word is not better known than the church: Therefore.

It is proved: because that which is the true & pure preaching of the word must be learned from the church. Therefore, the church must be known before the preaching of the word is known, and thus the pure preaching of the word is not better known than the church.

Resp. 1) I deny the minor. For the pure preaching of the word is better known, both by nature and to us, than the true church. To us, indeed; because it is closer to the senses. For the preaching of the word can be perceived by hearing, and the administration of the sacraments partly by hearing and partly by sight. But the church, in itself and as it is a congregation of the faithful, can be perceived by no sense. Now, that which is closer to the senses is better known to us. But by nature it is better known; because the pure preaching of the word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments is the principle and cause by which the church is gathered, nourished, and preserved. That which is known from its generating and preserving causes, its knowledge proceeds from things better known by nature. Moreover, there is no knowledge more certain and solid than that which is derived from causes. 2) Although a pagan man who is to be converted may receive a probable knowledge of Scripture from the church testifying and commending it; yet a Christian man attains an infallible knowledge of the true church from public doctrine conformable to Scripture. Therefore, a distinction must be made here between a man to be converted and one who is converted, and also between probable and infallible knowledge.

III. Whatever marks do not distinctly and certainly notify which men are truly believing and holy, those do not produce an infallible knowledge of the true church: But the pure preaching of the word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments do not distinctly and certainly notify, etc. Therefore. The major is clear: because the church, properly so called, is the assembly of those who truly believe and are holy. The minor is evident: because even hypocrites preach the divine word and administer the sacraments; who, however, are not truly believing and holy .

Resp. The pure preaching of the word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments are marks of the visible church, i.e., they are for a promiscuous assembly, aggregated from those who truly believe and the wicked mixed in, and these they show indeed distinctly, certainly, and infallibly. But if they are referred to those who truly believe alone, who properly constitute the church of Christ, then they can and ought to show them only confusedly. For of the church, taken precisely for those who truly believe and are holy, there are given no marks which show it distinctly, certainly, and infallibly. For which reason some authors rightly note that the question here is not about the marks of those who truly believe definitely, or by discernment according to individuals (which God alone knows, 2 Tim. II, 19. 1 Reg. VIII, 19.); but about the marks of those who truly believe indefinitely, by reason of the true assembly, or in which assembly the truly faithful are to be sought above others, or by what marks that assembly can be distinguished from false churches. Conf. D. SCHERZ. in system. loc. XXV. p. 710.

IV. Whatever is common to all sects, that is not a mark of the true & pure church: But the preaching of the word is common to all sects: Therefore. The major is clear: because an adequate and infallible mark of the true church ought to discern it from any sectarian and false church. The minor is proven: because all sects and churches, even false ones, boast of the purity of their doctrine.

Resp. I deny the minor. For although every sect, every church, even a false one, may boast of the purity of doctrine; yet it is one thing to have a vain boast or empty bragging, and another to demonstrate the purity of doctrine through practice itself.

By the very fact, however, that all sects appeal to the purity of doctrine, they show that it is the genuine mark of the true church.

V. The form of the true church is not its mark: The pure preaching of the divine word, etc.

Therefore. Resp. The pure preaching of the word is not the formal cause, but the efficient cause, and that an instrumental one, of the true church; however, the consensus regarding the external profession of that same pure doctrine is the form of the visible church.

But when the sincere preaching of the word founds, burns, and shines in its works, it certainly notifies the same, because science is the knowledge of a thing through its cause.

Instance: The pure preaching of the word is a mark of the ministers of the church, but not of the whole church.

Resp. The name of preaching is here taken generally for the profession of heavenly doctrine, common to all members of the church, pastors and hearers alike.

VI. There are more certain and evident marks of the true church than the pure preaching of the word and the legitimate administration of the sacraments, namely:

1) The name Catholic: 2) Antiquity: 3) Long duration: 4) Amplitude, or the multitude of believers: 5) The succession of Bishops in the Roman church, derived from the Apostles down to us: 6) Conspiracy in doctrine with the ancient church: 7) Union of members among themselves, and with the head, namely with the Roman Pontiff: 8) Holiness of doctrine: 9) Efficacy of doctrine: 10) Holiness of the life of the hearers, or of the first Fathers of the true religion: 11) The glory of miracles: 12) The prophetic light: 13) The confession of adversaries: 14) The unhappy end of enemies: 15) Temporal happiness conferred upon those who defended the church. Resp. a) generally. The mentioned marks of the true church, if the purity of doctrine and the legitimate use of the sacraments are removed, are doubtful and fallacious. b) Specifically, resp. to 1) The name Catholic was not always used in the church.

The name of Christians was used in the primitive church, Acts 11:26.

Of the Catholic [name] there is deep silence. To this is added that even heretics have attributed the Catholic name to their false churches. Concerning the Novatians, CYPRIAN testifies in epist. 37. that in the manner of those who, although they are not men, yet imitate men, they attributed to themselves the name of the Catholic church. Thus, SIXTUS Sen. refers concerning the Arians in bibl.

8. that they called themselves Catholics, but others Athanasians and Homousians. The Donatists called their assembly the Catholic church, as testified by AUGUSTINE in vol.

V. in the collation of the 3rd day with the Donatist. To 2): Without divine literature, antiquity is of no moment; for truth is older than all men, as judged by TERTULL. in apolog. c.

19. To 3): Long duration, with respect to past time, coincides with antiquity; duration with respect to future time is neither present nor certain to us.

The promise concerning the perpetual duration of the church does not pertain to this or that particular and visible church, but to the Catholic and invisible church of the elect, founded upon Christ as upon a rock.

Long duration is not proper to the true visible church, but common to the Muhammadan sect and the Jewish synagogue. To 4): Amplitude is not a proper and perpetual mark of the true church.

Indeed, in the times of Adam, Noah, and the suffering Christ, the true church was a little flock, Luke 12:32. The church of Satan is always larger than the church of Christ, because few enter the narrow way of salvation, Matth.

VII, 14. To 5): Succession in true doctrine and faith is to be highly valued: But the local and personal succession of bishops is not a proper and adequate mark of the pure church, because a) it does not belong to it perpetually and always.

Indeed, the primitive church, in which Christ and the Apostles taught, was the flower of the church, yet it lacked the local and personal succession of Bishops; nor b) does it belong solely to the true church.

The Jewish synagogue in the time of Christ had a succession of priests.

The Greek church [has had] a succession of Bishops down to the Apostl[es] extends the times of the Apostles ; nay, in the church of the Arians there was a succession of Bishops.

But if heresy breaks the thread of succession, the succession of the Roman chair long ago perished, which so many heretical and impious Pontiffs have infested.

Ad 6): By the ancient church is understood either that which indeed existed many centuries ago, but was very corrupt: or the apostolic church. If the former; the true church cannot be known from the corrupt ancient church: if the latter; that note indeed is correct, but it returns to our opinion. For to agree with the ancient apostolic church signifies to embrace the pure doctrine which it had .

Ad 7): By the union of members among themselves with the head, is understood either an internal union, which is made through faith, by which the members are joined to Christ the head, and the members are united to each other through charity: or an external one by reason of doctrine. If the former; the union of the members with the head and among themselves, therefore, cannot be a note, because internal faith and charity are not certainly known to us. If the latter; this note therefore finds no place, because it is common also to a false and impure church. Indeed, in the Arian church there was union regarding doctrine, but it could not be gathered from that, that the Arian church was a true and pure church.

Ad 8): Holy doctrine cannot be, unless it be true and pure. Ad 9): The efficacy of doctrine can be understood in two ways: a) as doctrine is efficacious which is received by many, b) by which men are effectively converted to God. In the former way it cannot be a note of the true church, because it belongs also to a false church, namely that of the Anti-Christ, as Paul testifies, 2 Thess.

II, 9. 11. In verse 9 the Apostle says that the advent of the Anti-Christ will be according to ἐνέργειαν, the efficacy of Satan, and in v. 11 he says: that God, because they did not receive the truth, would send the efficacy of error, so that infidel men might believe a lie. Indeed, in the false church the doctrine of heretics effectively moves and deceives many.

In the latter sense, efficacious doctrine is nothing other than true and pure doctrine.

Ad 10): Holiness of life is either internal or external. Neither can be a note of the true church: Not internal; for this consists in faith and inherent justice, which, just as it is not known to us, so it cannot be a note by which we may be led into the knowledge of the true church: nor external; since it is common also to a false church.

The Novatians called themselves Cathari, on account of the external holiness of life. The Donatists professed external holiness to such a degree that they denied that it was a church, where the good were defiled by the communion of the wicked.

Ad 11): The glory of miracles also is not a note of the true church: for St. Paul testifies, 2 Thess. II, 9. that the advent of the Anti-Christ will be according to the operation of Satan in all power, and signs, and lying miracles.

The glory of miracles in the church of the N. T. was only to last for a time, and many centuries have flowed by, in which the true church had no miracles. Miracles brought forth by Christ and the Apostles confirm the authority of the church.

Ad 12): Prophetic light is not a perpetual gift of the orthodox church, but peculiar to the beginnings of the church. False prophets sometimes boasted of the prophetic gift, e.g., Balaam, Num. XXIII. Samuel, i.e., a demon, foretold the destruction of Saul. Ad 13: The confession of adversaries is not a genuine mark of the true church. For how will the testimony of him be certain and infallible, who has not perceived the nature both of true doctrine and of the church, or, if he has perceived it, yet is unwilling to embrace that doctrine and associate himself with that church? The true church remains, even if it be entirely destitute of the confession of adversaries. Ad 14: The unhappy end of the enemies of the church is not a mark of the true church; because often enemies, e.g., TRAJAN, AURELIUS, ANTONINUS VERUS, SEPTIMIUS SEVERUS, etc., died peacefully; on the contrary, the Apostles, martyrs, and many pious men perished miserably. Ad 15: Temporal happiness is not a mark of the true church. For as scripture testifies: All who wish to live piously in Christ Jesus will suffer persecutions, 2 Tim. III, 12. The church was true in the time of the Apostles, though destitute of temporal happiness.

Latin:

II. Omnis vera nota debet esse notior notato: Pura verbi praedicatio non est notior ecclesia: Ergo

probatur: quia, quae vera & pura verbi praedicatio, ab ecclesia discendum est. Ergo prius ecclesia est cognoscenda, quam praedicatio verbi cognoscatur, adeoque pura verbi praedicatio non est notior ecclesia.

Resp. 1) Neg. minorem. Nam pura verbi praedicatio cum natura, tum nobis notior est, quam vera ecclesia. Nobis quidem; quia sensibus est propinquior. Potest enim praedicatio verbi auditu, & sacramentorum administratio partim auditu, partim visu percipi. Ecclesia autem secundum se, & vt fidelium congregatio est, nullo sensu percipi potest. Quod autem sensibus est propinquius, nobis notius est. Natura autem notior est; quia praedicatio verbi pura, & sacramentorum administratio legitima est principium & caussa, per quam ecclesia colligitur, alitur & conferuatur. Quod ex caussis generantibus & conferuantibus cognoscitur, illius notitia et notioribus natura proficiscitur. Nulla autem cognitio est certior & solidior, quam quae fit e caussis. 2) Quamvis homo paganus & conuertendus, ab ecclesia testificante & commendante accipiat notitiam scripturae probabilem; homo tamen christianus ex publica doctrina scripturae conformi assequitur notitiam verae ecclesiae infallibilem. Distinguendum igitur hic est inter hominem conuertendum, & conuersum, nec non inter notitiam probabilem, & infallibilem.

III. Quaecunque notae non distincte & certo notificant, quinam homines vere credentes & sancti sint, illae non pariunt notitiam verae ecclesiae infallibilem: Atqui pura verbi praedicatio, & legitima sacramentorum administratio non distincte & certo notificant &c. Ergo. Maior liquet: quia ecclesia proprie dicta, est coetus vere credentium & sanctorum. Minor euidens est: quia etiam hypocritae praedicant verbum diuinum, & administrant sacramenta; qui tamen non sunt vere credentes & sancti .

Resp. Pura verbi praedicatio & legitima sacramentorum administratio sunt notae ecclesiae visibilis, h. e. sunt pro coetu promiscuo, ex vere credentibus & malis admixtis aggregato, & hanc ostendunt vtique distincte, certo & infallibiliter. Si vero referantur ad vere credentes solos, qui proprie ecclesiam Christi constituunt, tum non nisi confuse eos ostendere possunt ac debent. Ecclesia enim, pro vere credentibus & sanctis praecise sumta, nullae dantur notae, quae eam distincte, certo & infallibiliter ostendant. Quam ob rem nonnulli auctores oppido notant, quod hic non quaeratur de notis vere credentium definite, seu per discretionem secundum indiuidua (quae solus Deus nouit, 2 Tim. II, 19. 1 Reg. VIII, 19.); sed de notis vere credentium indefinite, ratione veri coetus, seu in quonam coetu prae aliis vere fideles quaerendi sint, quibusue notis coetus ille a falsis ecclesiis dignosci queat. Conf. D. SCHERZ. in system. loc. XXV. p. 710.

IV. Quidquid omnibus sectis est commune, illud non est nota ecclesiae verae & purae: Atqui praedicatio verbi omnibus sectis est communis: Ergo. Maior clara est: quia nota adaequata & infallibilis verae ecclesiae eam discernere debet a qualibet fectaria & falsa ecclesia. Minor probatur: quia omnes sectae & ecclesiae, etiam falsae, gloriantur de puritate doctrinae.

Resp. Neg. minor. Nam etsi omnis secta, omnis ecclesia, etiam falsa, glorietur de puritate doctrinae; aliud tamen est vana gloriatio aut inanis iactantia, aliud puritatis doctrinae per ipsam praxin demonstratio.

Eo ipso autem, quod omnes sectae ad puritatem doctrinae prouocant, ostendunt, eam esse genuinam verae ecclesiae notam.

V. Forma ecclesiae verae non est eius nota: Praedicatio pura verbi diuini &c.

Ergo. Resp. Pura praedicatio verbi non est causa formalis, sed efficiens, eaque instrumentalis ecclesiae verae; consensus autem de externa professione eiusdem purae doctrinae est forma ecclesiae visibilis.

Cum autem sincera verbi praedicatio fundet, feruetque, & in ea opera fulgeat, vtique eandem certo notificat, quia scientia est cognitio rei per caussam.

Instantia: Praedicatio verbi pura est nota ministrorum ecclesiae, non autem totius ecclesiae.

Resp. Praedicationis nomen heic generaliter accipitur pro caelestis doctrinae professione omnibus ecclesiae membris, pastoribus & auditoribus communi.

VI. Dantur notae certiores & euidentiores verae ecclesiae, quam pura verbi praedicatio & legitima sacramentorum administratio, scilicet:

1) Nomen catholicum: 2) Antiquitas: 3) Duratio diuturna: 4) Amplitudo, siue multitudo credentium: 5) Successio Episcoporum in Romana ecclesia, inde ab Apostolis ad nos deducta: 6) Conspiratio in doctrina cum ecclesia antiqua: 7) Vnio membrorum inter se, & cum capite, scilicet cum Pontifice Romano: 8) Sanctitas doctrinae: 9) Efficacia doctrinae: 10) Sanctitas vitae auditorum, siue primorum Patrum verae religionis: 11) Gloria miraculorum: 12) Lumen propheticum: 13) Confessio aduersariorum: 14) Infelix exitus hostium: 15) Felicitas temporalis collata iis, qui ecclesiam defenderunt. Resp. a) generatim. Memoratae notae verae ecclesiae; remota puritate doctrinae, & legitimo sacramentorum vsu, sunt dubiae & fallaces. b) Speciatim resp. ad 1) Nomen catholicum non semper adhibitum fuit in ecclesia.

Christianorum nomen in primitiua ecclesia vsitatum fuit, Act. XI, 26.

De catholica altum est silentium. Huc accedit, quod etiam haeretici falsis suis ecclesiis nomen catholicum tribuerint. De Nouatianis testatur CYPRIANVS epist. 37. quod similium more, quae cum homines non sint, homines tamen imitantur, ecclesiae catholicae nomen sibi tribuerint. Sic de Arianis refert SIXTVS Sen. bibl.

8. quod se catholicos, alios vero Athanasianos & Homousianos appellarint. Donatistae suum coetum vocarunt ecclesiam catholicam, teste AVGVSTINO tom.

V. in collat 3. diei cum Donatistico. Ad 2): Sine diuina litteratura nullius momenti est antiquitas; antiquior quippe omnibus hominibus veritas, iudice TERTULL. in apolog. c.

19. Ad 3): Duratio diuturna, respectu temporis praeteriti, coincidit cum antiquitate, duratio respectu temporis futuri nec praesens, nec nobis certa est.

Promissio de perpetua duratione ecclesiae non pertinet ad hanc, illamue particularem & visibilem, sed ad catholicam & inuisibilem electorum ecclesiam in Christo, velut petra fundatam.

Duratio diuturna non est propria verae ecclesiae visibili, sed communis sectae Muhammedanae & synagogae iudaicae. Ad 4): Amplitudo non est propria & perpetua nota verae ecclesiae.

Sane temporibus Adami, Noachi, Christi patientis vera ecclesia grex pusillus erat, Luc. XII, 32. Ecclesia Satanae semper amplior est, quam ecclesia Christi, quia pauci angusta salutis via ingrediuntur, Matth.

VII, 14. Ad 5): Successio in vera doctrina & fide magni facienda est: At successio episcoporum localis & personalis non est propria & adaequata nota purae ecclesiae, quia a) illi non competit perpetuo ac semper.

Sane ecclesia primitiua, in qua Christus & Apostoli docuerunt, fuit flos ecclesiae, ea tamen caruit locali & personali Episcoporum successione; nec b) competit soli ecclesiae verae.

Synagoga iudaica tempore Christi habebat sacerdotum successionem.

Ecclesia graeca Episcoporum successionem vsque ad Apostolo Apostolorum tempora producit ; quinimo in ecclesia Arianorum fuit successio Episcoporum.

Quod si haeresis filum successionis abrumpit; pridem successio cathedrae Romanae intercidit, quam infederunt tot haeretici & impii Pontifices.

Ad 6): Per ecclesiam antiquam intelligitur vel ea, quae ante plura saecula exstitit quidem, sed valde corrupta: vel ecclesia apostolica. Si prius; ecclesia vera ex ecclesia antiqua corrupta cognosci nequit: sin posterius; nota illa quidem se recte habet, sed redit ad nostram sententiam. Consentire enim cum antiqua ecclesia apostolica significat doctrinam puram, quam illa habuit, amplecti .

Ad 7): Per unionem membrorum inter se cum capite, vel intelligitur unio interna, quae fit per fidem, qua membra Christo capiti sunt coniuncta, & membra per caritatem sibi invicem unita sunt: vel externa ratione doctrinae. Si prius; unio membrorum cum capite & inter se, ideo non potest esse nota, quia fides & caritas interna nobis non est certo cognita. Si posterius; nota haec ideo locum non invenit, quia communis est etiam ecclesiae falsae & impurae. Sane in ecclesia Ariana erat unio quoad doctrinam, sed inde non poterat colligi, Arianam ecclesiam esse veram & puram ecclesiam.

Ad 8): Doctrina sancta esse non potest, nisi sit vera & pura. Ad 9): Efficacia doctrinae dupliciter intelligi potest: a) ut efficax fit doctrina, quae a multis recipitur, b) qua homines efficaciter ad Deum convertentur. Priori modo non potest esse nota verae ecclesiae, quia competit etiam ecclesiae falsae, nempe Anti-Christi, teste Paulo, 2 Thess.

II, 9. 11. Versu 9. dicit Apostolus, adventum Anti-Christi fore secundum ἐνέργειαν, efficaciam Satanae, & v. 11. dicit: Deum ob non receptam veritatem missurum esse efficaciam erroris, ut homines infideles credant mendacio. Sane in ecclesia falsa doctrina haereticorum multos efficaciter movet & decipit.

Posteriori sensu efficax doctrina nihil aliud est, quam vera ac pura doctrina.

Ad 10): Sanctitas vitae est vel interna, vel externa. Neutra potest esse nota verae ecclesiae: Non interna; haec enim consistit in fide & iustitia inhaerente, quae sicut nobis non est cognita, ita non potest esse nota, per quam deducamur in notitiam verae ecclesiae: neque externa; quippe quae communis est etiam ecclesiae falsae.

Novatiani se appellarunt catharos, ob externam vitae sanctitatem. Donatistae externam sanctitatem adeo professi sunt, ut ecclesiam esse negarent, vbi malorum communione boni coinmacularentur.

Ad 11): Gloria miraculorum etiam non est nota verae ecclesiae: testatur enim S. Paullus, 2 Thess. II, 9. adventum Anti-Christi fore iuxta operationem Satanae in omni virtute, & signis, & miraculis mendacii.

Gloria miraculorum in ecclesia N. T. ad tempus tantum durare debuit, & multa fluxerunt saecula, quibus vera ecclesia nulla habuit miracula. Conciliant ecclesiae auctoritatem miracula a Christo & Apostolis edita.

Ad 12): Lumen propheticum non est donum ecclesiae orthodoxae perpetuum, sed primordiis ecclesiae peculiare. Pseudoprophetae interdum iactarunt donum propheticum, v. gr. Bileam, Num. XXIII. Sauli exitium praefagiit Samuel, i. e. daemon. Ad 13: Confessio adversariorum non est genuina nota verae ecclesiae. Quomodo enim testimonium illius erit certum & infallibile, qui & verae doctrinae & ecclesiae naturam non perspexit, vel, si eam perspexit, tamen doctrinae illam amplecti, & ecclesiae illi sese associare nolit? Manet vera ecclesia, si vel maxime confessione adversariorum destituatur. Ad 14: Infelix exitus hostium ecclesiae non est nota verae ecclesiae; quia saepe hostes, v. gr. TRAIANVS, AVRELIVS, ANTONINVS VERVS, SEPTIMIVS SEVERVS &c. placide obierunt; contra, Apostoli, martyres, multique pii miserabiliter perierunt. Ad 15: Felicitas temporalis non est nota verae ecclesiae. Nam teste scriptura: Omnes, qui volunt pie vivere in Christo Iesu, persecutiones patientur, 2 Tim. III, 12. Vera fuit ecclesia tempore Apostolorum, felicitate temporali destituta.


### Q. XXXIV. Are spiritual children of God also born in a false church?

A false church, insofar as it is false, does not beget spiritual children for God a). Yet in a corrupt, or false, church, spiritual children of God can be and are born through the word of God, which is still preached there, and through baptism, which is intact in its essentials b). Prob. a.

A false church is one in which false dogmas are joined to true ones. But just as true faith is not generated from false and erroneous dogmas: so in a false church, insofar as it is false and contaminated by errors, no spiritual children of God or true believers are begotten. Whence it is clear that he is not a child of God who pertinaciously adheres to the errors of a false church and strives to defend them.

Prob. b. 1) In that church where the word of God is publicly read and preached correctly, and baptism is administered intact in its essentials, in that church spiritual children of God and heirs of eternal life can be and are born: But this is the case in a certain corrupt church (Roman, Greek, etc.). Therefore. The major proposition is evident from the efficacy of the word and sacraments, Is. LV, 16. Tit. III, 5. 1 Petr. III, 21. Eph. V, 26. The minor, however, is established by experience. 2) If no salvation were given in a corrupt church, all infants baptized by Papists, when transferred into the bosom of our church, would have to be rebaptized. The consequent is false. Therefore, the antecedent.

You say: In a false church truth is oppressed, and errors prevail: Therefore, in a false church there is no true faith. Resp. Just as according to the parable of Christ in Matt. XIII, in that field where the householder sowed good seed, the enemy sowed tares, yet wheat can still be born from the good seed: so in those assemblies where errors are joined with true dogmas, faith can still be conceived from the word of God, as the errors do not penetrate the minds equally, or are cast out again, just as indeed believers through God's grace can discern between the precious and the vile.

Latin:

Ecclesia falsa, quatenus falsa est, non parit Deo filios spirituales a). In ecclesia tamen corrupta, sive falsa, nasci possunt, & nascuntur Deo filii spirituales per verbum Dei, quod ibi adhuc praedicatur, & per baptismum in substantialibus integrum b).

Prob. a. Ecclesia falsa est, in qua veris dogmatibus falsa iunguntur. Sicut autem ex dogmatibus falsis & erroneis non generatur vera fides: ita in ecclesia falsa, quatenus falsa & erroribus contaminata est, nulli gignuntur Deo filii spirituales, aut vere fideles. Vnde liquet, non esse filium Dei, qui erroribus falsae ecclesiae pertinaciter adhaeret, eosque defendere nititur.

Prob. b. 1) In qua ecclesia verbum Dei publice praelegitur & praedicatur iuxta, atque baptismus in substantialibus integer administratur, in illa nasci possunt, & nascuntur Deo filii spirituales, & haeredes vitae aeternae: Atqui in quadam ecclesia corrupta (Romana, Graeca &c.). E. Maior propositio patet ex efficacia verbi & sacramentorum, Es. LV, 16. Tit. III, 5. 1 Petr. III, 21. Eph. V, 26. Minor autem per experientiam constat. 2) Si in ecclesia corrupta nulla salus daretur, omnes infantes a Pontificiis baptizati, in gremium nostrae ecclesiae translati, essent rebaptizandi. Consequens est falsum. E. antecedens.

Dicis: In ecclesia falsa veritas opprimitur, & errores praevalent: E. in ecclesia falsa non datur vera fides. Resp. Quemadmodum iuxta parabolam Christi Matth. XIII. in eo agro, in quo paterfamilias bonum semen, inimicus zizania seminauit, tamen ex bono semine triticum nasci potest: ita in coetibus illis, vbi errores cum veris dogmatibus iunguntur, potest tamen ex verbo Dei fides concipi, erroribus non aeque ad animos penetrantibus, aut iterum eiectis, prout sane fideles per Dei gratiam inter pretiosum & vile discernere possunt.


### Q. XXXV. Must the true church be diligently sought by a man to be saved?

The inquiry into the true church is extremely useful for a man who is to attain eternal salvation, and in some respect necessary.

Obf. We admit that it is not simply and precisely necessary for salvation to know which and where the true visible church is. For we ourselves teach against the Papists that it is necessary only by ordinary, not absolute, necessity, and that a man can be saved even if he is ignorant of it, provided he exists as a member of the invisible church. For it can happen that someone may die blessed, even an adult, who does not yet know what the church is.

Prob. 1) The church is the body of Christ, the kingdom of heaven, the city of God, the house of God, the sheepfold of Christ, our mother, & a communion, to which spiritual goods (the word, sacraments, regeneration, etc.) are ordinarily entrusted, & the promise of the grace of presence has been made, Whence outside the visible church there is no salvation: And he who does not have the church as mother on this earth, does not have God as father in heaven, as Cyprian holds, lib. de unit. eccles.
